sections.heading: The IGCSE to IB Diploma handover, subject by subject
paragraphs: The IGCSE to IB Diploma handover is the one place in a two-board household where tutoring money reliably does more than it costs. It is also the place schools have least time for, because the students making the jump are in the middle of a summer and a change of teacher at the same time. A family that funds nothing else should consider funding this.

The gap is not about ability. It is about what each system rewards. IGCSE assesses a defined body of content with recognisable question shapes; the Diploma assesses whether a student can do something with content they have not seen arranged that way before. A grade 8 in Cambridge 0580 Extended is not a prediction of a 6 at Analysis and Approaches Higher Level, because the two assessments test different habits. Students who struggle in DP1 are usually not behind on content. They are behind on starting unfamiliar questions.

The hour counts in the table are what UAE families typically fund, not a requirement and not a promise about outcomes. They are deliberately ranges, because the right number depends on which tier the student came off, how long the summer gap was, and whether the school's DP1 group moves fast. What matters more than the number is the timing: hours spent in the term before the Diploma starts and the first term of DP1 do more than the same hours spent in DP2, when coursework deadlines already occupy the calendar.

One practical warning about money. The most common wasted spend at this transition is funding Higher Level preparation for a subject the student ends up taking at Standard Level, or funding Analysis and Approaches work for a student who should be on Applications and Interpretation. Subject and level choices are usually confirmed late in Year 11 or early in the summer. Confirm them with the school before buying a block of hours against them.

sections.heading: Budgeting a two-board household across one academic year
paragraphs: A household budget for tuition is not a price list. It is a set of lines, each with a driver behind it, and the useful exercise is deciding which lines belong in your year rather than totalling someone else's. The table lays out the lines a two-board UAE family usually has, with indicative market figures and what actually moves each one.

Start with the context, because it is unusually favourable this year. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private-school fees in Dubai would not rise for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package. For a household that had budgeted an annual fee increase, that is headroom which did not exist in previous years. Dubai is also adding seven private schools for 2026-27, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; enrolment rose six per cent during 2025-26 across 227 private schools serving 387,441 students.

The practical rule for allocating across two children is to fund risk, not fairness. A DP2 student with a wobbling Higher Level subject eight weeks from the papers has a harder deadline than a Year 10 student with eighteen months to run, and splitting the budget equally because there are two children is how families end up with two half-measures. Revisit the split at each reporting point rather than setting it once in September.

On what to avoid: prepaid blocks that expire, matching or registration charges that appear on a first invoice without having been mentioned, charges for past papers or mark schemes that are published free by the boards, and travel billed separately on top of an in-home hourly rate that was quoted as inclusive. Ask whether a quoted figure is per sixty-minute hour or per school period, and whether VAT is inside it. IB Gram's own answer on price starts with the free first lesson and the plan that comes out of it, not with a number on a page.

sections.heading: Where the marks actually go, and therefore where the hours should
paragraphs: Spending decisions get much easier once a household knows where marks are lost rather than where grades feel low. The two are rarely the same place. A student with a grade 5 in Chemistry usually does not have a Chemistry problem spread evenly across the syllabus; they have two or three recurring failures that show up in every paper, and an hour aimed at those is worth several aimed at revision in general.

On the Diploma side the internally assessed components are where the clearest, most fixable marks sit, because they are completed over weeks rather than in two hours under exam conditions. The Extended Essay is marked across five criteria totalling thirty-four marks, with critical thinking carrying the largest single share, which is why a fluent essay that never tests its own argument lands mid-band. The mathematics exploration is marked on criteria including presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Confirm current criteria and mark totals with your child's subject teacher or IB coordinator before planning around them, because the published subject guides are revised.

On the IGCSE side the recurring losses are narrower and even easier to diagnose. Students lose marks by not answering the command term, by abandoning working that would have earned method marks, by writing long answers out of sequence, and by treating a practical or alternative-to-practical paper as a memory test rather than a method test. None of those takes a term to fix. All of them take a tutor watching the student work rather than talking at them.

This is also where a household should decide what is not worth funding. Rereading notes, generic study-skills sessions, group revision eight weeks out for a student whose problem is one specific topic, and more hours in a subject the student is already comfortable in are all spend with low return. So is doubling the hours in the final month in the hope that volume substitutes for diagnosis. The question to ask after every session is what the hour produced, not what it covered.
bullets: Ask for the specific recurring failure, not a general progress comment
Fund the internally assessed components early, because late starts cap the mark
Treat practical and alternative-to-practical papers as method, not recall
Stop funding subjects that are no longer the household's biggest risk
Confirm criteria and mark allocations with the subject teacher or coordinator before planning spend

sections.heading: Entries, sessions and the costs that sit outside tuition
paragraphs: Buying hours without reading the calendar is the most common way a UAE household wastes money on tuition. Entry decisions are made months before papers are sat, tier choices are locked by the centre, and in some series results arrive in January rather than August. A plan that ignores those dates can fund the wrong tier, start a component too late, or pay for intensive work after the decision that mattered was already taken.

Cambridge publishes its key dates series by series, and in the UAE those series are June and November. Final entries for each close in the term before the papers, which is why a tiering decision taken in the exam month is taken too late, and the exact deadline is printed on the statement of entry your centre issues rather than published for parents to look up, so the exams officer is the only reliable source for it. Pearson's half of the same calendar does carry hard dates: the International GCSE November 2026 papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and the November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Ask the school which zone it sits in.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs in May/June and in November. The November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. For the June 2026 series, results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead, covering International GCSE November sittings that are still more than a year away, which is why a household should read the live official timetable rather than a date restated on any page, including this one.

For the IB Diploma, this page deliberately prints no session or results date. UAE schools sit the May session, and that is as specific as we are willing to be without a date read from the IB itself. Confirm every Diploma deadline with ibo.org or your school's IB coordinator before committing spend to a final-stretch plan. The costs that sit outside tuition altogether are entry fees set by the examination centre, late-entry charges, private-candidate arrangements, and remark or enquiry-upon-result requests, none of which a tutor controls or should be charging you for.

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and what a legitimate rate carries
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated, and a household paying for lessons is entitled to know on what basis. Individuals giving private lessons need a private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page lists it as private tutor licensing with no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system.

Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged fifteen to eighteen, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule has been published, so any specific figure a parent reads online should be treated with suspicion. A tutoring operation with its own premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal entirely and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute.

Because the permit itself is free, it explains nothing about a rate. What a household is paying for is teaching, preparation, marked feedback and continuity, and a permitted tutor at AED 300 an hour is charging for those rather than for paperwork. Abu Dhabi adds a further rule worth knowing: press-reported ADEK professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries a similar restriction. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it.

IB Gram is independent of every authority named on this page. We are not approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, we hold no training-institute permit, and we operate no office or centre in the Emirates. Naming what a regulator does is useful to a parent; implying it endorses a tutoring platform is not, and it is the single most common misrepresentation in this search.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and the five subjects it actually counts
paragraphs: Ministry of Education equivalency is the process that converts an international school certificate into something UAE authorities and universities recognise, and it is almost entirely absent from competitor pages in this search. For a household funding IGCSE subjects, the rule that matters is which subjects count, because a family can discover at the wrong moment that the five it needs are not the five it has.

On the British track, students must submit proof of five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced requirement is five, and a household planning its entries around the wrong count may fund a subject it did not need.

On the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB Diploma we publish no points threshold, because none has been read on a Ministry of Education source. Any page quoting an IB equivalency figure without citing moe.gov.ae or the emirate attestation authority is asking you to plan around an unverified number.

Two cautions for a household budget. Equivalency is a regulatory process carried out by the authorities, not something a tutoring platform performs, guarantees or should charge you for; if anyone offers to arrange it for a fee, check the official channel first. And tutoring is not a requirement for equivalency, university admission or school progression. Anyone implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a process that has published rules you can read yourself.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies in the same budget
paragraphs: The subjects most households forget to budget for are the ones the UAE requires alongside whichever international curriculum the school is licensed to teach. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of curriculum, and the KHDA mandatory subjects guidance required implementation by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. Behind that sits the federal rule: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

The requirements are specific enough to be checkable, which makes them a good test of whether a school is meeting them. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary the length of a lesson provided the total weekly time is met, and the guidance advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should last at least twenty-five minutes. Schools are also required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a concrete thing a parent can ask about at a meeting.

What this means for a household's money is mostly reassurance. The school is already obliged to deliver these subjects, so paid support is worth considering only where a child is genuinely behind, usually in Arabic as an additional language. One hard constraint applies to how any such support is described: for the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so nobody should be offering an alternative Arabic syllabus.

sections.heading: What no fee buys: the academic-honesty line
paragraphs: The most expensive mistake available in this search is not overpaying for an hour. It is paying someone to hand over assessed work. At least one page ranking for these queries sells finished Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. That is an academic-integrity breach, it is a malpractice trigger under IB rules, and the consequence lands on the student rather than on the seller. A household should treat the offer itself as disqualifying.

The line is clear and worth stating in full, because vagueness here is how families get into trouble. A tutor may teach the underlying content, explain the assessment criteria so the student can apply them, question a research question until it is workable, discuss a plan, point out where an argument is unsupported, give written feedback on a draft the student has written, and model the method on a different example. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite sections, edit a piece to completion, or hand over anything the student then submits as their own. Authorship stays with the student at every stage.

That boundary is not a limitation on what a household gets for its money; it is the point. A student who is coached through choosing a workable exploration topic and reading the criteria themselves can repeat the process on the next component. A student handed finished text learns nothing and carries the risk. The same applies to materials: published syllabuses, past papers and mark schemes belong to the examination boards and should be referenced and linked rather than reproduced or sold, and no household should be charged for documents the boards publish.

One related claim to be sceptical of at the top of the market. Describing a tutor as an examiner implies access to marking, boundaries or paper content that no legitimate tutor has, and it is used to justify a premium. If examiner experience is offered as the reason for a rate, ask what specifically it changes about the teaching. The useful answer is familiarity with how marks are awarded. Anything beyond that is a claim a household should not pay for.

process.title: Tell us about both children at once
process.description: The first conversation covers each child separately: board, subject, tier or level, the school's reporting language, and what the last report actually said. A two-board household gets two plans rather than one averaged plan, because the deadlines and the risks are different.

process.title: Match per board and per level
process.description: Each child is matched to a specialist for their exact board, subject and level, not to whoever is next available. Where the subject is thinly staffed, such as IGCSE Computer Science 0478 or Higher Level Economics, we say how long the match is likely to take rather than filling the slot with a generalist.

process.title: A free first lesson for each match
process.description: The first lesson with any new match is free and no payment details are taken before it. It runs the full session length and it is a teaching lesson, not a sales call. If the match is wrong, say so and we match again; nothing is owed for a first lesson that did not work.

process.title: Agree the plan and the spend in writing
process.description: Before anything is paid for, a household should have in writing the rate, whether it is per sixty-minute hour, the number of sessions, what marked feedback is included, the cancellation terms and what happens if a tutor becomes unavailable. Ask any provider for those six things, including us.

process.title: Review at each reporting point, not at the end
process.description: Schools report several times a year, and each report is a decision point about where the household's hours should go next. The question at each one is which subject now carries the most risk, and whether the hours currently funded are still pointed at it.

whyPoints.title: Two specialists for the price of one generalist
whyPoints.description: A household running IGCSE and the Diploma at once gets a match per board and per level, each at the ordinary rate for that level. Geography stops being the thing that decides who teaches your child, which is the practical benefit of delivering one-to-one over live video.

whyPoints.title: Figures you can check, with the publisher named
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the provider or source that published it, with October 2026 as the read date. Three of the six most visible competitor pages in this search publish no price at all, and we would rather show the market and our method than nothing.

whyPoints.title: Honest about delivery, before you book
whyPoints.description: Lessons for families in the Emirates are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visiting is a service offered only in India. That is stated here rather than discovered after a deposit.

whyPoints.title: Coursework support that keeps the student the author
whyPoints.description: Supervision for an exploration, an internal investigation, a commentary or an Extended Essay is teaching, questioning and feedback on the student's own drafts. Nobody supplies text. The boundary is written out in full on this page so a household knows exactly what it is buying.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built for the UAE year
whyPoints.description: Sessions are set in Gulf Standard Time around two school timetables, move to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan, and are planned backwards from each board's published entry and exam windows rather than from a generic term structure.

whyPoints.title: No guarantees, and no invented numbers
whyPoints.description: We publish no grade promise, no satisfaction percentage and no self-asserted star rating, because none of those could be evidenced. What a household can judge instead is the free first lesson, the written plan, and what each hour actually produces.

faqs.question: We have one child on IGCSE and one in the Diploma. Can a single tutor cover both boards?
faqs.answer: Occasionally, and it is usually a false economy. The two systems reward different habits: IGCSE assesses a defined body of content in recognisable question shapes, while the Diploma assesses what a student can do with content arranged in an unfamiliar way. Someone fluent in Cambridge 0580 Extended is not automatically the right person for Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. Because lessons are delivered over live video, there is no travel premium to amortise across two children, so booking two specialists costs the same per hour as stretching one person across both and wastes far less of the time you pay for.

faqs.question: What should a two-board household expect to spend across one UAE academic year?
faqs.answer: It depends on how many subjects are genuinely at risk rather than how many are taught. Using Bestimate's 2026 Dubai estimates for a weekly one-hour session, a qualified tutor sits around AED 600 to 1,200 a month and a specialist in an exam year around AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more. A household funding one weekly hour for a Year 11 and one for a Diploma student is therefore planning in the low thousands of dirhams a month, rising from January. Those are market figures from a published rate table, not our prices; start with the free first lesson and build the plan from there.

faqs.question: Can a tutor who drives to a UAE address realistically serve both of our children?
faqs.answer: The arithmetic rarely works. A visiting tutor can only teach families within a reasonable drive, and the chance that the nearest available person covers Cambridge Extended science and Diploma Higher Level maths well is small. In practice a household choosing proximity is choosing a generalist, and often paying a two-hour minimum per visit because the drive has to pay for itself. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address at all; home visiting is offered only in India, and teaching here is one-to-one over live video, which is what makes a specialist match per child possible.

faqs.question: Our Year 11 finishes Cambridge Maths 0580 in June. What should we set aside for the Analysis and Approaches handover?
faqs.answer: UAE families who fund this transition typically buy somewhere between twenty and thirty hours across DP1 for a student moving from Extended at grade 7 to 9 into Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level. That is what families fund, not a requirement and not a prediction. The gap is proof, calculus from first principles, vectors and a tolerance for questions that do not look like anything practised. Hours spent in the summer and the first term of DP1 do more than the same hours in DP2. Confirm the subject and level with the school before buying a block, because funding Higher Level work for a Standard Level entry is wasted.

faqs.question: Both children need help and we can fund one. Which one should get the hours?
faqs.answer: Fund risk rather than fairness. A DP2 student whose Higher Level subject is wobbling eight weeks from the papers has a harder deadline than a Year 10 student with eighteen months left, and splitting a budget equally because there are two children often produces two half-measures. Ask which subject, for which child, has the nearest irreversible date attached to it, and point the hours there. Then revisit at the next school report rather than at the end of the year, because the answer moves. A term of concentrated work in one place usually shows more than a year of thin coverage across two.

faqs.question: Does a Higher Level hour genuinely take more teaching than an IGCSE Extended hour?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the reason is preparation rather than difficulty alone. Higher Level question types are less predictable, so a tutor cannot work from memory and has to prepare against the specific paper and the specific student. The content is also deeper, and the internally assessed component runs alongside. That is why the UAE market prices IB Diploma support above IGCSE support: Unitors, for example, publishes IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A household should expect the gap and should ask what the higher rate buys in preparation and marked feedback rather than accepting it as a level surcharge.

faqs.question: Is there a household discount for booking two children at the same time?
faqs.answer: Ask, and ask what it is attached to. In the UAE market, discounting is usually tied to a prepaid block or a monthly package rather than to a household: eight online sessions at around AED 799 a month is the pattern most commonly published. Before accepting any block, check the expiry terms, whether unused hours roll over, whether the rate is per sixty-minute hour or per school period, and what happens if one child's match turns out to be wrong. A discount that comes with hours that expire unused is not a saving. We would rather set the plan after the free first lessons.

faqs.question: Our two children are three school years apart. Is there any version of a shared session that works?
faqs.answer: Not for subject teaching. Three school years apart means different content, different assessment and different command terms, and a shared hour becomes two half-hours with an audience. There is one exception worth considering: a single session with a parent present covering how each board reports and what the next deadlines are, so the household can plan. For teaching itself, two separate bookings is the honest answer. Because lessons are over live video with no travel to recover, two sixty-minute sessions on different evenings costs the same per hour as one shared hour would have, with none of the compromise.

faqs.question: Diploma coursework deadlines and IGCSE mocks both land in January. How should the weekly hours move?
faqs.answer: Decide rather than double. January is the collision point in almost every two-board UAE household, and the instinct is to add hours everywhere, which spreads attention at exactly the wrong moment. Work backwards from the dates: a school internal deadline for an exploration or commentary is fixed and close, while mocks are diagnostic and recoverable. Front-load the coursework support in the fortnight before the internal deadline, then move the hours to paper practice afterwards. Book the slots in advance, because January is when specialist availability in this market is thinnest and the rate negotiating position is weakest.

faqs.question: Must a tutor hold a permit before our household pays them anything?
faqs.answer: Yes. Individuals providing private lessons in the UAE need a private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and administered by MoHRE. It is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's service page lists a two-working-day completion time with no fee, applied for through its smart app, website or e-services system. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged fifteen to eighteen. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount you read with caution.

faqs.question: Our two children are licensed under different emirate authorities. Does that change who we may hire?
faqs.answer: It changes what you should ask, not who you may hire. Dubai schools answer to KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to ADEK, Sharjah to SPEA, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah approve assessment methods as well as fees, so confirm with each school which board and series its subjects actually sit. In Abu Dhabi, press-reported ADEK ethics rules bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school. The tutor's permit requirement is federal and identical everywhere.

faqs.question: No UAE-based Higher Level specialist is free at our slot. What happens to the plan and the price?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than filling the slot. The thinly staffed areas in this market are predictable: IGCSE Computer Science 0478, Higher Level Economics, and the less common Diploma languages. Where no UAE-based specialist is available at your Gulf Standard Time slot, the options are a different time with the right specialist, a specialist based outside the Emirates teaching over the same live video link, or a wait with an honest estimate attached. The rate follows the subject and level, not the tutor's location. What we will not do is put a generalist in a Higher Level slot and let a household discover it in February.

faqs.question: Which subjects in a nine-subject IGCSE timetable actually repay one-to-one hours?
faqs.answer: Three at most, and usually two. The test is not which grades are lowest but which subjects have a recurring, diagnosable failure and a decision attached. A subject where the entry tier is still being decided repays hours immediately, because the tier sets the grade ceiling. A subject where the student abandons working and loses method marks repays hours quickly. A subject the student finds dull but passes comfortably does not. Spreading a budget across nine subjects produces nine thin interventions; a household that picks two and pays attention to what each hour produced will see more movement.

faqs.question: What may a tutor do with an Extended Essay draft, and what is strictly off limits?
faqs.answer: A tutor may explain the assessment criteria so the student applies them, question a research question until it is workable, discuss structure, point out where an argument is unsupported, give written feedback on a draft the student wrote, and model method on a different example. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite sections, edit a piece to completion, or hand over anything submitted as the student's own. Authorship stays with the student throughout. One page ranking for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments for AED 3,750; that is a malpractice trigger under IB rules and the consequence falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: Our equivalency file needs five accredited IGCSE subjects. Does that change which ones we fund?
faqs.answer: It can. On the British track, students must show five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking competitor states six subjects are required; the sourced figure is five. Check the file early, because discovering late that the five you have do not qualify is more expensive than any tutoring decision. Equivalency is carried out by the authorities, not by a tutoring platform, and nobody should charge you to arrange it.

faqs.question: After one term, how do we decide which hours to keep and which to stop?
faqs.answer: Judge what each hour produced rather than what it covered. Four signals are usable after a term: whether the specific recurring failure named at the start has stopped appearing in marked work, whether the student can now start an unfamiliar question without prompting, whether written feedback arrives and gets acted on, and whether the student is doing more work alone between sessions than at the beginning. If none of those has moved in a term, change the match or stop funding that subject and move the hours to the one carrying the most risk. Say so plainly; a provider worth keeping will not argue.

ib-igcse-home-tutor.closingHeading: Start with one free lesson for each child, then decide what to fund
ib-igcse-home-tutor.closingBody: A two-board household does not need a decision about the whole year today. It needs to know what an hour costs in this market, which of its children carries the nearest deadline, and whether a particular tutor is any good. The first two are answered above, with every AED figure attributed to whoever published it. The third is answered by a free first lesson for each match, with no payment details taken beforehand, running the full session length as a teaching lesson. Tell us the board, the subject and the level for each child, and we will match per board rather than per postcode. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time.

ib-igcse-online-tutor.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach across both boards: Cambridge and Pearson International GCSE at Core and Extended tier, and IB MYP and Diploma at SL and HL. Each names the syllabus codes they work from, so you can match a tutor to the paper your child actually sits.

intro.heading: Two boards in one house, under one set of UAE rules
paragraphs: Most UAE families who search for an online IB and IGCSE tuition arrangement are not shopping for one subject. They have a Year 10 or Year 11 child working through Cambridge 0580 Extended Maths and 0625 Physics, and an older sibling eighteen months into the Diploma with an Internal Assessment due. The two children sit different papers, on different calendars, marked by different organisations, with different honesty rules attached. What they share is the school, the emirate, and the authority that licensed both. That shared layer is where most of the confusion lives, and it is the part almost nobody writes about.

The regulatory layer is not decoration. The authority that licensed your child's school approves its curriculum and, in several emirates, its fees. It requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies on the timetable no matter which international curriculum the school is licensed for. It sets the language each of those subjects must be taught in and forbids combined classes for Arab and non-Arab groups. Separately, the federal government regulates the tutor you are about to hire: private tutoring in the UAE runs on a MoHRE private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023.

Then there is the Ministry of Education equivalency file, which decides whether the certificate your child finishes with is recognised in the UAE. For the British track the published rule is specific: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at the same grade. One page currently ranking for these queries tells UAE parents they need six IGCSE subjects. That is the wrong number, and a family that plans around it wastes a year of subject choices.

For the IB Diploma we publish no equivalency figure at all. The Ministry's own guidance is the only source worth planning from, and we have not read an IB points threshold on it. The honest answer is to describe the process, name the authority and send you to moe.gov.ae and your school's IB coordinator. Three competitor pages in this market handle the same gap by inventing a number. A family that acts on an invented threshold finds out at attestation, which is the worst possible moment to find out anything.

This page is built around that regulatory and school-system context, because it is the part of the decision a parent cannot delegate. The subject teaching we can do. Choosing between Maths AA and AI, closing the gap between 0625 and DP Physics, reading a mark scheme properly, keeping an exploration honest while it improves — those are tutoring problems with tutoring answers. Knowing which authority to escalate to, which three subjects are already paid for inside the school week, and which certificate the attestation office will accept is different work, and it is yours. Here is what we know, with the sources attached.
bullets: Five authorities regulate UAE private schools; ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages we studied
The MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years
Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies run alongside every licensed international curriculum
Cambridge runs June and November series; the IB session UAE schools sit is May
Every UAE lesson is one-to-one over live video; home visits are an India-only service

ib-igcse-online-tutor.programmesIntro: Three programmes cover almost every dual-board UAE household: an International GCSE course in Years 10 and 11, the MYP where a school runs the IB continuum, and the Diploma in Years 12 and 13. The notes below say what each means inside the UAE school system specifically.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Two separate boards offering the same qualification level with different papers, codes and tiering. Cambridge splits many subjects into Core and Extended, with Extended carrying the full grade range. Pearson's International GCSE uses single-tier papers in most subjects under codes such as 4MA1 and 4PH1. A school is licensed for one board per subject, sometimes mixing boards across the subject list, so the first job of any tutor is to confirm which code your child is entered for.
programmes.countryNote: Across the UAE the British curriculum is the largest single stream in Dubai's private sector, and most of those schools run International GCSE in Years 10 and 11. The emirate's regulator approves the curriculum the school is licensed to teach, which is why a tutor cannot substitute a different syllabus for the one the school entered your child under.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The IB's middle-school programme, assessed against four criteria per subject lettered A to D, each marked out of 8. There are no external papers unless a school opts into eAssessment. Marks come from the school, which means an MYP report tells you about the teacher's judgement against published descriptors rather than about an examiner's. Families moving from MYP into the Diploma often find the step in formal technique sharper than the step in content.
programmes.countryNote: A UAE school running the full IB continuum will have MYP and Diploma under the same licence from the same emirate authority. Where a family moves from an MYP school to an International GCSE school mid-stage, the receiving school decides the entry point, and the regulator has no role in that judgement.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across three Higher Level and three Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. Each subject carries an internally assessed component marked by the teacher and moderated externally. The written papers are sat in the session the school enters candidates for. The Diploma's honesty rules are stricter and more explicit than the International GCSE's, which matters a great deal when one tutor supports both children in a household.
programmes.countryNote: The International Baccalaureate accounts for a small but growing share of Dubai's private school enrolment, and the emirate's 2026-27 intake adds three new IB schools among seven new openings. More Diploma places locally does not automatically mean more Diploma subject specialists locally, which is the supply problem online delivery exists to solve.

ib-igcse-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: Diploma subjects first, with the component that decides most grades named. Where a UAE family is running both boards at once, read this grid against the International GCSE grid below it: the gap between the two is the thing a tutor is actually paid to close.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most engineering and economics courses expect. HL adds proof by induction, complex numbers and a far heavier calculus load. Marks go missing in the unstructured Paper 2 questions where a candidate knows the method but never writes the working the mark scheme pays for.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics-led, with graphical display calculator technique running through every paper. SL suits social sciences and most business degrees. Check the published entry requirements of the universities on your child's list before switching from AA, because a few named courses still specify Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Uncertainty treatment separates a 5 from a 7 more often than content does. The internally assessed investigation rewards a tight research question and honest error analysis. Students arriving from Cambridge 0625 are usually fluent algebraically and unpractised at propagating uncertainty through a calculation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The data booklet is examined, not merely allowed: candidates who have not drilled finding values under time pressure lose marks they knew. HL organic mechanism and the equilibrium maths around Kc and Ka are the two topics that most often need dedicated hours rather than general revision.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms decide the mark. 'Outline', 'explain' and 'evaluate' pay for different things, and a strong recall answer written against the wrong command term still scores poorly. The statistical element — standard deviation, error bars, reading a t-test — catches students who were never taught it at International GCSE.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is unseen non-literary analysis, which is a different skill from the literature essays most students practise. The learner portfolio is where the habits form. Students from 0500 First Language English usually write well and under-read the guiding question.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries marks that prose cannot recover, and the evaluation sentences at the end of a 15-mark answer are where most of the gap between grades sits. The internally assessed commentaries need a real news article and a specific syllabus link, chosen early rather than hunted for in week eleven.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-driven: Ansoff, BCG, break-even, cash-flow forecasting. The HL-only extension and the pre-released case study for Paper 1 both reward systematic preparation. Students often arrive from 0450 Business Studies expecting the same answer structure and find the application demand noticeably higher.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode conventions are examined precisely, and the HL abstract data structures section is the usual stumbling block. The internally assessed solution needs a real client and a documented development process, which is a project-management problem as much as a programming one.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and CAS
subjects.description: The Extended Essay and the TOK essay together carry up to three points towards the Diploma total. Both are supervised in school and both are governed by the IB's academic honesty rules, so a tutor's role is to coach the research question, test the examples and give feedback on the student's own drafting.

ib-igcse-online-tutor.igcseSubjectsIntro: The International GCSE grid, with syllabus codes. Cambridge codes begin with a zero; Pearson Edexcel codes begin with a four. Confirm the code on your child's entry form rather than the name on the textbook, because several subjects exist in both boards' catalogues under near-identical titles.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (0580 Extended, 0607 International, 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.description: The tier decision sets the grade ceiling, and it is made by the school. Extended covers the algebra, functions and trigonometry a Diploma Maths course assumes. A child sitting Core who intends to take Maths AA at Higher Level has a real gap to close, and closing it after Year 11 takes longer than closing it during.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625, 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended, or single tier at Pearson
igcseSubjects.description: Formula recall and unit discipline carry the paper. The practical paper or alternative-to-practical rewards method description more than apparatus knowledge. Students who can rearrange equations quickly tend to finish; those who cannot lose marks to time rather than to understanding.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620, 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended, or single tier at Pearson
igcseSubjects.description: Mole calculations at speed and the qualitative analysis tables are the two places marks are routinely available and routinely missed. Organic chemistry is treated descriptively here, which is why the jump to Diploma mechanism work surprises strong candidates.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610, 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended, or single tier at Pearson
igcseSubjects.description: Content-heavy and recall-rewarding, so structured retrieval practice beats re-reading. Diagram labelling and the experimental-design questions are the two components that most often need teaching rather than revising. Students who score well here still need statistics taught before the Diploma.

igcseSubjects.name: English (0500, 0511, 4EA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: First Language and Second Language routes
igcseSubjects.description: 0500 First Language English and 0511 English as a Second Language are different qualifications with different ceilings, and the school decides which a child is entered for. If the Diploma plan involves English A rather than English B, the First Language route is the one that lines up.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (0455, 0450)
igcseSubjects.description: Definition precision pays at this level in a way it stops paying at Diploma, where application and evaluation take over. Both subjects reward learning the command words and answering the one that was asked. They are useful but not required groundwork for the Diploma equivalents.

ib-igcse-online-tutor.regionsTitle: Every emirate, and the authority above it
ib-igcse-online-tutor.regionsIntro: Where you live decides which authority sits above your child's school, where a complaint goes and who approved the fees you pay. The three smallest emirates are named by none of the competitor pages we examined, which is a strange gap given that families live there and sit the same papers.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The Knowledge and Human Development Authority oversees the quality of private education in the emirate. The 2024-25 sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula, so the board your child sits is rarely the only one on the street.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
regions.note: The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools here. Its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That approval reach is wider than inspection alone, and worth knowing before you query a fee.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority. Escalation is therefore a federal route, and the Ministry's general regulations are the baseline your child's school works to.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Very little is written about it online, which makes its own listing the source to use.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Families here sit the same Cambridge, Pearson and IB papers as families in Dubai, with a far shorter local list of subject specialists to draw on — which is precisely what live video delivery is for.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under federal Ministry of Education supervision. The smallest private-school market in the country, and the clearest case for teaching over video: a single Diploma Chemistry HL candidate here should not be limited to whoever happens to live nearby.

schoolClusters.note: Students we support in Dubai attend schools across both streams, and several of these run International GCSE in Years 10 and 11 before a sixth form that offers the Diploma, A Levels or both. That handover inside one school is where the dual-board question usually starts.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi, Al Ain and Sharjah
schoolClusters.note: Outside Dubai the specialist pool thins quickly, especially for Higher Level sciences and the two Maths routes. Students we support in these emirates are taught by the same tutors as students in Dubai, because the lesson travels over video rather than over Sheikh Zayed Road.

ib-igcse-online-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways a dual-board household usually buys hours. All three run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, with the session recorded in a shared document rather than in a notebook that gets left at school.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, per child per subject
modes.description: The default. One fixed slot a week for each subject that needs it, with the tutor working from the syllabus code your child is entered for. Two children on two boards means two independent schedules, which is straightforward over video and genuinely awkward with a visiting tutor who has to be in one place at a time.

modes.title: Transition block, Year 11 into DP1
modes.description: A short, finite set of sessions built around the specific gap between the International GCSE your child has just sat and the Diploma course they are about to start. Scoped per subject, usually run across the summer or the first term, and designed to end rather than to continue indefinitely.

modes.title: Coursework and Internal Assessment supervision
modes.description: Scheduled feedback on the student's own work, with the boundary stated in writing before the first session. The tutor teaches the criteria, questions the method and comments on drafts the student has written. The student writes, the school supervises, and the declaration is the student's to sign.

sections.heading: What a dual-board search is really asking
paragraphs: An IB IGCSE online tutor in the UAE is a tutor who can teach to two separate examination specifications and knows which one is in front of them. That is the literal answer. The practical answer is narrower: a Cambridge 0625 Physics paper and an IB Physics HL paper test overlapping content with different conventions, different command vocabulary and completely different internal assessment, so a tutor who is fluent in one is not automatically useful in the other.

Families usually arrive at this search for one of three reasons. The first is two children at different stages in the same house, which is a scheduling problem more than a teaching one. The second is one child crossing from International GCSE into the Diploma, which is a genuine content and technique problem. The third is a family that has moved emirate or country mid-stage and is not yet sure which board their child will finish under.

Each of those needs a different answer, and the regulatory layer runs underneath all three. The school's licence decides which syllabus is taught. The emirate authority approves that licence and the fees. The federal Ministry decides which certificate is recognised afterwards. The tutor you hire sits under a federal work permit. None of that changes the maths, and all of it changes the plan — which is why this page spends its first half on the system and its second half on the teaching. A parent who understands the system can ask a tutor better questions, and a tutor who understands it stops giving advice that only makes sense in another country.
bullets: Confirm the syllabus code before the first lesson, not the subject name
Two children on two boards need two schedules, not one shared slot
The school decides tier and board; the Ministry decides recognition
The tutor's permit is a federal matter, separate from the school's licence

sections.heading: The regulator map, read from a dual-board family's side of the table
paragraphs: Five bodies regulate private schools in the UAE, and the complete map is published on u.ae. Dubai sits with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah fall under the federal Ministry of Education.

The reach is wider than inspection. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That means the assessment route your child follows was approved by the emirate, not chosen freely by the school. If you are deciding between two schools that both advertise the Diploma, the question worth asking is which programmes each is actually licensed to run and at what stage, because a licence to teach IB MYP is not a licence to examine the Diploma.

For a dual-board household this matters twice over. A school licensed for International GCSE in Years 10 and 11 and the Diploma in Years 12 and 13 holds both under the same emirate licence, which is why the handover inside that school is an internal matter with no regulator to appeal to. A family splitting two children across two schools in two emirates is dealing with two authorities, two fee-approval regimes and two sets of inspection reports, and should expect the escalation routes to differ.

sections.heading: Year 11 to DP1: the handover nobody schedules
paragraphs: The single most useful thing a tutor does for a dual-board UAE family is close the gap between the International GCSE a child has just finished and the Diploma course they start in September. Schools handle the administrative side of that handover well and the technical side unevenly, largely because the summer sits in the middle of it and nobody owns the six weeks in between.

The gap is not mainly content. A student who scored well at 0580 Extended knows the algebra that Maths AA assumes; what they have usually never met is the expectation that working is written for a mark scheme rather than for an answer. In the sciences the gap is methodological: 0625 does not ask a candidate to propagate uncertainty through a calculation, and DP Physics does, on almost every internally assessed investigation. In Biology the missing piece is statistics, which barely features at International GCSE and appears in the Diploma from the first term.

Scoping that properly takes a diagnostic rather than a sales conversation. The table below is the version we work from, with the subjects UAE families most often raise and an honest estimate of the hours involved. Treat the week counts as a planning figure for a weekly one-hour session, not a promise about any individual student, and expect a strong candidate to need fewer and a tier-switching candidate to need more. The diagnostic session exists to replace that estimate with something specific to your child, and the output of it is a written list of gaps you keep rather than a recommendation to buy a package.

sections.heading: Two boards, two calendars, and the zone number on your timetable
paragraphs: A dual-board household runs on two unrelated clocks. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE papers are available in May/June and November each year. The IB session UAE schools sit is May. Three separate calendars, three separate sets of deadlines, and only one of them is likely to be pinned to your kitchen wall.

The detail most families have never been told is that every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone. Cambridge also states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. A UK cousin's timetable is not your child's timetable, and a screenshot from a revision group is not a source.

Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, which is the fact that changes behaviour. For a UAE candidate the Cambridge series that exist are June and November. The February and March sitting is offered in India and is not a route a Dubai or Abu Dhabi centre can enter a child for, and the March, May and October dates attached to Checkpoint belong to Primary and Lower Secondary year groups rather than to IGCSE. Cambridge publishes the closing dates for each series rather than one annual rule, and allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version, so both the window and the entry deadline that apply to your child come from the centre and not from a tutoring page. Pearson's picture is firmer in print: its International GCSE November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, months after the entry for it had to be lodged. On the IB side we publish no dates at all: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so every IB session, upload and results date on this page is left to your school's IB coordinator to confirm, and that is a deliberate choice rather than an omission.

sections.heading: The three Ministry subjects running under both licences
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are compulsory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and the federal position is the same: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. These subjects sit on your child's timetable whether that timetable leads to a Cambridge certificate or a Diploma, and they are already inside the fee you pay.

The rules about how they run are unusually specific, and worth reading before you buy any Arabic hours. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies; combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. For non-Arab students, Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies are taught in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two practical consequences follow. First, instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes — so a timetable that squeezes these subjects into fragments is doing something the guidance discourages. Second, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, which means a tutor cannot hand your child a better Arabic syllabus. A tutor can teach the material the school is required to use, and nothing beyond it.

sections.heading: Who the law permits to tutor, and how you check
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is a permitted activity, not an unregulated one. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws.

No fine schedule has been published. Khaleej Times reported that the ministry did not specify the fine amounts or detail the penalties, so a figure circulating online as a fixed maximum is not something any page should be quoting, including this one. The application route is MoHRE's own service, listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, with no fee shown and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

One category deserves a direct warning rather than a table row. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. If someone offers you your child's own classroom teacher privately, the correct answer is no. It is a bad deal for the teacher and a worse one for your child, and the conflict of interest is the reason the rule exists. Verify this against the current ADEK policy document before relying on the exact wording.

sections.heading: Two equivalency files, and the number we will not print
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process that makes a school-leaving certificate usable in the UAE, and a dual-board family may end up with two different files. For the British track the published requirements are specific. A student must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade.

Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. That exclusion is the detail that changes subject choices in Year 9, because a child counting Arabic towards the five arrives at attestation one subject short. A competitor page currently ranking for these queries states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The published rule is five, excluding Arabic and Islamic education, and that difference is worth more to your family than any marketing claim on this page.

For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT test, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB Diploma we publish nothing, because no IB points threshold has been read on the Ministry's own pages. Equivalency is also not a process IB Gram performs, influences or speeds up, and tutoring is not a requirement for it. Describe, cite, and point you to the official channel: that is the whole of our role here.

sections.heading: What an inspection band does not tell you about one programme
paragraphs: Inspection reports are the most-read and least-understood document in UAE school choice. A band describes the provision the inspectors examined across the school, at the phases they visited, against the framework in use. It does not resolve into a verdict on a single subject at a single level, and for a dual-board family that is exactly the question being asked. A report cannot tell you whether the Chemistry HL teaching in the sixth form is strong, because that is not the unit of judgement.

Read the report for the things it does cover well. The phase-by-phase breakdown shows whether secondary provision tracks the headline. The attainment and progress lines are reported against curriculum standards, which tells you what the school is measured on. The teaching and assessment judgements say something real about marking consistency, which is the single thing that most affects an internally assessed component. And the recommendations section tells you what the school has been asked to fix, which is the most honest page in the document.

Then read it against the emirate. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so a report there sits inside a wider approval regime than inspection alone. In the three emirates supervised federally, the Ministry's general regulations are the baseline. Quote only the rating published on the regulator's own site, and never a rating repeated on a listings page. The one competitor school table we found that includes a rating column ships it empty on every row, which is at least honest.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges for an IB or IGCSE hour
paragraphs: Three of the six ranking pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, which is not a currency UAE families transact in. The figures below are market rates read from competitor pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table in October 2026. They are the market, not an IB Gram price list. For our own numbers the honest route is the free trial lesson and a conversation about what your child actually needs.

The spread is the useful information. The same hour of IGCSE Maths is sold at AED 45 and at AED 650 in this market, and the difference is not always quality. It is often format, travel and who is carrying the risk of a replacement if the tutor leaves. A rate at the bottom of the range usually means a university student teaching from the textbook. A rate at the top usually means a named individual with a long waiting list. The middle band is where most qualified subject teaching sits.

Put it against the school fee for context. The Knowledge and Human Development Authority confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. A fee freeze is the right moment to look hard at what tutoring is adding, because it is the one line in the education budget that did not move on its own.

sections.heading: A tutor at a UAE address against live one-to-one video
paragraphs: This is the comparison the search usually hides. Many UAE families start by looking for someone to teach in the living room, and the honest version of that decision has four parts: what it costs, what the travel does to the hour, how wide a pool you can choose from, and whether the schedule survives a school run. IB Gram's answer is settled and we would rather say it plainly than bury it. Every UAE lesson we arrange is one-to-one over live video. Visits to a student's address are a service we offer only in India.

The reason is the specialist pool, not the technology. A family in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain searching within driving distance may find one Diploma Chemistry tutor, or none. The same family searching for a tutor who can teach on Gulf Standard Time is choosing from everyone qualified to teach that paper. For a dual-board household the effect compounds: a 0625 Physics specialist for the Year 11 and a Maths AA HL specialist for the Year 13, in the same week, without either lesson depending on traffic on Sheikh Zayed Road.

The things a visiting tutor genuinely does better are worth naming. Presence in the room helps a younger or more distractible student. Practical apparatus cannot be shared over a screen. A parent can see the lesson happening. Against that, the market rate is higher because travel is priced in, the hour is often shorter than the slot, and the choice is limited to whoever will drive to your community. Read the table and decide; we are not pretending the trade is one-sided.

sections.heading: Academic honesty under two rulebooks
paragraphs: A dual-board household has two honesty regimes to respect, and they are not identical. The Diploma's rules around the Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay are explicit and enforced through the school's declaration process. The International GCSE's coursework and practical requirements are administered by the examination centre under the board's own rules. Both end in the same place: the work submitted must be the student's, and a paid tutor who crosses that line puts the candidate's entry at risk, not their own.

The boundary is easy to state and worth stating in writing before the first session. A tutor may teach the criteria, explain what each letter is worth, question a method, point at a weakness in a paragraph the student wrote, and keep the student honest about deadlines. A tutor may not supply text, rewrite a section, source an argument, or hand over anything the student did not produce. One page ranking in this market sells finished Internal Assessments at a published price. That is a malpractice trigger for the student and the reason we gate this boundary rather than merely describe it.

The same logic covers board material. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson. A tutor should reference them and link the board's own page, and should not reproduce or redistribute them. If a tutor offers you a private library of mark schemes, that tells you something about how they work. We link; we do not supply.
