ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.programmesIntro: Three programmes account for almost every enquiry that starts as a search for IB IGCSE tuition near me: the IGCSE years themselves, the Middle Years Programme that feeds the Diploma in IB schools, and the Diploma. Each runs on its own clock, and the interesting work is at the joins between them.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, eight or nine subjects, and almost all the marks sat in written papers at the end. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE centres; Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. The two boards use different codes for the same subject, different paper structures and, in Pearson's case, a modular option that Cambridge does not mirror. The grade a student leaves Year 11 with sets the Diploma routes that remain open.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE the choice of board is made by the school and by the examination centre, not by the family, so the first question in any IGCSE tuition conversation here is which code appears on the entry: 0580 or 4MA1, 0625 or 4PH1. Centres also decide which practical route a science subject takes, and that decision changes what a tutor should be practising.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP assesses against criteria rather than against a paper, which changes what a strong student looks like on paper. MYP 5 students in UAE IB schools sit no external IGCSE unless the school chooses to enter them, so the first fully external examination many of them meet is a Diploma paper two years later. Criterion-referenced marking is excellent training for Internal Assessment work and poor training for timed recall under pressure.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools run MYP alongside an IGCSE cohort in the same year group, so siblings in one household can be assessed in two completely different ways at the same age. Where that happens, the useful tuition work in MYP 5 is building examination stamina and timed technique before DP1 starts, rather than more criterion practice.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. Internal components are marked by the school and moderated by the IB, and their deadlines are set by the school rather than by the board, which is why two children in the same city can face the same Internal Assessment four months apart. UAE schools overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May session.
programmes.countryNote: Diploma candidates in the UAE sit papers while Ramadan, Eid and the National Day break move around the academic year, so the usable revision weeks are not evenly spaced. Counting the real teaching weeks between now and the May session, rather than the calendar months, is the single most useful thing a parent can do in DP1 and it is where most planning conversations here start.

ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.subjectsIntro: These are the IB Diploma subjects UAE families most often put under one-to-one tuition, with what the examiner is actually testing and where marks tend to go. Matching is done by subject and level, so a Physics HL request is not filled by a general science tutor.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most UAE engineering and economics applicants need. HL adds proof, deeper calculus and a demanding Paper 3. Marks are lost on unjustified steps rather than on arithmetic: an answer with no visible reasoning scores the answer mark and nothing else. The exploration is a separate skill again, assessed against criteria the student can read in advance.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use, with a graphical calculator assumed throughout. Students who choose it to avoid proof often underestimate the statistical inference at HL. Common losses are interpretation marks: the calculation is right, the sentence explaining what the number means in context is missing, and that sentence is where the mark sits.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields reward precise definitions; the rest rewards unit discipline. Where students lose marks is in extended explanation questions, where a correct idea is written in two words instead of the three steps the mark scheme wants. The internal investigation needs a measurable, controllable variable chosen early, not a topic chosen because it sounds interesting.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Bonding and energetics early, organic mechanisms and equilibrium later, and a steady demand for mole arithmetic under time pressure. HL deepens almost every topic rather than adding new ones. The investigation needs an uncertainty treatment that is planned before the first measurement, because uncertainty cannot be reconstructed afterwards from a results table.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of recall plus a demanding data-analysis paper. Students who revise by rereading notes plateau quickly; those who practise command terms separately move. Outline, explain, distinguish and evaluate each earn marks differently, and treating them as synonyms is the most common single cause of lost marks across both levels.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams carry marks in their own right: axes labelled, curves named, the shift shown and the new equilibrium marked. Evaluation is the separating skill at HL, where a judgement has to be supported rather than asserted. The internal portfolio commentaries need real published articles and a tight word discipline.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application rather than tool recall. A student who can draw a decision tree but cannot say what the result means for the firm in the case study scores poorly. HL adds depth in operations and finance. The internal work requires primary or secondary research chosen with the assessment criteria in view from the start.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis, the individual oral and, at HL, an essay on a studied text. The oral is a global-issue argument built on two extracts and it is often the component UAE students prepare last and should prepare first. Marks come from sustained analysis of technique, not from summary of content.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Half theory, half programming logic, with a solution project that has to document a real client need. Students lose marks by building something impressive and documenting it thinly. HL adds abstract data structures and a case study released each year, which needs reading as a set text rather than skimming.

ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.igcseSubjectsIntro: The IGCSE side of the same household runs on syllabus codes. These are the subjects most often requested across UAE centres, with the code a parent should check on the entry before the first lesson.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended, or Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Tiered, and the tier decision sets the grade ceiling before any revision begins. Cambridge 0580 carries no coursework, so every mark is sat in written papers. Marks go on method presentation and on unrounded working, and a Cambridge IGCSE tutor should be marking timed papers rather than teaching topics in isolation by the final term.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity and waves produce the widest spread of marks in UAE classrooms. The practical route matters: a centre entering Paper 5 needs apparatus practice, while Paper 6 needs the alternative-to-practical skills of reading scales, spotting anomalies and describing a method precisely enough to be repeated.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic families. Extended asks for calculation that Core does not, and the step up between tiers is steeper here than in most subjects. Equation balancing under time pressure, and state symbols, account for a surprising number of lost marks that revision rarely targets directly.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Large recall load with precise terminology. Transport in plants, enzymes and inheritance recur in every series. Students who write around a term instead of using it lose the mark, so vocabulary drilling pays more here than extra content coverage in the last eight weeks before a series.

igcseSubjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 / Pearson 4EA1)
igcseSubjects.description: Directed writing and extended response, assessed on reading comprehension and on writing accuracy in parallel. The directed task fails most often on audience and form rather than on content. Timing is the other frequent loss: a strong first answer and an unfinished second answer scores worse than two complete middling ones.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies and Economics (Cambridge 0450 / 0455)
igcseSubjects.description: Case-study comprehension as much as subject knowledge. Candidates who answer in general terms rather than about the business in front of them lose application marks. Calculation questions on ratios and break-even are reliable marks that go missing when working is not shown line by line.

ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.regionsTitle: Where IB and IGCSE families are, emirate by emirate
ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.regionsIntro: A search for tuition near me means something different in each emirate, because each one has its own regulator, its own school density and its own school-run timings. What stays constant is the examination series, which is why a plan built on the calendar travels between them.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The largest market by a wide margin: 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25, with seventeen curricula licensed and the International Baccalaureate accounting for seven per cent of enrolment. KHDA regulates it, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven schools and 16,846 places.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, so the tutor a family hires here should be unconnected to the child's classroom.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Evening session timing matters here: a Sharjah-to-Dubai school commute can cost an hour each way and swallow the usable study slot.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a smaller and more spread-out school network than the Abu Dhabi corniche cluster. Families here feel the specialist shortage first, because a niche Higher Level subject may have no local teacher at all. Online delivery removes that constraint without changing the timetable.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than by an emirate authority. Returns zero mentions across the competitor pages researched for this project, which tells you how little published guidance Ajman families have had about either board.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Distances between communities are real here, which is exactly where a kilometre-based tutor search produces the thinnest result.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under the Ministry of Education's supervision, on the east coast and two hours from the Dubai school cluster. For an IGCSE or Diploma family here, a drive-time tutor search returns almost nothing, and a live video lesson in Gulf Standard Time returns the specialist instead.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: The smallest private-school market in the country and also Ministry-supervised. Families often commute into Sharjah or Ras Al Khaimah for school, which pushes the realistic start of a weekday tuition slot past 17:00 and makes weekend morning sessions disproportionately valuable.

schoolClusters.note: The densest IB and IGCSE cluster in the country, and the one where both boards most often appear in the same household. Students we support attend schools across this group, sitting Cambridge or Pearson papers in Year 11 and the Diploma above it. All are KHDA-regulated, and inspection reports for each are published by KHDA rather than by any tutoring provider.

ADEK-regulated, and the emirate whose regulator is named by none of the competitor pages researched for this project. Students we support here run the same two-board pattern, often with a Year 11 sibling and a Diploma candidate in the same house. Session timing has to survive an Abu Dhabi commute, which is why slots are set around the school day rather than against it.

Regulated by SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and the Ministry of Education in Ajman, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain. Specialist subject coverage thins out quickly north of Sharjah, which makes the fallback question in this cluster unavoidable: what happens when no tutor within reach teaches the subject at the level required.

ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.modesIntro: Three formats cover almost every plan that starts as a search for IB IGCSE tuition near me. All three run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and all three are chosen against the examination date rather than against a package length.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, split by board
modes.description: The default for a household running IGCSE and the Diploma at once. One hour per subject per week, each hour owned by a tutor matched to that syllabus code, with the two children's slots deliberately placed in different parts of the evening. Content is sequenced to arrive before the school teaches it where there is time, and to repair it where there is not.

modes.title: A dated revision block
modes.description: Booked backwards from a specific series rather than open-ended. The block starts by establishing where the marks currently go, using a returned mock or a timed paper, then allocates the remaining weeks to the topics with the most recoverable marks. The last fortnight is reserved for full papers under examination conditions, because nothing new can be learned there.

modes.title: Internal assessment and coursework process coaching
modes.description: Structured conversations about the student's own work: narrowing a research question, testing whether a variable is measurable, reading one draft and commenting against the published criteria. A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback. A tutor produces no part of an assessed submission, and that line is explained to the student in the first session rather than assumed.

sections.heading: What a search for IB IGCSE tuition near me actually returns
paragraphs: A search for IB IGCSE tuition near me in the UAE returns three kinds of result: agencies buying the location term, centres with premises in one community, and freelance tutors listing a drive radius. None of those three is sorted by whether anyone in the list has taught your child's syllabus code at the level required. The ranking is by marketing spend and proximity. The thing a parent actually needs is sorted by neither.

IB Gram answers the same search with one-to-one tuition delivered over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are part of what IB Gram offers in India and are not offered anywhere in the Emirates. That is stated here early and plainly so no family discovers it late. The trade being made is explicit: you give up a tutor in the room, and in exchange the pool you are choosing from stops being everyone within a twenty-minute drive and starts being everyone who teaches that subject at that level.

For a single-board household that trade is debatable. For the household this page is written for, running IGCSE tuition in the UAE for one child and IB Diploma Programme tuition for another, it is not close. Two specialists on two different timetables cannot both live nearby, and compromising on subject depth to keep the geography tidy is how a Year 11 Physics plan ends up in the hands of someone who last taught 0625 four series ago.

sections.heading: Two boards on one kitchen calendar
paragraphs: The hardest thing about running IGCSE and the Diploma in the same house is not the content. It is that the two calendars peak at the same time and nobody publishes them together. A Pearson November paper is sat in the same fortnight as a Diploma mock. The spring entry confirmation for the June series falls in the same weeks as the final Internal Assessment versions. Families meet these collisions one at a time, as surprises, because nobody laid the two years side by side in advance.

The table below does that. It is built from dates the boards publish themselves, and where a date belongs to the IB it is left as a coordinator question rather than filled in, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and an unverified examination date on a revision plan is worse than no date at all. Read it as a planning document: the right-hand column is the only one that describes what a tutor should be doing in that month.

Two patterns show up every year. The first is that the months with the most collisions, November and February, are also the months when families start looking for help, which is the latest useful moment rather than the earliest. The second is that the handover summer between IGCSE results and the start of DP1 is almost always left empty, and it is the cheapest eleven weeks of the entire two-board sequence. Nothing is being examined in those weeks, so nothing has to be rescued in them either, and work done there is the only work in the whole two years that costs no other deadline anything.

sections.heading: Picking the series, and what each one does to the year
paragraphs: Most UAE Year 11 cohorts sit a June series, but that is a default rather than a rule, and the alternatives change the shape of the year substantially. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level examinations in a June series and a November series; the February/March series is offered to India only and is not available to a UAE candidate. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. A retake, a late arrival into the UAE or a January school start can all make a non-June series the better choice.

The planning consequence is that the entry deadline, not the paper, is the date that constrains a family. Count the June series backwards and the shape is clear: papers in May and June, revision blocks from March, forecast grades submitted by the centre before that, and the final entry list closed in the spring, roughly four months ahead of the first paper. That entry date is held by the school's examinations officer rather than published as one national deadline, and the exact day appears on the statement of entry. The November route is the one with a published window: Pearson's November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A family that starts deciding in the spring which subjects to enter has usually already missed the only date that mattered.

For the Diploma, this page publishes no session or results date. The IB's own site returns an error to automated checking, so nothing in this project is confirmed from the IB itself, and secondary sources disagree. The honest planning instruction is to treat the May session as the one UAE schools sit, and to get the exact window and results date from your school's Diploma coordinator, who holds the registration anyway.

sections.heading: The eleven-week handover from IGCSE results to the first Diploma lesson
paragraphs: Pearson released June 2026 International GCSE results to students on 20 August 2026. DP1 in most UAE schools starts in the first days of September. That gap is the one stretch of the two-board sequence with no examination pressure in it, and it is almost universally wasted. Families treat it as a holiday, which it should partly be, and then DP1 term one arrives with three subject gaps and an unfamiliar assessment vocabulary at the same time.

The useful work in those weeks is narrow and finite. It is not pre-teaching the Diploma syllabus. It is closing the two or three specific places where IGCSE content stops short of where DP1 begins, and learning how Diploma work is actually judged before anything is judged. Chemistry is the clearest example: 0620 covers moles, but DP1 opens on quantitative chemistry and bonding at a depth the IGCSE never reaches, and a student who meets that in week three of term is already behind.

The second piece of handover work is vocabulary. IGCSE marking rewards an answer; Diploma marking rewards an answer presented against a criterion. A student who has never read a criterion descriptor cannot aim at one. Reading the criteria for one subject, with a tutor, before DP1 starts is a two-hour job that pays back across two years, and it costs nothing in a week where no other deadline exists. The student who has seen a criterion descriptor in August writes a different first draft in November from the student meeting one for the first time under a deadline.

sections.heading: Proximity, the four o'clock problem and Gulf Standard Time
paragraphs: The real argument for a tutor nearby was never geography. It was the clock. A UAE school day that ends between 14:30 and 15:30, a bus journey, and a parent back from work at 18:30 leave a narrow band of hours in which a session can happen at all, and a visiting tutor's travel time eats into it from both ends. Removing the journey does not add hours to the evening, but it does stop the two ends of the slot being negotiable.

What matters more is which hour gets used for what. Online IB tuition in Gulf Standard Time can be placed precisely, which means the slot can be chosen for the task rather than for the drive. A returned paper is worth going through within an hour of the school day ending, while the student still remembers the questions. A full timed paper is worth a weekend morning and is close to worthless at 20:00 on a Wednesday. Most families discover this by accident in DP2.

Ramadan moves the whole structure, and it moves it predictably enough to plan for. Sessions shift later in the evening, often after Iftar, and the school day compresses. Families who decide in advance which subject keeps its slot and which pauses come out of the month with a plan intact. Families who improvise lose four weeks, which in a DP2 spring is the difference between a finished revision block and an abandoned one.

sections.heading: What tuition within driving distance costs, and what the market actually publishes
paragraphs: The striking thing about this search is how few providers answer it. Of the UAE tutoring pages reviewed for this project in October 2026, one competitor's own frequently-asked-questions section asks what tutoring costs and then declines to answer. Another publishes a price range in its page markup that contradicts the figure printed on the page itself. The rates below are what providers have published, each attributed to the provider and dated, so a parent can price the market before speaking to anyone.

These are market figures, not IB Gram's. They are here because a parent comparing quotes needs a reference band, and because the single largest hidden variable in a quote from a visiting tutor is whether the drive is inside the hour or billed beside it. A tutor quoting AED 250 for sixty minutes and arriving forty minutes late from another community in Dubai has quoted a different product from a tutor giving sixty taught minutes over video.

The monthly packages seen across these pages run from around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions to AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits in the home. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 estimates for a weekly one-hour session put a budget plan at AED 240 to 600 a month, a mid-range plan at AED 600 to 1,200, and a specialist examination-year plan at AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above. For IB Gram's own plan, the honest answer is a trial lesson and a conversation about the series date rather than a number on a page.

sections.heading: Coursework ceilings, deadline owners and the line a tutor does not cross
paragraphs: Internal components are where a two-board household is most exposed, because the deadlines are set by schools rather than by boards and therefore differ between two children in the same city. The IB publishes the ceiling for each component and the criteria it is marked against. The school decides when the draft is due, when the final version is due, and how many rounds of feedback sit between them. Planning against the board's calendar instead of the school's is the most common scheduling mistake in DP1.

The second exposure is honesty, and it is worth being blunt because this part of the search results is genuinely unsafe. At least one provider ranking for UAE IB queries sells finished Internal Assessments. Submitting one is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the student, not on the seller. A tutor teaches the subject, questions the research design, reads a draft and comments against the published criteria. A tutor produces no part of an assessed submission, and that boundary is explained to the student at the start.

On the IGCSE side the shape is different. Cambridge IGCSE Mathematics 0580 carries no coursework at all, so every mark is sat in a written paper. The sciences carry a practical requirement whose route is chosen by the centre: a Paper 5 practical test needs apparatus work, while a Paper 6 alternative to practical needs scale reading, anomaly spotting and method description. A tutor who does not know which route the centre entered is practising the wrong skill.

sections.heading: Examination zones, centres and the timetable version that matters
paragraphs: This is the most expensive small detail in the IGCSE year and almost nobody mentions it. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and its own guidance to examinations officers is unambiguous: it is essential that the correct version of the timetable for the zone is used, and Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone's timetable was used. A parent downloading a timetable from a search result has roughly a one in six chance of holding the right one.

The practical instruction is short. Get the timetable from your child's examinations officer, not from a search engine, and confirm the zone in writing. Then build the revision plan on those dates. A plan built on a neighbouring zone's timetable can be wrong by several days on individual papers, which is enough to put a final revision session after the paper it was meant to prepare.

Private candidates face a longer version of the same problem, because they have no examinations officer. A student sitting as a private candidate has to find a centre willing to accept external entries, meet that centre's own deadline rather than the board's, and pay the centre's fee alongside the entry fee. Those arrangements are made months ahead. For a family arriving mid-year in the UAE, the centre search is the first task and the tutoring is the second, because a brilliantly prepared candidate with no centre to sit in has nothing to sit.

sections.heading: The Ministry of Education equivalency file, opened before results day
paragraphs: Equivalency is the deadline no two-board household counts backwards from, and it is the one that affects what a certificate is worth inside the UAE. The Ministry of Education's clarification of equivalency requirements, reported in July 2026, sets out the British track precisely: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Two details inside that matter more than the headline. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects, which changes the counting for a large number of UAE candidates. And the figure is five, not six. One provider currently ranking for UAE IGCSE queries publishes a requirement of six subjects; the sourced figure in the ministry's clarification is five. Getting that wrong at subject-choice time in Year 9 is expensive to fix in Year 11.

On the American track the same clarification gives English proficiency as a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Maths test before applying. For the IB Diploma, no points threshold is published here, because none has been read on the ministry's own site. Verify it on moe.gov.ae. IB Gram describes this process and points to the official channel; it does not perform, submit or guarantee any part of it.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies: the third timetable
paragraphs: Every household running IB and IGCSE in Dubai is also running a third set of subjects, and it is the set least discussed by tutoring providers. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. These subjects sit alongside the examined curriculum, not inside it.

The rules around them are specific enough to plan against. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for the two groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. Instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than twenty-five minutes.

Two consequences follow for tuition. First, for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, so support here means working with the school's prescribed material rather than importing a syllabus. Second, schools are required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach these subjects, which is a checkable credential and a reasonable question to ask of anyone offering help with them.

sections.heading: When no specialist is free in your week
paragraphs: Every tutoring provider implies infinite availability and none has it. The subjects where this bites are predictable: Further Pure Mathematics at IGCSE, Computer Science at Higher Level, Economics at Higher Level in a narrow evening window, and any Diploma subject needed at 15:30 on a weekday by a family in Fujairah. A platform that answers every such request immediately with a yes is either very large or not telling you something.

The honest sequence is this. A request is matched against tutors who teach that subject at that level, in that board, in a slot that fits. If more than one fits, the family sees a choice. If exactly one fits, the family is told that. If none fits, the family is told that too, with the realistic wait and the alternatives: a different slot, a different week, a broader subject specialist for the content gap while a specialist is found, or a recommendation to look elsewhere if the wait is longer than the calendar allows.

That last option is said out loud because of the dates at the top of this page. A family eight weeks from a June series cannot wait three weeks for a perfect match, and a provider that holds the enquiry rather than saying so has spent weeks that belonged to the student. The trial lesson exists for the same reason: it is a check on fit before money changes hands, not a sales appointment, and a family that ends it with a no has lost an hour rather than a term.

process.title: Start from the date, not from the subject
process.description: The first question is which series or session your child is entered for, and which board. From that date the number of real teaching weeks is counted, allowing for Ramadan, the National Day break and school holidays. Everything after this is allocation of a known quantity of hours rather than an open-ended plan.

process.title: Confirm the board, the code and the route
process.description: Check the entry rather than assuming. Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel, 0580 or 4MA1, Core or Extended, Paper 5 practical or Paper 6 alternative to practical. For the Diploma, the subject, the level and the school's own internal deadlines. A tutor matched against the wrong code will practise the wrong paper structure.

process.title: Diagnose with a timed paper before teaching anything
process.description: One paper under timed conditions, marked question by question, shows where marks are going in a way that a school report cannot. The pattern matters more than the total: lost method marks, unfinished final questions and misread command terms each need a different response and a different number of weeks.

process.title: Take a trial lesson and check the fit
process.description: A single session with the matched tutor, over live video, before any commitment. The point is to see whether the student talks in it. A student who stays silent for an hour with a technically excellent tutor is not matched, and finding that out in session one is the difference between a plan and a wasted term.

process.title: Hold one slot and review at the halfway point
process.description: Sessions are placed in a fixed weekly slot chosen for the task, in Gulf Standard Time, and each is followed by a short written note. At the midpoint of the block the diagnostic is repeated and the remaining weeks are reallocated to whatever is still costing marks rather than to the original plan.

whyPoints.title: The calendar is the plan
whyPoints.description: Sessions are counted backwards from the series your child is entered for, using dates the boards publish. Where a date cannot be verified, it is left as a question for the coordinator instead of being filled in. A revision block built on an invented date is worse than no block at all.

whyPoints.title: Two boards, two specialists
whyPoints.description: A household running IGCSE for one child and the Diploma for another gets a tutor matched to each syllabus code, not one generalist covering both. The two slots are placed in different parts of the evening so neither child is tutored at the hour their attention is lowest.

whyPoints.title: Rates are attributed, not asserted
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is a published market rate with the provider and the month of reading attached. IB Gram's own position is a trial lesson and a conversation about the date, because a price quoted before anyone knows the subject, level and weeks remaining is a guess dressed as a quote.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is drawn in session one
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the subject, questions the research design, reads a draft and comments against the published criteria. A tutor produces no part of an assessed submission. That is stated to the student at the start, because the consequence of malpractice falls on the candidate and nobody else.

whyPoints.title: Availability is disclosed, including when the answer is no
whyPoints.description: If no tutor covers the subject at the level and in the slot required, the family is told, with a realistic wait and the alternatives. Where the wait is longer than the examination calendar allows, the right advice is to look elsewhere, and it is given.

whyPoints.title: Independent, with no regulator or board affiliation claimed
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is a tutor-matching platform. It holds no accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none. Regulators and boards are named on this page to explain what they do and where to verify a fact, never to imply an endorsement.

faqs.question: Is there an IB and IGCSE tutor near me in the UAE, or do lessons have to be online?
faqs.answer: Lessons with IB Gram are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around a UAE school day. Home visits are part of what IB Gram offers in India and are not offered anywhere in the Emirates. The UAE market does have visiting tutors, and published rates for that format run roughly AED 180 to 500 an hour with travel often outside the quoted hour. The trade is straightforward: you give up a tutor in the room and choose from everyone who teaches that subject at that level, rather than from whoever lives within a short drive of your community.

faqs.question: We have one child in Year 11 IGCSE and another in DP1 — can one plan cover both?
faqs.answer: One calendar, two tutors. The calendar is shared because the collisions are the problem: a November series paper and a Diploma mock window land in the same month, and internal assessment deadlines land in the same weeks as the spring entry confirmation for the June series. The tutoring is split because the boards are different and one generalist covering both will be weaker at each. In practice the two weekly slots are deliberately placed in different parts of the evening, so neither child is being taught at the hour their concentration is lowest.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE exam series should my child sit, the June one or the November one?
faqs.answer: Most UAE Year 11 cohorts sit a June series and that is usually right. The only alternative open to a UAE candidate is November: Cambridge runs a June and a November series here, and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November. There is no February or March option in this country, whatever a search result suggests, because Cambridge offers that series to India only. A November entry suits retakers, mid-year arrivals and students whose school year does not finish in June. Either way the decision is constrained by the entry deadline rather than by the paper, and that deadline is held by your centre and set months ahead of the first paper.

faqs.question: How far before the exam does the Cambridge entry deadline actually fall?
faqs.answer: Further ahead than most families expect. For both series a UAE candidate can sit, the entry list closes months before the first paper and the deadline is held by the centre rather than published as one national date, so the examinations officer is the person to ask and the statement of entry is where the day is confirmed. The published end of the chain gives a sense of the distance involved: Pearson's November 2026 timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026 and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, while June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August and to students on 20 August 2026. From entry list to certificate is most of an academic year, which is why a subject added late is the one that goes wrong.

faqs.question: What should we actually do in the weeks between IGCSE results and the start of DP1?
faqs.answer: Three things, and none of them is pre-teaching the Diploma syllabus. Read the results subject by subject rather than as an average, because a 6 in Extended Maths and a 6 in Physics carry different signals for Higher Level choices. Close the two or three specific gaps where IGCSE content stops short of DP1 term one, with Chemistry the usual example. Then read the assessment criteria for one subject with a tutor, so the student has seen how Diploma work is judged before any of it is judged. Pearson sent June 2026 results to students on 20 August 2026, which leaves about eleven weeks.

faqs.question: Does searching for tuition near me get us a better hourly rate in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. Proximity sorts a list by travel time, which is unrelated to subject fit, and the local options that appear are not necessarily cheaper. Published UAE rates run from about AED 33 to 52 an hour at the budget online end, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for a visiting tutor in the home, and AED 500 to 650 and above at the premium end. Those figures were read from provider pages in October 2026 and are the market, not IB Gram's prices. The variable that moves a quote most is whether travel sits inside the hour.

faqs.question: What is a Cambridge exam zone, and why does it change my child's timetable?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the timetable. Cambridge's guidance to examinations officers states that using the correct version for the zone is essential, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. Practically, this means the timetable should come from your child's examinations officer in writing, not from a search result. A revision plan built on a neighbouring zone's dates can place a final session after the paper it was meant to prepare for.

faqs.question: Which months are worst for a household running both boards at once?
faqs.answer: November and February, by a clear margin. November puts November series papers and a DP2 mock window inside the same four weeks. February is when final internal assessment versions are submitted while the June entry list is being confirmed subject by subject at the centre. Those are also the two months in which families typically start looking for help, which makes them the latest useful moment rather than the earliest. The fix is unglamorous: in September, put every internal deadline from both schools onto one shared calendar, and protect one evening slot per child before anything is competing for it.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic education included in those five required subjects?
faqs.answer: No. The July 2026 clarification states that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. That matters at subject-choice time in Year 9, because a student who assumes those two count towards the five can end Year 11 one accredited subject short. It does not reduce the importance of those subjects themselves: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and they run on their own timetable alongside the examined one.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an Internal Assessment without breaking IB honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can teach the subject content the investigation needs, question whether a research question is answerable in the word limit, test whether a variable is actually measurable, read one draft and comment against the published criteria. A tutor produces no part of an assessed submission and does not rewrite the student's text. At least one provider ranking for UAE IB searches sells finished Internal Assessments; submitting one is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the candidate. The boundary is explained to the student in the first session rather than assumed.

faqs.question: What time can lessons start if school finishes at half past two in Gulf Standard Time?
faqs.answer: Any slot from about 15:30 onwards, and the choice of slot should follow the task. The hour right after school is the best time to go through a returned paper, while the questions are still fresh, and the worst time to introduce new Higher Level content. Late afternoon suits teaching and worked examples. Early evening suits timed questions. Weekend mornings are the only slot where a complete past paper under examination conditions genuinely works. During Ramadan sessions shift later, often after Iftar, and deciding in advance which subject keeps its slot protects the month.

faqs.question: Is nine weeks before the first paper too late to start tuition?
faqs.answer: It is late, not too late, and the honest version is that the plan has to change shape. Nine weeks is enough to diagnose where marks are going with a timed paper, repair two or three high-yield topics, and spend the final fortnight on complete papers under examination conditions. It is not enough to cover a syllabus that was never learned. The first session should be a marked timed paper rather than a teaching hour, because the allocation of nine weeks depends entirely on whether marks are being lost to content gaps, to method presentation or to running out of time.

faqs.question: How are IGCSE science practicals handled when the tuition is online?
faqs.answer: By teaching the assessed skill, which is not the same as handling the apparatus. The centre chooses the route: a Paper 5 practical test, taken in the school laboratory, or a Paper 6 alternative to practical, which is a written paper. Paper 6 assesses reading scales, spotting anomalous results, plotting and interpreting graphs, and describing a method precisely enough that someone else could repeat it. All of that is taught well over video with shared data and real past questions. For Paper 5 the laboratory work stays with the school and tuition covers technique, recording and analysis.

faqs.question: Does the tutor need a MoHRE permit to give private lessons in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. MoHRE's own service page is the application route, and the permit position is a fair question to ask any tutor before booking.

faqs.question: Which authority regulates my child's school in Ras Al Khaimah or Fujairah?
faqs.answer: Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates private education in that emirate and, like the Sharjah Private Education Authority, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Fujairah, along with Ajman and Umm Al Quwain, is supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Dubai sits with KHDA and Abu Dhabi and Al Ain with ADEK. Knowing which body holds the file matters because inspection reports, fee approvals and complaint routes all sit with the emirate authority rather than with the school, and because the school's own answer to a question may be checkable.

faqs.question: What happens if no tutor is free for our subject in the slot we need?
faqs.answer: You are told, with a realistic wait and the alternatives rather than an open enquiry that sits unanswered. The subjects where this happens are predictable: Further Pure Mathematics at IGCSE, Computer Science at Higher Level, and any subject needed at half past three on a weekday in a northern emirate. The options offered are a different slot, a different week, a broader subject specialist to close a content gap while a specialist is found, or a recommendation to look elsewhere. Where the wait is longer than the examination calendar allows, that last answer is the right one and it is given.

ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.closingHeading: Start from the date on the timetable
ib-igcse-tuition-near-me.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, take the arithmetic. Find the series or session your child is entered for, confirm it with the examinations officer or the Diploma coordinator, and count the real teaching weeks between tonight and the first paper. That number decides what tuition can still change and what it cannot. Then book a trial lesson, watch whether your child talks in it, and decide. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, matched by board and syllabus code, anywhere in the UAE. If nobody is free for the subject you need, you will be told that rather than left waiting.

ib-igcse-tutor.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are matched to a board, a syllabus code and a session. A family sitting Cambridge 0580 Extended in June needs a different plan from one sitting Pearson 4MA1 Higher in November, and a Diploma student working on an Internal Assessment needs a third. Tell us the dates and we will match on those.

intro.heading: Two exam calendars, one household
paragraphs: Most searches for an IB IGCSE tutor in the UAE come from a family managing two assessment systems at once. The younger child is in Year 10 or Year 11, entered by the school for Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE papers in a series that was decided months ago. The older one is in the Diploma Programme, where the dates that matter are not exam dates at all but internal submission dates the school sets for Internal Assessments, the Extended Essay and the Theory of Knowledge essay. The two calendars do not line up, and they collide in the same February week.

That collision is the practical problem this page is built around. An IGCSE entry deadline falls before the winter break. A Diploma IA first draft is usually due within a few weeks of the mocks. The UAE school year then puts a Ramadan term and the Eid break between the mocks and the papers, which shortens the revision block everybody assumed they had. Families who plan from the exam date forwards run out of weeks. Families who count backwards from the entry deadline, the coursework date and the first paper almost never do.

The dates themselves are not guesswork for the IGCSE side. Cambridge International publishes a June series and a November series for its UAE centres, and every centre is placed in one of six administrative zones with its own timetable version. Pearson publishes May/June and November series and releases provisional timetables ahead of each one. Those documents are public, dated and specific, which is why the IGCSE calendar is the better spine for a two-board plan than the Diploma calendar, whose exam window should always be confirmed with the school's IB coordinator rather than taken from a tutoring page.

What a tutor adds to a fixed calendar is sequence. There is an order in which topics should be revised for Cambridge 0625 Physics that is different from the order for Pearson 4PH1, because one syllabus assesses practical skills through a separate paper and the other does not. There is a point in Year 10 at which the Core or Extended tier decision becomes expensive to reverse. There is a window in DP1 after which an Internal Assessment topic cannot sensibly be changed. A tutor working from the calendar instead of a generic scheme of work puts the right fortnight against the right component.

Everything here is delivered as one-to-one tuition over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to addresses in the UAE; home visits are part of what we offer in India only. For a family in Dubai, Abu Dhabi or Sharjah the practical effect is that the tutor is chosen for the syllabus code rather than for the postcode, and the session can be set for 7pm after a late school run or shifted to a post-Iftar slot in Ramadan without anyone losing forty minutes to Sheikh Zayed Road.
bullets: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series in the UAE; your exams officer confirms which one your child is entered for and which of the six zone timetables applies
Pearson's November 2026 series shows the pattern clearly: the final timetable ran to 19 November 2026 and the entry list had closed months before that
Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran to 19 November 2026; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026
British-track MoE equivalency asks for five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, and Arabic and Islamic Education are not counted among the five
KHDA's mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons sit in the same week as exam revision and are timetabled in 40-minute units
Lessons are live online, one-to-one, in Gulf Standard Time; the trial is one lesson in one subject with no payment details taken

ib-igcse-tutor.programmesIntro: Four programmes cover almost every UAE family who searches this phrase. The IGCSE years are where the entry deadlines and tiering decisions live. The Diploma is where the coursework dates live. MYP and PYP are where the groundwork for both is either laid or missed, and where the cheapest intervention of the whole school career sits.

programmes.name: Cambridge Upper Secondary and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Two years, typically eight to ten subjects, assessed almost entirely by terminal papers. Cambridge syllabuses carry four-digit codes such as 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology. Pearson uses codes such as 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1. The board decides the paper structure, the tiering and whether a practical component is assessed separately, so the syllabus code matters more than the subject name.
programmes.countryNote: UK curriculum schools are the largest group in Dubai's private sector, accounting for 37 per cent of private-school enrolment in 2024-25 according to Dubai Media Office. That makes IGCSE the most commonly sat qualification in the emirate. Your child's school chooses the board and the series, and the exams officer submits the entry; neither is something a family or a tutor controls, which is why both belong at the top of a tuition plan rather than the bottom.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects across three Higher Level and three Standard Level choices, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment marked against named criteria with published mark allocations. The written papers happen once; the coursework happens continuously across two years, which is why Diploma families feel permanently behind even when the exams are far away.
programmes.countryNote: International Baccalaureate students were 7 per cent of Dubai's private-school enrolment in 2024-25, and Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds three new IB schools among seven new private schools, creating 16,846 new places. Your school's IB coordinator sets the internal deadlines for IA, EE and TOK drafts, and those are the dates a tutoring plan should be built against. Confirm the exam window itself with the coordinator or on ibo.org rather than relying on any third-party page.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four criteria per subject, each scored one to eight, with a Personal Project in the final year. MYP marks are criterion-referenced rather than percentage-based, which is the single thing parents most often misread on a report. A criterion C score of four is not fifty per cent of anything; it describes a level of performance against a published descriptor.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools run MYP to Year 11 and then move students into the Diploma, while others switch students to IGCSE for Years 10 and 11. The two routes produce very different starting points for DP1, and families in a continuum school often do not realise which one their child is on until options evening. Ask the school whether Year 10 and 11 will be MYP or IGCSE, because the answer changes what a tutor should be working on in Year 9.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led units with no external examinations. Support at this stage is about fluency rather than exam technique: number bonds, written methods, reading stamina and the habit of explaining a method out loud. Gaps left here surface as speed problems in IGCSE Mathematics five years later, when there is no longer time to fix them.
programmes.countryNote: Primary families in the UAE rarely search for tutoring against a deadline, which makes this the one stage where a plan can be built around the child rather than the calendar. KHDA's mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education requirements begin in primary too, and a child who falls behind in Arabic as an additional language in Year 4 carries that gap into secondary, where it competes with IGCSE revision for the same evenings.

ib-igcse-tutor.subjectsIntro: Diploma subjects first. Each line names what the assessment actually rewards and where marks leak, because that is what a session plan is built from. Internal Assessment work is always feedback on your child's own drafts against the published criteria, never material produced for them.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Rewards algebraic fluency and proof. Most lost marks are not conceptual: they are unjustified lines of working, a missing domain restriction, or a calculator answer given without the exact form the question asked for. HL Paper 3 is a two-question extended investigation and needs practising as a format, not just as content.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Rewards modelling and interpretation in context. Marks go missing in the sentence after the calculation, where a student states a number but never says what it means for the situation. Statistical tests are commonly performed correctly and then concluded wrongly. The IA is where AI students gain most ground.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Rewards definitions stated precisely and graphs read carefully. The repeated failure is the extended-response question where a student describes rather than explains. Uncertainty treatment in the IA is the single most common criterion D weakness, and it is fixable in two sessions if caught early.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics carry the heaviest tutoring demand. Students lose marks by giving mechanisms without curly arrows placed correctly and by rounding too early in multi-step calculations. Data-based questions reward reading the axes before reading the question.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A content-heavy course where the marks are won on command terms. 'Outline' and 'explain' expect different lengths, and students routinely write an essay for two marks and a sentence for six. Statistical reasoning in the IA is weaker than students expect because it is rarely taught twice.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams are the scoring engine. A correctly labelled diagram with axes, curves and a shifted equilibrium earns marks that prose cannot recover. Evaluation is the other half: a conclusion that weighs two sides against a named criterion scores, a summary does not.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Rewards application to the stimulus rather than textbook recall. Students who define a tool and stop lose the application and evaluation marks. The HL extended response needs a structure practised in advance, because there is no time to invent one in the exam.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Paper 1 is an unseen guided analysis, which is a technique rather than a body of knowledge. Most improvement comes from teaching students to build a line of argument about effect, not to list devices. The Individual Oral needs a global issue chosen early and defensibly.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode and tracing are examinable skills and are usually under-practised. Students who can code fluently still lose marks on paper when asked to trace an algorithm by hand. The solution must be documented against the criteria, which is a separate skill from building it.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge, Extended Essay and Internal Assessment supervision
subjects.description: Process coaching only: question formulation, scope, structure, criterion-by-criterion feedback on the student's own drafts, and referencing discipline. A tutor explains what criterion A asks for and reads what the student has written against it. The words on the page stay the student's own.

ib-igcse-tutor.igcseSubjectsIntro: The IGCSE grid is organised by syllabus code, because the code determines the paper structure. Confirm which code your child's school has entered them for before a plan is built; two children in the same year group at the same school can sit different boards for different subjects.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: Tiered, so the first question is which tier the school has entered. Extended and Higher papers reach topics the Core and Foundation papers never touch. Lost marks cluster in multi-step problems where a correct method is abandoned halfway and in questions that ask for an exact answer in surd or fraction form.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Cambridge assesses practical skills through a separate paper: either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical written paper. Pearson 4PH1 does not. That difference changes what revision looks like entirely, and it is the reason a Physics plan cannot be written before the board is known.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Qualitative analysis, ionic equations and mole calculations carry most of the demand. Students lose marks writing word equations where symbol equations were asked for, and forgetting state symbols. The alternative-to-practical paper rewards knowing apparatus by name and reading a results table critically.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: The largest recall load of the three sciences, which makes it the subject where spaced retrieval practice pays most. Marks go missing on command terms and on diagrams drawn without labels. Transport in plants and human physiology are the two topics most often re-taught in tuition.

igcseSubjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511 / Pearson 4ES1)
igcseSubjects.description: A skills qualification where technique moves grades faster than vocabulary. The summary-writing task has a strict structure and a word limit; students who write well and ignore the limit lose marks they never see. Listening needs practising under timed conditions with the audio played once.

igcseSubjects.name: English First Language (Cambridge 0500 / 0990)
igcseSubjects.description: Directed writing and the extended response are both assessed against reading and writing criteria at once. The commonest weakness is a response that retells the passage instead of analysing it. Timed practice with criterion-referenced feedback is the whole intervention here.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455 / 0450)
igcseSubjects.description: Definition, application, analysis and evaluation are separable mark pools, and students who answer in paragraphs rather than in that sequence lose the top band. Data-response questions reward quoting a figure from the extract. Diagram accuracy matters as much as it does at Diploma level.

igcseSubjects.name: Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies
igcseSubjects.description: Required alongside the licensed international curriculum in Dubai private schools, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students and the language of instruction set by KHDA. Tuition follows the school's own scheme of work; the mandatory subject content itself cannot be varied without prior MoE permission.

ib-igcse-tutor.regionsTitle: Where your child sits the papers, and who regulates the school
ib-igcse-tutor.regionsIntro: The exam board sets the timetable, but the regulator sets the school's licensing, curriculum approval and inspection, and that differs by emirate. Three of these emirates are mentioned by none of the pages currently ranking for this search, which tells you how much of the UAE the existing advice quietly ignores.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25 across 17 curricula. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees will not rise for 2026-27.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which is worth knowing before accepting an offer from a class teacher.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a smaller IB and IGCSE cohort and fewer subject specialists physically present in the city. This is where online delivery changes the options most sharply: a Chemistry HL or 0620 Extended specialist does not need to live within driving distance of the school to teach the Thursday evening session.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Curriculum approval sitting with the emirate regulator, not only inspection, is a distinction most tutoring pages never make.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and likewise approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. RAK families sitting Cambridge papers are in the same zone-allocated timetable system as everyone else, so the entry deadline is identical to Dubai's even though the school choice is narrower.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools here. Fewer IB schools means more families on the IGCSE route, and more students who will need the British-track equivalency file for a UAE university. That makes the five-subject rule a live planning question in Year 10, not an afterthought in Year 13.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Also supervised by the Ministry of Education. Returns zero mentions across the competitor pages researched for this cluster, which is a reasonable proxy for how much local tutoring supply exists. Live online sessions remove the geography problem without removing the board-specific preparation.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Ministry of Education supervised, and the smallest private-school market of the seven. Families here often commute to schools in Sharjah or Ras Al Khaimah, which shortens the usable evening further and makes a 7.30pm or 8pm online slot the realistic one rather than a late-afternoon session.

schoolClusters.note: The largest concentration of both IGCSE and Diploma cohorts in the country, and the one place where a family can realistically choose between boards. Students we support attend schools across these groups; the entry deadline and timetable zone are set by each school's exams officer, not by the emirate.

A smaller IB cohort spread over a wider area, with school runs long enough that a 4pm session is rarely practical. Evening online slots and weekend blocks do the work here. ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation for all of these schools.

Regulated by SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and the Ministry of Education in Ajman, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain. The subject-specialist shortage is real here, and it is the reason online matching changes the shortlist rather than just the commute.

ib-igcse-tutor.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named as ecosystem context for families recognising their own cohort; no affiliation, endorsement or partnership with any school or school group is implied or held.
ib-igcse-tutor.modesIntro: Four ways families use these lessons, chosen by where they are in the calendar rather than by preference. A Year 10 family in October wants something different from a DP2 family in February, and the same tutor should not deliver both the same way.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, term-time
modes.description: One or two sessions a week against the school's own scheme of work, with the week's topic set by what is being taught rather than by a fixed syllabus order. This is the mode that works from Year 9 to DP1 and it is the cheapest per unit of improvement, because nothing has to be re-taught under time pressure.
bullets: Session topic set from the school's weekly plan, not a generic sequence
Short retrieval check at the start of every session on the previous topic
Written note to the parent after each session naming what was covered and what was weak
Homework set is the school's own, reviewed rather than replaced

modes.title: Exam-term intensive block
modes.description: A fixed number of sessions booked across the weeks between mocks and the first paper, built from the mock paper itself. The block is counted in hours and planned on a calendar, so a family can see before booking whether the plan fits inside the weeks that actually remain once Ramadan and the Eid break are accounted for.
bullets: Built from the mock script, topic by topic, by marks lost
Timed paper practice under exam conditions with criterion-referenced feedback
Two or three sessions a week in the final six weeks if the gap justifies it
A named stop date, so the last week before a paper is left for rest and recall

modes.description: Where one child is on IGCSE and another on the Diploma, both calendars go into a single plan so the February pinch point is visible in October. Sessions for the two children are deliberately placed on different evenings, and the intensive blocks are staggered rather than stacked, which keeps one household from running two exam terms simultaneously.

sections.heading: What a family searching for an IB IGCSE tutor is actually managing
paragraphs: The search phrase joins two qualifications because the household contains both. An IB IGCSE tutor in the UAE is, in practice, a tutor who can work inside a Cambridge or Pearson syllabus for one child and inside an IB subject guide for another, and who understands that the two systems put their pressure in different places. IGCSE pressure is terminal and external: almost everything rides on papers sat in a published window. Diploma pressure is distributed and internal: coursework deadlines set by the school, spread across two years, each one quietly non-negotiable.

That difference changes what help looks like. An IGCSE student who is behind in January can still be rescued by a well-sequenced revision block, because the assessment has not happened yet. A Diploma student who misses an Internal Assessment draft deadline in January has lost something that cannot be recovered in the same way, because the school's internal timetable has moved on and the mark will be submitted from whatever exists. Families who treat both children the same way tend to over-invest in the one who has time and under-invest in the one who does not.

The honest framing is that there is no single right amount of tutoring. There is a calendar, a set of gaps, and a number of usable evenings between now and each date. Once those three things are written down, the number of sessions stops being a judgement call and becomes arithmetic. The rest of this page does that arithmetic for the IGCSE side, where the dates are published and verifiable, and then hangs the Diploma coursework calendar off it.

sections.heading: Four series a year, and the one your child is actually entered for
paragraphs: Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series; the February/March series is run for India only and is not open to a UAE candidate. Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests sit in March, May and October, and those are Primary and Lower Secondary only, not IGCSE. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year, and Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, sometimes for a November sitting that is two academic years out, which is why a tuition page should link the live official timetable rather than restate dates that can still be revised.

The practical consequence is that your child's deadline is not a national one. It is a series, chosen by the school, with its own entry date and its own timetable version. Pearson's November 2026 series is the clearest illustration of how early the real deadline falls, because that series has a published window: the final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, while the entry list fixing every subject, tier and option had gone in months earlier. Results then reach students the following January, the way Pearson's November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. Three terms separate the decision from the certificate.

Ask the school's exams officer three questions before booking any tuition: which series, which board for each subject, and which timetable version applies. The third question matters because every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone. Cambridge also states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. That is not a risk a family should be carrying unknowingly in May.

sections.heading: The entry deadline, not the exam date, is what actually bites
paragraphs: Parents plan backwards from the first paper. Schools plan backwards from the entry deadline, which arrives months earlier and locks in decisions that most families did not realise were being made. Tier, board, subject count and in some cases the practical option are all fixed at entry. After that date, changing any of them means a late entry if the board permits one, a withdrawal, or sitting the subject in a later series. None of those options is free, and two of them cost a year.

The June series makes the gap concrete when you count it backwards. Papers are sat in May and June; revision blocks start around March; before that the centre submits forecast grades; and before that again, in the spring, the entry list closes and the tier on each subject is fixed. A family who decides in March that their child should move from Core to Extended Mathematics is usually arguing with a list that has already gone in. Each of those is a different kind of date with a different owner, and treating them as one blurred deadline is how families get caught. The exact days are not national: they sit on the statement of entry your centre issues.

The useful move is a single sheet with four columns: the milestone, who owns it, how far ahead of the paper it falls, and what should already be true by then. Write it in October. A tutor working from that sheet can tell you in week one whether the tier is right, whether the practical option has been chosen sensibly, and whether the forecast grade the school is about to submit reflects what the student can currently do. Those three conversations are worth more than ten extra revision sessions in April.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: a tiering decision with a date attached
paragraphs: Several Cambridge IGCSE subjects are tiered. Mathematics 0580 is the one families meet first, and Physics 0625, Chemistry 0620 and Biology 0610 offer Core and Extended routes too. Pearson's equivalent in Mathematics A, 4MA1, is tiered Foundation and Higher. The tier determines which papers are sat, which syllabus content is examinable and what the attainable grade range is. Confirm the current grade range for your child's subject in the syllabus document on cambridgeinternational.org, because it is set per syllabus and per cycle.

The decision is usually made in Year 10 on the basis of a single internal assessment, and it is the highest-leverage decision in the two years. Entering a capable student at Core protects the school's results and caps the child's ceiling. Entering a struggling student at Extended exposes them to content they will not cover and produces a grade below what the Core papers would have given. Neither error is visible until results day, and by then the window to change it has been closed since the entry deadline.

A tutor is useful here in a specific and unglamorous way: by producing evidence. One full paper at each tier under timed conditions, marked against the board's mark scheme, tells you more than a term of classwork. If the Extended paper produces a clear pass with recognisable method errors, the tier is right and the work is technique. If it produces scattered part-marks and blank extended-response questions, the honest answer is that Core protects the grade. That conversation belongs in October of Year 10, not in February of Year 11.

sections.heading: Cambridge against Pearson Edexcel for the same subject
paragraphs: Two children at the same UAE school can sit different boards for different subjects, because the school chooses per department. The subject name on a report tells you nothing useful; the syllabus code does. A Physics plan built for Cambridge 0625 and then applied to Pearson 4PH1 wastes weeks, because one of those qualifications assesses practical skills through a dedicated paper and the other does not. Research across the pages currently ranking for these queries found exactly one syllabus code mentioned in an entire seven-page cluster, which is how little attention this gets.

The clearest structural difference sits in the sciences. Cambridge science syllabuses offer a practical route: either a practical test or the alternative-to-practical written paper, which examines apparatus, method and results interpretation on paper. Pearson's International GCSE sciences assess through written papers without that separate practical component. For a student tutored online, that distinction is the difference between drilling apparatus diagrams and results tables, and not needing to at all.

The second difference is series flexibility. Pearson runs two series a year, which means a candidate can in principle sit one subject in November and another in the following May/June. Whether a particular subject can be split across series is set by its specification, so check the specification for the exact subject rather than assuming. Cambridge candidates in the UAE have June and November, and nothing else: the February/March series belongs to India. In both cases the board, not the school's preference, sets what is possible.
