sections.heading: Thirty weeks counted backwards from the first IGCSE paper
paragraphs: A thirty-week plan sounds generous until the UAE school calendar is laid over it. Between a January mock and a June paper there is a Ramadan term, the Eid break, end-of-year school assessments that are not the real exams, and in many schools a study-leave period that starts later than families expect. The usable weeks are fewer than the calendar weeks, and the gap is typically four to six weeks. A plan that does not subtract them is a plan that runs out of time in the last fortnight.

Counted backwards, the structure is reasonably stable across subjects. The last fortnight is recall and timed papers only, with no new content. The six weeks before that are full-paper practice under timed conditions, marked and fed back. The twelve weeks before that are topic repair, sequenced by marks lost in the mock rather than by syllabus order. Everything earlier than that is content coverage and the tiering evidence described above. Working forwards from today produces a different and usually worse order.

Write the plan on a calendar with the Ramadan term and the Eid break marked, then count the evenings that remain. Most families discover they have between twenty and twenty-six usable sessions, which is enough to repair two subjects properly or four subjects partially. Choosing which is the real decision, and it is better made in October with information than in April under pressure. A tutor who will not have that conversation before taking a booking is not planning, only selling hours.

sections.heading: The summer when Year 11 ends and DP1 begins
paragraphs: The jump from IGCSE to the Diploma is the least-planned transition in UAE international education, and it is almost entirely predictable. IGCSE rewards accurate recall and clean method on short structured questions. The Diploma rewards sustained argument, modelling in context and independent investigation. A student who scored well at IGCSE by being neat and quick can arrive in DP1 and find that neatness and speed are no longer the things being measured.

The gaps are subject-specific and closeable. Mathematics AA expects algebraic fluency beyond anything the Extended paper demanded, plus proof as a technique. Physics and Chemistry expect uncertainty treatment and data analysis that IGCSE only touched. Every Diploma subject expects an Internal Assessment, which is an independent investigation with a published criterion structure that no IGCSE prepared anyone for. The transition work that matters is not more content; it is the three or four skills the new course assumes a student already has.

Six to ten weeks of light, well-targeted work across a summer closes most of it, and it is the cheapest intervention available at this stage because nothing is urgent yet. Schools that run MYP rather than IGCSE in Years 10 and 11 produce a different starting profile again: stronger on investigation and criterion-referenced work, often weaker on timed accuracy. Ask the school which route your child is on before deciding what the summer is for. The other thing worth settling before DP1 starts is the Mathematics route, because Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation lead to different university prerequisites, and a student who picks on the basis of which teacher they liked in Year 11 can find the choice closing a door two years later.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects sharing the same week as revision
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year starts in April. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. This is why the mandatory subjects appear alongside IGCSE and Diploma courses in every UAE timetable.

They also consume real hours in the exam term, which is the part no tutoring page accounts for. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson should be at least 25 minutes. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

Two things follow for a tuition plan. First, the week your child has is shorter than the subject list suggests, so a plan that assumes four free evenings in February is usually wrong. Second, support for these subjects follows the school's own scheme of work: for the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the MoE is strictly prohibited. KHDA also requires that schools ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects.

sections.heading: Equivalency: five subjects, not six, and the file you open in Year 11
paragraphs: If a UAE university is a possible destination, the Ministry of Education equivalency rules belong in the Year 11 plan rather than the Year 13 panic. For the British track, students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects.

That last clause is the one most often got wrong. A ranking competitor page currently tells UAE parents that candidates must take six IGCSE subjects. The sourced rule is five, excluding Arabic and Islamic Education from the count. Getting this right changes a subject-choice conversation in Year 10, because a student taking exactly six subjects including Arabic has a thinner margin than their parents believe. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority before acting on it, and treat any third-party restatement, including this one, as a prompt to check.

For the American track the sourced requirements are different: English proficiency through a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and at least 450 in the SAT Mathematics test before applying. No IB points threshold appears in the source we read, so no IB equivalency figure is published here. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation; the process belongs to the Ministry and the attestation authority, and tutoring is not a requirement of it.

sections.heading: What the market charges, and why February costs more than September
paragraphs: Three of the six pages that currently rank for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. The figures below are market ranges in AED, taken from published provider rate cards and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, read in October 2026. They describe what the UAE market charges across provider models. They are not an IB Gram price list, and no figure here should be read as our quote.

The pattern in the data is that format drives price more than qualification does. An in-home visit carries the travel inside the hourly rate, which is why the same tutor is more expensive at your kitchen table than on a video call. Exam proximity drives it next: a specialist with four free evenings in September has one by February, and scarcity does what scarcity does. A family who books the same block in October rather than February is usually buying it at the lower end of the same band.

Context helps too. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. School fees are flat; tutoring demand is not, because the 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools and 16,846 places. Plan the tuition budget on the calendar rather than on the assumption that rates hold steady through the exam term.

sections.heading: Live online against a visiting tutor when the dates are already fixed
paragraphs: This is the comparison most families actually want, and it deserves a straight answer rather than a sales line. A visiting tutor has genuine advantages: a younger child concentrates better with an adult physically present, and no equipment can fail. The cost of those advantages is travel inside the hourly rate, a tutor pool limited to people who live within driving distance, and a session time hostage to traffic. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, where distances are longer, that last constraint bites hardest.

IB Gram delivers UAE tuition as one-to-one lessons over live video. Nobody is sent to a UAE address; home visits are part of what we offer in India only. The case for the online format is not that it is cheaper, though the market data suggests it usually is. The case is selection: a family in Al Ain can work with a Cambridge 0620 Extended specialist or a Mathematics AA Higher Level specialist regardless of where that tutor lives, instead of choosing from whoever happens to be free within a twenty-minute drive.

The format also fits the calendar better, which matters on a page built around dates. A video session can be moved to a post-Iftar slot during Ramadan, run at 8pm after a long school run, held during a family trip abroad, or compressed into three evenings in a revision week without anyone absorbing travel time. During the exam period itself, a thirty-minute check between papers is practical online and almost never practical with a visiting tutor.

sections.heading: Academic honesty when the coursework deadline is on Friday
paragraphs: The pressure point on a two-board calendar is a Diploma coursework deadline landing in the same fortnight as IGCSE paper practice, and that is exactly when the market's worst offers start to look reasonable. One operation found in the research for this cluster sells finished Internal Assessments. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules, with consequences that fall on the student rather than the seller, and it can end a Diploma candidacy. No deadline is worth that exposure.

The boundary is not vague. A tutor may explain what a criterion asks for, interrogate a research question before the writing starts, teach a structure, read a draft and say which criterion is losing marks and why, show a worked example on a different topic, and teach referencing as the assessed skill it is. A tutor may not supply text that ends up in the submission, rewrite passages into their own prose, or produce assessed material on a student's behalf. IB Gram's position is the second list, stated plainly, because the pages competing for this search mostly leave it unsaid.

The practical defence is calendar discipline rather than willpower. Internal Assessments and Extended Essays go wrong when the research question is still unsettled three weeks before submission, and they go right when the question was pinned down early and the drafting had somewhere to go. Book the review sessions around the school's own draft dates, not around the final deadline. On the IGCSE side there is no coursework to protect in most subjects, which is precisely why the Diploma child's dates should be the ones anchoring the household plan.

process.title: Send the dates, not just the subject
process.description: Tell us the series, the board and tier for each subject, and the school's internal draft dates for any Diploma coursework. Those four facts decide the plan. If the exams officer has not confirmed the timetable zone, ask for it in the same email; it takes one reply and removes a real risk.

process.title: A free trial lesson in the subject that worries you most
process.description: One lesson, one subject, with no payment details taken and no obligation to continue. It is a diagnostic rather than a demonstration: the tutor works through a real question at the entered tier and reports what the gap actually is. Families often find the problem is in a different subject from the one they booked.

process.title: A plan counted backwards from each date
process.description: You get a calendar, not a package. Ramadan term, the Eid break and school study leave are marked, the usable evenings counted, and the session total derived from that rather than proposed in advance. If the arithmetic says two subjects can be repaired properly and four cannot, the plan says so.

process.title: Weekly sessions against the school's own scheme of work
process.description: Lessons follow what the school is teaching rather than a generic syllabus order, with a short retrieval check on the previous topic at the start of each session. A written note after every lesson names what was covered and what remained weak, so the plan can be corrected in week three rather than week twelve.

process.title: Review at the mock result, and again at results day
process.description: The mock script is the best planning document of the year, and it is read by marks lost rather than by grade. The plan is rebuilt from it. After results, the review covers whether a grade looks inconsistent with the evidence, what the enquiry route is, and whether a later series is worth entering.

whyPoints.title: Matched to a syllabus code, not a subject name
whyPoints.description: Cambridge 0625 and Pearson 4PH1 are different qualifications wearing the same subject name, and one includes a practical component the other does not. Matching on the code is why a plan holds up in week six instead of needing rewriting. We ask for the code before matching, which most providers never do.

whyPoints.title: Both calendars in one plan
whyPoints.description: Households with an IGCSE child and a Diploma child get a single timeline with both sets of dates on it, sessions deliberately placed on different evenings, and intensive blocks staggered rather than stacked. One consultation covers both children. The February pinch point becomes visible in October, which is when it can still be moved.

whyPoints.title: Dates and figures carry their source
whyPoints.description: Every exam date on this page is attributed to Cambridge or Pearson, every AED figure to the market source it came from, and every regulatory statement to u.ae, KHDA or the report that published it. Where a figure is unverified, including IB session dates and any IB equivalency threshold, we say so and do not publish a number.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Feedback on the student's own drafts against the published criteria, and nothing beyond that. No supplied text, no rewriting into our prose, no production of assessed material. This is written down because the alternative is sold openly in this market and the consequences of buying it fall on the student, not the seller.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling that survives Ramadan and a long school run
whyPoints.description: Lessons are live online, in Gulf Standard Time, so a session can move to a post-Iftar slot, start at 8pm after a late pickup, or continue through a family trip without losing a week. During the exam period a short check between papers is practical. No travel time is paid for, by anyone.

whyPoints.title: Honest about coverage, before you book
whyPoints.description: If no specialist is free for a Higher Level subject in the week you need to start, we say so and give the realistic date rather than matching whoever is available. Where a UAE-based tutor does not cover a niche subject, the specialist may be based elsewhere and the sessions still run live online in your time zone.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE exam series are there in a year, and which one will my child sit?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series for IGCSE, O Level and International A Level at its UAE centres. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. Which series your child sits is decided by the school, not the family, and it is fixed when the exams officer submits the entry. Ask the school three questions: which series, which board for each subject, and which timetable version applies. The third matters because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version.

faqs.question: What do Core and Extended mean, and when does that choice have to be locked in?
faqs.answer: Several Cambridge IGCSE subjects are tiered. Core covers the core syllabus content; Extended adds supplementary content that is examinable and opens the upper grades, with the exact range set in each syllabus document. Pearson's Mathematics A, 4MA1, is tiered Foundation and Higher instead. The choice is fixed at the final entry deadline, which falls months before the first paper and is held by your centre rather than published as one national date. After it passes, changing tier means a late entry if the board allows one, a withdrawal, or waiting for the next series, which in the UAE means June or November and nothing in between. Decide in Year 10, on the evidence of a timed full paper at each tier.

faqs.question: Are Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE the same qualification?
faqs.answer: No. They are separate qualifications from separate boards with separate specifications, and the subject name on a school report tells you very little. The clearest structural difference is in the sciences: Cambridge syllabuses such as 0625 Physics and 0620 Chemistry include a practical route, either a practical test or an alternative-to-practical written paper, while Pearson's 4PH1 and 4CH1 assess through written papers without that separate component. Tiering differs too. A revision plan built for one specification and applied to the other wastes weeks, so confirm the four-digit or alphanumeric code on your child's entry before any tuition plan is written.

faqs.question: Can my child take different subjects with different exam boards?
faqs.answer: Yes, and in UAE schools it is common, because the board is usually chosen per department rather than per school. One child can sit Cambridge 0580 Mathematics and Pearson 4BI1 Biology in the same series. The practical consequence is that there is no single revision approach for the whole timetable: each subject needs practice against its own specification, mark scheme and paper structure. Get the full list of codes from the exams officer in one request rather than subject by subject. It also means two children in the same year group at the same school can genuinely be preparing differently for a subject with the same name.

faqs.question: How do we find out which syllabus code each of my child's subjects is entered for?
faqs.answer: Ask the school's exams officer for the entry list, in one request covering every subject. What comes back is a set of codes rather than subject names: Cambridge syllabuses such as 0580, 0625, 0620 or 0610, or Pearson codes such as 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1 or 4BI1, each with the tier where the subject is tiered. That list is what a tuition plan should be written from. The codes also tell you whether a practical component applies, since Cambridge science syllabuses include a practical route and Pearson's International GCSE sciences assess through written papers without that separate component.

faqs.question: Are Arabic and Islamic Education counted among the five subjects the Ministry of Education asks for?
faqs.answer: No. For the British track, the sourced requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five. One page currently ranking for these searches tells UAE parents the requirement is six subjects, which does not match the rule as reported. That exclusion changes subject choices in Year 10: a student taking six subjects including Arabic has a thinner margin than the family assumes. Verify the current requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority before acting, and treat any third-party restatement as a prompt to check.

faqs.question: What is a forecast grade, and who decides it?
faqs.answer: A forecast grade is the school's own prediction of the grade a candidate will achieve, submitted to the board as part of the series administration. It is submitted on a schedule the board sets for each series, well before results and usually around the time revision blocks begin. The school sets it, not the family and not a tutor. What a tutor can do is make sure the forecast rests on recent evidence: a full paper sat under timed conditions and marked against the board's mark scheme, rather than classwork impressions. If the forecast looks out of step with that evidence, that is a conversation to have with the school before it is submitted.

faqs.question: My child's school will not enter one subject. Can they sit it as a private candidate?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, through a registered examination centre that accepts private candidates, and the UAE has several. Two practical points matter. First, private-candidate entry deadlines are administered by the centre and can fall earlier than a school's internal process, so start the enquiry a term before the series rather than a month. Second, subjects with a practical component need arrangements the centre must be able to provide, so confirm that before committing. Fees and availability are set by the centre, not by us. Tuition can prepare the subject, but the entry itself has to be arranged with the centre directly.

faqs.question: Is IGCSE tutoring more useful in Year 10 or Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10 work is cheaper and does more, because it still changes decisions. The tiering decision is made in Year 10, often on one internal assessment, and it sets the attainable grade range for two years. Evidence gathered early, through a timed full paper at each tier, makes that decision properly instead of by impression. Year 11 work is repair under a deadline: still worth doing, but it operates inside choices that have already been locked by the entry. If the question is where the same budget buys most, the answer is Year 10 for decisions and Year 11 for technique.

faqs.question: What should we ask the school's exams officer before booking any tuition?
faqs.answer: Four questions, and they take one email. Which series is each subject entered for. Which board and, where the subject is tiered, which tier. Which timetable version applies, since Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it is essential to use the correct version for your zone. And what the final entry deadline is for the series, because that date fixes tier, board and subject count. Cambridge also states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used, which is reason enough to ask.

faqs.question: How big is the jump from IGCSE to the IB Diploma, and when should we prepare for it?
faqs.answer: Larger than most families expect, and predictable. IGCSE rewards accurate recall and clean method on short structured questions. The Diploma rewards sustained argument, modelling in context and an independent Internal Assessment with published criteria that no IGCSE prepared anyone for. The specific gaps are subject-level: proof and exact-form answers in Mathematics AA, uncertainty treatment in Physics and Chemistry, analysis of effect rather than device-spotting in English. Six to ten weeks of light, targeted work across the summer between Year 11 and DP1 closes most of it, and it is the cheapest intervention available because nothing is urgent yet.

faqs.question: Can one tutor work with two children on different boards in the same family?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking rather than assuming. A tutor comfortable with Cambridge 0580 Extended and Mathematics AA Standard Level can reasonably cover both, because the content overlaps. A tutor covering 0620 Chemistry and Chemistry Higher Level is a narrower match and worth checking carefully, since the Higher Level course goes considerably further. Where one tutor does cover both children, scheduling gets easier and the household gets one point of contact. Where it does not, we say so rather than stretching a match, and the two children are placed separately with their session evenings deliberately kept apart.

faqs.question: Can my child sit an IGCSE in February or March in the UAE?
faqs.answer: No. Cambridge offers that series to India only, so a UAE centre cannot enter a candidate for it, and any page that quotes you a February exam window for a Dubai or Abu Dhabi school has copied Indian dates. What a UAE candidate has is June and November with Cambridge, and May/June and November with Pearson Edexcel. If June is not possible, November is the route, and it is a real one: Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026, with results reaching students the following January. Whichever of the two applies, the entry deadline sits months before the first paper and your exams officer holds it.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE tutor cost per hour in the UAE market?
faqs.answer: Market ranges in AED, from published provider rate cards and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table read in October 2026: roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for a budget online or university-student tutor, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for an in-home visit with travel inside the rate, AED 200 to 450 and above for an IB or IGCSE specialist, and AED 500 and above at the premium end. A monthly online package of eight sessions at AED 799 has been published in this market. Those are market figures, not an IB Gram price list; the first lesson with us is a trial with no payment details taken.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with an IGCSE coursework component without crossing the honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can explain what the assessment criteria ask for, help scope a title or investigation before the writing starts, teach a structure, read the student's own draft and say which criterion is losing marks and why, and teach referencing as an assessed skill. A tutor cannot supply text that ends up in the submission, rewrite passages into their own prose, or produce assessed material on a student's behalf. Finished coursework is sold in this market; buying it is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student rather than the seller. The words submitted have to be the student's own.

faqs.question: How do sessions fit around school hours, prayer times and Ramadan in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Because lessons are live online, the session moves rather than the family. Most UAE households settle on 6pm to 8.30pm Gulf Standard Time on weekday evenings, which clears the school run and, in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, a longer commute. During Ramadan, sessions commonly shift to a post-Iftar slot, and the usable revision block shortens, so an exam-term plan should subtract the Ramadan term and the Eid break before committing to a session count. Weekend blocks absorb the difference. A session can also be moved around a prayer time or a family trip without losing the week.

faqs.question: Where do lessons actually take place, and what equipment does my child need?
faqs.answer: Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, with a shared digital whiteboard, screen sharing for past-paper work and a written note to the parent afterwards. Nobody is sent to a UAE address: home visits are part of what IB Gram offers in India only. What your child needs is a laptop or tablet with a working microphone, a stable connection, and ideally a notebook and pen, because written working still matters in an exam. A quiet room helps more than any equipment. For science papers, having the current syllabus open alongside is useful, and we link the official board page rather than supplying copies.

ib-igcse-tutor.closingHeading: Start from the dates you already have
ib-igcse-tutor.closingBody: You do not need to decide how much tutoring to buy. You need four facts: the series each subject is entered for, the board and tier, the school's internal draft dates for any Diploma coursework, and the timetable zone. Send those and we will put both children's calendars on one timeline, mark the Ramadan term and the Eid break, and count the evenings that actually remain. The first lesson is a trial in the subject that worries you most, with no payment details taken and no obligation to continue. If nobody suitable is free in the week you need to start, we will tell you that instead of matching whoever is available.

intro.heading: Near me is a question about the calendar, not the map
paragraphs: A parent typing IB IGCSE tutor near me into Google on a Tuesday evening in October is almost never asking about distance. The question underneath it is whether somebody who knows the 0580 Extended paper, or Chemistry HL Paper 3, can start this week at a time that fits after the school run and before homework. Distance is a proxy for availability, and in the UAE it is a poor one. A family on Al Reem Island can be twenty minutes from a tutor who has never taught Pearson's modular International GCSE, and nine time zones from one who has taught it for a decade and happens to be free at 17:30 Gulf Standard Time.

Two things make this market different from the one the phrase was coined in. The first is that scarcity here runs by subject rather than by geography. Dubai's private schools taught 17 different curricula to 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum at 37% of enrolment, Indian at 26%, American at 14% and the IB at 7%, according to figures published by Dubai Media Office. A community with four schools in it can still have nobody within driving distance who teaches Economics HL. The second is that households here often run two exam calendars at once: an older child in the IB Diploma working towards the May session, and a younger one in Year 11 entered for a Cambridge or Pearson series.

So this page is organised the way a head of year organises a cohort: backwards from the exam window. Every section answers a when question. When do entries close, and who closes them. When does an Internal Assessment deadline actually bite, which is months before any paper is sat. When does the market tighten, so the specialist who was free in September is gone by February. When does a results-day decision expire. The Cambridge and Pearson dates below are taken from those boards' own published pages and attributed there, with the caveat the boards themselves attach: provisional timetables get revised, so the live official PDF is always the authority.

The delivery model is worth stating before anything else, because it is exactly what the phrase near me implies and it is the one thing we do not do. IB Gram teaches UAE students one-to-one tuition over live video. Home visits are part of what we offer in India and are not part of what we offer in any emirate. That is not a workaround dressed up as a feature. It is the reason a family in Fujairah can work with the same Physics HL specialist a family in Jumeirah works with, and the reason a 19:00 session after Maghrib is as easy to arrange as a 16:00 one.

What follows is long because the answers are specific. There are rate bands in AED attributed to the providers who publish them, a forty-week ladder counted back from exam week, the five-subject Ministry of Education equivalency rule with the two subjects that do not count towards it, the administrative mistake that ends a Cambridge series before the student has written a word, and the academic-honesty line a tutor may not cross on an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay. Sixteen questions at the end are the ones UAE parents actually ask about timing. If your child sits papers this academic year, read the ladder first.

ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: Four programmes sit under this one search, and each runs on a different clock. IGCSE has two or three sittings a year and a hard entry deadline months ahead of the paper. The Diploma has one session UAE schools use, plus coursework deadlines that land a year earlier. MYP and PYP carry no external papers at all, which changes what tutoring is for. Here is the timing reality of each.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson International GCSE
programmes.description: Two boards, overlapping content, different machinery. Cambridge splits most sciences and mathematics into Core and Extended, with 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry and 0610 Biology among the codes UAE centres enter most. Pearson runs linear and modular routes with Foundation and Higher tiers on codes such as 4MA1, 4PH1, 4CH1 and 4BI1. The tier decision is made months before the paper and caps the grade available, which is why it belongs at the top of any plan rather than in the revision term.
programmes.countryNote: UAE centres sit the June and November Cambridge series, and the May/June and November Pearson series. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable version differs by zone, so the exams officer at your child's school is the only reliable source for the actual paper dates. A November entry is the standard route for a June candidate who wants one subject again, and it keeps a Year 12 start intact.

programmes.name: IB Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, normally three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, each with an internally assessed component, plus the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and CAS. The IB Diploma May session is the one UAE schools use. The part families underestimate is that the coursework calendar runs a full year ahead of the papers: an Extended Essay research question is usually locked in DP1, and a science Internal Assessment is often drafted before the DP2 mock window opens.
programmes.countryNote: The IB accounted for 7% of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25, and KHDA has said Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. More Diploma places means more DP1 cohorts arriving from MYP and from IGCSE in the same September, which is the point in the year when Higher Level specialists get booked out first.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Criterion-referenced marking on a 1-8 scale against four published criteria per subject, with the Personal Project in the final year. There is no external paper for most students, so there is no entry deadline to count back from. What there is instead is a steady stream of assessed tasks, each tied to specific criteria, and a Personal Project with a process journal that schools weight heavily. Tutoring here is about reading the criteria accurately rather than past-paper drill.
programmes.countryNote: In UAE schools the MYP5 year doubles as a decision year: some students move into DP1, others transfer to an IGCSE or A-Level pathway at a different school, and a few sit IGCSE papers alongside MYP tasks. That decision has a deadline set by school admissions calendars rather than by any board, and it usually falls in the second term.

programmes.name: IB Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary inquiry with no external examinations, ending in the Exhibition in the final PYP year. The useful tutoring targets at this stage are narrow and measurable: reading fluency, number facts and written structure. Where a PYP student is heading into an MYP or IGCSE school, the gap that shows up later is almost always arithmetic fluency and the habit of writing to a prompt under a time limit, neither of which the Exhibition tests.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai private schools run Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the licensed curriculum from the early years, and KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a PYP family, that means the weekly timetable already carries subjects the home curriculum does not, which is worth knowing before adding anything else to a Tuesday evening.

ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: Each subject below is described by where the marks move and when in the year that happens. A Higher Level science is not uniformly hard; it is hard in three specific places, and those places have dates attached. Levels are listed as a UAE school would enter them.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most UAE engineering and economics applicants need. HL adds proof, complex numbers and the option content, and Paper 3 is a long investigative paper that rewards fluency with unfamiliar structure. Marks go missing in the move from a correct method to a fully justified one, and that habit takes months rather than weeks to build.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Technology-permitted throughout, with modelling, statistics and financial mathematics carrying the weight. The common failure is treating the graphing calculator as the answer rather than as the working. HL students lose marks on interpreting a regression or a confidence interval in context, which is a writing skill grafted onto a maths paper.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Energetics, equilibrium and organic mechanisms are where HL grades are decided, and the Internal Assessment is the component most often left too late. A mechanism answer either shows curly arrows with correct charges or it does not, so progress here is unusually measurable week to week once the gaps are named.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields, circuits and the HL option content separate grades. The recurring pattern in UAE cohorts is strong algebra paired with weak diagram reasoning: a student can rearrange the equation but cannot say which way the force points. Data-analysis questions reward uncertainty handling that is almost never practised in school time.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem rather than difficulty. Students who revise by rereading notes stall around the middle grades; students who revise by answering command terms move. Structured questions punish vague language, so vocabulary precision on processes such as osmoregulation or translation is the fastest available gain.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy plus evaluation. Most lost marks sit in the evaluation sentences, not the theory, and in the Internal Assessment commentaries where students summarise an article instead of applying a model to it. HL adds quantitative content that is straightforward once the terminology stops shifting.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool-led. Students who can produce a correct break-even or working-capital calculation under time pressure, then say what it means for the business in the stimulus, score well. The frequent error is answering about businesses in general rather than about the one in front of them.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The Individual Oral and the Paper 1 unseen analysis carry the stress. Both improve through rehearsal against a mark scheme rather than through reading more. For UAE students writing in English as an additional language, sentence-level control is usually the ceiling, and it lifts with targeted drafting.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode under exam conditions behaves differently from code in an editor. HL adds abstract data structures and the case study, which requires reading far beyond the syllabus text. The internally assessed solution needs a scoped problem agreed early, because an ambitious one eats the DP2 autumn term.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case-study recall with precise figures and places, plus the HL core extension. Students lose marks writing generically about urbanisation when the question wanted a named place and a number. Building a compact, accurate case-study bank is a term-long job best started before the mock window.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Chosen by many UAE students who have studied Arabic as an additional language at school. The productive skills carry the grade, and the gap between classroom Arabic and the register the papers expect is wide. Regular short speaking practice beats long infrequent sessions here more clearly than in any other subject.

ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.igcseSubjectsIntro: IGCSE sits on the other side of the household, often in the same week. The codes below are the ones UAE centres enter most, with the Cambridge code first and the Pearson equivalent after it where one exists. Confirm the code on the entry form before booking anything, because the papers differ even where the content overlaps.

igcseSubjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
igcseSubjects.levels: Core and Extended / Foundation and Higher
igcseSubjects.description: The tier decision caps the grade, so it is a planning question rather than a revision one. Extended and Higher candidates lose most marks on multi-step problems where the first line is wrong, and on the non-calculator fluency that underpins everything else. Both are trainable in a term if started before the mock window.

igcseSubjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Electricity and circuits, then waves, account for most of the lost marks in UAE cohorts. Practical and data-handling questions ask students to read a graph and justify a conclusion, which is a separate skill from recalling the formula. Candidates studying online still need the practical skills, because the papers assess them in writing.

igcseSubjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
igcseSubjects.description: Moles calculations and organic families decide grades. The Extended paper assumes comfort with reacting masses and concentration in the same question, and students who learned each separately stall. Qualitative-analysis recall is pure marks and is usually the quickest single improvement available.

igcseSubjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
igcseSubjects.description: Heavy on terminology and process sequencing. Marks go on describing exactly what happens in what order, so a student who understands a process but cannot write it in the expected words is graded as if they did not understand it. Command-term practice is the fix.

igcseSubjects.name: Co-ordinated Sciences (0654)
igcseSubjects.description: Three sciences compressed into two grades, which changes revision economics: breadth beats depth, and the student who tries to study it as three separate subjects runs out of weeks. Mapping which topics are examined thinly is the first job and should happen in Year 10, not Year 11.

igcseSubjects.name: Economics (0455)
igcseSubjects.description: Definition precision then diagram accuracy. Many UAE candidates take this as a first social science and underestimate how exactly the mark scheme reads definitions. Data-response questions reward quoting the figures in the stimulus, which students routinely skip.

igcseSubjects.name: First Language English (0500) and English as a Second Language (0510)
igcseSubjects.description: Two different qualifications that are often confused at entry. 0500 demands sustained writing craft; 0510 rewards accuracy and task completion. Entering a student for the wrong one wastes a year, and the decision is made by the school long before the paper.

igcseSubjects.name: Business Studies (0450)
igcseSubjects.description: Calculation plus applied judgement on a case. Candidates who memorise definitions and never practise applying them to the stimulus business plateau in the middle grades. Six weeks of marked case questions moves the needle more than rereading the textbook does.

ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.regionsTitle: What the evening looks like, emirate by emirate
ib-igcse-tutor-near-me.regionsIntro: The regulator changes with the emirate, and so does the realistic start time for a session. The notes below are about timing and oversight rather than scenery, because those are the two things that decide whether a weekly slot survives past half term.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA oversees private education here. Most secondary timetables finish mid-afternoon, so the first workable slot is usually 16:30 and the last useful one around 19:30. Families with children at two different schools often need two different start times on the same evening.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi city and Al Reem Island
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. School-bus routes across the bridges stretch arrival home past 16:00 for many families, which pushes Diploma sessions towards 17:30 and makes a fixed weekly slot more valuable than a flexible one.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK. The IB cohort is smaller than on the island, so a Higher Level specialist in a minority subject is rarely available locally at any price. This is the clearest case in the country for matching on subject and accepting a live-video slot.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Many families commute to Dubai schools, so the realistic session start is later than the school finish time suggests.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools here. Cohorts are smaller and IGCSE is the dominant international route, so November resit planning matters more than in emirates with large Diploma populations. Evening slots are generally easier to protect.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah, approves curricula and assessment methods as well as fees. Distance from the main school clusters makes the drivable tutor pool very thin, which is why most planning here starts from the calendar instead.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under the federal Ministry of Education. The east coast has the smallest international cohort in the country, and a Chemistry HL or Further Pure Maths specialist is effectively a video-only proposition. The upside is that evening timetables are less congested than in Dubai.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised by the Ministry of Education. Families here often sit papers at a centre in another emirate, so the logistics conversation has to start with which centre holds the entry, not with which tutor is nearest. That question needs answering by the autumn term.

schoolClusters.note: These schools run both boards in volume, which means mock windows, option-form deadlines and Internal Assessment hand-in dates differ from one to the next even on the same street. A tutoring plan has to follow the school's own calendar, not a generic one.

The Abu Dhabi cluster carries a high proportion of Diploma students relative to its size, so Higher Level demand concentrates in a short booking window each autumn. Several of these schools publish their assessment calendars to parents, which is the document a tutoring plan should be built on.
schools: Repton Al Barsha and Abu Dhabi campuses

schoolClusters.note: Smaller international cohorts and longer commutes, with several families attending school in a different emirate from the one they live in. Entry arrangements for private candidates come up more often here, which makes the centre question the first one to settle.

modes.description: One fixed slot a week on live video, same tutor, same time. This is the mode that builds method rather than patching panic, and it is the only one that reliably fixes the slow problems: algebraic fluency, command-term accuracy, diagram reasoning. It also gives a tutor enough contact to notice a coursework deadline drifting before the school does.

sections.heading: What an IB IGCSE tutor near me actually gets you here
paragraphs: An IB IGCSE tutor near me is a search with a hidden premise: that the right teacher is the nearest one. In the UAE that premise breaks on two facts. Specialists are scarce by subject rather than by postcode, and the usable evening window between the school run and bedtime is about three hours wide for everybody. A tutor fifteen minutes away who is free only at 20:30 is functionally further from you than one on live video at 16:45.

It helps to work out what the distance was standing in for. Usually it is three things: that the person knows the exact syllabus your child is entered for, that they are free in your window, and that they are accountable week to week. None of the three is a function of geography. The syllabus code on the entry form tells you more than the community name does. Cambridge 0580 Extended Mathematics and Pearson 4MA1 Higher cover overlapping content through different papers, different question styles and different formula support, and a tutor who has only ever taught one of them will cost marks in the other.

An online IB and IGCSE tutor in the UAE is matched on three things in this order: the board and syllabus code, the level or tier, and the slot. Lessons run one-to-one over live video with the student's own written work on screen, which is where the marks actually are. Home visits are a service IB Gram runs in India, not in any emirate, and this page says so here rather than in a footer. What that buys a UAE family is the whole pool rather than the drivable part of it: a Physics HL specialist for a family in Fujairah and a Pearson modular mathematics specialist for one in Mirdif, in the same week.

The rest of this page is built backwards from exam week, because that is the only genuinely fixed point in the year. Everything else is calculated from it: when to start, what the market will charge by then, which board to resit with, and when the coursework deadline actually bites. Families who plan forwards from today tend to discover the entry deadline after it has passed.

sections.heading: Two boards, four series and one session your household is working to
paragraphs: A combined IB and IGCSE household is tracking at least three calendars. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. The IB Diploma May session is the one UAE schools use, and alongside it sit internal coursework deadlines that no board publishes.

The sourced dates are worth reading closely, because they show how far ahead the real deadlines sit. A UAE candidate has two Cambridge series available, June and November, because the February and March sitting is offered to India only; a date lifted from it describes a paper your child cannot sit. For the two series that do apply, Cambridge publishes the entry and forecast-grade dates series by series, and they land months ahead of the exam window rather than weeks. Pearson gives the firmer published anchor: its International GCSE November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A centre's own internal cut-off is earlier still than any board deadline, and that is the number that actually governs your year.

On the Pearson side, the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, often a full academic year before the November papers are actually sat, which is why the table below names the board's own page as the source rather than restating dates that can be revised.

For the IB, no date appears on this page. ibo.org returns an error to automated checking, so nothing in this project is confirmed from the IB itself, and publishing an unverified session or results date across a large set of pages would be worse than publishing none. Treat the May session as the window UAE schools work to, and get the actual dates from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org directly before you plan around them.

sections.heading: Counted backwards: a forty-week ladder to the first paper
paragraphs: Nobody plans an exam year forwards successfully, because the fixed point is at the end. The ladder below starts forty weeks out, which for a June series means the previous September, and works down to the week of the paper. It applies to both boards with the obvious substitutions: read tier for level, and centre for school where the student is a private candidate.

The two rungs families most often skip are the first and the fifth. The first is locking the level or tier, which caps the grade available and is decided long before anyone feels ready to decide it. A Core entry in Cambridge mathematics or a Foundation entry with Pearson sets a ceiling, and changing it later means re-teaching content and persuading a centre to amend an entry. The fifth is the forecast grade, which some series require on a fixed date and which a student cannot influence in the week it is submitted.

The middle of the ladder is where coursework and papers collide. Weeks 24 to 12 carry Internal Assessment drafts, Extended Essay drafts, TOK essay outlines and mock papers in whatever order the school has arranged them, and that order varies between schools in the same emirate. This is the stretch where a weekly tutor earns their place, because the work in front of the student each week keeps changing and a generic revision plan simply does not fit it.

The last four weeks should contain no new content at all. By then the job is timing, command terms, calculator and formula-booklet habits, and triage of the two or three topics still costing the most marks. Adding a new topic in the final fortnight reliably displaces something already secure, which is the single most common self-inflicted grade drop in an exam year.

sections.heading: Where the UAE school year puts the pressure: Ramadan, Eid and the long summer
paragraphs: The UAE academic year has a shape that generic revision advice ignores. Ramadan moves about eleven days earlier in the Gregorian calendar each year, which has walked it steadily into the second term, close to the mock window many schools run for the May session. School hours shorten during the month, energy patterns change, and the sensible response is to move sessions to post-Iftar timing rather than to pretend the month is a normal one. Check the dates for your year with the school, because they shift annually.

Eid breaks then remove teaching days at short notice, usually in a stretch of the year where there is no slack left. A family that has kept a fixed weekly slot absorbs this without much damage; a family that books ad hoc tends to lose two or three weeks and only notices at the mock results. The winter break sits immediately before mock season for many UAE schools, which makes it the most valuable two weeks in the year and the most commonly wasted.

Then there is the summer, which in this market is long and falls in the gap between IGCSE results and the start of the Diploma or Year 12. That gap is the only clear stretch available for bridging content, and the bridge is real: a student who finished 0580 Extended in June is missing specific prerequisites for Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL in September, and six focused weeks closes most of it. The same applies to the MYP5 to DP1 move, where the gap is usually written structure rather than content.

Sitting underneath all of this is a weekly timetable that already carries more than the home curriculum did. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited. KHDA calculates the instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. Those slots are real hours, and they are the reason a Tuesday evening fills up faster than parents expect.

sections.heading: The six Cambridge zones and the administrative mistakes that end a series
paragraphs: There is a class of problem in an exam year that has nothing to do with how well a student knows the content, and it is almost entirely absent from tutoring pages. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six Cambridge administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. A Pearson International GCSE timetable carries the same risk in a different form, because provisional versions are published ahead of each series and then revised.

The second category is entry. A centre's internal cut-off runs weeks ahead of the board's own deadline, because the exams officer has to collate and submit. A family that asks about adding a subject in January for a June series is usually too late, and the answer is the next series rather than this one. Private candidates have a harder version of the same problem: a private candidate must be entered by a centre that accepts private entries, and finding that centre is the first task, not the last.

The third is the forecast grade. Some series require them on a date the board publishes for that series alone, and a teacher submits them rather than the family. If nobody at the school has been asked who submits it and by when, it is an unmanaged dependency sitting in the middle of the exam plan. None of these three problems is expensive to prevent. All of them are expensive to discover late.

The practical move is a single email in September to the exams officer asking four questions: which zone is this centre in, what is your internal entry cut-off, which syllabus codes is my child entered for, and who submits forecast grades. Keep the reply. Every later decision on this page depends on those four answers, and a tutor working from them is working on the same calendar as the school.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges, and the month the price stops moving
paragraphs: Published IGCSE tutor rates in AED cluster into five tiers, and the figures below belong to the providers named beside them rather than to IB Gram. They were read in October 2026 from those providers' own pages and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. Three of the six competitor pages examined for this project publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. That is the only reason this table is unusual.

The calendar sits inside the pricing in a way rate cards never show. A qualified subject tutor who is available in September is competing with nobody; the same tutor in February is competing with every family whose mock results just arrived. Higher Level sciences and Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches are the first to go, and in smaller cohorts such as Al Ain, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah they can be gone entirely as a local option. Booking in the autumn is not an upsell, it is simply when the supply exists.

For context on scale, monthly packages advertised in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Against school fees those numbers read differently depending on the year: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for 2026-27, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion.

IB Gram does not publish a rate card on this page, and that is deliberate rather than coy. The number depends on the subject, the level and how many weeks are left, and a figure invented to fill a table would be worth less than the market bands above. The honest route is the free trial lesson and a short consultation, which also establishes whether the specialist you need is actually free in the window you need them.

sections.heading: Coursework deadlines are internal, and that is what catches families out
paragraphs: Parents reasonably assume that because the IB sets the papers, the IB sets the coursework deadlines. It does not, in any way a family can see. Your school sets the hand-in dates for the Internal Assessment in each subject, the Extended Essay milestones and the TOK essay drafts, and it sets them to leave itself room for internal marking and moderation. Two schools three kilometres apart in Dubai can be two months apart on the same component. The only calendar that matters is the one your child's school published, and many parents have never read it.

This has a direct consequence for timing. A Diploma student in DP2 who starts tutoring in January for the May papers has usually already passed the point where coursework could be improved, and a significant share of the final grade is therefore already fixed. Working backwards, the coursework rungs sit at roughly 24 to 12 weeks before the papers, and in the Extended Essay's case a year earlier. A family that reads the school's assessment calendar in September is making decisions; a family that reads it in February is reacting.

The boundary on what a tutor may do with that work is firm and worth stating plainly, because this SERP contains providers who sell finished coursework for a fee. Internal Assessment feedback means a tutor pressure-tests a research question, teaches the skill a criterion is testing, shows a student where a reader loses the thread, and hands the draft back for the student to change in their own words. It does not mean supplying text, re-drafting to a finished state, or handing over anything for submission. Under IB academic-honesty rules that second category puts the student's diploma at risk, and no grade is worth that trade.

A simple test works for any provider: ask what happens to the file. If the answer is that the student edits their own document after a session, you are buying teaching. If the answer is that something comes back finished, you are buying a problem that surfaces at moderation. Ask the question before the first payment, not after the first draft.

sections.heading: Results day, and the windows that close quietly after it
paragraphs: Results day feels like an ending and is actually the start of four or five short decision windows, most of which run through your centre rather than directly with the family. A review of marking has to be requested within a period the board fixes and the centre submits. A resit entry has to go in before the next series closes, which for a Cambridge June candidate usually means the November series and for a Pearson November candidate means the following summer. A school place or a university offer has its own deadline that is set by neither board.

The dates that are sourced here show how the rhythm works in practice. Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge posts June-series results on Cambridge Direct in August and November-series results in January. That spacing means a November resit decision is made within weeks of August results, and a January results release lands in the middle of a school term rather than a holiday.

What tutoring can and cannot do in this period is worth being clear about. In the days immediately after results there is nothing to teach: the useful work is getting the script and the mark scheme comparison through the school and reading them properly. Once a resit is decided, eight to twelve weeks of focused work on the specific papers that fell short is a reasonable plan, and it is a much more precise brief than a general course, because the gap has been measured by an examiner rather than guessed at.

The decision that most often gets made badly is switching tier or board for a resit. It can be the right move, but it means re-teaching whatever the other specification adds, and it has to clear the centre's entry deadline for the next series. Settle that with the exams officer before promising a student anything, because an entry that does not exist cannot be revised for.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency: the clock nobody counts backwards from
paragraphs: Equivalency is the deadline families discover last and should have planned first, because it is driven by a university admission calendar rather than by an exam board. MoE equivalency for IGCSE students on the British track requires proof of five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, as reported by Gulf Today in July 2026.

The detail that changes plans is which subjects count. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That single line reorders an option form: a student taking six subjects, two of which are Arabic and Islamic Education, is carrying four towards the count and not five. One competitor page currently ranking on this topic states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which is not what the sourced reporting says. Check your own child's entry list against the five-subject rule in Year 10, while the option form can still be changed.

On the American track, the same reporting sets English proficiency through one of three routes, a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB there is no published points threshold in that reporting, so none appears here. Anyone quoting an IB equivalency score should be asked which page on moe.gov.ae it came from.

Two boundaries matter. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation, and nothing about tutoring is a requirement for either. These are processes run by the Ministry and your emirate's attestation authority, and the official channels are where the current rules live. What a tutor can usefully do is read the subject count against the entry list early enough that the option form is still open, which is a planning conversation rather than a paid service.

sections.heading: Is the person teaching your child permitted to tutor in the UAE?
paragraphs: Private tutoring here is regulated by permit, and that is a check a parent can carry out in one question. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and the eligible categories are wide: teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, and the application runs through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two things follow. The first is that anyone offering private lessons without the permit is, in the Government's own words, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts is published, so no figure appears here, and a page quoting a specific fine should be treated with caution. The second is that eligibility is not the same as competence. A university student may hold the permit perfectly legitimately and still have never seen a Chemistry HL Paper 3 mark scheme.

There is a separate constraint that affects a tempting arrangement. The permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi have been reported to prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school. Those are press-reported terms rather than quotations from the current policy document, so verify them against ADEK before relying on them. The practical point stands: your child's own class teacher is not the right person to pay privately.

A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor. That requires a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps and renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit and occupies no UAE premises, which is exactly why it should never be described as having regulator endorsement of any kind.
