ib-math-aa-vs-ai-guidance.programmesIntro: The route decision belongs to the Diploma, but the signals that should inform it are generated earlier, and one IB route removes the decision almost entirely. These are the three a UAE family will be weighing.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme mathematics
programmes.description: Every Diploma candidate takes exactly one Group 5 subject: Analysis and Approaches or Applications and Interpretation, at Higher or Standard Level. There is no option to take both and no option to take neither. Standard Level in either route is two written papers plus the exploration; Higher Level adds a third paper. The exploration is a student-chosen piece of mathematical writing and carries a fifth of the grade in all four combinations.
programmes.countryNote: In UAE schools the two routes are usually timetabled in the same block, which is convenient for a move between them and inconvenient for anything else: the block that holds both maths courses cannot also hold a second Group 4 subject, so a route decision sometimes constrains the Group 6 substitution a family wanted.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme mathematics
programmes.description: MYP mathematics is assessed against four criteria, and in MYP 4 and 5 many schools split into standard and extended mathematics. That split is the closest thing to a route signal the programme produces, and the criterion profile behind it is more informative than the overall grade: a student strong on investigating patterns is showing something different from one strong on applying mathematics in real-life contexts.
programmes.countryNote: Continuum schools in Dubai and Abu Dhabi usually have the MYP 5 teacher's view available at route-choice time, and in the UAE that view is worth more than a predicted grade. Ask specifically whether the student reaches for an algebraic method or a calculator-driven one when a problem is unfamiliar, because that preference maps onto the two routes directly.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Students on the Career-related Programme take Diploma courses alongside a career-related study, and may take a mathematics course within that without the full Diploma's Group 5 obligation. Where mathematics is included, the route question still applies, but it is answered against the career-related study rather than against a six-subject balance.
programmes.countryNote: Offered at a small number of UAE schools. Where it exists it is worth asking about for students whose difficulty is specifically the compulsory mathematics requirement, because the programme structure changes what mathematics has to do in the qualification.

ib-math-aa-vs-ai-guidance.subjectsIntro: The route decision is rarely about mathematics alone. These are the subjects whose own demands should be on the table when the Group 5 choice is made, with the mathematics each one actually assumes.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches HL
subjects.description: Further calculus, proof by induction and contradiction, complex numbers, three-dimensional vectors and demanding series work, plus a third paper of extended unprompted problem solving. The standard route for engineering, physics and calculus-taught economics. It is the most common mid-DP1 step-down in UAE schools, and almost always for genuine reasons rather than effort.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches SL
subjects.description: The core algebra, functions, trigonometry, differentiation, integration and probability, examined across one non-calculator paper and one calculator paper plus the exploration. It satisfies a wide range of degree requirements and is the sensible default for a student who wants algebraic mathematics without a third paper.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation HL
subjects.description: Statistical inference including hypothesis testing, matrices, graph theory, complex numbers in modelling contexts and differential equations approached numerically, with a third paper built on extended modelling tasks. A demanding statistics and modelling qualification that is routinely misdescribed as the easier Higher Level.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation SL
subjects.description: Descriptive and inferential statistics, functions used as models, financial mathematics and geometry, with a calculator permitted in both papers. It suits students heading for business, design, psychology or social sciences, and is a poor fit for any degree that teaches first-year calculus from scratch.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Physics at Higher Level assumes algebraic fluency and benefits substantially from calculus, so Analysis and Approaches is the natural partner. Physics HL with Applications is survivable but awkward: several derivations in fields and motion assume differentiation the student has not formally met, and the gap has to be covered twice.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Chemistry's quantitative demands sit in logarithms, equilibrium calculation and rate work rather than in calculus, so either route can support it. The exception is a student heading for chemical engineering, where the degree's own mathematics requirement rather than the chemistry drives the route decision.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The Diploma Economics course itself does not require Analysis. Economics degrees frequently do, because first-year modules are taught with calculus and increasingly with econometrics. This is the single most common route mismatch we see in the UAE: Applications chosen for the Diploma, an economics degree chosen two years later.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The finance and operations content pairs naturally with Applications, including its financial mathematics and statistics. Business degrees rarely name a mathematics route, though some quantitative finance and analytics programmes do, which is worth checking rather than assuming.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Computer Science at Higher Level benefits from the discrete and abstract reasoning in Analysis, while Applications contributes graph theory and matrices that map onto parts of the course directly. Computer science degree requirements vary widely by country, so verify the named route for each target institution.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Research methodology and the statistics behind study design sit much closer to Applications than to Analysis, and the Applications statistics content genuinely helps. Few psychology degrees name a route, though some research-heavy programmes expect demonstrable statistical competence.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: Modelling, tolerance and data handling align with Applications, and students combining Design Technology with an engineering ambition are the group most likely to need Analysis anyway for the degree. The two pulls have to be resolved against the destination, not against the subject.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: The fieldwork and the internal assessment reward confident data handling and statistical presentation, which Applications supports well. It is a useful reminder that a route can be the better fit for five subjects and still be wrong for the degree, which is why destinations come first.

ib-math-aa-vs-ai-guidance.regionsTitle: Where UAE higher education sits, and why the route follows it
ib-math-aa-vs-ai-guidance.regionsIntro: A route decision is really a bet on where a student applies. The UAE has its own concentration of universities and licensed branch campuses, and the cluster your child is likely to apply into shapes which mathematics course is defensible. Verify every requirement on the institution's own admissions pages.

regions.name: Dubai International Academic City and Knowledge Park
regions.note: The emirate's largest concentration of licensed branch campuses and private universities, spanning engineering, business, media and computing. Entry criteria differ institution by institution rather than by emirate, so the practical step is to read the specific programme page for any course your child names.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi: Khalifa City, Saadiyat and Masdar City
regions.note: The capital hosts research-intensive and specialist institutions with strong engineering and science provision. Engineering programmes in this cluster are the ones most likely to specify a calculus-based mathematics background, which in Diploma terms points to Analysis and Approaches.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Home to long-established federal higher education with a broad faculty spread. Families in Al Ain frequently apply both locally and overseas in the same year, which makes the route decision a compromise between two sets of published requirements rather than a response to one.

regions.name: Sharjah University City
regions.note: A dense cluster of universities and colleges serving Sharjah and the northern emirates. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private schools in the emirate, including approving curricula and assessment methods, which is a separate matter from university entry but affects which Diploma routes a school can run.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: A smaller higher education footprint, with the Department of Knowledge regulating private schools in the emirate. Diploma provision is thin here, and families more often face the question of whether both mathematics routes will run at their school at all.

regions.name: Ajman and Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Private schools in both emirates are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Diploma cohorts are small, and where only one mathematics route is timetabled the decision is made for the family, which makes checking in term two of Year 11 rather than in September genuinely important.

regions.name: Fujairah and the east coast
regions.note: Almost no published tutoring provision and a small number of international schools. Students here needing Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level are the clearest case for live online teaching, because the local specialist pool for that specific combination is effectively empty.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai schools running both mathematics routes
schoolClusters.note: Where both courses are timetabled at both levels, a route change in the first weeks of DP1 is administratively possible. These Dubai schools have Diploma cohorts large enough that both routes usually run, though the Higher Level combination in each is the part to confirm.

Capital schools with engineering-heavy destination patterns tend to run Analysis and Approaches at Higher Level reliably, while Applications at Higher Level is less consistently available. The Department of Education and Knowledge supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate.

Smaller cohorts mean a school may run one route at Higher Level and the other only at Standard Level. That is the single most important thing to establish before a route preference forms, because a preference for an unavailable combination wastes the only easy window.

ib-math-aa-vs-ai-guidance.modesIntro: Mathematics route work divides cleanly into three jobs: deciding, catching up after a change, and teaching the course the student is actually sitting. These are the formats UAE families ask for.

modes.title: Route diagnostic before the decision
modes.description: Two short online sessions, one on an Analysis topic and one on an Applications topic, both pitched at DP1 content rather than at Year 11 revision. The purpose is to see which kind of mathematics the student reaches for under unfamiliarity, because that preference predicts two years of work better than any grade does.

modes.title: Catch-up block after a route change
modes.description: A defined block of sessions covering the content the new route assumes and the old one did not. For a move into Analysis that means algebraic fluency and early calculus; for a move into Applications it means statistical method and calculator technique, which students coming from Analysis genuinely lack.
bullets: Scoped to the gap, with the topic list written down before it starts

modes.title: Weekly teaching in the route being sat
modes.description: Ongoing one-to-one in Analysis or Applications at the level registered, following the school's scheme of work. The components practised differ by route: non-calculator fluency and unprompted problem solving in Analysis, calculator technique and model justification in Applications.

sections.heading: What Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation actually are
paragraphs: Analysis and Approaches is a course about mathematical structure. Its spine is algebraic manipulation, functions treated formally, trigonometric identity work, and calculus developed far enough that a student can differentiate and integrate unfamiliar expressions and justify what they have done. At Higher Level it adds formal proof, complex numbers and vectors in three dimensions. The course assumes the student will work by hand, and one of its papers is sat with no calculator at all.

Applications and Interpretation is a course about mathematical modelling. Its spine is data: describing it, drawing inferences from it, and building functions that represent real situations well enough to be useful. At Higher Level it extends into statistical inference, matrices, graph theory and numerically approached differential equations. A graphical display calculator is assumed throughout, and the mathematics being assessed includes choosing and justifying a model rather than only executing a technique.

Both courses carry an exploration worth a fifth of the final grade, both are offered at Higher and Standard Level, and both produce a grade from 1 to 7 that counts identically in the Diploma total. Neither is a remedial version of the other. The published syllabuses overlap in basic functions, sequences and elementary trigonometry, and then diverge quickly enough that a student who has done a year of one cannot simply sit the other.

The framing that causes the most damage in UAE schools is the phrase the easier maths. Applications is not easier; it is different, and Applications at Higher Level is a demanding qualification that defeats students who chose it to avoid effort. Equally, Analysis is not better; it is specific, and a student forced into Analysis by family pressure for a degree they will never apply for spends two years on calculus they do not need and loses marks that Applications would have given them.
bullets: Analysis: algebra, proof, calculus, one paper with no calculator
Applications: data, inference, modelling, calculator assumed throughout
Both carry an exploration worth a fifth of the grade and both are graded 1 to 7
Neither course is the remedial version of the other

sections.heading: The two syllabuses compared, topic area by topic area
paragraphs: A comparison that lists course titles is useless for a decision. What a family needs is the specific treatment each route gives to the areas both of them touch, because the overlap is where people assume equivalence and the divergence is where a route change becomes expensive. The table below does that area by area, with a final column stating what the student is expected to do unaided.

Read the calculus and the statistics rows together, because they are the two halves of the trade. Analysis develops calculus properly: differentiation from first principles, chains and products, integration techniques, and at Higher Level enough further calculus to handle unfamiliar expressions under examination conditions. Applications develops statistics properly: distributions, correlation and regression, and at Higher Level hypothesis testing and inference. Each course is thin where the other is thick, and the thinness is structural rather than a matter of emphasis.

Syllabus content and component weightings are published by the IB in the subject guide and revised between cycles, so the table describes the shape of the two courses rather than serving as a substitute for the guide your school is teaching to. Where a specific topic matters to a decision, check it in that guide with the subject teacher before committing a form.

One row in the table is doing more work than the others. The technology row is not a note about equipment; it is the structural consequence of everything above it. Because Analysis assesses by-hand execution directly and Applications assesses calculator judgement directly, a student's existing working habits are being examined as well as their mathematics. That is the row families skip and the one that predicts how the first term of DP1 will feel.

sections.heading: The non-calculator paper, and why it decides more than families expect
paragraphs: Analysis and Approaches candidates sit a paper with no calculator. That single structural fact carries more weight in a route decision than any syllabus list, because it converts a preference into a requirement. A student who is accurate and quick with algebraic manipulation finds that paper a straightforward place to collect marks. A student who has leaned on a calculator since Year 7 finds it the hardest paper of their Diploma, and no amount of conceptual understanding compensates, because the marks go to correctly executed working.

The habit is formed well before DP1, and in UAE schools it is formed unevenly. A student arriving from a curriculum with early calculator access, or from an IGCSE route where a calculator was permitted in most papers, may have real mathematical ability and no by-hand fluency. The route diagnostic that matters therefore is not a test of knowledge. It is watching what the student does when the calculator is taken away and the expression is unfamiliar: whether they reach for a method, or stall.

Applications candidates face the mirror-image problem, and it gets discussed far less. A graphical display calculator is assumed in every paper, which means calculator technique is itself assessed: knowing which function to use, entering a regression correctly, reading a distribution output and interpreting it in context. Students who come to Applications from an algebra-first background routinely lose marks not because they cannot do the mathematics, but because they do the mathematics the long way and run out of time.

Both failures are teachable, and both take weeks rather than days. That is the practical content of the route decision: the question is not which course is harder, but which set of habits your child already has and which set they would be building from nothing.
bullets: Analysis assesses by-hand fluency directly through a non-calculator paper

sections.heading: Which degree families name which route, and where to verify it
paragraphs: Route requirements are set by individual universities and individual programmes, not by countries, and they change between admissions cycles. What follows is the pattern that holds across most published criteria, with the explicit instruction to verify each one on the institution's own admissions page before planning around it. A tutoring site is not a source for an entry requirement, including this one.

The pattern itself is stable enough to be useful. Degrees that teach first-year mathematics from a calculus base, which means most engineering, physics, mathematics and an increasing share of economics and finance programmes, expect Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level. Degrees that use statistics as their quantitative core, which covers much of psychology, social science, business and design, accept either route and sometimes prefer Applications. Medicine and the life sciences usually name chemistry and biology rather than a mathematics route, and the mathematics requirement, where one exists, is satisfied by either course.

For UAE destinations there is an additional layer that sits before admission: Ministry of Education equivalency. The published British-track requirement is specific, naming five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from the five, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. No equivalent Diploma points figure has been read on a Ministry source for this project, so none is published here. Check the current Diploma requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate's attestation authority, and do not rely on a figure quoted by a tutoring provider, including the one competitor page that publishes a subject count at odds with the Ministry's own.

sections.heading: The exploration differs between the routes more than the papers do
paragraphs: Every Diploma mathematics student writes an exploration, a piece of independent mathematical writing worth a fifth of the grade. The task carries the same name in both routes and it is not the same task. An Analysis exploration is expected to develop mathematics: to take a question somewhere through manipulation, proof or calculus, and to show the mathematics working. An Applications exploration is expected to model something real: to find or collect data, choose a representation, justify the choice, and interpret what the mathematics says about the situation.

That difference catches students who change route late. A student who has been thinking in Analysis terms for a year and then moves to Applications often writes an Analysis exploration under an Applications title, and the criteria that reward engagement with a real context and justified modelling choices have little to reward. The reverse happens too: an Applications-trained student in an Analysis course produces a well-presented data exercise with no mathematical development in it.

The honest boundary on exploration support matters here, because this is the component where families most often ask for more than a tutor can legitimately give. A tutor may teach the mathematics, explain what each criterion rewards, discuss whether a proposed question has enough mathematics in it to sustain a piece, and give feedback on the student's own draft. A tutor may not supply the mathematics, hand over finished work, or edit a draft to the point where the writing is no longer the student's. The work is submitted with the student's declaration of authorship and a breach is handled as malpractice, with the consequence landing on the student. There are providers in this market selling completed internal assessments at a published price; that is a different product and buying it puts a Diploma at risk.
bullets: Analysis explorations develop mathematics; Applications explorations model a real situation
A late route change frequently produces an exploration written in the wrong register
Legitimate support is teaching, criteria explanation and feedback on the student's own draft
Supplying the mathematics or the writing is malpractice and falls on the student

sections.heading: What the wrong route costs, in hours and in AED
paragraphs: This is the arithmetic families never see before the decision and always see afterwards. Each row in the table below is a scenario we meet regularly in UAE schools, with the point at which it usually surfaces, what fixing it actually involves, and an indicative cost built from published market rates rather than from our own price list. The rate bands are taken from providers that published them in October 2026 and are attributed in the row.

The reference points are these. Unitors advertised online IGCSE tutoring from AED 150 and IB from AED 200 per hour. TutorChase listed AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table put specialist examination-year support at AED 200 to 450 and above, and in-home one-to-one at AED 180 to 350, with independent home tutors reaching 500. BartyED listed AED 650 at the premium end. Those are market figures. IB Gram's own position is a free trial lesson followed by a consultation, and the price conversation belongs there rather than on a comparison table.

Two conclusions come out of the arithmetic reliably. The first is that correcting a route inside DP1 is expensive but bounded: a term of catch-up alongside the current course, which at mid-band rates is a defined number of sessions with an end date. The second is that failing to correct it is unbounded, because the cost moves from tutoring hours into a changed degree plan, a foundation year, or an application cycle spent on courses the student did not want. Of the ranking competitor pages examined for this project, three publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars, which makes this arithmetic impossible for a UAE family to do from their pages.

sections.heading: What IGCSE, MYP and CBSE results actually predict about the route
paragraphs: Families want a grade threshold and there is not one. What prior qualifications give is a set of signals, some genuinely predictive and some misleading, and in the UAE the mix differs by the curriculum a student is arriving from. Reading them correctly is cheaper than correcting a route later.

From IGCSE, the useful signal is not the overall grade but whether the student took Additional Mathematics or the extended tier and how they performed on the algebra-heavy questions within it. A grade 8 or 9 achieved largely through accuracy on procedural questions is weaker evidence for Analysis at Higher Level than a grade 7 achieved with visible comfort on unfamiliar algebra. Board differences matter too: Cambridge and Pearson tier and structure their mathematics differently, so two students with the same letter have not necessarily demonstrated the same thing.

From MYP, the criterion profile is the signal and the overall grade is noise. A student scoring highly on investigating patterns is showing the disposition Analysis rewards. A student scoring highly on applying mathematics in real-life contexts is showing the disposition Applications rewards. Both are good mathematicians and they are good at different things, which is precisely the distinction the two routes exist to serve.

From CBSE or ICSE, which is a large share of the UAE's school population, the signal is usually strong procedural algebra and comparatively little exposure to open-ended modelling or to writing mathematics up. That profile often points to Analysis on aptitude while the student's own preference points elsewhere, and it reliably predicts difficulty with the exploration in either route, because an extended independent write-up is unfamiliar as a task rather than as mathematics.
bullets: IGCSE: the extended or additional paper and the algebra questions within it, not the overall grade

CBSE and ICSE: strong procedural algebra, less exposure to open modelling and write-ups
No prior qualification predicts exploration performance; the task itself is the unfamiliar part

sections.heading: Switching route: what transfers and what has to be re-taught
paragraphs: A route change is mechanically similar to a level change, in that it depends on the school's internal window in early DP1 and then on IB candidate registration, both of which the Diploma coordinator holds and neither of which is usually printed in the option booklet. Ask for both dates in writing. What differs from a level change is the content arithmetic, because a route change is a move between syllabuses rather than a move within one.

The table sets out each realistic move with what carries over and what has to be built from nothing. The two cross-route moves are the expensive ones, and they are not symmetrical: moving into Analysis means acquiring algebraic and calculus fluency that takes sustained practice, while moving into Applications means acquiring statistical method and calculator technique that can be taught faster but is genuinely new material rather than a skill gap.

One practical note on timing that applies to both directions. A student who changes route in the first weeks of DP1 arrives in a class that has covered three or four weeks of content, which is recoverable. A student who changes at the end of term one is behind on a syllabus they have never seen, while also sitting the assessments of a course they have only just joined. The cost difference between those two timings is larger than the cost difference between the routes themselves, which is the argument for testing the decision early rather than waiting for certainty.

process.title: Name the three or four destinations that are genuinely in play
process.description: Specific programmes at specific universities, not a country. We read each one's published criteria for a named mathematics route and level, and mark those as fixed. Where a criterion cannot be found on the institution's own pages, we say so rather than filling the gap with an assumption.

process.title: Two diagnostic sessions, one in each route
process.description: Free, online, and deliberately unfamiliar: one algebraic or calculus task without the method given, and one modelling or inference task with real data. What the student does when stuck is the evidence, which is why the tasks are not revision of material already covered.

process.title: A written comparison you can take to the subject teacher
process.description: A short note setting out how each session went, naming the specific points where the work stopped, and stating which route the evidence supports. It is written for the mathematics teacher and the Diploma coordinator, with topics named rather than impressions offered.

process.title: Confirm what your school can actually timetable
process.description: Both routes at both levels is not universal in the UAE, particularly in smaller cohorts in Sharjah and the northern emirates. Ask which combinations are expected to run, and ask in term two of Year 11, because a preference for a combination the school cannot offer wastes the one easy window.

process.title: Teaching scoped to the gap, with an end date
process.description: Where a catch-up block is needed after a change, the topic list is written down before it starts and the block ends when those topics are closed. Where ongoing teaching is the right answer, it follows the school's scheme of work rather than a parallel syllabus.

whyPoints.title: Route is treated as a separate decision from level
whyPoints.description: Most guidance collapses the two, and the costs are completely different: a level move within a route keeps nearly all the content, while a route move is a change of syllabus. This page prices them separately because families making one decision usually think they are making the other.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure names its publisher and its month
whyPoints.description: The cost table draws on rates published by Unitors, TutorChase, Bestimate and BartyED in October 2026, attributed row by row. They are market figures rather than IB Gram prices, and our own numbers come from the consultation after a free trial rather than from a table.

whyPoints.title: University requirements sent back to the source
whyPoints.description: The degree-family table states patterns and then tells you to verify each one on the institution's own admissions pages, because route requirements are set per programme and revised per cycle. No Ministry of Education Diploma points figure is published here, because none has been read on a Ministry source.

whyPoints.title: Diagnostics remove the calculator and the method
whyPoints.description: A test of what a student already knows cannot answer a route question. Our diagnostic gives an unfamiliar task without the method, once with a calculator and once without, because the habit a student brings is what the two routes actually assess differently.

whyPoints.title: Exploration support stays inside IB rules
whyPoints.description: Teaching the mathematics, explaining the criteria and giving feedback on your child's own draft is the work. Supplying mathematics or writing for an exploration is malpractice with the consequence falling on the student, and providers pricing per assignment are selling something other than teaching.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery, so route specialism beats proximity
whyPoints.description: Teaching is one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not send tutors to UAE homes, which means a student in Fujairah needing Analysis at Higher Level reaches that specialist rather than the nearest available mathematics tutor.

faqs.question: Is Applications and Interpretation the easier IB maths course?
faqs.answer: No, and the assumption is the most expensive one in this decision. Applications is a different course built on statistics, inference and modelling, and at Higher Level it includes hypothesis testing, matrices, graph theory and an extended modelling paper. Students who choose it to reduce work meet that content in DP2 and find it demanding. What is true is that Applications makes different demands: it asks for judgement about models and fluency with a calculator rather than algebraic manipulation by hand. Easier is the wrong axis; different is the right one.

faqs.question: Which maths route do UAE engineering programmes expect?
faqs.answer: Engineering programmes that teach first-year mathematics from a calculus base generally expect Analysis and Approaches, often at Higher Level, and that pattern holds across most published criteria in the UAE and overseas. The important caveat is that requirements are set by individual programmes and revised between cycles, so the only reliable source is the admissions page of each university your child names. Read three or four specific programme pages rather than relying on a summary, including this one, and treat any named route and level as fixed before the rest of the option form is discussed.

faqs.question: My child used a calculator all through IGCSE. Does that rule out Analysis?
faqs.answer: It does not rule it out, but it names the work. Analysis candidates sit a paper with no calculator, and the marks on it go to correctly executed working rather than to understanding. A student with real mathematical ability and no by-hand fluency can build that fluency, and it takes weeks of deliberate practice rather than a few sessions. The decision point is whether there is time and appetite for that alongside five other subjects. A diagnostic that removes the calculator and uses unfamiliar algebra answers the question better than any grade does.

faqs.question: Can my child change from AI to AA after DP1 has started?
faqs.answer: In the first weeks of DP1, usually yes, subject to the school's timetable and the receiving class having space. After the school's internal cut-off it becomes difficult, and after IB candidate registration it is a formal amendment the coordinator submits. The content problem is the bigger one: moving into Analysis means acquiring algebraic manipulation and early calculus that the Applications course does not develop. That is a term of work alongside the new course, which is manageable in September and much harder in January.

faqs.question: Does the exploration differ between the two maths routes?
faqs.answer: Substantially, though it carries the same name and the same weighting of a fifth of the grade. An Analysis exploration is expected to develop mathematics, taking a question somewhere through manipulation, proof or calculus. An Applications exploration is expected to model a real situation, with data, a justified choice of representation and an interpretation. Students who change route late often write one in the register of the other, which leaves the criteria with little to reward. Deciding the route early also settles what kind of piece the student is preparing to write.

faqs.question: How much would it cost to catch up after a maths route change in Dubai?
faqs.answer: At published market rates, a term of weekly specialist sessions. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table put specialist examination-year support at AED 200 to 450 and above per hour, TutorChase listed AED 270, and Unitors advertised online IB tutoring from AED 200. A bounded catch-up block of ten to fourteen sessions in that range is the realistic shape of the bill. Those are market figures from the providers named in October 2026, not IB Gram prices; ours are discussed in the consultation that follows a free trial lesson.

faqs.question: Is Analysis and Approaches Standard Level enough for an economics degree?
faqs.answer: For many programmes yes, and for the most quantitative ones no. Economics degrees increasingly teach with calculus and econometrics from first year, and the competitive end of that market frequently names Analysis at Higher Level. Less quantitative programmes accept Standard Level and some accept Applications. Because the spread is this wide, economics is the degree family where we see the most route mismatches in UAE cohorts. Check the specific programmes rather than the subject, and treat the strictest requirement on your child's shortlist as the binding one.

faqs.question: What does Applications and Interpretation Higher Level actually add over Standard Level?
faqs.answer: Statistical inference including hypothesis testing, matrices used for transformations and networks, graph theory, further work on complex numbers in modelling contexts, differential equations approached numerically, and a third paper built around extended modelling tasks. The step is real and it is concentrated in content that has no Standard Level equivalent, so it cannot be reached by studying the Standard Level course more thoroughly. Provision at Higher Level is also thinner across UAE schools than Analysis at Higher Level, so confirm the class will run before building a plan around it.

faqs.question: Which route suits a student coming from CBSE into DP1?
faqs.answer: The common profile from CBSE or ICSE is strong procedural algebra with less exposure to open-ended modelling and to writing mathematics up as an extended piece. On aptitude that often points to Analysis, and the honest complication is that the same profile predicts difficulty with the exploration in either route, because an independent write-up is unfamiliar as a task rather than as mathematics. The useful step is a diagnostic on unfamiliar algebra without a method given, plus an early conversation about what the exploration will require.

faqs.question: Can a student take both IB maths courses?
faqs.answer: No. Every Diploma candidate takes exactly one Group 5 subject, which is one of the two mathematics courses at one level. There is no option to take both, and no option to take neither within the full Diploma. Students on the certificate route, taking individual Diploma courses rather than the full award, are not bound by the Group 5 requirement, but they still choose one course if they take mathematics at all. That single-choice structure is what makes the route decision worth more attention than most option-form entries.

faqs.question: Does the route affect how many taught hours my child gets?
faqs.answer: The level does, not the route. The IB recommends 240 taught hours for a Higher Level course in either route and 150 at Standard Level. What the route changes is what those hours are spent on and what the student has to be able to do unaided at the end of them: algebraic execution and calculus in Analysis, statistical method and calculator technique in Applications. Two students with identical hours in different routes finish with genuinely different mathematical skills, which is the point of having two courses.

faqs.question: How do I tell whether my child's difficulty is the route or the level?
faqs.answer: Watch which kind of task stalls. A level problem looks like competence on core material and collapse on extension content: the student handles the standard question and cannot start the extended one. A route problem looks like difficulty with the whole character of the course: an Analysis student who is lost whenever an expression has to be rearranged, or an Applications student who cannot decide which model to use. Two short sessions, one on each kind of task, usually separate them, and the answers point to different fixes.

faqs.question: Will our school definitely offer both routes at both levels?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Smaller Diploma cohorts, which is the norm in Sharjah, Ajman, Ras Al Khaimah and the smaller Dubai schools, often run one route at Higher Level and the other only at Standard Level, and that pattern can change year to year with numbers. In Sharjah the Private Education Authority approves curricula and assessment methods, so a school cannot add a class mid-year because demand appeared. Ask in term two of Year 11 which combinations are expected to run, and build the decision around the answer.

faqs.question: Is there an IB points figure for UAE Ministry of Education equivalency?
faqs.answer: Not one this page will publish, because no Diploma figure has been read on a Ministry of Education source for this project. What is sourced is the British track: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. For the Diploma requirement, check moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority directly. One competitor page publishes a subject count that disagrees with the Ministry's own.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help choose the route, or only teach it afterwards?
faqs.answer: Both, with the boundary stated. A diagnostic session in each route produces evidence about which kind of mathematics a student can work in, and the written note afterwards says which route that evidence supports and where the work stopped. What the note will not do is predict a grade, promise an admissions outcome, or recommend a route in which no specialist is free to teach. The decision belongs to your family, the mathematics teacher and the Diploma coordinator; IB Gram holds no board or regulator accreditation.

ib-math-aa-vs-ai-guidance.closingHeading: Price the decision before the form closes
ib-math-aa-vs-ai-guidance.closingBody: The mathematics route is the one Group 5 entry that can quietly remove a degree, and it is also the one most often decided on a rumour about which course is easier. Read the published criteria for three or four specific programmes. Test your child on one algebraic task without a calculator and one modelling task with real data, both unfamiliar. Then decide against evidence rather than reputation. A free trial lesson is one hour, online and one-to-one, and the written note afterwards names the topics attempted and where the work stopped.

intro.heading: What a UAE family is really asking for when the exploration is due
paragraphs: The IB mathematical exploration is a 12 to 20 page piece of individual written work that every Diploma maths student produces, whichever route and level they sit. It is marked out of 20 against five criteria, moderated externally, and worth a fifth of the final grade. A student who sits strong papers and submits a thin exploration loses more than most families expect, because that fifth is banked months before the written examinations begin. That arithmetic is why requests for IB math IA help in the UAE cluster in two short windows each year: the weeks when a topic has to be agreed, and the fortnight before the school's upload deadline.

The second thing families are asking for, usually without saying it out loud, is a reading of where the work currently stands. Parents who studied mathematics in another system recognise the equations on the page and have no way to judge criterion C or criterion D, because nothing in A Levels, CBSE or the American high-school diploma resembles them. A maths teacher who has marked explorations can say, in one session, which of the 20 marks are already safe, which are reachable before the deadline and which have been closed off by a topic choice made six weeks earlier.

Where you sit in the Emirates changes the practical picture more than the mathematics. Dubai had 227 private schools and 387,441 pupils in 2024-25 across 17 different curricula, with IB programmes accounting for roughly seven per cent of enrolment, so the pool of teachers who have supervised an exploration is wide in Dubai and much narrower in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain. Abu Dhabi schools sit under ADEK, whose professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school, which removes the obvious first option for many Abu Dhabi families.

IB Gram works as a matching platform, not a centre. There is no IB Gram office in the Emirates and no tutor is sent to a residential address here; every UAE session runs over live video with a shared screen, and home visits are something we offer only in India. For a maths exploration that turns out to be an advantage rather than a compromise, because the document, the graphing file and the spreadsheet are all on a screen that both people can annotate, and because a family in Al Ain can book a specialist in Applications and Interpretation rather than whoever is free locally.

What follows is the detail a parent needs to make a decision this week: the five criteria with their mark allocations, the places UAE students lose marks, what the market charges in AED, what the honesty rules permit a tutor to do with a draft, how the school calendar and your emirate's regulator shape the deadline, and what happens to the mark after it leaves the teacher's hands.

Length 12 to 20 pages; the IB sets no word count for maths
Worth 20 per cent of the grade in Maths AA and Maths AI, SL and HL
The teacher marks it; the IB moderates the mark, up or down
Your school sets the internal deadline, not the IB

ib-math-ia-help.programmesIntro: Exploration-style assessed work does not start in DP1. The IB builds towards it from the middle years, and the programme your child sits determines what a tutor is actually preparing them for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The mathematical exploration sits in DP Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches and DP Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation, at both Standard and Higher Level. It is 20 marks, 12 to 20 pages, and 20 per cent of the subject grade. The IB allocates around 10 to 15 hours of teaching time to it, which in practice means a handful of lessons spread over two terms while the taught syllabus continues around it.
programmes.countryNote: UAE DP cohorts are unusually mobile: a DP1 class in Dubai or Abu Dhabi often contains students who arrived from IGCSE, CBSE, the American curriculum and the French system within the same year. That shows up in exploration topic choice, because a student who has never written extended mathematics before will reach for a topic that looks impressive and cannot be sustained for 15 pages.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP Mathematics is marked against four criteria, including criterion D, applying mathematics in real-life contexts. That criterion is the direct ancestor of the exploration: it asks a student to pick a situation, model it, and comment on the limits of the model. A student who has written MYP criterion D tasks seriously arrives in DP1 already knowing what mathematical writing looks like.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools run the MYP through Year 11 instead of IGCSE, and those students reach DP1 with stronger writing habits but sometimes thinner algebraic fluency than an IGCSE cohort. Both gaps affect the exploration differently, so a tutor who knows which route a Dubai or Sharjah school uses can predict which criterion will cost marks before reading a line.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs DP subjects with a career-related study and a Reflective Project rather than the full Diploma core. CP students who carry a DP maths course still sit the same exploration under exactly the same criteria and the same page range, so nothing about the marking changes; what changes is the timetable pressure, because the Reflective Project deadline often lands in the same term.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision is thinner across the Emirates than full DP provision, and a CP student taking one DP maths course may be the only person in the room writing an exploration that term. That isolation is the usual reason a CP family in Dubai or Ajman books outside support: there is no cohort to compare drafts with.

programmes.name: Diploma core: EE, TOK and CAS
programmes.description: The Extended Essay can be written in mathematics, and families often confuse it with the exploration. The Extended Essay runs to 4,000 words, has a named supervisor, formal reflection sessions and its own criteria; the exploration is shorter, has no word count, and is marked inside the subject. A student doing both in mathematics needs them kept deliberately apart in topic and in method.
programmes.countryNote: In most UAE schools the Extended Essay deadline and the maths exploration deadline fall within the same academic year, often within the same term, and the school decides the order. Asking the DP coordinator for both internal dates in writing is the single most useful thing a parent can do in DP1, because the sequencing is a local decision, not an IB one.

ib-math-ia-help.subjectsIntro: Explorations and internal assessments are not interchangeable between subjects. The criteria, the mark allocations and the failure modes differ, and so does what a useful session looks like. These are the courses UAE families most often pair with exploration support.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The AA exploration rewards mathematics developed with precision: a derivation, a proof sketch, an analytical model handled correctly. Criterion E at HL expects work commensurate with HL content, so a topic resting on quadratics will cap the mark however neatly it is presented. Most AA marks are lost on unjustified steps rather than on arithmetic.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The AI exploration is built for modelling and real data: regression, chi-squared tests, financial mathematics, networks at HL. The common failure is the opposite of AA's. Students generate output from technology, present it accurately, and never interpret it, which empties criterion D of anything to reward while criterion E looks superficially full.

subjects.name: MYP Mathematics
subjects.description: MYP criterion C, communicating, and criterion D, applying mathematics in real-life contexts, are where exploration habits are built. Work here is marked on a 0-8 scale per criterion against task-specific clarifications, which is why an MYP student's first DP exploration draft often reads like an MYP investigation and needs reframing rather than correcting.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The physics internal assessment is a scientific investigation with its own criteria and a 3,000-word ceiling, not an exploration. Students taking Physics and Maths AA together frequently plan both around the same data set; separating them matters, because reusing one piece of work across two subjects is a route into an academic-honesty investigation.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Chemistry's investigation shares the sciences criteria rather than the maths ones, and the overlap with a maths exploration is usually uncertainty and error handling. A student who can propagate uncertainty for chemistry often writes much better reflection in maths, because the habit of saying what the number cannot tell you transfers directly to criterion D.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Biology students often arrive at the maths exploration with a statistics question already in hand from fieldwork or a database. That is a reasonable starting point for Applications and Interpretation, provided the mathematics is genuinely the subject of the write-up rather than a test applied once and reported.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: DP Economics is assessed through three commentaries on published news articles, not an exploration, so the two pieces of coursework pull in different directions in the same term. Economics students writing a maths exploration gravitate to elasticity and index numbers, which work well at AI and need real care at AA HL.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Business Management's internal assessment is a research project with its own word limit and its own criteria. Where it helps a maths exploration is sourcing: a student who has already handled a real company's figures understands why a model needs its assumptions stated, which is exactly what criterion D asks for.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Computer Science students often want to code the exploration. Programming is allowed as a tool and the output can be presented, but criterion E rewards the mathematics, not the implementation, so a session usually spends its time deciding which part of the algorithm is the mathematical argument worth writing up.

subjects.name: Extended Essay in Mathematics
subjects.description: A 4,000-word mathematics Extended Essay with a named supervisor and recorded reflection sessions. Families sometimes ask for exploration support and actually need Extended Essay support, or the reverse. The two use different criteria and different research depth, so the first session is often spent working out which document is actually in front of us.

ib-math-ia-help.regionsTitle: Exploration support across the seven emirates
ib-math-ia-help.regionsIntro: Which regulator oversees your child's school changes the calendar, the reporting and sometimes who is allowed to tutor your child. These are the practical differences by emirate, rather than a list of place names.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA oversees 227 private schools serving 387,441 pupils across 17 curricula, and the 2026-27 intake adds seven schools, three of them IB. Deep DP maths provision, but exploration deadlines cluster, so specialist availability in the fortnight before a school upload window is the binding constraint.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK licenses and accredits private schools in the emirate. Its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of pupils at their own school, so the familiar route of asking a child's own maths teacher is closed, and an outside specialist is the normal answer here.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Al Ain sits under ADEK with Abu Dhabi, and the same staff-ethics position applies. The DP cohort is smaller, which means fewer students in a year group writing the same route of exploration and less informal comparison of drafts. Most Al Ain families we work with book earlier in DP1 for that reason.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Several Sharjah families commute to Dubai schools, so a 4pm session often has to become a 6.30pm session once the drive home is counted.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority. IB Diploma provision is limited, so a DP maths student here may be one of a handful locally, and online delivery is less a preference than the only way to reach an Applications and Interpretation specialist.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: RAK's Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like SPEA, approves curricula and assessment methods. The emirate returned effectively zero mentions across the competitor pages we studied, which is a fair proxy for how much local DP maths tutoring capacity actually exists.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Fujairah's private schools fall under the Ministry of Education. For a DP maths student the practical issue is distance from any DP maths specialist on the coast, so exploration support here is almost always booked as a short block of video sessions around the topic decision and the draft.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Umm Al Quwain is also supervised by the Ministry of Education. With the smallest private-school population in the country, a student taking DP Mathematics may have no local tutor in the route they sit, and we match from outside the emirate rather than pretend otherwise.

schoolClusters.note: The widest DP maths provision in the country, and the tightest competition for a tutor in the weeks before an upload deadline. Schools set their own internal exploration dates, so two Dubai students in the same neighbourhood can be six weeks apart on the same piece of work.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain IB schools
schoolClusters.note: ADEK territory, where the staff-ethics position rules out a child's own teacher as a paid tutor. Cohorts are smaller than Dubai's, so the number of students sitting Applications and Interpretation HL in one year group can be in single figures.

IB Diploma provision thins sharply north of Dubai, and the regulator changes with the emirate: SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, the Ministry of Education in Ajman, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain. Online delivery is what makes a route specialist reachable at all.

ib-math-ia-help.modesIntro: Exploration work is not open-ended tuition. It has a document, a deadline and a mark scheme, so it suits a defined block better than an indefinite weekly commitment. These are the three shapes UAE families book.

modes.description: A short, bounded block that runs from topic decision to the student's final version. Session one tests whether the topic can carry 20 marks, session two fixes the mathematics the topic actually needs, and the remaining sessions work criterion by criterion. The student writes between sessions; the tutor reads what exists and names which marks are now in reach.

The weekly session follows the school's scheme of work, and three or four of those sessions across the year are reassigned as exploration checkpoints at the points where the school has asked for something: a topic, a plan, a draft. This is the usual pattern for a DP1 student starting early.

The tutor reads it against the five criteria and reports what is secure, what is one revision away and what cannot be recovered in the time left. Feedback only: no text is supplied, and the student decides what to change.

sections.heading: What IB math IA help means in practice
paragraphs: IB math IA help means working on the mathematical exploration: the 12 to 20 page individual piece of written mathematics that is worth 20 per cent of the final grade in both DP maths courses, at both levels. It is marked out of 20 by the class teacher against five published criteria and then moderated by the IB. It is not an exam paper, there is no past-paper technique to drill, and no amount of exam practice improves it.

That makes the work different from the rest of maths tutoring. A session on sequences has a right answer and a method to rehearse. A session on an exploration is a reading: does this topic contain enough mathematics for criterion E at this level, has the student explained why each step follows, is there any genuine reflection, and will a reader who has never met this student follow the argument from the first page to the last. Those are judgement calls, which is why families want someone who has marked the thing rather than someone who is good at maths.

The second half of the job is sequencing. An exploration has a topic decision, a mathematics decision, a writing phase, one permitted round of school feedback and a final version. Each of those has a different useful intervention, and several of them cannot be undone later. A topic agreed in week one that caps criterion E at three marks out of six will still cap it in the final week, however much work goes in between.

Families searching for IB maths exploration help usually arrive at one of two moments. Either the school has asked for a topic and nothing has come, or there is a document and no way to judge it. Both are workable. The second is tighter, and the honest answer in that situation is sometimes that two criteria are already settled and the remaining time is best spent on the two that still move.
bullets: Not an exam component: no past papers, no mark-scheme drilling
Marked internally by the teacher, then moderated by the IB
Same weighting at SL and HL, in AA and in AI
Topic choice sets a ceiling that later effort cannot lift

sections.heading: The twenty marks, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: Five criteria, 20 marks, and they are not evenly weighted. Criterion E, use of mathematics, carries six marks on its own, nearly a third of the total, and it is the one most tied to the topic decision. Criteria A and B carry four marks each and are the most recoverable late, because presentation and mathematical communication respond to editing. Criteria C and D carry three marks each and are the ones UAE students most often leave empty, because nothing in an IGCSE, CBSE or American transcript has ever asked a student to explain why they personally chose a question or what the answer failed to capture.

Reading the IB maths IA criteria in order also tells you what a session should cover and when. Criterion A rewards a coherent, organised, concise piece of work: an introduction with a stated aim, a visible structure, a conclusion that answers the aim. Criterion B rewards mathematical language used correctly throughout, which means defined variables, consistent notation, labelled graphs, units carried, and no spreadsheet screenshot standing in for an explanation. Both are checkable without knowing the topic, which is why they are the first thing a tutor looks at.

Criterion C, personal engagement, and criterion D, reflection, are where the marks hide. Engagement is not an anecdote about liking maths; it is evidence that the student made decisions, tried something, adapted when it failed. Reflection is not a summary paragraph; it is commentary at the points where a result arrived, on what it means, what the limits of the method are, and what the student would do differently. A tutor cannot supply either of those, which is exactly why they need to be taught rather than fixed at the end.
The table below is the version of this most families want on one screen, with the mark allocation beside the failure mode we see most often in UAE cohorts.

sections.heading: Analysis and Approaches and Applications and Interpretation are different briefs
paragraphs: The two DP maths courses share the exploration criteria and share the weighting, and that similarity misleads people. The mathematics each one rewards is not the same, so a topic that scores well in one route can be mediocre in the other. Analysis and Approaches is built around analytical technique and argument: calculus handled properly, algebraic manipulation that goes somewhere, a result derived rather than asserted. Applications and Interpretation is built around modelling and data: a real data set, a model fitted and criticised, statistics that answer a question somebody might actually ask.

That difference shows up most sharply in criterion E, where the examiner is asked whether the mathematics is commensurate with the level of the course. A Maths AA HL student writing a Maths AA exploration about a regression line drawn by a spreadsheet has not reached HL content, however accurate the regression. A Maths AI SL student writing a Maths AI exploration that spends ten pages on an analytical derivation has gone away from the course rather than beyond it, and criterion D suffers because there is no real-world interpretation left to make.

The practical consequence for a parent is that advice from a friend's older child may be actively wrong if they sat the other route. We ask which course and which level before anything else, and the answer changes the shape of the first session completely: AA students usually need their topic narrowed and their justification tightened, while AI students usually need their interpretation built after the technology has produced a result.

sections.heading: Where UAE students lose exploration marks
paragraphs: The losses are predictable enough to list. The first is topic size. Students pick something they can describe in one sentence and then discover there are only two pages of mathematics in it, so the document is padded with background, history and screenshots. Criterion A notices the padding and criterion E notices the absence. The fix has to happen at the topic stage, which is why the first session is usually spent stress-testing the topic rather than looking at any writing.

The second is the missing voice. Criterion C and criterion D together carry six marks, the same as criterion E, and they are the two that transferring students have never been asked for. A student who came through IGCSE in Year 11 has spent two years being marked on correct answers and has no reason to believe that explaining a decision earns anything. Those six marks are usually the difference families notice most once the moderated mark comes back.

The third is technology without interpretation, which has grown as graphing and spreadsheet tools have become standard across UAE schools. A page of correct output with no commentary reads as effort to a parent and as an empty page to a moderator. The counterpart failure, more common in Analysis and Approaches, is a correct derivation with every intermediate step shown and no sentence explaining why the next line follows from the last.

The fourth is the calendar, and it is specific to this region. UAE school terms, the Ramadan timetable and family travel over the long winter and spring breaks mean the weeks a student expects to use for the exploration are often not available. A draft planned for the break rarely survives the break. The schools that handle this well set an internal date before the break rather than after it, and a parent can ask which one their school has done.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not do with an exploration
paragraphs: This is the question that decides whether outside support is safe, and it deserves a straight answer. The exploration must be the student's own work. Every line of mathematics and every sentence of commentary has to come from the student, and the student signs a declaration of authenticity before it is submitted. A tutor teaches the mathematics, questions the argument, points at a criterion and says what is missing. A tutor does not supply text, does not rewrite sentences, and does not hand over a worked version to be copied.

The IB's own process already has a feedback step built in: the teacher may read and comment on one draft, and that comment is advisory. The teacher does not edit the document or mark up corrections line by line. An outside tutor working honestly stays inside the same boundary. Feedback can be detailed and specific about what is wrong without ever being a correction to transcribe, which is the distinction the sessions are designed around.

It matters because the consequences land on the student, not on the tutor. Work that is not a student's own is academic misconduct, and the IB's response can reach as far as withholding a grade. The essay-mill pages that sit in this same search result sell finished internal assessments outright; a family buying one is buying an investigation risk for their child. Our position is the opposite and we would rather state it plainly than be vague about it to win a booking.

There is also a local layer. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi prohibit teachers from paid private tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the permit-holder's school. Between them, those rules mean the comfortable option of paying your child's own maths teacher to supervise the exploration privately is not an option in Abu Dhabi, and should be checked carefully anywhere else.

sections.heading: Your school sets the deadline, not the IB
paragraphs: Parents often assume the exploration has a date published by the IB that applies to every candidate. It does not work that way. The IB sets the submission and upload requirements for the session, and each school builds its own internal timeline backwards from them, adding time for marking, moderation sampling and the inevitable late candidate. That means two students in the same emirate, sitting the same course in the same session, can be six weeks apart on the same piece of work, and the only authority on your child's date is the school's DP coordinator.

This is why we ask for the school's internal dates in the first session rather than quoting a national calendar. The question to ask the coordinator is specific: when is the topic due, when is the one permitted draft due, and when is the final version due. Three dates, in writing, usually by email. With those, the block of sessions can be positioned where it does something, instead of arriving after the draft window has closed.

Dates for the examination session itself are a different matter and we deliberately do not publish them. IB session and results dates should be confirmed with your school's DP coordinator or on ibo.org, because secondary sources circulate windows that get revised. Where a student also sits Cambridge or Pearson qualifications, those boards do publish their own timetables, and the published pattern is a useful illustration of how far ahead entry deadlines sit: Cambridge runs two series a UAE candidate can enter, June and November, with the February and March sitting reserved for India, and for both of the real ones the entry closes months before the first paper rather than in the term the papers fall in. Pearson's International GCSE November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, which is the kind of published window an internal assessment schedule can safely be built backwards from.

sections.heading: KHDA, ADEK, SPEA and what your regulator changes
paragraphs: Five bodies regulate private schools in the UAE and most tutoring pages mention none of them. Dubai's Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

For an exploration the relevance is indirect but real. Your regulator determines what inspection information you can read about the school that is teaching your child DP Mathematics, what route a complaint takes, and which authority approves the programmes and assessment methods a school may run. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, which is a wider remit than inspection alone. Knowing which body holds that remit tells a parent who to ask when a school's internal arrangements look unusual.

There is also a mandatory-subject layer that affects the timetable the exploration has to fit into. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum they are licensed for, with KHDA requiring the arrangements to be in place from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA calculates mandatory instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises that no mandatory lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes, and it requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies. Those hours are in the week before any DP subject gets a slot.

One thing we will not do is borrow any of these names as a credential. IB Gram holds no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education or MoHRE approval, accreditation or licence, and anyone advertising their tutors as endorsed by a regulator should be asked for the permit number. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific instrument issued to training institutes with premises, renewed annually, and it is not what a matching platform holds.

sections.heading: What exploration support costs in the UAE market
paragraphs: Most pages in this search result publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. Here is what the market actually charges, in AED, with the source and the date attached to each band rather than presented as our own price list. These figures were read from published provider rates and from a Dubai tutoring cost table compiled for 2026, reviewed in October 2026. Rates move, and a quote older than a term should be re-checked.

Two features of exploration pricing differ from ordinary subject tuition. The first is that the work is finite, so it is bought in blocks rather than as an open weekly commitment; four to six sessions is the usual shape and a parent should expect to be told roughly how many at the start. The second is that supervision and review are often priced separately from weekly teaching, which is where unexpected invoices come from. Ask whether reading a document between sessions is included or billed, and ask before the block starts.

A note on where our own pricing sits. IB Gram does not publish a rate card on these pages, because the rate depends on route, level and how much of the work is teaching rather than review. The free trial lesson comes first, with no card details taken, and a quote follows that conversation. Anything quoted here as an AED figure belongs to the market and is attributed, not to us.

What the table cannot tell you is whether a given price is worth paying, and that depends almost entirely on when you buy. Four sessions spent on topic scoping in DP1 change the ceiling of the mark. The same four sessions spent a week before the final version is due can only tidy criteria A and B. The cheapest effective spend on an exploration is early, and that is the opposite of how most families end up buying it.

sections.heading: How a maths write-up actually works over video
paragraphs: A fair question from a parent whose child does mathematics on paper: how does any of this work over a screen? In practice better than the alternative, because the exploration is a document and a set of files, and documents are easier to share than to pass across a table. The student shares their screen with the write-up open, the graphing file beside it, and the tutor annotates as they read. Where the student works by hand, a phone camera on the page or a photograph sent before the session covers it, and many DP students write directly into a tablet by this stage of the course anyway.

Sessions are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the UAE school week, which for most families means a slot between 4.30pm and 9pm on a weekday or a longer block at the weekend. Sharjah and Ajman families commuting into Dubai schools usually need the later end of that range. During Ramadan the pattern changes and sessions move to the post-Iftar evening, which coincidentally suits exploration work: it is reading and writing rather than new content, and it holds up well in a late-evening slot.

Online delivery is also what makes a route match possible. A student in Fujairah taking Applications and Interpretation HL needs a tutor who has marked AI HL explorations, and the chance of that person living within driving distance is small. Live video removes the geography from the problem, which is why every UAE session runs this way; IB Gram does not operate a centre or send a tutor to a residential address anywhere in the Emirates, and we would rather say that in the first paragraph of a page than in the small print.

What stays constant is the record. Each session ends with a written note of what was discussed and what the student is doing next, which is what lets a parent see progress without sitting in the room and lets a student show, if ever asked, how the work developed. For coursework that depends on being demonstrably the student's own, that trail is worth keeping.

sections.heading: Equivalency, universities and what the exploration mark feeds into
paragraphs: The exploration mark does not travel anywhere on its own. It is scaled into the subject grade, and the subject grade is what appears on the diploma and what a university sees. That is worth saying because families sometimes treat the exploration as a separate credential to be optimised, and sometimes dismiss it as coursework that will not matter. Neither is right: it is a fifth of a grade that a conditional offer may hinge on.

For families planning to use UAE qualifications locally, Ministry of Education equivalency is the process that sits behind the planning, and it is worth describing accurately because a competing page already publishes the wrong version. On the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five required subjects. On the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test.

For the IB there is a point we will not fill in. No IB points threshold for equivalency has been read on an official Ministry of Education source, so none is published here. Check moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation channel, and treat any page quoting an IB number without that citation with suspicion. Equivalency is also not a service IB Gram performs, influences or guarantees; it is a government process and the official channel is the only one that can confirm your child's position.

On route choice, the honest answer is to read the requirement for the specific programme rather than the general advice. Engineering, mathematics and most physics degrees expect Analysis and Approaches, frequently at Higher Level; business, economics, psychology and many design routes accept Applications and Interpretation. Some UAE universities state a preference and some do not, and the admissions page for the named programme is the only source worth acting on. Nothing about tutoring is required for equivalency or admission, and anyone telling you otherwise is selling urgency.
