faqs.question: What exactly is MYP eAssessment and does my child have to sit it?
faqs.answer: MYP eAssessment is the IB's externally assessed route to the IB MYP Certificate, taken in MYP Year 5 at roughly 15 or 16. It combines two-hour on-screen examinations in four subject groups plus interdisciplinary learning, externally moderated ePortfolios in four others, and the compulsory Personal Project. Whether your child sits it is a school decision, not a parental one. Some schools enter every Year 5 candidate for the full certificate, some enter individual course results only, and some do not use eAssessment at all. Ask the MYP coordinator which applies to your child's year group, and ask early: registration closes months before the session.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the May session should MYP eAssessment preparation start?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on which component you mean, which is why one answer misleads. ePortfolio subjects need support from the start of Year 5, roughly 36 weeks out, because the grade is decided by evidence produced in terms one and two and nothing added after the school's upload date counts. The Personal Project needs a journal habit from about week 34. On-screen examinations respond well to an eight to ten week block, so starting there in the spring term is reasonable rather than late. If you are reading this at 12 weeks, the on-screen components and final report polish are what remain movable.

faqs.question: Which MYP subjects are examined on screen and which are submitted as an ePortfolio?
faqs.answer: On-screen examinations cover language and literature, individuals and societies, sciences and mathematics, plus a separate interdisciplinary examination drawing on two subject groups. Each runs two hours with media-rich unseen stimulus. ePortfolios cover language acquisition, arts, design and physical and health education, and are coursework portfolios moderated externally against the subject-group criteria. The Personal Project is moderated separately and is compulsory. The split matters because the two halves reward different preparation: timed rehearsal on screen for the first group, documentation discipline across months for the second. Confirm which ePortfolio subject your child is entered for before registration closes, since it cannot be swapped afterwards.

faqs.question: What does my child need to be awarded the IB MYP Certificate?
faqs.answer: The certificate is awarded on eight results, with a required points total, a minimum grade in each result, and a satisfactory record of Service as Action recorded by the school. The eight cover the five on-screen components, two ePortfolios and the Personal Project. We deliberately do not print the exact threshold here, because the IB updates its requirements by session and a number copied from a tutoring page is worth nothing. Your school's MYP coordinator works from the current handbook for the session your child is entered for, and that is the one source worth relying on. Ask for it in writing early in Year 5.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project without breaking IB academic honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can help narrow a goal to something achievable, teach the habit of dated weekly journal entries, teach research skills and referencing, explain report structure, and explain what the academic honesty form the student signs actually commits them to. A tutor can give feedback on what the student has already produced. A tutor cannot supply content, draft sections, rewrite the report or edit it to a level the student could not reach alone. Assessed work must be the student's own. The consequence of crossing that line falls on the student's result, which is why we state it before booking.

faqs.question: How is a two-hour on-screen examination different from a paper one?
faqs.answer: The format changes what can be asked. Stimulus can be audio, video, interactive data or a long scrollable source set, so the reading load cannot be skimmed the way a printed insert can. Answers are typed, which rewards students who structure a response before typing. There is no margin for annotation unless a tool is provided. Practically, three things matter: read the whole task set before answering anything, allocate minutes per task in advance, and build stamina with full-length timed sittings on the real interface. A student who has only done 40-minute class tests runs out of concentration at task four.

faqs.question: What do MYP criteria A to D mean on my child's report card?
faqs.answer: Each subject group is assessed against four criteria, marked out of eight each, giving 32 raw marks that convert to a grade from 1 to 7. Criterion A is knowing and understanding. B is inquiring and analysing, investigating or organising depending on subject. C is communicating or thinking critically. D is the application criterion, such as applying mathematics in real-world contexts. The 1 to 7 grade hides which criterion is weak, so a grade 4 could be band 6 on knowledge and band 2 on application. Ask the school for the criterion-level breakdown; it turns a grade into something a tutoring plan can act on.

faqs.question: What does MYP-level tutoring cost per hour in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Market rates observed in October 2026 run roughly as follows. Budget online support, usually university students, AED 45 to 150: EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65, Tutopiya from AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors online, AED 150 to 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home visits, AED 180 to 500, including travel. IB specialists, AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270 and BartyED at AED 650 at the premium end. Those are market figures, not ours. We start with a 30-minute trial lesson at no charge and quote for the specific subject group afterwards.

faqs.question: My child's school enters course results rather than the full certificate. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It changes what your child leaves Year 5 holding, and it is worth understanding rather than worrying about. Individual course results confirm externally assessed achievement in named subject groups; the full certificate additionally requires the points total across eight results, the Personal Project and Service as Action. Neither is a school-leaving qualification for UAE equivalency purposes, so the practical difference is mostly about internal placement into Diploma subject levels and about how a transfer school reads the record. Ask the coordinator which route the school uses and why, and ask what it means for higher level placement in Year 12.

faqs.question: Should a UAE student sit MYP eAssessment or move to IGCSE for Year 11?
faqs.answer: The useful question is which assessment model fits the student, not which qualification is harder. MYP puts four of eight results into externally moderated portfolios, so it suits students who document their process and work steadily across a year. IGCSE is predominantly examination-based, which suits students who perform under timed conditions and struggle to sustain coursework. The administrative calendars also differ: Cambridge closes final entries months before its June and November papers, and those two are the only series a UAE candidate can sit. For MYP, the equivalent risk is registration locking the subject list early. Discuss it with both the MYP and DP coordinators.

faqs.question: If my child finished at MYP Year 5, what would the certificate be worth for a UAE application?
faqs.answer: On its own, very little, and that is by design rather than a defect. Equivalency is assessed on the qualification a student leaves school with, which for an MYP student means the IB Diploma, or IGCSE and A-Levels if the family changes track. On the British route the published requirement is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from those five, plus one A-Level at E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. We do not publish an IB points threshold because we have not read one on the Ministry's own pages. Check moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation authority directly.

faqs.question: How do Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies fit around MYP Year 5?
faqs.answer: They sit on top of it. These subjects are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social studies, with combined classes prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and additional or different content needs prior Ministry of Education permission. For a family this means the Year 5 timetable is fuller than a British Year 11 equivalent, so one weekly tutoring subject is realistic and three is not. Plan the load accordingly rather than adding sessions.

faqs.question: Can MYP sessions move to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most families they should. School days shorten during Ramadan and afternoon concentration drops, so an after-school slot that worked in January often produces very little. Post-Iftar sessions from around 20:30 tend to work better, and because everything is scheduled in Gulf Standard Time a tutor based elsewhere simply teaches inside your evening. Two further scheduling points matter in the UAE: half-terms do not line up with the UK calendar, so a revision block planned on UK dates will collide with a school holiday, and the May session sits in the final term when the school's own deadlines are heaviest.

faqs.question: What can be done about a weak ePortfolio subject six weeks before submission?
faqs.answer: Less than parents hope, and that is the honest answer rather than a sales one. Six weeks out the usual gap is missing process evidence, and process evidence cannot be created retrospectively without crossing into misrepresentation. What can still be done: check every existing piece against its criterion and band, make sure annotation and referencing are complete, and make sure nothing strong has been left out of the submission by accident. If a development stage genuinely does not exist, the realistic move is to protect the on-screen components instead and to start the next portfolio subject properly if there is one.

faqs.question: Does MYP eAssessment actually prepare a student for the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the gap is predictable. MYP builds inquiry, documentation and the habit of working to published criteria, all of which transfer directly to Diploma internal assessment. What does not transfer is examination technique against a mark scheme: Diploma papers reward a different kind of precision from criterion-marked tasks, and students who relied on strong portfolios in Year 5 often find their first Year 12 papers a shock. The useful window is the weeks straight after results, when higher and standard level placements are still reversible. Reading the Year 5 criterion profile against proposed subject levels takes two sessions and prevents a two-year problem.

faqs.question: Who registers my child for eAssessment, and what happens if we miss the deadline?
faqs.answer: The school registers candidates with the IB; parents cannot enter a child independently. The subject list, including which ePortfolio subject your child takes, locks at registration, typically around 20 to 22 weeks before the session. If the deadline passes with the wrong entry on it, the options are limited to what the school can negotiate and are rarely good. Two practical steps: confirm in writing at the start of Year 5 which subject groups your child is entered for, and check that the ePortfolio subject matches the one they have actually been producing evidence in all year. Mismatches usually surface far too late.

ib-myp-eassessment-preparation.closingHeading: Start from the week you are in, not from the subject list
ib-myp-eassessment-preparation.closingBody: The useful first move is not choosing a tutor. It is counting the weeks to the session and working out which of the eight results can still change. If that number is above 30, the ePortfolios and the Personal Project are where the leverage sits and a single weekly subject is enough. If it is under 12, the on-screen components are the whole game and narrowing matters more than adding. Tell us the session, the school and which components are open, and we will say what is worth doing and what is not. Lessons are live one-to-one video in Gulf Standard Time, starting with one 30-minute trial lesson at no charge and no card details taken.

intro.heading: The MYP is marked differently from everything around it
paragraphs: The Middle Years Programme is marked against criteria, not percentages. Every MYP subject carries four criteria, A to D, and each is marked out of eight. The school adds the four together, lands on a figure out of 32, and converts that to the 1 to 7 grade a parent sees on the report. That is why a child can revise hard, know the content, and still come home with a 4. The marks were not lost on knowledge; they were lost on the criterion the task was actually assessing. An IB MYP home tutor in the UAE who cannot name that criterion is guessing.

Around that sits a school system with two rulebooks. Your child's school answers to an emirate authority — KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah — or, in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, to the federal Ministry of Education. The Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, according to u.ae. The IB writes the MYP. The emirate decides how a school may run it and report it. A tutoring plan that ignores the second half of that sentence keeps colliding with it.

There is a third layer most MYP families meet in the second week of term. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required them in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. They take real timetable minutes beside the eight MYP subject groups, they are reported on their own terms, and their content is fixed: using different or additional material without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited. An MYP child in Dubai is therefore carrying more subjects than the programme model shows, and the squeeze usually lands on Design, Arts and the Personal Project.

IB Gram matches that child with one teacher and runs the work as one-to-one MYP tuition online, over live video, on Gulf Standard Time. Nobody is sent to a UAE address; home visits are a service we run only in India. The gain is not convenience, it is supply. An MYP Sciences teacher who has marked Criterion B several hundred times is a different hire from the nearest available graduate with a science degree. Every AED figure on this page belongs to the market, attributed and dated. MYP Personal Project support is process coaching, and the student writes every word of the report.

This page is built around the system rather than the pitch: what the criteria are, where the marks go, which authority decides what, what the UAE market charges, and what an MYP year looks like counted against a real school calendar.

ib-myp-home-tutor.programmesIntro: The MYP is five years long and does not feel like one programme from end to end. MYP 1 is a child learning what a criterion is; MYP 5 is a candidate running a Personal Project and, in some UAE schools, sitting on-screen examinations. These four phases ask for different teaching, which is why we match by phase and not simply by subject.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, the first three years
programmes.description: Students arrive from the PYP or from a national curriculum and meet criterion marking for the first time. Each subject reports four criteria out of eight, so a strong content recall can still produce a 4 if the investigation, the communication or the real-life application was thin. Interdisciplinary units begin. In MYP 3 most schools split mathematics into Standard and Extended, which is the first decision with a Diploma consequence attached.
programmes.countryNote: In UAE schools this phase collides with the mandatory Ministry subjects, which arrive on the timetable at the same age. Families moving in from CBSE or an American system notice it most: the content load feels familiar, the marking does not. Ask the school for the assessment policy and for the subject-group criteria it reports, in writing, during the first term rather than at the first parents' evening.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme, the final two years
programmes.description: Subject choices narrow, the criteria tighten, and the gap between a 5 and a 7 stops being about effort. Criterion D does most of the damage here: applying mathematics in real-life contexts, reflecting on the impacts of science, thinking critically in Individuals and Societies. MYP 5 also carries the Personal Project and, where the school uses it, MYP eAssessment in the May session.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools enter MYP 5 students for a small number of IGCSEs alongside the programme, which puts Cambridge or Pearson entry deadlines into an MYP year. Ask which board, how many subjects and who makes the entry. Those deadlines sit months before the papers and the school owns them, so a family that finds out in February has already lost the decision.

programmes.name: The Personal Project
programmes.description: An independent piece of work with three criteria — Planning, Applying skills, Reflecting — each marked out of eight, moderated externally by the IB. The product matters less than the evidence: a process journal that shows decisions being made, success criteria that can actually be tested, and a report that reflects honestly on what went wrong. Most lost marks are evidential, not creative.
programmes.countryNote: This is where UAE families are most often sold something they should refuse. Essay services in this market advertise finished coursework, and one competitor page in our research sells completed Internal Assessments outright. A tutor may teach what a criterion wants and ask the questions that expose a weak success criterion. A tutor who drafts, rewrites or finishes any part of it has put the student's whole MYP record at risk.

programmes.name: What the MYP feeds into
programmes.description: The Diploma Programme reuses MYP habits and then raises the technical floor. Analysis and Approaches expects algebraic fluency the MYP never demanded; the science Internal Assessment expects uncertainty handling that Criterion C only gestured at; Language A expects comparative work against a conceptual question. Students who were comfortable 6s in MYP 5 often see a 4 in the first DP1 report and read it as failure rather than recalibration.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP 5 to DP1 transition is the single most common reason a UAE family contacts us about a 15-year-old. The useful window is the summer between the two years, and the work is specific — not revision, but the handful of technical gaps listed further down this page. Most families need between six and fourteen weeks of one-to-one time, depending on the subject group.

ib-myp-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: The MYP has eight subject groups and an interdisciplinary strand, and every one of them reports four criteria. What follows is what each group actually assesses and where UAE students lose the marks — which is rarely where parents expect.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Criteria: Analysing, Organizing, Producing text, Using language. Marks go missing on Analysing, where students summarise a text instead of examining how the writer's choices create effect. Criterion D rewards register and accuracy, which is where strong readers who write loosely stall at a 5.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria: Listening, Reading, Speaking, Writing — the only group where the four criteria are the four skills. UAE schools place students in a phase rather than a year, so a child can sit in MYP 4 in Phase 2 French. Knowing the phase is the first thing a tutor needs.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria: Knowing and understanding, Investigating, Communicating, Thinking critically. Criterion D is the usual gap: students describe sources rather than evaluate their origin, purpose and limitation. Criterion B asks for a research question narrow enough to answer, which few students have been taught to write.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.levels: Integrated, then Biology, Chemistry and Physics
subjects.description: Criteria: Knowing and understanding, Inquiring and designing, Processing and evaluating, Reflecting on the impacts of science. MYP Sciences Criterion B is where UAE students bleed marks — a hypothesis with no scientific reasoning behind it, and variables that are listed rather than controlled.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Criteria: Knowing and understanding, Investigating patterns, Communicating, Applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Criterion B asks students to find a general rule and justify it; Criterion D asks them to defend a model's assumptions. Both are taught less than they are assessed.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria: Inquiring and analysing, Developing ideas, Creating the solution, Evaluating. The build is the part students enjoy and the smallest part of the mark. Specifications that cannot be tested and a plan with no evidence of following it are the two recurring losses.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria: Investigating, Developing, Creating or performing, Evaluating. The process portfolio carries more weight than the final piece, and students who work quickly often cannot show development. Evaluating against their own stated intentions is the criterion most often left half-written.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria: Knowing and understanding, Planning for performance, Applying and performing, Reflecting and improving performance. Two of the four criteria are written work, which surprises sporty students and their parents. A training plan with no measurable targets loses Criterion B outright.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Criteria: Evaluating, Synthesizing, Reflecting. Assessed separately from the subject groups and often the lowest line on a UAE report, because nobody owns the teaching of it. Synthesising two disciplines into one explanation is a skill, not a by-product.

subjects.name: Arabic and the Ministry subjects
subjects.description: Arabic as a first or additional language, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run alongside the programme under KHDA mandatory subjects rules. They are reported on the school's scheme, not against MYP subject-group criteria, and their content is set by the Ministry of Education.

ib-myp-home-tutor.regionsTitle: Where MYP families are, emirate by emirate
ib-myp-home-tutor.regionsIntro: MYP provision is not spread evenly across the UAE. Dubai and Abu Dhabi hold most of the IB continuum schools; the northern emirates have a handful, and a thinner pool of experienced MYP teachers to go with them. Online delivery is what flattens that difference, which is the honest reason we work this way.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: 227 private schools and 17 curricula in 2024-25, with International Baccalaureate programmes accounting for 7% of the roll (Dubai Media Office, January 2025). Most UAE MYP continuum schools sit here, and so does most of the competition for their teachers.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK licenses and accredits the private schools here. Its professional-ethics rules for school staff reach into paid private tutoring, which changes who may legitimately teach your child outside school hours.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK, not KHDA — a point families moving from Dubai get wrong. Fewer MYP cohorts, so an Al Ain family looking for a Design or Phase 4 Spanish teacher is almost always looking outside the city.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Assessment-method approval is the clause that matters to an MYP family: how the school reports criteria is not purely the school's call.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority. Fewer MYP places, and most enquiries here involve a child commuting to a Sharjah or Dubai school.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education and, like Sharjah, approves curricula and assessment methods. A new MYP cohort needs that approval before it can run, which is why provision grows slowly here.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education supervision and very little MYP provision on the east coast. Online one-to-one teaching is not a convenience here; for an MYP 4 Extended mathematics student it is often the only route to a specialist.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under Ministry of Education supervision, and the emirate named by none of the competitor pages in our research. Families usually travel to Sharjah for an IB school and do everything else over video.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai holds the densest group of IB continuum schools in the country, which is also why its MYP teachers are the most heavily recruited. Seven new private schools open for 2026-27 — four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate — adding 16,846 places (KHDA, 2026).

ADEK territory, with a smaller MYP cohort than Dubai and a tighter staffing market. Its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar paid tutoring of students at a teacher's own school, so the convenient option is often the one to decline.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.note: Sharjah, Ajman and Ras Al Khaimah have IB provision, but a family looking for a specific MYP subject group rarely finds a specialist within driving distance. This is the cluster where online delivery changes what is available rather than merely how it arrives.

ib-myp-home-tutor.modesIntro: Three ways MYP families use us, and they are not interchangeable. A criterion problem, a Personal Project problem and a transition problem need different lesson shapes, different session lengths and different numbers of weeks.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one on a criterion cycle
modes.description: One 60-minute lesson a week, built around the criterion the next summative task will report. The teacher works from the school's own task sheet and rubric, screen-shared, so the student practises on a parallel task rather than on the live one. Progress is measured in criterion bands, not in topics covered.

modes.description: Short, spaced sessions across MYP 5 rather than a block before the deadline. The teacher reads what the student has written and asks the questions a moderator would: can this success criterion be tested, does the journal show the decision being made, does the reflection admit anything. MYP Personal Project support stops at the questions.

modes.description: Six to fourteen weeks over the summer, aimed at the specific technical gaps between an MYP subject group and the Diploma course it feeds. Usually two subjects, usually mathematics plus one science or one language. The point is to arrive in DP1 without the first six weeks being spent on algebra the MYP never required.

sections.heading: What a UAE parent is actually asking for when they search for an MYP tutor
paragraphs: The search term is "home tutor" and the need underneath it is almost never geography. In the enquiries we take, the parent has a report in front of them with a 4 or a 5 beside a subject their child says they understand, and no explanation of the gap. That is a criterion problem, and it is solved by a teacher who knows the subject group's rubric, not by someone who can reach your community before 5pm.

The second thing behind the search is phase. An MYP 1 child who has just left the PYP needs to be taught what a criterion is. An MYP 3 child is choosing between Standard and Extended mathematics. An MYP 5 child is running a Personal Project and may be entered for a couple of IGCSEs on the side. Those are three different hires, and a provider who matches on subject alone will send the same person to all three.

So we answer the search honestly. One-to-one MYP tuition online, over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, with the teacher chosen for the subject group and the phase. Nobody travels to a UAE address. A family searching for an IB MYP tutor in Dubai and a family in Fujairah doing the same search get the same shortlist from us, which is the practical difference an MYP online tutor makes in a country where the middle-years teacher pool is concentrated in two emirates. The table below maps the MYP year onto the school-year labels UAE schools actually print on reports, because British and American labelled schools in the same emirate number the same child differently, and a provider who asks for the year rather than the MYP phase will match on the wrong information.

sections.heading: How an MYP grade is built: four criteria, eight marks each, 32 in total
paragraphs: Every MYP subject group reports four criteria, labelled A to D, and each is marked out of eight against published descriptors. The school combines the four into a total out of 32 and converts that total to the 1 to 7 grade on the report. The conversion boundaries are published in the MYP's general grade descriptors and schools restate them in their own assessment policy, which is the document to ask for — the boundaries are the same across subjects, which is why a 24 in Sciences and a 24 in Design are the same grade.

Two consequences follow, and neither is obvious from a report card. First, criteria are not averaged across the year in most schools: the latest and best evidence against each criterion carries, so one weak task in September does not sink a June grade, and one strong task does not rescue a criterion never retested. Second, a single weak criterion costs the same as a weak subject. A student at 7, 7, 7 and 2 is on 23 out of 32 — a grade 5 — while a flat 6, 6, 6, 6 is 24 and a grade 6.

That arithmetic is the whole case for criterion-led teaching. The 32 MYP criterion marks tell you exactly where the hour should go, and they are printed on the report most parents file without reading. The table lists the four criteria for each subject group, as the current MYP subject guides name them, so you can match the letters on the report to what the task was testing.

sections.heading: Where MYP marks are actually lost, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The pattern across UAE MYP cohorts is consistent enough to predict. Criterion A, knowing and understanding, is the one students revise for and the one they rarely fail. The losses concentrate in B and D — the investigative criterion and the application criterion — because both assess a skill that is assessed more often than it is taught. A child can be fluent in the content of a Sciences unit and still score 3 on Inquiring and designing because nobody showed them what a controlled variable section looks like when it is written properly.

In mathematics the losses are specific. Criterion B asks for a pattern, a general rule and a justification of that rule; students produce the first two and stop. Criterion D asks them to apply mathematics in a real-life context and then comment on whether the model's assumptions hold; students produce an answer with no reflection on the assumptions. In Individuals and Societies, Criterion D asks for evaluation of a source's origin, purpose and limitations, and what arrives is description with an adjective attached.

Command terms are the other recurring loss, and they cut across every group. "Describe", "explain", "analyse" and "evaluate" each instruct a marker to reward something different, and the descriptor language mirrors them. A student who answers an "evaluate" task with a very good "explain" answer is capped, however much they know. This is diagnosable in one lesson from a marked task and a rubric, which is why we ask for both before the first session rather than for a general account of how things are going.

sections.heading: The Personal Project, the Community Project and the line a paid tutor must not cross
paragraphs: The Personal Project is assessed against three criteria — Planning, Applying skills, Reflecting — each marked out of eight, and it is externally moderated. The Community Project, where a school runs it in MYP 3 or 4, works the same way at a smaller scale. Both are student-owned by design, which makes them the components a UAE family is most likely to be offered illegitimate help with. Our research found a page in this market selling completed Internal Assessments outright at AED 3,750; the same business model reaches down into MYP coursework.

What a tutor may do is substantial and worth paying for. Explain what each criterion rewards and what its mark allocation is. Ask whether a success criterion can actually be tested, which is the question that most improves a weak project. Teach the student how to keep a process journal that shows a decision being made rather than a diary of activity. Read a reflection and say, without touching it, that it does not yet admit anything went wrong — which is where Criterion C marks live.

What a tutor must never do is produce any of it. No drafting, no rewriting, no editing to completion, no proofreading a report into shape, no building any part of the product. Your child's coordinator will ask them to declare outside support, and a truthful declaration of criterion coaching is routine. A declaration that cannot be made truthfully is a malpractice investigation, and the sanction lands on the student, not on the person who was paid. Keep a written record of what each session covered; it makes the declaration easy.

sections.heading: Which authority licensed your child's MYP school, and what it reaches into
paragraphs: Private schools in the UAE are regulated emirate by emirate, and the differences are not cosmetic. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi, including Al Ain. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah and the Department of Knowledge does so in Ras Al Khaimah, while the Ministry of Education plays the supervisory role in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. All of that is stated on u.ae.

For an MYP family the operative clause is what each body approves rather than what it inspects. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Assessment methods are how the school converts criterion marks into the grade on your child's report. Federally, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations — which is the rule behind every emirate's mandatory-subject requirement.

Two practical consequences. An inspection report is a document about teaching quality across phases, so read the middle-years judgements rather than the Diploma headline a school markets on; a school with strong Diploma outcomes can still be weak in MYP 4 Design. And a tutoring business with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which is a specific thing with initial approval, a six-month completion window and annual renewal. IB Gram holds no regulator approval, accreditation or licence of any kind, and any provider telling you otherwise should be asked for the permit number.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies beside the MYP timetable
paragraphs: The MYP has eight subject groups. A Dubai MYP student carries those plus the Ministry subjects, because Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required them in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year — April 2026 for schools whose year starts in April. KHDA calculates the required instructional time in 40-minute lesson units, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that no mandatory-subject lesson runs under 25 minutes.

The organisational rules are specific, and they explain something parents often query. Schools must run separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies; combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; the school's licensed-curriculum language is used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic must hold appropriate KHDA approval.

This changes what outside help can honestly offer. For the mandatory subjects, using any different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited — so a tutor works through the school's own material, practising reading, script and written answers, and does not import a parallel syllabus. These subjects are reported on the school's scheme rather than against MYP subject-group criteria, which is why they appear on a UAE report in a different format from the eight groups and are easy to overlook until the grade arrives.

sections.heading: MYP 5 into DP1: the gaps that actually bite
paragraphs: The MYP is not light preparation for the Diploma, but it is differently shaped, and the mismatch is technical rather than general. MYP mathematics rewards investigation and modelling; Analysis and Approaches opens with algebraic manipulation done without a calculator. MYP Sciences rewards designing an inquiry; the Diploma Internal Assessment expects uncertainty propagation and significant-figure discipline from the first draft. MYP Language and Literature rewards analysis of a single text; Language A expects comparison driven by a conceptual question. None of that is a step in difficulty so much as a step in specificity.

Which is why the first DP1 report shocks families who had a comfortable MYP 5. A student who held 6s across four criteria can see a 4 in November of DP1 and read it as collapse, when what has happened is recalibration against a different scale. The useful response is not more hours; it is the right eight hours on the named gap. A student whose MYP Extended mathematics profile shows a strong Criterion B and a weak Criterion A almost always needs fluency work, not more investigation work.

The summer between MYP 5 and DP1 is the window, and the MYP 5 to DP1 transition is the most common reason a UAE family with a 15-year-old contacts us. Six to fourteen weeks, usually two subjects, built from the student's own criterion profile rather than a generic bridging course. sections.heading: MYP eAssessment, school-based results, and what the Ministry looks at later
paragraphs: MYP eAssessment is optional, and a great many UAE schools do not use it. Where a school does, MYP 5 students sit on-screen examinations in subjects such as Language and Literature, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics and interdisciplinary learning, and submit externally moderated ePortfolios in Language Acquisition, Arts, Design and Physical and Health Education, with the Personal Project moderated alongside. Where a school does not, MYP 5 results are school-based and internally standardised. Ask which, because it changes the whole shape of the final MYP year.

Sessions run in May and in November. We do not publish IB session or results dates on this site: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so every date in circulation is second-hand, and an MYP calendar built on a wrong date costs a family more than a missing one. Your child's MYP coordinator holds the real dates, and any certificate requirement — the number of results needed and the minimum total — should be confirmed with them or on ibo.org rather than taken from a tutoring page, including this one.

The thing to understand about Ministry of Education equivalency is that the MYP does not feed it. Equivalency is built later, from terminal certificates. On the British track, as reported in July 2026, a student must show five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education not counted among the five, plus one A-level at no less than E or two AS-levels at the same grade. One competitor page in this market publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong. No IB points figure appears in that source, so we publish none — verify on moe.gov.ae before you plan around any number.

sections.heading: What MYP tutoring costs in the UAE market, and who publishes what
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. The figures below are the market's, read in October 2026, with the source named — they are not IB Gram's price list, and nothing on this page is an offer. Middle-years rates generally sit a band below Diploma rates, which is the one piece of good news in the table: an MYP family is buying at AED 150–300 an hour where a Diploma Higher Level family is quoted AED 200–450 and upwards.

Monthly packages are where the market gets confusing. Published UAE offers include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599–1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table estimates AED 240–600 a month for a weekly hour at the budget end, AED 600–1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000–2,000 or more for specialist exam-year work. Compare on cost per hour of teaching, not on the monthly headline, and check what a package does with an unused session.

Set it beside the school fee to see the real proportion. Dubai had 387,441 private-school students across 227 schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, and KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no fee increase for 2026-27 under Dubai's second economic incentives package. For most MYP families the tutoring decision is a few thousand dirhams a year against a fee that is holding flat — which argues for buying fewer, better-targeted hours rather than a standing weekly commitment in every weak subject.

sections.heading: A tutor travelling to a UAE address, against one-to-one MYP tuition online
paragraphs: The honest version of this comparison starts with what the visiting model is good at. A teacher in the room reads a 12-year-old's body language better over video, can take a pen to a page without screen-sharing it, and removes the question of whether the child is actually working. For MYP 1 and MYP 2 students with an attention problem rather than a criterion problem, that is a genuine advantage and worth saying out loud.

What it costs is a two-hour minimum and a tutor pool defined by driving distance. Market rates of AED 180–500 an hour carry travel inside them, and the economics push providers towards longer sessions than a middle-years child can use well. The deeper cost is selection: in an emirate with a limited MYP cohort, the set of people who can reach your community before 5pm and also know what Sciences Criterion B wants is often empty. An Al Ain or Fujairah family looking for MYP Extended mathematics is rarely choosing between candidates at all.

IB Gram resolves that by not competing on proximity. Lessons run over live video, 45 or 60 minutes, with the school's rubric and task sheet shared on screen and a written summary afterwards. Home visits are a service we run only in India, and no UAE page of ours will tell you otherwise. For an MYP 1 attention problem a visiting teacher may genuinely be the better buy, and we would rather say that than sell you the wrong thing; for a criterion problem in any of the eight subject groups, the teacher's knowledge of the rubric decides the outcome and their postcode does not. The table sets the two models side by side on the things a parent is actually weighing.

sections.heading: The MYP year counted against a UAE school calendar
paragraphs: An MYP year has its own rhythm and it does not match the exam-season rhythm parents know from the Diploma. There is no single terminal series to count backwards from unless the school uses eAssessment or enters MYP 5 students for IGCSEs. What there is instead is a sequence of summative tasks, each reporting specific criteria, plus the Personal Project running underneath MYP 5 from the autumn. Starting support in April because a report was poor in March is starting after the criteria that produced it were already reported.

Where board examinations do enter an MYP year, the published deadlines are months ahead of the papers and the school owns them. The useful exercise is to count a Cambridge June series backwards. The papers themselves sit in a window that opens in late spring and runs into June; final entries close months before that, in the second half of the school year; and the statement of entry that confirms every subject, paper and timetable zone reaches the family earlier still. Cambridge does not publish one universal entry date, because every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and it says it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. So ask the school for its zone and its statement of entry rather than working from a date read anywhere else, this page included, and check the subject list on that statement line by line. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE is easier to pin down: it runs May/June and November series, the November 2026 timetable finished on 19 November 2026, and June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026. In the UAE those are the sittings on the table, Cambridge June with November as the resit route; the February and March sitting is one Cambridge offers to India.

Ramadan moves revision rather than removing it. Evening sessions after Iftar work better than tired afternoon ones, and in practice families shift a weekly slot by two or three hours for the month and keep the cadence. School holidays are the other planning point: the summer between MYP 5 and DP1 is the most productive block in the five years, and the winter break is when a Personal Project either gets ahead or quietly stalls.

process.title: Send the report and one marked task
process.description: Not a description of how things are going. A recent report showing the criterion letters, plus one marked summative task with its rubric. That pair tells an MYP teacher in ten minutes what three conversations would not, and it is enough to decide whether tutoring is even the right purchase.

process.title: A 15-minute call about phase, not subject
process.description: Which MYP year, which school and emirate, whether mathematics has split into Standard and Extended, whether the school uses eAssessment, and whether any IGCSEs are being sat alongside MYP 5. We also ask what the school has already put in place, because paying for a repeat of it is common.

process.title: Matched to a subject group, not a subject
process.description: An MYP Sciences teacher, a Language Acquisition teacher who works at the right phase, a Design teacher who has moderated Criterion A. If nobody with that profile is free in the week you want to start, we say so and give a date rather than sending whoever is available.

process.title: A first lesson with a written outcome
process.description: The teacher works from your child's own rubric and task, and the summary afterwards names the criteria to target, the number of weeks it is likely to take, and anything that does not need paid help at all. You decide after reading it, and the conditions of the first lesson are stated before it is booked.

process.title: Review against criterion bands, not vibes
process.description: Every four to six weeks we look at the criterion letters on the next reported task. Going up on B and D is the point. If the bands are flat after a fair run, the match or the diagnosis was wrong, and changing teacher is the right answer rather than adding hours.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the criterion, not the postcode
whyPoints.description: The constraint in a visiting arrangement is drive time; the constraint in an MYP problem is whether the teacher knows what Inquiring and designing rewards. Teaching over live video removes the first constraint entirely, which is the only reason we can solve the second one in Fujairah as readily as in Dubai.

whyPoints.title: The school's own material, on screen
whyPoints.description: Lessons run from your child's rubric, task sheet and unit planner rather than a generic worksheet pack. For the Ministry subjects this is also a rule: using different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is prohibited, so a tutor who imports a parallel syllabus is working outside it.

whyPoints.title: A stated line on coursework
whyPoints.description: Criterion coaching, questions and feedback on the student's own work. No drafting, no editing to completion, no proofreading into shape, and a written record of each session so the academic-honesty declaration your child signs is easy to make truthfully.

No invented statistics, no self-awarded ratings, no claim of regulator approval we do not hold.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what we do not have
whyPoints.description: No UAE office. No regulator licence. No IB session dates, because ibo.org cannot be checked automatically and a wrong date is worse than a missing one. If no MYP specialist for your subject group is free, you get a date instead of a substitute, and you can wait or go elsewhere.

faqs.question: What is the MYP, and how is it different from the Diploma my older child sits?
faqs.answer: The Middle Years Programme covers five years, roughly ages 11 to 16, and sits between the PYP and the Diploma. The difference that matters day to day is the marking. The Diploma reports examination grades and internally assessed components; the MYP reports four criteria per subject, each out of eight, and converts the total out of 32 into a 1 to 7 grade. So a Diploma parent reads a percentage and an MYP parent reads criterion letters. The same child can look strong in one system and middling in the other without anything about them having changed.

faqs.question: My son is in MYP 3 and his report shows letters instead of percentages. What do they mean?
faqs.answer: Those letters are the four assessment criteria for each subject group, A to D, and each is marked out of eight against published descriptors. In Sciences, for example, A is knowing and understanding, B is inquiring and designing, C is processing and evaluating, and D is reflecting on the impacts of science. The letters tell you precisely what was being tested, which a percentage never does. A 7 on A beside a 3 on B is not a weak scientist; it is a student who has never been taught to write a controlled-variables section properly.

faqs.question: How do 32 criterion marks turn into the 1 to 7 grade on an MYP report?
faqs.answer: The school adds the four criterion marks, each out of eight, to a total out of 32, then applies the MYP general grade boundaries to convert that total to a grade from 1 to 7. The boundaries are the same across every subject group, which is why totals are comparable between Design and Mathematics. Schools restate them in their own assessment policy, so ask for that document rather than relying on a summary. The arithmetic matters: 7, 7, 7, 2 is 23 marks and a lower grade than a flat 6, 6, 6, 6 on 24.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Personal Project without breaking IB academic-honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the useful help is narrower than most families expect. A teacher may explain what criteria A to C reward and how the marks are allocated, ask whether a success criterion can actually be tested, show what a process journal entry needs to evidence, and say that a reflection does not yet admit anything went wrong. A teacher may not draft, rewrite, edit to completion, proofread into shape or build any part of the product. Your child declares outside support to their coordinator, so keep a written record of what each session covered.

faqs.question: Does the MYP produce a certificate the UAE Ministry of Education will attest?
faqs.answer: No. Equivalency is built from terminal certificates, not from middle-years results. On the British track, as reported in July 2026, the Ministry looks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic Education excluded from that count, plus one A-level at no less than E or two AS-levels at the same grade. No IB points figure appears in that source, so we publish none. Verify current requirements on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate before planning around any number.

faqs.question: Which MYP subject groups do UAE families ask for help with most often?
faqs.answer: Mathematics first, usually at the point where MYP 3 splits into Standard and Extended and the route decision arrives before the family understands its Diploma consequences. Sciences second, almost always on Criterion B. Then Language and Literature, where strong readers lose Criterion A marks by summarising rather than analysing. Design and the interdisciplinary units generate fewer enquiries and more surprise, because both are commonly the lowest line on a report and neither has an obvious owner in most school timetables.

faqs.question: Is MYP mathematics split into Standard and Extended, and which should my child take?
faqs.answer: Most schools split it in MYP 3 or MYP 4. Extended carries additional content and is the usual route into Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches at Diploma level; Standard leads more naturally to Applications and Interpretation. The decision should be made on the criterion profile, not on ambition. A student strong on Criterion A and weak on Criterion B can usually cope with Extended content with support; a student weak on A will find Extended compounds the gap. Ask the school what the movement rules are between the two before choosing.

faqs.question: What does MYP eAssessment involve, and does my child's UAE school even use it?
faqs.answer: It is optional, and many UAE schools do not use it. Where a school does, MYP 5 students sit on-screen examinations in groups such as Language and Literature, Individuals and Societies, Sciences, Mathematics and interdisciplinary learning, and submit externally moderated ePortfolios in Language Acquisition, Arts, Design and Physical and Health Education, with the Personal Project moderated too. Where a school does not, MYP 5 results are school-based and internally standardised. Ask the coordinator directly, because it changes what the final MYP year is actually building towards.

faqs.question: My daughter moves from MYP 5 into DP1 next August. What should we fix first?
faqs.answer: Her criterion profile tells you. For Analysis and Approaches the usual gap is non-calculator algebraic fluency and the language of proof, which takes eight to twelve weeks of weekly one-to-one work. For a science the gap is uncertainty, significant figures and data processing of the kind the Internal Assessment demands. For Language A it is comparative analysis against a conceptual question. Pick two subjects, not five, and use the summer. The first DP1 report often drops a grade against MYP 5, and that is recalibration rather than collapse.

faqs.question: Does my child still take Arabic and Islamic Education inside an MYP timetable?
faqs.answer: In Dubai, yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required them in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. They sit beside the eight MYP subject groups rather than replacing any of them, and KHDA calculates the required time in 40-minute lesson units while advising that no mandatory-subject lesson runs under 25 minutes. They are reported on the school's own scheme, not against MYP subject-group criteria.

faqs.question: Why is the Arabic class split between Arab and non-Arab students at my child's school?
faqs.answer: Because KHDA requires it. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited, since the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; non-Arab students are taught Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education must hold appropriate KHDA approval.

faqs.question: What does an MYP home tutor charge in the UAE, and what does online cost instead?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates for a visiting tutor run AED 180–500 an hour with travel inside the figure, according to the Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, usually with a two-hour minimum. Qualified subject tutors working online are published at AED 150–300, and programme specialists at AED 200–450 and upwards. Monthly offers seen in this market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599–1,799 for four two-hour visits. Those are market figures read in October 2026, not IB Gram's prices; ours are quoted after the first lesson.

faqs.question: Does an MYP tutor need a UAE permit, and how do I check they hold one?
faqs.answer: Individuals giving private lessons in the UAE need the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023. It is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. Ask to see the permit, and check the official route on the MoHRE private tutor licensing service page rather than taking a website's word for it.

faqs.question: Can my child's own MYP teacher at school tutor them privately for a fee?
faqs.answer: In Abu Dhabi, no. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. That is press-reported, so confirm it against the current ADEK policy document. The arrangement is usually a bad idea anyway: the person who sets and marks the assessment should not also be paid to prepare your child for it.

faqs.question: How does Ramadan change when MYP revision actually happens?
faqs.answer: It moves the time of day rather than the amount of work. Families generally shift a weekly slot to after Iftar, where an hour of criterion work lands better than a tired afternoon session during fasting, and keep the same cadence through the month. Because lessons run over live video, moving a slot by two or three hours costs nothing and needs no travel rethink. Plan around it in advance if a summative task or a Personal Project checkpoint falls inside the month, since those dates will not move.

faqs.question: No MYP Design teacher was free when we asked. What happens then?
faqs.answer: You get a date, not a substitute. Design, the interdisciplinary units and Language Acquisition at the higher phases are the thinnest parts of the UAE middle-years pool, and an emirate with a small MYP cohort makes that worse. We will say which week a teacher with the right profile is likely to be free, and you can wait, start with a different subject group, or go elsewhere. Sending a general subject tutor to a Criterion A problem in Design wastes your money and tells us nothing useful about the student.

faqs.question: What does the first lesson cost, and what conditions come with it?
faqs.answer: The first one-to-one lesson is free and runs to 45 or 60 minutes depending on the MYP phase. The conditions are stated before you book: one free lesson per student, with the subject group and phase agreed in advance, no card details taken to arrange it, and the lesson delivered over live video like every other. What you receive afterwards is a written summary naming the criteria to target and an estimate of the weeks involved. There is no obligation to continue, and no fee is charged if you do not.

ib-myp-home-tutor.closingHeading: Start from the report, not from the search term
ib-myp-home-tutor.closingBody: If you are looking for an IB MYP home tutor in the UAE, the fastest useful step is not a shortlist of providers. It is to pull out the latest report, find the criterion letters beside the weak subject, and get hold of one marked task with its rubric. That pair tells an MYP teacher what the problem is, and often tells you that the problem is one criterion rather than a subject. Send it over and we will match a teacher to that subject group and phase, run the first lesson over live video on Gulf Standard Time, and put in writing what we think the work actually is — including when it is less than you feared.

intro.heading: What an MYP hour costs in the UAE, and what it has to buy
paragraphs: IB Middle Years Programme tuition in the UAE is the hardest tutoring purchase a parent makes, for one structural reason: there is usually no external exam to point at. A Diploma family can read a weighting - Paper 1 is worth this much, the internal assessment that much - and work out whether an hour was well spent. An MYP family gets a report card carrying four letters, four numbers out of eight, and a single grade from 1 to 7. Nothing on that page tells you which of the four is the problem, and almost nothing in the tutoring market is priced against it.

So the honest version of the cost question is not what an hour costs. It is what the hour is aimed at. Published rates across the UAE run from roughly AED 33 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 for a premium named tutor, and the spread exists because providers are selling four different things under one word: homework supervision, topic re-teaching, criterion coaching and assessment mentoring. Buy the wrong one and the grade does not move, however many hours you pay for. Buy the right one in MYP 3 and you often need fewer hours in MYP 5.

The MYP is five years long - MYP 1 to MYP 5, roughly ages 11 to 16 - and that length is the whole opportunity. It is also where families waste the most money, because spending concentrates in MYP 5 when a child is suddenly close to the Diploma, and the criteria that were never taught properly in MYP 2 have by then become four years of habit. Criterion D in sciences is reflection on the impacts of science. A thirteen-year-old can learn to do that in six weeks. A sixteen-year-old who has written four years of conclusions without it needs considerably longer, and you will pay the exam-year rate for the privilege.

What drives the hourly number in this market is reasonably predictable. Subject group comes first: mathematics and sciences tutors are plentiful across Dubai and Abu Dhabi, while Design, Arts and the upper phases of Language acquisition are thin, and scarcity prices itself. Format comes second - a tutor who travels absorbs the drive into the rate, which is why in-home figures in the UAE sit at AED 180 to AED 500 while comparable online work sits at AED 150 to AED 300. Then comes seniority, then the year: a February booking in an exam-facing year costs more than the same help in September.

IB Gram delivers all of this as one-to-one online tuition over live video. We do not send a tutor to a UAE address - home visits are a service we run only in India. That is not a limitation dressed up as a feature; it is the reason a family in Ras Al Khaimah can book a Design specialist at all, and the reason an MYP 5 student in Khalifa City is matched on subject group rather than on who happens to live twenty minutes away. The comparison table further down this page makes that case on cost, travel time and tutor pool rather than on adjectives.

Everything priced on this page is market data, collected in October 2026 and attributed to whoever published it. IB Gram's own figure is not a published rate card, because the sensible number depends on subject group, year and how many hours you actually need - which is what the first lesson and a written plan are for.

ib-myp-online-tutor.programmesIntro: An MYP tutor has to know what sits either side of the five middle years, because a UAE family rarely stays in one programme for a decade. Below are the four IB programmes as UAE schools run them, with what each one means for a tutoring plan that starts in the middle years.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups, each assessed against four criteria lettered A to D and each criterion marked out of eight. Teaching is organised around key concepts, related concepts and six global contexts, with a statement of inquiry on every unit. Service as action runs throughout, interdisciplinary units join two subject groups, and MYP 5 carries the Personal Project. The five Approaches to Learning skill categories - thinking, communication, social, self-management and research - are reported separately in many schools.
programmes.countryNote: In UAE schools the year labels collide: MYP 1 is Year 7 in a British-style school and Grade 6 in an American-style one, and MYP 5 is Year 11 or Grade 10 depending on the campus. Ask the coordinator which MYP year your child is in before booking anything, because a tutor planning for Year 11 IGCSE and a tutor planning for MYP 5 criteria are preparing for two different sets of marks.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units, six organising themes and an exhibition in the final year. Assessment is descriptive rather than criterion-lettered, which is why the first MYP report card lands as such a shock: the vocabulary changes from learner-profile language to four criteria with numerical descriptors, and parents who understood the PYP report often cannot read the MYP one.
programmes.countryNote: Several Dubai and Abu Dhabi campuses run the full IB continuum from PYP through to the Diploma, so a child can move from exhibition to MYP 1 without changing schools. The reading and research habits that the exhibition builds map directly onto MYP criterion B in individuals and societies, and a tutor who knows both can use that continuity instead of starting from nothing.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and creativity, activity, service. External examinations carry most of the grade, internal assessment the rest. The jump from criterion-referenced MYP marking to externally examined papers with published weightings is the single steepest transition in the IB, and it happens over one summer.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP to IB Diploma transition is where UAE families spend most urgently and least efficiently. The decisions that matter - extended or standard mathematics in MYP 4 and 5, which sciences to keep, whether Higher Level is realistic - are made while the child is still in the middle years, and a tutor is more useful advising on that fork than rescuing a Higher Level choice made badly twelve months earlier.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Diploma Programme courses combined with a career-related study, a reflective project, a personal and professional skills course, service learning and a language-development requirement. It suits a student who wants IB rigour in two or three academic subjects alongside an applied qualification rather than the full six-subject Diploma.
programmes.countryNote: Fewer UAE campuses offer the Career-related Programme than the Diploma, so it is worth asking in MYP 4 rather than discovering in MYP 5 that your child's school does not run it. For a student whose MYP grades are strong in two subject groups and weak across the rest, it is a route worth raising with the coordinator before the family starts buying hours to force a full Diploma.

ib-myp-online-tutor.subjectsIntro: The MYP has eight subject groups, not a subject list, and each group has its own four criteria with its own names. Below is what each group assesses and where UAE students most often leave marks behind. Tutoring is matched to the group and the criterion letters, not to a topic title from the textbook.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5 · standard and extended in MYP 4 and 5
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B investigating patterns, C communicating, D applying mathematics in real-life contexts. An MYP maths tutor spends most of the useful time on B and D, because A is drillable from a textbook and C and D are where UAE students lose marks: a correct answer with no justified general rule scores badly on B, and a modelling task with no comment on the limitations of the model scores badly on D.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5 · integrated, then biology, chemistry and physics strands
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B inquiring and designing, C processing and evaluating, D reflecting on the impacts of science. An MYP sciences tutor works on the design of a fair test and the evaluation of method, not on content recall. Criterion D is the one almost nobody teaches explicitly, and it is a quarter of the subject's raw marks.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5 · English, Arabic and other school languages
subjects.description: Criteria A analysing, B organizing, C producing text, D using language. Students who read well still lose criterion A marks for retelling the plot instead of analysing the writer's choices, and criterion B marks for an essay with no visible structural plan. Lessons use the school's own set texts, because the command terms differ by task and the task sheet is the mark scheme.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Criteria A listening, B reading, C speaking, D writing, with the standard of each set by the phase rather than the year group. A child can be in MYP 4 and phase 2, or MYP 2 and phase 5. Most UAE families book French, Spanish or Arabic as an additional language here, and the first useful thing a tutor establishes is which phase the school has placed the child in.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B investigating, C communicating, D thinking critically. Criterion B is an actual research process with a question, a plan and an evaluation of sources, and it is marked separately from the content. UAE students who memorise case studies and never practise source evaluation routinely score well on A and badly on B and D.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: Criteria A inquiring and analysing, B developing ideas, C creating the solution, D evaluating. The design cycle is the mark scheme: a beautiful final product with no documented research, no design specification and no testing against that specification scores poorly. Design tutors are among the scarcest in the UAE market, which is exactly where live online matching earns its place.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B developing skills, C thinking creatively, D responding. The process journal carries more marks than students expect, and criterion D asks for a response to the artwork of others as well as to their own practice. Online sessions work on the journal, the artist statement and the exploration of a stimulus rather than on technique drills.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Criteria A knowing and understanding, B planning for performance, C applying and performing, D reflecting and improving performance. Criteria A, B and D are written work, which surprises families who assume the subject is graded on the field. A tutor can genuinely move three of the four criteria without ever watching the child play.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary Units
subjects.levels: MYP 1-5 · two or more subject groups combined
subjects.description: Assessed on its own criteria - evaluating, synthesising and reflecting - rather than on the criteria of either parent subject. Students treat an interdisciplinary unit as a double homework and lose marks for never explaining how the two disciplines together produced an understanding neither could reach alone. One session on that single idea is usually enough.

subjects.name: The MYP Personal Project
subjects.levels: MYP 5 · goal, process journal and report
subjects.description: A self-directed project with a goal, a process journal kept throughout, a product or outcome and a written report, supervised by a school-appointed supervisor and marked against the criteria in the IB guide your school works from. MYP Personal Project support from a tutor is process coaching and feedback on the student's own drafts, and nothing else.

ib-myp-online-tutor.regionsTitle: Where MYP families are, emirate by emirate
ib-myp-online-tutor.regionsIntro: MYP provision is not spread evenly across the UAE, and neither is tutor supply. The regulator changes at the emirate border, the school-run timing changes what hour a session can start, and in four emirates the realistic choice is a live online slot or a long drive. Here is the picture, emirate by emirate.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Regulated by KHDA, with 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25 across 17 curricula. IB programmes account for 7 per cent of that roll, so MYP specialists exist but are concentrated in a handful of communities. An online MYP tutor in Dubai removes the Al Khail Road problem from a 4pm slot entirely.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, so the teacher-who-knows-the-class shortcut is not available here. Sessions from Khalifa City, Al Reef and Saadiyat usually settle at 5pm or later.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK. MYP provision is thinner than in Abu Dhabi city, and the drive to the coast is not a weekly option for a Wednesday evening lesson. Subject groups that are scarce nationally - Design, Arts, upper-phase Language acquisition - are effectively unavailable locally, which is where live video stops being a compromise.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A Sharjah family commuting to a Dubai campus loses the 4pm to 6pm window to traffic, so MYP sessions here are commonly booked at 7pm or at the weekend.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here sit under the federal Ministry of Education, which supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. MYP enrolment is small, so most families searching for an MYP tutor in Ajman are supporting a child who commutes to a Sharjah or Dubai campus and gets home late.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah, approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Ras Al Khaimah returned zero mentions across the entire competitor corpus we reviewed, which tells you how much local MYP tutoring supply there is to compete for.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under the federal Ministry of Education. The east coast is the clearest case for online delivery in the country: a specialist in a scarce MYP subject group is not going to be found within driving distance, and the same session that would cost ninety minutes of road time costs nothing extra over video.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. The smallest private-school market in the UAE, and another emirate absent from every competitor page in our research. Families here are usually planning a move into a Sharjah or Dubai programme, which makes the transition conversation more useful than a weekly homework hour.

schoolClusters.note: Students we support in Dubai attend IB continuum campuses where the MYP runs from MYP 1 through to MYP 5 before the Diploma. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places - which means more MYP cohorts and the same thin pool of criterion-literate subject tutors.

In the capital the regulator is ADEK rather than KHDA, and the MYP cohorts are smaller and more spread out - Khalifa City, Al Raha, Saadiyat and Al Bateen rather than one or two school corridors. Session timing matters more here than subject availability, because a 4pm start is rarely realistic for a family crossing the island.
