ib-myp-online-tutor.modesIntro: Four ways UAE families buy MYP support, each priced differently because each is aimed at a different thing. The commonest mistake is buying the first one when the report card called for the second.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one, by criterion
modes.description: A fixed slot in one subject group, planned around the two criterion letters that the last report flagged rather than around this week's homework. The tutor reads the task sheet before the session, and the session ends with the student having produced something markable against the descriptor. This is the pattern most MYP families settle into, and at UAE market rates for a qualified subject tutor online it is the predictable line in the budget.
bullets: One subject group, one 60-minute slot, same time each week on Gulf Standard Time
Planned against two named criteria, not a topic list
The school's own task sheets and texts, never a parallel syllabus
A short written note after each session saying what moved and what did not

modes.title: A diagnostic block after the report card
modes.description: Three or four sessions, bought once, to answer a specific question: which of the four criteria is actually costing the grade. A UAE parent holding an MYP report with four numbers out of eight usually cannot tell, and neither can a tutor who has not seen the marked work. This is the cheapest useful purchase in the MYP and the one families most often skip in favour of a year of weekly hours aimed at the wrong letter.
bullets: Three to four sessions, with a written finding at the end
Built around the child's own marked tasks and the teacher's comments
Ends with a recommendation, including the recommendation to book nothing further
Usually the right first purchase in MYP 1 to MYP 3

modes.title: MYP Personal Project support
modes.description: Process coaching through MYP 5 for the student's own project: narrowing a goal that is actually achievable, keeping the process journal as evidence rather than as an afterthought, planning the report against the criteria in the school's guide, and giving feedback on drafts the student has produced. The supervisor the school appoints remains the person who signs the work off, and the words in the report are the student's throughout.
bullets: Goal-setting sessions early in MYP 5, before the journal has gone cold
Feedback on the student's own drafts, spoken and in the margin, never replacement text
Help reading the criteria in the guide the school works from
An honest conversation about what the academic-honesty declaration commits the student to

modes.title: The MYP to IB Diploma transition block
modes.description: A short, dated block in the months around the end of MYP 5, aimed at the gap between criterion-referenced marking and externally examined papers. The work is specific: command terms as the Diploma uses them, the standard-or-extended mathematics decision and what it does to the Analysis and Approaches route later, and the reading load in Higher Level sciences. Booked once, in the right eight weeks, it is cheaper than a term of rescue in DP1.
bullets: Subject-by-subject mapping of what MYP 5 covered against what DP1 assumes
The extended-mathematics question answered with the child's actual MYP marks in hand
Practice in writing to a weighting rather than to a criterion descriptor
Scheduled in the summer window, not in October of DP1

sections.heading: What a UAE family is actually buying when they hire an MYP tutor
paragraphs: An IB MYP online tutor in the UAE is being paid to read a mark scheme the family cannot see. The MYP reports a grade from 1 to 7 per subject, built from four criterion scores each out of eight. The grade is the output; the four numbers are the diagnosis. Almost every provider in this market quotes an hourly rate for a subject - maths, physics, English - and almost none quotes against a criterion, which is why two families can pay the same rate for the same subject and get completely different value.

The second thing being bought is interpretation of the school's own task. MYP assessment is set by the school, moderated internally, and expressed on a task sheet carrying a statement of inquiry, a global context and the specific criterion strands being marked. That sheet is the mark scheme. A tutor who teaches the topic from a textbook and never asks for the task sheet is teaching in the dark, however well they know the content, and that is the commonest way an MYP tutoring budget produces nothing.

The third thing, and the one families value only in hindsight, is timing information. In the five MYP years there is no external deadline forcing anybody's hand - no entry deadline, no published exam window, nothing like the Cambridge or Pearson series dates that discipline an IGCSE year. The absence of a deadline is why MYP support gets postponed until it becomes Diploma rescue. Buying four sessions in MYP 2 to fix criterion B habits is a different purchase from buying thirty hours in DP1 to fix the same habits under exam pressure.

So the sensible way to read the rate table in the next section is as a price per diagnosis, not a price per hour. A tutor at AED 300 who identifies in two sessions that the problem is criterion C communication across every subject has sold you something. A tutor at AED 80 who marks homework for a year has sold you supervision, which is a real service and a different one.

sections.heading: MYP tutoring rates in AED, and why they sit below Diploma figures
paragraphs: Published UAE rates for one-to-one tuition run from about AED 33 an hour to about AED 650, and MYP work tends to land in the lower half of that range. The reason is supply, not difficulty: a competent graduate can teach MYP 2 mathematics content, whereas Higher Level Diploma chemistry needs a specialist, so the MYP pool is wider and the price softer. That is genuinely good news for a family in MYP 1 to MYP 3 and a trap in MYP 5, where criterion-literate teaching in a scarce subject group costs what Diploma teaching costs because it is the same scarcity.

Three of the six competitor pages in our October 2026 research published no price at all, and the two that did quoted in US dollars - a currency a UAE family does not transact in. The figures in the table below are therefore collected from the providers and rate trackers that did publish, each attributed, each read in October 2026. They are the market. They are not an IB Gram price list, because the number that matters for your child depends on subject group, MYP year and how many hours are actually needed, and quoting a flat rate before the first lesson would be guesswork dressed as pricing.

Read the monthly figures with particular care. A package advertised at AED 799 a month for eight sessions is about AED 100 a teaching hour, which looks like the budget tier until you check the session length and who is teaching. In-home packages at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits work out near AED 200 to AED 225 an hour, and a meaningful share of that is travel rather than teaching. Dividing any package by its actual teaching hours is the single most useful sum a parent can do in this market.

One piece of UAE context worth holding alongside these numbers: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. School fees are flat this year. Tutoring spend is the variable line in a UAE education budget, which is an argument for planning it across five MYP years rather than reacting to one report card.

sections.heading: MYP criteria A to D, subject group by subject group
paragraphs: Here is the thing no competitor page in this market publishes: the actual criterion names. Each of the eight MYP subject groups is assessed against four criteria, lettered A to D, each marked out of eight, so every subject carries 32 raw marks before the school converts the total into a grade from 1 to 7 using the boundaries in the IB subject guide. The letters are the same across subjects. The names behind them are not. Criterion B in mathematics is investigating patterns; criterion B in design is developing ideas; criterion B in language acquisition is reading. They have nothing in common.

This is why a general tutor underperforms in the MYP even when their subject knowledge is strong. Teaching sciences criterion B means teaching the design of a fair test - variables, control, method a stranger could repeat - which is a research skill, not a content skill. Teaching individuals and societies criterion D means teaching the evaluation of a source's origin, purpose, value and limitation. Neither appears in a topic syllabus, and both are a quarter of the raw marks in their subject.

Use the table as a shopping list. Take your child's last report, find the subject group, read across to the criterion that scored lowest, and that is the phrase to put in your enquiry. A provider who can tell you how they would teach sciences criterion D, with an example, is selling teaching. A provider who answers with how many years of experience their team has is selling something else. We do not publish IB, Cambridge or Pearson guides, mark schemes or boundary tables on this site - they are the boards' copyright - but your child's coordinator has them and the task sheet quotes the relevant strands.

One caution on the final row. Interdisciplinary units are assessed on their own criteria rather than on those of either parent subject, and the Personal Project is marked against the criteria in the current IB guide your school works from. Guides are revised; confirm the live criterion set with the coordinator before anybody plans a session around it.

sections.heading: Which criterion repays paid hours, and which one does not
paragraphs: Not all four criteria respond to tutoring at the same speed, and a family on a fixed budget should know which is which before booking. Criterion A - knowing and understanding, under one name or another, in five of the eight subject groups - is the most drillable and the one most tutoring hours are spent on. It is also the one a motivated student can largely fix alone with the textbook and a fortnight. Paying AED 250 an hour for content revision that a quiz app would deliver is the most common waste in this market.

The research and process criteria are the opposite. Sciences criterion B, individuals and societies criterion B, design criteria A and B: these are procedures, they are taught by watching someone do them and then being corrected, and they are almost impossible to self-teach from a book because the student cannot see what is missing. Four to six focused sessions on one of these typically changes the mark pattern for the rest of the year, and the skill transfers to every later task in that subject group. On a per-hour basis they are the best buy in the MYP.

The communication criteria sit in the middle. Criterion C in mathematics and in individuals and societies rewards notation, labelling, referencing and structure - mechanical things, quickly fixed, but only once somebody shows the student what the descriptor actually wants. One session plus a checklist often moves it. The reflection criteria - sciences D, physical and health education D, arts D - take longer, because reflection is a habit of mind and a thirteen-year-old writing two reflective paragraphs a term will not build it in three weeks.

The practical rule for a UAE family: buy diagnosis first, buy the process criteria second, buy content last and buy it cheapest. And if a provider cannot tell you which criterion a proposed block of hours is aimed at, the block is not a plan.

sections.heading: Where MYP marks actually go missing
paragraphs: In mathematics it is criterion B. A student finds the pattern, states the rule, gets the answer right and scores in the middle band because they never justified the general rule or tested it beyond the cases given. The second loss is criterion D: a modelling task answered as a calculation, with no sentence on whether the model is reasonable or where it breaks. Both are visible in thirty seconds of looking at marked work, and neither is a content problem.

In sciences it is the method. Criterion B asks for a question, a hypothesis with reasoning, named independent, dependent and controlled variables, and a method somebody else could follow. UAE students who have done well in a content-heavy primary curriculum write excellent conclusions on top of a method that would not survive a repeat. Criterion D then asks for the implications of the science beyond the lab - and because it is rarely taught directly, it is routinely the lowest of the four scores on the report card.

In language and literature the loss is structural. Criterion A wants analysis of the writer's choices, and a strong reader who summarises the text instead sits in the middle band however fluent the prose. Criterion B wants a structure the reader can see. In individuals and societies the pattern repeats one letter over: strong on content, weak on criterion B investigation and criterion D critical thinking, because memorising a case study is not the same as evaluating a source's origin, purpose, value and limitation.

In design and the arts the marks go missing in the documentation. The design cycle is the mark scheme: research, a specification, ideas with annotations, a plan, testing against the specification you wrote. A good final product with none of that paperwork scores badly, and students are genuinely surprised by it. The same is true of the arts process journal, which carries more weight than the finished piece in most schools' task design.
bullets: Maths: a pattern found but never justified or tested, and modelling with no comment on limitations

Design and arts: a finished product with no documented specification, testing or process journal

sections.heading: Five years of spending, and where the dirhams do most work
paragraphs: The MYP is the longest run of school years in which a tutoring budget can be deployed with no external deadline forcing the timing, which is precisely why it is spent badly. The pattern we see from UAE families is a near-zero spend from MYP 1 to MYP 3, a small spend in MYP 4 when option blocks appear, then a sharp spend in MYP 5 when the Diploma becomes visible and the Personal Project has a date on it. It is the inverse of where the money works hardest.

Consider the arithmetic rather than the sentiment. Four diagnostic sessions in MYP 2 at the qualified-tutor end of the published range cost somewhere around AED 600 to AED 1,200 depending on who you book. Thirty hours of DP1 rescue at the specialist rate, at AED 270 as TutorChase publishes it, is roughly AED 8,100 - and buys you the same criterion habits, three years later, against a clock. The cheap intervention is early, narrow and aimed at one criterion. The expensive one is late, broad and aimed at a grade.

The second structural point is that MYP 4 is where the irreversible decisions sit, not MYP 5. Standard or extended mathematics, which subject groups to carry, whether a Higher Level science is realistic in two years: those are MYP 4 conversations in most UAE schools, and a tutor who has seen the child's criterion scores is worth more as an adviser in that term than as a weekly teacher the following year. Families who book one honest advisory block in MYP 4 frequently spend less overall across the five years.

The table below sets out the pattern we actually see against the pattern that uses the same money better. Hours are indicative, in teaching hours per term, and assume one subject group at a time rather than three at once - which is the other reliable way to overspend.

sections.heading: MYP 4 and MYP 5, or IGCSE instead: the UAE fork that changes your bill
paragraphs: Before you buy a single hour, establish what your child's school actually teaches in the last two middle years. A significant number of UAE schools that run the MYP in the early years switch to Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE for Years 10 and 11, either because parents want an externally examined certificate at sixteen or because the school's licensed curriculum is British with IB layered on top. Dubai's private roll is 37 per cent UK curriculum against 7 per cent International Baccalaureate, so the pull in that direction is strong and the hybrid is common.

The consequence for a tutoring budget is complete. An MYP 5 student is working towards internally assessed criterion scores, a Personal Project and possibly on-screen eAssessment. A Year 11 IGCSE student is working towards a dated external examination with a syllabus code, published papers and an entry deadline that falls months before the exam. In the UAE that examination arrives in two sittings, and a family effectively chooses between them: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series, June as the main attempt at the end of Year 11, November as the resit route about five months later for the one subject that went wrong. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE works the same way, May/June and November, and its November 2026 timetable finished on 19 November 2026 with results reaching students in January, the way November 2025 results landed on 22 January 2026. Entries for either series close months before the first paper, and the exact date comes from the centre on the statement of entry rather than from a page like this one. There is nothing comparable in the MYP calendar.

So the first question in an enquiry is not which subject but which assessment. If the answer is IGCSE, a tutor should be talking about syllabus codes, paper structure, tiering and the entry deadline. If the answer is MYP 5, the same tutor should be talking about criterion strands, the process journal and the interdisciplinary unit. A provider who gives you the same answer either way has not read the question, and an IGCSE revision plan sold to an MYP 5 family is thirty hours aimed at papers the child will never sit.

Cambridge also allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. If your child is on the IGCSE side of the fork, that is a fact worth checking with the school's exams officer this term rather than in May.
bullets: Ask the coordinator in writing: is my child assessed on MYP criteria or entered for an external IGCSE series?
Dubai's roll in 2024-25: 37 per cent UK curriculum, 26 per cent Indian, 14 per cent US, 7 per cent IB, across 17 curricula
MYP 5 has no external entry deadline; a Cambridge or Pearson series has one months before the papers
A hybrid school may run MYP 1-3 then IGCSE in Years 10 and 11, with no Personal Project at all
Entry, tiering and timetable zone are the school's responsibility, but the consequences land on your child

sections.heading: The Personal Project, and the line a paid tutor must not cross
paragraphs: The Personal Project in MYP 5 is the only MYP component with a hard internal deadline, a formal supervisor and an academic-honesty declaration attached, and it is where the tutoring market in this region behaves worst. One site in our research sells finished internal assessments outright at AED 3,750. Under IB rules that is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on the seller. Any provider willing to supply assessed work is telling you precisely how much they care about your child's record.

The honest boundary is clear and it is worth stating in full, because it is a genuine differentiator in this search result rather than a disclaimer. A tutor may help a student narrow a goal until it is achievable, explain what the criteria in the school's guide are asking for, ask the questions that make a vague process journal specific, review a draft the student has produced and say where it falls short, and teach the referencing conventions the report needs. A tutor may not supply sentences for the report, restructure it on the student's behalf, choose the goal, make the product, or edit the text into its final form.

That boundary is also where the value is. A supervisor in a UAE school may be carrying twenty-five project students alongside a full timetable, and the most common failure is not dishonesty but drift: a goal too broad, a journal written retrospectively in the last fortnight, a report that describes the product instead of evaluating the process against the criteria. Fortnightly process coaching from MYP 5 term one prevents all three, costs a fraction of a crisis block in term three, and leaves a document that is unambiguously the student's own.

Keep one more thing in view. We do not reproduce or supply IB guides, mark schemes or past material on this site; they are the IB's copyright and your coordinator issues the current versions. If a tutor offers you a guide as a download, that tells you something about their relationship with the rules your child is bound by.

sections.heading: eAssessment, Arabic and the other bills the MYP brings
paragraphs: Two things sit on an MYP family's budget that almost nobody puts in a tutoring quote. The first is eAssessment. Some schools enter MYP 5 students for the IB's on-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to the MYP certificate, and others award the school's own MYP record of achievement and move straight on. Whether your child sits anything externally is a school decision, not a parental one, and it changes a revision plan completely. Ask the coordinator which route the school uses, and ask in MYP 4 rather than MYP 5. We do not publish IB session or results dates on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and an unverified date is worse than no date; confirm every one with the coordinator.

The second is the Ministry subjects. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required those arrangements to be in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. They are not MYP subject groups, they are not marked on criteria A to D, and they appear on the report card all the same. A family budgeting for MYP support and discovering in Year 9 that Arabic as a first language needs its own weekly hour has simply not been told.

The rules around those subjects are specific enough to matter. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes.

One consequence for tutoring: for those subjects, KHDA states that the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Support for Arabic, Islamic Education or social studies therefore works on the school's own material and the school's own stream placement. A tutor offering a parallel Arabic curriculum is offering something the school cannot use.

sections.heading: Live one-to-one online for an eleven-to-sixteen-year-old
paragraphs: Families searching for MYP help in the UAE usually picture somebody at the dining table. The market will sell you that: published in-home rates run from AED 180 to AED 500 an hour, with monthly packages at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour visits. IB Gram does not sell it anywhere in the UAE. Our tuition is delivered one-to-one over live video, and home visits are a service we run only in India. The case for that is not convenience, it is who your child gets taught by.

A search by distance returns whoever is within a twenty-minute drive. For MYP mathematics in Dubai Marina that is a reasonable pool. For MYP design, upper-phase language acquisition, visual arts or an interdisciplinary unit in Al Ain, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain it is frequently nobody at all, and the family ends up paying a specialist rate for a generalist because the generalist was nearby. Removing the drive-time filter is what makes a subject-group match possible, and in the MYP the subject group is the whole point.

There are real advantages at this specific age, too. An eleven to sixteen-year-old works on a screen anyway, and MYP evidence is largely digital: a process journal, a design portfolio, a shared document, a spreadsheet of results. Screen-sharing a journal and annotating it live is better than reading it over somebody's shoulder. Sessions are recorded or summarised in writing, so a parent can see what happened without sitting in. And a child in the house with a parent in the next room is a safeguarding arrangement many UAE families prefer to a stranger in a bedroom.

The honest costs of online delivery are the ones to plan for: a quiet room, a stable connection, a headset, and a tutor who can hold the attention of a thirteen-year-old over video, which is a real skill and not every subject specialist has it. That last point is what the first lesson is for, and why we would rather you judge a match on one session than on a biography.

sections.heading: When no MYP specialist is free, and what that does to the price
paragraphs: No competitor page in the ten query clusters we researched discloses a coverage limit, and several conceal non-UAE delivery behind an overseas phone number. Here is ours, plainly. MYP mathematics, sciences, English language and literature and individuals and societies are the subject groups we can usually match within a few days. Design, visual arts, music, physical and health education theory and the upper phases of language acquisition take longer, and for a specific combination - MYP 5 design with a Diploma transition in view, say - there are weeks when nobody suitable has a free slot in UAE evening hours.

What we do in that situation is tell you, before you pay anything. The options are a waiting list with a date, a different subject group now and the scarce one later, a shorter diagnostic block with a tutor who covers the adjacent group, or a recommendation to look elsewhere. What we will not do is put a generalist in the slot at a specialist price and let you find out in week four. That is the failure mode families describe most often when they arrive from another provider, and it is entirely avoidable by saying no.

Timing changes availability as well as price. Gulf Standard Time evening slots between 5pm and 8pm are the busiest hours in this business, and a family that can take a 4pm or a weekend-morning slot will be matched faster and with more choice. The weeks after a UAE term report are the hardest to book into, because every family is reacting to the same document at the same time. Booking a diagnostic block a fortnight before reports go out, rather than the week after, is a free upgrade in choice.

Ramadan shifts the whole week. Many UAE families move sessions to post-Iftar slots or to the late morning, school hours compress, and a weekly plan built for an ordinary term stops fitting. We reschedule rather than cancel, and the sensible approach is to agree in advance what the Ramadan pattern will be instead of renegotiating it week by week.

sections.heading: Permits, inspection reports and the two documents to read before you spend
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system.

Two things follow for a parent. The permit is free, so any provider presenting licensing as a cost inside your hourly rate is adding a line that does not exist. And individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws - no schedule of amounts is published, so treat any specific figure you are quoted as unverified. In Abu Dhabi there is a further constraint: ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school, so the offer of your child's own teacher, privately, is one to decline.

The second document to read is your school's inspection report. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai; ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi; the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulate private education in their emirates and approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods; and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. An inspection report names the subject departments that are weaker, which is better targeting information than any tutoring advertisement.

IB Gram holds no permit, licence or accreditation from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and nothing on this page should be read as implying one. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai would need a KHDA educational services permit for a training institute; we run no UAE premises and claim no such permit. What we can do is tell you what to ask for and where to verify it, which is the part no advertisement covers.

process.title: Send the criterion letters, not just the subject
process.description: Tell us the MYP year, the subject group and which of the four criteria scored lowest on the last report. Those three facts shorten the diagnosis by two sessions. If you cannot read the report card - most parents cannot at MYP 1 - send a photograph of it and the last marked task sheet instead, and we will read it with you.

process.title: We read the marked work before we quote anything
process.description: A rate quoted before anybody has seen the child's work is guesswork. We look at the task sheet, the teacher's comments and one marked piece, then say which criterion the hours should be aimed at, how many we think are needed, and whether a diagnostic block or a weekly slot is the right shape. Sometimes the answer is that tutoring is not what this needs.

process.title: One introductory lesson at no charge
process.description: The first lesson is free, and the conditions are these: one lesson, one subject group, 45 to 60 minutes, booked through the enquiry form, no card details required and no obligation afterwards. Its purpose is to test the match, because a specialist who cannot hold a thirteen-year-old's attention over video is the wrong tutor whatever their subject record says.

process.title: A written plan with hours, criteria and a review date
process.description: You get a short plan naming the criteria being targeted, the number of sessions, what will be different by the review point and the date of that review. Hours are agreed in blocks rather than open-endedly, so the decision to continue is made against evidence instead of inertia. Ramadan and travel patterns are built in at this stage, not improvised later.

process.title: Notes after every session, and an honest exit
process.description: A short written note after each session says what moved and what did not. If the match is wrong, say so and we change the tutor without an argument or a notice period. If the plan has done its job, we say that too and stop - a provider who never tells a family to stop buying hours is not advising, it is selling.

whyPoints.title: Matched on subject group, not on postcode
whyPoints.description: Because lessons run over live video, the pool is not limited to whoever is within a twenty-minute drive of your community. For MYP design, arts and the upper phases of language acquisition that is the difference between a specialist and whoever was available, and in a criterion-marked programme the specialism is the whole value.

whyPoints.title: Teaching aimed at criteria, not at topics
whyPoints.description: Sessions are planned against the criterion letters the school is marking, using the school's own task sheets and texts. That is why a tutor asks for the task sheet before the first lesson. A parallel syllabus, however well taught, produces work the school's mark scheme cannot reward.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure on this page has a source
whyPoints.description: Three of the six competitor pages we reviewed in October 2026 publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. Each band here is attributed to the provider or rate tracker that published it, with the month it was read, and none of it is presented as an IB Gram price list.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions, reviews and gives feedback on work the student has produced. The Personal Project report is the student's own throughout, and the supervisor the school appoints is the person who signs it off. One competitor in this market sells completed assessed work outright; we say plainly where the line is and stay on the right side of it.

whyPoints.title: Coverage stated honestly, including the gaps
whyPoints.description: If no MYP specialist in your child's subject group has a free UAE evening slot, we tell you before you pay and offer a date, an alternative or a recommendation elsewhere. No page in the ten competitor clusters we researched discloses a coverage limit at all, which is a strange thing to hide from a parent.

whyPoints.title: Five years planned, not one report reacted to
whyPoints.description: MYP support works best as a small, early, well-aimed spend across MYP 1 to MYP 5 rather than a large late one in MYP 5. The plan we write says which years to spend in and which to leave alone, which occasionally means recommending fewer hours than you asked for.

faqs.question: What should a UAE family expect to pay for sixty minutes of MYP teaching?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates in October 2026 span AED 33 to AED 650 an hour, and MYP work usually sits in the lower half. Budget online providers advertise from AED 33 to AED 65, qualified subject tutors online from AED 150 to AED 300, and specialists AED 200 to AED 450 and above. In-home figures run AED 180 to AED 500 because the drive is inside the rate. Those are market numbers attributed to the providers and rate trackers that published them, not an IB Gram price list. Our own figure depends on subject group, MYP year and how many hours are genuinely needed, which is what the first lesson establishes.

faqs.question: My son's MYP report shows four letters and four numbers out of eight. What am I looking at?
faqs.answer: Those are the four assessment criteria for that subject group, lettered A to D, each marked out of eight. Together they give 32 raw marks, which the school converts into the single grade from 1 to 7 using the boundaries in the IB subject guide. The letters mean different things in different subjects: criterion B is investigating patterns in mathematics, developing ideas in design and reading in language acquisition. The useful information is not the overall grade but which of the four is lowest, and whether the same letter is low across several subjects. That pattern is what a tutoring plan should be aimed at.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for tutoring in MYP 1 when there is no external exam?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but for a narrow purpose and a small number of hours. The useful purchase in MYP 1 is not content support; it is teaching the child, and frankly the parent, what the four criterion descriptors are actually asking for. Four to six sessions is usually enough. A student who understands in MYP 1 that a conclusion needs an evaluation of method, and that a maths answer needs a justified general rule, builds habits that pay for the next five years. Thirty hours of content coaching at this age is almost always the wrong spend, because the content is the part a textbook covers perfectly well.

faqs.question: Which of the four MYP criteria is hardest to move with weekly lessons?
faqs.answer: The reflection criteria - sciences criterion D, physical and health education criterion D, arts criterion D. Reflection is a habit of thought rather than a technique, and a student who writes two reflective paragraphs a term has few chances to practise it. Expect a term, not three weeks. The fastest to move are the communication criteria, where marks go on notation, labelling, referencing and structure: one session and a checklist frequently changes the score. The best value per hour sits in between, on the inquiry, investigation and design criteria, which need four to six corrected attempts and then transfer to every later task in that subject group.

faqs.question: Our school teaches IGCSE in Year 10 instead of MYP 4. Does that change what we should pay for?
faqs.answer: Completely. An MYP 4 student is working towards internally assessed criterion scores with no external deadline. A Year 10 IGCSE student is working towards a dated external series with a syllabus code, published papers and an entry deadline months before the exam. The published windows are the thing to plan against: Pearson's Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 timetable ran through late autumn and finished on 19 November 2026, and Cambridge sits its UAE candidates in a June series and a November series, never in the February and March window it offers to India. The tutoring is different work on each side: criterion strands and process journals for the MYP student, paper structure, tiering and timed practice for the IGCSE one. Ask the coordinator in writing which assessment your child is entered for, and for which series, before you buy anything.

faqs.question: How many hours of MYP maths support does a UAE family usually book in a term?
faqs.answer: It depends far more on the year than on the subject. In MYP 1 to MYP 3, four to ten teaching hours a term aimed at one criterion is a realistic plan and frequently enough. In MYP 4, when option choices and the standard-or-extended mathematics decision appear, ten to fourteen is common. In MYP 5, with the Personal Project and Diploma choices running at the same time, fourteen to twenty. Those figures assume one subject group at a time. Families who book three subjects simultaneously in MYP 5 usually spend the most and see the least, because nothing gets enough continuous attention to change.

faqs.question: Where exactly is the line between Personal Project help and malpractice?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor may help narrow a goal until it is achievable, explain what the criteria in the school's guide ask for, press a vague process journal for specifics, give feedback on a draft the student has produced and teach the referencing conventions the report needs. A tutor may not supply sentences, restructure the text, choose the goal, make the product or edit the report to a final version. The school-appointed supervisor signs the work off, and the student signs an academic-honesty declaration. Any provider offering to hand over finished assessed work is putting your child's record at risk, not helping.

faqs.question: What does the MYP interdisciplinary unit grade actually depend on?
faqs.answer: On its own criteria - evaluating, synthesising and reflecting - rather than on the criteria of either contributing subject group. That is the detail students miss. They treat an interdisciplinary unit as two homeworks and produce good science beside good geography without ever explaining how the two disciplines together produced an understanding neither could reach alone. That explanation is the marked thing. One session on the structure of a synthesis paragraph usually fixes it, and the gain carries to every interdisciplinary unit afterwards. Ask your child's coordinator which subject groups are paired this year, because the pairing changes what evidence is needed.

faqs.question: Does my child need separate support for Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE social studies?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and it is a line most families have not budgeted. Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA required those arrangements from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. They are not MYP subject groups and they are not marked on criteria A to D, but they appear on the report. Support for them has to use the school's own material: KHDA states that different or additional content without prior Ministry of Education permission is strictly prohibited. Placement into the Arab or non-Arab stream is the school's decision, not yours.

faqs.question: Will MYP tuition prepare my daughter for Diploma Higher Level sciences?
faqs.answer: Only if it is aimed at the right things. Higher Level sciences assumes a reading load, a tolerance for extended written answers and a command-term fluency that MYP criterion marking does not force. The MYP work that transfers best is sciences criterion B and C - designing a fair test, processing data, evaluating method - because internal assessment in the Diploma rewards exactly those. Content coverage transfers least, since the Diploma syllabus restarts. The practical move is a short transition block in the summer between MYP 5 and DP1, mapping what was covered against what DP1 assumes, rather than a term of rescue in October.

faqs.question: Does MYP eAssessment change how much tutoring we should book?
faqs.answer: It changes what the tutoring is for, so ask early. Some schools enter MYP 5 students for the IB's on-screen examinations and ePortfolios leading to the MYP certificate; others award their own record of achievement and move straight to the Diploma. If your school enters students, timed on-screen practice and portfolio curation become real work in MYP 5. If it does not, that same budget is better spent on the Personal Project and the Diploma transition. It is a school decision, so put the question to the coordinator in MYP 4. We do not publish IB session dates here; confirm those with the coordinator too.

faqs.question: Is a cheaper MYP tutor at AED 60 an hour a false economy?
faqs.answer: Not automatically - it depends what you need. At the budget end of the published UAE range, from about AED 33 to AED 65 an hour, you are generally buying homework supervision and content re-teaching, and for a MYP 2 student who simply is not doing the work, that may be exactly right and good value. What you are unlikely to get is criterion literacy: somebody who can look at a marked task and say that the problem is criterion B rather than the topic. If the report shows uneven criterion scores rather than low marks across the board, the cheap hour will not touch it.

faqs.question: How do we tell whether MYP tutoring is working before the next report card?
faqs.answer: Do not wait for the report; it arrives too late to act on. Agree in advance what will be different at a review point four to six sessions in, stated against a criterion rather than a grade - a method section that names controlled variables, a maths investigation with a justified general rule, a journal entry written on the day. Then look at the child's own marked work against that. A written note after each session makes this visible. If nothing in the marked work has changed by the review point, the plan was aimed at the wrong letter and should be changed, not extended.

faqs.question: Can MYP lessons move to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan, and does that cost more?
faqs.answer: Yes to the first, no to the second. Ramadan compresses the UAE school day and shifts family routines, and many of our MYP families move sessions to post-Iftar evenings or to the late morning at weekends. Rates do not change for the timing. What helps is agreeing the Ramadan pattern in advance rather than renegotiating it week by week, because the popular post-Iftar slots fill quickly. Terms report deadlines and internal assessment dates set by the school usually do not move for Ramadan, so the sensible plan reduces frequency slightly and keeps continuity rather than pausing altogether.

faqs.question: What happens if no UAE-based MYP specialist is free for my child's subject group?
faqs.answer: You are told before you pay. MYP mathematics, sciences, English language and literature and individuals and societies are usually matched within a few days. Design, visual arts, music, physical and health education theory and language acquisition phases 5 and 6 can take longer, and some combinations have weeks with no suitable free slot in UAE evening hours. The options we offer are a waiting list with a date, a different subject group now and the scarce one later, a shorter block with a tutor covering the adjacent group, or a recommendation to look elsewhere. We do not fill the slot with a generalist at a specialist rate.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in the UAE need a permit, and does that cost sit inside our rate?
faqs.answer: A permit is required and it costs nothing. The MoHRE private tuition work permit came in under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years; eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. So any provider presenting licensing as a cost inside your hourly rate is adding a line that does not exist. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no schedule of amounts is published.

faqs.question: What exactly is included in the free first MYP lesson?
faqs.answer: One lesson, one subject group, 45 to 60 minutes, at no charge, booked through the enquiry form with no card details and no obligation afterwards. Before it runs we ask for the last report card and one marked task sheet, because a lesson planned without them is a conversation rather than teaching. The purpose is to test the match: whether the tutor can hold your child's attention over live video and whether they can read the school's task sheet and say which criterion the work should target. Afterwards you get a short written view of what the hours should be aimed at, including when the answer is none.

ib-myp-online-tutor.closingHeading: Start with the criterion, not the subject
ib-myp-online-tutor.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, make it this: find the lowest of the four criterion scores on your child's last MYP report, and make that letter the first line of your enquiry. It will shorten the diagnosis, it will stop you buying content coaching for a process problem, and it is the question that separates a tutor who knows the Middle Years Programme from one who knows the textbook. Send us the report card, the subject group and the MYP year. We will read the marked work, tell you how many hours we think it needs, run the first lesson at no charge, and say plainly if the honest answer is that you do not need us.

intro.heading: Why a Personal Project term in the UAE is a school-system problem before it is a study problem
paragraphs: The Personal Project is the only piece of MYP work a student designs, runs and evidences largely alone. In MYP 5 — Year 11 in most British-system schools in Dubai, Grade 10 in most American-system ones — your child states a learning goal, names a product, builds success criteria for it, keeps a process journal, meets a supervisor three times and submits a report. The school marks that report against three criteria worth eight marks each. There is no external exam paper anywhere in the process, which is exactly why families underestimate it until February.

In the UAE that sits inside a second structure parents rarely see on a school website. Your child's school answers to an emirate regulator: KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. That regulator licenses the curriculum the school may teach, and in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah it approves 'tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods' directly, according to the UAE government's own private-schools page on u.ae. The project deadline your child is working to was set inside those constraints.

Running alongside the MYP timetable are the subjects federal rules require of every private school whatever its licensed curriculum: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies. KHDA's mandatory-subjects guidance calculates the weekly requirement on a 40-minute lesson unit, requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups 'are strictly prohibited' because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. For a student in a project term, those periods are not spare capacity to borrow back.

IB MYP personal project help in the UAE, done honestly, works inside all of that. We deliver it one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, scheduled around your school's published calendar. A specialist reads the process journal, asks the questions a supervisor will ask, explains what each criterion strand is actually looking for, and then stops. The goal, the product, the journal entries and every sentence of the report remain your child's own work, because IB academic-integrity rules make this the student's project and nobody else's. A tutor who offers more than that is offering your child a malpractice finding.

This page is the school-system version of the answer. It sets out the three criteria and the marks behind them, the report formats and their limits, what each emirate regulator actually controls, the mandatory UAE subjects that sit beside the project, the project year counted backwards from the school's report deadline, where coaching ends and malpractice begins, what the MoHRE private tuition work permit means for anyone you pay, what the MYP does and does not do for Ministry of Education equivalency, and what the UAE market charges. Rates are attributed to their source and dated; none of them is our price list.

ib-myp-personal-project-help.programmesIntro: The Personal Project belongs to the MYP, but the family decision around it usually spans two programmes: the one your child is finishing and the one they are about to start. Here is where each sits in a UAE school, and what the local system adds to it.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years across eight subject groups, assessed internally against four criteria per subject, each marked out of eight. There is no external paper unless the school opts into MYP eAssessment. The programme closes with the Personal Project in MYP 5, which is assessed against its own three criteria and reported as a separate 1–7 grade. Interdisciplinary units and the earlier Community Project are the rehearsal for it.
programmes.countryNote: UAE MYP cohorts often sit beside an IGCSE stream in the same building, because many schools switch to Cambridge or Edexcel at Year 10. That makes MYP 4 and 5 a smaller, more exposed group, and it is why a UAE family looking for project support frequently cannot find anyone inside their own school with spare capacity.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Inquiry-led primary learning across six transdisciplinary themes, closing with the PYP Exhibition — a collaborative, teacher-supported investigation that is the first cousin of the Personal Project. Children who have done an Exhibition arrive in MYP 5 already understanding what a research question and a reflection log are for, which shortens the planning stage considerably.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's private sector served 387,441 students across 227 schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with the IB accounting for 7% of enrolment according to the Dubai Media Office. A family moving between UAE schools can easily cross from a PYP setting into a British primary and back, so prior Exhibition experience is worth asking about rather than assuming.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects at Higher or Standard Level plus the core: Theory of Knowledge, Creativity Activity Service and the 4,000-word Extended Essay. The Extended Essay is the Personal Project's successor — a single long independent piece with a supervisor, a reflection record and an integrity declaration. Students who kept a real process journal in MYP 5 find the EE reflection sessions straightforward.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places according to KHDA. More DP places in the emirate means more MYP 5 students staying in the IB rather than transferring out at 16, and a project done properly is the cleanest evidence a DP coordinator has of independent working.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The IB's fourth programme, combining DP courses with a career-related study and a reflective project. Provision in the UAE is thin — most IB World Schools here run PYP, MYP and DP only — so treat it as an option to verify on the IB's own programme list for a specific school rather than something to plan around.
programmes.countryNote: If a UAE school offers the CP, the reflective project carries the same academic-integrity architecture as the Personal Project: a supervisor, recorded meetings and a signed declaration. Families weighing it after MYP 5 should ask the school's coordinator which pathway their current project work actually feeds, because the two are assessed differently.

ib-myp-personal-project-help.subjectsIntro: A Personal Project is not a subject, but it always leans on one. The learning goal almost always sits inside an MYP subject group, and the marks follow the quality of the thinking there. These are the eight groups plus the project itself, with what each actually assesses.

subjects.name: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Analysing and producing texts, assessed on analysing, organising, producing text and using language. Project goals here tend toward writing a novella, a magazine or a translation. The usual marks problem is a product that demonstrates skill but a report that never names which analytical technique the student actually learned.

subjects.name: Language Acquisition
subjects.description: Listening, reading, speaking and writing in an additional language, placed by phase rather than year group. Popular project goals include reaching a conversational level in a new language or subtitling a film. Criterion B marks depend on evidencing the ATL skill used, not the fluency reached.

subjects.name: Individuals and Societies
subjects.description: History, geography, economics and civics, assessed on knowing and understanding, investigating, communicating and thinking critically. This group produces the strongest project goals in UAE schools — local heritage, urban planning, migration — and the weakest success criteria, because social outcomes resist measurement.

subjects.name: Sciences
subjects.description: Biology, chemistry and physics taught as integrated sciences in earlier years, assessed on knowing and understanding, inquiring and designing, processing and evaluating, and reflecting on the impacts of science. Science-led projects fail on scope more than on method: a controlled investigation sized for a term, not a career.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: Assessed on knowing and understanding, investigating patterns, communicating, and applying mathematics in real-life contexts. Extended mathematics in MYP 4 and 5 is the route into DP Analysis and Approaches. Projects that use statistics need the success criteria to specify sample size and method before any data is gathered.

subjects.name: Arts
subjects.description: Visual arts, music, drama and media, assessed on knowing and understanding, developing skills, thinking creatively and responding. Arts projects usually have the best products and the thinnest criterion C, because evaluating your own creative work against stated criteria feels unnatural to a fifteen-year-old without practice.

subjects.name: Design
subjects.description: The inquiring and analysing, developing ideas, creating the solution and evaluating cycle. Design is the closest subject to the project's own structure, which is why Design students often score well on criterion A. The risk is the opposite: a specification so detailed the student never reflects on learning.

subjects.name: Physical and Health Education
subjects.description: Assessed on knowing and understanding, planning for performance, applying and performing, and reflecting on performance. Fitness and coaching projects are common in the UAE. Marks hinge on whether the training plan was a documented plan with measures, or a log of what happened.

subjects.name: Interdisciplinary units
subjects.description: Required units that combine two or more subject groups, assessed on evaluating, synthesising and reflecting. These are the formal rehearsal for the Personal Project's integrative demands, and a student's interdisciplinary grades are the single best predictor of how much planning support the project will need.

subjects.name: The Personal Project
subjects.description: Planning, Applying skills and Reflecting, each marked out of eight, converted by the school into a 1–7 grade. The learning goal, product, success criteria, process journal and report are all the student's own. A tutor's role is explaining the criteria and questioning the evidence, never supplying either.

ib-myp-personal-project-help.regionsTitle: Every emirate answers to a different authority — here is what that changes
ib-myp-personal-project-help.regionsIntro: Where your child's school sits determines who approved its calendar, who inspects it, and who you would escalate a question to. The surveyed competitor pages for this query name none of these bodies except KHDA, and two emirates appear nowhere in that corpus at all.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate, and publishes the mandatory-subjects guidance every licensed school follows. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private-school fees would not rise for 2026-27 under Dubai's economic incentives package, so tutoring is the variable cost in a Dubai MYP family's year.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and it is named by none of the competitor pages surveyed for this query. Press reporting also describes ADEK ethics rules barring school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school — relevant the moment a supervisor offers extra paid hours.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Al Ain falls under ADEK with Abu Dhabi, so licensing and the staff-ethics position are identical, but the IB continuum is thinner here. Families more often need a specialist from outside their own school and outside their own city, which is the clearest case for a live-video session over a commute.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is broader than inspection: a Sharjah school's published assessment calendar has already passed the authority, so a project deadline there is less negotiable than parents expect.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority. IB continuum provision is limited, and a number of Ajman families keep an MYP child at a Sharjah or Dubai school and absorb the commute — which is why evening slots after 7pm are the norm here.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees and curricula rather than only inspecting. Ras Al Khaimah returned zero mentions across every competitor page surveyed for this cluster, so published local detail is genuinely scarce.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Fujairah's private schools fall under the federal Ministry of Education. There is no emirate-level education authority to put a calendar query to, and MYP provision on the east coast is narrow, so most Fujairah families working on a project are pairing their school with a specialist joining over live video.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Umm Al Quwain is also supervised by the Ministry of Education and is the smallest private-school market in the country. Like Fujairah, it carries no MYP-specific tutoring content anywhere in the local search results, which is a gap worth naming rather than papering over with generic copy.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai holds the densest IB continuum provision in the country, and most MYP 5 cohorts here run the project between October and March. Programme status changes year to year, so check the IB's own programme list and KHDA's school listing for any school below before you assume it runs the MYP rather than the DP alone.

Abu Dhabi's IB schools sit under ADEK, and several run the DP without the MYP, which matters because a Year 11 student in a non-MYP school has no Personal Project to submit at all. Confirm the programme before buying project support — we have had families book it for a child sitting IGCSEs.
schools: The American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah, Ajman and the northern emirates
schoolClusters.note: Provision thins quickly north of Dubai, and the regulator changes twice across this group: SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education in Ajman. The schools below include both IB settings and the alternatives families weigh against them locally.
schools: Ras Al Khaimah English Speaking School

ib-myp-personal-project-help.modesIntro: Project support is not a weekly subject lesson, because the workload is not weekly. It clusters around the three recorded meetings and the report deadline. These are the shapes UAE families actually book, all delivered one-to-one over live video.

modes.title: Weekly planning sessions through the autumn term
modes.description: One hour a week from the project launch to the second recorded meeting, aimed entirely at criterion A. The session works on the learning goal, the product definition and the success criteria, and ends with the student writing the journal entry themselves while the tutor is still on the call. This is the cheapest stage to fix anything in.

modes.title: Milestone blocks before each recorded meeting
modes.description: A two-hour block in the week before each supervisor meeting. The tutor reads the journal, lists what a supervisor will ask, and rehearses the answers with the student. Families who use only this shape typically book three blocks across the year and nothing else, which is the lowest-cost route for a well-organised student.

modes.title: Report-stage review in the final six weeks
modes.description: Sessions concentrated between the product being finished and the report deadline, working on criterion C and on keeping the report inside its format limit. The tutor reads the student's draft back to them with questions attached. No text is supplied, rewritten or edited to completion, because that would make the submission inadmissible.

modes.title: Subject support running alongside the project
modes.description: Where the project leans on a subject the student is also struggling with, a separate weekly slot in that subject group runs in parallel. Keeping them apart matters: project sessions are about criteria and evidence, subject sessions are about content. Mixing the two is how a project term quietly becomes maths tuition.

sections.heading: What a UAE parent is actually buying when they search for Personal Project help
paragraphs: IB MYP personal project help in the UAE is one-to-one teaching, delivered online, that prepares a student to run their own project against the IB's three criteria. It is not a writing service and it is not a product-building service. The marks belong to the school, the work belongs to the student, and the tutor's job is to make the criteria legible and the plan realistic enough to survive a UAE school year.

What a family wants at the moment of searching is usually narrower than the word 'help'. Three requests dominate. The learning goal is too broad to evidence in a term. The success criteria are adjectives rather than measures, so there is nothing for criterion C to evaluate against later. Or the report is six weeks away and the process journal has four entries in it, three of them from September. Those are three different pieces of teaching and they take very different numbers of hours.

The second thing families want, and rarely say out loud, is somebody who recognises the school system the deadline came from. A Dubai MYP 5 cohort, a Sharjah one and an Ajman one are working to calendars approved under three different authorities, and how much a deadline can move differs accordingly. A tutor who asks which emirate the school sits in before quoting a plan is asking a better question than one who asks only for the subject.

The third is scheduling that survives a UAE school week. Sessions run in Gulf Standard Time, after the school run and around mandatory-subject periods that cannot be traded away, and they continue through the February break and the Ramadan timetable shift rather than pausing exactly when the report deadline tightens. That is the practical case for live video over a tutor's driving radius: the specialist is chosen for the subject group, not for proximity.
bullets: Goal too broad to evidence — a planning problem, two to four sessions
Vague success criteria — a criterion A and C problem, fixable early, expensive late
Thin process journal — a criterion B problem, and the hardest to repair
Report over its format limit — a structure problem, not a word-trimming one

sections.heading: The three Personal Project criteria, strand by strand, and the marks behind them
paragraphs: The Personal Project is assessed against three criteria, each marked out of eight, for a total of 24. Criterion A is Planning. Criterion B is Applying skills. Criterion C is Reflecting. The school converts the total into the 1–7 grade that appears on the report, using the project grade boundaries published in the IB's MYP Projects guide. No part of that conversion is a percentage, which is the first thing most parents have to unlearn.

Criterion A carries three strands and the order of them matters. The student states a learning goal and explains how a personal interest led to it; states an intended product and develops appropriate success criteria for that product; then presents a clear, detailed plan for achieving the product against those criteria. Most lost marks here are not effort, they are specificity. 'Learn more about marine conservation' is an interest, not a goal. 'A good website' is not a success criterion.

Criterion B has two strands, both about Approaches to Learning skills: how an ATL skill was applied to help achieve the learning goal, and how one was applied to help achieve the product. The evidence has to exist in the process journal before it can appear in the report. A journal kept twice a term produces a thin criterion B no matter how impressive the finished product is, and no amount of report-stage polish recovers it.

Criterion C also has two strands: the impact of the project on the student or their learning, and an evaluation of the product against the success criteria set out back in criterion A. If those criteria were vague, criterion C has nothing to measure against, so a weak A quietly caps C. Repairing criterion A in January, after the product is already half-built, is the single most common piece of work UAE families ask us for.

Confirm every figure in this section against your own school's copy of the IB Projects guide before planning around it. Schools moved to the current three-criterion model from an earlier four-criterion version, and the older material is still circulating on tutoring sites and in school handbooks that were never updated.

sections.heading: Report formats, their limits, and what still has to be evidenced in each
paragraphs: The report is where the three criteria are actually awarded, and it does not have to be a document. Written and electronic reports — a word-processed file, a website, a blog — run 1,500 to 3,500 words. Oral formats such as a podcast or a radio broadcast, and visual formats such as a film, run 13 to 15 minutes. The bibliography and the appendices sit outside the limit, so citing properly costs nothing in word count.

Format choice is a marks decision rather than a presentation one. A film looks compelling and eats the exact weeks criterion C needs, because editing time is not reflection time. A website lets a student hide criterion A behind navigation a marker has to hunt through. A written report is the easiest to over-write and the easiest to structure criterion by criterion, which is why most UAE students who choose it score more evenly even when their product is less showy.

Whatever the format, the same evidence has to be present and findable: the goal and its origin, the product and its success criteria, the plan, the ATL skills with journal evidence behind them, the impact on the student, and the evaluation against the criteria. Extracts from the process journal go in the appendices. A report that reads beautifully but leaves a marker reconstructing which strand is being addressed loses marks it never had to lose.

Students running close to a limit should cut structurally rather than sentence by sentence. Three paragraphs of background that no criterion asks for are worth more as space than as prose. In report-stage sessions the tutor reads the student's own draft back to them with questions attached and the student makes every change, because supplying text or editing to completion would make the submission inadmissible under IB rules.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, and what each authority actually controls
paragraphs: Five separate bodies regulate private schools across the seven emirates, and only one of them appears anywhere in the competitor pages surveyed for this query. KHDA oversees the quality of private education in Dubai. ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah. The Department of Knowledge does so in Ras Al Khaimah. The Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The distinction that matters to a project term is between inspection and approval. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, according to the UAE government's private-schools page. A calendar that has been through that process is not something a head of year adjusts by email. In Dubai, by contrast, KHDA's published mandatory-subject requirements shape the timetable that project work has to fit around rather than the project deadline itself.

Inspection ratings are worth reading for a different reason. A regulator's published report on a school tells you where that school is already strong, and therefore where paid support adds least. If the inspection notes weak provision in a subject group your child's project leans on, that is a signal to look outside the school for subject depth. If it notes strong provision, the gap is more likely to be the student's planning discipline than the teaching.

None of this makes any tutoring provider a regulated education body. IB Gram is not a licensed UAE training institute and does not present itself as one: a KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific authorisation issued to training institutes holding premises in Dubai, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. Any provider describing itself as regulator-endorsed should be asked to show the permit number.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects that run beside the project, and why they cannot be borrowed from
paragraphs: Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific national curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but they must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That federal baseline is the reason an IB World School in Dubai teaches Arabic alongside the MYP rather than instead of it, and it is the reason a project term has less free timetable in it than a parent counting IB subject blocks would expect.

KHDA's mandatory-subjects guidance puts numbers on this. Weekly requirements are calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary the lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Schools must organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

Language of instruction is specified too. Standard Arabic is required for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students; and for non-Arab students, Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies are delivered in the school's licensed-curriculum language. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic must hold the appropriate KHDA authorisation for those subjects, which is a credential a parent can actually ask about.

There is one more constraint worth knowing before anyone offers your child extra material for these subjects. For the mandatory UAE subjects, using any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. That rules out the sort of improvised supplementary workbook a tutor might reach for in any other subject, and it is why Arabic and Islamic Education support has to track the school's own approved scheme of work closely.

sections.heading: The project year counted backwards from the report deadline
paragraphs: Nobody publishes this table, and it is the one most families would use. Unlike an IGCSE or DP session, Personal Project dates are set by the school rather than by a board, so the windows below are typical rather than official. Take your own school's published milestone dates from the MYP coordinator and lay them over this shape; the sequence holds even when the months move.

The spine of the year is the three recorded supervisor meetings, because they are what the academic integrity form documents. Everything else arranges itself around them. The first meeting needs a stated goal, a named product and drafted success criteria. The second needs a plan with journal evidence behind it and the ATL skills identified. The third needs the work finished enough to be evaluated, and the form signed by both parties.

Counting backwards is what changes behaviour. If the report is due in early March, the product has to be finished in late January, which means the plan has to be real by the end of November, which means the goal has to be narrow by early October. A family that starts support in February is not buying project teaching; they are buying triage on a criterion A that was written five months earlier and cannot now be rebuilt.

Two later stages belong to the school rather than the student. Reports are standardised internally so that marking is consistent across supervisors, and where a school registers candidates for the IB MYP certificate, the personal project is submitted for IB moderation. Neither stage asks anything further of your child, but both are reasons a school's internal deadline sits well before the date the grade appears on a report card.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line a paid tutor does not cross
paragraphs: This is the section the essay mills in this search result do not have. One site found during research sells finished Internal Assessments outright. Under IB rules that is malpractice, and the consequence lands on the student, not the seller: an authentication failure on the project puts the MYP result and the student's standing with their own school at risk. A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on work the student has produced.

The practical test is simple. If a session ends with something on the page that the student did not think of and could not explain to their supervisor unprompted, the line has been crossed. That is why our project sessions end with the student writing the journal entry while the call is still running, and why report-stage work is done by reading the student's draft back to them with questions rather than by handing over revised text.

The academic integrity form is the formal mechanism. It records the supervisor meetings and is signed by student and supervisor, and it exists precisely so that a school can show the work developed over time with proper oversight. A student who has kept a dated journal and attended the recorded meetings has a paper trail. A student whose project appeared fully formed in February does not, and that absence is what triggers questions.

Parents sometimes ask where editing stops being feedback. A useful boundary: a tutor may explain what a criterion strand asks for, point to where a draft does not yet answer it, and ask the question that would expose the gap. A tutor may not supply sentences, restructure a draft on the student's behalf, choose the journal extracts, or build any part of the product. The table below sets this out task by task.
