sections.heading: Academic honesty when the deadline is Friday
paragraphs: The pressure point in the Diploma is predictable. A coursework deadline is three days away, the draft is not working, and the family is at the exact moment when it is most likely to buy something it should not.

What a tutor may do is teach, question and give feedback on work the student has produced. Reading a draft against the published criteria and naming which criterion is underserved is legitimate, and it is most of the value available in that week. Rehearsing a reflection session with the Extended Essay supervisor is legitimate. Teaching the statistics a student needs in order to handle their own data set is legitimate. Marking a timed question and explaining the mark scheme is legitimate.

What a tutor must never do is supply any part of assessed work. Not a paragraph of an Extended Essay, not an analysis section for an investigation, not a rewrite that comes back as prose the student did not author. There are operators in this market selling finished Internal Assessments at four-figure AED prices; one competitor page researched for this project advertised exactly that. Buying one is malpractice under the IB's academic-honesty rules, the student carries the consequence, and the consequence can be the Diploma itself.

Two practical tests for a family. Ask what the tutor will do with a draft: an answer about criteria is a good sign, an answer about improving the writing is not. Then ask whether the student could explain their own method, line by line, in a conversation with their teacher. Every IB coursework component is submitted through the school with authenticity checks attached, and a student who cannot defend their own work has a problem no tutor can fix on the Thursday night.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in the same week
paragraphs: Every private school in the UAE teaches these alongside its licensed international curriculum, which means a Diploma student's week is not six subjects plus the core. Families planning tuition hours routinely leave them out of the arithmetic and then wonder where the evenings went.

The federal position is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, while adhering to the Ministry's general regulations. In Dubai, KHDA requires these subjects in all private schools regardless of the international curriculum licensed, with its requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April.

The organisation rules are specific and they explain the timetable your child actually has. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and KHDA states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and the guidance advises that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes.

Two constraints follow for tuition. Teachers of Arabic and Islamic Education in Dubai schools are required to hold appropriate approval from KHDA for those subjects, so ask what a tutor's experience with the mandatory stream actually is. And the use of different or additional content for these subjects without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, which means support here works the school's own material rather than importing a parallel course from elsewhere.

process.title: Tell us the date, then the subject
process.description: Start with what you are working towards: the next internal deadline, the mock window, or the session itself. Add the subject, the level, and the school. Three lines is enough. The date decides what kind of help is worth buying, and it changes the answer more than the subject does.

process.title: We match one specialist, not a shortlist
process.description: You are sent one tutor who teaches that subject at that level, with the reason for the match stated. If nobody is free in your slot for a Higher Level option, you are told that in the same reply rather than offered a near-enough alternative. A near-enough tutor costs a term.

process.title: A free first lesson that produces a plan
process.description: One free trial lesson, in one subject, with the matched tutor, arranged before any payment. It ends with a dated plan: the next deadline, the two weakest topics, the session length and the slot. If the match is wrong, say so and we change it before anything is booked.

process.title: A fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time
process.description: Sessions are booked at the same time each week, in Gulf Standard Time, so they survive the school run and the autumn diary. Lessons run online, one-to-one, over live video, with the school's scheme of work open. A written note follows each session naming the next target.

process.title: Reviewed at each deadline, not each term
process.description: The plan is checked at the points the calendar sets: after the Internal Assessment deadline, after the mocks, and at six weeks out. That is when session length and frequency change. Reviewing in December because December arrived is how families pay for hours that no longer match the need.

whyPoints.title: Dates before promises
whyPoints.description: The first thing we ask for is the date you are working towards, because it determines whether coursework feedback or paper technique is the right purchase. No tutor on this platform will tell you that six weeks and two years need the same plan, and no one will quote you a grade.

whyPoints.title: Delivered online, said plainly
whyPoints.description: Lessons are one-to-one over live video, in every emirate. Nobody travels to a UAE address, and we do not pretend otherwise in order to match a search phrase. Home visits are a service we run in India only. In the UAE, online is what reaches a Higher Level specialist from Fujairah.

whyPoints.title: Sources named, numbers dated
whyPoints.description: Every Cambridge and Pearson date on this page comes from the board's own published page, read in October 2026. AED figures quoted anywhere on this site are market rates attributed to whoever published them. Where a figure is not verified, such as an IB session date, it is left off rather than guessed.

whyPoints.title: One specialist per subject and level
whyPoints.description: A Chemistry Higher Level teacher and a Chemistry Standard Level teacher are not interchangeable, and neither covers Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches. Matching is by subject and level, and where a student needs two subjects, that is two tutors rather than one generalist stretched across both.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question and give feedback on the student's own drafts against the published criteria. No part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay is ever supplied by a tutor. This market contains operators who sell finished coursework; that route risks the student's Diploma and we will not compete on it.

whyPoints.title: Honest about coverage
whyPoints.description: Where no UAE-based specialist is free for a niche Higher Level subject, you are told at the point of enquiry, along with what is available instead and how the session would run. A disclosed coverage limit is worth more than a confident silence followed by a mismatched tutor.

faqs.question: When should an IB student in the UAE start working with an online tutor?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families do, and the reason is the coursework calendar rather than the exams. The highest-value window is the second half of DP1 and the first term of DP2, because the mathematics exploration, the scientific investigations, the Extended Essay drafts and the TOK exhibition are all live then, and those marks are banked long before study leave. A student who begins in DP1 is buying feedback on work that still counts. A student who begins in March of DP2 is buying paper technique, which is a genuinely smaller lever. If you are choosing a term, choose the one that contains a deadline.

faqs.question: How late in DP2 can online IB tuition in the UAE still change a predicted grade?
faqs.answer: A predicted grade is formed from the evidence the school holds, mostly the mocks and internal assessments, so it changes when that evidence changes. Realistically, work that lands before the mock still moves the prediction; work that lands after it moves the final result rather than the prediction. Online IB tuition in the UAE started eight to ten weeks before mocks can show up in a predicted grade. Started in April, it is aimed at the paper, not the prediction. Tell the tutor which of the two you are chasing, because the session plans differ completely.

faqs.question: Which IB deadlines are set by my child's school and which by the IB?
faqs.answer: The IB sets the exam session and the windows in which the school must upload candidate work. The school sets everything your child actually experiences as a deadline: when the exploration is due, when the Extended Essay draft is handed to the supervisor, when the TOK essay is collected, when the mocks run. Those dates differ between two campuses in the same emirate, sometimes by several weeks. Ask the Diploma Programme coordinator for the written internal calendar in September of DP1, and plan tuition against that document rather than against anything a tutoring site tells you is typical.

faqs.question: When do Cambridge and Pearson run their exam series?
faqs.answer: Cambridge International runs a June series and a November series, and those are the two sittings open to a candidate entered through a UAE centre. Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests run on their own windows earlier in the year, but they are diagnostic tests for younger year groups rather than IGCSE series, and they are easy to mistake for one. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, with the November 2026 papers finishing on 19 November 2026 and results reaching students the following January. Those are the boards' own published positions, read in October 2026. The IB, by contrast, runs the May session that almost every UAE school sits and a November session used by a minority. We do not print IB dates here because they could not be verified from the IB directly; your coordinator and ibo.org are the sources for those.

faqs.question: Why does the entry deadline fall months before the exam?
faqs.answer: Because entries drive logistics: paper allocation, zone timetables, access arrangements and component choices all have to be fixed before material is printed and shipped. Pearson's International GCSE November 2026 series shows the gap clearly. The written papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and the entry deadline printed on that series timetable sat months earlier in the year, long before any mock result could have informed it. Cambridge works the same way across its June and November series: entries close well ahead of the papers, and a subject added after the deadline is simply not sat. If a subject or tier change is under discussion at home, raise it with the exams officer well before the deadline, not after the mock results arrive.

faqs.question: What is a Cambridge exam zone, and why does the timetable version matter?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the timetable. The board states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. For a UAE family this is a two-minute task with a very large downside: ask the exams officer which zone your school is in, download that version of the timetable, and work from it alone. Timetables circulating in parent groups are frequently the wrong zone, and a missed paper is not a mark problem.

faqs.question: How does the tuition schedule change during Ramadan and Eid?
faqs.answer: School days shorten across the emirates, afternoons become unproductive, and serious study moves to the hours after Iftar. Sessions move with it: shorter and more frequent, scheduled as post-Iftar sessions and agreed a fortnight in advance rather than cancelled week by week. Ramadan shifts about eleven days earlier each year, which has pushed it into the mock and pre-exam window rather than a quiet part of the year. Eid al-Fitr then removes the last clear revision week before study leave, so the fortnight before it is the one worth protecting with extra sessions rather than the week after.

faqs.question: How many weeks does an Internal Assessment take from idea to final draft?
faqs.answer: Plan on a term rather than a fortnight. A workable sequence is two to three weeks settling a question that can actually be answered with available data, two to three weeks collecting or sourcing that data, two weeks on a first full draft, then a criterion check and a revision pass. Compressing it is where the marks go, because the evaluation criterion rewards reflection that only exists if something went wrong early enough to be discussed. A tutor in that window tests feasibility first and only then reads drafts, which is the opposite order to the one panicking families usually want.

faqs.question: How long does the Extended Essay take, and when should the first reflection session happen?
faqs.answer: The IB recommends around forty hours of student work for an essay of no more than 4,000 words, and schools generally run the first reflection session with the Extended Essay supervisor late in DP1 once a research question exists. Treat that session as the real deadline, because a question that cannot be answered in 4,000 words is the single most common structural failure and it is cheapest to fix before any reading is done. Tutoring here is question feasibility, source quality and rehearsal for the supervisor conversations. The writing is the student's own, start to finish.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the TOK essay without crossing the academic-honesty line?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the line is clear. A tutor can unpack the prescribed title, test whether the argument answers that title rather than a neighbouring one, press on the quality of the real-world examples, and point out where the 1,600 words are being spent on description instead of analysis. What a tutor cannot do is supply any of the prose. If feedback comes back as replacement sentences rather than questions and criterion references, that is not teaching, and the student is the one who carries the malpractice risk under the IB's rules, not the tutor.

faqs.question: What happens if a grade looks wrong on results day?
faqs.answer: The route is an enquiry upon results, and the school's coordinator submits it rather than the family. There is a deadline that sits close to release, measured in days, and a fee depending on the route chosen. Before asking for it, ask the subject teacher what the script and the internal evidence suggest, because a remark can move a grade down as well as up. Put the request in writing in the same week, and run the university conversation in parallel rather than waiting for the outcome. Deferral requests made early read very differently from those made in late August.

faqs.question: Is the November session a realistic option after a disappointing May?
faqs.answer: For one or two subjects, often yes. A minority of UAE candidates use the November session as a retake route. The constraints are administrative rather than academic: entries close well before those papers, the school or an approved examination centre has to make them, and a retake has to be agreed with whichever university holds the offer. The decision therefore belongs in the week after results, not September. The teaching plan for a retake looks different too: it starts from the actual script and the enquiry outcome rather than from the syllabus.

faqs.question: When in the final year should we start the Ministry of Education equivalency file?
faqs.answer: Begin gathering documents before results, and open the file as soon as certificates exist. The slow parts are rarely the academic requirements; they are attestation of documents issued in another country and name mismatches between a certificate and a passport. For the British track the published requirement is five accredited subjects at GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Levels. Verify your own case with the Ministry or the emirate's attestation authority, because no tutoring platform should be your source for a regulatory process.

faqs.question: Does the MoHRE private tuition work permit apply to an online tutor?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals providing private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure you see quoted with suspicion. MoHRE's own service page is the place to check the current position for a tutor resident in the UAE.

faqs.question: How do lessons work if the specialist is not based in the UAE?
faqs.answer: The same way they work if the tutor lives in Dubai: one-to-one over live video, in a slot set to Gulf Standard Time. For niche Higher Level subjects the pool of UAE-resident specialists is genuinely thin outside Dubai and Abu Dhabi, and when nobody local is free we say so at the point of enquiry and tell you where the tutor is working from. What we will not do is present a non-UAE tutor as a local one, or route a UAE family to a foreign phone number without saying what it is.

faqs.question: Can we pause sessions during mocks and the heaviest coursework weeks?
faqs.answer: You can, though it is usually the wrong instinct. Mock fortnight is when a tutor is most useful, because a marked mock script is the best diagnostic available all year and it expires quickly as a teaching tool. The weeks worth pausing are the ones immediately after a major upload, when the student has nothing live to work on. A better default is to change the shape rather than stop: 45 minutes on a marked script during mocks, then back to the normal slot once the results and the feedback are in hand.

faqs.question: Do Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies take time away from Diploma revision?
faqs.answer: They occupy real timetable hours, so yes, and the arithmetic should be done before you book tuition. These subjects are required in UAE private schools regardless of the international curriculum licensed, and in Dubai KHDA sets out how they run: separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, Standard Arabic as the language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. For a Diploma student that is several periods a week that revision cannot use, which is an argument for planning the weekly tuition slot around them rather than against them.

faqs.question: How many sessions a week does an exam-year student need, and when should that rise?
faqs.answer: One weekly session per subject through the term is the normal shape, and it should rise at two specific points rather than gradually. The first is the month before a coursework deadline, when a second session a week buys criterion-level feedback on successive drafts. The second is after the mocks, when the useful pattern becomes two shorter slots a week with a marked paper between them. Going to three or four sessions a week in the final fortnight rarely helps, because at that stage the limiting factor is marked practice and sleep rather than contact hours.

ib-online-tutor.closingHeading: Start from the date, then book the hours
ib-online-tutor.closingBody: Send three lines: the subject and level, the school, and the date you are working towards. That might be an Internal Assessment deadline in three weeks, the mock window, or the first paper of the May session. We match one subject specialist at that level, arrange one free trial lesson in that subject before any payment, and if nobody is free in your slot we say so in the same reply. Lessons run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, in every emirate. Bring the coordinator's internal calendar to the first session if you have it; it is worth more than anything else you could send us.

ib-past-papers-practice.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover the Diploma subjects UAE families most often ask for paper practice in. Each works through marked scripts rather than slides, so a session ends with a specific correction rather than a general sense that revision happened.

intro.heading: Why a stack of printed papers rarely moves a grade on its own
paragraphs: Almost every Diploma student in the UAE has a folder of past papers by the start of the second year. Very few of them gain much from it. The folder gets opened, the first question looks unfamiliar, the student checks the answer, decides they understood it, and moves on. Four hours disappear and nothing is diagnosed. The paper was never the problem; the absence of marking was.

A past paper is a measuring instrument, not a teaching one. It tells you what your child can do under a clock, in a room, against a mark scheme written by someone who has never met them. That information is worth a great deal, but only if someone reads the output. A script marked properly shows whether a lost mark came from not knowing the content, not reading the command term, not showing the method, or simply running out of minutes on question seven. Those four causes have four different fixes, and three of them have nothing to do with revising the topic again.

The second thing that goes wrong in the UAE specifically is sourcing. Past papers for IB subjects are not public documents in the way GCSE papers often are. They sit behind the IB's own resource channels, which are reached through your child's school, or they are bought from the official store. Everything else circulating on WhatsApp groups and free download sites is of unknown provenance, frequently from a replaced syllabus, and sometimes material that was never meant to leave an exam room. A student who spends March on papers from a guide that no longer applies has practised the wrong examination.

Then there is the calendar. Paper practice has a correct season. Attempting full timed papers in the first term of the Diploma, before a syllabus has been taught, produces a low mark and a demoralised student and measures nothing useful. Leaving all of it to the final fortnight produces exhaustion and no time to act on what the papers reveal. The useful window is wider than most families think and starts earlier than most families start, and it narrows sharply once the entry deadline has passed and the timetable is fixed.

This page is the practical version. It covers where IB papers legitimately come from, how to tell a current paper from a stale one, what timed and untimed practice each achieve, how to mark a script against a mark scheme without either flattering or crushing the student, what the command terms actually demand, why the same raw mark converts to different grades in different sessions, and what the published Cambridge and Pearson dates mean for IGCSE families sitting the board exams alongside. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, which is what makes a specialist in a particular Higher Level subject reachable from Fujairah or Al Ain rather than only from a Dubai postcode.
bullets: An unmarked paper tells you nothing; a marked script tells you which of four failure types applies
IB papers reach families through the school or the official store, not through download sites
A paper from a replaced subject guide practises an examination your child will not sit
Timed practice has a season, and it opens earlier than most families assume
Raw marks do not convert to grades at a fixed percentage from one session to the next

ib-past-papers-practice.programmesIntro: Paper practice means something different in each IB programme, because the assessment it points at is different. Here is what each programme examines externally, and what that implies for a UAE family planning practice.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examination and therefore no past papers. Assessment is through the exhibition in the final year, teacher judgement and portfolio evidence. Any provider offering PYP past papers is selling something the programme does not produce. What a PYP child benefits from instead is mathematical fluency, reading stamina and written explanation, because those are the three capacities that make later timed assessment survivable.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah, PYP children also sit mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons set by the emirate regulator alongside the PYP framework. Those subjects do carry school assessments, and they are often the first place a non-Arabic-speaking family discovers their child is behind. Work there is content teaching, not paper practice.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP assessment is criterion-referenced against four criteria per subject, marked out of eight each. Schools that take the optional eAssessment at the end of Year 11 sit on-screen examinations and ePortfolios, and specimen material for those does exist. For schools that do not, the useful practice is criterion-referenced task practice: being given a task sheet, a criterion strand and a mark band, and learning to write to it.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools split roughly into those that run MYP to eAssessment and those that run MYP then move pupils onto IGCSE for Years 10 and 11. Which one your child's school does changes everything about Year 10 and 11 practice, and it is the single most useful question to put to the school before planning any revision. A parent who assumes IGCSE and finds eAssessment loses a term.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is where past papers earn their reputation. Each subject sets externally marked papers in a May or November session, with distinct papers testing distinct things, plus internally assessed coursework. Higher Level subjects generally carry an additional paper or an extended component that Standard Level does not. Practice therefore has to be paper-specific, because a child strong on one paper can be weak on another in the same subject.
programmes.countryNote: The overwhelming majority of UAE schools enter candidates for the May session, which puts the examination period in the UAE's exam-heavy late spring, after Ramadan in most years. A smaller number of schools, and almost all private candidates retaking, use the November session. Confirm your child's session with the school's IB coordinator before building any practice plan around a date.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a language development portfolio and a personal and professional skills course. The Diploma courses within it are examined exactly as they are in the full Diploma, so past paper practice applies to those components in the normal way. The career-related study and reflective project are not examined by paper.
programmes.countryNote: CP provision in the UAE is thin compared with the Diploma, concentrated in a small number of Dubai and Abu Dhabi schools. Families moving into the country mid-programme often find there is no local CP place at all and have to choose between the full Diploma and a British sixth form. That is a decision to take with the school, not with a tutor.

ib-past-papers-practice.subjectsIntro: Paper practice is only useful subject by subject, because each subject loses marks somewhere specific. Below is what each paper set actually tests and the pattern of loss a marked script usually reveals.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The non-calculator paper and the calculator paper reward entirely different habits, and most students are much weaker on one. Marked scripts typically show method marks thrown away by jumping to an answer, and accuracy marks lost by rounding early. Higher Level adds an extended investigative paper that cannot be revised for by topic, only by practising the genre.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics carry much of the paper, and the losses are usually in interpretation rather than computation: a correct regression with no comment on what it means in context earns part marks. Technology use is assumed, so a student who cannot drive their calculator fluently loses time they need for the written reasoning.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Multiple-choice sections punish shallow understanding of definitions, while the longer structured questions punish poor diagram and graph work. On marked scripts, the recurring loss is units and significant figures on otherwise correct calculations, and verbal explanations that restate the question instead of naming the mechanism.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, equilibrium and energetics generate the heaviest losses in UAE cohorts we see. The data booklet is permitted and most students underuse it. Extended-response questions frequently ask for an explanation in terms of structure and bonding, and an answer that describes without explaining stops at half marks.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Biology papers are a reading test as much as a knowledge test: unfamiliar data, graphs and experiments the student has never seen. Practice on past papers is especially valuable here because stamina with novel stimulus material is itself the skill. Losses cluster in command-term misreads and in answers that give one named example where three were required.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy is worth real marks and is the cheapest thing to fix. Beyond that, the extended-response papers reward evaluation, and most scripts stop at explanation. Higher Level carries a quantitative paper that students from a Standard Level maths background routinely underprepare for because it looks like a smaller component than it is.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The case-study paper is released in advance of the examination, which makes it the one component where preparation can be genuinely targeted. Most lost marks come from tool-dropping without application: naming a framework and not using it on the stimulus. Past papers show how narrow the gap between a described tool and an applied one is.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Guided analysis of an unseen text is the component that most rewards past-paper work, because the only way to get faster at an unseen is to meet more of them. Losses are in unsupported assertion and in structural analysis that notices features without connecting them to effect. The Higher Level essay is coursework, not an examined paper.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Pseudocode under time pressure is where most marks go missing, along with questions on the prescribed case study at Higher Level, which changes periodically and cannot be revised from older papers. Older papers remain useful for the theory sections and misleading for the case study, which is a good example of why paper vintage matters.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Studies have to be named, dated and used, not merely referred to. Marked scripts show students losing most of the available marks on the longest questions by narrating a study instead of deploying it as evidence for a claim. Practice here is partly about building a usable bank of studies and partly about essay architecture under a clock.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: The source paper has a fixed question architecture that repeats across sessions, which makes it the most trainable paper in the Diploma. Students lose marks by paraphrasing sources rather than using them, and by ignoring provenance when value and limitation marks are explicitly available for it.

ib-past-papers-practice.regionsTitle: Paper practice across the seven emirates
ib-past-papers-practice.regionsIntro: Where a family lives in the UAE changes which regulator oversees the school, which session the school enters, and how realistic an evening session is once the school run is done. Here is what differs.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The largest IB cohort in the country and the easiest place to find a school-run revision programme, which means paper practice at home should supplement rather than duplicate it. KHDA oversees the private sector here. Evening sessions from 18:00 generally work once Sheikh Zayed Road has cleared.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and its professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid tutoring of their own enrolled pupils. Families in Khalifa City, Al Reef and Saadiyat usually run practice sessions after 17:30 because of the school-bus timings on the island.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves curricula, courses and assessment methods, not just fees. IB provision is narrower than in Dubai, and many Sharjah families drive into Dubai for school, which pushes a workable session start later into the evening.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a smaller international sector and noticeably fewer local specialists for Higher Level sciences and Higher Level maths. This is where live online delivery changes the available tutor pool most sharply, because the alternative is a long drive or nothing.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here fall under the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority. Diploma places are limited, so a significant number of Ajman families commute to Sharjah or Dubai, and practice sessions have to fit a two-leg commute on either side.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The emirate's Department of Knowledge regulates private education and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. RAK appears in almost no tutoring provider's coverage list, which is a sourcing problem for parents rather than a demand problem.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education supervision applies, and the IB cohort is small enough that a subject-specific specialist is very unlikely to live within driving distance. Live video sessions remove the geography from the problem entirely, which matters more here than in any other emirate.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under federal Ministry of Education supervision, with the smallest private international sector in the country. Families here typically plan around a school in another emirate, so the practical constraint on paper practice is travel time rather than tutor availability.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai's Diploma cohort sits across a broad set of IB World Schools, and their internal mock calendars differ by several weeks. That matters because a mock is the most useful full-paper data point of the year, and the practice plan either leads into it or wastes it.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain IB schools
schoolClusters.note: Abu Dhabi's Diploma provision is concentrated on the islands and in the eastern suburbs, under ADEK oversight. Several of these schools run their own after-school clinics, so an external tutor is most useful on a specific paper rather than a whole subject.
schools: The International School of Choueifat Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.note: Provision thins quickly north of Dubai, and families frequently cross an emirate border for school while living under a different regulator. Practice timing here is set by the commute more than by anything academic.
schools: Our Own English High School Fujairah

ib-past-papers-practice.modesIntro: Paper practice is not one activity. These are the three formats UAE families use most, and they suit different points in the year rather than different budgets.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one with script review
modes.description: The student attempts a section or a whole paper between sessions, submits it, and the session is spent on the marked script rather than on new teaching. This is the format that produces the most change per hour, because the agenda is set by evidence rather than by a syllabus checklist. It works from roughly thirty weeks out through to the final fortnight.
bullets: One paper or one section attempted between sessions, under timing
Marked against the published mark scheme before the session starts
Session agenda set by the losses, not by the next topic in the book
Running error log carried forward week to week
Delivered live over video with a shared screen on the script

modes.title: Pre-mock intensive block
modes.description: A short, dense block of sessions in the four to six weeks before the school's mock examinations, aimed at making the mock a genuine measurement rather than a shock. Mocks are the only full-length, properly invigilated data point most students get before the real session, and a wasted mock costs a term of planning information.
bullets: Two or three sessions a week for four to six weeks
Full papers under exam conditions and exam timing
Separate attention to the paper the student is weakest on
Deliberate practice of exam-day sequencing and question order
A written list of what to do differently after the mock returns

modes.title: Single-paper clinic
modes.description: A short series aimed at one component only: an investigative maths paper, a source-based history paper, a quantitative economics paper, a pseudocode section. Families use this when a marked mock shows one paper dragging an otherwise solid subject down, and it is the cheapest useful intervention available in exam term.
bullets: Scoped to one paper, typically three to six sessions
Built from past questions on that component across several sessions
Focused on the paper's recurring question architecture
Priced and planned as a block with a defined end point
Suitable from the mock results onward

modes.title: Final-fortnight review
modes.description: In the last two weeks, new content is not learnable and full papers are often counterproductive because a bad score at that stage damages more than it diagnoses. The work becomes selective: timed single questions on known weak spots, mark-scheme language drills, and the sequencing decisions a student makes in the first five minutes of a paper.
bullets: Short timed questions rather than full papers
Mark-scheme phrasing practised until it is automatic
A fixed plan for the first and last five minutes of each paper
No new topics introduced
Sessions kept short and early enough to protect sleep

sections.heading: What parents are actually asking for when they search for IB past papers practice
paragraphs: IB past papers practice in the UAE means sitting authentic examination questions under examination conditions and then having the script read by someone who knows the mark scheme. The search is almost never a request for more PDFs. Families who type it have usually already found files; what they cannot find is someone to mark them and say what the losses mean.

There are three distinct requests hiding inside the same query. The first is sourcing: where do legitimate papers for this subject and this syllabus come from. The second is sequencing: in what order and at what point in the year should they be attempted. The third is diagnosis: given this marked script, what should change next week. A provider who answers only the first has handed you a folder, which is where this started.

The honest position on the first request is that IB examination material is copyright and reaches students through their school's access to the IB's own resource channels, or through purchase from the official store. We do not host, reproduce or supply IB papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables or subject guides, and nobody who respects your child's position with their school should. What a tutor does is work with the material your child already has legitimate access to, and tell you precisely which components to ask the school for.

On the second and third requests, this page is specific. Sequencing is set out as a schedule counted backwards from the examination session, because that is the only direction the calendar runs in. Diagnosis is set out as four failure types, each with a different remedy, because treating a command-term misread as a knowledge gap is how a term of revision produces no movement at all.

sections.heading: Where IB papers legitimately come from, and where they do not
paragraphs: Past IB examination papers are not in the public domain. They are copyright material released by the IB through controlled channels, which is why a parent cannot simply download a complete set the way they can for some national qualifications. Understanding the channels saves a lot of wasted effort and avoids putting a student in an awkward position with their school.

The first and best route is the school. Diploma coordinators and subject teachers have access to the IB's programme resource channels, which carry past papers, mark schemes, subject guides, specimen material and examiner reports for current syllabuses. A direct, specific request works far better than a general one: naming the subject, the level, the paper and the sessions you want makes it a two-minute task for a teacher rather than an open-ended one. Most teachers say yes to that request and are glad someone is planning.

The second route is purchase. The IB sells past papers and related material through its official store, by subject, level and session. This matters for private candidates and for families whose school is cautious about releasing material, and it is the only route that does not depend on anyone's goodwill. The third category is everything else: free download sites, shared drives, social-media groups and resellers. Some of that material is genuine and out of date; some is from a replaced guide; some was never released at all. None of it is worth the risk when the first two routes exist.

The table below sets out what each route gives you. The practical advice is to secure mark schemes at the same time as papers, because an unmarked paper is a measuring instrument with no scale on it, and families routinely obtain one without the other.

sections.heading: A paper-practice plan counted backwards from the session
paragraphs: The examination date is the one fixed point in the Diploma. Everything else is negotiable, and the only sensible way to plan practice is to start at the papers and count back. UAE schools overwhelmingly enter candidates for the May session, which puts the heavy practice months in the UAE academic calendar's second and third terms.

The common error is to treat the whole second year as one undifferentiated revision period. It is not. There are at least five distinct phases, each with a different right activity. Attempting full timed papers nine months out, when half the syllabus is untaught, produces a score that measures coverage rather than ability and tells a student they are failing when they are merely early. Doing single untimed questions in the final fortnight, when the need is pace and sequencing, wastes the one thing that is genuinely scarce.

Note what sits outside the practice schedule but inside the same calendar: the entry deadline. Candidates are entered by the school months before the first paper, and the registration decisions taken then — which level, which subjects, whether a retake is in play — are far harder to change afterwards. A family counting backwards hits that deadline well before they hit the examination, which is the main reason to count backwards at all.

The schedule below is a template, not a prescription. A student who arrives with a subject already secure compresses the early phases; a student joining a UAE school mid-Diploma from another curriculum may need the earliest phase to run alongside catch-up teaching rather than after it.

sections.heading: Untimed, timed, and timed in sequence are three different exercises
paragraphs: Most students use one mode of practice all year and wonder why progress stalls. The three modes measure and build different things, and the order matters.

Untimed, open-book practice is for learning the shape of a question. The student is allowed to look things up, take as long as they like and change their answer. Its purpose is recognition: meeting the twelve ways a particular concept gets examined so that none of them is a surprise later. Scoring it is almost pointless, and marking it as though it were an examination is actively harmful, because the student concludes they cannot do something they have simply not yet practised.

Timed single-paper practice is the measurement. Closed book, correct duration, correct equipment, phone in another room. This is the only mode that produces a number worth tracking, and it is the mode families underuse because it is unpleasant and takes a committed two or three hours. One properly timed paper is worth four casual ones, and a student who has never finished a paper inside its own time limit does not know whether their problem is knowledge or pace.

Timed in sequence is the mode almost nobody practises and the one the examination actually tests. Real sessions put two or three papers in the same subject within days, sometimes two papers on the same morning. The capacity to write a strong second paper after a difficult first one is a trainable skill, and the first time most students experience it is in the examination hall. Running one sequence pair in the final six weeks, at the real spacing, is usually enough to make the real thing unremarkable.
bullets: Untimed and open-book: for recognising question types, not for scoring
Timed single paper: the only mode that generates a trustworthy number
Timed in sequence: trains recovery between papers, almost never practised
Correct equipment every time, including the permitted calculator and booklets
Phone out of the room, or the timing data is worthless

sections.heading: Command terms decide what a question is worth before the content does
paragraphs: The IB publishes command terms for every subject, and they are not stylistic. A command term sets the cognitive level required and, in practice, the number of marks available. A student who answers a six-mark discuss question with the content of a two-mark state answer has not misunderstood the topic; they have misread the instruction, and the mark scheme gives them no way back.

This is the most common single loss we see on marked UAE scripts, and the most fixable. It takes very little subject teaching and a great deal of repetition: reading the stem, naming the command term aloud, saying what structure that term demands, and only then writing. Students resist it because it feels slow, and then stop resisting once they see a marked script where four questions were answered one level below the instruction.

The table gives the terms that recur across the sciences, humanities and mathematics, what the examiner is looking for, and the structural signature of an answer that satisfies the term. Mark values vary by subject and paper, so treat the figures as the usual band rather than as a rule. The underlying point holds everywhere: the verb is the specification.

One caution worth stating plainly. Command-term drilling is a technique for expressing understanding, not a substitute for having it. A student who can structure an evaluation but has no content to evaluate ends up writing elegant, empty paragraphs, and examiners are entirely used to spotting those. The sequence is content first, then the structure that lets the content earn what it is worth.

sections.heading: When the guide changes, an old paper teaches the wrong examination
paragraphs: IB subject guides are revised on a rolling cycle, and each revision has a first-assessment year. Papers from before that year were written against different content, different assessment models and sometimes different paper structures. They are not useless, but they are useful for specific things and misleading for others, and almost no family is told the difference.

The first step is factual, and it takes one message to the school: which guide is my child assessed against, and what was its first assessment year. Every current subject guide states this, and the DP coordinator knows it. Once you have that year, every paper is sortable. Papers from the current guide are the gold standard and there are usually only a handful of sessions' worth, which is exactly why the older ones get used.

Older papers remain genuinely valuable for content that did not change, for question styles that persist, and for sheer volume of practice on a topic that survived the revision. They become actively harmful when they test removed content, when the paper structure differs enough that timing practice transfers badly, or when a prescribed element — a case study, a set text, a named option — has been replaced. A student spending February on a removed option is doing homework for an examination that no longer exists.

The table gives a component-by-component read on what survives a guide change and what does not. Where you are unsure about a specific topic, the subject guide's own content list settles it in a minute, and that is a document your child's school has.

sections.heading: The error log that turns a marked script into next week's lesson
paragraphs: A marked paper has done half its job. The other half is converting the losses into a short, specific list that drives the next few sessions, and then checking weeks later whether the same error recurs. Without that second half, a student sits ten papers and makes the same mistake in all ten, which is the single most common pattern on scripts we review in exam term.

The log is deliberately crude: date, paper, question, the mark lost, and which of a small number of error types it was. Four or five types is enough. A knowledge gap means the content was not known. A command misread means the content was known and answered at the wrong level. A method loss means the thinking was right and the working did not show it, or units and precision were dropped. A timing loss means the question was never properly attempted. A stimulus misread means the data, graph or source was misunderstood before any subject knowledge was applied.

Sorting a term's losses by type usually surprises families, because the distribution is rarely what they assumed. A student who has been revising content for six weeks frequently turns out to be losing most of their marks to command misreads and timing, both of which are fixed by technique rather than by content. That is a much faster repair than another pass through the textbook, and it is only visible once the losses are counted by type.

The table gives the types, their signature on a script, the remedy, and how to confirm the remedy worked. The confirmation column is the one families skip and the one that makes the whole exercise worth doing.

sections.heading: Raw marks, boundaries and why 62 per cent is not a grade
paragraphs: Families treat a raw percentage on a past paper as though it converts directly to a Diploma grade. It does not, and the gap between the two is wide enough to cause real distress in both directions. A raw mark is a number out of the paper's total. A grade is awarded after grade boundaries are set for that specific session, and those boundaries move.

They move for a reason. If a paper turns out harder than intended, the boundary for a given grade falls, because the award process is meant to hold the standard constant rather than the arithmetic. A mark that was a 5 in one session can sit in a different band in another. Boundaries are set after marking, per subject, per level, per session, and are published to schools afterwards. That is why a tutor who tells you a score is definitely a 6 is telling you something they cannot know.

The practical consequences are worth stating. First, do not publish or rely on an old boundary table as though it were a conversion chart; treat it as an indication of the usual range. Second, track raw marks against themselves over time rather than against a predicted grade, because the trend in your own scores is real data and the grade conversion is an estimate. Third, be careful with the arithmetic of paper weightings: a strong performance on a lightly weighted paper does less for the final grade than a modest improvement on a heavily weighted one, and students routinely spend their effort on the wrong component.

We do not reproduce or supply grade-boundary tables. Your child's school holds the published boundaries for past sessions and the subject teacher can put a raw mark into context far better than any external estimate, because they also know the cohort. The useful question to ask is not what grade this score is, but which component is costing the most weighted marks.

sections.heading: IGCSE families sitting Cambridge or Pearson papers alongside
paragraphs: A large number of UAE families have one child in the Diploma and another in IGCSE, or a child who moved from IGCSE into the Diploma and still has board examinations in play. Cambridge and Pearson publish their dates and administrative deadlines openly, which makes their calendars easier to plan against than the IB's, and there are two details that catch UAE families specifically.

The first is series. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examinations are available in May/June and November each year. Past papers are published by series, so practice material has to be matched to the series your child is actually entered for, and a November candidate practising only on June papers is working from a narrower set than they need to.

The second is zones. Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after using the wrong zone timetable. A UAE centre is not in the same zone as a UK one, so a timetable copied from a British school's website is the wrong document. Ask the school's examinations officer which zone your centre sits in, and work from the official timetable for it.

Entry deadlines sit a long way before the papers, which is the single most useful thing in the published calendars. The table uses Cambridge's own series structure and Pearson's published dates as worked examples of that gap: Pearson's International GCSE November 2026 papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026 and the results only reached students the following January, while entries for a Cambridge series close months before its first paper, on the date the centre confirms in the statement of entry. Always check the live official timetable before relying on any date, because provisional timetables are revised.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and the papers that are not yet public
paragraphs: Paper practice has an integrity boundary and it is sharper than most families realise. The IB treats unauthorised access to examination material as malpractice, and the consequences land on the student rather than on whoever supplied the file. A page about past papers that does not say this is not being helpful.

Three things sit clearly on the wrong side of the line. Obtaining or sharing a paper before its session has been sat anywhere in the world, including across time zones, is unauthorised access to live material. Buying worked answers to a current component and presenting them as the student's own is malpractice. And obtaining completed coursework of any kind, for any subject, is the offence that ends Diploma candidacies, which is why one of the sites ranking for these searches sells exactly that and should be avoided on those grounds alone.

On the legitimate side, almost everything a family actually wants is permitted. A student may sit any released past paper. A tutor may mark it, explain the mark scheme, model an answer to a past question, teach the content it tests and coach the technique. On internally assessed work, a tutor may teach the underlying skills, discuss a proposed approach, give feedback on the student's own draft and explain what the published criteria reward. What a tutor must not do is produce any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay, or edit a draft to the point where the words are no longer the student's. We say this to students directly in the first session, because it protects them.

There is also a copyright dimension. IB, Cambridge and Pearson examination papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are their property. We reference them and point families to the official sources rather than hosting or distributing copies, and we would say the same about any provider that offers you a complete paper archive as an inducement.
bullets: Released past paper, sat and marked: entirely legitimate
Live or unsat material, in any time zone: unauthorised access to examination material
Purchased answers or completed coursework: malpractice, with the student carrying the consequence
Feedback on the student's own draft: permitted, and the only form of coursework help we give
Papers and mark schemes: referenced and linked, never hosted or redistributed by us

sections.heading: What one-to-one IB exam practice costs across the UAE market
paragraphs: Published rates in this market are scarce, and three of the six providers that rank for these searches quote no figure at all. Two of the three that do quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. The bands below are what the market charges, drawn from competitors' own published rates and from Bestimate's Dubai 2026 tutoring rate table. They are the market, not an IB Gram price list.

The pattern across the bands is consistent. A university-student tutor working online sits at the bottom, from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. A qualified subject tutor online runs roughly AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A visiting tutor who travels to a home in the Dubai market costs AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is in the number, with Bestimate putting the band at AED 180 to AED 350. A named IB or IGCSE specialist runs AED 200 to AED 450 and upward, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium examiner-branded provision reaches AED 650, which is BartyED's published figure.

Marking changes the arithmetic in a way hourly rates hide. A tutor who marks a three-hour paper properly has spent close to an hour on it before the session begins, and the honest versions of this market either include that or price it separately. When comparing quotes, ask directly whether script marking is inside the hourly rate, because a cheaper hour that excludes marking is not cheaper for paper practice specifically. Monthly packages seen in this market run to AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits.

For context on the household budget these sit inside, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Our own model is a free trial lesson first and a plan agreed afterwards, rather than a published rate card, because an exam-term block for one paper and a two-year Diploma plan are not comparable products.

sections.heading: Live online paper practice against a visiting tutor, on the merits
paragraphs: Families search for a tutor who will come to the house, and the honest answer is that for paper practice specifically, the format that works best is the one where the script is on a shared screen and the specialist is whoever is best at that paper. IB Gram delivers tutoring to UAE families as one-to-one live online lessons. Home visits are a service we run in India only, and we would rather say so on this page than discover it at the booking stage.

The case is not that video is a tolerable substitute. It is that the constraint a visiting tutor imposes is severe in this particular task. A home visit limits your child to tutors within a reasonable drive of your address at the hour your child is free. For a Higher Level subject, in Al Ain or Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain, that pool may contain nobody who has taught the current guide. Over video, the pool is everyone who teaches that subject at that level, and the selection criterion becomes the paper rather than the postcode.

The mechanics also favour the screen. Paper practice runs on documents: the script, the mark scheme, the examiner's report, the error log. All four are easier to annotate together on a shared screen than on paper across a kitchen table, and the annotated version is still there next week. A student can send a photographed script on Tuesday and arrive at Thursday's session to find it already marked, which is time that a visiting model spends on marking in the room or on travel.

Travel is the hidden cost. Two sessions a week at a villa in Khalifa City or Arabian Ranches means four journeys, and that time is paid for inside the hourly rate whether or not anyone itemises it. process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the paper
process.description: Not just the subject. For paper practice the useful unit is the component: the non-calculator maths paper, the source-based history paper, the quantitative economics paper. Send the last marked script if you have one, and the school's mock dates. That is enough for us to say what the work should be and roughly how many sessions it needs.

process.title: A free trial lesson on a real question
process.description: The trial is a working session on an actual past question in your child's subject, not a consultation. By the end of it you will have seen how the tutor marks, what they notice on a script, and whether your child talks to them. If that does not work, nothing has been booked and nothing has been paid.

process.title: Sort the papers you already have
process.description: Before any schedule, we check which papers match the guide your child is assessed against and which predate it. We also list exactly what to request from the DP coordinator by subject, level, paper and session. Families regularly find they have fifteen papers, four of which are current and useful.

process.title: Agree a phase, not a term
process.description: Where your child sits relative to the first paper determines whether the work is untimed question practice, half papers, full papers or final-fortnight drills. We set the phase, the number of papers and who marks them, and revisit after the mock, which is the point at which most plans need adjusting.

process.title: Run the loop, and keep the log
process.description: Paper attempted between sessions, marked before the session, session spent on the losses, error log updated. Repeat errors escalate out of general practice into targeted drilling. The log is the record you can look at in April and see whether anything actually changed.

process.title: Change the tutor if the fit is wrong
process.description: A tutor who is excellent on one paper may not be the right person for another, and some pairings simply do not work. Tell us early and we move your child; there is no argument to be had about it and no notice period to serve. The alternative is paying for sessions that nobody is getting anything from.

whyPoints.title: We mark the script, not the subject
whyPoints.description: The session agenda comes from what the mark scheme actually took away, which is why families notice progress in places they were not revising. A term of content review does nothing for a student whose losses are command misreads and timing, and you cannot know which it is until someone counts.

whyPoints.title: We will not host or supply papers
whyPoints.description: IB, Cambridge and Pearson material is their copyright, and unreleased material is a malpractice exposure for your child. We tell you precisely what to request from the school, point you at the official store for anything else, and work with what you legitimately hold.

whyPoints.title: Paper vintage is checked before anything is scheduled
whyPoints.description: The first thing we establish is which guide your child is assessed against and what its first assessment year was. Sorting a folder by that one fact routinely removes a third of it from the practice plan and prevents a month of work on removed content.

We do not produce any part of an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or TOK essay, and we say so in the first session. faqs.question: Where can my child legally get IB past papers in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Two routes. The first is the school: DP coordinators and subject teachers have access to the IB's own resource channels, which hold past papers, mark schemes, specimen papers and examiner reports for current guides. Ask by subject, level, paper and session rather than generally, because that makes it a short task for a teacher. The second is purchase from the IB's official store, which sells papers by subject, level and session and works for private candidates too. Free download sites and shared drives are the third category, and they frequently carry off-syllabus or unreleased material. We do not host or supply papers ourselves.

faqs.question: How many past papers should a Diploma student complete in each subject?
faqs.answer: Fewer than families expect, marked far better than families expect. A reasonable target across the final thirty weeks is eight to twelve full papers per subject, built up from individual questions and half papers rather than attempted cold from the start. The constraint is marking capacity, not paper supply. Twelve papers properly marked, with an error log and repeat errors drilled, moves a grade; twenty-five papers checked against an answer key does very little. If time is short, cut the number of papers and keep the marking.

faqs.question: Should past papers be done timed or untimed?
faqs.answer: Both, in order. Untimed and open-book practice is for meeting the question types and learning what each concept looks like when it is examined; scoring it is close to meaningless. Timed closed-book practice is the measurement, and it is the mode most families underuse because it needs an uninterrupted two or three hours with the phone elsewhere. In the last six weeks, add a third mode almost nobody practises: two papers in the same subject at the real spacing, so that writing a strong second paper after a hard first one is not a new experience in the examination hall.

faqs.question: Can a tutor send us IB papers and mark schemes to keep?
faqs.answer: No, and you should be wary of any provider that offers to. IB examination papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are IB copyright, and redistributing them is infringement. Material that has not yet been sat anywhere in the world is worse than that: obtaining it is unauthorised access to live examination material, and the consequence falls on the student, not the supplier. What a tutor can legitimately do is work on the papers your child already holds through their school or has bought officially, tell you exactly which components to request, and mark what your child produces.

faqs.question: My child's subject guide changed. Are older papers still worth using?
faqs.answer: Partly, and the distinction matters. Ask the DP coordinator which guide your child is assessed against and what its first assessment year is, then sort the folder by that year. Older papers remain useful for content that survived the revision, for command-term practice and for sheer volume on a persisting topic. They become misleading where content was removed, where paper structure or length changed enough that timing practice transfers badly, or where a prescribed case study, option or set text has been replaced. For internal assessment criteria and word limits, use the current guide only.

faqs.question: How should a student mark their own paper against the mark scheme?
faqs.answer: Strictly, and in two passes. First pass: award only what the scheme explicitly allows, with no credit for what was meant. Students inflate their own marks by ten to fifteen per cent almost without exception, and a generous first pass destroys the measurement. Second pass: for every mark lost, write which of a few error types caused it, rather than simply noting the correct answer. Self-marking is genuinely valuable as training in reading a scheme, but it needs auditing for the first few papers, because learning to mark honestly is itself a skill.

faqs.question: What do IB command terms like discuss and evaluate actually require?
faqs.answer: They set the cognitive level and, in practice, the mark value. State wants a bare correct statement. Describe wants features or a sequence with no causes. Explain wants the mechanism named. Discuss wants a balanced review of several sides, supported. Evaluate wants a judgement with stated criteria and limitations. The commonest loss we see on marked UAE scripts is a correct answer written one level below the instruction, which the scheme cannot credit. The fix is procedural: read the stem, name the term aloud, state the structure it demands, then write.

faqs.question: Why does the same raw mark give a different grade in different sessions?
faqs.answer: Because grade boundaries are set after marking, per subject, per level, per session, to hold the standard constant rather than the arithmetic. If a paper turns out harder than intended, the boundary for a given grade falls. A raw score of 62 per cent therefore is not a grade and cannot be converted reliably by anyone, including a tutor. Treat older boundary tables as an indication of the usual range. Track your child's raw marks against their own earlier raw marks, which is real data, and ask the subject teacher to put a score in cohort context.

faqs.question: When in the two-year Diploma should paper practice begin?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families start, but with the right activity for the phase. From roughly forty to thirty weeks before the first paper, practice should be individual past questions on taught content only, untimed and open-book. Half papers follow, then full timed papers in the window that leads into the school mocks, which are the only properly invigilated full-length measurement most students get. Attempting full timed papers before the syllabus is taught produces a low score that measures coverage rather than ability, and it discourages students for no diagnostic gain at all.

faqs.question: How do we fit timed papers around Ramadan and the Eid holiday?
faqs.answer: Deliberately, because for a May-session candidate the Ramadan weeks fall inside the heaviest practice phase in most years. Full three-hour timed papers are hard to place well during fasting hours, so families typically move them to the first available non-fasting window or to the weekend, and use the fasting weeks for shorter marked components and error-log work. Post-Iftar sessions work for many students and are commonly requested. Plan the Eid break as a genuine break, and schedule the next full paper for the week after it rather than the day school resumes.

faqs.question: Is a leaked or unsat paper a malpractice risk even if we did not ask for it?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the exposure sits with the student. The IB treats unauthorised access to examination material as malpractice, and because sessions are sat across time zones a paper circulating before the last candidate has taken it is live material, not a past paper. If something arrives in a year-group WhatsApp group, the right move is not to open it and to tell the DP coordinator it is circulating. That protects your child. Anything already released and sat is fine to use freely, which covers everything a practice programme actually needs.

faqs.question: What does a Higher Level additional paper demand that the earlier papers do not?
faqs.answer: Usually a different genre rather than more content. Across several subjects the additional Higher Level component works on unfamiliar material, extended investigation or a prescribed element rather than on recall, which means it cannot be revised topic by topic. The only preparation that transfers is meeting the genre repeatedly: past versions of that component specifically, done under timing, with the structure of a strong response made explicit. Students who are strong on the earlier papers and weak on this one are common, and that profile is a technique problem rather than a knowledge problem.

faqs.question: Which Cambridge or Pearson past papers match my child's IGCSE entry?
faqs.answer: Match them to the series and the zone. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and publishes past papers by series. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE sits in May/June and November. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that using the correct zone timetable is essential, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination otherwise. Ask the examinations officer which series and zone apply before gathering papers.

faqs.question: What does an examiner report add that a mark scheme does not?
faqs.answer: A mark scheme says what earns marks. An examiner report says what the cohort actually did, question by question, including the specific misconceptions that cost most candidates marks. That makes it the most undervalued document in the set, because it tells you where the predictable traps are before your child walks into one. Reports are written for teachers, so they take some translation, and they reach families through the school's resource access rather than publicly. Asking the DP coordinator for the report alongside the paper and scheme costs nothing and roughly doubles the value of both.

faqs.question: Are there past papers for Arabic, Islamic Education and UAE Social Studies?
faqs.answer: Those subjects are mandatory in private schools alongside the licensed international curriculum, and they are assessed by the school against Ministry of Education content rather than through an IB paper set. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with specified languages of instruction, and prohibits using different or additional content without prior Ministry permission. Practice material therefore comes from the school, not from an external archive. Plan the time these subjects take in an exam term, because families consistently underestimate it.

faqs.question: Does marked-paper work really function over video, or does it need a tutor in the room?
faqs.answer: It functions well over video, and for this task the screen has real advantages. Paper practice runs on documents: the script, the mark scheme, the examiner report, the error log. All four are easier to annotate together on a shared screen, and the annotated version is still there the following week. Your child photographs a script on Tuesday and arrives on Thursday to find it marked, so no paid minute goes on marking in the room or on travel. IB Gram delivers UAE tutoring as one-to-one live online lessons; home visits are a service we run in India only.

faqs.question: How much does one-to-one IB exam practice cost in the UAE market?
faqs.answer: Market rates, not ours. A university-student tutor online sits around AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik publishing from AED 45 to AED 65. A qualified subject tutor online runs about AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IB from AED 200. A visiting tutor in Dubai costs AED 180 to AED 500 once travel is inside the rate. A named IB specialist runs AED 200 to AED 450 and upward, TutorChase publishing AED 270. Ask every provider whether script marking is included in the hour, because for paper practice that changes the real price substantially.

faqs.question: What should my child do with a past paper that went badly?
faqs.answer: Count the losses by type before reacting to the score. Sort every lost mark into a knowledge gap, a command misread, a method or units loss, a timing loss or a stimulus misread. The distribution is usually not what the family assumed, and three of those five are fixed by technique rather than by further content revision. Then pick the single largest category and work only on it for a fortnight. A bad paper eight weeks out is useful information; a bad paper that nobody analysed is just a bad afternoon and a discouraged student.

ib-past-papers-practice.closingBody: If you are weighing up IB past papers practice in the UAE, the cheapest useful step is to have one paper sat under proper timing and marked properly against the scheme. That single script tells you more than a term of general revision reports: which component is costing the most weighted marks, and whether the losses are content, command terms, method or pace. Book a free trial lesson and bring whatever your child has already attempted. Sessions run one-to-one over live video in Gulf Standard Time, for families in Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Sharjah, Al Ain and the northern emirates, and nothing is booked or paid for until you have seen the tutor mark something.
