ib-physics-ia-help.tutorsIntro: The specialists below teach IB Physics at Higher and Standard Level and supervise investigation work for UAE families over live video. Each one has marked student drafts against the four published criteria and can tell you, in the first session, which criterion your child's current draft is losing marks on.

intro.heading: A Physics investigation is 24 marks, and most of them are won before the data is collected
paragraphs: The internal assessment in IB Physics is a single scientific investigation of the student's own design, reported in no more than 3,000 words, marked by the school against four criteria and then moderated by the International Baccalaureate. It is worth 24 raw marks and a fifth of the final Physics grade at both Higher and Standard Level. That makes it the largest single block of marks your child will ever be able to work on without a clock running, and the only one where a teacher is permitted to give structured feedback before submission.

Parents in the UAE usually come looking for IB Physics IA help at one of two moments. The first is when a research question has been approved and the student cannot see how to turn it into a measurable experiment. The second is three weeks before the school's internal deadline, when a draft has come back with a low mark on one criterion and nobody at home can read the criterion wording well enough to know what is missing. The two problems need completely different hours, and they cost different amounts.

What makes this assessment unusual is how front-loaded it is. Criterion A rewards the design decisions: a research question narrow enough to answer, an independent variable with a stated range and units, a dependent variable with a stated measuring instrument and resolution, and controlled variables that are actually controlled rather than merely listed. A student who gets that stage right has already made Criterion B arithmetic possible and Criterion D evaluation honest. A student who gets it wrong will spend four weekends processing data that cannot answer the question, and no amount of later polish recovers those marks.

The UAE adds its own constraints. Most IB World Schools here run laboratories on a timetable, so after-school bench access is limited and holiday access is often nil. Families travel over Eid and the summer break, which is exactly when pilot data should be collected. School-run traffic in Dubai and Abu Dhabi pushes a realistic weekday session past five in the afternoon. And the pool of teachers who can genuinely supervise an uncertainty propagation at Higher Level is small in any one neighbourhood, which is why this is sold as online IB Physics tutoring in the UAE rather than as a visiting service.

This page is built around the money question, because it is the one nobody in this search answers properly. You will find the published AED bands for the UAE market with the survey date attached, a breakdown of the six things that move a quote for the same investigation, a realistic view of how many hours a Physics write-up actually needs at each stage, and the point at which paying more stops buying anything. You will also find the honesty boundary stated plainly, because a provider that will not state it is selling you a malpractice risk rather than tutoring.

A hard 3,000-word ceiling on the report, excluding data tables and references

ib-physics-ia-help.programmesIntro: The investigation sits in the Diploma Programme, but the skills it marks are built earlier. Families who come to us with an investigation problem in DP2 very often have a Middle Years Programme gap underneath it, so it is worth knowing where each programme asks for what.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Physics in the Diploma Programme is examined by three written papers plus the scientific investigation. The investigation is the student's own design, reported in up to 3,000 words and marked against Criteria A to D. It is the only component where a teacher may legitimately give feedback on a draft before it is handed in, which is why the hours spent on it have a different value from exam-paper hours.
programmes.countryNote: UAE Diploma cohorts are small, so a school may run Physics Higher Level in a single class of eight or nine students with one teacher supervising every investigation in the year group. That teacher is doing their job properly and is still stretched. One-to-one online support is how a family adds reading time on a draft without asking the school for something it cannot timetable.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Middle Years Programme sciences are marked on four criteria of their own, including inquiring and designing, and processing and evaluating. A student who has practised stating a hypothesis with a scientific reason, tabulating raw data with units and resolution, and drawing a graph with a line of best fit arrives in DP1 able to attempt a real research question. A student who has not will struggle with Criterion A.
programmes.countryNote: Many UAE families move into the Diploma from a British or Indian Year 11 rather than from the Middle Years Programme, so the design and evaluation habits were never taught. That transition gap is the single most common reason a UAE student's first investigation draft scores badly on Criterion A, and it is fixable in two or three sessions if it is caught in DP1 rather than DP2.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Career-related Programme students take two or more Diploma Programme courses alongside the career-related study. Where one of those is Physics, the scientific investigation is identical in form, mark allocation and word ceiling to the one a full Diploma candidate submits. The reflective project is separate and is assessed on its own criteria, so a Career-related student can be carrying two long pieces of written work at once.
programmes.countryNote: Only a handful of UAE schools run the Career-related Programme, and a Physics course inside it may be taught in a mixed class with full Diploma candidates. The supervision load on the teacher is the same, the internal deadline is usually the same, and the student has a reflective project competing for the same weekends. Sequencing matters more here than in any other route.

ib-physics-ia-help.subjectsIntro: Every IB science and maths course carries an internal assessment, and families rarely need help with only one of them. The grid below sets out what each internal assessment actually asks for, so you can see whether one specialist covers the problem or whether two subjects genuinely need two people.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The scientific investigation: one self-designed experiment, up to 3,000 words, 24 marks across Criteria A to D, moderated by the IB. The marks that separate a four from a six are almost always uncertainty propagation in Criterion B and a specific, costed improvement in Criterion D rather than extra prose.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Same four criteria, same 24 marks, same word ceiling, but the practical constraints differ. Titration and calorimetry work needs reagents and a fume cupboard, so a UAE student without holiday laboratory access often pivots to a database or simulation investigation, which changes what Criterion A has to justify.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The investigation is marked on the same letters, but statistical treatment carries more weight in practice: standard deviation, error bars and a named significance test. Students who can run a physics gradient analysis often freeze on choosing between a t-test and a chi-squared test, and that is a one-session fix.

subjects.name: Sports, Exercise and Health Science
subjects.description: Human-participant work brings an ethical approval step that physics rarely needs, and UAE schools apply it strictly. The design stage therefore takes longer, consent and anonymity have to be documented, and the available measuring instruments are usually heart-rate monitors and timing gates rather than laboratory apparatus.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a developed computational solution with documentation rather than an experiment, assessed on planning, design, development, functionality and evaluation. Students who want measurable data often choose an algorithm timing study, which overlaps neatly with the physics habit of plotting a controlled variable against a measured one.

subjects.name: Design Technology
subjects.description: The design project runs across both years and is assessed on analysis, conceptual design, development and testing. Physics students who take it alongside find the testing stage familiar, but the documentation load is far heavier and the deadlines rarely line up with the Physics investigation deadline.

subjects.name: Environmental Systems and Societies
subjects.description: The individual investigation follows the same four-criterion structure as the sciences. UAE students have genuinely local material available here: desalination outputs, district cooling loads, urban heat island measurements between a shaded and an unshaded street, and groundwater salinity data published by federal authorities.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The mathematical internal assessment is a 12 to 20 page piece of personal mathematics, marked on presentation, mathematical communication, personal engagement, reflection and use of mathematics. Physics students often reuse their own experimental data here, which is permitted, but the same data cannot be submitted as two assessments.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Same criteria as Analysis and Approaches, different mathematical toolkit, with modelling and statistics carrying more of the load. A regression analysis on real UAE data, correctly reported with residuals, scores better here than a decorative piece of pure mathematics copied from a textbook example.

ib-physics-ia-help.regionsIntro: Which emirate you live in changes who regulates your child's school, how much laboratory access is realistic outside lesson time, and what a weekday session can start. It does not change the price of IB Physics IA help, because the lesson happens over video and the specialist is matched on subject rather than on postcode.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA figures for 2024-25 record 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7 per cent of enrolment. That is the largest Diploma cohort in the country and the deepest pool of Physics teachers, but it is also where school-run traffic pushes a realistic weekday session past 17:00.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school, so an Abu Dhabi family looking for investigation feedback cannot simply pay their child's own Physics teacher.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education here and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Diploma provision is thinner than in Dubai, so a Sharjah student wanting Higher Level Physics supervision is usually choosing between a long commute and a video call.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under the Department of Education and Knowledge. School sites are spread across a wide, low-density city, which makes a visiting tutor expensive in travel time before any teaching happens. Laboratory access outside timetabled lessons is the binding constraint on an experimental investigation here more often than tutor availability is.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools fall under the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority. Diploma Physics at Higher Level runs in very few Ajman schools, so the students we support here are frequently the only candidate in their year group taking it, with one supervising teacher and no peer group to compare a draft against.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Regulated by the Department of Knowledge, which, like Sharjah's authority, approves curricula, fees and assessment methods. RAK families routinely tell us that the nearest subject specialist is a ninety-minute drive each way. A video session removes the drive and makes a weekday evening slot viable during the investigation write-up weeks.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under the federal Ministry of Education, which supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. The east-coast Diploma cohort is small enough that a single Physics teacher may cover both years. Online supervision is not a compromise here, it is the only way to add a second pair of eyes to a draft.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also federally supervised. Families here often enrol in Sharjah or RAK schools and commute, which means an after-school session competes with a return journey rather than with homework. A 19:30 start, with the report open on a shared screen, is usually the first slot that actually works.

schoolClusters.note: The deepest Diploma Physics provision in the country, and the cluster where Higher Level classes are large enough that a teacher is supervising fifteen or more investigations at once. Students we support in these schools most often arrive with an approved research question and a Criterion B problem.

Smaller Diploma cohorts than Dubai and a regulator with explicit professional-ethics rules on staff tutoring their own pupils. Students we support here frequently need help sequencing the Physics investigation against the Extended Essay, because both internal deadlines tend to land in the same term.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.city: Sharjah, Ajman and Ras Al Khaimah
schoolClusters.note: Diploma provision across the northern emirates is concentrated in a handful of schools, so Higher Level Physics candidates are often a group of three or four in a year. Travel distances make a visiting specialist impractical, and families here were the first to ask us for evening video slots.

ib-physics-ia-help.modesIntro: Investigation support is bought in three shapes, and the shape matters more than the hourly rate. A family that books eight weekly hours when they needed three concentrated ones has spent more and learned less. Each option below is delivered one-to-one over live video.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one across the investigation cycle
modes.description: A fixed slot held from research-question approval through to the final read of the report, typically one hour a week for eight to twelve weeks. This is the cheapest route per mark gained, because design errors get caught at Criterion A stage rather than after four weekends of data collection. It also means the student, not the tutor, holds the timeline.

It is the most common purchase on this page and the one most often bought a week later than it should be.

sections.heading: What the IB Physics scientific investigation actually asks your child to produce
paragraphs: One experiment, designed by the student, reported in up to 3,000 words, marked out of 24 by the school and then moderated by the International Baccalaureate. It is worth 20 per cent of the Physics grade at Higher Level and at Standard Level, which means a Standard Level student carries exactly the same investigation workload as a Higher Level one for exactly the same proportional reward.

The report is not a laboratory write-up in the school sense. There is no prescribed method to follow and no marks for neatness. What is assessed is the quality of the student's own decisions: whether the research question is narrow enough to answer with the apparatus available, whether the measurement chosen can detect the effect being looked for, whether the raw data is recorded with its uncertainty, whether the processing is mathematically correct, whether the conclusion is tested against accepted physics, and whether the evaluation identifies specific weaknesses and costs their effect on the result.

Word count is a real constraint and students routinely misjudge it. Raw data tables, processed data tables, graphs, labels, references and a bibliography sit outside the 3,000 words. Prose does not. A student who writes two pages of textbook theory before stating the research question has spent a tenth of the ceiling on marks that do not exist. The investigations that score well tend to read as short, dense, and almost brusque.

The last thing to understand is the moderation step. The school marks the investigation, applies its own internal standardisation, and submits the mark with a sample to the IB. The IB moderator can adjust a school's marks up or down. This is why a teacher's generous read of a draft is not the final word, and why a specialist who has marked against the published criteria is reading for what survives moderation rather than for what pleases a supervisor.
bullets: One self-designed experiment, 3,000 words maximum of prose
24 marks across four criteria, six marks each
20 per cent of the final grade at both levels
Tables, graphs and references sit outside the word ceiling
School-marked, internally standardised, then IB-moderated

sections.heading: The four criteria, letter by letter, and what each six marks is paying for
paragraphs: No competitor page in this search names a single IB Physics IA criterion. That is strange, because the criteria are the whole assessment: a student who can read the wording of Criterion B and check their own report against it does not need a tutor to tell them the mark is low. Most students have never been shown the wording at all, and work instead from a school rubric summary that compresses six marks into one sentence.

Each criterion is marked in bands, and the gap between bands is usually one specific omission rather than a general weakness. Criterion A loses marks when the methodology is described but never justified. Criterion B loses them when processing is shown but uncertainty is not propagated through it. Criterion C loses them when a result is stated but never compared with an accepted value or published source. Criterion D loses them when weaknesses are listed generically rather than costed against the result.

That pattern is why a diagnostic read of a draft is worth more than a general tuition hour. A specialist reading against criterion wording can usually tell a family within twenty minutes which two of the four criteria are carrying the lost marks, and whether the fix is a rewrite, a recalculation, or another afternoon of data collection. The recalculation is cheap. The extra data collection is the one that needs a laboratory slot and therefore a decision this week rather than next.

Criterion wording is published in the subject guide your child's school holds. We do not reproduce or distribute IB subject guides, past papers, mark schemes or grade boundary tables, because they are the IB's copyright. Your child's teacher or IB coordinator can show the current wording, and the subject page on ibo.org is the authoritative place to check which guide your cohort is assessed under.

table.caption: IB PHYSICS SCIENTIFIC INVESTIGATION - THE FOUR CRITERIA AND WHAT EACH REWARDS
columns: What a weak draft looks like here
rows: A - Research design
A research question narrow enough to answer; a justified methodology; independent, dependent and controlled variables stated with units, ranges and instrument resolution
The question is stated and the method is described, but no sentence explains why that method rather than another, and controlled variables are listed without saying how they were held
B - Data analysis
Raw data recorded with its uncertainty, correct processing shown, graphs with error bars, and a gradient treated with its own uncertainty rather than read off by eye
Processing is arithmetically fine but uncertainty stops at the raw table and never travels into the processed values or the gradient
C - Conclusion
A conclusion that answers the research question, interpreted against accepted physics and compared with a published value or an established relationship
The trend is described in words, the relationship is never tested against theory, and no accepted value appears anywhere in the section
D - Evaluation
Specific strengths and weaknesses of the method, the direction and size of each weakness's effect on the result, and improvements that are realistic with named apparatus
A list of generic limitations, human error among them, with no statement of which way each one pushed the result or by roughly how much

sections.heading: Where Physics investigation marks go missing, and what each fix actually takes
paragraphs: The failures are repetitive. Across UAE drafts the same half-dozen symptoms account for most of the lost marks, and each has a different cost to repair. Knowing which one you are looking at is the difference between booking three hours and booking ten, which is the real reason this page leads with diagnosis rather than with a rate card.

The most expensive symptom is a research question that cannot be measured with the apparatus the student can reach. A question about the dependence of a pendulum period on amplitude at small angles, for instance, asks a student to detect a change smaller than their timing uncertainty. No amount of careful work rescues it, and the fix is a new question and new data. Caught in week one that costs an hour. Caught after the data is collected it costs a term.

The cheapest symptom is a missing comparison in Criterion C. A student who measured the acceleration due to gravity and reported 9.6 metres per second squared without ever naming the accepted value has given away marks that a single paragraph recovers. Between those extremes sit the uncertainty problems, which are arithmetic rather than experimental, and the evaluation problems, which need the student to think harder about their own method rather than to collect anything new.

This table is the diagnosis sheet a specialist works from on a first read. It is deliberately specific, because a generic statement that a draft needs more detail is the least useful sentence anybody says about an investigation.

sections.heading: What IB Physics IA help costs in the UAE, and what the number is made of
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for this kind of search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. So here are the AED bands, surveyed from published UAE provider rate cards in October 2026, together with a cost table published for the Dubai market in 2026 by the estimating site Bestimate. These are market rates, not IB Gram prices. Our own model starts with a free trial lesson and a consultation, and the quote follows the match.

Read the table as a map of what each band buys on a scientific investigation specifically, which is not the same as what it buys on general Physics tuition. The low band is adequate for reading the criteria together and tidying report structure. It is not adequate for propagating an uncertainty through a logarithmic plot, and a family who buys it for that will pay twice. The specialist band is where uncertainty treatment, gradient analysis and Criterion C comparison against published values sit reliably.

The honest limit of the table is the top row. Above roughly AED 450 an hour, the surveyed rates buy scarcity and reputation rather than any syllabus capability the band below lacks. The highest single advertised UAE rate found in the October 2026 survey was AED 650 an hour. There is no evidence in the published market that an investigation marked against four criteria needs that, and we do not recommend paying it for investigation work.

One more figure matters more than the hourly rate: how many hours. A design-stage conversation is one to two hours. A full weekly cycle across a term is eight to twelve. A rescue block on a marked draft is three to five. Multiply the band by the realistic hour count before comparing two quotes, because a provider at AED 200 selling a twenty-hour package is dearer than a provider at AED 350 selling four.

sections.heading: Six things that move the quote for the same investigation
paragraphs: Two UAE families can ask for support on the same pendulum investigation and be quoted rates that differ by AED 300 an hour. The difference is almost never the subject. It is a combination of six factors, and four of them are inside your control if you start early enough.

The first is level and scarcity. A Higher Level Physics specialist who can supervise an uncertainty propagation is scarcer in the UAE than a Standard Level science tutor, and scarcity sets the rate. The second is proximity to the internal deadline. A draft arriving ten days before submission needs the specialist to read it before the session and to hold two slots that week, and the market charges for that urgency. The third is session timing: a Saturday mid-morning slot is the most contested hour in the UAE tutoring week, and weekday evenings after 19:00 are the least.

The fourth is whether you are buying feedback or supervision. A single diagnostic read of a marked draft is priced differently from a term-long weekly commitment, and per hour the diagnostic read is dearer while the total is far lower. The fifth is delivery format. The in-home bands in the rate table above sit AED 30 to 100 an hour above the online bands for the same tier, and that gap is travel time rather than teaching. The sixth is subject combination: a family that needs Physics and Maths Analysis and Approaches investigation support frequently pays less per hour by using one specialist who covers both than by matching two.

What does not move a defensible quote is a promise about the mark. Any provider pricing on an outcome rather than on hours and expertise is selling something no teacher can deliver, because the school marks the investigation and the IB moderates it. Nobody outside that chain controls the number.

sections.heading: The investigation counted backwards from your school's internal deadline
paragraphs: Nobody in this search publishes a plan. Competitor pages talk about support in the abstract and leave the parent to guess when to start. The table below counts backwards from the school's internal submission date, which is the only date that actually governs a student's work, and it uses relative timing rather than calendar dates for a deliberate reason.

That reason is accuracy. IB session and results dates are set by the International Baccalaureate and are not restated here, because we will not publish an IB date we have not read on an official source. Your child's IB coordinator holds the school's internal deadline and the IB upload schedule, and the subject and assessment pages on ibo.org are where to confirm anything about the session itself. Any page that quotes you a confident IB results date without citing where it came from is guessing on your behalf.

The structure of the plan holds regardless of which session your child sits. Design work belongs in the term before data collection. Data collection belongs where laboratory access exists, which in most UAE schools means term time rather than holidays. Processing belongs immediately after collection, while the student still remembers how the apparatus behaved. Writing belongs last and takes less time than families expect, because a well-designed investigation almost writes itself from its own tables.

The common UAE failure is to put data collection in the summer or Eid break on the assumption that free time equals progress. Laboratories are shut, families travel, and the student returns in the new term with nothing collected and a shorter runway than before. Collect in term time, write in the break.

sections.heading: Apparatus a UAE student can actually reach, and what makes a question measurable
paragraphs: The single most useful hour of IB Physics IA help in the UAE is usually spent on this question: with the equipment your child can get at, what change is large enough to measure? A research question is only as good as the smallest difference the apparatus can resolve, and students pick questions from interest rather than from resolution.

UAE conditions narrow the field in specific ways. School laboratories run on a timetable and after-hours bench access is rare, so a student who needs forty measurements has to plan around lesson slots. Holiday access is usually nil. Local hardware shops stock ramps, springs, magnets and timber readily, but calibrated laboratory instruments are not domestic purchases. What every student does have is a phone with an accelerometer, a magnetometer, a microphone and a camera that records at a known frame rate, and free video-tracking software that turns that camera into a position-time instrument.

That matters for Criterion A, because the criterion rewards a justified choice of instrument with its resolution stated, and a phone camera at 240 frames per second has a defensible temporal resolution that a hand-held stopwatch does not. It matters for Criterion B, because a tracked video gives dozens of position points rather than five stopwatch times, which is what makes a random uncertainty supportable. And it matters for Criterion D, because the student can name a real improvement, a higher frame rate or a longer lever arm, rather than wishing for better equipment.

Database and simulation investigations are legitimate and are assessed on the same four criteria, but Criterion A then has to justify the data source rather than the apparatus: who published it, over what period, with what stated uncertainty. UAE students have genuinely local options here, from published meteorological records to district cooling and desalination data, and a local data set is harder to fault than a generic one pulled from a tutorial website.

sections.heading: Uncertainties, gradients and the arithmetic that separates a four from a six
paragraphs: If a UAE family buys only three hours of investigation support, this is where to spend them. Uncertainty treatment is the most reliably under-taught part of the IB Physics investigation, it carries Criterion B outright, it feeds the quantitative conclusion Criterion C wants, and it is pure arithmetic on data the student already has. No laboratory slot is needed to fix it.

The sequence is mechanical once it is learned. Every raw measurement carries an absolute uncertainty, taken from instrument resolution, from the spread of repeats, or from both combined. Those absolute uncertainties convert to fractional ones. Fractional uncertainties add when quantities multiply or divide, and multiply by the power when a quantity is raised to one. Absolute uncertainties add when quantities add or subtract. That single set of rules propagates uncertainty from the raw table all the way to the processed column, and it is the step most drafts skip entirely.

Graphs are where the marks become visible. Error bars drawn from the processed uncertainties, a line of best fit, then a maximum gradient line and a minimum gradient line drawn through the extremes of the error bars. Half the difference between those two gradients is the gradient uncertainty, and that number is what lets a student write a result as a value with a range rather than as a bare figure. Where theory predicts a straight line through the origin, whether the error bars include the origin is itself a finding worth a sentence in Criterion C.

Linearisation is the other skill worth an hour. Many physics relationships are not linear in the measured variables, and a student who plots period against length sees a curve and stops. Plotting the square of the period against length turns the same data into a straight line whose gradient has a physical meaning that can be compared with an accepted value. That one move frequently converts a described trend into a tested relationship, which is exactly the distance between Criterion C bands.
bullets: Absolute uncertainty from instrument resolution and from the spread of repeats
Fractional uncertainties add on multiply and divide; absolute ones add on plus and minus
Error bars from processed uncertainties, not from the raw table
Maximum and minimum gradient lines give a defensible gradient uncertainty

Quote the final result as a value with a range and a unit

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line between coaching an investigation and producing one
paragraphs: This has to be said plainly, because one page ranking in this search sells finished internal assessments for a four-figure sum in AED. Buying one is academic malpractice under IB rules. The consequence lands on the student, not on the seller: a malpractice finding can cost the subject grade or the whole Diploma, and it follows the candidate rather than the website.

What a tutor may legitimately do is bounded and still substantial. A tutor may teach the physics. A tutor may explain the criterion wording. A tutor may ask questions about a research question until the student discovers it cannot be measured. A tutor may demonstrate uncertainty propagation on a different data set, teach linearisation on a textbook example, show how maximum and minimum gradient lines are drawn, and give written feedback that names which criterion a section is weak against and why. A tutor may read a draft and say that the evaluation does not cost its weaknesses.

What a tutor may not do is author or correct the work. No tutor on this platform will supply a research question for a student to adopt, type a section of the report, rewrite a paragraph into better prose, insert a calculation into the student's file, or hand over a model investigation to be adapted. The work has to be the student's own in substance and in wording, and feedback is given as comments and questions rather than as edits. If a student brings a draft that is not their own, the session stops and the family is told why.

The practical test we use is simple and you can apply it yourself: after the session, could the student explain every decision in their report to an examiner who asked why? If the answer is no for any part, that part is not theirs, whatever the file history says. Schools apply broadly the same test, and so do IB moderators looking at a mark that does not match a candidate's examination performance.

sections.heading: Who regulates your child's school, who permits the tutor, and what you can ask to see
paragraphs: Five authorities regulate UAE private schools, and most pages in this search name none of them. Dubai sits with the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah the Department of Knowledge, both of which approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah fall to the federal Ministry of Education.

Separately from the school, the tutor needs a permit. Private tuition in the UAE is regulated through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, which introduced private tuition work permits. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure is quoted here.

There is one condition UAE parents consistently do not know about. The permit carries a code of conduct that bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school, and ADEK professional-ethics rules for Abu Dhabi private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school. Paying your child's own Physics teacher for investigation feedback is therefore the one arrangement a family should not ask for, however convenient it looks.

IB Gram holds no regulator accreditation and claims none. We are not approved, licensed or endorsed by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, the International Baccalaureate, Cambridge or Pearson, and any provider telling you otherwise should be asked to show the permit or centre number. What we do is match a subject specialist and deliver the lesson over live video. The official route for the private tutor permit is the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation service page, its smart app and its e-services system.

sections.heading: Where the Physics grade travels: UAE university entry and Ministry of Education equivalency
paragraphs: A fifth of a Physics grade sounds abstract until you follow where the grade goes. For a UAE-resident student applying to a local or regional university, the Diploma result usually has to pass through a Ministry of Education equivalency step before it is recognised, and that is a process no page in this search explains. It is worth understanding before the investigation is treated as optional.

The published requirements are clearest on the British track. A student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the published rule is five.

On the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the International Baccalaureate, no points threshold is published here, because we have not read one on an official Ministry of Education source. Verify the IB requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate, and treat any page that quotes a confident IB figure without a citation with caution.

IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency or attestation, and tutoring is not a requirement for any part of it. The reason this sits on a Physics investigation page is narrower: Physics is a prerequisite subject for engineering and most physical-science degrees, the investigation is a fifth of that grade, and a grade that drops a band because of a weak internal assessment can close a prerequisite the student needed.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the weeks when investigation writing actually happens
paragraphs: The UAE academic calendar interacts with the investigation in ways a UK or Indian tutoring page never has to consider, and getting this wrong costs families a month of runway. Three features matter: shortened school days during Ramadan, the Eid breaks, and the long summer that sits between DP1 and DP2 for most UAE schools.

During Ramadan, school days are shortened across UAE schools and afternoons change shape entirely. Fasting students are not at their sharpest at four in the afternoon, and the practical answer is to move sessions to a post-Iftar slot, usually from around 20:30. Investigation work survives this shift better than examination practice does, because reading a criterion and recalculating an uncertainty is a shorter, more contained task than sitting a full past paper. Families who plan for it keep their momentum; families who simply cancel for a month lose four weekly sessions at the worst possible point in the DP2 year.

The Eid breaks and the summer are where the planning error lives. Parents reasonably assume free time means progress, and schedule data collection into the holidays. School laboratories are shut, technicians are on leave, and families travel. The result is a student returning in September with an approved research question, no data, and a shorter runway than they had in June. The rule that works is simple: collect data in term time when the bench exists, and use the break for processing, drafting and reading, none of which needs apparatus.

One more timing detail specific to this market. Saturday mid-morning is the most contested hour in the UAE tutoring week, and during the investigation write-up weeks it books out first. Families who need a specialist for a rescue block in the fortnight before an internal deadline do better asking for a weekday evening after 19:00, which is both easier to get and, across the surveyed rate cards, at the softer end of the price band.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the date
process.description: Start with three facts: Physics at Higher or Standard Level, where the investigation currently stands, and your school's internal deadline. That is enough to tell you whether you are buying a design conversation, a weekly cycle or a rescue block, and roughly how many hours each needs. If a specialist is not free for the slot you want, we say so rather than offering a substitute.

process.title: One free trial lesson with the specialist
process.description: The trial is a single lesson with the person who would teach your child, at no cost and with no card details collected. It is a working session, not a sales call: the specialist looks at the research question or the marked draft and says which criterion is carrying the lost marks. If the match is wrong, you stop there and owe nothing.

process.title: Session one tests whether the question can be measured
process.description: Before anything else, the specialist and the student check that the effect being investigated is larger than the uncertainty of the chosen instrument. This is the cheapest hour in the whole process and the one that prevents the most expensive failure. If the question cannot survive that test, a new one is built in the same session rather than discovered after four weekends at the bench.

process.title: The weekly cycle: data, processing, draft, feedback
process.description: Each session the student brings what they have produced since the last one. The specialist reads it against criterion wording and responds with comments and questions, never with edits. The student does the rewriting between sessions. Over eight to twelve weeks that rhythm produces a report the student can defend line by line, which is the only kind that survives moderation.

process.title: Handover to paper work
process.description: Once the investigation is with the school, the same slot usually turns into examination preparation on the topics the investigation touched, because those are already fresh. Nothing has to be rebooked and nothing has to be rematched. Families who keep the slot through the mock window tend to use fewer total hours than those who stop and restart.

whyPoints.title: Rates on the page, with their source and date
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page carries where it came from and when it was surveyed, because three of the strongest pages in this search publish no price at all. You can compare any quote you receive against the October 2026 market bands above before you commit to a single hour.

whyPoints.title: Diagnosis before hours
whyPoints.description: The first thing a specialist does with a draft is name which of the four criteria is losing the marks. That determines whether you need three hours or twelve, and it is the difference between a recalculation your child can finish this week and another round of data collection that needs a laboratory slot.

whyPoints.title: A stated honesty boundary
whyPoints.description: Our tutors teach, explain criteria and give written feedback on the student's own work. They do not supply research questions, type sections, rewrite prose or hand over model investigations. The boundary is published here because a provider who will not state it is selling a malpractice risk that lands on the student.

whyPoints.title: Subject match rather than postcode match
whyPoints.description: A Higher Level Physics specialist who can supervise uncertainty propagation is scarce in any one UAE neighbourhood and available nationally. Delivering over live video means a family in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain gets the same specialist a family in Emirates Hills does, with no travel cost loaded into the rate.

whyPoints.title: Honest about coverage
whyPoints.description: If no specialist is free for your subject, level and slot, you are told that in the first conversation. We do not substitute a generalist for a Higher Level Physics specialist and let you find out in week three, which is the failure mode families describe most often when they arrive from another provider.

whyPoints.title: Planned around the UAE calendar
whyPoints.description: Sessions are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, shift to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan, and assume laboratory access exists in term time rather than in the holidays. That one assumption, applied early, is what keeps a DP2 investigation off the critical path in the fortnight before an internal deadline.

faqs.question: What does one-to-one help with an IB Physics investigation cost in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Surveyed UAE provider rate cards in October 2026 put online one-to-one Physics support in three broad bands: roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for a generalist or university-student tutor, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified science teacher, and AED 200 to 450 for an IB Physics Higher Level specialist. The highest single advertised rate found was AED 650. In-home bands sit AED 30 to 100 an hour above the online equivalent, which is travel rather than teaching. Those are market figures, not IB Gram prices. Our own route starts with one free trial lesson and a consultation, and the quote follows the match.

faqs.question: How many hours of investigation support does a Physics student usually need?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on when you start. A design-stage conversation that tests whether the research question can be measured takes one to two hours and prevents the most expensive failure available. A full weekly cycle from question approval to final read runs eight to twelve hours across a term. A rescue block on a draft that has already been marked is typically three to five hours inside a fortnight. Multiply the hourly band by the realistic hour count before comparing quotes, because a lower rate attached to a twenty-hour package costs more than a higher rate attached to four.

faqs.question: What are the four assessment criteria for the IB Physics scientific investigation?
faqs.answer: Criterion A covers research design: a focused question, a justified methodology, and variables stated with ranges, units and instrument resolution. Criterion B covers data analysis: raw data with uncertainties, correct processing, graphs with error bars, and a gradient treated with its own uncertainty. Criterion C covers the conclusion: an answer to the question, interpreted against accepted physics and compared with a published value. Criterion D covers evaluation: specific strengths and weaknesses, the effect of each on the result, and realistic improvements. Six marks each, 24 in total, worth 20 per cent of the Physics grade. The exact wording sits in the subject guide your child's school holds.

faqs.question: How long is a Physics IA allowed to be, and what counts towards the word count?
faqs.answer: The report has a ceiling of 3,000 words of prose. Raw data tables, processed data tables, graphs, axis labels, calculations, references and the bibliography sit outside that count. Prose does not. The most common way UAE students waste the ceiling is an opening two pages of textbook theory before the research question appears, which spends a tenth of the allowance on marks that do not exist. Strong reports read short and dense. If your child is over the limit, the first cut is almost always background theory rather than evaluation, because the evaluation is where Criterion D marks live.

faqs.question: What makes a Physics IA research question good enough to be worth investigating?
faqs.answer: One test matters more than any other: is the change being measured larger than the uncertainty of the instrument measuring it? A question about how a pendulum's period depends on amplitude at small angles asks a student to detect a difference smaller than their timing error, and no amount of careful work rescues it. A good question also names its independent variable with a range, its dependent variable with a measuring instrument and that instrument's resolution, and the variables being controlled with a method for controlling them. Narrow beats interesting. A narrow question answered properly scores above a broad one answered vaguely.

faqs.question: Can my child run a Physics investigation experiment without laboratory access over the holidays?
faqs.answer: Often yes, but it changes the design. UAE school laboratories run on a timetable and are generally shut over Eid and the summer, so a student who needs bench apparatus should collect in term time. What is available year round is a phone: an accelerometer, a magnetometer, a microphone and a camera recording at a known frame rate, plus free video-tracking software that turns the camera into a position-time instrument. A tracked video gives dozens of data points with a defensible temporal uncertainty of half a frame interval, which supports a gradient uncertainty far better than five stopwatch readings do.

faqs.question: Is a database or simulation investigation marked as generously as an experimental one?
faqs.answer: It is marked against exactly the same four criteria and the same 24 marks. What changes is what Criterion A has to justify. Instead of apparatus and resolution, the student justifies the data source: who published it, over what period, with what stated uncertainty, and why that source suits the question. A locally relevant data set, such as published UAE meteorological records or district cooling figures, is harder to fault than a generic set pulled from a tutorial site. Criterion D then evaluates the limitations of the model or the data set rather than of a bench setup, and the same costing discipline applies.

faqs.question: How should uncertainties be handled in a Physics investigation report?
faqs.answer: Every raw measurement carries an absolute uncertainty, from instrument resolution, from the spread of repeats, or both. Those convert to fractional uncertainties. Fractional uncertainties add when quantities multiply or divide and multiply by the power when a quantity is raised to one; absolute uncertainties add when quantities add or subtract. That propagates uncertainty from the raw table into the processed column, where error bars come from. Then draw maximum and minimum gradient lines through the extremes of the error bars, and take half their difference as the gradient uncertainty. This is the step most drafts skip entirely, and it is pure arithmetic on data the student already holds.

faqs.question: Why does a gradient need maximum and minimum lines rather than a single line of best fit?
faqs.answer: Because a single line gives a number with no range, and Criterion C rewards a quantified conclusion rather than a described trend. Drawing a steepest and a shallowest line that still pass through the extremes of the error bars gives two gradients, and half the difference between them is a defensible gradient uncertainty. The student can then write the result as a value with a range and a unit, and compare that range against an accepted value. A useful extra sentence: where theory predicts a line through the origin, whether the error bars include the origin is itself a finding worth stating.

faqs.question: When should a UAE Diploma student start the Physics investigation?
faqs.answer: Working backwards from the school's internal deadline, a research question shortlist belongs about twenty to twenty-four weeks out, approval and a justified methodology sixteen to twenty weeks out, a pilot run fourteen to sixteen weeks out, and full data collection ten to fourteen weeks out. Processing, then a first full draft, then teacher feedback fill the remainder. The common UAE error is scheduling data collection into Eid or the summer, when laboratories are shut and families travel. Collect in term time and write in the break. Confirm the actual dates with your child's IB coordinator, who holds both the internal deadline and the school's upload schedule.

faqs.question: What exactly may a tutor do with a Physics investigation draft, and what is off limits?
faqs.answer: A tutor may teach the physics, explain criterion wording, ask questions until the student sees that a research question cannot be measured, demonstrate uncertainty propagation on a different data set, show how gradient lines are drawn, and give written feedback naming which criterion a section is weak against and why. A tutor may not supply a research question to adopt, type any part of the report, rewrite prose, insert a calculation into the student's file, or provide a model investigation to adapt. The test we use: could the student explain every decision in the report to an examiner who asked why? If not, that part is not theirs.

faqs.question: Is paying someone to supply a finished Physics investigation actually a problem?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the consequence lands on the student rather than on the seller. Submitting work that is not the student's own is academic malpractice under IB rules, and a finding can cost the subject grade or the whole Diploma. One site ranking for this search advertises completed internal assessments for a four-figure AED sum; the fee is irrelevant to the risk. Moderators compare internal marks against examination performance, and a mark that does not fit attracts exactly the scrutiny a family does not want. Teaching, criterion feedback and process coaching are legitimate and get the student to a better report anyway.

faqs.question: Does the Physics investigation mark the school gives stay the same?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. The school marks the investigation, applies its own internal standardisation across the year group, and submits the mark to the International Baccalaureate with a sample of work. An IB moderator can adjust a school's marks upwards or downwards. That is why a supervising teacher's encouraging read of a draft is not the final word, and why a specialist reading against the published criterion wording is looking for what survives moderation rather than for what pleases a reader. It also means an unusually generous internal mark is not a safe thing for a family to rely on.

faqs.question: Is the investigation different at Higher Level and Standard Level?
faqs.answer: The form, the four criteria, the 24 marks and the 3,000-word ceiling are the same, and it is worth 20 per cent of the grade at both levels. A Standard Level student therefore carries the same investigation workload as a Higher Level one. What differs is the physics available to draw on, and in practice the depth of theory a Higher Level student can bring to Criterion C. Standard Level students sometimes assume the investigation is scaled down for them and underinvest in it, which is the opposite of what the mark allocation suggests they should do.

faqs.question: My child's draft lost marks on Criterion D. Is that expensive to fix?
faqs.answer: It is one of the cheaper repairs, because it needs thinking rather than apparatus. Criterion D asks for specific strengths and weaknesses, the direction and size of each weakness's effect on the result, and improvements that name real apparatus. Most lost marks come from a generic list with human error in it and no statement of which way each limitation pushed the measurement. A rewrite directed by questions rather than by corrections usually takes one session plus the student's own work between sessions. No new data is needed, which is why this is a good use of a short rescue block.

faqs.question: Does IB Physics IA help happen over video, or does a tutor travel to our address in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, with the report and the graphs open on a shared screen. No tutor travels to a UAE address; visiting tuition is something IB Gram offers only in India. For investigation work the video format is a genuine advantage rather than a compromise: a Higher Level Physics specialist who can supervise uncertainty propagation is scarce in any one neighbourhood and available nationally, so a family in Fujairah gets the same specialist a family in Dubai does. It also removes the travel loading that puts in-home rates AED 30 to 100 an hour above online ones.

faqs.question: Can sessions move to a post-Iftar slot during Ramadan?
faqs.answer: Yes, and for most families they should. School days are shortened during Ramadan and a fasting student is not at their sharpest at four in the afternoon. A slot from around 20:30 works better, and investigation work survives the shift more comfortably than full past-paper practice does, because reading a criterion or recalculating an uncertainty is a contained task. Families who simply cancel for a month lose four weekly sessions, and in DP2 that month usually sits uncomfortably close to an internal deadline. Sessions are booked in Gulf Standard Time, so no conversion arithmetic is needed at your end.

faqs.question: Can one specialist cover both the Physics investigation and the Maths internal assessment?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and when it works it is cheaper than matching two people. The overlap is real: both reward correct data treatment, honest reflection and mathematics that does something rather than decorates. A Physics student may reuse their own experimental data for the Maths internal assessment, which is permitted, though the same piece of work cannot be submitted twice. Where the Maths requirement is a statistics-heavy Applications and Interpretation report, a dedicated mathematician is usually the better match. We will tell you which case you are in during the first conversation rather than after you have paid for hours.

ib-physics-ia-help.closingHeading: Start with the criterion that is losing the marks
ib-physics-ia-help.closingBody: If your child has a Physics investigation in progress, the useful first step is not booking a block of hours. It is finding out which of the four criteria is costing the marks, because that answer decides whether you need three hours of arithmetic or another afternoon at the bench. Send the research question or the marked draft, tell us your school's internal deadline, and take the free trial lesson with the specialist who would teach your child. You will get a straight read on where the report stands, the realistic hour count, and a plain answer if no specialist is free for the slot you need. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time.

ib-predicted-grades-improvement.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are Diploma specialists who work on one subject at a time, at Higher or Standard Level, with the student's own marked scripts and the school's assessment calendar open in front of them. Each teaches online one-to-one IB tuition on UAE evening hours; none of them visits a UAE address.

intro.heading: A prediction is a document, not an opinion
paragraphs: A UAE parent who searches for IB predicted grades improvement usually has a piece of paper in hand: a December report, a mock transcript, or a university portal showing 32 points against an offer that asks for 36. The useful thing to understand first is that the prediction is not a forecast issued by the IB. It is a judgement your child's Diploma Programme coordinator and subject teachers write, from evidence held inside the school, and it travels on the university application with the school's name attached to it rather than yours.

That changes where the work goes. Nobody outside the school can edit the number, and any service that implies it can should be treated with real scepticism. What outside help can do is change the evidence the school is reading — the structure of a timed Paper 2 essay, the command-term discipline in a six-mark answer, the data treatment in a draft exploration — and then make sure the coordinator sees that change before predictions are written or revised. Money spent on prediction work is money spent producing better evidence inside a window that closes.

The window is narrower than most families assume. In a UAE Diploma school the two heaviest pieces of evidence are the DP1 end-of-year examinations sat in June and the DP2 mock results marked in school, usually in late November, December or January. Overseas applications then sit on top of that calendar: an October deadline for the earliest course group, a mid-January deadline for equal consideration in the United Kingdom, and autumn early-action deadlines for United States universities. Confirm every one of those dates on ucas.com or the university's own admissions page, because they move by cycle.

The cost side is where UAE families are quoted the widest range and given the least information. Published market rates run from roughly AED 45 an hour for a university-student tutor to AED 650 an hour at the premium end, and the figure a family is quoted is driven by four things: the level taught, whether the tutor is a Diploma subject specialist, whether anyone is travelling, and how close the session sits to an assessment. Nobody prices the fifth driver, which is wasted hours spent on components whose marks are already banked and cannot move a prediction at all.

This page is built around that arithmetic. It names the four grade documents a DP2 family handles, shows the evidence a coordinator reads, costs prediction support product by product in AED with the source named, and sets out what happens when July results land under the prediction. One point to state plainly before any of it: IB Gram does not sell in-person lessons in Dubai or anywhere else in the Emirates, and it does not run home visits in the UAE — that service exists only in India. A Diploma family in Khalifa City gets a Physics HL specialist who has marked the paper, rather than whoever happens to live twenty minutes away.
bullets: A prediction is written by the school, from school evidence; no tutor and no platform can issue one.
The two heaviest pieces of evidence are DP1 June examinations and DP2 mock results, both marked inside your child's school.
Market rates for IB-specialist support run roughly AED 200-450 an hour (Bestimate Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026; TutorChase quotes AED 270).
An internal assessment mark already submitted is banked: paid hours spent there buy nothing for the prediction.
A reprediction request is a conversation with the school, made by you, supported by evidence of the student's own work.

ib-predicted-grades-improvement.programmesIntro: Predictions work differently depending on which IB programme your child sits, and UAE schools run three of them side by side. The Diploma Programme produces the predicted grades universities read. The Career-related Programme predicts its DP courses the same way but adds a reflective project. The Middle Years Programme produces criterion levels that schools use privately to project a future Diploma grade.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS. The IB points total runs to 45: six subject grades of 1-7 giving 42, with up to three further points from the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay combination. A prediction is issued per subject, and the coordinator also states an expected points total. Both figures sit on the university application.
programmes.countryNote: In UAE schools the DP2 mock sitting is the single event that most often rewrites a prediction, and it usually falls between late November and January. Most Diploma schools here are inspected by KHDA in Dubai or ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, and every one of them is also the examination centre for the session, which means entry and upload deadlines reach you through the school rather than from the IB.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller UAE cohort takes the Career-related Programme: at least two Diploma courses, a career-related study, and the core of personal and professional skills, service learning, language development and the reflective project. The Diploma courses carry ordinary 1-7 predictions, so prediction work on them looks identical to Diploma work. The reflective project is assessed against its own criteria and marked in school.
programmes.countryNote: CP students applying from the Emirates usually face an extra explanatory step, because some admissions teams are less familiar with the certificate than with the full Diploma. Ask the coordinator what the school writes in the reference about course predictions versus the overall programme, and keep the Ministry of Education equivalency question separate: equivalency is decided on final certificates, never on a prediction.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP subjects are graded on criteria A to D, each with its own mark band, which the school converts to a 1-7 level. There is no predicted grade for universities at this stage, but schools do use MYP5 levels to advise on Higher Level choices and to project a future Diploma grade. A weak criterion D in sciences at MYP5 is the most common reason a school advises against three Higher Level sciences.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai and Abu Dhabi, the MYP-to-Diploma handover is where most prediction problems are born. A student who arrives in DP1 with a criterion-based report and no experience of timed, externally marked papers will often post a DP1 June result two grades below their MYP level. Fixing that in DP1 costs a fraction of fixing it in February of DP2, which is the clearest value argument on this whole page.

ib-predicted-grades-improvement.subjectsIntro: Predictions are written subject by subject, and each subject gives the coordinator a different kind of evidence. The grid below describes what a school is actually looking at in each course, and where a weekly hour tends to pay for itself before a prediction is entered.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Predictions here lean heavily on timed paper evidence, because the course rewards technique under pressure. Higher Level adds Paper 3, a longer problem-solving paper that frequently separates a 5 from a 6. Schools also weigh the exploration mark once it is in. Paid hours move most when they are spent on method marks and on the proof and calculus questions students routinely abandon.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The technology-rich route, with a graphic display calculator required throughout. Predictions tend to track how reliably a student sets up a model and interprets output in context, rather than raw algebra. Common evidence of weakness is a student who reaches the right number and loses the interpretation marks. Prediction work is normally about writing conclusions that answer the question asked.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Higher Level predictions usually turn on the extended-response questions and on data analysis skills from the practical programme. UAE schools often run DP2 mocks before the full HL option content is taught, which depresses mock marks and therefore predictions. If that is your child's situation, say so to the coordinator — it is a reprediction argument that a tutor can evidence with topic-by-topic work.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium are where UAE Diploma students most often lose the marks that cap a prediction at 4 or 5. Multiple-choice performance is a fast diagnostic: a student scoring well there but poorly on structured questions has an answer-writing problem, not a content problem, and that is the cheaper of the two to fix before predictions.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content volume makes Biology the subject where mock results most often understate a student, because revision was incomplete rather than ineffective. Coordinators know this, which makes Biology one of the more repredictable subjects when a student can show accurate recall plus command-term control. Evidence that persuades is a set of marked past-paper questions across topics not yet revised at mock time.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation are the two mark drivers, and both are visible in a mock script. Higher Level adds quantitative questions and a policy paper that rewards structured judgement. Internal assessment commentaries are marked in school, so a student whose commentary marks are already strong has a prediction floor that paper work can lift further.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Predictions draw on the individual oral, the paper on unseen non-literary texts, and the comparative essay at Higher Level. The oral is internally assessed and often already banked by mock season. Where paid hours work is on the unseen analysis paper, because a repeatable reading method visibly changes a script between December and February.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The pre-release case study drives a large part of the final paper, and schools can see from a mock whether a student is applying tools or describing a company. Predictions tend to move when application and evaluation improve together. The internal assessment is a research project on the student's own chosen organisation, reviewed and fed back on, never produced for them.

ib-predicted-grades-improvement.regionsIntro: Predictions are a school-level process, so the emirate your child studies in changes who inspects the school, what the school calendar looks like, and which admissions route the family is planning for. The notes below cover the seven emirates as they actually affect a prediction timetable.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The largest Diploma cohort in the country, inspected by KHDA, which confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for 2026-27. Mock sittings cluster in late November and December, so DP2 prediction work in Dubai schools is usually priced and planned in September.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK licenses and accredits private schools in the emirate, and its professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. For a prediction that means the person writing the number should not also be the person being paid to lift it.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a smaller Diploma cohort and fewer Higher Level option blocks per school. Families here most often hit the problem of a subject the school cannot timetable, which shows up later as a prediction written from thin evidence in that subject.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves curricula, fees and assessment methods, not just inspection outcomes. Commutes into Dubai schools are common from Sharjah, which pushes realistic session start times past 18:00 on weekdays.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority. Diploma provision is limited, so a number of Ajman families have a child enrolled in a Dubai or Sharjah school and a prediction calendar set by that school, not by where they live.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and, like Sharjah, approves curricula and assessment methods. Distance from the Dubai tutoring market is exactly why online delivery matters here: subject specialism stops depending on driving radius.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education supervision, a small private sector, and almost no published competitor content for IB families on the east coast. Prediction support is realistically online here, because the pool of Diploma specialists within reach of a car journey is very small.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised by the Ministry of Education. Families typically plan around a school in a neighbouring emirate, so the practical questions are session timing against the commute home and whether a mock result from another emirate's school is being read correctly.

schoolClusters.note: These are schools UAE families name most often when they call about a prediction. Programme offerings and inspection ratings change by year, so confirm both with the school and against KHDA's own school listing before you rely on them. Students supported by IB Gram attend schools like these; there is no affiliation in either direction.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School, Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.note: Abu Dhabi Diploma schools sit under ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Mock windows and internal coursework deadlines differ from Dubai schools by a fortnight or more, which matters when a family is costing a block of prediction work against an application deadline.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.note: Outside Dubai and Abu Dhabi the number of schools running the full Diploma drops sharply, and so does the local supply of Higher Level specialists. Check each school's current programme authorisation with the school and with SPEA, the Ras Al Khaimah Department of Knowledge, or the Ministry of Education as appropriate.

ib-predicted-grades-improvement.modesIntro: Prediction work is bought in four recognisable shapes in this market, and they cost very different amounts for very different reasons. All four are delivered as online one-to-one IB tuition over live video, scheduled around a UAE school day and the commute that follows it.

modes.title: A single diagnostic hour on one marked script
modes.description: The cheapest useful purchase available to a DP2 family. You send the marked mock script, the mark scheme comments the school gave, and the current prediction. One hour produces a written read of where the marks went, split into content gaps, technique gaps and timing losses. Families routinely discover that the subject they were about to fund is not the subject with the gap.
bullets: Needs the actual script, not a transcript of grades
Output is a written note you can keep and forward
Often redirects spending to a different subject

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through the prediction window
modes.description: One hour a week per subject from September to the reprediction window in February or March. This is the shape that produces the evidence a coordinator can act on, because it generates a steady run of timed work under the same conditions as the school's own assessments. Two subjects a week is the practical ceiling for most DP2 students carrying coursework deadlines at the same time.
bullets: 60 or 90 minutes, Gulf Standard Time, after the school run
Timed questions marked to published command terms
A fortnightly progress note you can share with the school
Pausable during mock week and coursework deadlines

modes.title: A post-mock evidence block
modes.description: A concentrated block of six to twelve hours in the four weeks after mock results, aimed squarely at the evidence the school will read before revising a prediction. The work is paper technique on the specific question types the mock exposed, plus a set of timed questions the student completes unsupervised and has marked. It is the highest-value block in the Diploma year for a family that cannot fund a full year.
bullets: Starts from the mock script and the school's own feedback

Timed to land before the coordinator's review, not after

modes.title: Core supervision hours on TOK and the Extended Essay
modes.description: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay carry up to three points on the IB points total, so they are frequently the cheapest route to a higher predicted total. Sessions are process coaching: reading the criteria together, questioning an argument, checking a research question is answerable, reviewing the student's own draft and giving feedback on it. The student writes every word themselves.

Research-question and argument coaching, not content supply
Referencing and academic-honesty checks before submission

sections.heading: Four documents say grade, and only one of them reaches a university
paragraphs: A DP2 family in the Emirates handles four or five different numbers in the same term, and they are not the same animal. The termly report grade is a teacher's running judgement on classwork and effort. The DP2 mock result is a school examination, marked in school, against the school's own reading of IB standards. The IB predicted grade on the university application is a formal statement of what the school expects the student to achieve in the final session. The awarded grade in July is the only number the IB itself issues.

Confusing them costs money. A parent who sees a 5 on a December report and books forty hours is often buying hours against a document no admissions officer will ever read. The figure that decides an offer is the one the coordinator enters on the application, and in most UAE schools it is written once, inside a short window, from a small and identifiable evidence pile. Working out which document you are trying to change is the first piece of cost control available to a family, and it is free.

There is a further prediction families rarely hear about. Subject teachers also submit predicted grades to the IB for its own administration and moderation purposes. That submission has no bearing on your child's university file and is not something a parent negotiates. So when a coordinator says predictions have already gone, ask which set has gone — the application predictions or the IB submission. The answer tells you whether a reprediction request is still live this term or whether the spending should move to the final papers instead.
