sections.heading: The evidence a coordinator reads before writing a number
paragraphs: Ask ten UAE Diploma coordinators how a prediction is set and you will get ten slightly different processes, but the inputs are consistent. The DP1 June examination result establishes a baseline. The DP2 mock result is the heaviest single input, because it is the most recent full-length evidence under examination conditions. Internal assessment marks, once submitted, are hard evidence of attainment in that component. Class assessments, timed questions and the student's deadline record fill in the gaps, and the subject teacher's professional judgement arbitrates between them.

This matters commercially because evidence has a production date. Nothing a family buys in March can change what the June DP1 examination showed, and nothing bought in February changes a mock sat in December. The whole value of early spending is that it lands inside an evidence window rather than after it. A family who starts weekly hours in September is paying for better mock evidence; a family who starts in February is paying for better final papers and hoping the school will revisit the number on request.

There is one input families consistently underrate: the deadline and attendance record. A student who has missed internal deadlines has given the coordinator a reason to predict conservatively that has nothing to do with subject ability. Fixing that costs nothing. Hand in the next three pieces on time, and the reprediction conversation becomes a conversation about marks rather than about reliability. Ask the coordinator directly which of the two is driving the current number, because the answer decides whether you need to buy hours at all.

sections.heading: The prediction year, counted backwards from an application deadline
paragraphs: A Diploma family planning an overseas application is working to two calendars at once, and they do not line up. The IB calendar runs to the May session the vast majority of UAE schools sit. The admissions calendar runs much earlier: an October deadline for the earliest United Kingdom course group, autumn early-action deadlines in the United States, a mid-January deadline for equal consideration in the United Kingdom, and rolling dates for universities in the Emirates and elsewhere in the Gulf. Confirm each one on the university's own admissions page, because they change between cycles.

Counted backwards, that produces a hard conclusion about spending. Predictions for a January application are written from evidence that exists in December. So the money that changes a January application has to be spent in September, October and November. Money spent in February and March cannot change what was sent in January; it can only support a reprediction request and improve the final grade. Families who understand this stop buying crisis hours in spring and start buying cheaper, steadier hours in autumn.

Local applications run on a different logic again. A UAE university reading an application from a Diploma student will usually make a conditional offer against the final award and will want the Ministry of Education equivalency file built on certificates, not predictions. Keep the two tracks separate in your planning. The overseas track is prediction-driven and front-loaded; the local track is final-result-driven, which means the May papers, not the December mock, are where the spending belongs.

sections.heading: What prediction-focused support costs across the Emirates
paragraphs: The UAE tutoring market quotes a range of roughly fourteen to one for the same hour, and almost no ranking page publishes a single AED figure. Here is what the published sources actually show. EdFlik advertises from AED 45-65 an hour and Tutopiya from AED 33-52 at the budget end. Unitors publishes IGCSE support from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. TutorChase quotes AED 270. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts in-home visits at AED 180-350 and specialist IB, IGCSE and A-Level work at AED 200-450 and above, with BartyED at AED 650 at the premium end.

IB tutoring rates in AED are driven by level and specialism far more than by anything else. A Higher Level Diploma subject with a Paper 3 narrows the pool of people who can teach it credibly, and the price follows the scarcity. Travel is the second driver, and it is the one families pay for without seeing it on the invoice: an in-home hour that includes a forty-minute drive each way is an hour of teaching priced to cover two and a half hours of a tutor's day. Monthly packages seen in this market run around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599-1,799 for four in-home two-hour sessions.

Set those numbers against the fee context. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27, under an economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. The figures in the table below are market figures from the sources named, read in October 2026. They are not IB Gram prices; our own fee comes with a free trial lesson and a consultation first, so you can see the tutor before any block is agreed.

sections.heading: Banked, live or closed: where paid hours actually land
paragraphs: The Diploma is not one grade; it is a set of components in different states. Some are banked, meaning the mark is submitted and settled. Some are live, meaning the student can still change the mark. Some are closed, meaning the opportunity has passed and only the final paper remains. A family that knows which components are in which state can cut a quoted block of forty hours down to twelve without losing anything that moves a prediction.

Here is the test. Ask of each component: has a mark for this already been submitted? If yes, no amount of paid work changes it, and work there can only help indirectly by building subject understanding for the papers. If no, and a deadline is still ahead, the component is live and this is where hours have the most leverage, because a prediction is partly built from internal assessment marks that have not yet been finalised. If the deadline has passed and no mark exists yet, ask the school when the mark is confirmed before spending anything.

This is also where the Higher Level grade improvement question gets an honest answer. The components most responsive to a short block are the externally examined papers, because technique, timing and command-term control change quickly and visibly. The least responsive is a submitted internal assessment, which is simply finished. Between them sit Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay, which can carry up to three points on the IB points total and are often the cheapest point on the board for a student sitting at 33 against a 34-point offer.

sections.heading: How a reprediction request is really handled
paragraphs: A reprediction request is a school process, not an appeal to anybody outside the school. There is no form, no regulator and no third party. It is a parent or student asking the Diploma Programme coordinator to review a number in the light of evidence that did not exist when the number was written. Schools that allow it usually do so in a defined window, often February or March, and usually once. Ask when that window is before you plan any spending around it.

What persuades is dated, marked work in the student's own hand that postdates the evidence the prediction was built on. A set of past-paper questions on the topics the mock exposed, marked against published criteria, with the marks written on them, is worth more than any letter of support. A written progress note from a tutor can accompany it, describing what has been taught and what the student now does independently, but it is corroboration. The student's own work is the case.

What does not persuade: a request framed as a complaint about the mock, a request that arrives with an offer attached as leverage, or a bundle of tutor-produced material. Coordinators read dozens of these. The ones that succeed are specific — one subject, one gap, evidence that the gap is closed — and they arrive before the window shuts rather than the week after. If the school declines, the sensible response is to redirect the money at the final papers, because the awarded grade in July can still clear a conditional offer even when the prediction did not.

One more point worth saying plainly to a UAE family. A tutor should never contact your child's school on your behalf without being asked, and should never approach a coordinator to argue for a number. If a service offers to do that, or implies it has influence over how a school predicts, it is selling something it does not have.

sections.heading: Which grade is the cheapest point to buy
paragraphs: Offers are made in points, and points are not all equally expensive. A student predicted 33 against a 35-point offer has a two-point gap, and there are usually three or four different ways to close it. One is to lift a Standard Level subject sitting on the boundary, which often needs nothing more than consistent exam technique. Another is to lift a Higher Level subject where the student is a long way from the next band, which is the most expensive option on the board. A third is the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay combination, which can be worth up to three points on the IB points total.

Work it out before buying anything. Take the current prediction subject by subject, mark the distance to the next grade in each, and ask the subject teacher where the student actually sits inside their band. A student two marks below a boundary in Economics Standard Level and fifteen marks below in Physics Higher Level should not be funding Physics first, however much the Physics grade matters for the course applied for. The exception is a course with a subject-specific condition, where a particular Higher Level grade is non-negotiable and the arithmetic does not apply.

The scenarios below are worked examples at published market rates, not promises about outcomes. No tutor can promise a grade, and anybody selling a points total should be treated with suspicion. What the arithmetic does is stop a family spending AED 5,000 on the hardest point available when a cheaper one was sitting in another subject the whole time. That is the cost-and-value core of prediction work: not more hours, but hours aimed at the point that is closest to being won.

sections.heading: When July results land under the prediction
paragraphs: It happens, and it is not the catastrophe families fear in the first hour. A conditional offer is a contract about the final award, not about the prediction, so the question on results day is whether the awarded grades meet the condition. Where they do, the prediction is irrelevant. Where they fall short by a small margin, the university may still confirm the place, particularly where the shortfall is in a subject not named in the condition. The first call is to the university, not to the school.

After that, there are defined routes and each has a cost and a clock. An enquiry upon results is a school-initiated process asking for a component or a candidate's marks to be checked, and in the UAE it is your child's school, as the examination centre, that submits it. Fees apply and are set by the board. A retake in the next session is a second route, and for a Diploma student that means the November session, which the school must be running and must enter the candidate for. Deferred entry is a third, and a different offer through the clearing process is a fourth.

The cost planning here is simple and nobody publishes it. Build a contingency into the Diploma budget rather than treating results day as a surprise. Families who have set aside the equivalent of a short block of specialist hours find the November decision much easier to make, because the decision becomes a choice about the best route rather than a choice about what is affordable in August. Ask the coordinator in March, not July, what the school's policy and deadlines are for enquiries and for November entries.

sections.heading: Who answers for a prediction in each emirate
paragraphs: The UAE has five separate authorities regulating private schools, and no competitor page in this market maps them properly. In Dubai, the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge does so in Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

Two of those bodies go further than inspection. The authorities in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is worth knowing because it shapes what a school can and cannot change mid-year. None of the five, however, arbitrates an individual predicted grade. A prediction is a professional judgement made inside the school, and the route for a dispute is the school's own process, escalated through its leadership.

The regulator does matter for who may teach your child privately. Private tuition in the UAE runs on a permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, granted free of charge for two years through MoHRE, with registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18 among those eligible. Anyone offering private tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted to you. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules also bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school — which is exactly the person who would otherwise be writing the prediction.

sections.heading: What a tutor refuses, even with an offer on the line
paragraphs: This part of the market has a genuine integrity problem, and a UAE parent under offer pressure is exactly who it targets. One competitor researched for this project sells finished Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Accepting that is academic malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence lands on the student, not the seller: a malpractice finding can cost the Diploma entirely. No prediction is worth that, and no offer survives it.

The line is clear and it is worth stating in plain terms. A tutor teaches, questions, reviews and gives feedback. A tutor reads the criteria with the student, asks whether an argument holds, points at a paragraph that does not answer the research question, and shows how a method should be reported. A tutor does not supply sentences for an assessed submission, does not edit a draft into a finished state, and does not provide material to be handed in as the student's own. If a family asks for that, the honest answer is no, with the reason given.

There is a second refusal worth knowing about. Do not accept an offer of paid lessons from a teacher who teaches your child at their own school, especially one involved in writing the prediction. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar it outright, and the MoHRE permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Beyond the rules, it puts the person who grades your child in a paid relationship with you, which is not a position any family should want to be in during prediction season.
bullets: A tutor gives feedback on the student's own draft; the student writes every word.
No service can supply assessed work, and accepting one risks the whole Diploma.
Past papers, mark schemes and subject guides are referenced and linked, never reproduced or supplied.
Your child's own teacher should not be the person being paid to lift your child's prediction.

sections.heading: Predictions, equivalency and the Ministry subjects in the same week
paragraphs: Two things sit alongside the prediction in a UAE Diploma year and both get forgotten in planning. The first is Ministry of Education equivalency, the process that makes a school certificate usable for a UAE university or for employment here. It is decided on final certificates, so a prediction plays no part in it. For the British track, the published requirement is five subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education not included among the five, plus one subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

For the American track, the published requirement includes English proficiency shown by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics shown by at least 450 in the SAT Math test. No IB points threshold for equivalency has been read on an official Ministry page for this project, so none is published here. Verify your child's track on moe.gov.ae or with the school's university counsellor, and note that IB Gram describes the process but does not perform it or influence its outcome.

The second forgotten item is the mandatory UAE subject load. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies are required in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. These subjects do not affect a Diploma prediction, but they sit in the same week as the mock revision and they need their own line in the budget.

process.title: Send the evidence, not a summary
process.description: Start by sending the marked mock script, the school's own feedback, the current prediction and the offer conditions. A grade on its own says a student is at a 5; a script says why. Families who send the paperwork get a useful plan in one conversation rather than three.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson first
process.description: One lesson with the proposed tutor, on a real piece of work, at no charge and with no card required. Your child decides whether the explanation lands. Nothing is booked, and no block is agreed, until after that lesson has happened.

process.title: Get a written plan keyed to your school's dates
process.description: The plan names the subject, the components still open, the school's mock and coursework dates, the number of hours and what each hour is for. If the plan cannot say which piece of evidence it is trying to improve and by when, it is not a plan worth paying for.

process.title: Run weekly hours with a note you can forward
process.description: Sessions are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Every fortnight you get a short written note on what has been taught and what the student now does unsupported. That note is the thing you keep for the reprediction conversation.

process.title: Make the reprediction request yourself
process.description: You and your child approach the Diploma Programme coordinator, inside the school's window, with dated marked work in the student's own hand. A tutor supplies the progress note if you want one. A tutor does not contact the school on your behalf or argue for a number.

process.title: Decide early what happens in July
process.description: Agree in March what the family does if a result lands under the prediction: call the university, ask the school about an enquiry upon results, consider the November session, or take a different offer. Deciding in advance makes results day a process rather than a panic.

whyPoints.title: Hours aimed at the point closest to being won
whyPoints.description: A quoted block of forty hours usually contains twelve that matter. The diagnostic is about finding the component that is still open and closest to a boundary, and then spending there. That is the difference between a bill and an investment in a UAE Diploma year.

whyPoints.title: Every AED figure on this page has a source
whyPoints.description: Market rates here are attributed to the provider or rate table that published them, with the month they were read. Three of six ranking competitors publish no price at all and two quote in dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in.

whyPoints.title: Specialism instead of driving radius
whyPoints.description: Online one-to-one IB tuition means a family in Fujairah or Ras Al Khaimah picks a Higher Level specialist on subject fit rather than on who can reach the villa by 17:00. For Paper 3 subjects, that is often the difference between help and company.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what paid work cannot touch
whyPoints.description: A submitted internal assessment mark is banked and no block of hours changes it. Saying so costs us a sale and saves a family several thousand dirhams, which is the only version of this business worth running at scale.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is published, not implied
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, reviews and gives feedback on the student's own work. Nothing is produced for a student to submit. In a market where finished coursework is openly sold, that boundary is written on the page rather than left to be assumed.

whyPoints.title: Scheduled around a UAE school week
whyPoints.description: Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time, after the school run and around the commute, and move to post-Iftar slots during Ramadan. Mock weeks and coursework deadlines can be paused rather than paid for twice.

faqs.question: What exactly is an IB predicted grade, and who in a UAE school writes it?
faqs.answer: It is a formal statement of the grade your child's school expects them to achieve in the final session, written per subject and used by universities to assess an application. In a UAE Diploma school it is produced by the subject teacher and confirmed by the Diploma Programme coordinator, from evidence the school holds: DP1 examinations, DP2 mock results, internal assessment marks and class work. The IB does not issue it, no tutor can issue it, and no platform can change it directly. What outside support can change is the evidence the school reads before the number is written or reviewed.

faqs.question: When do UAE Diploma schools usually enter predicted grades for applications?
faqs.answer: Most UAE schools write predictions around the DP2 mock sitting, which typically falls between late November and January, and enter them in time for the application deadlines the student is working to. Because an early United Kingdom course group closes in October and the equal-consideration deadline sits in mid-January, the evidence behind a prediction often has to exist by December. Ask your coordinator for two dates in September: when predictions are written, and whether there is a review window afterwards. Those two dates determine when money spent on tuition can still affect what a university reads.

faqs.question: Can a predicted grade be revised after it has already been sent to a university?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is a school decision rather than an entitlement. Where a school allows a revision it normally does so in a defined window, often February or March, and usually once per subject. The school then updates the figure through the application system. Universities vary in how much weight they give a revised prediction that arrives late in the cycle, and some will have made their decision already. Ask the coordinator whether the school revises predictions at all before you build a spending plan around the possibility, because a number of UAE schools simply do not.

faqs.question: What evidence does a coordinator actually want before revising a prediction?
faqs.answer: Dated, marked work in the student's own hand that postdates the evidence the original prediction was built on. A set of past-paper questions covering the topics the mock exposed, marked against published criteria with the marks shown, is the strongest single item a family can bring. A short written progress note from a tutor can accompany it, describing what has been taught and what the student now does independently. What does not work is a complaint about the mock, an offer letter used as leverage, or a bundle of material the tutor produced rather than the student.

faqs.question: How much does prediction-focused IB support cost in the Emirates?
faqs.answer: Published market rates run wide. Budget online tutors advertise from AED 33-65 an hour, qualified subject tutors from AED 150-300, Diploma specialists at AED 200-450 and above, in-home visits at AED 180-500 including travel, and premium named tutors up to AED 650. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are the market figures published by EdFlik, Tutopiya, Unitors, TutorChase, BartyED and Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 table, read in October 2026. They are not IB Gram prices; ours come with a free trial lesson and a consultation first.

faqs.question: Is it better value to fund one subject hard or three subjects lightly?
faqs.answer: One subject, almost always, when the goal is a prediction. Three subjects at one hour a week each spreads a small amount of teaching across three evidence trails and rarely moves any of them far enough to cross a boundary. One subject at one hour a week, plus marked timed work between sessions, produces a visible change in a single evidence trail that a coordinator can act on. Pick the subject by distance to the next grade rather than by how much the subject matters to the course applied for, unless the offer names that subject specifically.

faqs.question: Our daughter is predicted 33 points and her offer asks for 36. What now?
faqs.answer: Map the gap before spending anything. Take each subject, find how far she is from the next grade, and ask each teacher where she sits inside her current band. A subject two marks below a boundary is a cheap point; one fifteen marks below is not. Then check whether the Theory of Knowledge and Extended Essay combination is still open, because that pair carries up to three points on the IB points total and is frequently the least expensive route. Finally, call the university: some will discuss a three-point shortfall directly, particularly where no subject-specific condition is attached.

faqs.question: Does an internal assessment mark that is already submitted still move with tutoring?
faqs.answer: No. Once the school has submitted the mark it is banked, and the only remaining variation comes from IB moderation, which nobody outside the process influences. Paid hours on that component can still help indirectly, because the subject understanding feeds the examined papers, but they will not change the submitted mark or the part of the prediction built on it. This is the single most common way UAE families waste money in DP2. Ask the school which internal marks are already submitted before agreeing any block of hours.

faqs.question: Should a tutor speak to my child's Diploma Programme coordinator about the prediction?
faqs.answer: Not on your behalf and not to argue for a number. The reprediction conversation belongs to you and your child, inside the school's own process. A tutor's proper contribution is a written progress note describing what has been taught and what the student can now do unsupported, which you hand over as corroboration for the student's own marked work. Any service that offers to lobby a school, or that implies influence over how a UAE school predicts, is selling something it does not have and should be declined.

faqs.question: What happens if the July results come in below the predicted grades?
faqs.answer: The conditional offer is about the final award, not the prediction, so the first question is whether the awarded grades meet the stated condition. Call the university early on results day; a small shortfall in a subject not named in the condition is often confirmed anyway. After that the routes are an enquiry upon results submitted by the school as examination centre, a retake in the next session that the school must enter the candidate for, deferred entry, or a different offer through clearing. Each has a board or university deadline, so ask the coordinator in March what the school's policy is.

faqs.question: Do predicted grades matter for a UAE university, or only for overseas applications?
faqs.answer: Predictions carry most weight in overseas applications, particularly in the United Kingdom and the United States, where offers are made months before results. Universities in the Emirates typically make a conditional offer against the final award and want the certificate itself, alongside a Ministry of Education equivalency file where required. The practical consequence for spending is useful: a family applying locally should put money into the May papers rather than into mock-season evidence, because the final grade is what the local admissions file reads.

faqs.question: Are predicted grades part of a Ministry of Education equivalency file?
faqs.answer: No. Equivalency is decided on final certificates and transcripts, not on predictions. For the British track the published requirement is five subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from those five, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. No IB points threshold has been read on an official Ministry page for this project, so none is published here. Verify your child's track on moe.gov.ae, and treat the process as something you complete, not something a tutoring service performs.

faqs.question: Does a weak Arabic or Islamic Education report grade pull a Diploma prediction down?
faqs.answer: Not directly. Those are mandatory UAE subjects required in Dubai private schools whatever the licensed curriculum, taught and assessed by the school, and they sit outside the six Diploma subjects a prediction is written for. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. What they do affect is the week: they occupy timetable space during mock revision, and they need their own line in a family budget rather than being absorbed into Diploma tuition.

faqs.question: Is a predicted grade the same thing as the grade on my child's school report?
faqs.answer: No, and treating them as the same is an expensive mistake. A report grade is a running judgement on recent classwork, written several times a year. A prediction is a single formal statement of expected final attainment, written once, for an external audience, from a specific evidence pile. A student can carry a 6 on a December report and a 5 on the application if the mock evidence pointed that way. Before booking anything, ask the school which number you are looking at and which one went to the universities.

faqs.question: Can anything useful still be done in the four weeks after mock results?
faqs.answer: Yes, and those four weeks are the highest-value block in the Diploma year for a family that cannot fund a full year of weekly hours. The work starts from the marked script, targets the specific question types the mock exposed, and produces dated timed work the student completes and has marked. It needs to land before the school's review window rather than after it, which is why the date of that window is the first thing to establish. Six to twelve hours in one subject is the usual shape at this point.

faqs.question: Can lessons move during Ramadan and around the UAE school week?
faqs.answer: Yes. Sessions run on Gulf Standard Time and are normally scheduled after the school run, with a later start for families commuting from Sharjah or Ajman into Dubai schools. During Ramadan the school day shortens and most families move sessions to post-Iftar slots; the pattern usually holds for the month and reverts afterwards. Mock weeks, coursework deadline weeks and family travel can be paused rather than paid for twice. Because delivery is online, a schedule that follows a family abroad over a holiday break costs nothing extra to arrange.

ib-predicted-grades-improvement.closingHeading: Start with the evidence, not with a block of hours
ib-predicted-grades-improvement.closingBody: If you have a mock script, a current prediction and an offer condition, you have everything a useful first conversation needs. Send those three things and take the free trial lesson: one hour on a real piece of your child's work, no card required, before anything is booked. You may be told that the subject you were about to fund is not the one with the gap, or that the component you were worried about is already banked and closed. That answer is worth having either way. Lessons that follow are one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, keyed to your school's own mock and coursework dates.

intro.heading: Private tuition is a regulated arrangement here, not an informal favour
paragraphs: Most families start looking for IB private tuition in the UAE in the week after a report card. The search is usually about one subject, because Chemistry HL has slipped from a 5 to a 4 or Mathematics has stopped making sense. The arrangement you are about to enter, though, has a legal and administrative shape that nobody at the school will walk you through. Knowing that shape before you pay anyone changes the questions you ask, and it changes which providers survive those questions.

Three separate systems meet inside a single private tuition arrangement. The first is federal: private tutoring runs on a work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 through the Ministry of Human Resources and Emiratisation, and u.ae states that individuals offering private tutoring without that permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. The second is the emirate. Whoever licensed your child's school, whether that is KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Sharjah Private Education Authority, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah or the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, also decides what else your child must study, and in two emirates approves the curriculum and the fees as well. The third is the IB itself, whose academic-honesty rules fix how close any tutor may come to an Internal Assessment.

None of that makes private tuition hard to buy. It makes it checkable. A tutor who holds the permit can say so and name the category it was issued under. A provider with premises in Dubai can produce an Educational Services Permit number from the training-institute route. A platform teaching from outside the country can say that in one sentence instead of routing a UAE parent to a foreign dialling code. The providers that fail those three questions tend to be the same ones quoting a price in US dollars and showing a star rating nobody can trace to a countable review.

IB Gram works to one model in the UAE. A parent describes the subject, the level and the deadline; we match one subject specialist; lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. Nobody travels to a UAE address, and we state that on every country page we publish, because implying a visit we do not make is the most common misrepresentation in this market. What a Dubai or Sharjah family gets instead is a tutor chosen for the syllabus rather than for the driving distance: a Physics HL specialist who has taught the current assessment model, not whoever happens to cover your community on a Tuesday evening.

The rest of this page is the system, laid out in the order it affects you. Who may legally give private tuition. Who licensed the school. What the Dubai market looks like in numbers. What the market charges by the month. What information you should hand over at enquiry and what you should keep back. Which teaching material may properly change hands. The Ministry subjects that run beside the Diploma. The equivalency file your child will eventually need. And the exam calendar that decides whether tuition is already running or still being arranged.

ib-private-tuition.programmesIntro: IB Gram covers the IB programmes a UAE private school is likely to run. Each one meets the emirate regulator differently, because the licence that permits the programme carries the Ministry-subject requirement with it, and that is usually where a private tuition plan has to make room in an already full week.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units built around six subject areas, with the exhibition in the final year as the first piece of extended independent work a child produces. There are no external exams, so progress is read from the school's own reporting against the learner profile and the unit objectives. Private tuition at this stage is almost always about reading fluency, number sense or written English, and the useful version is short, frequent and tied to the unit the class is on.
programmes.countryNote: In a Dubai private school the Ministry subjects start here, not at secondary. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies sit in the timetable from the primary years, with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, so a parent arranging Arabic support needs to know which stream their child is in before anyone quotes an hourly rate.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Eight subject groups assessed against four published criteria, each marked out of 8, which is why an MYP report reads nothing like an IGCSE one. A student can hold a 6 in a criterion and a 3 in the one next to it, and the average hides the problem. The Personal Project in the final year is the first assessed independent task with a real supervision process attached to it.
programmes.countryNote: The MYP route into DP1 is where UAE families most often arrive at private tuition, because criterion marks do not convert into a predicted Diploma grade and nobody tells a parent that until October of DP1. Two of the three new IB schools opening in Dubai for 2026-27 add more MYP cohorts to an already small specialist pool.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, marked out of 45 points in total. Every subject carries an internally assessed component alongside the written papers, and the internal work is set by the school's own calendar rather than the exam board's. The May session is the one UAE schools sit, with November available for retakes at some centres.
programmes.countryNote: The IB accounted for a 7% share of Dubai's private-school roll in 2024-25, the smallest of the four main curricula in the emirate, which is exactly why a Higher Level specialist is harder to find locally than an A-Level or CBSE one. It is also the programme whose equivalency position a UAE family should check on moe.gov.ae early rather than in Year 13.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: A smaller set of DP courses taken alongside a career-related study, with personal and professional skills, service learning, language development and a reflective project making up the core. Students sit the same DP examinations in the subjects they take, so the tuition need is identical in those subjects, with the reflective project needing process supervision rather than teaching.
programmes.countryNote: Far fewer UAE schools are licensed for the CP than for the DP, so check the school's own programme listing with the emirate authority before assuming it is on offer. Where it runs, the career-related study is usually delivered with a local partner institution, and tuition is sensible only in the examined DP subjects.

ib-private-tuition.subjectsIntro: These are the IB subjects UAE families most often arrange private tuition for, with what each one actually assesses. A request is matched on syllabus and level rather than on a general subject label, because Biology HL and Biology SL sit different papers with different weightings and the hours needed are not the same.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency carries the whole course. HL adds Paper 3, a long problem-solving paper where marks go to students who cannot sustain an argument over several linked parts. The exploration is marked against criteria A to E for a total of 20 marks, and personal engagement and reflection are where most UAE students lose them.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology use, with the graphical calculator expected rather than optional. Students who moved from CBSE or an American system often arrive strong on computation and weak on interpretation, and the marks sit in the interpretation. Check the route against the entry requirements of the universities on your child's list before switching.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics and fields decide the grade, and the HL extensions are where a strong MYP student is most likely to stall. Data analysis is assessed throughout, not only in the internal work, so uncertainty handling and graph treatment need practising weekly rather than revisiting before the mock.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics generate most of the tuition requests we see from UAE families. Marks are lost on precision of language, on failing to state conditions and on treating a multi-step calculation as arithmetic rather than as chemistry with units attached to every stage.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the trap. Students revise breadth and get caught by command terms, because explain, outline and discuss earn different answers from identical knowledge. Statistical treatment of data in the internal work is the other recurring weakness, and it is fixable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and evaluation carry the paper marks. The internally assessed commentaries need current articles with real policy content, which is where students stall first, and HL adds a quantitative paper that rewards consistent working rather than memorised definitions.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application separates grades: students who can place a tool against a decision score, and students who describe the tool do not. HL has a longer assessed written task, and the case-study paper needs timed practice because reading the material thoroughly is itself a timed skill.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the written assessments need a line of argument sustained across texts, which is a different skill from the essay writing most UAE schools teach in Year 11. HL adds the essay component, and planning time is the single most useful thing a tutor can impose.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: A language acquisition course, not a literature one, and students placed in it from an EAL background often sit at the wrong level. Productive skills carry the grade, so writing in the specified text types and speaking under timed conditions are where the sessions should go.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.description: Which Arabic course a student sits depends on the stream the school placed them in, and in a Dubai private school that placement follows the KHDA requirement for separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students. A tutor has to match the stream and the school's own material rather than importing a parallel course.

ib-private-tuition.regionsTitle: Where your child's school sits, and which authority answers for it
ib-private-tuition.regionsIntro: Private tuition questions change by emirate, because the authority that licensed the school is not the same everywhere and neither is what that authority controls. Lessons reach every emirate the same way, over live video on Gulf Standard Time, so the geography below matters for the paperwork and the school calendar rather than for scheduling.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA oversees private education in the emirate and publishes the mandatory-subject guidance that fixes Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in every private school timetable. It licensed 227 private schools in 2024-25 across 17 curricula, and seven more open for 2026-27.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and sets professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff, including the position on teachers tutoring their own students. It is the one regulator the competing pages in this market never mention.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, with a smaller IB cohort than Abu Dhabi island, which makes a local Higher Level specialist genuinely scarce. Online delivery is the practical answer here rather than a preference, and UAE University admissions requirements are worth reading before subject choices are locked.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education and, unlike KHDA, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A tuition plan built on another emirate's assumptions can therefore miss what the school is actually approved to teach this year.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here sit under the federal Ministry of Education, which u.ae describes as playing a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Parents read the Ministry's general regulations rather than an emirate inspection handbook.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education and, like Sharjah, approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. The emirate appears in none of the competitor pages reviewed for this project, which is a fair indication of how little IB-specific support is marketed here.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Federal Ministry of Education supervision, a small private-school sector and a long drive to the nearest IB specialist. Families here are the clearest case for one-to-one online tuition, since subject match is decided by syllabus rather than by what sits within an hour's drive.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under federal Ministry of Education supervision, with the smallest private-school sector of the seven emirates. Diploma students typically travel to Sharjah or Dubai for school, which pushes any evening tuition slot later than families expect.

schoolClusters.note: The largest IB cluster in the country, and the one where the gap between curricula is most visible. Students we support attend schools across the emirate; a tutor is matched to the syllabus and board the school actually teaches, which is worth confirming from the school rather than assuming from its name.

ADEK-regulated, with a smaller Diploma cohort than Dubai and a correspondingly thinner local specialist pool at Higher Level. Students we support attend schools in both cities, and the practical constraint is usually the school run finishing late rather than tutor availability.

A mixed curriculum picture across SPEA, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and federal Ministry of Education supervision. IB provision is concentrated in a few schools, so families here most often ask for subjects their school cannot staff deeply.

ib-private-tuition.schoolDisclaimer: School names appear here as context for the UAE school system; IB Gram has no affiliation with, and claims no endorsement from, any school named.
ib-private-tuition.modesIntro: Three shapes of private tuition cover almost every request that reaches us from the UAE. All three run one-to-one over live video, and the choice is really about what the deadline is and whether the problem is teaching, pace or process.

modes.title: A held weekly slot
modes.description: One subject, one tutor, the same time each week, booked against the school's own assessment calendar rather than against a generic syllabus order. This is the version that moves a grade, because it lets a tutor see the same misconception twice and fix the cause instead of the symptom. Most UAE families start with one subject and add a second only once the first is stable.
bullets: Session notes shared after each lesson, in one document per subject
Timed questions set between sessions, marked against published criteria
Slots on Gulf Standard Time, including post-Iftar timing during Ramadan
Paused for school exam weeks rather than paid for and missed

modes.title: A block before a session
modes.description: Three to six weeks of concentrated work when the first paper is close and the diagnosis is already clear. The structure is fixed: a past paper under timed conditions, a marking walkthrough against the published criteria, then targeted teaching on what the paper exposed. It is the most expensive way to buy tuition per point gained, which is a reason to start earlier rather than an argument against it.
bullets: Two or three sessions a week instead of one
Papers sourced from the school or the board's own channel, never a downloadable archive
A written list of the topics that are still costing marks
An agreed stopping point, so the block does not drift into the exam week

modes.title: Coursework process coaching
modes.description: For the Internal Assessment, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and the Personal Project. The student is the author throughout. The tutor asks questions, points at the criterion wording, explains what a criterion is rewarding and says plainly when a plan will not reach it. Nothing is supplied as text for the student to submit, and the school supervisor stays the authority on the process.
bullets: Criterion wording read together, with the mark allocation stated
Feedback given as questions and as references to the criteria
The student's own supervisor and school deadlines treated as the controlling calendar
A written record of what was discussed, available to the school on request

sections.heading: Who may legally give private tuition in the UAE
paragraphs: Private tuition in the UAE runs on a permit. The federal government introduced the private tuition work permit through Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and u.ae describes it as granted free of charge for two years. MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, lists no fee, gives a two-working-day completion time, and takes applications through the MoHRE smart app, the website and the e-services system. That is the whole official process: a form, no money, two working days. Any provider telling you the paperwork is expensive or slow is describing something else.

Eligibility is broader than most parents expect. u.ae lists teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students among those who may apply. The permit carries a code of conduct, and this is where the detail becomes useful to a parent. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and says the permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Confirm the current wording against ADEK's own policy before treating it as settled, but take the direction seriously.

What this leaves you with is a short set of questions, each of which has a specific answer. Which category was the permit issued under, since a university student and a registered schoolteacher are not the same proposition for Higher Level work. Does the employer approval the category requires exist. Does your child's own school employ this person. And treat any provider that uses an authority's name as a credential, without a permit or licence number you can read, as making a claim it has not evidenced. u.ae is explicit that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so anyone quoting you a figure is guessing.

sections.heading: Which authority licensed your child's school, and what else it controls
paragraphs: The u.ae private-schools page sets out the complete map, and it is worth reading once because the competing pages in this market do not. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in that emirate, the Department of Knowledge does the same in Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in the emirates of Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Five bodies, seven emirates.

The difference between them is not cosmetic. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, which means curriculum and fee approval sits with the emirate rather than with the school's head office. A Dubai family reading a KHDA inspection report and a Sharjah family reading an approved curriculum list are looking at different kinds of document, and advice written for one does not transfer cleanly to the other. For the three emirates under federal supervision, the reference point is the Ministry's general regulations rather than an emirate handbook.

Underneath all of it sits one federal rule that explains the mandatory subjects. Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That single sentence is why a school licensed for the IB still has Ministry subjects in the timetable, and why those subjects turn up in a tuition conversation that started about Chemistry. Before arranging anything, find out which authority licensed the school, what it publishes, and which of its requirements your child is currently meeting.

sections.heading: Dubai's private-school numbers, and what they do to tutor supply
paragraphs: Dubai's private school sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum on 37% of enrolment, Indian on 26%, American on 14% and the International Baccalaureate on 7%. Those four numbers explain more about the tutoring market than any price list does. The IB is the smallest of the four main curricula in the emirate, so the pool of adults who have taught a current Diploma syllabus is correspondingly small, while the pool marketing itself as able to teach it is not.

The sector is also growing in a direction that matters. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places, after six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. Three new IB schools means three new sets of Diploma cohorts recruiting from the same thin specialist pool. On the cost side, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for 2026-27, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

For a parent, the practical consequence is to stop treating subject tutoring as a local search. A family in Al Barsha looking for Mathematics AA Higher Level is not choosing between the specialists in Al Barsha; it is choosing between everyone who can teach that syllabus at a time the family can sit down. That is the whole argument for one-to-one online delivery, and it is why IB Gram matches on syllabus and level rather than on postcode. It also explains why the scarce skills are specific: HL Paper 3 technique and Internal Assessment process coaching, not general subject help.

sections.heading: Private tutor, tuition centre, platform: four arrangements, four obligations
paragraphs: Parents use private tuition to mean any paid help outside school, but the four common arrangements are different legal animals with different things you can ask to see. An individual tutor needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit. A tuition operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which starts with initial approval, allows a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and requires annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. Those are two separate regimes, and a provider that conflates them is worth a second question.

A matching platform is a third thing again. It introduces a tutor and takes responsibility for the match, the records and the replacement when a match fails, and the tutor's own permit position remains the tutor's. The honest version of that model tells you where the tutor is based before you book. The fourth arrangement is school-run support, which sits inside the school's own licence and is usually the cheapest option on the table, though it is group teaching by the staff whose teaching your child has already had.

IB Gram is the third kind, and says so. One-to-one lessons are delivered over live video to families across the UAE, we name the tutor and their location before the first session, and we do not operate premises in the country. Home visits are a service we run only in India. If a provider's answer to where the lessons happen is vague, that vagueness is the answer: in this market the gap between what is advertised and what is delivered usually sits exactly there, alongside a foreign phone number and a price in dollars.

sections.heading: What private tuition costs across the UAE market, by the month
paragraphs: Hourly rates make tuition look cheap, and monthly commitments are what families actually pay. Across the UAE providers reviewed for this page in October 2026, published hourly figures ran from about AED 45 at the budget online end to AED 650 for a premium named specialist, with qualified subject tutors online between roughly AED 150 and AED 300, visiting one-to-one tuition between roughly AED 180 and AED 500 including travel, and IB or IGCSE specialists between roughly AED 200 and AED 450 and above. Three of the six competitor pages reviewed published no figure at all.

Convert those to a month and the decision changes shape. A monthly online package advertised in this market at AED 799 for eight sessions works out near the middle of the qualified-tutor band. A visiting package advertised at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions is paying for travel inside the hourly rate. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget tier, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for a specialist in an exam year.

None of those are IB Gram prices, and we do not publish a rate card on a landing page because the honest number depends on subject, level and how many weeks are left. What we do publish is the structure: the first lesson is free, no card details are taken to book it, and you are told the tutor's location and subject history before it happens. Set the market numbers against the context KHDA provided on 22 May 2026, when it confirmed no school fee increase for 2026-27; tuition is the part of an education budget that is still moving.

sections.heading: What you hand over at enquiry, and what you should keep back
paragraphs: A tuition enquiry about a child is a request for personal data about a minor, and the UAE has a law about that: Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection. The practical reading for a parent is simple. A provider should be able to say what it collects, why it needs each item, how long it keeps it and how you have it deleted. If those four answers are not available before you send anything, send less.

Most of what gets requested at first contact is not needed to run a first lesson. A subject, a level, a year group and a time zone are enough to match a tutor. A school name helps, because it tells a tutor which board and which internal calendar apply, and it is reasonable to give. A recent report, a predicted grade or a marked piece of work is genuinely useful at the point a plan is being written, which is after the free lesson rather than before it. A photograph of the child, a passport copy or an Emirates ID scan is not needed by a tutoring provider at all, and a request for one at enquiry stage deserves a direct question.

IB Gram collects the subject, the level, the school where you choose to give it, a parent contact and a time zone to schedule against. Lessons are delivered over live video, so there is no visit to arrange and no address required. Where session notes or a marked piece of work are stored, they sit in one document per subject that you can see, and you can ask for them to be removed. Ask any provider the same four questions before the first payment; the ones that answer crisply tend also to be the ones with a permit number ready.

sections.heading: Past papers, mark schemes and what may properly change hands
paragraphs: The material a tutor uses tells you most of what you need to know about them. Past papers, mark schemes, examiner reports and subject guides are copyright works owned by the board that set them, which means they are to be referenced and linked rather than redistributed. A provider advertising a downloadable archive of papers and mark schemes is advertising a copyright problem, and for unreleased material it is advertising something considerably worse. Ask instead for the tutor's own worked examples, because that is the thing they are allowed to give you and the thing that shows whether they can teach.

The second boundary is academic honesty, and it is sharper than most marketing in this market admits. An Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay, a Theory of Knowledge essay and a Personal Project must be the student's own work. A tutor teaches the skill, reads what the student has produced, asks questions about it, points at the criterion wording and says where a plan will not reach a criterion. A tutor does not supply text for submission, does not edit a piece to completion and does not hand over another student's assessed work as a template. One page ranking in this market sells completed Internal Assessments outright; that is a malpractice trigger for the student, and the risk lands on the child rather than the seller.

Say the boundary out loud before the first session and the whole arrangement gets easier. Your child's school supervisor stays the authority on the process and on the deadlines. The tutor's notes should be available to the school on request, which is both a trust signal and a sensible protection for the student if a question is ever raised. IB Gram states this in writing at the start of any coursework work and keeps a record of what was discussed in each session, for exactly that reason.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies: what the school's licence requires
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's guidance states that its requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year starts in April. This is the part of the timetable IB families most often discover late, because nothing in the Diploma documentation mentions it and nothing in a tuition advertisement does either. It is also where a surprising number of UAE students carry a weakness for years without anyone treating it as a subject problem.

The guidance is specific enough to plan around. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson is at least 25 minutes. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and the school's licensed-curriculum language applies for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Two further details matter for tuition. The use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the Ministry, is strictly prohibited for these subjects, so a tutor's job is to support the school's own material rather than to import a parallel course. And schools are required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA approval to teach these subjects, which gives a parent a credential question with a precise answer. Before arranging Arabic support, find out which stream the school placed your child in, which course that stream leads to, and what the weekly time allocation currently is.

sections.heading: The equivalency file, and what it asks of each curriculum
paragraphs: At some point the certificate your child earns has to be recognised in the UAE, and that is the Ministry of Education's equivalency process. It is worth understanding early because it is a document-collection exercise, and documents are easier to collect while a child is still enrolled. IB Gram does not perform equivalency or attestation and cannot promise an outcome; what we can do is tell you where the requirements are published and when to start reading them.

For the British track, reporting on the Ministry's clarification states that students must submit proof of one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five required subjects. That last detail is where at least one page currently ranking for these searches goes wrong, publishing a six-subject requirement; the reported rule is five accredited subjects with those two excluded from the count.

For the American track, the same reporting sets English proficiency at a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics at a minimum of 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB Diploma, the source we read publishes no points threshold at all, so no figure appears on this page. If a provider quotes you an IB points number for equivalency, ask which moe.gov.ae page it came from, and check it against the emirate attestation authority before you act on it.

sections.heading: The exam year, and when private tuition has to be running
paragraphs: Entry deadlines sit months before the papers, and that is the single calendar fact that changes how a family buys tuition. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series; the Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests that run in March, May and October are a different assessment entirely and are not IGCSE. The series with the hardest published dates to work from is Pearson's: the Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Read either board backwards and the decisions about tier and subject are being made a full term before anyone sits down in a hall, because entries close long before the first paper and the exact deadline comes from the school as exam centre, on the statement of entry, rather than from a timetable a parent found online.

There is a second Cambridge detail almost nobody tells parents. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and Cambridge states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. That is why your child's paper can be on a different day from a cousin's at another school. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May or June and in November; the November 2026 final timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always check the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

For the IB, the May session is the one UAE schools sit, and no IB session or results date appears on this page because none has been confirmed from the IB itself for this project. Get those dates from your school's IB coordinator or from ibo.org and write them into the plan. Then work backwards: tuition should be running by the term in which entries close, not being arranged in the term the papers start.

sections.heading: Why we sell this one way in the UAE
paragraphs: Searches for private tuition in this market usually assume a person arriving at a UAE address, and it is a fair thing to want. It is also the expensive option, because travel is priced inside the rate and paid for in the evening either way, and it narrows the choice of tutor to those within a reasonable drive of your community. For a Standard Level subject taught in many schools, that pool is adequate. For Mathematics AA Higher Level, Physics HL or a Group 1 language at Higher Level, it often is not.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition to UAE families over live video, and nobody travels to a UAE address. Home visits are a service we run only in India. We say it plainly rather than leaving it to be discovered, because the alternative is the thing this market does worst: an advertisement implying a visit, and a tutor who turns out to be on a video call from another country, reached through a phone number that is not a UAE one.

The case for the online format does not rest on convenience. It rests on who ends up teaching your child. A Sharjah family gets a Chemistry HL specialist who has taught the current assessment model rather than whoever covers their community; a Fujairah family gets the same tutor as a family in Dubai Marina. Sessions move when a school assessment week lands badly, slots shift to post-Iftar timing during Ramadan, and the full hour is teaching rather than the last ten minutes of someone's drive. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, so the location is information rather than a constraint. Ask about permit category and current teaching; those answers should arrive in writing.

process.description: The first session is free, booked without card details, and run as a real lesson rather than a sales call. By the end you should know what the tutor thinks is actually wrong, which is the only useful output of a first session. If the match is not right, say so and we match someone else.
