process.description: After the first lesson you get a short plan: topics in order, how many sessions, what happens between them, and your child's own school assessment dates written into the sequence. Entry deadlines and internal coursework dates set the order, not a generic syllabus running from chapter one.

process.title: Notes every session, and a change of tutor when needed
process.description: Each session leaves notes in one document per subject, available to you and to the school on request. Sessions pause for school exam weeks instead of being paid for and missed. If progress stalls for three sessions, that is a match problem rather than a child problem, and changing the tutor costs nothing.

whyPoints.title: One specialist per subject
whyPoints.description: A tutor is matched to a syllabus and a level, not to a subject label. Biology HL and Biology SL are different courses with different papers and weightings, and a tutor who has taught the current assessment model is worth more than one who covers five subjects at every level.

whyPoints.title: The delivery model stated before you pay
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video, on Gulf Standard Time, and nobody travels to a UAE address. Home visits are an India-only service. That sentence appears on every country page we publish, which is a low bar that much of this market still does not clear.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary in writing
whyPoints.description: Before any work on an Internal Assessment, Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essay or Personal Project, we set out what a tutor does and does not do. The student is the author; the tutor teaches, questions and points at the criteria. Session records are available to the school on request.

whyPoints.title: Numbers with a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is attributed to the market and dated, and every regulatory statement is drawn from u.ae, KHDA's own guidance, MoHRE's service page or named reporting. Where a figure is not verified, including IB session dates, the page says so rather than filling the gap.

whyPoints.title: A timetable built on the UAE calendar
whyPoints.description: Sessions are scheduled around the school run, prayer times and Ramadan, with evening slots moved after Iftar rather than cancelled. Blocks tighten before a session and pause during school exam weeks. The calendar that controls the plan is your child's school calendar, not ours.

faqs.question: Is private tuition legal in the UAE, and what should a tutor be able to show me?
faqs.answer: It is legal and it is permitted. Private tutoring runs on a work permit introduced through Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, applied for through MoHRE, and u.ae describes it as granted free of charge for two years. The same page states that individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. A tutor should be able to tell you they hold the permit and name the eligibility category it was issued under. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific penalty figure you are quoted as unverified.

faqs.question: Who can apply for the UAE private tuition work permit?
faqs.answer: u.ae lists teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students among those eligible to apply. MoHRE's service page for Private Tutor Licensing lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, with applications made through the MoHRE smart app, website or e-services system. The breadth of that list is the reason to ask which category applies to your tutor: a registered schoolteacher and a university student are both permitted to tutor, and they are not the same proposition for Higher Level Diploma work.

faqs.question: Can my child's own schoolteacher be paid to tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: Treat that as the one arrangement not to buy. Press reporting on ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi describes a prohibition on teachers providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and notes that the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document, since the detail above is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy. The underlying concern is plain enough: the person who assesses your child should not also be paid to prepare them.

faqs.question: What is the difference between hiring a private tutor and enrolling at a tuition centre?
faqs.answer: They sit under different regimes. An individual tutor needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit. An operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which begins with initial approval, allows a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and requires annual renewal requested at least 30 days before expiry. So the questions differ: a tutor should name a permit category, a centre should give you a permit number and renewal date. A provider that cannot distinguish between the two regimes is unlikely to hold either.

faqs.question: Who regulates private schools in Ras Al Khaimah, Ajman and Fujairah?
faqs.answer: Ras Al Khaimah has its own body: the Department of Knowledge, which u.ae describes as regulating private education in the emirate and approving tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit under the federal Ministry of Education, which u.ae says plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in those three emirates. The practical consequence is that advice written for Dubai does not transfer cleanly. Parents in the northern emirates read the Ministry's general regulations, or the Department of Knowledge's approvals, rather than a KHDA inspection handbook.

faqs.question: What do monthly private tuition packages cost in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Monthly figures published across the UAE market in October 2026 included an online package at AED 799 for eight sessions and visiting packages at AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 for four two-hour sessions. Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table puts a weekly one-hour arrangement at AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget tier, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for an exam-year specialist. Those are market figures rather than IB Gram prices. Our first lesson is free and the quote that follows depends on subject, level and weeks remaining.

faqs.question: Should I send my child's school report and photograph to a tutoring company?
faqs.answer: Not at enquiry stage. A tuition enquiry about a child is personal data about a minor, and UAE Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021 on Personal Data Protection is the reason to expect four answers before you send anything: what is collected, why, how long it is kept and how it is deleted. A subject, a level, a year group and a time zone are enough to match a tutor. A report or a marked piece of work is useful when a plan is being written, which is after a first lesson. A photograph or an identity document is not needed to teach a video lesson at all.

faqs.question: Can a private tutor give us past papers and mark schemes to keep?
faqs.answer: Past papers, mark schemes, examiner reports and subject guides belong to the board that set them, so they are to be referenced and linked rather than redistributed as downloads. A tutor can work through a paper your school has provided, or one obtained from the board's own channel, and can show you how marks are awarded against published criteria. What should worry you is a provider advertising a downloadable archive, or claiming access to unreleased marking material. Ask instead for the tutor's own worked notes and examples, which they are free to share and which show whether they can actually teach the syllabus.

faqs.question: How much Arabic teaching time does a Dubai private school have to provide?
faqs.answer: KHDA's mandatory-subjects guidance calculates instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. The subjects themselves are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes are strictly prohibited. Ask the school which stream your child is in and what the current weekly allocation is before you arrange any Arabic support.

faqs.question: How many IGCSE subjects does the Ministry of Education count towards equivalency?
faqs.answer: Reporting on the Ministry's clarification states that students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five required subjects. The British track also asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. At least one page currently ranking for these searches publishes a six-subject requirement instead. Check the figure on moe.gov.ae or with the emirate attestation authority before acting on anything, including this page.

faqs.question: Is there a published IB points requirement for UAE equivalency?
faqs.answer: Not in the source read for this page. The reporting that sets out the British and American track requirements states no IB points threshold, so no figure appears here. That matters because an unsourced number travels fast: if a provider quotes you an IB points requirement for equivalency, ask which moe.gov.ae page it came from and verify it with the emirate attestation authority. IB Gram does not perform equivalency or attestation and cannot promise an outcome from it. Treat tutoring and the equivalency file as two separate pieces of work, and start the paperwork while your child is still enrolled.

faqs.question: When is the entry deadline for a Cambridge exam series, and why is it so early?
faqs.answer: Far earlier than families expect, and the honest answer is that the exact day comes from the school. Cambridge sits UAE candidates in a June series and a November series, and for each one final entries close months ahead of the first paper, because the board has to build zone timetables, allocate papers and register candidates before anything is printed. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after working from the wrong zone's timetable, so the date that matters to you is the one on your own centre's statement of entry. Pearson's published series show the same gap in a form you can check for yourself: its Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 timetable ran to 19 November 2026, with entries closed well before it. For a parent the consequence is a planning rule: subject and tier decisions should be settled, and tuition already running, by the term in which entries close.

faqs.question: Why does my child's exam timetable differ from a cousin's at another school?
faqs.answer: Because Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, and the timetable differs by zone. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Two UAE schools can therefore sit the same paper on different days. Pearson works differently again, publishing provisional timetables ahead of each series before a final one, with its November 2026 International GCSE timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. Always work from the school's own confirmed timetable.

faqs.question: Can IB private tuition start in the middle of the school year?
faqs.answer: Yes, and most of it does. The sequence changes rather than the subject: instead of running a syllabus from the beginning, the plan starts from your child's next assessment and works outward. What limits a late start is not the calendar but the kind of help needed. Teaching a topic properly takes weeks; fixing exam technique on content a student already knows takes less. Internal coursework is the real constraint, because a school's internal deadlines are fixed and cannot be shifted to suit a tuition plan. Send us the deadline and the subject, and the free first lesson will tell you what is realistic.

faqs.question: How does a live online private tuition lesson actually run?
faqs.answer: One student, one tutor, a scheduled video session with a shared writing surface, timed on Gulf Standard Time. The tutor works through problems with your child rather than presenting slides, so you will hear questions more than explanation. Notes land in one document per subject afterwards, with the work set for the gap before the next session. You are welcome to sit in. Nothing is pre-recorded and no group joins the call. Nobody travels to a UAE address, because home visits are a service we run only in India, and the whole booked hour is therefore teaching time.

faqs.question: We have had two tutors who did not work out. What should we ask differently?
faqs.answer: Ask three questions that are answerable with facts rather than impressions. First: which papers of the current syllabus have you taught, and in which year. Second: what will you do in the first twenty minutes of the first session, since a tutor with a diagnostic plan answers immediately. Third: what does your written record after each session look like. A tutor who cannot answer the first question has subject-level knowledge rather than syllabus-level knowledge, which is the usual reason a match fails. If progress stalls for three sessions, change the tutor rather than the child's effort.

ib-private-tuition.closingHeading: Three questions first, then the free lesson
ib-private-tuition.closingBody: Before you pay anyone for IB private tuition in the UAE, ask which permit category the tutor holds, where the lessons are actually delivered from, and what the provider will and will not do with an Internal Assessment. The answers take a minute and they remove most of this market's problems. When you are ready, send the subject, the level and the deadline that matters. We name a tutor, tell you where they are based, and run the first lesson free with no card details taken. It will be one-to-one and live online, on Gulf Standard Time, which is the only way we teach UAE families.

ib-private-tutor.tutorsIntro: These are the specialists UAE families book for Diploma subjects at Higher and Standard Level. Each works from your child's own marked scripts and the deadlines their school has set, and the match is made on subject and level rather than on where anybody happens to live.

intro.heading: Work backwards from the first paper, not forwards from today
paragraphs: Almost every family that asks us about an IB private tutor starts the conversation in the month after a report card arrives. The calendar does not care. An IB Diploma is assessed against fixed windows - a coursework hand-in your child's school sets, a registration deadline the board sets, an exam window the board sets, a results date the board sets - so the useful first question is not whether to hire a tutor but which of those windows comes next. Answer that and the number of sessions, the order of the subjects and the length of the commitment all follow from it instead of being guessed.

Counting backwards changes what you are actually buying. Thirty weeks out, the sensible purchase is one subject taught properly, because there is still time to repair understanding rather than drill technique. Twelve weeks out, the same money buys past-paper discipline and a mark-scheme habit. Four weeks out it buys triage: the two topics that appear in every paper and are currently costing the most marks. Same tutor, same hourly rate, three completely different jobs. Families who book without naming the window usually pay for the thirty-week product four weeks before the exam, then wonder why it did not land.

The UAE adds its own layer to that clock. Schools across the seven emirates run a September-to-June year with a winter break in December and a spring break early in the second half, and mock season lands in January for most Diploma cohorts. Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year, which means that for several cycles running it sits inside the revision run-in rather than safely after it. School-run traffic in Dubai and Abu Dhabi decides whether a weekday session can realistically start at four o'clock or seven. None of that is decoration; it is the timetable a plan has to survive.

There is a regulatory calendar too, and no tutoring advert mentions it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA required its current arrangements to be in place by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. A Ministry of Education equivalency file is what turns an international certificate into a document a UAE university will read, and it is far quicker to open before results day than after. Both carry dates. Both get discovered late, usually by a family already deep in exam term.

So this page is built as a clock rather than a pitch. It sets out the entry deadlines that sit months ahead of the papers, what DP1 is genuinely for, a thirty-week map back from paper one, how to read a January mock, where the internal coursework deadlines fall and what a tutor may legitimately do beside them, what results day still offers if a grade looks wrong, and what the ministry asks for. Delivery is simple and stated up front: one tutor, one student, over live video. Home visiting is a service IB Gram runs in India only.
bullets: Entry deadlines sit months ahead of the papers: UAE candidates sit Cambridge's June and November series, and the centre's cut-off for each one passes long before the first paper.
Mock week in January is a diagnosis, not a verdict - the useful output is a topic list.
The Internal Assessment deadline your child must meet is the school's, not the board's.
Results day opens a short window for an enquiry upon results, and it closes fast.
A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own work. Nothing more.
Every AED figure on this page is a market rate published by somebody else, with the source named.

ib-private-tutor.programmesIntro: The IB runs four programmes and UAE schools licence them in different combinations, so a family can meet two or three of them as one child moves up. What matters for planning is which assessments are external and dated, and which are internal and set by the school. The two behave completely differently on a calendar.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations and no board deadlines, which is exactly why it is easy to misread. Progress is judged through units of inquiry, portfolios and the Year 6 exhibition. The useful calendar here is internal: when reports land, when the exhibition is presented, and when a school signals that a child's reading or number fluency is behind the cohort. Support at this stage is about fluency and habits, not examination technique, and short weekly sessions over a long run do more than an intensive block.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE the PYP year also carries the ministry subjects. Arabic begins early and continues throughout, and KHDA calculates mandatory-subject time in 40-minute lesson units, so these lessons occupy genuine weekly hours from Year 1. Families moving in from another country often find their child joining an Arabic stream mid-sequence, and that gap compounds quietly until the MYP, where it starts to show in reports.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP is marked against four criteria per subject, each out of eight, and the grade a parent sees is a conversion of those criterion scores rather than a percentage. Year 11 may sit MYP eAssessment, which is externally marked and dated, and the personal project runs across the final year with internal checkpoints. The calendar risk here is the personal project: it is assessed on process as much as product, so a late start cannot be rescued by a strong final write-up.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools use the MYP in two ways: as a full five-year continuum feeding their own Diploma, or as a middle-school phase before an IGCSE route. Which one your school runs changes the dates your child is working to. Ask whether Year 11 will sit MYP eAssessment or Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE papers, because the second option brings a published board timetable and an entry deadline months in advance.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is where the calendar becomes unforgiving. Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and CAS, all assessed across two years with the external papers concentrated into one window. Internal Assessments in every subject are marked by the teacher, moderated by the IB, and due on school-set dates that cluster in DP1 summer and DP2 autumn. Points total 45, and the Diploma requires the core as well as the subjects.
programmes.countryNote: UAE IB World Schools sit the May session, the northern-hemisphere series. We do not print IB session or results dates anywhere on this page: ibo.org is the only source we would stand behind for them and it cannot be checked automatically, so a date published here would quietly go stale. Ask your school's DP coordinator for the session timetable and, more importantly, for the internal cut-offs that sit ahead of it.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines at least two DP courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a service-learning requirement and a language-development strand. The DP courses inside it are assessed exactly as they are in the full Diploma, so those papers follow the same external window. The reflective project is internally supervised and dated by the school. For a student strong in two subjects and stretched by six, the CP can be a better structural fit than a repeated DP1.
programmes.countryNote: Only a small number of UAE schools licence the CP, so the usual reason a family asks about it is a mid-DP1 decision about whether to continue with the full Diploma. That decision has a date attached, set by the school, and it is almost always earlier in the year than parents expect. If it is on the table, get the deadline in writing before buying any tutoring at all.

ib-private-tutor.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects UAE families book most often, described by where their marks sit and when their coursework falls due. Each has its own internal deadline inside the school year, and that date, rather than the exam window, is usually what dictates when support needs to start.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Algebraic fluency decides this course. The exploration is proposed in DP1 and submitted in DP2, and the commonest failure is a topic that cannot actually be explored mathematically, chosen eight months before anyone notices. Marks in the papers are lost to unjustified steps rather than wrong answers.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology-assisted work, with a paper that assumes confident calculator use. The route choice between AA and AI matters for admissions: engineering and many science degrees name AA, so the decision belongs in DP1, not in the term before applications are submitted.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The data-and-practical paper separates students more reliably than the theory papers do. Uncertainty, significant figures and graph linearisation account for a steady drip of lost marks, and they are learnable in weeks. The scientific investigation needs data in hand well before the school's draft deadline.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics carry the HL difficulty, and the extra HL content arrives late in DP2 when revision has already started. Candidates who leave the investigation until mock season end up with a rushed analysis section, which is where the criterion marks sit.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content volume is the problem, not conceptual difficulty, so retrieval practice spread across months beats intensive blocks. Command terms matter unusually much here: outline, explain, evaluate and distinguish each expect a different answer shape, and marks go missing when a student writes everything they know.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Three commentaries on published news articles form the internal portfolio, each with its own school-set date spread across both years. Diagrams must be drawn, labelled and then used in the argument. HL adds quantitative work and the policy paper, where answers are often descriptive when they need to be evaluative.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The research project is HL coursework and depends on real organisational data, which takes weeks to obtain and cannot be invented. Case-study papers reward structured application of tools to the stimulus rather than textbook recall, and the pre-release material sets the preparation clock for the final months.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral is internally assessed and recorded on a school date, usually before the written papers, so it frequently collides with science coursework. Paper 1 is unseen analysis and improves with weekly practice on texts nobody has pre-taught. HL adds the essay, which is dated internally.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The internal assessment is a developed solution with documentation, and it fails on scope far more often than on code. Proposing it in DP1 and fixing the client and success criteria early is what keeps DP2 from becoming a build sprint during revision season.

subjects.name: Arabic B
subjects.description: Taken by many UAE students alongside the mandatory Arabic their school must provide, which means two Arabic strands on one timetable with separate expectations. The oral is internally assessed and dated by the school, and the writing paper rewards register control rather than vocabulary volume.

ib-private-tutor.regionsIntro: Delivery is identical everywhere in the UAE, because lessons are online. What differs by emirate is the regulator whose inspection report describes your child's school, and the hour at which a weekday session can realistically begin once the school run is finished.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA regulates the emirate's private schools, which numbered 227 in 2024-25 across 17 curricula. Marina, Downtown and Al Barsha school runs push weekday sessions past six o'clock for many families; mornings in a school break are the easier slot.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and is named by none of the competitor pages we examined. Island-to-mainland commutes mean a 4pm start is rarely realistic during term; 6.30pm onwards works better.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, with a smaller IB cohort than the capital, so a Higher Level specialist in a minority subject is unlikely to live locally. Online delivery removes that constraint entirely, which is the practical reason it matters here more than in Dubai.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and, like Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves curricula, fees and assessment methods rather than only inspecting. Cross-border commutes to Dubai schools stretch the evening further than families expect.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here fall under the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority. The IB cohort is small, so subject choice at Higher Level is often the deciding factor in whether local tutoring exists at all for a given paper.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and approves programmes and assessment methods. Distance from the Dubai and Abu Dhabi tutor pools is the usual complaint; it stops being relevant once sessions are delivered over video.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education territory on the east coast, and a zero-mention emirate across the competitor pages we read. Families here are the clearest case for online delivery: the specialist for an HL subject simply is not within driving distance.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised federally by the Ministry of Education. The smallest private-school market in the country, which makes the published board timetables and an online specialist more useful than any local search, especially in a Diploma subject with one teacher.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai's private sector taught 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, and the International Baccalaureate accounted for seven per cent of that enrolment. Seven new private schools open for 2026-27, three of them IB, adding 16,846 places. Students we support sit the Diploma at schools including these.

ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation across the capital and Al Ain, and its inspection reports are the document to read before booking anything. The Diploma cohort is smaller than Dubai's, so minority Higher Level subjects often have a single teacher per school.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.note: SPEA regulates Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge regulates Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education supervises Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. The IB footprint thins quickly north of Dubai, which is why session timing and tutor availability behave differently here.

ib-private-tutor.schoolDisclaimer: Named schools are ecosystem context for families comparing options; no affiliation, partnership or endorsement is implied, and every name should be checked against the relevant regulator's own school listing.
ib-private-tutor.modesIntro: Three booking patterns cover almost every family, and which one fits depends entirely on how many weeks sit between today and the next deadline. All three are delivered the same way: one tutor, one student, over live video, with the recording of what was covered sent afterwards.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one through DP1
modes.description: One sixty-minute session a week per subject, running across terms rather than weeks. This is the pattern that repairs understanding, because there is time to go back to the topic underneath the problem instead of patching the symptom. It is also the cheapest way to reach the exam window, since fewer total hours are needed when nothing is urgent.
bullets: Best started thirty or more weeks before the first paper
One subject at a time; a second is added only when the first is stable
Homework between sessions is short and set against the school's own scheme of work
Pauses over the winter break without losing the specialist

modes.title: Twice weekly through the run-in
modes.description: From roughly twelve weeks out the work changes shape: whole past papers under time, marked scripts, and mark-scheme discipline. Two sessions a week on the weakest two subjects is the usual pattern, with every session built on a script the student has already attempted. Nothing new is introduced in the final ten days.
bullets: Each session opens with a marked question, not a lecture
Timing is fixed before accuracy, because it is quicker to shift
A written list of recurring errors is kept and checked down
Sessions move inside the week when school revision clashes

modes.title: A coursework clinic around an internal deadline
modes.description: Three to six sessions compressed into a fortnight ahead of a school-set Internal Assessment, Extended Essay or oral date. The tutor questions the method, the research question and the analysis, and gives feedback on what the student has already produced. The words, the data and the decisions stay the student's throughout, which is the only version of this that is safe.
bullets: Booked against the school's date, not the IB's upload window
Feedback is given on a draft the student brings; no text is supplied
Most useful before a first draft exists, not after it is finished
Ends when the deadline passes, then weekly sessions resume

sections.heading: What a UAE parent is really buying when the exam date is already fixed
paragraphs: An IB private tutor in the UAE is a subject specialist who works one-to-one with your child against the school's and the board's deadlines, usually for sixty minutes a week per subject, and for IB Gram that work is delivered over live video rather than by anyone arriving at a UAE address. Market rates for that service, as published by other providers, run from AED 45 an hour at the budget online end to AED 650 at the premium examiner-led end. What distinguishes a good appointment from a wasted one is almost never the hourly rate. It is whether the plan is built around the next date.

Think of the purchase as a quantity of weeks rather than a quantity of hours. Weeks are what make a repair possible: reteaching a topic from first principles, rebuilding algebraic fluency, or fixing the habit of answering an evaluate question with a description. Hours bought late can only redistribute marks that are already nearly there. Both are legitimate purchases, and they cost roughly the same per hour, but they do very different things, and the difference is set by the calendar rather than by the tutor.

That is why the first conversation we have with a UAE family is about dates rather than subjects. Which session is your child entered for. When is the next coursework hand-in, as the subject teacher has written it. When is mock week. Has the Extended Essay supervisor been allocated. What does the school's internal cut-off look like, as opposed to the board's. Five answers, and the shape of the support follows from them. Without those answers, any recommendation is a guess dressed up as a plan, and the family pays for the guess.

sections.heading: The entry deadline sits months before the first paper
paragraphs: The single most expensive date in the year is not an exam. It is the registration cut-off, and it falls so far ahead of the papers that families routinely assume it has not happened yet. The UAE calendar is easiest to check against a series that has already run end to end: Pearson Edexcel's International GCSE November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, entries for it closed with the centre on a date the exams officer sets and circulates internally weeks before that first paper, and results from the equivalent November 2025 series reached students on 22 January 2026. One sitting therefore occupies most of a school year end to end — the entry decision, the papers, then a wait of roughly two months for the grade — and the entry decision has to be made while the subject still feels unfinished.

Boards also publish more than one series. Cambridge runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October; those Checkpoint tests are not IGCSE and do not give a UAE IGCSE candidate an extra sitting. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE papers are available in May/June and November each year: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and confirms them later, so the live PDF on its own site is the only version worth working from.

One Cambridge detail catches UAE centres specifically. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong one was used. Ask your exams officer, in writing, for the zone, the series, the syllabus code for each subject and the internal entry cut-off. For the IB Diploma, registration is made by the school: ask the DP coordinator for the same list.

sections.heading: DP1 is not a warm-up year
paragraphs: The Diploma is marked out of 45 across two years, but the decisions that cap the total are nearly all made in the first one. Higher Level choices settle in the opening term. Internal Assessment topics are proposed before the summer. An Extended Essay supervisor is allocated and a research question agreed. The predicted grades universities eventually read are built on DP1 internal examinations. Almost none of that is externally dated, which is exactly why it drifts, and why a family's first tutoring spend usually arrives a year after the moment it would have done the most good.

The most useful thing a tutor does in DP1 is ask awkward questions early. Is this Higher Level choice consistent with how the student performed in the equivalent MYP or IGCSE subject. Can this exploration actually be explored, with data the student can obtain in the UAE, or is it a title with no method behind it. Does this research question have a counter-argument. Each of those questions costs one session in DP1 and saves a term in DP2, and none of them involves teaching any content at all.

The DP1 summer is the other underused block. Four weeks of nothing is a reset for some students and a slow erosion for others, and the difference shows in September. A short intensive block on the single subject that would otherwise define DP2 is the highest-yield purchase of the two years, because it is the only point where a student has time and no competing deadline. After that, every hour of tutoring is competing with coursework, mocks or revision.

sections.heading: Thirty weeks back from paper one
paragraphs: A revision plan that starts at the beginning tends to die in the middle. The version that survives is written from the finish line: put the first paper on a page, count backwards in blocks, and give each block one job. Thirty weeks out the job is content. Twelve weeks out it is conversion of understanding into marks. Four weeks out it is triage. Each block has a different session shape and, more importantly, a different test of whether the money is working, which is the part families almost never define in advance.

The checks in the final column matter more than the activities. A student can attend thirty sessions and still arrive at the exam unable to produce a topic without their notes. The signal that the thirty-to-twenty-four-week block has worked is that they can teach a topic back, out loud, with nothing in front of them. The signal that the twelve-to-eight-week block has worked is narrower and stranger: the same mistake stops recurring across three consecutive papers. Progress at that stage is the disappearance of a pattern, not a rising percentage.

The last two weeks are where good plans are usually sabotaged with good intentions. New content introduced inside that window displaces something already secure, so a sensible tutor refuses to teach anything new in the final ten days and spends the time on the six things to check in the hall and on protecting sleep. If a family arrives four weeks out, nothing above is wasted - the plan simply starts at the four-week row and the honest expectation is redistribution of marks rather than transformation.

sections.heading: How to read a January mock without panicking
paragraphs: Mock results arrive in January for most UAE Diploma cohorts and they are routinely misread in both directions. A mock is not a prediction and it is not a verdict; it is the only piece of diagnostic data a family gets while there is still time to act on it. Read properly, a mock script tells you which of four different problems you are facing, and those four problems have completely different costs in weeks. Read as a grade, it tells you nothing except how everyone felt that week.

The diagnosis comes from the shape of the script rather than the total. Strong early questions with marks falling away is a pace problem and the cheapest of the four to fix. Correct method with the wrong final answer is arithmetic and unit discipline, fixable in two or three weeks of self-marking against a mark scheme. Blank extended-response questions almost always mean command terms were never taught explicitly: evaluate, justify, compare, to what extent. Marks lost on one topic across every paper is a genuine content gap, and it is the only one on the list that needs reteaching.

Insist on the script itself, not the grade. A reported percentage conceals all four patterns, and schools in Dubai and Abu Dhabi will generally release annotated papers on request. Then do the arithmetic that actually matters: how many weeks remain, what the diagnosed problem costs in weeks, and whether the remaining time covers it. If it does not, the plan becomes a choice about which subjects get the weeks, and that is a far better conversation to have in January than in April.

sections.heading: The coursework deadline that matters is your school's
paragraphs: Parents look for an IB deadline for the Internal Assessment and cannot find one, because the date their child must meet is not the IB's. Each subject teacher sets a draft and final date, the school builds in weeks of margin before its own upload window, and those internal dates are the ones with consequences. They also cluster: a science investigation, a mathematics exploration, an English oral and an Extended Essay checkpoint can land within a fortnight of each other, which is why DP2 autumn is the busiest tutoring period of the year in the UAE.

Beside those dates sits a line a tutor must not cross, and it is worth being explicit because one page ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments outright. Under IB academic-honesty rules the work has to be the student's own, from the research question to the final sentence. A tutor may explain the assessment criteria and what each is testing, question a method, point at a weak analysis section, and give feedback on a draft the student has produced. A tutor may not supply sentences, rewrite a paragraph into its final form, or hand over data. We say no to that, every time it is asked.

This is a genuine advantage rather than a compliance note. Feedback on a student's own draft is what actually moves a criterion mark, because the examiner is marking the student's reasoning, not their prose. Work that has been polished by somebody else reads as inconsistent with the rest of the file and puts the candidate at risk of a malpractice finding, which costs the Diploma rather than a grade. Ask any tutor you are considering what they will do with a draft. The answer tells you everything about what you are buying.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the ministry subjects sharing the same timetable
paragraphs: A revision plan written without the UAE calendar in it will break twice. Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each year, which places it inside the revision run-in for several cycles running rather than comfortably after the papers. School days shorten, energy peaks at different hours, and most families find late-morning or post-Iftar sessions work better than the usual after-school slot. Because lessons are delivered over live video, a slot can be rebooked inside the same week without anybody driving across an emirate to make it happen.

Eid breaks are the second trap. A full weekly schedule across Eid gets cancelled session by session; one short block on a single subject, agreed in advance, actually happens. The same logic applies to the winter break and to the long UAE summer, where four undirected weeks in DP1 is the quiet erosion described earlier. Decide which breaks are working weeks and which are genuinely off before term starts, and hold the tutor rather than the time slot across the pause.

Then there is the part no tutoring page mentions. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Schools must run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, and combined classes are prohibited. Instructional time is calculated in 40-minute lesson units. These subjects therefore occupy real weekly hours beside six Diploma courses, and their assessments fall in the same terms as IA drafts.

sections.heading: Results day, and the short window that follows it
paragraphs: Results day feels like the end of the calendar and is actually the start of a very short one. If a grade looks inconsistent with everything that preceded it, two routes exist and both run on deadlines measured in days. An enquiry upon results on an externally assessed IB component is requested by the school rather than by the family, inside the window the IB sets once results are released. For Cambridge or Pearson International GCSE, a review of marking is submitted by the exam centre against that board's published deadline for the series.

Be clear about what these routes can and cannot do. They look for a clerical or marking error on a specific component. They do not revisit a mark an examiner applied correctly, and internally assessed work that has already gone through moderation is rarely in scope. A review can move a grade down as well as up in some boards' processes, which is a conversation to have with the exams officer before anything is submitted. The decision needs the script, the component weightings and a clear head, all within about a week.

The retake question runs in parallel. Cambridge and Pearson both run a November series, and the IB runs a November session, so a second attempt is a route rather than a consolation prize. Registration happens months ahead of the papers and is arranged by the school or by a centre that accepts private candidates, which means the decision is effectively made in the weeks after results. What usually carries forward is the coursework mark, turning a retake into a papers-only project. That is the easiest kind of preparation to plan, because past papers and mark schemes are the entire syllabus of it.

sections.heading: What the calendar does to the price
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages we examined publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. So here are the AED figures, taken from what other providers have themselves published and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. These are market rates rather than ours. IB Gram's own number comes after the free trial lesson and the conversation about which window your child is in, because the same subject costs a different amount of effort in September and in April.

The pattern in the table is not that rates rise near the exams. The published hourly bands are reasonably stable across the year. What rises is the number of hours a family buys, because late work is denser: two sessions a week instead of one, two subjects instead of one, a coursework clinic on top. A family that starts in DP1 at one hour a week usually spends less in total than a family that starts at Easter, even though both pay a similar rate per hour. The calendar sets the quantity, and the quantity is what the invoice reflects.

Two honesty notes. Monthly packages circulating in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits at home, and a package only saves money if the sessions are actually taken in the month. Whether any quoted figure includes VAT is a question to ask of whoever quotes it; we do not state the tax treatment of tuition fees on this page because we have no Federal Tax Authority citation for it. Ask, and get the answer in writing.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor against live online, with the clock running
paragraphs: Home tutoring is a real market in the UAE and parents are right to ask about it. A visiting tutor arrives, works at the dining table, and leaves. The market charges AED 180 to 500 an hour for it with travel priced into the rate, and monthly in-home packages of AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour visits are commonly advertised. The honest problems with it are two, and both get worse as a deadline approaches: the tutor pool shrinks to whoever teaches your subject within a reasonable drive, and a meaningful share of each paid hour is travel.

IB Gram delivers this as one-to-one online tuition instead, everywhere in the UAE. Home visiting is a service we run in India only, and we would rather say that on the page than discover it at the booking stage. The case for the online version is not that it is cheaper, though it usually is. It is that a family in Fujairah or Al Ain gets the Chemistry Higher Level specialist rather than the available generalist, that a cancelled slot can move the same evening instead of becoming a wasted journey, and that a marked script can be annotated on screen and then saved for revision.

In the final eight weeks those differences stop being conveniences. The work at that point runs on marked scripts, and a script shared on screen, annotated live and kept afterwards is a better artefact than a paper passed across a table and taken away. Rescheduling matters more too, because school revision timetables change weekly in April. The table below compares the two formats on the things that actually differ, rather than on the usual claim that one is simply better than the other.

sections.heading: The equivalency file to open before results day
paragraphs: A UAE certificate equivalency from the Ministry of Education is what turns an international qualification into a document a UAE university will accept, and the time to understand it is while your child is still in DP2. The requirements are published and specific. On the British track a student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

Two details inside that rule are routinely got wrong. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects, which changes how a subject basket should be built. And one page currently ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five. On the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying.

For the IB Diploma specifically we publish no points threshold, because we have not read one on the ministry's own site and an unsourced number on a page like this is worse than a gap. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring service performs, guarantees or accelerates: it is a process run by the ministry and the emirate attestation authority, and tutoring is not a requirement of it. Describe it, verify it on moe.gov.ae, and start the paperwork early, because document attestation is the step that takes weeks nobody has planned for.

process.title: Tell us the session and the subjects
process.description: The first message we need is short: which session your child is entered for, which subjects are in trouble, whether they are Higher or Standard Level, and the next date their school has set. That is enough to say honestly whether the problem is content, timing, technique or retrieval, and therefore how many weeks it needs.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the subject specialist
process.description: One sixty-minute session, at no cost and with nothing to pay afterwards, with the specialist who would teach the subject rather than a salesperson. It is a diagnostic as much as an introduction: by the end there should be a named problem, a rough number of weeks, and a clear answer on whether this tutor is the right match.

process.title: A plan counted backwards from the first paper
process.description: We write the plan from the exam window back to today, in blocks, with one job per block and one check that tells you it is working. School coursework dates go in first, because they are immovable and they cluster. You get the plan in writing, which means you can hold us to it later.

process.title: Weekly sessions with a checkpoint at each milestone
process.description: Sessions run one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with a short written note after each one saying what was covered and what to practise. At every milestone on the plan, a mock, a coursework hand-in, the start of the run-in, we check the plan against reality and change the shape rather than carrying on regardless.

process.title: A handover before the exam window
process.description: In the last fortnight the work narrows deliberately: no new content, a written list of the things to check in the hall, and sessions on request rather than on a fixed slot. If a retake or a November entry becomes the route after results, the same specialist picks it up already knowing which topics were weak.

whyPoints.title: The calendar drives the plan, not the other way round
whyPoints.description: Every plan we write starts at the date of the first paper and counts backwards in blocks. That is why the recommendation for a family thirty weeks out looks nothing like the recommendation for a family four weeks out, and why we will tell you when the honest answer is fewer hours rather than more.

whyPoints.title: Matched on subject and level, not on drive time
whyPoints.description: A Higher Level specialist in a minority subject does not necessarily live in your emirate, and in Fujairah, Umm Al Quwain or Al Ain they almost certainly do not. Because lessons are delivered over live video, the match is made on who teaches the subject best rather than on who can reach you by seven.

whyPoints.title: Timed to Gulf Standard Time
whyPoints.description: Sessions are scheduled in your time zone, around the school run and, during Ramadan, around late-morning or post-Iftar slots. A session can be rebooked inside the same week when a school revision timetable changes, which in April it does, without anyone losing a journey over it.

whyPoints.title: Coursework support that stays on the right side of the line
whyPoints.description: A tutor explains the assessment criteria, questions a method, challenges a research question and gives feedback on a draft the student has produced. No sentences are supplied and no data is handed over. One page ranking for these searches sells finished Internal Assessments; that is a malpractice risk carried entirely by the student.

whyPoints.title: No invented price list, and no invented statistics
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page is a rate somebody else published, attributed to them. Our own number follows the free trial, because it depends on subjects, level and how many weeks are left. You will not find a satisfaction percentage or a star rating here either, because we cannot show you the data behind one.

whyPoints.title: Sources named, including where they run out
whyPoints.description: Cambridge and Pearson dates come from the boards' own published timetables and are cited as such. IB session and results dates are not printed here at all, because ibo.org is the only source worth trusting for them and we could not verify it. Where the ministry has not published a figure, we say so instead of guessing.

faqs.question: When do IB exams take place for schools in the UAE?
faqs.answer: UAE IB World Schools sit the May session, the northern-hemisphere series, and the papers run across several weeks of the spring term. Your child's school publishes the subject-by-subject timetable once the IB releases it. We deliberately print no IB session or results dates on this page: ibo.org is the only source we would stand behind for them, it cannot be checked automatically, and a date published here would quietly go out of date. Ask your DP coordinator for the session timetable and, more usefully, for the internal cut-offs that sit ahead of it. Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE dates are published openly and appear in the table above.

faqs.question: How far ahead of the first paper should we start with an IB private tutor?
faqs.answer: Thirty weeks is the point at which an IB private tutor can still change understanding rather than only technique. At that distance one hour a week per subject is usually enough and there is room to reteach a DP1 topic properly. Twelve weeks out the work shifts to past papers, mark schemes and timing, which needs two sessions a week on the weakest subjects. Four weeks out it becomes triage. Families who start earlier tend to buy fewer hours in total, because the expensive part of the year is the part where every deadline is urgent at the same time.

faqs.question: Who enters my child for the exams, and when does that deadline fall?
faqs.answer: The school does, through its exam centre, and the deadline is far earlier than most parents expect. A Cambridge candidate in the UAE sits either the June series or the November one, and the centre's final entry date for each falls months ahead of the papers — roughly four months before the June window — with the exact day printed on the statement of entry rather than on any public page. Pearson Edexcel centres work to their own cut-offs ahead of each May/June and November series; its November 2026 papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and grades from the previous November series reached students on 22 January 2026. For the IB Diploma, registration is handled by the school against the IB's own window. Ask the exams officer in writing for the internal date, the series and the syllabus code for each subject, because a missed entry is not something a tutor or anyone else can repair afterwards.

faqs.question: The January mocks went badly. What should we change first?
faqs.answer: Separate timing from knowledge, because they look identical on a report. If the first questions were strong and the marks fell away, the problem is pace and the fix is whole papers against a clock. If the method was right and the answer wrong, it is arithmetic and unit discipline. Extended-response questions left blank almost always mean the command terms were never taught explicitly: evaluate, justify, compare, to what extent. Marks lost on the same topic across every paper is a real content gap, and it is the only one of the four that needs reteaching from first principles. Ask for the annotated script, not the grade.

faqs.question: Is there a point in the year when it is too late to start an Internal Assessment?
faqs.answer: There is no IB-set date you can look up, because the deadline your child must meet is the one their subject teacher sets, and schools build weeks of margin in before their own upload window. Practically, an investigation or exploration proposed after mock season is already compressed: collecting data, analysing it and redrafting do not fit into a fortnight alongside revision. If you are in that position, the honest move is to protect the marks still winnable in the papers and keep coursework support to feedback on what the student has already produced, rather than starting something new.

faqs.question: How does the schedule change during Ramadan and the Eid break?
faqs.answer: Sessions move, and they move with notice rather than by improvisation. Ramadan shifts about eleven days earlier each year, so for several cycles running it falls inside the revision run-in rather than after it. School days shorten, concentration peaks at different hours, and most families prefer late-morning or post-Iftar slots. Because lessons are delivered over live video, a slot can be rebooked inside the same week without anybody driving anywhere. Eid breaks are usually better spent on one short block on a single subject than on a full weekly schedule that nobody attends once the holiday starts.

faqs.question: What can we do if a grade looks wrong on results day?
faqs.answer: Two routes exist and both are short. An enquiry upon results on an externally assessed IB component is requested by the school, not by the family, inside a window the IB sets once results are released. For Cambridge or Pearson International GCSE, a review of marking is submitted by the exam centre against the board's published deadline for that series. Neither route revisits a mark an examiner applied correctly, and internally assessed work already moderated is rarely in scope. Speak to the exams officer on the day, because the clock starts immediately and the decision needs the script in front of you.

faqs.question: Is the November session a realistic second attempt?
faqs.answer: For many students, yes, provided the decision is made in weeks rather than months. Cambridge and Pearson both run a November series and the IB runs a November session, so a retake is a route rather than a consolation. Registration happens long before the papers and is arranged by the school or by a centre that accepts private candidates. The practical question is what carries forward: coursework marks usually do, which turns the retake into a papers-only project. That is the easiest kind of preparation to plan, because past papers and mark schemes are effectively the whole syllabus of it.

faqs.question: How many weeks of support does one subject usually need before the exams?
faqs.answer: Judge it by what has to change rather than by a package size. Repairing one genuine content gap takes roughly two weeks of focused work per topic. Fixing paper timing takes three to four weeks of whole papers under conditions. Command-term technique takes four to six weeks, because it has to be practised across several question types. Retrieval under pressure is the slowest to shift and needs six weeks or more of low-stakes timed questions. A tutor should be able to tell you after the free trial which of those four your child is facing, and roughly how long it will take.

faqs.question: Which weeks of the UAE school year are the worst time to start?
faqs.answer: The fortnight before a coursework hand-in, and mock week itself. In both, the student has no capacity left to absorb new teaching, so sessions become supervision rather than instruction and the money buys very little. The weeks straight after the winter break and straight after mock results are the opposite: there is a marked script to work from and enough runway to act on what it says. If you are deciding in a bad week, book the free trial anyway and begin the weekly pattern once the immediate deadline has passed.

faqs.question: How is a live online lesson actually run, and what does my child need?
faqs.answer: One tutor, one student, over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time so nobody is studying at midnight. Tutor and student share a whiteboard and both write on it. A marked script or a photographed piece of work is shared on screen, annotated as they talk, and saved for revision afterwards. A laptop or tablet, a stable connection and a headset are enough, with no software to buy. Sessions usually run sixty minutes, and the short note sent afterwards says what was covered and what to practise before the next one.

faqs.question: Can a tutor work with my child during the exam period, between papers?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is one of the few points where a short session beats a long one. Between papers the useful work is narrow: the six things to check in the hall, one past-paper question of the type that went badly, and sleep. New content introduced inside the exam window tends to displace something already secure, so a sensible tutor refuses to teach anything new in the final ten days. Sessions in that period are booked on request rather than on a fixed weekly slot, because the timetable belongs to the exam board rather than to us.

faqs.question: Which board sets my child's IGCSE dates, Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel?
faqs.answer: Whichever the school enters them with, and it can differ by subject inside the same school. The practical difference is the timetable. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, publishes a separate timetable version for each, and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone version was used. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and confirms them later. Ask the exams officer for the board and syllabus code for every subject, then work only from the official timetable for your centre's zone.

faqs.question: Should we open the Ministry of Education equivalency file before results day?
faqs.answer: Starting early costs nothing and saves weeks. Equivalency is what turns an international certificate into a document a UAE university will accept, and the requirements are published. The British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A Level at E or two AS Levels at the same grade. The American track adds SAT and English-proficiency thresholds. We publish no IB points figure, because we have not read one on the ministry's own site. Verify everything on moe.gov.ae.

faqs.question: Do Arabic and Islamic Education deadlines collide with IB coursework?
faqs.answer: Often, and families rarely plan for it. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated in 40-minute lesson units, so these subjects occupy real weekly hours beside six Diploma courses, and their assessments land in the same terms as IA drafts. Put them on the same planner as the Diploma deadlines before DP2 begins, rather than after the first clash.

faqs.question: Can we pause lessons during the exam weeks and restart afterwards?
faqs.answer: Yes. Pausing is normal and it is usually right twice a year: during the exam window itself, and in the fortnight a major coursework deadline swallows. Because sessions are booked week by week rather than as a locked term, there is nothing to forfeit. What is worth keeping across a pause is the tutor rather than the time slot, since the same specialist picking up in September already knows which topics were weak in May. Tell us about the pause in advance and the subject specialist is held for you rather than released to another family.

ib-private-tutor.closingHeading: Put the first paper on a page, then work backwards
ib-private-tutor.closingBody: If you do one thing after reading this, write the date of your child's first paper at the top of a page and fill in what sits between now and then: the school's coursework dates, mock week, the entry cut-off from the exams officer, the breaks you intend to work through. The plan usually becomes obvious once that page exists, and so does the honest number of hours. Then book a free trial lesson with the subject specialist, bring the page and the most recent marked script, and we will tell you which of the four problems your child actually has and roughly how many weeks it needs. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time.
