ib-psychology-ia-help.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Psychology at Standard and Higher Level and have supervised experimental reports through a full DP cycle. For an IA the useful credential is narrow: can they justify a design, defend a statistical choice, and read a draft against four criteria? Ask exactly that in the trial session.

intro.heading: The Psychology IA is a deadline problem before it is a psychology problem
paragraphs: Almost every enquiry about the Psychology Internal Assessment arrives late. A parent in Dubai or Abu Dhabi hears about the IA properly for the first time in DP2, usually in the week the school announces its submission date, and asks what can be rescued in a fortnight. The honest answer is: less than you would like. The report carries 22 raw marks, which scale to 25% of a Standard Level grade and 20% of a Higher Level one, and most of those marks are settled by decisions the student made months earlier. The last three weeks decide presentation. The nine months before them decide the mark.

So this page is built as a calendar rather than a pitch. The IB does not set the date your child hands the report in. Your school's IB coordinator does, and they set it comfortably ahead of the IB's own spring upload window so there is room to mark, standardise and send a moderation sample. Work backwards from that one published school date and the whole project turns into a sequence of small, dateable tasks: read the original study, fix the design, get the ethics form signed, recruit participants, collect data, run one statistical test, assemble a full version, and use the single permitted round of teacher feedback while it can still change something.

The second thing worth knowing is what this IA actually is in Psychology, because it is narrower than the word suggests in other subjects. It is a report on a simple experiment the student runs themselves, modelled on a published study, with one manipulated independent variable and one measured dependent variable. Correlational designs, a questionnaire on its own, naturalistic observation and anything involving participants who cannot properly consent are all outside the brief. A student who spends six weeks on a survey idea has not made a weak IA. They have made something the criteria cannot mark at all, and the only fix is to start the design again.

The third is statistics. Criterion C holds six of the 22 marks, and it is where UAE students most often meet an inferential test for the first time. The test has to match the design, be chosen before any data arrive, and be reported properly: the statistic itself, the sample size, the significance level and the direction of the hypothesis. Switching to a Mann-Whitney U after seeing that a t-test gave a dull result is the most expensive single mistake available on this task, because an examiner can see the design and the data and tell exactly what happened.

Everything here is taught, not supplied. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, starting with one trial lesson per student before any payment is taken. A tutor explains the criteria, questions the design, teaches the statistics, and reads what the student has assembled against the mark bands. A tutor does not pick the topic, fill in the ethics form, run the test, or hand over a sentence of the report. That boundary is not a marketing position. It is the difference between legitimate support and an IB malpractice investigation that lands on the candidate, not on the tutor.
bullets: 22 raw marks: Criterion A 6, Criterion B 4, Criterion C 6, Criterion D 6.
1,800 to 2,200 words, with the title page, references and appendices excluded.
The IB allots 20 teaching hours to the IA; the project occupies far longer than that.
One draft, one round of written teacher feedback. That is the IB's limit, not the school's.
The experiment must be modelled on a published study: no correlations, no lone questionnaire.
Ramadan now falls in February and moves earlier each year, landing inside DP2's final IA weeks.

ib-psychology-ia-help.programmesIntro: Psychology sits in Group 3 of the Diploma Programme, but the research skills the IA tests start much earlier in an IB school. These are the programmes a UAE family is likely to be inside when the IA becomes urgent, and what each one actually asks for.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Psychology runs at Standard and Higher Level over two years. Standard Level sits two papers and the IA; Higher Level adds Paper 3 on approaches to research and the HL extensions inside each approach. The IA is the same task at both levels: one experimental report on a study of the student's own design, modelled on published work, marked out of 22 by the teacher and moderated externally.
programmes.countryNote: Most UAE DP cohorts are small. In a Dubai school with two Psychology classes the IA deadlines of forty students land in the same fortnight, so teacher feedback queues and lab-room bookings both bottleneck at once. In Al Ain, Ajman or Fujairah a student may be one of three Psychology candidates in the year, which solves the queue and creates a different problem: nobody in the room has done this before either.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Individuals and Societies in MYP 4 and 5 is where the habits that earn Criterion B marks are built, or not built: defining a variable so someone else could measure it, choosing a sample and saying why, naming a control. The MYP Personal Project is assessed against its own criteria and is not a rehearsal for the IA, but students who planned one properly recognise the shape of the work.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools running the MYP also carry the KHDA, ADEK, SPEA or Ministry of Education requirement for Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IB framework, which compresses the timetable in MYP 4 and 5. A student arriving in DP1 from a crowded MYP week has usually had less practice at designing an investigation than the IA assumes, and that gap is best closed in DP1 Term 1, not DP2.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme combines DP courses with a career-related study and its own core, including a reflective project. A CP student taking Psychology as one of their DP courses sits the same papers and submits the same IA under the same criteria and the same word limit. The reflective project is a separate assessment with separate requirements and a separate internal deadline.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is offered by a small number of UAE schools, concentrated in Dubai and Abu Dhabi. Where a family is weighing it, the practical point for Psychology is that nothing about the IA is relaxed: the same 22 marks, the same 2,200-word ceiling, the same single round of feedback. Two internal deadlines in one term is the real planning problem, and it is why the backwards calendar below matters more, not less.

programmes.name: Extended Essay in Psychology
programmes.description: The Extended Essay in Psychology is a 4,000-word research question answered from published literature, not from new data collected by the student. It is a different task from the IA and is marked against different criteria, with its own supervisor meetings and reflection sessions recorded on the Reflections on Planning and Progress Form.
programmes.countryNote: Families in the UAE often ask whether the two can share a topic. They can share a literature base and should not share a question. The IA needs a study simple enough to replicate in a school room; the Extended Essay needs a question broad enough to argue across several studies. Where both fall due in the same DP2 term, the IA goes first, because its mark is locked by the school's internal deadline.

ib-psychology-ia-help.subjectsIntro: Psychology IA questions almost always arrive attached to a content topic, because the study a student replicates has to come from somewhere in the syllabus. These are the areas UAE students bring to IA sessions, and what each one tends to hand them.

subjects.name: Biological approach to behaviour
subjects.description: Localisation, neuroplasticity, neurotransmission, hormones and pheromones, and genetics. A rich source of replicable experiments only if the student picks a behavioural measure rather than a physiological one: a school cannot scan a brain, but it can measure reaction time, recall or a rated response.

subjects.name: Cognitive approach to behaviour
subjects.description: Models of memory, schema theory, reconstructive memory, thinking and decision-making, and the reliability of cognitive processes. This is where most workable IAs come from, because memory and attention studies produce clean two-condition designs with a measurable dependent variable inside a single lesson.

subjects.name: Sociocultural approach to behaviour
subjects.description: Social identity theory, social cognitive theory, stereotypes, culture and cultural dimensions, and acculturation. Tempting for IAs and frequently a trap: many classic sociocultural studies rely on deception or on manipulating self-image, which the ethical requirements rule out for a school replication.

subjects.name: Abnormal psychology
subjects.description: Classification, prevalence, aetiologies and treatment of disorders. Almost never a safe IA source, because any design that screens, labels or distresses participants fails on ethics. It is a strong Paper 2 option and a poor experiment, and knowing that early saves a student several weeks.

subjects.name: Developmental psychology
subjects.description: Brain development, attachment, gender identity, peer and play influences, and the role of poverty and trauma. The ethical constraint is participant age: most of the interesting work involves children, and a school IA has to use participants who can consent for themselves.

subjects.name: Health psychology
subjects.description: Determinants of health, health problems, promoting health, and health beliefs. Workable for an IA when the manipulation is framing rather than behaviour change, for instance how a message about a risk is worded against how it is rated, which can be run in one sitting with consenting participants.

subjects.name: Psychology of human relationships
subjects.description: Personal relationships, group dynamics, social responsibility, prosocial behaviour and bystander effects. A frequent IA source. Designs here need careful debriefing, because anything that implies a participant failed to help touches on self-image and has to be handled in the ethics plan.

subjects.name: Research methodology for the IA
subjects.description: Experimental designs, independent and repeated measures, operationalisation, sampling methods, extraneous and confounding variables, demand characteristics, standardised instructions and controls. This is the backbone of Criterion B and the part a student can learn in two sessions and then apply for the rest of the project.

subjects.name: Inferential statistics for the IA
subjects.description: Levels of measurement, descriptive statistics and measures of dispersion, significance levels, one- and two-tailed hypotheses, and the four tests a school IA realistically uses: Mann-Whitney U, Wilcoxon signed-ranks, the independent-samples t-test and the paired-samples t-test.

subjects.name: Paper 3: approaches to research
subjects.description: An unseen stimulus with three short-answer questions on method, credibility, bias, sampling and generalisation. Paper 3 and the IA teach each other: a student who can defend their own design in Criterion B can answer Paper 3 on somebody else's, and the revision overlaps almost completely.

subjects.name: Ethics in psychological research
subjects.description: Informed consent, right to withdraw, protection from harm, anonymity, debriefing, and the limits on deception. Examined in Paper 1 and Paper 3 and gating the IA: without a signed ethics approval from the supervising teacher, data collection cannot begin and the project stalls.

subjects.name: Command terms and Paper 2 technique
subjects.description: Discuss, evaluate, contrast, to what extent. Paper 2 essays are marked on how far the command term is answered rather than on how much was recalled, and the same discipline earns Criterion D marks when a student evaluates their own design instead of listing its features.

ib-psychology-ia-help.regionsTitle: Psychology IA support across the seven emirates
ib-psychology-ia-help.regionsIntro: Lessons are delivered online, so where a family lives changes the schedule and the school context rather than the availability of a tutor. What does change by emirate is which regulator licenses the school, how large the Psychology cohort is, and how hard it is to find twenty willing participants.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Dubai's private sector held 387,441 students across 227 private schools in 2024-25, offering 17 curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for 7% of enrolment. Large Psychology cohorts mean long teacher feedback queues and competition for a free room to collect data in.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools here, and its professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students at their own school. So the teacher who sets your child's IA deadline and marks the report cannot also be the paid tutor coaching it.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with fewer DP Psychology cohorts than the coast. A student may be one of three candidates in the year, which removes the feedback queue but also removes the peer group. Recruiting twenty participants from a small sixth form takes planning, not luck.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Many Sharjah families attend school in Dubai, so the IA deadline that matters is the one set by the school, not the one set where they sleep.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman. The IB cohort is small, and a Psychology specialist who can argue about a repeated-measures design is unlikely to live within driving distance. Online is not a compromise here; it is the only route to the specialism.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and approves curricula and assessment methods alongside fees. For a family here, an evening video slot replaces a ninety-minute drive each way to a Dubai tutor, and that is the difference between weekly sessions and monthly ones.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the Ministry of Education, on the other side of the Hajar mountains from the main IB belt. East-coast DP students are the clearest case for online delivery: nothing about the IA requires a room, and everything about it requires a specialist.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: The smallest private sector in the country, also under the Ministry of Education. Psychology candidates here are rare enough that the practical question is usually not which tutor but which published study can realistically be replicated with the participant pool actually available.

schoolClusters.note: The largest DP Psychology cohorts in the country sit here, which is why internal IA deadlines in Dubai are typically earlier than elsewhere: a department marking forty reports needs more runway before the moderation sample goes out. Students from these schools arrive at sessions with a departmental IA booklet, and the first job is reading it against the IB criteria.

Cohorts are smaller and feedback is usually faster, but participant recruitment is harder and the ADEK ethics position means the subject teacher cannot double as the paid tutor. Students from these schools most often arrive with a design already approved and a statistics problem they did not see coming.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi
The British International School Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.note: A thinner IB belt regulated by SPEA, the RAK Department of Knowledge and the Ministry of Education depending on the emirate. Psychology is not offered in every school here, so some candidates are taught in a class of four by a teacher covering two Group 3 subjects, and external method support carries more weight than it would in a large Dubai department.

ib-psychology-ia-help.modesIntro: Four ways families use Psychology IA support, matched to how far the project has actually got rather than to a package name. All of them run one-to-one over live video, with the draft, the data file and the criteria open on screen together.

modes.description: One session a week across the months when the IA is actually built. The sequence follows the backwards calendar on this page: study selection, design, ethics, recruitment, collection, analysis, assembly. The tutor's job each week is to ask the question the criteria will ask, and to send a short written note of what the student committed to doing before the next session.

Four sessions cover levels of measurement, descriptive statistics and dispersion, choosing between the four tests a school IA uses, running it in a spreadsheet or in SPSS, and reporting the result in the form Criterion C expects.

The tutor reads the student's own material against the four criteria and the mark allocations, and names what each criterion is currently missing. The student makes every change themselves; nothing is edited for them, and no replacement text is supplied.

sections.heading: What IB Psychology IA help can honestly include
paragraphs: Start with the literal question. Searched from the UAE, this phrase almost always means one of four situations: my child has no topic; my child has a topic the criteria cannot mark; my child has data and no idea what to do with them; or my child has a full version and three weeks left. Each needs a different first session, and only the last is really a matter of writing at all.

A tutor's job in all four is teaching. The IB's position on authenticity is not subtle: the submitted report must be the student's own work, and the supervising teacher may give advice on one draft. Everything beyond that is malpractice. The practical consequence is that a useful IA session looks like a seminar, not a service. The tutor asks why the design controls what it claims to control, what the operational definition of the dependent variable is, how the sample was recruited, and which test the data will need once they exist.

This matters practically as much as ethically. The IB checks authenticity at the point of moderation, and the penalty for submitted work that is not the candidate's own falls on the candidate, where it costs the diploma rather than a single subject grade. Any site offering to hand over a finished report is selling a family a risk it has not priced. Our line is plain: we teach method, criteria and statistics, we read what the student has already assembled, and we say where it sits against the mark bands. Nothing leaves a session that the student did not make.

The table below is the boundary we teach to, stage by stage. It is worth reading with your child rather than instead of them, because the commonest honesty failures on this task are not deliberate. A student who accepts a ready-made design from a well-meaning adult, or who lets a relative run the statistics, has usually not understood that those are the assessed parts.

Ethics forms and standardised instructions are assessed material, not admin
Statistical output the student did not generate cannot be defended in Criterion C
One draft, one round of written teacher feedback: plan the calendar around it

sections.heading: The Psychology IA counted backwards from the May session
paragraphs: Here is the most useful thing on this page. Take the date your school has published for final IA submission and count backwards in weeks. Not from the May examination window, which has nothing to do with the IA. Not from the IB's own upload window, which your coordinator has already padded. From the school date. Every milestone in the table below sits a fixed distance from that one number, and each has a failure mode that costs weeks rather than days.

Two of these milestones are outside the student's control, which is exactly why they have to be scheduled early. Ethics approval depends on a teacher reading and signing a form, and teachers read forms in batches. The one permitted round of written feedback depends on a marking queue, which in a large Dubai department with a full Psychology cohort can run a fortnight long. A student who has a complete version eight weeks out gets feedback they can still act on. A student who gets there at three weeks out gets a tick and a kind sentence.

Data collection is the other reliable disaster. A school experiment needs participants who turn up, in a room that is free, during a period nobody else needs. In the UAE that means negotiating with a timetable that already carries Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies alongside the IB courses. If the first attempt fails because of a fire drill, a sports fixture or an inter-school event, the next genuinely free window is often three weeks away. Collect early enough that one failure is survivable, and treat the second attempt as part of the plan rather than as bad luck.

One note on dates. No specific IB session or results date appears anywhere on this page, because the IB publishes those itself and they change. Confirm every date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org before planning around it. What does not change is the ordering, and the ordering is what the table gives you.

sections.heading: The 22 marks, criterion by criterion
paragraphs: The Psychology IA is marked out of 22 against four criteria, and the mark allocations are public. Criterion A, the introduction, carries six marks. Criterion B, exploration, carries four. Criterion C, analysis, carries six. Criterion D, evaluation, carries six. Both Standard and Higher Level students submit the same task against the same criteria; the only difference is what the mark is worth in the final grade, 25% at SL and 20% at HL.

Criterion A is not a literature review. It asks for the published study the investigation is based on, the theory or model behind it, and a clearly stated aim with hypotheses whose direction is explicit. Most lost marks here come from a student summarising a theory accurately and then never tying it to the specific manipulation they chose. If the reader cannot see why this independent variable should move this dependent variable according to that theory, the marks are gone whatever else is on the page.

Criterion B is the smallest band and the most mechanically earned. It wants the design named and justified, the sampling technique named and justified, and the controls and ethical considerations stated rather than listed. Criterion C is where UAE students most often slip: descriptive statistics with a measure of dispersion, a graph that shows something, and an inferential test whose choice is justified against the design and the level of measurement. Criterion D then asks for a discussion against the original study, limitations specific to this design, and modifications that would actually address them.

Read the table with your child's draft open. The fourth column is not a list of style complaints; each line is a mark band a real report has fallen out of, and almost all of them are fixable in one session if there is still time to fix anything.

sections.heading: Choosing the statistical test before the data exist
paragraphs: The order of operations is the whole lesson. A student decides the design, which decides the level of measurement, which decides the inferential test, which decides what has to be recorded during collection. Doing it the other way round, collecting first and then looking for a test that fits, produces reports where the test is defensible by accident and indefensible in writing. An examiner reading Criterion C can see which order it happened in.

There are only four tests a school Psychology IA realistically needs, plus one it should avoid. Two conditions with different participants and ordinal or non-normal data takes a Mann-Whitney U. The same participants in both conditions with ordinal data takes a Wilcoxon signed-ranks test. Interval data that is roughly normal takes an independent-samples t-test for separate groups or a paired-samples t-test for the same participants twice. A chi-square test of independence handles frequency counts, which is rarer in an experimental IA because it usually signals that the dependent variable was never properly measured.

Reporting is a separate skill from running the test. The criterion wants the statistic itself, the sample size, the significance level, whether the hypothesis was one- or two-tailed, and a sentence that states what the result means for the hypothesis rather than for the theory. A result that fails to reach significance is not a weak IA. Students lose far more marks pretending an effect exists than they ever lose reporting honestly that it did not, because Criterion D rewards exactly that discussion.

sections.heading: Ethics, consent and finding twenty participants in a UAE school
paragraphs: Ethics is the gate, not the garnish. Data collection cannot begin until the supervising teacher has approved the plan, and the approval covers how participants are recruited, what they are told, what they consent to, how they can withdraw, how their data are anonymised, and what the debriefing says. Those documents go into the appendices and are read as part of Criterion B. A student who treats the form as paperwork ends up with four marks hanging on a page they filled in at speed.

Participant choice is where UAE students hit the real constraint. The pool has to be people who can give informed consent for themselves, which in practice means older students, staff or adults in the family's own network. That rules out most of the developmental psychology topics students find interesting, and it rules out anything that screens for a disorder, measures distress, or leaves a participant feeling they performed badly. A design that cannot be run ethically is not a design, however elegant the hypothesis.

Then there is simple logistics. Twenty to thirty participants, in two conditions, in a free room, during a period when none of them has a lesson. In a small Al Ain or Fujairah sixth form that arithmetic is tight enough that the design has to bend to the pool rather than the other way round. In a large Dubai school the pool exists but competes with every other DP2 student collecting data in the same fortnight. Either way, recruitment is a scheduling task that belongs sixteen weeks out, not a thing that happens the week before analysis.

sections.heading: Where Psychology IA marks actually leak
paragraphs: Most IAs that come to us at six weeks out are not badly written. They are structurally short of two or three specific things, and the same ones recur across schools and emirates. The first is a hypothesis without direction. A student writes that there will be a difference, then runs a one-tailed test, and Criterion C unravels because the test no longer matches what was predicted. Directionality is a sentence, and it has to be decided before collection.

The second is an operational definition that is not operational. Measuring recall is fine; measuring memory is not. If another person could not take the written procedure and produce comparable numbers, the definition is not doing its job, and the consequences land in Criterion B and again in Criterion D when the student tries to evaluate reliability. The third is a results section that reports a mean and nothing else. A mean without a standard deviation or an interquartile range tells a marker nothing about whether the difference is worth discussing.

The fourth is evaluation by template. Small sample, lack of generalisability, demand characteristics, in that order, on thousands of reports. Six marks sit in Criterion D and they are awarded for limitations specific to this design and modifications that would plausibly fix them. If the limitation would read identically on any other IA in the year group, it is not earning anything. The fifth is the word count: going past 2,200 words is a self-inflicted loss, and it is almost always the introduction that caused it.
bullets: Hypotheses stated with direction, decided before any data arrive
Operational definitions another person could follow without asking a question
Every mean reported with a measure of dispersion beside it
Limitations that could only be written about this study, not any study
Appendices complete: consent, instructions, debriefing, raw data, calculations

sections.heading: What Psychology IA support costs in the UAE market
paragraphs: Nobody ranking for this search publishes a rate in dirhams, so here is the market as it stands, attributed. These are other providers' published figures and market survey bands, not IB Gram prices. They are useful because they tell you what a quote should look like before you receive one, and because the spread is wide enough that a family can pay three times the going rate for the same hour of teaching.

At the bottom, group revision and budget online platforms publish rates from AED 33 to AED 150 an hour. Those sessions teach content, not IA method, and for a student stuck on a repeated-measures design they are the wrong purchase at any price. A qualified subject tutor working online sits roughly between AED 150 and AED 300, which is where most IB Psychology teaching happens. A named IB or IGCSE specialist runs from about AED 200 to AED 450 and upward, and premium examiner-positioned tutors are advertised as high as AED 650 an hour.

Monthly packages advertised in this market include online blocks around AED 799 a month for eight sessions and in-home blocks of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. Bestimate's 2026 Dubai tutoring cost table puts weekly one-hour tutoring at AED 240 to AED 600 a month at the budget end and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. For context, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, so the tutoring line in a family budget is the one that moved.

What we do instead of a price list: one trial lesson per student before any payment, then a quote for the specific block of work the IA actually needs. A statistics block is four sessions. A criterion review before a deadline is usually two. A weekly clinic from DP1 Term 3 is a different conversation, and it should be priced as one.

sections.heading: Online support against an in-home IA tutor in the UAE
paragraphs: Parents searching for IA help in the UAE usually start by looking for somebody who will sit at the dining table. That is a reasonable instinct and it is worth answering honestly rather than deflecting. A visiting tutor in Dubai or Abu Dhabi charges between AED 180 and AED 500 an hour according to published market figures, and a meaningful part of that is travel: crossing Dubai at five in the afternoon can take forty minutes each way, and a tutor who spends ninety minutes travelling for a sixty-minute lesson prices that in.

IB Gram delivers UAE tutoring as one-to-one online tuition over live video. Home visits are a service we run in India, not here, and no sentence on this site should suggest otherwise. The case for online on this particular task is unusually strong, because an IA is document work. The report, the spreadsheet of raw data, the statistical output and the IB criteria all need to be visible at once, and two people sharing a screen can do that better than two people sharing one printed copy.

The second argument is the tutor pool. IB Psychology with confident inferential statistics is a narrow specialism, and the number of people holding it who also happen to live within a drivable radius of Khalifa City or Al Hamra is small. Online removes the radius from the selection criteria entirely. The third is the shape of IA crunch weeks: a student six days from a deadline needs a 7am slot or a 10pm one, and those exist in a calendar but not on a driving route.

There is one honest point against. A student who will not open a laptop without being watched does better with somebody in the room, and for that family a visiting tutor is the right answer even at the higher rate. We would rather say so than take the booking.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and the UAE school year around the IA
paragraphs: The IA calendar runs through a UAE school year that has its own shape, and two parts of it reliably eat working weeks. Ramadan now falls in February and moves about eleven days earlier each year, which puts it squarely inside the final stretch of DP2 for the current cycle. School days are shortened across UAE schools for the month, which removes exactly the free periods a student was going to use for data collection, and the Eid Al Fitr break removes another working week straight afterwards.

The practical answer is to move work, not to lose it. Sessions shift to post-Iftar slots, which in the UAE means a tutor working on Gulf Standard Time after about eight in the evening. The tasks that survive a shortened day are reading, design, statistics and assembly. The task that does not survive is data collection, because it needs other people's free periods, and during Ramadan there are fewer of them. So collection belongs before the month starts, and the calendar earlier on this page is built on that assumption.

The other compression is the DP2 mock window, which in most UAE schools sits in the winter term and swallows two to three weeks of a student's attention. Mocks are useful and should not be sacrificed to the IA, which is another argument for having a complete version assembled before them. A student who finishes mocks and then has only teacher feedback left to act on is in a good position. A student who finishes mocks and still has to collect data is in trouble, and no amount of tutoring buys back those weeks.

sections.heading: Who sets what: your school, your emirate and the IB
paragraphs: Three different authorities touch a UAE student's IA, and families routinely attribute decisions to the wrong one. The IB owns the task: the criteria, the 22 marks, the word limit, the one-draft feedback rule and the moderation sample. Your school owns the internal deadline, the ethics approval process, the room you collect data in and the marking queue. The emirate's regulator owns the school, not the assessment, and that distinction saves a lot of misdirected email.

The regulator map is worth knowing anyway. Dubai's private schools answer to KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, both of which approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah come under the federal Ministry of Education. None of them marks an IA, and none of them can extend a deadline.

One regulator decision does affect tutoring directly. Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is open to registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone tutoring without one is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you. Abu Dhabi adds a professional-ethics rule reported to bar school staff from paid tutoring of students at their own school, which is why your child's Psychology teacher cannot be the paid IA tutor. IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform and holds no approval, licence or partnership from any of these bodies.

MoE equivalency sits in the same category: a real process, not ours to perform. For British-curriculum students the published requirement is five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited A-Level at grade E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. For the American track, English proficiency is evidenced by IELTS 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in SAT reading and writing, and mathematics by at least 450 in SAT Math. No IB points threshold is published in that source, so we publish none; verify any IB figure on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate.

process.title: Send the four facts that matter
process.description: Subject and level, the school's published IA deadline, where the project has actually reached, and which emirate the school is in. Those four lines are enough to say whether the problem is a design problem, a statistics problem or a calendar problem, and they decide what the first session is spent on.

process.title: One trial lesson, read against the criteria
process.description: One trial lesson per student, before any payment. The tutor reads whatever exists, whether that is a title or a full version, against the four criteria and the mark allocations, and names the two things that would move the mark most. You get that assessment whether or not you book anything further.

process.title: A plan counted backwards from the school date
process.description: Not a package. A list of milestones with weeks attached, taken from the backwards calendar on this page and adjusted to your school's deadline, Ramadan and the mock window. It names which milestones depend on a teacher, because those are the ones that have to be requested early rather than chased late.

process.title: Weekly sessions with a written note after each
process.description: Sessions run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time. After each one the tutor sends a short note of what was covered and what the student committed to before the next session. That note is what keeps the project alive through a missed week, a travel trip or an exam fortnight.

process.title: If no Psychology specialist is free
process.description: Sometimes there is no IB Psychology tutor with the right statistics background available in the hours a family needs. We say so and offer the nearest honest alternative: a research-methods specialist for the design and analysis, a later start date, or a recommendation to look elsewhere. We would rather lose the booking than fill it badly.

process.title: Stop when the work is done
process.description: An IA block ends at submission. Higher Level students usually continue into Paper 3 because the method vocabulary transfers directly; Standard Level students often stop and come back for Paper 2 technique closer to the session. Nothing renews automatically and nothing is bundled into a longer commitment than the task needs.

whyPoints.title: The calendar is the actual product
whyPoints.description: Most IA failures are scheduling failures wearing a subject costume. A plan counted backwards from the school's own date, with the teacher-dependent milestones flagged, prevents more lost marks than any amount of last-fortnight polishing. It is the first thing we build and the thing we revisit every session.

whyPoints.title: Criteria and mark allocations, not impressions
whyPoints.description: Six marks for the introduction, four for exploration, six for analysis, six for evaluation. Feedback that does not name a criterion and a band is decoration. Every session ends with the student able to say which criterion they worked on and what it is currently missing.

whyPoints.title: Statistics taught before the data arrive
whyPoints.description: The test follows the design, and the design follows the research question. Teaching inferential statistics at the design stage costs two sessions and protects six marks. Teaching it after collection means fitting a test to numbers that were never recorded with any test in mind.

whyPoints.title: A hard line on whose work it is
whyPoints.description: We teach, question and give feedback on the student's own material. We do not choose topics, sign ethics forms, run tests or supply text. That boundary is published here so a family can hold us to it, and because a report that is not the candidate's own puts the whole diploma at risk.

whyPoints.title: Independent, and saying so
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. It holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from the IB, KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE or the Ministry of Education, and no school named on this page is a client or partner. Anyone claiming regulator approval for tutoring is worth a second question.

whyPoints.title: Built for Gulf Standard Time
whyPoints.description: Sessions are scheduled on UAE time, including early-morning and late-evening slots in deadline weeks and post-Iftar slots through Ramadan. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video, so a family in Fujairah gets the same tutor availability as a family in Jumeirah.

faqs.question: How long should an IB Psychology IA be?
faqs.answer: The report runs to between 1,800 and 2,200 words. The title page, the reference list and the appendices sit outside that count, which means the raw data, consent form, standardised instructions, debriefing script and statistical calculations do not eat into it. Going past the upper limit is a mechanical loss of marks rather than a judgement call, and in practice it is nearly always the introduction that caused it: three studies summarised where one was needed. If a draft is 2,600 words, cut Criterion A first and check that every sentence there connects the theory to the specific variable being manipulated.

faqs.question: How many marks is the Psychology IA worth, and how are they split?
faqs.answer: Twenty-two raw marks across four criteria: Criterion A, introduction, six marks; Criterion B, exploration, four; Criterion C, analysis, six; Criterion D, evaluation, six. That total is scaled to 25% of the final grade at Standard Level and 20% at Higher Level, where Paper 3 takes a share of the weighting instead. Standard and Higher Level students submit the same task against the same criteria, so there is no easier version. Knowing the split changes how a student spends their last fortnight: ten of the twenty-two marks sit in analysis and evaluation, which are the two sections most often thinnest.

faqs.question: Which inferential test does my child need for their Psychology IA?
faqs.answer: It follows from the design, so it should be decided before any data are collected. Two separate groups with ordinal or skewed scores points to a Mann-Whitney U. The same participants measured twice with ordinal data points to a Wilcoxon signed-ranks test. Interval data that is roughly normal takes an independent-samples t-test for separate groups or a paired-samples t-test for repeated measures. Frequency counts take a chi-square test of independence, though that usually signals a dependent variable that was never properly measured. The justification matters as much as the choice, because Criterion C marks the reasoning.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with the Psychology IA without breaking IB academic honesty rules?
faqs.answer: Yes, within a clear boundary. A tutor can teach research methods, explain the criteria and their mark allocations, question a design, teach statistics, and read what the student has already assembled and say where it sits against the bands. A tutor cannot choose the topic, draft the ethics form, write the standardised instructions, run the statistical test, or supply text for the report. The submitted work has to be the candidate's own, and the supervising teacher may give advice on one draft. Anything beyond that is malpractice, and the consequence falls on the student's diploma.

faqs.question: When should a UAE student actually start their Psychology IA?
faqs.answer: Thirty weeks before the school's submission date, which for most UAE schools means DP1's final term. That sounds early until you count the dependencies: a published study has to be read in full, a design fixed, an ethics form approved by a teacher who reads forms in batches, participants recruited around a timetable, and data collected in a room that is free. Each of those can slip by a fortnight without anyone being careless. Students who start in DP2 are not doomed, but they are choosing to run the project without any slack at all.

faqs.question: Who can be a participant in a school Psychology experiment in the UAE?
faqs.answer: People who can give informed consent for themselves, which in practice means older students, staff and adults in the family's own network. That constraint rules out most developmental psychology topics and anything that screens for a disorder, induces distress, or leaves a participant feeling they performed badly. The approved plan has to cover recruitment, what participants are told, the right to withdraw, anonymisation and the debriefing. In a small sixth form in Al Ain or Fujairah the pool is the binding constraint on the whole design, so identify it before falling in love with a hypothesis.

faqs.question: What happens if the Psychology IA goes over 2,200 words?
faqs.answer: It costs marks, and it is the most avoidable loss on the task. Examiners work to the published limit, so material beyond it cannot reliably be credited, and a student who has put their best evaluation in the final paragraph can lose it entirely. The fix is almost always structural rather than editorial. Trim the introduction to the one published study the investigation is based on and the theory that links it to the manipulation. Move anything procedural into the appendices, where the word count does not reach. Then recount before submission, not after.

faqs.question: Does the Psychology IA have to be based on a published study?
faqs.answer: Yes. The task is a simple experiment modelled on published work, with one manipulated independent variable and one measured dependent variable. That rules out correlational designs, a questionnaire on its own, naturalistic observation and purely qualitative approaches, however interesting the question. It also makes study selection the single highest-leverage decision in the project: a published study that cannot be replicated in a school room with consenting adult participants will generate weeks of effort and no markable data. Read the original paper in full before committing, not the abstract and not a textbook summary of it.

faqs.question: How many drafts of the IA can my child's teacher read?
faqs.answer: One. The supervising teacher may give advice on a single draft, and that advice has to be written rather than a conversation that leaves no record. This one rule should shape the entire calendar. A student who assembles a complete version eight weeks before the deadline gets feedback with time to act on it. A student who gets there three weeks out gets a tick. It also explains why external method support is legitimate and useful: a tutor can question a design in October without spending the one feedback round the IB allows.

faqs.question: What does Criterion B, exploration, actually ask for?
faqs.answer: Four marks for design choices defended rather than described. The marker wants the experimental design named and justified against the research question, the sampling technique named and justified, the controls identified, and the ethical considerations stated in a way that shows they shaped the procedure. The commonest loss is a report that names a repeated-measures design and never says why that design suits this manipulation, or that lists ethics as a checklist of five words. It is the smallest band on the task and the most mechanically earned, which makes it the cheapest four marks available.

faqs.question: What does Psychology IA support cost in the UAE market?
faqs.answer: Published rates in this market run from about AED 33 to 150 an hour for budget online platforms and group revision, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online, AED 200 to 450 and upward for a named IB specialist, and AED 180 to 500 for a visiting tutor where travel sits inside the fee. Premium examiner-positioned tutors are advertised as high as AED 650. Those are other providers' figures, not ours. We quote for the specific block of work after one trial lesson, because a statistics block and a two-year clinic are not the same purchase.

faqs.question: Does Ramadan change the IA timetable for UAE students?
faqs.answer: It changes what is possible, so it should change the plan. Ramadan currently falls in February and moves roughly eleven days earlier each year, which places it inside the final IA stretch for DP2 students. School days are shortened across the country, so the free periods a student intended to use for data collection largely disappear, and the Eid Al Fitr break removes another working week. Reading, design, statistics and assembly all survive a shortened day and move comfortably to post-Iftar sessions. Data collection does not, so it belongs before the month begins.

faqs.question: Is online support as useful as sitting with a tutor in Dubai for IA work?
faqs.answer: For this task it is usually better, and the reason is practical rather than ideological. An IA is document work: the report, the raw data, the statistical output and the IB criteria all need to be visible at the same moment, which two people sharing a screen manage more easily than two people sharing a printout. Online also removes the drivable radius from tutor selection, and IB Psychology with confident inferential statistics is a narrow specialism. The honest exception is a student who will not work without somebody physically present. For that family, a visiting tutor is the right answer.

faqs.question: Can my child's own Psychology teacher be their paid IA tutor?
faqs.answer: Not in Abu Dhabi, and it is a poor idea anywhere. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported to bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct that also addresses serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Beyond the rules, the teacher who will mark the report and sign the ethics form should not also be paid to coach it. Verify the current position with the school before arranging anything.

faqs.question: Do private tutors in the UAE need a permit, and how do I check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Applications go through MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit for Private Tutor Licensing, via its app, website and e-services. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so treat any specific figure quoted at you with scepticism. Ask a tutor directly whether they hold one.

faqs.question: Does the Psychology IA mark affect UAE certificate equivalency?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is assessed on the final certificate, not on a single internal assessment, so the IA matters only through the grade it helps produce. For the British track the Ministry of Education's published requirement is five accredited IGCSE or GCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at grade E or two AS-Levels. No IB points threshold appears in that published source, so we quote none. Check the current IB requirement on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate before planning around any number.

ib-psychology-ia-help.closingHeading: Start from the date, not from the draft
ib-psychology-ia-help.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, take the arithmetic. Find your school's published IA submission date, count back thirty weeks, and see where your child actually is against the milestones in the calendar above. That single exercise tells you whether this is a design conversation, a statistics conversation or a salvage operation, and it costs nothing. Then send us the four facts: subject, level, that deadline, and where the project has reached. One trial lesson per student, read against the four criteria, before any payment. Lessons are delivered one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, anywhere in the UAE.

intro.heading: A primary parent is not buying hours. They are buying timing.
paragraphs: Search for an IB PYP home tutor in the UAE and you will find page after page offering subjects, levels and hourly rates. Almost none of them answer the question a primary parent actually has, which is when. Your child has no entry deadline, no paper one, no results day. The Primary Years Programme is deliberately built that way: it reports against descriptors rather than marks, and it keeps the first externally dated qualification years out of sight. The effect on parents is predictable. Support gets bought in reaction - after a report, after a comment at a conference, three weeks before the Exhibition - rather than in advance of anything.

There is a calendar, though. It is just a school calendar rather than an examinations calendar, and nobody publishes it from a parent's side. A UAE primary year normally opens in late August or early September, breaks for a fortnight around the winter holidays, runs a long second term into the spring, loses teaching days to Ramadan and Eid, and finishes in late June or early July. Schools licensed on an April-start year sit on a different rhythm again. Inside that frame sit the dated items that genuinely matter to a seven-year-old: the first reading assessment, the two parent-teacher conferences, the mid-year benchmark window many schools now run, the portfolio review, and in the final year, Exhibition presentation week.

Reading that calendar forwards tells you when the school will tell you something. Reading it backwards tells you when to act. A child who is a year behind in reading fluency in Grade 2 does not need an emergency in May; they need two short sessions a week from September, when the teaching weeks are intact and the child is not tired. A Grade 5 student heading into the Exhibition does not need a crash course in presentation the week before; they need help with research questions and note-making roughly ten weeks out, while the inquiry can still change shape.

The second thing a primary parent is timing is the exit. The PYP finishes and something external starts: MYP 1 with its criterion marks out of eight, or a British-track Year 7 that leads to Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel International GCSE entries, or an American-track middle school. Each of those has a real, published deadline somewhere down the line - a Cambridge IGCSE entry in the UAE is made for either the June series or the November one, and the centre closes entries months ahead of the papers, early enough that the subject is still mid-syllabus when the decision is locked. A primary parent does not need to meet that deadline. They need to know it exists, because it is the first point at which a date stops being negotiable.

So this page is organised as a calendar rather than a catalogue. It covers what each PYP year produces and when, how to read the Exhibition backwards, which primary-stage assessments in UAE schools carry published windows, how the Ramadan timetable moves the teaching weeks, what the market charges and when families tend to buy, and what the Ministry of Education will eventually ask for at the far end of school. Where IB Gram is concerned the delivery answer is short: one-to-one tuition over live video, anywhere in the Emirates, and no visit to a UAE address.

ib-pyp-home-tutor.programmesIntro: The PYP runs for six or seven years and behaves differently at each end of it. Grouping it by stage, rather than treating it as one block, is what makes a dated plan possible - the Early Years have no assessment worth planning around, and the exit year has one that governs everything.

programmes.name: Early Years of the Primary Years Programme
programmes.ageRange: Ages 3-6 - FS1 to Year 1, or Pre-KG to Grade 1
programmes.description: Inquiry through play, spoken language, phonological awareness and the first idea that a numeral stands for a quantity. Nothing here is assessed in a way a tutor can revise towards, and any provider offering exam technique at this stage is selling something that does not exist. What one-to-one time buys is conversation: an adult who waits for a four-year-old to finish a sentence, names things precisely, and repeats a counting game until the quantity stops needing to be counted.
programmes.countryNote: Early Years rooms in the Emirates are among the most linguistically mixed classrooms anywhere, with children arriving from five or six home languages. A child who is quiet in FS2 is often not behind at all but silent in a second language. The dated items are the two parent conferences, and the useful move is to ask at the first one whether the silence is language or comprehension, before a label is attached to it.

programmes.name: Lower primary - the reading years
programmes.ageRange: Ages 6-8 - Year 2 to Year 3, or Grade 1 to Grade 2
programmes.description: Decoding becomes fluency, fluency becomes comprehension, and number bonds become written method. This is the only window in the whole of school where a reading gap can be closed cheaply, because the gap is still measured in months rather than years. Two short sessions a week through a full term usually does more than a single long weekly hour, because the skill being built is automaticity and automaticity needs frequency.
programmes.countryNote: Most UAE primary schools run a reading assessment in the first weeks of term and again before the mid-year report, which gives a parent two comparable numbers roughly five months apart. Those two numbers are the cheapest diagnostic available in the country and they are free. Ask for the band, the date it was taken and the instrument used, then plan the hours against the gap rather than against the comment on the report.

programmes.name: Middle primary - the written method years
programmes.ageRange: Ages 8-10 - Year 4 to Year 5, or Grade 3 to Grade 4
programmes.description: Fractions, decimals, formal written methods for multiplication and division, comprehension of texts the child cannot fully decode by sight, and the first pieces of extended writing. Marks are not the issue; habits are. A child who still counts on fingers in Grade 4 is not slow, they are carrying an unfinished job from Grade 2, and that job takes about a term of short, regular sessions to finish properly.
programmes.countryNote: A majority of UAE international primaries now sit a standardised benchmark test in a mid-year window, often January, and report the result as a standardised score alongside the descriptors. That window is the natural point to start or stop paid support, because it produces the only comparable number of the year. Booking hours in September and reviewing them against the January result is a cleaner plan than reacting to the June report.

programmes.name: The exit year and the Exhibition
programmes.description: One extended, student-directed inquiry presented to an audience, plus the transition into criterion-marked work. The Exhibition is the first time a child owns a piece of work end to end: the question, the research, the evidence, the structure and the delivery. It is also the first point where adult help can tip from teaching into doing, which is why the boundary is worth settling in writing before the first session.
programmes.countryNote: Exhibition presentation week is set by your school, not by the IB, and in most UAE schools it falls in the second half of the year, which puts the research phase squarely across the Ramadan weeks in several years of the cycle. Ask the PYP coordinator for the presentation date in September rather than in March. It is the one primary date worth writing into a family calendar twelve months ahead.

ib-pyp-home-tutor.subjectsIntro: Primary subjects are worth choosing by the dated milestone they feed rather than by the label on the report. Each of the areas below is tied to something that happens at a known point in the UAE school year, which is what makes it possible to say how many weeks of support it needs.

subjects.name: Reading fluency
subjects.description: Words read correctly per minute, and whether the child can still answer a question about what they read. UAE schools test this early in term one, which gives a start point. Fluency responds to frequency rather than to session length, so two twenty-five minute slots beat one long hour.

subjects.name: Reading comprehension
subjects.description: Inference, retrieval and sequencing - the three things benchmark tests in UAE primaries weight most heavily. A child who decodes well and still scores low is almost always losing marks on inference, which is taught by talking about texts rather than by reading more of them.

subjects.name: Writing: sentence to paragraph
subjects.description: Sentence boundaries, tense consistency, then paragraphing. The mid-year report is where this surfaces, because teachers describe it in prose rather than scoring it. Bring a piece of your child's unedited writing to a first session; it says more than any assessment summary.

subjects.name: English as an additional language
subjects.description: Academic vocabulary rather than conversational English. A child fluent in the playground can still miss the language of instruction - compare, justify, in order to. This is the single most common reason a bright primary child in the Emirates reads as underperforming on a benchmark test.

subjects.name: Number sense and mental calculation
subjects.description: Number bonds, place value and recall. Unfinished recall in Grade 2 reappears as slow written method in Grade 4 and as fraction confusion in Grade 5. It is the cheapest gap to close and the most expensive to leave, and it closes in about a term of short regular sessions.

subjects.name: Fractions, decimals and percentages
subjects.description: The point where UAE primary maths stops being arithmetic. Equivalence is the actual obstacle, not procedure. This is the topic most likely to be flagged in a January benchmark score and the one most often still unresolved at MYP 1, where it immediately costs criterion marks.

subjects.name: Measurement, shape and data handling
subjects.description: Reading scales, converting units and interpreting a graph someone else drew. Data handling is where the PYP and the MYP overlap most directly, so time spent here in Grade 5 pays off inside the first term of MYP 1 rather than years later.

subjects.name: Science skills inside the units of inquiry
subjects.description: Fair testing, variables, recording and drawing a conclusion the evidence supports. PYP science is not a syllabus to be revised, so support is about method. The same method is what MYP criterion B and C ask for, under different names.

subjects.name: Research and note-making
subjects.description: Turning a broad interest into an answerable question, finding two sources that disagree, and taking notes that are not transcription. This is the work of the ten weeks before Exhibition presentation week and it is the part most often skipped in favour of making the slides look finished.

subjects.name: Speaking to an audience
subjects.description: Pace, eye contact, handling a question the student did not expect, and finishing inside the time allowed. Rehearsal with an adult who interrupts with questions is worth more than a dozen silent run-throughs, and three or four sessions in the fortnight before presentation week are usually enough.

subjects.name: Arabic as an additional language
subjects.description: Script, high-frequency vocabulary and the sentence patterns the ministry framework uses. Dubai private schools must timetable this regardless of the licensed curriculum, and the material comes from the approved framework, so support means practice and consolidation rather than a parallel course.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first language
subjects.description: A separate stream with separate expectations. KHDA requires schools to teach Arab and non-Arab groups in separate classes for Arabic as a first language, so a child's stream is set by the school and support must match the stream rather than the year group.

subjects.name: Islamic Education
subjects.description: Taught in Standard Arabic for the Arab stream and in the school's curriculum language for non-Arab students. Teachers of this subject need approval from KHDA to teach it, which is a useful question to ask of anyone offering primary support in the subject.

subjects.name: Self-management and the homework hour
subjects.description: Not a subject on any report, and frequently the actual problem. Where the bag is packed, when the homework happens, how long before a break - a fortnight of structure here often removes the need for subject support altogether, which is the honest answer in more primary cases than providers admit.

ib-pyp-home-tutor.regionsTitle: The emirates, read as calendars rather than as catchment areas
ib-pyp-home-tutor.regionsIntro: Delivery is identical across the country, because every lesson runs over live video. What changes by emirate is the regulator behind your child's school, the shape of the term dates, and the hour of the evening at which a primary child is still able to learn anything.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The deepest primary IB pool in the country, regulated by KHDA, which also publishes the mandatory-subject framework in the most detail. The competitive hour here is the one straight after the school bus, roughly 4pm to 5.30pm, and it books out first in term one rather than in the spring.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of children enrolled at their own school, so a primary tutor here is by design somebody from outside the classroom. Khalifa City and Yas commutes push sessions past 5pm.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a smaller set of primary IB schools and a longer drive between them. Online delivery removes the geography problem entirely: an Al Ain family gets the same reading specialist as a family on Reem Island, at the same hour, without anyone counting kilometres on a Tuesday evening.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves curricula, programmes and assessment methods as well as fees. Families commuting to Dubai schools often run the whole primary week on Sharjah term dates and Dubai traffic, which makes a fixed post-dinner slot more reliable than an after-school one.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here answer to the federal Ministry of Education rather than to an emirate authority. The practical consequence for a primary plan is a shorter list of local specialists and a stronger case for video delivery, particularly for Arabic as an additional language at the lower primary stages.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah, approves curricula and assessment methods rather than only inspecting. RAK primary families often sit outside any local tutoring market at all, which is exactly the gap a dated online plan fills.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under the federal Ministry of Education. The east coast has almost no primary IB tutoring market, and a request for a Grade 4 fractions specialist is not a request a local network can fill. Live video is not a compromise here; it is the only version that exists.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised federally by the Ministry of Education. Term dates follow the federal calendar, which matters during Ramadan, when the school day shortens and the only usable teaching block for a primary child moves to the hour after Iftar.

schoolClusters.note: These schools run the PYP at primary level and set their own Exhibition presentation weeks, their own benchmark windows and their own conference dates. Two schools three kilometres apart can differ by a month on all three, which is why a plan is built from your school's calendar rather than from a generic one.

ADEK-regulated primaries, where the professional-ethics position on staff tutoring their own students is the clearest in the country. Conference and report dates here tend to sit a fortnight off the Dubai pattern, so a family moving between the two emirates mid-year inherits a different calendar as well as a different regulator.

A short list, long distances between them, and in several cases the nearest alternative primary IB school is in another emirate. Families here are the ones for whom the travel arithmetic in the comparison table below decides the question on its own.

ib-pyp-home-tutor.modesIntro: Primary support works best when the shape of the booking matches the point in the year. Four shapes cover almost every primary request we see, and the difference between them is a calendar difference rather than a price difference.

modes.title: The term-time weekly anchor
modes.description: One or two short sessions a week, held at the same hour, running for a full term and reviewed against the next dated item - a reading check, a benchmark window, a report. This is the default for a reading or number gap at lower primary, because the skill being built needs frequency rather than duration and a primary child's attention does not survive a long evening hour.
bullets: Twenty-five to forty-five minutes, matched to the child's age rather than to a standard hour
Same slot each week so it survives the school run and bedtime
Reviewed at the next dated school assessment, not at a random four-week mark
Short written note to the parent after each session, not a monthly report

modes.title: A dated block before Exhibition week
modes.description: A fixed number of sessions counted backwards from your school's Exhibition presentation date, starting at roughly ten weeks out and ending with rehearsal in the final fortnight. The sequence is research question, sources, notes, structure, then delivery. Booked this way the block has a finish line, which is the main reason primary families do not drift into paying for support that has stopped having a purpose.
bullets: Ten weeks out: narrowing the question into something answerable
Six weeks out: two sources that disagree, and notes that are not transcription
Three weeks out: structure, and cutting what does not answer the question
Final fortnight: rehearsal with interruptions and a timed run

modes.title: Holiday blocks: winter, spring and summer
modes.description: Intensive short blocks in the breaks, when the school is not setting work and the child is not tired. The winter fortnight and the first two weeks of the summer are the two most productive windows in the UAE primary year for closing a reading or number gap, because sessions can run in the morning rather than at the end of a school day.
bullets: Morning slots, which no term-time plan can offer a primary child
Daily or alternate-day frequency for two to three weeks
Best used for automaticity work - recall, fluency, written method
Finishes before term restarts, so it does not become an open-ended commitment

modes.title: The exit bridge into MYP 1
modes.description: A short run of sessions across the final term of Grade 5 and the first weeks of MYP 1, aimed at the one real change: work starts being marked against criteria out of eight instead of described against descriptors. Students who understand what criterion B is asking for before the first graded task lose far less time in term one of MYP 1.

sections.heading: A PYP child has no exam date, and that is the whole planning problem
paragraphs: Search volume for an IB PYP home tutor in the UAE is driven almost entirely by two moments: a report landing, and the Exhibition appearing on a school newsletter. Neither of those is a good moment to start. By the time a report says a child is working towards expectations, the term that produced the judgement is already over, and by the time Exhibition week is on a newsletter the inquiry is usually half-built. The Primary Years Programme has no external examination, no entry deadline and no results day, so the planning signals a secondary parent takes for granted are simply absent.

What exists instead is a thin set of dated items, most of which schools publish but parents rarely collect in one place. Early Years has two parent conferences and a portfolio. Lower primary adds a reading assessment, usually sat in the first weeks of term one and again before the mid-year report. Middle primary adds a standardised benchmark window, commonly in January. The exit year adds the one date that genuinely cannot move, Exhibition presentation week, which the school sets rather than the IB.

Collecting those dates is a ten-minute job and it changes what support costs, because it converts an open-ended worry into a finite block. A reading gap identified against a September assessment can be worked on for a term and re-measured in January against the same instrument. A fractions gap flagged by a January benchmark has a full second term in front of it. An Exhibition has ten usable weeks before presentation if the question is settled early, and two if it is not. None of that is visible from a report comment on its own.

The table below is the version of the PYP that a parent can actually plan against: what each year produces, the one item in it that carries a date, and the thing paid hours are usefully spent on in that year. It is deliberately not a list of subjects. At primary level the year matters more than the subject, because the same reading gap costs about a term of short sessions in Grade 2 and most of a school year in Grade 5.

sections.heading: The UAE primary year counted in weeks that can actually be taught
paragraphs: A UAE school year looks like forty weeks on paper and behaves like rather fewer. Term one opens in late August or early September and the first fortnight is settling rather than teaching. A fortnight disappears around the winter break. Ramadan shortens the school day for several weeks, and the days either side of Eid and of National Day are effectively gone. Add the examination and assessment weeks the school itself runs and the number of weeks in which a primary child can absorb new work steadily sits closer to thirty.

That arithmetic matters because primary gaps close by repetition, not by intensity. A child who needs two short sessions a week for a term needs about twenty-four of them. There are only two or three places in a UAE year where twenty-four consecutive useful weeks exist, and all of them start in September or early January. A plan that starts in April is not a smaller version of the same plan; it is a different plan, with different aims, and it should be sold as such.

The second thing the arithmetic changes is pricing behaviour. Primary demand in the Emirates peaks twice - the fortnight after term one reports and the month before Exhibition week - and both peaks sit in the parts of the year with the fewest usable weeks left. Families who book in September buy the same number of hours into a far better calendar. Nothing about the hourly rate changes; the weeks do.

Schools licensed on an April-start academic year, of which the Emirates has a number, invert the whole table. Their long teaching block runs from April through the summer, their mid-year sits in the autumn, and KHDA's own mandatory-subject requirements were set to apply from the start of the 2025-26 academic year, which for those schools meant April 2026. If your child's school starts in April, read every window below shifted by roughly seven months.

sections.heading: The Exhibition, read backwards from presentation week
paragraphs: The PYP Exhibition is the only hard deadline in the Primary Years Programme and it is the one piece of primary work most parents misjudge. The misjudgement is consistent: families treat it as a presentation, and so they ask for help in the fortnight before presentation week, when the only thing left to change is the slides. The Exhibition is a piece of research. The marks that exist in it, and more importantly the learning in it, are won eight to ten weeks earlier, at the point where a vague interest becomes an answerable question.

Each school sets its own presentation week and its own internal checkpoints, and the IB sets neither. That is why the first thing to do in September of the exit year, not in February, is ask the PYP coordinator for the presentation date and the school's internal milestone dates. With that date in hand the whole block becomes countable, and a parent can see immediately whether the ten useful weeks fall before or across Ramadan - in several years of the cycle they fall across it, which is the single biggest practical constraint on Exhibition planning in the Emirates.

The boundary question matters more here than anywhere else in primary school, because the Exhibition is the first piece of work a child owns outright. A tutor may teach research method, ask questions that expose a weak argument, model note-making on a different topic, and rehearse the delivery. A tutor may not choose the question, find the sources, write the notes, structure the argument or edit the student's text into something the student could not have written. That line is not a formality; it is the habit that keeps the same child out of trouble six years later when an Internal Assessment carries real marks.

Read backwards, the block has a natural shape, and the table below is the version we work to. The weeks are approximate because schools differ, but the order does not change: question, sources, notes, structure, delivery. Families who start at week ten rarely need the fortnight of emergency sessions. Families who start at week two almost always do, and there is a limit to what those sessions can honestly achieve.
