ib-revision-classes.programmesIntro: Revision means a different exercise in each IB programme, because each one assesses differently. The Diploma ends in external papers and closed internal components. The MYP ends in on-screen eAssessment or in school-moderated work. The Career-related Programme carries a Diploma course load beside a separate professional qualification. The Primary Years Programme has nothing to revise at all, which is worth saying out loud.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the extended essay and CAS. The written papers at the end of DP2 carry most of each subject grade, and the internally assessed component in each subject is closed long before study leave. Revision at Diploma level therefore splits cleanly: anything still open is coachable, anything submitted is a sunk mark that should stop consuming hours. The Higher Level third paper, which Standard Level candidates never sit, is the single most under-revised component in the programme.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE the Diploma sits inside a two-year school calendar that breaks for a long Gulf summer, Eid holidays that shift annually and Ramadan, which usually lands in the DP2 revision term. Dubai's private sector taught 17 different curricula to 387,441 pupils across 227 schools in 2024-25 and the International Baccalaureate accounted for seven per cent of that enrolment, so a DP cohort in a UAE school is often small enough that one teacher covers both levels of a subject. That is where a specialist revision hour earns its place.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: Five years of interdisciplinary teaching assessed against four criteria per subject, each carrying its own achievement levels. MYP 5 candidates in many schools sit on-screen eAssessment, which rewards reading the task command precisely rather than reproducing content. Revision here is mostly technique and criterion literacy: a student who can recite the content and still scores in the middle band is almost always misreading what the criterion asks for. Personal Project marks are internally assessed and close at the school's own deadline.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools differ widely on whether MYP 5 leads to eAssessment, to a school-awarded certificate, or sideways into Cambridge or Pearson International GCSE for the final two years. That choice decides what a Year 11 revision plan looks like, and it is a question for your child's coordinator rather than for a tutor. Families moving from MYP into the Diploma in the same school usually find the gap is in mathematical fluency and in writing under time, not in subject knowledge.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: Two or more Diploma courses taken alongside a career-related study, a reflective project, a language development strand and personal and professional skills. CP candidates sit the same external papers as Diploma candidates in their DP subjects, so the revision mechanics for those courses are identical. The reflective project is internally assessed and has a school deadline, which means it drops out of a revision plan the moment it is handed in.
programmes.countryNote: A small number of UAE schools run the CP, usually alongside a business, hospitality or engineering partner qualification. The practical effect on revision is a compressed timetable: the career-related study takes timetabled hours that a full Diploma candidate spends on a sixth subject, so the DP papers a CP candidate does sit have to be revised in fewer available weeks. Counting those weeks honestly at the start of DP2 is the whole exercise.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP has no external examinations and no revision in the sense this page uses the word. What parents searching for revision classes at this stage usually want is either a diagnosed gap closed before it compounds, or preparation for an entrance assessment at a selective secondary school. Both are real pieces of work and neither is revision. Calling them by their proper names stops families buying exam technique for a nine-year-old who needs number fluency.
programmes.countryNote: In UAE schools the PYP exhibition in the final primary year is a presentation and inquiry exercise, not an examination, and coaching it to a script defeats its purpose. The genuinely useful early intervention for a UAE primary family is usually Arabic, because the mandatory subject stream runs from the start of schooling and a gap there follows a child into secondary school with its own examined requirements attached.

ib-revision-classes.subjectsIntro: IB DP revision classes have subject-specific priorities, and the differences are concrete rather than a matter of style. Below is what the final three passes should look like in the subjects UAE families book most, with the component where marks most often leak. Confirm every assessment detail against the subject guide your child's cohort is actually following, because guides change between cohorts.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Revision is proof technique, algebraic fluency and calculator discipline. Higher Level candidates lose marks in proof by induction, complex numbers and the harder calculus questions, almost always through setting out rather than through ignorance. The exploration is internally assessed and closes at the school deadline, so after that date every hour belongs to the papers.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistical tests, modelling and graphical calculator technology carry the paper. The commonest leak is reporting a statistical result without interpreting it in context, which costs the final mark on a long question repeatedly. Revision here is best done as whole questions rather than topic drills, because the paper rewards reading a context correctly before any mathematics starts.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Define-and-derive questions are recoverable in weeks; graph and uncertainty work takes longer. Revision should separate the recall load from the technique load, then attack uncertainties, significant figures and unit algebra as their own exercise. Higher Level candidates who skip the extension topics in revision are skipping the paper where unfamiliar material is deliberately placed.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, equilibrium and energetics reward structured recall; data-based questions reward technique. The repeated pattern on marked scripts is a correct mechanism drawn without curly arrows placed properly, which scores nothing. Revision should include at least one session purely on drawing conventions, because the marks are allocated to them explicitly.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content volume makes retrieval practice unavoidable; reading notes does not work in this subject at all. Command terms decide the mark here more than in any other science, as outline, explain and evaluate carry different structural demands on the same content. Diagram labelling and data interpretation are the two fastest places to recover marks late.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagrams first, then evaluation. A correctly drawn and fully labelled diagram carries marks on its own, and most candidates arrive at revision drawing from memory with axes unlabelled. Higher Level calculation work is a separate exercise and is usually under-practised. Real-world examples should be chosen and rehearsed before study leave rather than improvised in the hall.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Tool application and the case study decide the grade. Revision is best spent rehearsing frameworks against unfamiliar scenarios rather than memorising definitions, since the paper gives the context and asks for judgement. Candidates lose the evaluation marks by describing both sides without reaching a supported conclusion, which is a structural fix rather than a knowledge one.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Unseen analysis improves with timed practice on texts the student has never met, which is the one exercise most candidates avoid. Revision should build a reusable approach to an unseen text and a bank of comparative points across studied works. The Higher Level essay is internally assessed and closes at the school deadline, taking its weighting with it.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: Source skills and essay structure are both trainable in the final two passes; content breadth is not, which is why the coverage audit has to happen early. Revision essays should be planned in ten minutes and written in thirty-five to match paper timing. The Higher Level regional option paper rewards narrow, deep preparation over broad reading.

subjects.name: Psychology
subjects.description: Named studies with dates, methods and findings are the currency, and a vague recollection of a study earns almost nothing. Revision should produce a study bank the candidate can reproduce from a blank page, then practise selecting from it under a question stem. Research methods and ethical considerations are the marks most often left on the table.

ib-revision-classes.regionsTitle: Revision term emirate by emirate, and the authority behind each one
ib-revision-classes.regionsIntro: Which authority answers for your child's school changes the published inspection evidence you can read, the fee framework the school works inside and sometimes the holiday pattern your revision plan has to fit. All seven emirates are covered below. Sessions are delivered online to all of them on Gulf Standard Time, so an address changes the calendar rather than the availability.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Schools are overseen by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate and publishes inspection reports families can read before buying any tutoring. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for 2026-27. Mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies sit in every timetable here.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and is named by almost no competitor page in this market. Its professional-ethics rules for school staff have been reported as barring teachers from paid private tutoring of pupils enrolled at their own school, so a revision tutor should be someone outside that relationship.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Al Ain schools fall under ADEK alongside the capital, though the school-run distances and the smaller Diploma cohorts change the practical picture. A subject offered to a handful of candidates may be taught by one teacher across both levels, which is the situation where a Higher Level revision specialist makes the clearest difference.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is curriculum and fee approval rather than inspection alone, so the published SPEA framework is worth reading before assuming a school's exam-term support matches a Dubai neighbour's.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools in Ajman are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which plays a supervisory role across Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Families here often commute to Sharjah or Dubai schools, which means a revision session has to clear a long evening return before it can start on Gulf Standard Time.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. The emirate returns effectively no mentions across the competitor pages researched for this market, which is a gap rather than a signal that no Diploma candidates live here.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Fujairah's private schools sit under the Ministry of Education's supervision. The east-coast location makes a centre-based revision class a genuine logistical problem rather than an inconvenience, and it is the clearest case in the country for a Higher Level subject specialist delivered over live video instead of a local availability search.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised by the Ministry of Education, Umm Al Quwain has the smallest private-school population of the seven emirates. A family looking for Diploma revision in a less common subject will not find a local match at any price, which is precisely the problem online one-to-one delivery was built to solve.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai carries the largest Diploma cohort in the country, spread across schools that run the programme alongside a British or American primary phase. Revision patterns differ by school: some run full mock weeks in January, others two separate sitting windows, and a few publish study-leave dates only in the spring term.

Capital-region Diploma cohorts are smaller per school than Dubai's, and subject combinations are correspondingly narrower. That raises the chance that a Higher Level option is taught by a single teacher, and lowers the chance of finding a second opinion on a marked script inside the building.

Diploma provision thins out north of Dubai, and curricula vary sharply between schools in the same emirate. Check the regulator's own school listing for what a school is currently licensed to teach before planning a revision year around an assumption about its programme.

ib-revision-classes.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named here as context for the UAE Diploma and International GCSE ecosystem; no affiliation, endorsement or relationship with any school or school group is implied, and curriculum details should be verified against the school and its regulator.
ib-revision-classes.modesIntro: Online IB revision classes are bought in four shapes, and they suit different points in the calendar. All four run one to one over live video, so an IB revision timetable can be built around the school day rather than around a tutor's route across the city. Gulf Standard Time revision sessions start at the hour you choose, with marking returned in between. The right shape depends on how many weeks are left and on whether the gap is content, technique or pacing.

modes.title: Weekly revision cycle through DP2
modes.description: One or two sessions a week from September, running the four passes in order against a dated plan. This is the cheapest version of revision per mark recovered, because it uses the whole year rather than the last six weeks, and it lets the repair pass happen while school is still teaching the content. It also survives Ramadan and travel better than a block, since a missed week is a week rather than a third of the purchase.
bullets: Coverage audit in the first fortnight, written down in syllabus order
One timed component marked every two to three weeks
Plan re-dated after the January mocks rather than restarted
Session times move for Ramadan and Eid by arrangement

modes.title: A dated block before a session
modes.description: A fixed number of hours bought for a known date: a mock window, study leave, or a November re-sit. The block is quoted in hours and dates before anything is paid, and it ends with a written handover rather than drifting into a subscription. Blocks work when the content has been taught once and the problem is retrieval and pacing. They do not work as a substitute for teaching that never happened.
bullets: Scoped in hours, dates, subject and level before payment
A named number of full timed papers, marked by the tutor
Cancellation notice stated on both sides
Ends with a written handover and a decision point

modes.title: Per-paper clinic
modes.description: A short run of sessions aimed at one component: Higher Level Paper 3, an unseen analysis paper, a data-based paper, or source-skills work. Clinics suit candidates whose overall grade is fine but who lose the same marks on the same component every sitting. Two to four hours on the structural fault usually moves more than ten hours of general revision, because the fault is structural rather than informational.
bullets: Starts from a marked script, not from a topic list
One component, one error pattern, one fix at a time
Useful immediately after mocks, when the evidence is fresh
Often the cheapest intervention that changes a grade

modes.title: Exam-fortnight standby
modes.description: Short, scheduled sessions inside the examination window itself, placed in the gaps between papers. The job is narrow: a timing plan, a structure drill, one section of the next paper, then stop. Standby sessions are deliberately short because the candidate's sleep is worth more than the hour, and they are scheduled around the actual timetable rather than at a fixed weekly slot.
bullets: Thirty to sixty minutes, placed against the real paper timetable
No post-mortems on papers already sat

Scheduled on Gulf Standard Time, including early mornings

sections.heading: What the UAE market sells under the words IB revision classes
paragraphs: Five different products are advertised as IB revision classes in this market, and they diagnose different things. A school revision session re-teaches the syllabus at class pace. A tuition-centre group class works on errors common to a cohort. A holiday camp covers content in volume. One-to-one work isolates one candidate's lost marks. Unsupervised past-paper practice at home tests whether content can be retrieved at all. Only the last two produce evidence about your child specifically, and only one of them produces a second opinion on a script.

The distinction matters because families usually buy the cheapest product and then conclude that revision does not work. A group class of nine students cannot name why your child drops the final mark on a long Economics question, because that mark is lost in a way specific to how that candidate writes. Equally, one-to-one hours spent re-teaching content that a school revision session covers adequately are hours bought at four times the necessary rate. The products are complements, and the order in which they are used decides whether the spend was sensible.

Read the table below as a purchasing order rather than a ranking. A candidate three topics behind should be in the school sessions and working through past papers alone before any paid hour is bought, because paid hours are wasted on a gap the student has not yet mapped. A candidate whose content is secure and whose marks are stuck has the opposite problem: the group formats have nothing left to tell them, and the only remaining diagnostic is a marked script read by a specialist.

sections.heading: Four passes over one syllabus, and the window each one belongs in
paragraphs: A syllabus has to be crossed four times before a final paper, and each crossing does a different job. The first pass is an audit: the candidate marks every subtopic as secure, shaky or never properly taught, in the syllabus document's own order. This takes two or three hours per subject and it is the step almost everyone skips, which is why so many revision plans are built on a guess about where the gaps are. A gap list in syllabus order is the only honest input to everything that follows.

The second pass repairs. It runs while school is still teaching, which is the point: a topic re-learned in November has six months of incidental reinforcement ahead of it, and the same topic re-learned in April has none. The third pass is retrieval, and IB mock exam revision is where it starts, because mock scripts are the best diagnostic material a family will ever own for free. Retrieval means blank-page recall and question sets, not reading. The fourth pass is rehearsal: whole papers, timed, in paper order, marked by somebody who is not the candidate.

The hour counts in the table are per subject and assume the content was taught once, competently, the first time. They are deliberately unflattering. Four passes across three Higher Level and three Standard Level subjects is a substantial commitment, which is exactly why the audit pass exists: it is what lets a family spend the repair and retrieval hours on four subtopics instead of across a whole syllabus. Families who start in March can still run passes three and four properly, and should be told plainly that pass two has gone.

sections.heading: The hour audit: where revision time actually comes from in a UAE school week
paragraphs: Every revision plan is a claim about hours that exist. Most plans are built by asking how many hours the work needs, which produces a number nobody can supply. The useful question runs the other way: how many hours are genuinely unclaimed in a UAE Diploma student's week, and what has to go to create more. The audit below is the one worth doing on paper with your child before any tutoring is booked, because it usually settles the argument about whether the plan is ambitious or fictional.

Two claims on the week are routinely left out. The mandatory UAE subject stream is the first: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies run in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA calculates the required instructional time in 40-minute lesson units, advising that no mandatory subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. Those lessons are examined in their own right, so they are not spare capacity. The second omission is CAS and service, which is logged across eighteen months and which students habitually leave until the term they can least afford it.

The honest bottom line in most UAE households is six to ten hours a week genuinely available for revision in DP2, including weekends. That is the budget. A plan requiring twenty is not a stretch target, it is a plan that will fail in week three and take the family's confidence with it. Front-loading CAS into DP1, negotiating homework expectations with the school in the final term, and moving a weekly session to a Friday morning are the three levers that actually create time. Buying more hours is not one of them.

sections.heading: Revision that leaves evidence, and revision that leaves a feeling
paragraphs: The most common complaint in a diagnostic lesson is that a candidate revises for hours and the grade does not move. Almost always the hours were real and the activity was wrong. Re-reading notes and re-watching lessons produce recognition, which feels like knowledge and is not tested by any paper. Recall, structure and pacing are tested, and those three are trained only by exercises that produce something a third party can mark. The test of a revision activity is simple: at the end of it, is there an artefact somebody else can read?

That question sorts the list quickly. A blank-page topic dump produces a page whose holes are the week's syllabus. A set of topic questions with the answers hidden produces a marked set and an error pattern. Timed past paper practice produces a script. Re-reading a chapter produces nothing, and the four hours spent on it are gone with no residue to plan against. Candidates gravitate towards the activities that produce nothing precisely because those activities cannot fail, which is the whole problem with them.

Marking is the step families most often leave out, and it is the one that converts practice into revision. A candidate self-marking against a mark scheme reliably awards marks for intention rather than for what is written, because they can see what they meant. Somebody else reading the same script sees only the words on the page, which is exactly what an examiner sees. That is why one-to-one revision with marking returned between sessions does different work from the same number of unsupervised hours, and why an unmarked past paper is practice rather than revision.

sections.heading: Where a revision hour still pays, component by component
paragraphs: Revision hours should follow the marks that are still movable, and in the Diploma a significant share of each subject grade stops being movable long before study leave. The internally assessed component in the sciences and in mathematics carries 20 per cent of the subject grade under the current guides, and the moment the school's internal deadline passes that fifth of the grade is fixed. Theory of Knowledge and the extended essay together contribute up to three points on the 45-point total, assessed against published criteria, and both close on school dates in the spring.

What that means for a plan is unglamorous and specific. For most DP2 candidates reading this in the second half of the year, between a fifth and a quarter of each subject grade is already banked, and the revision budget should be reallocated to the written papers accordingly. Families who keep paying for extended essay sessions after submission are buying nothing. Families who have not yet reached the school deadline should be spending there first, because an open internal component is the highest-yield hour available and it will never be available again.

Among the written papers, the Higher Level third paper is the most consistently under-revised component in the programme. It exists only at Higher Level, it usually presents unfamiliar material or extension content, and it is the paper candidates are least likely to have sat under timed conditions before the real one. Every weighting in the table below should be confirmed against the subject guide your child's cohort follows, because the IB revises guides between cohorts and a figure that was right for last year's candidates is a liability for this year's.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and National Day: the holes every UAE revision calendar has
paragraphs: A revision plan drawn on a European school calendar will be wrong by several weeks in the Gulf. Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier each Gregorian year, and for the current run of years it falls inside the Diploma revision term. During Ramadan, UAE school days shorten, evenings reorganise around Iftar, and a late-afternoon tuition slot that worked in January becomes the worst possible hour. The schools adjust their timetables and families adjust their routines; a revision plan that does not adjust simply stops running, usually without anyone deciding to stop it.

The workable pattern is to move sessions rather than cancel them. A Ramadan revision schedule that places work in the late morning at weekends and after Iftar on school nights keeps continuity through the month, and continuity is what pass three depends on. Eid al-Fitr then removes several consecutive days, often at short notice, because the holiday is confirmed close to the date. National Day at the start of December and the long Gulf summer take their own blocks. Put all of them on the calendar in September, before they become surprises.

There is a scheduling advantage here that is specific to online delivery. A session booked for a fixed slot at a tuition centre cannot move to post-Iftar at two days' notice, and a tutor crossing Dubai or Abu Dhabi in traffic cannot either. One-to-one sessions over live video can be re-timed within the week, which in practice is the difference between a plan that survives Ramadan and one that resumes in April having lost the retrieval pass altogether. The same flexibility covers travel, which Gulf families do a great deal of.
bullets: Mark Ramadan, Eid, National Day and the summer break on the plan in September
Move sessions to late morning at weekends and post-Iftar on school nights
Expect Eid dates to be confirmed close to the day
Continuity through Ramadan is what protects the retrieval pass

sections.heading: Revising inside the exam fortnight, between one paper and the next
paragraphs: The examination window is a distinct piece of the calendar with its own rules, and almost nothing published for UAE families covers it. Papers in a subject are often a day or two apart, different subjects are separated by gaps of anything from an evening to nine days, and candidates are tired in a way they have not been before. Revision in this window is not the same activity as revision in March. It is narrow, short and almost entirely about structure, timing and sleep.

Two mistakes dominate. The first is the post-mortem: a candidate comes out of Paper 1, reconstructs their answers with classmates on a group chat, and spends the evening before Paper 2 convinced of a mark nobody can actually calculate. The paper is finished and unchangeable, and the only useful information it carries is how the timing felt. The second mistake is treating a long gap as a holiday, then panicking on day seven. A four-to-nine-day gap before a late subject is enough time for a proper retrieval pass, run from the error log, at a sane two hours a day.

The planning unit inside this fortnight is the individual paper rather than the week. Write the real timetable on one page, mark every gap, and decide in advance what each gap is for. Standby sessions in this window are deliberately short, because an extra hour bought at the cost of sleep is a bad trade in a measurable way. In the final seventy-two hours before any paper, the only work worth doing is structure drills, a timing plan and equipment checks.

sections.heading: Predicted papers, leaked papers and the line a revision class will not cross
paragraphs: Revision is where academic honesty questions get asked most often, because the material in play is examination material. The rules are clear and worth stating in a family's own terms. Released past papers and published mark schemes are legitimate revision material, obtained through the school's own access to the board's store or from your child's teacher. They are also the board's copyright, which is why this page cites them and links out rather than hosting anything. A tutor who offers a library of downloads is offering a copyright problem.

Two things sold into this market are not legitimate at all. The first is the predicted paper, marketed before each session as a close approximation of what will be asked. Nobody outside the board knows the content of an unsat paper, and teaching a guessed paper as though it were known narrows a candidate's preparation for no reason. The second is material circulating before its timetabled sitting, which happens occasionally and which must be refused and reported to the coordinator. Using it puts the candidate's diploma at risk, not the seller's.

On internally assessed work the boundary is the same one stated throughout this site. A tutor asks questions, teaches technique, explains a criterion, points at a weakness and marks a practice attempt. The sentences, the data and the analytical choices in any submitted component are the candidate's own, and a tutor supplying them would be creating a malpractice case against the student. That boundary is also the most useful thing a parent can check when comparing providers in this market, because several in this SERP do not hold it.

sections.heading: What IB revision classes cost across the UAE market
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages researched for this market publish no price at all, and two of those that do quote in US dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. The table below collects the AED figures providers in this market actually publish, with the source and the date each was read. They are market rates, not IB Gram prices. Our own figure comes from a scoped quote after a diagnostic lesson, because an hourly rate quoted before anyone has seen a marked script is a number without content.

Read the ranges as a function of what is included rather than of quality. An hour at the bottom of the band is an hour of talking: no marking between sessions, no specialist at Higher Level, often a tutor one or two years ahead of the student. An hour in the specialist band usually includes marked work returned between sessions, which is the component that makes revision work. The figures for a tutor travelling to a UAE address carry the travel inside the hourly rate, and a 90-minute round trip across Dubai at five o'clock is paid for whether it is itemised or not.

For budgeting purposes, cost per recovered grade is the only number worth comparing, and it cannot be read off an hourly rate. Twelve well-placed hours on a single structural fault frequently move a component more than forty hours of general revision at half the rate. Monthly packages seen in this market run at around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions. Check what happens to unused sessions before buying any package, because that term varies and is rarely prominent.

sections.heading: A group revision class against one-to-one revision over live video
paragraphs: The honest comparison is not online against in-person. It is an hour pitched at a room against an hour pitched at one candidate's error log, and the format follows from that. A group revision class is a reasonable purchase during pass two, when several students genuinely need the same content re-covered. It is a poor purchase during pass three and four, when the remaining marks are lost in ways that differ from student to student and an hour aimed at the median teaches nobody their own mistakes.

IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are a service we run only in India. For revision that is a straightforward trade rather than a limitation. A candidate in Al Ain who needs Higher Level Chemistry Paper 3 technique gets a specialist in that paper instead of the best available tutor within a 25-minute drive, scripts are marked between sessions rather than skimmed in the room, and the session can move to post-Iftar during Ramadan or to seven in the morning during study leave. The comparison table sets out what actually differs.

Where a group format wins, it wins on price per student and on the usefulness of hearing other candidates' questions. Those are real advantages and worth paying for at the right point in the calendar. What a group cannot do is read one script closely, and reading one script closely is the entire content of the last two passes. Most families get the best result from both: school and centre sessions for coverage, and a small number of one-to-one hours placed where the evidence says the marks are going.

sections.heading: What to ask your child's school in revision term, and who answers for it
paragraphs: Most of the information a revision plan needs is held by the school and given freely when asked precisely. Parents tend to ask how their child is getting on, which produces an adjective. The questions below produce dates and documents. Put them in one email to the right person: the IB coordinator owns assessment deadlines and sessions, the exams officer owns entries, and the head of secondary owns study leave and what support runs during it.

Which authority answers for the school is worth knowing too, because it decides what independent evidence exists. KHDA oversees private education in Dubai. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah and, with Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Published inspection reports are the only independent read on teaching your fees already buy.

One answer changes a plan more than any other: whether your child is actually entered, and for which session. An entry is an administrative act with a deadline months ahead of the paper, and the boards publish those deadlines series by series. In the UAE there are two Cambridge sittings to be entered for, June and November, and the February and March sitting that Cambridge offers to India is not one of them, so a revision runway here is counted back either from the June papers or from the November ones. Pearson's Edexcel International GCSE works the same way and its dates are concrete: the November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, which puts the serious revision block in the weeks either side of the autumn half-term rather than in the spring. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and warns that the correct zone timetable must be used, so the first revision session should start with the statement of entry on the table rather than with a date from a search result. For IB session dates, ask the coordinator and check ibo.org; this page publishes none.

sections.heading: After results: enquiries, equivalency and the re-sit decision
paragraphs: The calendar does not end at the last paper. Results arrive, and a short window follows in which three decisions are live: whether to ask the school to request a review of a mark through the board's own process, whether to re-sit a component in the next session, and whether a university offer can be renegotiated. All three run on the board's published timetable through the school, not through a tutor, and the school's coordinator or exams officer is the only person who can file any of them. Diarise the deadlines the day results land.

A separate piece of paperwork opens at the same time for families who intend to study in the UAE. Ministry of Education equivalency assesses a school certificate against the national framework, and the requirements differ by curriculum. On the British track, as reported in July 2026, candidates must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or International GCSE certificates at no lower than grade E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level. One ranking competitor publishes a six-subject requirement, which is wrong.

On the American track the same reporting sets English proficiency at a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with at least 450 in SAT Mathematics. No verified IB points threshold exists for publication here, so confirm the IB route on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate before planning around a number. Equivalency is a process the ministry runs; IB Gram neither performs it nor influences it, and no tutoring is required for it.

process.title: Send the dates before you send the subjects
process.description: Start with the calendar. A mock week, the school's internal deadlines, study leave and the session your child is entered for are enough to begin. Add the subjects, the levels and the last reported grade. Say what the family's ceiling on spend is, because that figure is what makes the difference between a plan on paper and a plan that gets bought.

process.title: One free diagnostic lesson, on a marked script
process.description: Every student gets one free first lesson, one per student, booked through the site. Bring a marked mock paper if there is one. The tutor reads it, asks the candidate to attempt something live, and forms a view on what the lost marks are actually caused by. Families who decide against going further owe nothing after it.

process.title: A written plan in passes and dates
process.description: What comes back is a plan, not a rate: which pass the candidate is in, which subtopics the audit flagged, how many hours each pass needs, how many full timed papers are included and who marks them. If the honest answer is that school sessions and unsupervised past papers would do the job for now, the plan says that instead.

process.title: Run it on Gulf Standard Time, with marking in between
process.description: Sessions are one to one over live video, scheduled around the school day rather than around a tutor's route across the city. Marked work goes back between sessions with the lost marks named. Timings move for Ramadan, Eid, National Day and travel by arrangement, which is how a plan survives a Gulf academic year instead of pausing in March.

process.title: Re-date the plan after the mocks, then stop on time
process.description: Mock scripts are the best evidence a plan will get, so the plan is re-dated against them rather than restarted. After the final paper the arrangement ends with a short written handover: what moved, what did not, and what is still open for a re-sit decision. Carrying on into the next term is a fresh decision, made on that evidence.

whyPoints.title: A plan with dates on it
whyPoints.description: Revision is a sequence with windows, so the deliverable is a dated plan rather than a weekly slot. Each pass has a purpose, an hour count and an end. That makes the spend legible: a family can see what they bought, when it finishes, and what evidence will show whether it worked.

whyPoints.title: Specialist match rather than local availability
whyPoints.description: Online delivery decouples the choice of tutor from the drive time. A candidate in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain who needs a Higher Level third-paper specialist gets one, which is not a search a local availability filter can satisfy anywhere north of Dubai. The hour is matched to the component, not to the postcode.

whyPoints.title: Marked work instead of progress adjectives
whyPoints.description: Scripts are marked between sessions and the lost marks are named with a cause attached, because marking is the step that converts practice into revision. A parent gets an error log rather than a reassurance, and the next session's content is visibly derived from it. That is also what makes it obvious when a plan is not working.

whyPoints.title: Numbers with a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page carries the provider that published it and the month it was read, including the ranges that sit below what a specialist hour costs. Our own number comes after a diagnostic, not before. Market context, regulator facts and board deadlines are cited so a parent can check them rather than take them on trust.

whyPoints.title: A boundary on assessed work that does not move
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, question, mark and coach. The sentences, data and analytical decisions in any assessed component belong to the candidate. We state the line because the alternative is a malpractice case against a student, and because several providers in this market are selling the thing on the wrong side of it.

whyPoints.title: Coverage told honestly, including the gaps
whyPoints.description: Some subject and level combinations have no UAE-based specialist free at a workable Gulf Standard Time hour. When that happens we say so and offer a specialist in another time zone at the same standard, or say that we cannot cover it this term. Discovering a coverage gap in week three is worse than hearing about it in week zero.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the IB exams should revision classes start?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families start, and the reason is structural rather than motivational. The repair pass has to run while school is still teaching the content, which puts it nine to five months out. The retrieval pass starts from the mock scripts, so it belongs in the two to five months before the session. The rehearsal pass needs the final six weeks and study leave. A family starting in March can still run retrieval and rehearsal properly and should be told plainly that the repair window has closed, which changes what the hours can achieve.

faqs.question: What should one IB revision class actually contain?
faqs.answer: A revision session should start from evidence and end with an artefact. The evidence is usually a marked script or a question set the candidate attempted beforehand. The hour is then spent on the error pattern it reveals, with the tutor teaching the technique the marks were lost on and the candidate attempting it live. It ends with named work to do before the next session, and that work comes back marked. A session that consists of a tutor explaining a topic while the student listens is a lesson, not revision, and should be priced and timetabled as one.

faqs.question: My child revises for hours and the grade will not move. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Almost always the hours are real and the activity is wrong. Re-reading notes and re-watching lessons build recognition, which feels like knowledge and is not what any paper tests. Papers test recall, structure and pacing, and those are trained only by exercises that leave something a third party can mark: a blank-page topic dump, a question set with the answers hidden, a full timed paper. The second common fault is self-marking, which awards credit for what the candidate meant rather than for what they wrote. Switch the activity and have somebody else mark it.

faqs.question: Is a weekly revision cycle better than an intensive block before the papers?
faqs.answer: A weekly cycle through DP2 recovers more marks per dirham, because it uses the repair window while school is still teaching and it survives Ramadan, travel and illness without losing a third of the purchase. A block is the right instrument when the content has been taught once and the problem is retrieval and pacing, or when a specific date is driving the spend, such as a mock week or a November re-sit. Blocks do not substitute for teaching that never happened, and a provider quoting a block before anyone has read a marked script is quoting a number without content.

faqs.question: Can revision classes still help if my child has not finished the syllabus?
faqs.answer: Yes, but the work is repair rather than revision and should be named accordingly. The first step is the coverage audit: the candidate marks every subtopic in the syllabus document as secure, shaky or never properly taught. That list is what makes the remaining hours affordable, because it concentrates them on four or five subtopics instead of spreading them across a whole course. Starting timed full papers before the gaps are closed wastes both the paper and the hour, since the script will be dominated by content the candidate has not met rather than by technique faults.

faqs.question: How many past papers should a candidate sit before the first exam?
faqs.answer: The number matters less than the condition they are sat in. Untimed practice with notes open, timed practice with the book closed, and timed practice in paper order on consecutive days are three different exercises that train different things. A workable pattern is topic question sets through the retrieval pass, then four to six full papers per subject under timed conditions in the final six weeks, each marked by somebody other than the candidate. Sitting a dozen papers nobody marks produces a dozen scripts and no information, which is the commonest waste of the final month.

faqs.question: Can a revision tutor tell us which topics will be on the paper?
faqs.answer: No, and anyone who implies otherwise should be treated with real scepticism. Nobody outside the board knows the content of an unsat paper. Predicted papers sold before each session are guesswork, and teaching them as though the questions were known narrows a candidate's preparation for no benefit. If material from a paper circulates before its timetabled sitting, it must be refused and reported to the IB coordinator, because using it puts the candidate's diploma at risk. What a tutor can legitimately do is teach the assessment structure and the command terms, which is far more useful.

faqs.question: Should revision hours still go on the Internal Assessment at this stage?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on whether the school's internal deadline has passed. Before it, an open internal component is the highest-yield hour available: in the sciences and mathematics that component carries 20 per cent of the subject grade under the current guides, and it will never be movable again. After the deadline, that fifth of the grade is banked and every hour spent there buys nothing. Check the school's own dates with the coordinator rather than assuming the IB's, then reallocate the budget to the written papers on the day each deadline passes.

faqs.question: What does a tutor do with coursework that is still in draft?
faqs.answer: They teach, question and give feedback on the candidate's own attempt. A tutor can explain what a criterion is asking for, show worked examples of the technique, point at a weakness in an argument or a data set, and mark a practice piece. What a tutor does not do is supply sentences, data or analytical decisions that end up in the submitted version, because that creates a malpractice case against the student rather than against the provider. Ask any prospective tutor to state this boundary in writing; the answer sorts this market quickly.

faqs.question: How do IB revision classes work around Ramadan in the UAE?
faqs.answer: By moving, not by pausing. Ramadan falls inside the Gulf revision term for the current run of years, school days shorten and evenings reorganise around Iftar, so a late-afternoon slot that worked in January becomes the worst hour of the day. A workable Ramadan revision schedule puts sessions in the late morning at weekends and after Iftar on school nights. The practical advantage of one-to-one sessions over live video is that they can be re-timed inside the week, which a fixed slot at a tuition centre cannot do at two days' notice.

faqs.question: How should the days between two papers be used?
faqs.answer: Narrowly, and with the real timetable written on one page in advance. The evening after a paper is for twenty minutes of logistics for the next one, never for reconstructing answers on a group chat about a paper that cannot be changed. A free day between two different subjects takes one timed section, marked, and then rest. The gap between Paper 1 and Paper 2 in the same subject is for structure drills, not for re-learning content the first paper already tested. A long gap before a late subject is a full retrieval pass at two hours a day.

faqs.question: Do group revision classes work as well as one-to-one sessions?
faqs.answer: They do different jobs at different points. A group class of four to twelve students is a sensible purchase during the repair pass, when several candidates genuinely need the same content re-covered, and hearing other students' questions has real value. It cannot read one script closely, and reading one script closely is the entire content of the last two passes, where the remaining marks are lost in ways that differ from candidate to candidate. Most families get the best result from both: group or school sessions for coverage, a small number of one-to-one hours placed on the evidence.

faqs.question: What do IB revision classes cost per hour in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Published rates in this market run from roughly AED 45 to AED 650 an hour, read in October 2026. EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65, Unitors publishes IB from AED 200, TutorChase shows AED 270, Bestimate's Dubai 2026 table gives 200 to 450 and above for specialists, and BartyED lists AED 650. Those are other providers' figures, not ours. What the range mostly reflects is inclusion: an hour at the bottom has no marking between sessions and rarely a Higher Level specialist. IB Gram quotes after a diagnostic lesson, because a rate quoted before a script is read is a number without content.

faqs.question: Who is legally permitted to run private revision classes in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Private tutoring in the UAE runs on a permit. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through its app, website or e-services. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Does my child need revision support for Arabic and Islamic Education as well?
faqs.answer: Often yes, and the timetable makes it easy to forget. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and they are examined in their own right. KHDA calculates the required instructional time in 40-minute lesson units and advises that no mandatory subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes, organises separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and requires teachers of these subjects to hold the appropriate KHDA approval. Any additional or different content needs prior permission from the ministry, so material here follows the school's.

faqs.question: What happens if no UAE-based specialist is free for my child's subject?
faqs.answer: We say so rather than substituting quietly. Some Higher Level subject and paper combinations have no UAE-based specialist available at a workable Gulf Standard Time hour, and that is especially true north of Dubai and in Al Ain. In that case the options are a specialist in another time zone teaching at the same standard and on your child's hours, a different pass sequence that uses school and group provision for coverage, or an honest answer that we cannot cover it this term. Finding out in week three is worse than hearing it before anything is booked.

ib-revision-classes.closingHeading: Start with the calendar, then buy the hours the calendar asks for
ib-revision-classes.closingBody: Revision is a dated sequence, and the windows do not move for a family that started late. Do the coverage audit this month, do the hour audit on paper with your child, and write the school's internal deadlines, mock dates and study leave on one page before buying anything. Then place the hours where the evidence says the marks are going. Book one free diagnostic lesson, bring a marked script, and ask for a plan in passes and dates rather than a rate. If the honest answer is that school sessions and marked past papers will do for now, the plan will say that.

ib-score-45-coaching.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IB Diploma subjects at Higher and Standard Level and supervise the core. For a top-band attempt the question is narrower than usual: which paper, which criterion, which topic is costing the seventh mark. Ask for that specialism by name when you book the trial.

intro.heading: What the last three points actually cost
paragraphs: A 45 is not a harder version of a 40. It is a different purchase. At 38 or 40 a family is buying teaching: content that was never properly covered, a topic that was skipped, a habit of leaving Paper 2 half-finished. At 43 or 44 the teaching is already done. What is left is the margin between a strong answer and a complete one, and that margin does not respond to more hours in the same way. Understanding which of those two things you are buying is the single biggest determinant of whether IB score 45 coaching in the UAE is worth the money.

The arithmetic is unforgiving and worth stating plainly. Six subjects are graded one to seven, which caps the subject total at 42. The remaining three points come from the combination of the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge grades, awarded through the IB's published core-points matrix. A 45 therefore requires a seven in all six subjects and the full three core points, with no failing condition triggered anywhere. Confirm the current matrix and the current failing conditions with your child's IB coordinator, because they are revised and this page is not the IB.

That arithmetic changes where the money should go. Most UAE families chasing the top band spend on their child's weakest Higher Level subject, because that is where the school report draws attention. The cheaper point is almost always in the core. A student predicted 43 with one core point available is one well-supervised Extended Essay away from 44, and that supervision is six to ten hours of work spread over months, not two hours a week for two years. The subject point, by contrast, can absorb eighty hours and still not arrive.

UAE market rates make the comparison concrete. Published rates run from roughly AED 45 an hour at the budget end of the online platforms to AED 650 for a premium named tutor, with IB and IGCSE specialists sitting at AED 200-450 and above. Those are market figures, each attributable to a provider who published it, and they are set out in full further down this page. What none of the providers publish is the thing a parent at 43 actually needs: how many of those hours convert into a point, and at what stage they stop converting at all.

This page is built around that question rather than around a sales pitch. It sets out how the 45 is assembled, what the UAE market charges and who charges it, where the next point is cheapest from each starting profile, what a tutor may and may not touch on an Internal Assessment, how one-to-one online tuition compares with a home visit bought locally, and how to check that the person you are paying is permitted to teach privately in the UAE at all. It also says, in plain terms, where the honest answer is to stop paying.

ib-score-45-coaching.programmesIntro: Only one IB programme produces a score out of 45. The other two matter to a top-band attempt for a different reason: they decide how well prepared a student is when DP1 starts, and whether the first term is spent learning content or learning how the IB marks.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two-year Diploma is the only IB programme scored out of 45. Students take six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, and complete the three core elements: the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge and Creativity, Activity, Service. Subject grades run one to seven and are set by a mixture of externally examined papers and internally assessed work that is externally moderated.
programmes.countryNote: Across the UAE the Diploma is the smaller share of a large private-school market. In Dubai, KHDA recorded 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with IB programmes accounting for 7 per cent of that enrolment. The intake for 2026-27 adds seven new private schools, three of them International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. A thin DP cohort in one school is why top-band specialism is often found online rather than nearby.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The Middle Years Programme assesses against criteria rather than against papers, and reports on a one-to-eight scale per criterion. Students arrive in DP1 fluent in criterion language and inquiry, and often unfamiliar with timed, closed-book examination technique. That gap is the most common reason a capable MYP student posts a five in the first DP mock and a family starts looking for coaching.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools running MYP into DP usually transition in a single August, with the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies timetable continuing unchanged through both. For a student aiming at the top band, the useful work happens in the MYP5 summer: examination technique, Higher Level subject choice, and an honest look at whether Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL is the right route rather than the prestigious one.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme combines at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project and a personal and professional skills course. It is a genuine IB qualification and it is not scored out of 45. Diploma courses taken within it are still graded one to seven, so subject-level coaching works the same way, but the core-points arithmetic on this page does not apply.
programmes.countryNote: Fewer UAE schools offer the Career-related Programme than offer the Diploma, so families comparing the two are usually choosing between schools as much as between programmes. If your child is on CP and someone quotes you for 45-point coaching, that is a signal to ask what they think they are selling. The right question for a CP student is which Diploma courses are being taken and what each one needs.

ib-score-45-coaching.subjectsIntro: At the top of the scale the subject matters less than the component. A seven is usually lost in one identifiable place: a paper, a criterion, a topic. The notes below name where that tends to happen for UAE candidates rather than restating the syllabus.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The Higher Level course carries Paper 3, an extended problem-solving paper that rewards sustained reasoning rather than recall. Top-band candidates rarely lose marks on technique; they lose them on the unfamiliar opening of a Paper 3 question and on exploration criteria, where personal engagement and reflection are marked but seldom practised.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Applications and Interpretation is modelling-led and technology-heavy, and a seven depends on reading context accurately before touching the calculator. Students who switched from Analysis and Approaches mid-DP1 often carry an algebraic reflex that costs marks here, where the examiner wants interpretation of the model and a stated limitation.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Physics sevens are won on the long-answer and data-analysis components rather than on multiple choice. The recurring loss for strong candidates is uncertainty treatment in the internal assessment and an unexamined assumption in an extended answer. Both are coachable in a handful of sessions once the specific pattern is identified from marked scripts.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics absorb most revision time, while the marks at the top end move on data-based questions and on the internal assessment's evaluation section. A candidate already at six usually needs criterion-level feedback on their own write-up, not another pass through the reactions of alcohols.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Biology rewards precision of command terms more than breadth. Strong UAE candidates frequently describe where the paper asks them to explain, and lose the seventh mark across many small deductions rather than one failure. Marking their own past-paper answers against the published criteria is the intervention that moves this.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and real-world evidence carry the grade, and Higher Level adds quantitative demands that catch out students comfortable with the theory. The internal assessment commentaries are the component where a top-band student most often leaves marks on the table through article choice rather than through analysis.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the Higher Level essay reward a controlled argument about a global issue, not a tour of the text. Candidates predicted six tend to be assessment-literate but under-rehearsed on the oral, where ten minutes of unstructured talk costs a band. Rehearsal with criterion feedback is the whole of the fix.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study response discipline decides the grade: tools applied to the stimulus, with a conclusion that answers the command term. Higher Level candidates lose marks by writing everything they know about a tool rather than the part that bears on the case. The internal assessment stands or falls on the research question.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Higher Level adds abstract data structures and resource management, where strong coders often under-perform because the paper wants explanation rather than implementation. The solution component is where sevens are decided, and it needs supervision on documentation and testing rather than help with the code.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Arabic language courses matter twice over for UAE candidates: once as a Group 2 subject graded one to seven, and once because Arabic is a mandatory school subject under KHDA requirements regardless of the licensed curriculum. Written productive skills and the individual oral carry the grade, and both are rehearsable.

ib-score-45-coaching.regionsTitle: Where our UAE students sit the Diploma
ib-score-45-coaching.regionsIntro: Which emirate a family lives in changes who regulates the school, who approves its fees and curriculum, and how deep the local pool of Higher Level specialists goes. The last of those is the practical reason top-band coaching in the smaller emirates tends to happen online.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Regulated by KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate. KHDA recorded 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools and 17 curricula in 2024-25, with IB programmes at 7 per cent of enrolment. Three of the seven new schools opening for 2026-27 are IB.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which is why an external specialist is the normal route here.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK. The Diploma cohort per school is smaller than in Abu Dhabi city, so a student needing Physics HL or Mathematics Analysis and Approaches HL at top-band level will often find no local specialist free at the hour they can actually study.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Fee and curriculum approval sitting with the emirate regulator is worth knowing before a family compares two schools' Diploma offerings.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman. The IB cohort is small and concentrated in a handful of schools, which makes evening online sessions the only realistic way to reach a subject-and-level specialist without a cross-emirate commute.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in Ras Al Khaimah and approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Competitor pages in this market mention the emirate essentially not at all, which tells you how thin local provision is.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Families here are usually choosing between a local school and a longer commute to Dubai or Sharjah, and the commute is exactly what a DP2 evening cannot absorb once the Extended Essay and internal assessment deadlines land.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. The smallest private-school market of the seven emirates, and the clearest case for delivering specialist Diploma coaching over live video rather than waiting for a specialist to exist within driving distance.

schoolClusters.note: The deepest IB market in the country, and the one where top-band candidates most often sit in a cohort with several other students chasing the same grade. Named here as ecosystem context for families comparing where the Diploma is taught.
schools: Jumeirah English Speaking School - Arabian Ranches

schoolClusters.note: A smaller Diploma market under ADEK, where the per-school cohort is often a single teaching group. That is the structural reason an external Higher Level specialist is usually the practical option for a student already predicted six.
schools: American Community School of Abu Dhabi

schoolClusters.note: Provision thins quickly outside Dubai and Abu Dhabi, and the regulator changes with the emirate: SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain.

ib-score-45-coaching.modesIntro: Three shapes of support cover almost every top-band request we receive. All three are delivered as one-to-one online tuition over live video in Gulf Standard Time. The right one depends on how many points are genuinely available and where they sit.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one subject work
modes.description: A fixed hour each week with a specialist in one subject at one level, built around the student's own marked scripts rather than a generic scheme. At top-band level the session is usually half diagnosis and half rehearsal: find the component where the seventh mark is going, then practise that component against the published criteria until the pattern changes.

modes.description: A short, dense block of sessions at the points in the year where the core actually moves: research-question design, the first full draft, the reflection, the final check against the criteria. The tutor reads, questions and gives feedback. The student is the sole author of every word that is submitted, and the school supervisor remains the person who signs the work off.

modes.title: Final-stretch sprint before the May session
modes.description: An intensive block in the last eight to ten weeks, usually across two subjects, aimed at components rather than syllabus. For a student holding a predicted 43 or 44 this is where the available points are, and the sessions look less like teaching and more like supervised examination practice with immediate marking and a short list of repeat errors.

sections.heading: What a 45 is made of, before anyone quotes you a price
paragraphs: A 45 is six sevens plus the full three core points, with no failing condition triggered. That is the whole specification, and it is worth writing down before a single hour is bought, because it tells you immediately which points are still available to your child and which are already gone. A student with a five in one Standard Level subject in DP1 is not out of the top band, but the path there now runs through a two-grade lift in that subject, which is a different and more expensive purchase than the one most families think they are making.

The six subject grades are produced by externally examined papers plus internally assessed work that is marked by the teacher and externally moderated. Both halves can cost a seven, and they fail in different ways. Papers are lost to technique and timing. Internal assessments are lost to criteria: a research question that cannot be answered in the space available, an evaluation section that lists limitations without weighing them, a reflection that reports feelings rather than learning. The second kind is cheaper to fix because it is fixable once, in writing, before submission.

The three core points are awarded on the combination of the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge grades through the IB's published matrix, and a sufficiently weak result in either can also trigger a failing condition that removes the diploma entirely. Those rules are revised, so confirm the current matrix and failing conditions with your child's IB coordinator or on the IB's own assessment pages rather than taking them from any tutoring site, this one included. What does not change is the shape of the arithmetic: the core is three points out of forty-five decided by two pieces of written work, and it is the part of the diploma over which a student has the most control and the longest run-up.

sections.heading: What top-band IB coaching costs in the UAE, and who publishes those numbers
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible tutoring pages in this market publish no price at all, and the two that do quote United States dollars, which is not the currency a UAE family transacts in. The table below is the AED version, assembled from rates those providers published themselves plus Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. These are market rates, not IB Gram's price list. Our own figure comes out of a conversation about how many hours the point gap actually needs, which is the only responsible way to quote for a 44-or-45 attempt.

Read the table by what the hour buys rather than by the number. At the budget end, AED 45-150 an hour buys supervision and content catch-up from a tutor who may be a university student, and that is a reasonable purchase for a student at 32 who skipped a term. It is a poor purchase at 43, because the work left is criterion-level feedback on Higher Level components, and a tutor who has not marked at that level cannot give it. The middle band, AED 150-300, is where a properly qualified subject tutor sits. IB and IGCSE specialists run AED 200-450 and above.

The premium band deserves a specific warning. AED 500-650 an hour is a defensible spend on a narrowly defined problem: one Paper 3 technique, one internal assessment criterion, one oral rehearsal. It is rarely a defensible weekly habit over two years, and the arithmetic of IB DP HL tutoring rates at that level is brutal once multiplied by eighty weeks. Be sceptical of anyone selling examiner status as a general advantage rather than as a specific skill, and more sceptical still of any page that attaches a grade to a price. Nobody can sell you a point.

sections.heading: The marginal point: where the next point is cheapest from each starting profile
paragraphs: Hours do not convert into points at a constant rate. The first ten hours spent on a subject a student has genuinely not understood can move two grades. The eightieth hour spent on a subject where the student already answers correctly but slightly incompletely may move nothing at all. This is the single piece of analysis the UAE tutoring market does not publish, and it is the one a family at 43 needs before signing up to a weekly slot for eighteen months.

The table below is a planning tool, not a promise, and it is built from the shape of the assessment rather than from any claim about outcomes. Read down the left column to your child's current prediction, then read the right-hand column first. In most profiles there is something cheaper than hours: a set of marked scripts nobody has read properly, a research question that needs narrowing, a Paper 2 timing habit that costs eight marks an hour. Those cost a conversation and a fortnight of discipline.

Two profiles deserve particular attention. A student predicted 40-42 with a core point still in play is in the best position on the table, because core supervision is the lowest-cost point available anywhere in the diploma. A student predicted 44 with both core points already secured is in the worst, not because they are weak but because there is nothing cheap left: the remaining point sits in a component where they already perform well, and buying it means a large number of hours with a low conversion rate. The honest advice at that point is to protect sleep, protect the deadlines, and stop paying.

sections.heading: The three core points are the cheapest points on the board
paragraphs: The Extended Essay and TOK core points are worth three of forty-five, which is the same weight as moving three subject grades. They are decided by two pieces of written work with deadlines a student knows a year in advance, and they are the only part of the diploma where a candidate controls both the question and the timetable. Despite that, the Extended Essay and TOK core points are the part of the Diploma UAE families most often buy support for last, usually in the term when the draft is already due.

Length limits are the practical constraint and the most common cause of a lost band. A research question that would need twelve thousand words to answer properly cannot score well in four thousand, however good the student is, and no amount of later editing rescues it. The same applies to the TOK essay on a prescribed title and to the exhibition with its three objects: each has a published limit, and each rewards an argument sized to that limit. Confirm every figure in the table below against the current subject guide your child's school issues, because the guides are revised.

What supervision looks like here is narrower than people expect. The useful sessions are a question-design session before any drafting, one round of criterion-by-criterion Internal Assessment feedback or essay feedback on the student's own draft, and a reflection session before the final submission. That is six to ten hours across several months. At market specialist rates of AED 200-450 and above, that is a defined and modest spend for a point that is genuinely available, which is why it belongs at the front of a top-band plan rather than at the end.

sections.heading: Where UAE families waste money chasing a 45
paragraphs: The most expensive mistake is buying hours in six subjects at once. It feels thorough and it is the standard response to a report card with three sixes on it, but it produces a student with no free evenings, six sets of homework from six tutors, and less time for the timed practice that actually moves a Higher Level grade. A top-band plan is narrow by design: two components at a time, with everything else held steady by the school.

The second is paying for teaching when the problem is marking. A student predicted six in Biology who describes where the paper says explain does not need the content taught again. They need twenty of their own answers marked against the criteria with the deduction named each time. Many families pay a premium hourly rate for a tutor to re-present material the student already knows, because re-teaching is what a tutoring session looks like and marking is not. Ask explicitly for marked work to come back, in writing, after every session.

The third is late buying. Core supervision purchased three weeks before a deadline can tidy a draft; it cannot change a research question. Subject coaching started six weeks before the May session can fix timing and technique, which is real, but it cannot build two years of content. Both are worth doing and both cost more per point than the same money spent a year earlier. The fourth mistake is paying anything at all to a provider who offers to produce the work: that is an academic-honesty breach, it is an expulsion risk for the student, and it is sold openly in this market at four-figure AED prices.
