ib-tok-essay-help.programmesIntro: Theory of Knowledge belongs to the Diploma Programme, but the habits it assesses are built earlier. Families usually arrive at TOK with a child who has come through the MYP in the same school, or who transferred into DP1 from a British or American system and has never been asked to argue about knowledge at all. The programme notes below describe where each one leaves a student.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The two-year Diploma carries three core components beside the six subjects: Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. TOK is taught across both years, with a recommended 100 hours of teaching time, and is assessed twice: an exhibition of three objects with a written commentary inside the school, and a 1,600-word essay on a prescribed title read by an external examiner. The TOK grade is reported as a letter from A to E. It does not sit in the 42 subject points; it feeds the three additional points instead.
programmes.countryNote: UAE Diploma cohorts are small relative to the school. Dubai's private sector enrolled 387,441 students across 227 schools in 2024-25, with the IB accounting for 7% of enrolment, so a school with three hundred DP students may still run TOK with a single teacher and no specialist cover. Three of the seven schools joining Dubai's 2026-27 intake are IB schools, which means more first-cohort TOK teaching, not less. Ask the DP coordinator how many sessions that teacher has taken an essay through before you decide whether outside help is proportionate.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP has no TOK, but it has the two things TOK depends on: interdisciplinary units that ask a student to hold two subject lenses at once, and the Personal Project in the final year, which is the first piece of extended independent work most IB students produce. Students arrive in DP1 from the MYP already used to criterion-referenced marking and to a supervisor who comments on process rather than content. What they usually lack is practice at sustaining a single argument for 1,600 words.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools run the full IB continuum, so a student may have been in the same building since PYP. That continuity helps with the vocabulary and hurts with the examples: a cohort taught by the same staff for a decade tends to reach for the same three case studies in every essay. Where a student has moved into the UAE mid-MYP from a national system, the gap is usually the opposite one, and the first few sessions go on reading an argument rather than summarising a source.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs DP courses with a career-related study and its own core, which includes Personal and Professional Skills, a reflective project and a language development component. CP students do not sit Theory of Knowledge and do not submit a TOK essay. Families sometimes assume otherwise because the two programmes share a timetable and a coordinator. If your child is on the CP, the reflective project is the piece of extended writing that needs supervision, and the ethical dilemma at its centre is the part that most often goes thin.
programmes.countryNote: The CP is offered by a small number of UAE schools and is easy to confuse with the Diploma when both run in the same year group. Before booking anything, check the programme on the report card rather than the school's prospectus. A parent who buys TOK support for a CP student has bought the wrong thing; a parent who buys reflective-project supervision for a DP student has bought the wrong thing in the other direction.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP ends with the Exhibition, a collaborative inquiry presented at the close of Year 6. It is not assessed by the IB and carries no grade, but it is where a student first meets the idea that a question can be better or worse than another question. The transferable skill is the one TOK examiners reward six years later: treating a claim as something that needs justification rather than something to be reported accurately.
programmes.countryNote: Most UAE families meet the IB at this stage and make a continuum decision here without knowing TOK exists. Worth knowing early: the subjects KHDA requires alongside the licensed curriculum, Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies, start in primary and run on into DP, so the timetable pressure a DP2 student feels in the TOK drafting weeks was built into the week years before.

ib-tok-essay-help.subjectsIntro: TOK is organised around a compulsory core theme, five areas of knowledge and a choice of two optional themes. The essay has to draw on areas of knowledge, so the pairing a student chooses decides most of what the argument can do. The notes below say what each one gives an essay and where students run out of material.

subjects.name: Knowledge and the Knower
subjects.description: The core theme every TOK course teaches: how a person's position, communities and assumptions shape what they take to be known. It is the richest source of material for the exhibition and the thinnest for the essay, because a prescribed title asks about areas of knowledge, not about the student. Essays that stay in the core theme tend to describe perspective rather than argue with it.

subjects.name: Natural Sciences
subjects.description: The default choice, and the one examiners see most. It offers method, replication, peer review and paradigm change, so counterclaims are easy to construct. The failure mode is a student with HL Chemistry writing a chemistry lesson: the essay explains the science accurately and never asks how the knowledge was justified. Specificity helps here, including a named study with a date and a dispute attached to it.

subjects.name: Human Sciences
subjects.description: Economics, psychology and geography students usually have the strongest examples and the weakest framing. Human sciences give an essay measurement problems, model dependence and the difficulty of controlled study in a social setting. Paired with natural sciences it produces a contrast that collapses easily into a ranking exercise, so the pairing needs a reason beyond convenience.

subjects.name: History
subjects.description: History carries evidence, selection and the problem of writing about what cannot be observed directly. It is the strongest partner for almost any title because it makes the role of the knower visible without leaving the area of knowledge. Students taking DP History have the examples; students who are not often reach for a single war and no historiography at all.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.description: The most powerful and most mishandled area of knowledge. Mathematics lets a student argue about proof, axioms, certainty and whether mathematical objects are discovered or invented. It fails when the essay confuses being certain with being true, or treats a worked calculation as evidence. Analysis and Approaches students handle this better than Applications and Interpretation students, mostly because proof appears on their syllabus.

subjects.name: The Arts
subjects.description: The arts give an essay interpretation, intention, convention and the question of whether a work can be wrong. Students who take Visual Arts, Music or Theatre have real material; students who do not tend to write about a single painting in general terms. Used as the second area of knowledge against the sciences, it produces the sharpest contrasts available in TOK.

subjects.name: Knowledge and Technology
subjects.description: Covers algorithmic recommendation, data, automation and the place of machine-produced output in what counts as knowing. The most current of the optional themes and the easiest to fill with opinion. An essay drawing on it needs a concrete mechanism, not a general worry about screens, and it should still route its argument through an area of knowledge.

subjects.name: Knowledge and Language
subjects.description: Translation, metaphor, framing and the limits of what a vocabulary allows a person to say. Useful to bilingual students, who have direct evidence that a concept can survive one language and not another. In a UAE classroom with Arabic, English and often a third home language in the same room, this theme produces examples no textbook supplies.

subjects.name: Knowledge and Politics
subjects.description: Authority, expertise, propaganda and who is permitted to speak for a body of knowledge. It gives an essay real traction on justification and consensus. It also tempts students into contemporary commentary, which examiners read as assertion. Sessions on this theme spend most of their time converting a political example into a knowledge question.

subjects.name: Knowledge and Religion
subjects.description: Faith, revelation, interpretation of texts and the relationship between religious and empirical knowledge. Taught carefully it is one of the strongest themes for an essay about certainty and justification. Students who have studied Islamic Education alongside their licensed curriculum often bring a more precise account of interpretive tradition than the theme's reading list expects.

subjects.name: Knowledge and Indigenous Societies
subjects.description: Oral transmission, custodianship, place-based knowledge and what happens when knowledge is recorded by someone outside the community that holds it. Rarely chosen and therefore rarely seen by examiners. It rewards a student willing to read properly and punishes one looking for a quick second theme.

subjects.name: Extended Essay
subjects.description: Not part of TOK, but assessed on the same core and graded on the same A to E scale, and the two grades are read together in the points matrix. Families almost always need both supervised in the same year. Extended Essay supervision is a separate piece of work with a separate supervisor, a separate reflection form and a different kind of research question.

ib-tok-essay-help.regionsTitle: TOK essay support across the seven emirates
ib-tok-essay-help.regionsIntro: The TOK essay is the same task everywhere. What changes by emirate is which authority licenses the school, which rules govern the person helping, and what the school week looks like around the drafting period. Online delivery is what makes the same specialist reachable from Umm Al Quwain and from Dubai Marina at the same session time.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA licenses 227 private schools here and publishes an inspection report for each. It also sets the mandatory subject requirements that sit beside the IB, and confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for 2026-27. Dubai has the deepest DP cohort in the country and the longest queue for its TOK teachers in February.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and sets professional-ethics rules for school staff that restrict paid private tutoring of a teacher's own students. Diploma families here are the most likely to discover that the supervisor they trust is the one person who cannot be engaged privately.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK, which surprises families who assume a separate Al Ain authority. The practical difference is distance: DP cohorts are smaller, specialist TOK teaching is thinner, and a student wanting a second reader has fewer options inside a reasonable radius. Online sessions remove the radius from the decision entirely.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Term rhythms here differ from Dubai's in practice, and families often want TOK drafting sessions placed later in the evening than a Dubai family would choose.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority. Fewer schools run the full Diploma, so a DP2 student may be one of a handful taking TOK in the building, with no second teacher to read a draft and no peer group to argue with.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah's authority, approves curricula and assessment methods. RAK appears in none of the competing pages in this search, which is a reasonable signal of how much attention Diploma families here get from tutoring providers.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. The commute between Fujairah and the Dubai-Sharjah corridor is the single biggest constraint on anything delivered in person, which is why an online model changes the available tutor pool here more than anywhere else in the country.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under the federal Ministry of Education, and the smallest private-school market in the UAE. A family here looking for someone who has taken TOK essays through more than one session is looking outside the emirate by definition, and almost certainly outside the country.

schoolClusters.note: Diploma cohorts in Dubai are large enough that TOK is usually timetabled properly and taught by someone who has done it before. The pressure point is February and March, when every DP2 student in the building wants supervisor time in the same fortnight and the one TOK teacher is also marking exhibitions.

ib-tok-essay-help.modesIntro: TOK support works in blocks rather than as an open-ended weekly slot, because the task has a fixed shape and a fixed end date. All four formats below run one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the student sharing their own document on screen. Nothing is delivered at a UAE address.

modes.description: Two or three sessions in the fortnight after the IB releases the prescribed titles for the session. The student arrives having read all six; the work is deciding which one their course and their examples can actually sustain for 1,600 words. Most students pick the title that sounds most interesting rather than the one they have material for, and that choice is responsible for more lost marks than anything that happens afterwards.

The tutor asks where the counterclaim is, which area of knowledge is doing the work in this paragraph, and whether the example would survive a reader who disagreed. No text is supplied; the student leaves with questions and rewrites between sessions.

It complements the school's formal comment rather than replacing it.

sections.heading: What searching for IB TOK essay help in the UAE should get you
paragraphs: A legitimate TOK service does three things: it helps a student choose a prescribed title they can sustain, it interrogates the argument while there is still time to change it, and it reads a complete draft against the assessment requirements before the school's internal deadline. It does not supply paragraphs, rewrite sentences in the student's name, or hand over a finished piece of work. Everything in this search that offers the last three is offering the student an academic misconduct investigation.

The distinction matters more in TOK than anywhere else in the Diploma, because the essay is unsupervised writing on an abstract question and therefore the easiest component to buy. Sites in this market sell completed Diploma coursework outright, at prices that sit above what a term of honest supervision costs. The IB treats submitted work that is not the student's own as malpractice, and the consequence falls on the candidate, not the vendor. No tutoring arrangement is worth that exposure.

What a UAE family should be checking is narrower and more practical. Who is the person in the session, and have they taken a TOK essay through a full session before? Do they hold the MoHRE private tuition work permit if they are tutoring from inside the UAE? Will the written output of each session be questions addressed to the student, or text the student could paste? Does the provider accept that the school supervisor remains the person the IB holds responsible for the process?

IB Gram answers all four in writing before a family pays anything. Lessons are one-to-one online TOK tuition in the UAE, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, with a free trial lesson first and no card details collected at that stage. There is no office in the UAE and no tutor travelling anywhere; what you are buying is an hour of a specialist's attention on your child's own argument.

sections.heading: The two TOK tasks, and which one a tutor can legitimately touch
paragraphs: Theory of Knowledge is assessed twice, and the two tasks behave completely differently. The exhibition is internal: the student selects three objects, writes a commentary connecting each to one of the IB's internal-assessment prompts, and the school marks it before the IB moderates a sample. The essay is external: one of six prescribed titles released by the IB for that session, 1,600 words, read by an examiner who has never met the student. The exhibition carries one third of the TOK grade and the essay two thirds.

The practical consequence is that the exhibition is the earlier and more forgiving of the two. It is produced in DP1 in most schools, the prompts are published in advance, and the teacher who marks it will have explained what a strong commentary looks like. By the time a family starts searching for help, the exhibition is usually finished and the mark is already in. What remains movable is the essay, which is why almost every enquiry we take on this page is about the essay specifically.

Both tasks are documented through a planning and progress record that the student completes with their supervisor. The IB requires a set number of documented interactions for the essay, with comments from both the student and the supervisor, and the form is submitted alongside the work. This is the mechanism that makes buying an essay detectable: a submitted piece that bears no relationship to the recorded planning sequence is exactly what a moderator looks for.

A paid tutor works inside that structure rather than around it. The student's recorded interactions remain with the school supervisor. Outside sessions are additional practice on the student's own thinking, and the student should be able to describe, in their own words, what changed between drafts and why. If they cannot, the help was the wrong kind. Confirm the current requirement counts and deadlines with your school's DP coordinator, because the IB updates its assessment procedures between sessions.

sections.heading: What the TOK grade is actually worth in Diploma points
paragraphs: TOK does not score points of its own. The six subjects provide up to 42 points, and the TOK and Extended Essay grades are read together against a matrix that awards between zero and three additional points, for a maximum of 45. A student needs 24 points for the Diploma to be awarded, alongside a set of conditions that the points total alone does not capture.

The matrix is where parents misjudge the stakes in both directions. A family that treats TOK as decorative is wrong: moving from a C to an A, with a B in the Extended Essay, is the difference between one point and three, and a single point regularly separates an offer from a near miss. A family that panics is also wrong: moving TOK from a C to a B, with a C in the Extended Essay, moves nothing at all. Which cell you are sitting in decides whether more support is worth buying.

The hard edge is the E. A grade E in either TOK or the Extended Essay is a failing condition for the Diploma. A student can hold 38 subject points and still leave with Course Results rather than a Diploma, and that distinction is exactly the one a Ministry of Education equivalency file turns on. This is the single most important fact on this page for a UAE family, because the equivalency route for a Diploma student assumes an awarded Diploma.

Read the matrix below with your child's current predicted grades in front of you, then ask the coordinator what the school's internal TOK marks have looked like against final IB grades in past sessions. Schools vary in how generously they mark exhibitions, and a school that has run the Diploma for two years has less calibration than one that has run it for fifteen. Confirm the matrix against the IB's current assessment procedures before making a decision on it.

sections.heading: Who at a UAE school may be paid to help, and who may not
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permitted and regulated. The route is a private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and issued through MoHRE, which lists teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students among those eligible to apply. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you.

The restriction that matters for TOK is not about the permit itself. The ADEK professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the code of conduct attached to the MoHRE permit carries the same bar. Your child's TOK teacher is also their essay supervisor. That person cannot be engaged privately, and a provider that offers to arrange it is proposing something a parent should refuse. These rules are press-reported, so ask the school to confirm its own policy in writing.

A school that wants to go further than individual permits, by running a tuition centre with premises and staff, needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute in Dubai, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested ahead of expiry. That is a different legal animal from one tutor with a permit, and the two are frequently conflated in this search. Nobody should describe themselves as approved by a regulator on the strength of the wrong one.

IB Gram holds no permit, licence, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and no page here will tell you otherwise. What the platform does is match a family to a tutor and state plainly where that tutor is based and what their position is. You can verify an individual permit through MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, which lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time.

sections.heading: Academic honesty: the line each person stands on
paragraphs: IB academic honesty rules are not vague about TOK. The essay must be the student's own response to the prescribed title, with sources acknowledged, and the supervisor's role is to guide the process and comment formally a limited number of times. A parent may discuss ideas at the dinner table. A tutor may question an argument until it breaks. Neither may put a sentence into the document, and neither may restructure a paragraph so that the student is submitting someone else's reasoning in their own voice.

The grey area families worry about is proofreading. The safe position is that the student fixes their own errors after someone points to where errors exist. Marking a sentence as unclear is teaching; replacing it is not. The same logic governs structure: telling a student that their second area of knowledge appears only in the final paragraph is feedback, and moving it for them is not. The test we apply in sessions is whether the student could explain every change to their supervisor without help.

This is also where a parent can usefully be sceptical about any provider's written output. If a session produces a document the student could paste, the provider has crossed the line regardless of what the invoice says. Our session notes are deliberately useless as text: they are questions, page references and one-line observations, because that is what survives an academic honesty conversation and what actually improves a draft.

If a school does raise a concern about outside support, the honest response is complete disclosure: who the tutor is, what the sessions covered, and what the student changed afterwards. A family that has kept the supervisor informed from the start never reaches that point. Tell the coordinator in DP1 that your child is working with an outside tutor; in our experience schools treat that as responsible rather than suspicious, and it removes the only real risk in the arrangement.

sections.heading: Counting back from submission inside a UAE school year
paragraphs: The TOK essay fails on timing more often than on ability. The prescribed titles are released months ahead of submission, the school sets an internal deadline well before the IB's, and the drafting period lands squarely in the stretch when Diploma students are also finishing subject explorations and sitting mocks. A student who starts late is choosing a title they have no examples for, in the week they have least time to find any.

We publish this calendar in weeks rather than dates on purpose. IB session and results dates are set by the IB and are revised between sessions, and no date in this project has been confirmed against ibo.org, which blocks automated checking. Get the actual dates from your school's DP coordinator or the IB's own assessment pages, then map them onto the sequence below. The relative spacing is what matters and it is stable across sessions.

The UAE school year adds two local complications. The first is that the mandatory subjects KHDA and the other authorities require, Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies, occupy timetabled periods that a DP2 student cannot drop, so the free hours in a week are fewer than a parent counting six subjects would assume. The second is Ramadan, which shortens the school day and shifts the usable study hours to after Iftar in the year it falls across the drafting window.

Work backwards from the school's internal deadline rather than the IB's, because the internal one is the one your child will actually be held to and it is usually several weeks earlier. Then put the pre-submission read two to four weeks before it, so there is still room to act on what the read finds. A complete draft that arrives three days before the deadline can be corrected for clarity and nothing else.

sections.heading: Where TOK drafting meets the mandatory UAE subjects
paragraphs: Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific national curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but they must follow the Ministry's general regulations, and each emirate authority applies that federally. In Dubai, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and social and moral studies in all private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with its current requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year.

KHDA's mandatory subjects guidance is unusually specific about how that time is organised. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary the lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and the advice is that no mandatory subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social studies, and combined classes for both groups are not permitted because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ.

For a DP2 student in the TOK drafting weeks, this is a timetable fact rather than a policy debate. Those periods are fixed, they are graded on the school report, and they cannot be traded for study time. A parent working out how many hours a week are genuinely available for essay work should count them out first. It is also why evening sessions in Gulf Standard Time, rather than daytime slots, are what families here actually book.

There is an upside worth naming. Students who have studied Arabic as a first language or Islamic Education alongside their licensed curriculum arrive at the knowledge and language and knowledge and religion themes with concrete material: direct experience of a concept that does not survive translation, or of an interpretive tradition with its own standards of justification. Examiners reward specific examples, and these are specific in a way a generic reading list is not.

sections.heading: What DP core support costs in the UAE market
paragraphs: Three of the six pages competing for this search publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars. The figures below are market bands, published by the providers named, checked in October 2026. They are not IB Gram's prices: what a session costs here is quoted after the free consultation, because it depends on the specialist, the session length and how many weeks are left before the deadline.

Read the bands as a description of who is in the room rather than a quality ranking. At the bottom of the market the hour is usually a university student doing content revision, which is a reasonable purchase for a subject gap and the wrong purchase for a core component with an external examiner. At the top, named and examiner-led providers publish rates several times higher. TOK supervision sits in the middle of the market because the work is argument-level teaching, and the useful question is how many hours it takes, not what an hour costs.

Blocks are more honest than hourly rates for this component. A title-selection block is two or three sessions. A weekly clinic through the drafting period is six to ten. A pre-submission read is one longer session. Most UAE families we work with on TOK buy somewhere between eight and fourteen hours across the whole cycle, which is a very different number from an open-ended weekly subject slot running for two years.

Set that against the wider cost picture. KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27, under the emirate's second economic incentives package. School fees are the fixed cost in a Diploma family's year; core supervision is the variable one, and it is bought in a window a few months wide rather than across two years. Ask any provider to quote the block, not the hour.

sections.heading: Ramadan, term dates and where drafting actually fits
paragraphs: In the years when Ramadan falls across the spring term, it lands on the part of the Diploma calendar where TOK drafting and subject explorations overlap. School days are shortened, the usable concentration hours move to the evening, and a family that keeps a 4pm session in place through the month is usually paying for an hour nobody is present for. The sessions that work are after Iftar, and they are shorter.

Plan the month rather than cancel it. A sensible pattern is to front-load the structural work before Ramadan begins, hold one shorter weekly session at a post-Iftar time through the month, and schedule the pre-submission read for the week after. The structural decisions, which title, which areas of knowledge, which examples, are the ones that need a clear head; checking citations and trimming to the word limit does not.

The rest of the UAE calendar has its own rhythm worth planning around. The winter break sits in the middle of the drafting period for most DP2 cohorts and is the single largest uninterrupted block of time a student will get before submission. Families who travel over that break should decide in advance whether sessions follow them across time zones, because an online schedule can, and a two-week gap at that point is expensive to recover from.

One practical note on scheduling: everything here is timed to Gulf Standard Time and confirmed slot by slot, and a tutor in another time zone is matched to a slot that works for the student rather than for the tutor. Where a specialist genuinely cannot cover a time, we say so at the consultation instead of booking a session nobody can keep.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, the Diploma and TOK
paragraphs: Families ask whether TOK counts towards Ministry of Education equivalency. The honest answer is that equivalency is assessed on the certificate a student holds, not on individual core components, and the published requirements differ by curriculum track. For the British track, students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no lower than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not among the five required subjects, a point one ranking competitor publishes incorrectly as a six-subject rule.

For the American track, the published English requirement is a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, with mathematics requiring at least 450 in the SAT Math test. No IB points threshold appears in the source we read, so this page publishes none. Any figure you see quoted for the IB should be checked on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate before you plan around it.

Where TOK does matter to equivalency is indirectly, and decisively. The route for a Diploma student assumes a Diploma that has actually been awarded. A grade E in TOK is a failing condition, so a student in that position holds Course Results rather than the Diploma, and the equivalency file they open is a different file. That is the clearest financial argument on this page for taking a borderline TOK grade seriously in DP1 rather than DP2.

Equivalency is also not something a tutoring provider performs. IB Gram does not submit, process or guarantee an equivalency or attestation file, and nobody should offer to. Describe it, verify it at the source, and use the official channel. Tutoring is not required for equivalency, for university admission or for school progression, and any provider suggesting otherwise is manufacturing urgency about a regulatory process.

process.title: Tell us where the essay actually is
process.description: The first conversation establishes four things: which session the student is entered for, whether the titles have been released, what the school's internal deadline is, and which two optional themes the course covered. That is enough to say honestly whether a block of sessions can still change the outcome or whether the realistic target is the Extended Essay instead.

process.title: A free trial lesson, on the real work
process.description: One trial lesson before any payment, with no card details collected. The student brings whatever exists, even if that is only a shortlist of titles, and the hour is spent on it rather than on a diagnostic test. Parents are welcome to sit in. If the match is wrong, the consultation suggests another specialist or says plainly that we do not have one free.

process.title: Agree the block and the calendar
process.description: Sessions are booked as a block counted back from the school's internal deadline, not as an open weekly slot. You see how many hours the block is, what each session is for, and where the pre-submission read sits. Slots are confirmed in Gulf Standard Time, and the schedule is written down so a missed week is visible immediately.

process.title: Tell the school
process.description: We ask families to let the DP coordinator know that outside support is in place. It takes one email, it removes the only genuine risk in the arrangement, and in our experience schools read it as responsible. The supervisor keeps the recorded interactions the IB requires; outside sessions are additional practice on the student's own thinking.

process.title: Work in questions, not corrections
process.description: Each session the student defends the current draft out loud and leaves with questions rather than edits. Session notes are page references and one-line observations, deliberately unusable as text. Between sessions the student revises their own document, and the next hour starts with what changed and why.

process.title: Stop at the right point
process.description: The block ends after the pre-submission read, with two to four weeks still in hand. Submission is between the student, the supervisor and the coordinator, and no tutor is involved in it. If the family wants to continue into Extended Essay supervision or a subject, that is a new conversation with its own calendar.

whyPoints.title: A specialist, not whoever is nearby
whyPoints.description: TOK supervision experience is thin in any single emirate, and thinnest in Al Ain, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain. Delivering one-to-one online removes distance from the match, so a family outside the Dubai corridor gets the same specialist a Dubai family would, at a session time that suits the student rather than a driving route.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line is written down
whyPoints.description: What a tutor may and may not do with a draft is set out on this page as a table, not buried in terms. The student types every word, session notes are questions, and the school supervisor keeps the recorded interactions the IB requires. That position is what makes the help usable if a school ever asks about it.

whyPoints.title: No regulator borrowed for credibility
whyPoints.description: IB Gram claims no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson. The pages here explain what those bodies do and point to their own sites. A provider that implies endorsement it does not hold is telling you something about the rest of its claims.

whyPoints.title: Market rates shown, with sources
whyPoints.description: The AED bands on this page are other providers' published figures with the provider and the month of checking named, so you can price a block against the market rather than against a sales call. Our own number is quoted after the consultation, because it depends on the specialist and how many weeks are left.

whyPoints.title: Blocks with an end date
whyPoints.description: TOK work has a deadline, so it is sold as a block counted backwards from the school's internal date rather than as a subscription. Most cycles run between eight and fourteen hours in total. You know the number before you start, and the block ends while there is still time to act on the final read.

whyPoints.title: Availability stated before you pay
whyPoints.description: If no TOK specialist is free at your session times, the consultation says so and offers either a different slot or nothing. The alternative, which is common in this market, is a general essay tutor booked against a core component with an external examiner, and that costs a family a term they cannot get back.

faqs.question: Does the school choose the TOK prescribed title, or does the student?
faqs.answer: The student chooses. The IB releases six prescribed titles for each session and the candidate responds to one of them, using the exact wording as issued. A school may discuss the titles in class and a supervisor will explain what each is asking for, but the choice and the justification belong to the student. This is the decision that most affects the final mark, because a title with no usable examples behind it cannot be rescued later by better writing. Spend real time on it: read all six, test each against the areas of knowledge your child actually has material in, then decide.

faqs.question: Can the teacher who supervises the TOK essay also be paid to tutor my child privately?
faqs.answer: Generally not. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the code of conduct attached to the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries the same restriction for teachers tutoring outside school hours. Since the TOK supervisor is by definition a member of staff at your child's school, that person is the one person who cannot be engaged privately. These rules are press-reported rather than quoted here from the policy document, so ask your school to confirm its own position in writing, and treat any provider offering to arrange it as a warning sign.

faqs.question: What is the planning and progress record, and why does it matter to a parent?
faqs.answer: It is the form on which a student records their documented interactions with the TOK essay supervisor, with comments from both the student and the supervisor, submitted alongside the essay. It is not separately graded. It matters because it is the mechanism that makes a bought essay visible: a submitted piece bearing no relationship to the recorded planning sequence is precisely what a moderator looks for. For a family using outside support, the form is also the reason to keep the school informed, since the recorded interactions stay with the supervisor and outside sessions are additional practice rather than a substitute.

faqs.question: Our son's predicted TOK grade is a D. Is it worth paying to move it?
faqs.answer: Look at the Extended Essay prediction before deciding. Under the DP core points matrix, a D in TOK with an A in the Extended Essay gives two points, and moving TOK to a B would give three. The same D with a C in the Extended Essay gives nothing, and moving TOK to a B gives one point. Whether a block of sessions is worth buying depends entirely on which cell you are in. The exception is a predicted E, which is a failing condition for the whole Diploma regardless of subject points, and that is always worth addressing immediately.

faqs.question: Does a tutor need a MoHRE permit to review a TOK draft over video?
faqs.answer: If the tutor lives and works in the UAE and is paid for private tuition, the private tuition work permit introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 applies, and it is issued through MoHRE free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private sector employees, unemployed residents and university students. Tutoring without a permit attracts fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published. For a tutor living outside the UAE, MoHRE's eligibility list addresses people in the country, so ask MoHRE about any other arrangement.

faqs.question: Which two optional themes make the essay easier to argue?
faqs.answer: Your child does not choose: the school teaches two optional themes and those are the ones the course covered. Knowledge and technology and knowledge and language are the most commonly taught and give an essay accessible material. Knowledge and politics and knowledge and religion reward careful reading and punish opinion. Knowledge and indigenous societies is rarely chosen and therefore rarely seen by examiners, which helps a student willing to read properly. Whichever two your school taught, remember that prescribed titles ask about areas of knowledge, so the themes are a source of examples rather than the backbone of the argument.

faqs.question: Is TOK counted anywhere in a UAE Ministry of Education equivalency file?
faqs.answer: Equivalency is assessed on the certificate a student holds rather than on individual core components, so TOK is not counted as a subject. It matters indirectly and seriously: a grade E in TOK is a failing condition, which means the student is awarded Course Results rather than the Diploma, and the equivalency route for a Diploma student assumes an awarded Diploma. No IB points threshold is published on this page because the source we read states none; verify any figure on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate. IB Gram does not submit, process or guarantee an equivalency file.

faqs.question: How early in DP1 should TOK work start, and what should it look like?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families think, and lighter than they expect. In DP1 the useful work is the exhibition and the habit of treating a claim as something needing justification, not essay drafting. A student who reaches the end of DP1 able to turn a political or scientific story into a knowledge question will find title selection straightforward. Essay-specific work begins when the IB releases the prescribed titles for the session, and the first block is title selection rather than writing. Starting in DP2 is possible but narrows what any support can achieve.

faqs.question: My daughter's school has no TOK teacher this term. What are our options?
faqs.answer: Tell the DP coordinator in writing and ask what interim supervision arrangements are in place, because the recorded interactions and the formal comment are school responsibilities that do not disappear with a staff absence. This happens most often in schools running their first or second Diploma cohort, and three of the seven schools joining Dubai's 2026-27 intake are IB schools, so first-cohort TOK teaching is becoming more common rather than less. Outside support can cover the argument-level teaching in the meantime, but it cannot replace the supervisor the IB requires, and no provider should claim otherwise.

faqs.question: Can a TOK essay be built around my child's own Diploma subjects?
faqs.answer: Yes, and the strongest essays usually are. A student taking HL History has historiography available; a student taking Analysis and Approaches has proof and axioms; a Visual Arts student can argue about interpretation with real works in front of them. The common failure is the opposite of abstraction: an HL Chemistry student writes an accurate chemistry explanation and never asks how the knowledge was justified. The subject supplies the example, the area of knowledge supplies the argument, and the examiner is marking the second of those.

faqs.question: What should I check before paying anyone to look at a TOK draft?
faqs.answer: Four things. Whether the person has taken a TOK essay through a complete session before, rather than written essays generally. Whether they hold a current MoHRE private tuition work permit if they are tutoring from inside the UAE. Whether the written output of a session is questions and page references, or text a student could paste. And whether they accept that the school supervisor remains the person the IB holds responsible. A provider offering a finished piece of work at any price is offering your child a malpractice investigation, and the consequence falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: Where does the TOK deadline fall against Ramadan and the UAE term dates?
faqs.answer: In years when Ramadan sits in the spring term, it overlaps the stretch where TOK drafting and subject explorations collide. School days shorten and usable study hours move to after Iftar, so a 4pm session through that month is usually an hour nobody is present for. Front-load the structural decisions before Ramadan, hold one shorter post-Iftar session weekly through it, and put the pre-submission read in the week afterwards. The winter break is the largest uninterrupted block before submission; decide in advance whether sessions follow a family that travels.

faqs.question: Will a KHDA or ADEK inspection report tell me whether a school teaches TOK well?
faqs.answer: Not directly. Inspection reports judge provision across a school and are published per school by the authority, but they do not grade individual Diploma core components, and a strong overall rating says nothing about how many sessions the TOK teacher has taken essays through. Read the report for context, then ask the coordinator the specific question: how long has this teacher taught TOK, and how have the school's internal exhibition marks compared with final IB grades? That answer is more useful for your decision than any band on the cover.

faqs.question: How many hours does a TOK essay cycle usually take, and what do UAE families pay?
faqs.answer: Most families we work with buy between eight and fourteen hours across the whole cycle: two or three sessions on title selection, six to ten in a weekly clinic through drafting, and one longer pre-submission read. That is a different purchase from an open weekly subject slot. For market context, published UAE rates run from AED 45-150 at the budget end, AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor, and AED 200-450 for a core specialist, as published by those providers and checked in October 2026. Our own figure is quoted after the free consultation.

faqs.question: Can the TOK exhibition mark still be improved once it has been submitted?
faqs.answer: No. The exhibition is marked inside the school and a sample is moderated by the IB, and once the school has submitted there is nothing a family or a tutor can change. If the exhibition mark is already in and disappointing, the useful response is to put the remaining effort into the essay, which carries two thirds of the TOK grade and is read by an external examiner. That is the single most common reason families reach this page in DP2 rather than DP1, and it is a reasonable reason to start.

faqs.question: My son writes well in English but keeps scoring badly in TOK. Why?
faqs.answer: Because TOK is not marked on writing quality. A fluent essay that describes two perspectives, reports what people believe and reaches a balanced conclusion is doing the wrong task well. The examiner is looking for an argument about how knowledge is produced and justified, with claims that have counterclaims strong enough to be a genuine problem, and specific examples carrying the argument rather than illustrating it. Strong writers are often the hardest students to redirect, because the draft reads convincingly and nothing looks broken. The fix is structural and it takes several sessions.

faqs.question: Do lessons ever happen in person anywhere in the UAE?
faqs.answer: No. Every lesson for a UAE family runs one-to-one over live video, in Gulf Standard Time, with the student sharing their own document on screen. IB Gram has no office, centre or branch in the UAE, and home visits are offered only in India. For TOK specifically the online model is an advantage rather than a compromise: supervision experience in this component is thin in any one emirate, and a family in Al Ain, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain gets the same specialist a Dubai family would, at a session time chosen for the student.

ib-tok-essay-help.closingHeading: Start with the title, not the draft
ib-tok-essay-help.closingBody: If the prescribed titles for your child's session are out, the next useful hour is spent choosing between them against the examples they actually hold. If the titles are not out yet, the next useful hour is spent on the habit the examiner rewards: turning a claim into a question about how it was justified. Either way, book the free trial lesson, bring whatever exists, and let the session run on the real work. We will tell you honestly whether a block can still change the grade, which cell of the points matrix you are sitting in, and whether a specialist is genuinely free at your times. If not, we will say so rather than book you anyway.

intro.heading: The exhibition is marked long before anyone timetables an exam
paragraphs: Most searches for IB TOK exhibition help in the UAE arrive in the middle of DP1, usually in the fortnight after a TOK teacher has said the words "your objects are due". By then the task has stopped being abstract. Your child has to choose three objects, connect all three to one of the thirty-five IA prompts published by the IB, photograph them, and write a commentary of no more than 950 words that explains what each object is, where it sits in the real world, and why it answers that prompt. The grade for all of it comes from one ten-mark instrument.

That is a document task with a fixed ceiling, and it behaves nothing like exam revision. There is no past paper to drill. A student who has learned to revise by doing questions has no habit that transfers. What the exhibition rewards is specificity: one object, one date, one owner, one place, and a justification that points at evidence rather than restating the prompt. Students who lose marks here almost never lose them for weak writing. They lose them for choosing objects so general that no real-world context exists to describe.

The second thing families discover late is who owns the calendar. The IB sets the submission window for the school; the school's TOK teacher and DP coordinator set the date your child actually has to meet, and that internal date typically sits several weeks earlier. In the UAE this matters more than it does in a European timetable, because the exhibition term collides with Ramadan in some years, with National Day and winter break in others, and always with the Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies lessons that KHDA requires every Dubai private school to run alongside its licensed curriculum.

So this page is organised as a countdown. It starts with what the task is, then works backwards from the upload date in weeks — what should be settled by week ten, what cannot be left past week four, and the two things that still move a mark in the final seven days. Every table on the page is either the task itself, the calendar, the marking, the market rate, or the regulator who sits above the school. None of it is a promise about a grade, because no one can honestly make one.

IB Gram delivers all of this as one-to-one tuition over live video. There is no visit to a UAE address; home visits are a service we run only in India. For a 950-word commentary that is an advantage rather than a compromise: the draft is open on screen, the tutor and the student are in the same paragraph at the same time, and a Sharjah family gets a Theory of Knowledge tutor in the UAE time zone who has actually taught the course, instead of whoever covers their area. A free trial lesson comes first, with no card details taken, so you can see the work before you commit to a block.

ib-tok-exhibition-help.programmesIntro: Theory of Knowledge exists only in the Diploma Programme, but the habits it tests are built earlier and the word "exhibition" appears in two different programmes. Parents regularly book TOK support for a child who is actually facing the PYP exhibition, which is a different task with different rules.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: TOK runs across both DP years as a core requirement alongside the Extended Essay and CAS. The exhibition is normally taught and submitted in DP1; the TOK essay, written against one of six prescribed titles released by the IB, belongs to DP2. The exhibition carries one third of the TOK grade and the essay the other two thirds, and the two together with the Extended Essay decide up to three points on top of the six subject grades.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools schedule the exhibition unusually early, often finishing it before the DP1 summer, because the second year is crowded with Internal Assessments and the Extended Essay. That compresses the whole task into one or two terms. A DP1 student in Dubai or Abu Dhabi who starts thinking about objects in the week the deadline is announced has already lost the planning weeks that make the commentary easy to write.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: MYP has no TOK and no exhibition. Its capstone is the Personal Project in MYP Year 5, assessed against its own criteria, plus interdisciplinary units that ask students to connect subjects. The transferable skill is the one the exhibition later needs: making a claim about an object or a source and then justifying it with evidence rather than opinion. Students who were never pushed on that in MYP find the exhibition's justification requirement genuinely new.
programmes.countryNote: A large share of UAE IB schools run MYP straight into DP, so the gap between a Personal Project in May and TOK objects the following January can be eight months. Where a school instead offers IGCSE in Years 10 and 11, students arrive in DP1 having been assessed almost entirely on recall and method, and the exhibition is the first task that asks them to argue about knowledge itself.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP exhibition is the Year 6 culminating project: a collaborative inquiry presented to the school community, assessed against the programme's own expectations rather than any IB mark scheme. It shares a name with the TOK exhibition and nothing else. There is no 950-word ceiling, no IA prompt, no external moderation and no contribution to a diploma grade. Support looks like inquiry coaching and presentation practice, not commentary review.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai and Abu Dhabi schools run PYP exhibitions in the spring term, which is why a parent searching for exhibition support in February may be looking at either task. If your child is in Year 6, the page you want is about inquiry and presentation. If your child is in DP1 and a TOK teacher has mentioned IA prompts, you are in the right place.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP core includes Personal and Professional Skills, a Reflective Project, language development and service learning. It does not include Theory of Knowledge, so CP students never sit an exhibition or a TOK essay. The Reflective Project asks for an ethical dilemma arising from the student's career-related study, which has a surface resemblance to TOK and a completely different assessment structure.
programmes.countryNote: CP is offered by only a handful of UAE schools, which is why its requirements are frequently misdescribed in tutoring enquiries. If your child is on CP and has been asked for objects and an IA prompt, check with the DP coordinator before booking anything: either the school runs both programmes and the message was for a DP cohort, or the task has been misnamed.

ib-tok-exhibition-help.subjectsIntro: The exhibition is anchored in one TOK theme and draws on the areas of knowledge the course covers. Choosing the theme is what narrows the field of objects from everything to something a student can argue about in 950 words, so this is where a first session usually goes.

subjects.name: Knowledge and the knower (core theme)
subjects.description: The core theme asks how the knower's own position shapes what they accept as knowledge. Most exhibitions sit here because the objects can be personal: a document, a family possession, a school report. The risk is the opposite of generic — commentaries drift into autobiography and stop analysing the prompt.

subjects.name: Knowledge and technology (optional theme)
subjects.description: The most popular optional theme in UAE classrooms, partly because digital objects are easy to source and timestamp. A specific post, a recommendation feed, a dataset or a piece of software all qualify. Students who choose this theme must resist making the commentary a general argument about social media.

subjects.name: Knowledge and language (optional theme)
subjects.description: Strong ground in a country where most students work in English and live in Arabic, Hindi, Malayalam, Tagalog or Russian. Translated documents, bilingual signage and untranslatable terms make excellent objects because the real-world context is immediate and the knowledge claim is visible in the object itself.

subjects.name: Knowledge and politics (optional theme)
subjects.description: Powerful but demanding. Objects need to be specific artefacts — a named treaty page, a ballot, a published figure — and the commentary must analyse how knowledge is produced and contested rather than taking a political position. Teachers in the UAE usually steer students towards documents and data over contemporary controversy.

subjects.name: Knowledge and religion (optional theme)
subjects.description: Chosen less often, and handled carefully. The task is epistemological: how religious knowledge is justified, transmitted and interpreted. The commentary analyses the processes around an object rather than evaluating belief. Students taking Islamic Education alongside the diploma often have unusually good material here.

subjects.name: Knowledge and indigenous societies (optional theme)
subjects.description: The least-used theme and therefore the least generic. Objects tied to transmitted, place-based knowledge work well, and UAE students have genuine access to them through heritage collections and oral tradition. Research load is higher, so this theme suits a student who starts early.

subjects.name: The natural sciences (area of knowledge)
subjects.description: Supplies objects about method, measurement and replication: an instrument, a retracted paper, a calibration certificate. Science students often pick these and then write about the science instead of the knowledge question, which is the single most common way a promising object produces a middle-band commentary.

subjects.name: The human sciences (area of knowledge)
subjects.description: Census forms, survey instruments and published indicators make precise objects with datable contexts. The strength of this AOK for the exhibition is that the object usually embodies a methodological choice, and a methodological choice is exactly what an IA prompt about evidence or certainty wants examined.

subjects.name: Mathematics (area of knowledge)
subjects.description: Harder to object-ify and therefore distinctive when done well: a proof as printed in a named edition, a geometric pattern on a specific building, an abacus with a provenance. Students must avoid turning the commentary into mathematics; the assessment is about how mathematical knowledge is justified.

subjects.name: History (area of knowledge)
subjects.description: The most reliable source of good exhibition objects because every historical artefact arrives with a date, a place and a chain of custody. UAE students have strong local material, from pearling-era implements to founding-era documents, and local material is by definition not what every other candidate has chosen.

subjects.name: The arts (area of knowledge)
subjects.description: Specific works, not genres. A named painting in a named collection, a particular recording, one photograph. The frequent error is choosing a famous work whose context is so well rehearsed that the commentary cannot say anything a marker has not read twenty times.

subjects.name: TOK essay planning (DP2 follow-on)
subjects.description: Not part of the exhibition, but the reason families keep a TOK slot after upload. The essay responds to one of six prescribed titles, runs to a published word ceiling, and is marked outside the school. Families who plan TOK essay and exhibition planning together avoid rebuilding the habit from scratch a year later.

ib-tok-exhibition-help.regionsTitle: Where your child's school sits, and who sets the date there
ib-tok-exhibition-help.regionsIntro: The exhibition deadline is always set inside the school, but the regulator above the school decides how fees, calendars and mandatory subjects are approved, and that shapes which weeks are actually available for the work. Here is the practical position across the seven emirates.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The largest DP cohort in the country and the tightest term calendar. KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in every private school alongside the licensed curriculum, so a DP1 week already carries lessons that do not count towards the diploma. Exhibition work has to fit around them.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. DP cohorts here are smaller per school and TOK is often taught by a single teacher, which means one person reads every commentary. IB DP1 TOK support in Abu Dhabi usually works best booked around the school's own draft-feedback date.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with fewer IB World Schools and longer school-run distances. Families here feel the travel argument most sharply: a visiting tutor prices the drive into the hour, while a live video session costs the same at 8pm as at 4pm and does not depend on who happens to live nearby.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. TOK exhibition help for Sharjah students is frequently booked late because the exhibition is taught in a term already carrying heavy coursework from other subjects.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. IB provision is limited, so some Ajman families have a child at a Dubai or Sharjah school with a commute of an hour each way. That commute is the reason an online slot at 7.30pm is often the only realistic session time.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which also approves curricula and assessment methods. Distance from the Dubai tutoring market is absolute for an in-home visit and irrelevant for a video lesson, which is why northern-emirates families are among the clearest beneficiaries of online delivery.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under the federal Ministry of Education. East-coast families typically have the fewest local options for a subject as narrow as Theory of Knowledge, and the exhibition is narrower still. Matching on specialism rather than postcode is the whole point of the model.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised by the Ministry of Education, and the smallest private-school market in the country. Where no local tutor teaches TOK at all, we say so before you book rather than after, and the free trial lesson is where that gets established.

ib-tok-exhibition-help.modesIntro: Exhibition work has a shape: a research phase, a choosing phase, a writing phase and a review phase. The format that suits it changes as the deadline approaches, so most families use more than one of the four below across a single term.

modes.description: A single 60-minute session, usually booked eight to ten weeks out, that ends with a shortlist of candidate objects and one IA prompt the student can defend. The student does the choosing; the tutor's job is to ask why each object is that object and not a category, and to stop a weak shortlist from consuming a whole term.

sections.heading: What a UAE parent is actually asking for when they search for TOK exhibition help
paragraphs: The search is almost always triggered by a specific message from school, and the question underneath it is narrow: what exactly has my child been asked to produce, and is what they have produced any good? The answer is that the TOK exhibition is a single document plus three images. Your child chooses three objects, links all three to one IA prompt from the thirty-five the IB publishes, and writes a commentary of no more than 950 words that identifies each object, places it in a specific real-world context, and justifies why it answers that prompt.

Three details catch families out. The first is that all three objects share one prompt — students who pick a different prompt for each object have misread the task and usually have to restart. The second is that the objects must be particular things, not kinds of thing: a specific passport issued to a specific person on a specific date, not "passports". The third is that the commentary is not an essay with an introduction and a conclusion. It is three justifications, written tightly enough that 950 words is comfortable rather than crushing.

What support looks like, then, is not content delivery. There is no syllabus to teach through. It is a sequence of questions that force specificity: whose object is this, when did it enter the world, what happened to it, what knowledge claim does its existence support, and what would count as evidence for the link you are asserting? A student who can answer those five questions about each of three objects has a strong commentary available to them. A student who cannot has a middle-band commentary no amount of editing will rescue.

The table below sets out the task element by element, with the error each element reliably produces and what a session actually does about it. It is the version of the task most UAE schools communicate in a single slide, expanded into the detail parents ask for afterwards.

sections.heading: The thirty-five IA prompts, grouped so a DP1 student can choose one in an afternoon
paragraphs: The IB publishes a fixed list of thirty-five IA prompts and students must use one of them unaltered. We do not reproduce the list here — it belongs to the IB and lives in the current TOK guide your child's teacher will have issued. What is useful is a map of the families the prompts fall into, because a student who knows which family they want can scan the official list in minutes instead of reading all thirty-five as if they were interchangeable.

Broadly, the prompts cluster around six concerns. There are prompts about evidence and what counts as adequate justification. There are prompts about certainty, doubt and the limits of what can be known. There are prompts about method and the tools knowledge is produced with. There are prompts about the knower's perspective, position and bias. There are prompts about values, ethics and responsibility in knowledge production. And there are prompts about change: how knowledge is replaced, revised, or quietly abandoned.

The choosing order matters more than the choice. Students who pick a prompt first and then hunt for objects to fit it almost always end up with one strong object and two forced ones. Students who assemble six or seven objects they genuinely know something about, and then ask which prompt all three of a subset could honestly serve, end up with a commentary that writes itself. The prompt is a lens, and lenses are chosen after you know what you want to look at.

One practical constraint: the prompt has to be answerable three times without repetition. If two of the three justifications would say the same thing in different words, the commentary will read as thin even if each object is well chosen. Testing for that in week eight is a twenty-minute job. Discovering it in week two of a three-week writing phase means starting the selection again with no time left.

sections.heading: Choosing three objects that can carry a 950-word commentary
paragraphs: Object selection is where the exhibition is won or lost, and it is the part of the task a tutor can help with most legitimately and most carefully. The student must choose; that selection is assessed. What a session does is interrogate candidates — and interrogation is teaching, not substitution. The test applied to every candidate object is the same: can you tell me, in three sentences, what this thing is, when and where it existed, and who had it?

Objects that pass that test share a property. They are instances, not classes. A grandparent's identity document issued in a named year passes. "Identity documents" does not. A specific recording of a specific performance passes. "Classical music" does not. Digital objects are explicitly acceptable and often excellent, because a post, a dataset or a software release carries a timestamp and a URL — the provenance is built in. What disqualifies an object is not its subject matter but the absence of a single real-world context to describe.

The second filter is distinctiveness. Nothing in the assessment rewards obscurity, but a commentary about a famous object has to work harder, because the marker has read the standard account of it many times. UAE students have an advantage here that they consistently fail to use: local material. Pearling-era implements, founding-era documents, a bilingual street sign, a school's own first enrolment register, a family's migration papers. These are objects with verifiable contexts that no other candidate in the cohort has chosen.

The last filter is practical. Each object needs an image the student can legitimately include, and a context they can check rather than assume. An object in a museum the student has visited is easier than one they have only read about. The table below is the triage we run on a shortlist in the first consultation.

sections.heading: The exhibition counted backwards from your school's upload date
paragraphs: Ask the school one question before you plan anything: what is the internal date by which the commentary must be with the TOK teacher? That date, not the IB's submission window, is the one your child has to meet, and in most UAE schools it sits between three and eight weeks earlier. Schools that read a draft before the internal date have a second, earlier deadline that matters just as much, and it is frequently communicated once, verbally, in a lesson.

With that date fixed, the work divides cleanly. Weeks ten to eight are research and shortlisting, and they are the weeks families skip. Weeks seven to five are selection and justification, done out loud before anything is drafted. Weeks four to two are writing, with a word budget per object agreed in advance. The final fortnight is review against the instrument and the mechanical checks — images, citations, file format, the school's submission platform. None of this requires more than one hour a week until the writing phase.

The counting-backwards habit also protects against the specific UAE problem of a term that is not as long as it looks. Between a winter break, National Day, an Eid holiday whose dates move, and the internal assessment calendar of six other subjects, a notional ten-week run frequently contains seven working weeks. A plan built on calendar weeks fails. A plan built on sessions and deliverables survives, because a missing week pushes a deliverable rather than collapsing the task.

sections.heading: Where the ten marks go, and what moves a commentary up a band
paragraphs: The exhibition is marked out of ten against a single global assessment instrument with five bands, by the school's own TOK teacher, and the school's marks are then externally moderated by the IB. There are no separate criteria letters to collect, which surprises families who have come through subject Internal Assessments with their lettered criteria and per-criterion mark allocations. One instrument, applied to the whole commentary, is the entire mechanism.

What the instrument rewards is not writing quality. It is whether all three objects are clearly identified, whether each is placed in a specific real-world context, and whether the link to the IA prompt is justified with explicit evidence. A commentary can be elegant and still sit in the middle bands because its links are asserted rather than argued. A plainer commentary that names its evidence for each of three links reads much higher, and this is the single most actionable thing a DP1 student can be told.

The diagnostic shortcut is to read each object's paragraph and ask: which sentence here is the justification? If the answer is "all of it" or "none of it", the paragraph is describing. A justification is identifiable — it contains a because, a therefore, or an appeal to something checkable. Students who learn to point at their own justification sentence stop producing the middle-band commentary almost immediately, because they can see the gap themselves.

sections.heading: How the exhibition sits inside the TOK grade and the diploma
paragraphs: The exhibition carries one third of the TOK grade. The TOK essay, written in DP2 against one of six prescribed titles released by the IB and marked by an examiner outside the school, carries the other two thirds. The two components produce a single letter from A to E. That letter is then read together with the Extended Essay grade to award up to three points on top of the six subject grades, using a matrix the IB publishes.

The consequence families need to understand early is asymmetric. A strong exhibition does not guarantee a strong TOK grade, because the externally marked essay weighs twice as much. But a weak exhibition is very hard to recover from, because the only remaining component is the one your child has least control over — a title they did not write, marked by someone who has never met them. The exhibition is the part of TOK where effort converts most directly into grade.

There is also a failing condition. A grade E in Theory of Knowledge or in the Extended Essay prevents the award of the diploma regardless of subject points. This is the reason a DP1 student who treats TOK as the course that can be ignored until it matters is taking a risk out of proportion to the time involved. An hour a week through one term is a small insurance premium against the only component that can void an otherwise good diploma.

sections.heading: Academic honesty on an internally assessed component: the line, and who draws it
paragraphs: The exhibition is marked inside the school, which makes the honesty question sharper than it is for an exam. Your child signs that the work is their own, the teacher authenticates it, and the IB moderates the result. A commentary containing sentences the student did not compose is a malpractice finding, and the consequence falls on the student rather than on whoever supplied the sentences. That asymmetry is why every tutoring arrangement for this component should have an explicit boundary.

Ours is simple and we state it on the page because the alternative is parents guessing. A tutor may ask questions, explain what a requirement means, challenge a weak justification, point at a paragraph and say which requirement it fails to meet, and confirm mechanical matters like word count and citation format. A tutor may not select objects for the student, supply justifications, compose or rewrite commentary text, or hand over a model commentary to work from. Any provider offering to supply finished assessed work is selling the student a malpractice risk.

Generative AI sits in the same frame. Unattributed machine-written text in a commentary is not a style problem; it is undisclosed authorship, and the IB and your child's school both have policies on it. The school's policy is the one that applies, and it is worth reading before the writing phase rather than during it. Using a tool to find candidate objects and then verifying each one independently is a different activity from having a tool produce the justification.

The school's own rules take precedence over anything on this page. If your child's TOK teacher sets a narrower limit on outside feedback than the IB's general position, that narrower limit is the operative one and we work inside it.
