process.description: Which school, which authority licenses it, which programme year your child is in and which board, if the school runs IGCSE alongside the IB. This is not administration. It determines the guide version, the internal deadline pattern and whether the problem in front of you is a subject gap or a transfer gap.

process.title: Name the subject, the level and what has already been tried
process.description: The specific subject and level, the last two grades, and what the school has already done about it. If a head of department has written to you about a particular criterion or topic, send that. A specialist reading one sentence from a teacher is better informed than one reading a paragraph of parental worry.

process.title: Ask the school what it already provides
process.description: Before you pay for anything, ask what intervention, clinic or catch-up provision exists and what the department thinks is costing the marks. Some of what families buy is already timetabled and unused. We would rather you book two subjects that need it than four, and this step is how that gets decided.

process.title: A free trial lesson with the subject specialist
process.description: One lesson, free, with the tutor your child would actually work with, not a sales call. It is a diagnostic: the specialist works through real material and tells you plainly what they think the gap is and roughly how long it takes. If the match is wrong, say so and we change the tutor before any money is involved.

process.title: Fix a slot that survives the school run and Ramadan
process.description: A weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time, set after the commute home rather than at the time that suits a timetable elsewhere. We agree in advance how the slot moves during shortened Ramadan hours and around examination weeks, so the first calendar collision is a scheduling note rather than a lost month.

process.title: A written record, reviewed every six to eight weeks
process.description: After each session the tutor records what was covered and what is still weak. Every six to eight weeks we look at whether the school's own assessment has moved. If it has not, we change the approach or the tutor, or we say honestly that the problem is not one tuition can solve.

whyPoints.title: Built around the system, not the brochure
whyPoints.description: The regulator that licenses your school, the mandatory subjects on your timetable, the entry deadline that closed in November and the equivalency rule that excludes Arabic from the count are the things that actually constrain a UAE family. This page names them with sources because they decide what tuition should be pointed at.

whyPoints.title: Independent of any school, group or authority
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no permit, licence, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and is not affiliated with any school named here. That independence is why we can tell you to ask your school for something free before paying us for anything.

whyPoints.title: Honesty boundaries written down before you book
whyPoints.description: What a tutor will do with an Internal Assessment or Extended Essay, and what they will refuse to do, is stated in writing before the first paid session. In a market where completed coursework is openly sold, a clear boundary is a service feature rather than a disclaimer.

whyPoints.title: Specialists matched to the programme, not to the postcode
whyPoints.description: Because lessons run over live video, the pool is not limited to tutors who can drive to your address by seven. A student in Fujairah and a student in Emirates Hills get the same access to a Higher Level specialist working from the current subject guide.

whyPoints.title: Continuity when the family moves
whyPoints.description: Transfers between schools and emirates are a defining feature of UAE schooling and the most common reason tuition starts. An online arrangement survives a change of address, a change of emirate and a change of school, which is exactly when a student can least afford to lose their tutor as well.

whyPoints.title: Numbers with a source and a date
whyPoints.description: Every figure here is attributed to the body or provider that published it, with the date it was read. Where a number could not be verified, including IB session dates and any IB equivalency threshold, this page says so and points to the official channel instead of guessing.

faqs.question: Only 7% of Dubai's private-school students take the IB. Does that limit who can tutor my child?
faqs.answer: It limits the local pool, not the available pool. Dubai had 387,441 private-school students across 227 schools in 2024-25, with UK curriculum at 37%, Indian at 26%, American at 14% and the IB at 7%, per the Dubai Media Office. A tutoring bench built from that market skews towards other boards, which is why families often get a tutor who knows the content but not how the component is marked. Because IB Gram teaches over live video, the match is made from specialists in the programme rather than from whoever is nearby, so the 7% figure stops being a constraint on your child.

faqs.question: Who approves the fees and the curriculum at a UAE private school?
faqs.answer: The emirate's authority, and in two emirates that power is explicit. Government guidance on u.ae states that Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Dubai's schools sit with KHDA, which confirmed on 22 May 2026 that fees would not increase for 2026-27 under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, which supervises licensing and accreditation. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised federally by the Ministry of Education. Check which authority is named on your school's licence, because its published guidance is the one that applies to you.

faqs.question: Does a UAE private school have to teach a UK or IB curriculum at all?
faqs.answer: No. Federal guidance states that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That is the rule that allows 17 different curricula to operate in Dubai alone and lets a school license the IB continuum, an IGCSE route, or both at once. It is also the rule behind the mandatory subjects on your child's timetable: whatever international curriculum a school is licensed for, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies sit alongside it. Confirm what your school is actually licensed to run on the regulator's own school listing.

faqs.question: We are moving from Dubai to Abu Dhabi part-way through the Diploma. What actually breaks?
faqs.answer: Three things, usually. The internal sequence changes, so topics your child has not met yet may already have been taught at the new school. Internal deadlines for the Internal Assessment and Extended Essay shift, and a draft can stall between an old supervisor and a new one. And the licensing authority changes from KHDA to ADEK, which affects paperwork rather than teaching. The academic damage is concentrated in one term and is fixable with bounded bridging work plus a written handover the receiving teacher can read. Ask both registrars, in writing, who holds the examination entry and what the new internal deadlines are before the move, not after.

faqs.question: My child switches from IGCSE to the Diploma in September. What should we fix over the summer?
faqs.answer: Not content. IGCSE students usually arrive with a solid content base and examination stamina. The gap is criterion-referenced assessment and a style of writing that evaluates rather than recalls, which is why strong IGCSE students often score mid-range on their first Diploma internal task and conclude they chose the wrong subject. A six-to-eight-week transition block on one subject's criteria, plus written-response structure, covers most of it. Choose the two subjects with the biggest gap rather than the two your child likes most, and get a written note of what was covered that the new teacher can read in September.

faqs.question: Our child came from a CBSE school after Class 10. Is the Diploma realistic?
faqs.answer: Usually yes, and the mathematics and science content is normally the strongest part of the profile. The gap is extended writing, evaluation, and coursework that is judged on process rather than on the final answer. The pattern is recognisable: top marks on mechanical questions, low marks on anything asking for judgement. Eight to ten weeks of deliberate work on written response and on what each criterion rewards usually closes it, and it is far cheaper to do before the first term than to repair after the first reporting round. Choose Higher Level subjects on evidence from that work, not on Class 10 marks alone.

faqs.question: Can my child's own school teacher tutor them privately?
faqs.answer: Treat that as the wrong place to start. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported to prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit's code of conduct has been reported to bar serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That reporting is press-sourced rather than quoted from the policy itself, so verify it against ADEK's current document before relying on the exact wording. The direction is clear enough. Ask the teacher for a department-level conversation about what is costing marks instead, which costs nothing and is often more useful.

faqs.question: Which Arabic stream will my non-Arab child be placed in, and can a tutor use the school's material?
faqs.answer: A non-Arab student is placed in Arabic as an additional language, and KHDA's mandatory-subject guidance requires schools to organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, stating that combined classes are strictly prohibited. For these subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. So useful support works within the school's own material, building productive vocabulary, sentence structure and the written forms the assessment asks for. A provider offering a parallel Arabic syllabus has not read the guidance.

faqs.question: When are exam entries actually made, and can a level be changed afterwards?
faqs.answer: Entries are made by the school, months before the papers. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, which tells you how early that autumn entry had to be lodged. Cambridge sits UAE candidates in a June series and a November series and closes entries for each one well before its first paper, with the operative date printed on your own centre's statement of entry. Changing a level after entry is a question for the examinations officer, not the class teacher, and the answer depends on the board and the series. Ask the school in writing well before the deadline, and ask in the same email whether a November entry is the realistic fallback if the change cannot be made in time for June. For IB components, get the registration and upload deadlines from the IB coordinator directly.

faqs.question: Our child sits the Cambridge November series rather than May. Does that change the plan?
faqs.answer: Yes, in two ways. The whole preparation cycle shifts, so revision peaks while other students are starting a new academic year, and results arrive on a different schedule: Pearson's November 2025 International GCSE results reached students on 22 January 2026, for example. There is also a zone question. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, says it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. Confirm the zone timetable with your centre and work from the official PDF.

faqs.question: What does the Ministry of Education count towards equivalency if my child has IGCSEs and an IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Ask the attestation channel which certificate they will assess before you apply, because the answer depends on which document is the qualifying one. For the British track the reported requirements are five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one A-Level at no less than E or two AS-Levels at the same grade. No IB points threshold is published here, because none has been read on an official Ministry source. Verify the IB position on moe.gov.ae. IB Gram does not perform, submit or guarantee equivalency for anyone.

faqs.question: What does my child's coordinator have to declare about outside help?
faqs.answer: Internally assessed work is submitted on the basis that it is the student's own, and a school supervisor is part of that process, meeting the student and recording how the work progressed. That is why outsourced coursework is detectable: a supervisor can tell whether a finished essay matches the student they supervised, and a student can be asked questions about their own work. Telling the coordinator that your child has a tutor is normal and generally welcomed. A tutor who teaches, questions and gives feedback on the student's own draft gives the coordinator nothing to worry about. One who supplies text creates a malpractice exposure for your child.

faqs.question: What happens to Extended Essay supervision if we change school in the second year?
faqs.answer: The supervision relationship does not travel with the student, and this is the part of a mid-programme move families underestimate. A new supervisor picks up an essay they did not scope, often with an internal deadline already close. Before you move, get the previous school's written record of the essay's progress, the research question as approved, and any supervisor comments. Then ask the receiving school's coordinator, in writing, how supervision will be allocated and what the new internal deadline is. Outside support at that point is useful for one thing only: reading the student's own draft and asking the questions a reader would ask.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send a tutor to a UAE address?
faqs.answer: No. Every lesson for a UAE family is one-to-one over live video, on a fixed weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time. Visits to a family's address are something IB Gram offers only in India. The trade is deliberate: instead of choosing from tutors who can drive to you and back in an evening, your child is matched with a specialist in the exact subject, level and guide version they are sitting. Published market tables price a visiting tutor at AED 180-500 an hour against AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor online, so the travel is a real cost as well as a real constraint.

faqs.question: We live in Ras Al Khaimah. Is there any IB support this far from the Dubai schools?
faqs.answer: Yes, and distance is precisely the case online delivery answers. Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. Diploma provision in the northern emirates is thinner than on the Dubai side, so the Higher Level subject combination a student wants may exist at one school, and a travelling specialist is not a realistic option at all. A live video session removes the drive from the equation entirely: the same specialist is available to a family in Ras Al Khaimah as to one in Dubai, on the same weekly slot.

faqs.question: What do you need to know about our school before the first lesson?
faqs.answer: Four things, and they take a minute. Which school and which authority licenses it, because that tells us the published requirements your child is working under. Which programme year, because the Diploma's first and second years need very different work. The subject and level, plus the last two grades. And anything a head of department has written to you about what is costing marks, which is worth more than any description a parent can give. With those, the trial lesson is a diagnostic with real material in it rather than a conversation about how things are going.

ib-tuition.closingHeading: Start with the system, then book the hour
ib-tuition.closingBody: If you take one thing from this page, make it the order of operations. Find out which authority licenses your child's school and what it has published. Ask the school what support already exists and what the department thinks is costing marks. Check who holds the examination entry and when it closes. Then, if an outside specialist is still the answer, book a free trial lesson with the subject teacher your child would actually work with, see what they say about the gap, and decide. Lessons run one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, with a written record you can take back to the school.

intro.heading: Why a proximity search is the wrong tool for an IB question
paragraphs: A search for IB tuition near me in the UAE assumes the useful variable is distance. For almost every other service that assumption holds. For the IB Diploma it does not, because the thing that governs your child's week is not geography but regulation. Dubai's private schools answer to KHDA. Abu Dhabi's and Al Ain's answer to ADEK. Sharjah's answer to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah's to its Department of Knowledge, and schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Two families living four streets apart can sit under different authorities if their children attend schools in different emirates, which happens constantly along the Dubai-Sharjah commute.

That authority decides more than inspection. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the regulator approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. In Dubai, KHDA sets which mandatory UAE subjects every private school must teach whatever international curriculum it is licensed for, down to how many minutes a week each one gets and which language it is taught in. None of that changes because a tutor lives in the next tower.

The second problem with proximity is supply. In 2024-25 Dubai had 387,441 pupils across 227 private schools offering 17 different curricula, and the International Baccalaureate accounted for seven per cent of that enrolment against 37 per cent for UK curricula, 26 per cent for Indian and 14 per cent for American, according to figures published by the Dubai Media Office in January 2025. The nearest capable tutor to your villa is therefore, on probability alone, an IGCSE or CBSE teacher. A Diploma family searching by radius is drawing from the wrong pool and will usually be offered a very good A-Level tutor for a course that is not A-Level.

What a Diploma student actually needs is somebody who knows the command terms of their subject, the internal assessment criteria their coordinator will apply, how many marks each paper carries, and the internal deadlines their own school has set. Those four things are completely independent of postcode. They are the reason IB Gram delivers one-to-one online IB tuition across the UAE rather than sending anybody to an address: online delivery lets us match a Higher Level Chemistry specialist to a family in Fujairah on the same terms as a family in Jumeirah.

This page is built around the system your family has to work inside. It names every regulator and what each one actually controls, sets out the mandatory UAE subjects sitting beside the Diploma and the rules governing how they may be taught, explains who the UAE permits to give a private lesson and how you verify it, shows the exam dates that are officially published and states plainly which ones are not, and compares what the market charges for a visiting tutor against live online delivery. Where a figure appears, its source and the month it was read appear with it.

ib-tuition-near-me.programmesIntro: The IB runs four programmes, and UAE schools are licensed for them separately. A school licensed for the Diploma may not offer the Middle Years Programme below it, which is why so many UAE students arrive in Year 12 from an IGCSE or American background. Support is shaped by which programme your child is actually enrolled in.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is inquiry-led and has no external examinations. Assessment is continuous and reported through learner profiles and the Year 6 exhibition. Support at this stage is about literacy, number fluency and the habit of explaining reasoning aloud, because the Middle Years Programme will ask for written justification rather than answers. Families usually come to tuition here for reading age, English as an additional language, or maths confidence before a transition.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE a PYP school still has to deliver the mandatory ministry subjects from the earliest years, and in Dubai those are organised in separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils. A non-Arab child in a PYP school is therefore learning Arabic as an additional language from the start, which is the single most common reason UAE primary families ask for support.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks work against subject criteria scored out of eight and converted to a 1-7 grade, which is the first point where UAE families meet criterion-based assessment. Students lose marks for failing to address a criterion rather than for being wrong. The Personal Project in the final year is the first piece of long-form independent work, and it carries the same honesty expectations as the Diploma core.
programmes.countryNote: Many UAE schools run the MYP only to Year 9 or 10 and then move students to IGCSE for two years before the Diploma, because parents want an external certificate on file. That shift matters for Ministry of Education equivalency later, since the British track counts accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects. Ask the school which route it is licensed for before Year 9 choices close.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject is graded 1-7 with up to three bonus points from the core, out of 45. Internal assessment is marked by the teacher against published criteria and moderated externally, so a strong piece badly matched to a criterion still loses marks.
programmes.countryNote: A Diploma student in the UAE carries the mandatory ministry subjects on the same timetable, sits exams through a school registered as a centre, and will need a Ministry of Education equivalency file before applying to a UAE university. The Diploma also runs across two calendar years that include Ramadan twice, which changes where revision realistically fits.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The CP combines at least two Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, personal and professional skills, service learning and a language development component. It suits students who want applied study with recognised academic subjects attached, and it is assessed through a mix of IB examinations for the DP courses and provider assessment for the career-related study.
programmes.countryNote: Only a small number of UAE schools are licensed for the CP, and its recognition for Ministry of Education equivalency and for UAE university entry should be checked case by case with the ministry and the admissions office rather than assumed. Tuition here tends to focus on the Diploma courses inside the CP, which are examined exactly as they are for a full Diploma candidate.

ib-tuition-near-me.subjectsIntro: These are the courses UAE families most often ask about, with what each one actually assesses. Where a subject exists at both levels, the Higher Level paper load is different rather than simply longer, and the internal assessment weighting shifts with it.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The algebraic route, expected by most engineering and physical science courses. Higher Level adds proof, complex numbers and deeper calculus, and allows a paper without technology. Marks are lost in method presentation rather than final answers, and in the exploration where students choose a topic too wide to develop against the criteria.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: The modelling and statistics route, technology-assumed throughout. It suits economics, business, psychology and design pathways. Students who choose it because it sounds easier often struggle with the statistical interpretation and the exploration, which demands real data handled honestly rather than a formula applied once.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Mechanics, waves, electricity, nuclear and energy production, with HL extension topics and a further paper. The internal investigation carries a significant share of the grade and is where most marks are recovered, because it rewards a controlled method and honest uncertainty treatment rather than an impressive result.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: The subject UAE families most often cannot staff locally at Higher Level. Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium carry the hardest marks, and the multiple-choice paper punishes gaps in definitions. The internal investigation needs a question narrow enough to measure something properly in the time available.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content-heavy with precise terminology expectations. Students lose marks writing around a command term rather than answering it, and in data-based questions where the graph is described instead of interpreted. HL adds plant biology, genetics depth and further physiology.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Microeconomics, macroeconomics, the global economy and development. Diagrams must be accurate, labelled and referred to in the prose to earn their marks. The portfolio of commentaries on real published articles is the component where planning time pays most, and where sources need recording as they are found.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Popular across UAE schools and frequently under-taught at Higher Level. Quantitative tools, the business research project and the case study paper all need practice under timed conditions. Strong candidates lose marks by writing general theory instead of applying it to the named organisation in front of them.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Textual analysis, the individual oral and, at Higher Level, the essay. Students with strong English frequently underperform here because the course rewards close reading of form and context rather than fluent opinion. The oral needs a global issue chosen early and defended with two texts.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: A language acquisition course sat by many UAE students whose schooling has been in English but whose first language is not. Productive skills carry most of the risk: the written task needs the right text type, register and audience, and the oral needs sustained interaction rather than a prepared speech.

subjects.name: Arabic A and Arabic B
subjects.description: Arabic appears in the Diploma as a language A or B and, separately, as a ministry-mandated subject on the same timetable. The two are assessed by different bodies to different standards, and conflating them is a common planning error in UAE schools that offer both.

subjects.name: Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay
subjects.description: Together worth up to three points and capable of failing a Diploma outright. TOK is assessed through an exhibition and a prescribed-title essay; the Extended Essay is a 4,000-word independent piece with a supervisor and recorded reflection sessions. Both are the student's own work, and both have internal school deadlines that arrive earlier than families expect.

ib-tuition-near-me.regionsIntro: Where you live changes which authority holds your child's school file, what that authority approves, and how thin the local pool of IB specialists is. It does not change who can teach your child, because sessions run over live video in every emirate.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: KHDA regulates the emirate's 227 private schools and publishes both inspection reports and the mandatory-subject requirements. IB tuition in Dubai is the most competitive market in the country, and also the one where school fees were held flat for 2026-27 under a KHDA announcement made in May 2026.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate and sets professional-ethics rules for school staff. Families asking about IB tuition in Abu Dhabi should know that a teacher at your child's own school may not be paid to tutor them privately.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory rather than a separate authority, which surprises families who assume an inland city has its own regulator. The local IB cohort is smaller than Abu Dhabi island's, so Higher Level sciences and the maths routes are routinely covered from outside the city.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Many Sharjah-resident families send children into Dubai schools, which means their household sits under one authority and their school file under another.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority. The practical effect is that inspection material and school-level documentation are less readily available to parents, so a tutor should be briefed from the school's own reports instead.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under federal Ministry of Education supervision, with the smallest private-school market in the country. Diploma students here are frequently the only candidate in their subject at Higher Level, which makes a national rather than local tutor pool the only workable answer.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Distance from the Dubai school cluster limits which visiting tutors will travel, which is precisely the constraint online delivery removes.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: On the east coast, supervised federally by the Ministry of Education. A family here searching by radius will usually find no IB specialist at all, and a session that depends on somebody driving over the mountains is the first thing to fail in exam term.

Dubai's intake for 2026-27 adds seven new private schools, three of them IB, creating 16,846 new places, so cohorts in individual subjects are shifting year on year.

sections.heading: What a search for IB tuition near me returns in a seventeen-curriculum market
paragraphs: A proximity search returns the tutors closest to you, weighted by whoever has paid for visibility. In Dubai, the emirate with the deepest market, that pool is shaped by what the schools actually teach: 227 private schools, 17 licensed curricula and 387,441 pupils in 2024-25, of which the International Baccalaureate accounted for seven per cent against 37 per cent UK, 26 per cent Indian and 14 per cent American, on figures published by the Dubai Media Office in January 2025.

Those proportions decide who is available locally. For every ten competent secondary tutors within driving distance of a UAE community, the arithmetic says roughly four know UK specifications best, between two and three know the Indian boards, one or two know American high-school courses, and fewer than one is a Diploma specialist. That last figure is not a complaint about quality. A first-class A-Level Chemistry teacher is a first-class A-Level Chemistry teacher, and the IB internal investigation is not an A-Level practical endorsement.

The difference shows up in the detail that earns marks. Diploma courses are assessed against published criteria with mark allocations per criterion, use command terms with fixed meanings, and carry an internally assessed component the school marks and the IB moderates. A tutor who has not worked inside that structure will teach the content well and leave the marks on the table, usually in the internal assessment and in the paper where command terms carry the weight.

The honest conclusion from the market data is that a Diploma family should search by subject and level first and by location not at all. That is why every lesson here runs over live video: it widens the pool from whoever lives nearby to whoever actually teaches the course, and it is the only way a family in Umm Al Quwain gets the same Higher Level cover as a family in Al Barsha.

sections.heading: Licensed, inspected, approved, supervised: five authorities and four different jobs
paragraphs: UAE parents use the word regulator loosely, and the five bodies involved do measurably different things. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. KHDA private school regulation in Dubai is described in its own terms as enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. The Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge each regulate private education in their emirate, and the Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The sharpest practical difference is in what gets approved rather than merely watched. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A school in those emirates does not simply choose its assessment arrangements; they are approved. ADEK private school licensing means a school's right to operate and its accreditation status sit with the authority, which is also why ADEK sets professional-ethics rules for staff, including a prohibition on paid private tutoring of pupils enrolled at a teacher's own school.

Underneath all five sits a federal baseline. Private schools are not obliged to follow any specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but they must comply with the ministry's general regulations. That single rule is why a British, American or IB school in any emirate still teaches the ministry subjects, and why the licensed curriculum and the mandatory subjects appear on the same timetable.

For a tuition plan this matters in three concrete ways. It tells you which body publishes material about your school, so a tutor can read it before the first lesson. It tells you whose rules govern a teacher who offers you private lessons. And it tells you which attestation channel your emirate uses when the Diploma finishes and the paperwork begins.

sections.heading: Seven new schools, 16,846 places, and who is actually free at five o'clock
paragraphs: Dubai's private school sector is growing fast enough to change tutor availability year on year. Six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose six per cent. For 2026-27 the emirate adds seven more private schools, four of them UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places. Those are figures published by KHDA, and they describe a genuine expansion of IB capacity.

Growth of that kind has an awkward side effect for families looking for help outside school hours. New schools staff themselves largely from existing ones, so experienced Diploma teachers move, often mid-cycle, and the teachers who move are exactly the people a local tuition market depends on. A tutor who was free at five o'clock in September may have taken a full timetable plus a coordinator role at a new school by January.

The second effect is on cohort size. Three new IB schools means more Diploma places, but spread thinly: a new school opening its first Diploma cohort may run Higher Level Chemistry for a handful of students with one teacher who also teaches Standard Level and the Middle Years Programme. That is not a failing school. It is an arithmetic constraint, and it is the single most common reason a UAE family who likes their school still wants outside subject support.

A radius search cannot see any of this. It returns whoever is both nearby and advertising, which in a growing market skews towards people with spare capacity rather than people with the exact subject expertise. Matching nationally, and teaching over video, means availability is a question about one named course rather than about who happens to live within twenty minutes of your community this term.

sections.heading: The subjects already on your child's timetable, and the rules that govern them
paragraphs: Whatever international curriculum a UAE private school is licensed for, Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory alongside it. In Dubai, KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 the equivalent point for schools whose year begins in April. These subjects are not an optional cultural add-on; they occupy real timetable minutes beside Diploma lessons.

The organisation rules are specific. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must run separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students, and combined classes for both groups are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language. Social Studies is taught primarily in Arabic for Arab students, and in the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arabs.

Instructional time is calculated in 40-minute lesson units. Schools may vary the length of individual lessons provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. That gives parents something checkable: if a timetable shows a mandatory subject in fifteen-minute fragments, the weekly total is worth asking about at a parents' evening.

For planning, the point is collision. A Diploma student in the UAE is carrying six IB subjects, the core, and these ministry subjects with their own assessments and deadlines. The weeks that break students are the ones where an internal assessment deadline, a mock paper and a mandatory-subject assessment land together. Mapping those three calendars onto one page in September is the cheapest piece of work a family can do.

sections.heading: The content rule, and what a tutor may legitimately put on screen
paragraphs: There is a rule about the ministry subjects that almost no tutoring page mentions, and it constrains what any honest provider can offer. For the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited. A tutor cannot bring their own Arabic or Islamic Education syllabus and teach that instead. Support means working with the content the school is required to deliver.

The credential position is equally concrete. Schools must ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects. That is a requirement on schools and their staff, and it is a useful question for a parent to ask about any Arabic tutor: what is your background in this specific curriculum, as opposed to in the language generally. A fluent speaker is not automatically equipped for a ministry-set assessment.

The same restraint applies to examination material across every subject. IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are the awarding bodies' copyright. A tutoring provider may reference them and link to the official source. Supplying them as downloads is not something we do, and a provider offering a package of papers and mark schemes is telling you something about how it handles rules generally.

What a session legitimately contains, then, is teaching: explanation, worked questions, practice the student does under supervision, and feedback measured against criteria the awarding body has published. Where the ministry sets the content, that content is what gets taught. Where a board publishes the criteria, those criteria are what feedback refers to. Both constraints make the support more useful, not less, because they keep it aligned with what is actually being marked.

sections.heading: Who the UAE permits to give a private lesson, and what to ask to see
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is permit-based. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and MoHRE's own service page lists it as the issuance of a new work permit for private tutor licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time. The permit is granted free of charge for two years, which removes the usual excuse that paperwork is too expensive to bother with.

Eligibility is broader than parents expect. It covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No schedule of amounts is published, so any figure you see quoted online for that penalty should be treated as unverified.

One permitted category comes with a condition worth refusing an offer over. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, and the permit's code of conduct likewise bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. If your child's subject teacher offers evening lessons for a fee, the correct answer is no, however convenient it seems and however good the teacher is.

A centre is a different legal object again. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs an Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which starts with initial approval, allows a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and is renewed annually at least thirty days before expiry. A centre holding that permit does not make the individual tutor in its classroom permitted, and an individual's permit does not license a centre. IB Gram holds neither of those permits and makes no claim of approval, accreditation or endorsement from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson.

sections.heading: The dates that are published, and the ones this page will not print
paragraphs: Three different organisations set dates that govern a UAE student's year, and only two of them publish in a form we are willing to restate. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level examinations in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSEs are available in May/June and November each year.

Entry deadlines sit months before an examination, and the cleanest UAE example is the series with a published end date: Pearson's Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and results for the equivalent November 2025 series reached students on 22 January 2026. Cambridge, the other board most UAE centres use, runs a June series and a November series here, not the February and March sitting it offers to India, and it closes entries for each one earlier in the same school year, with the exact day depending on which of six administrative zones your centre sits in. This page will not print a Cambridge day and month it cannot stand behind, because Cambridge itself says it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for a candidate who misses an exam after using the wrong one. The planning point survives without the precise date: a family starting support in the spring for the June series is starting after the decisions about tier and subject have already been filed.

Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, and it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, because Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone timetable was used. This is why two cousins at different UAE schools can sit the same paper at different times. On the Pearson side, the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

For the IB itself this page publishes no dates at all. The IB's own site blocks automated checking, and a date restated from a secondary source is exactly the sort of detail that turns into a missed deadline when it drifts. Confirm every IB session, upload and results date with your child's IB coordinator or on ibo.org, and treat any tutoring site that prints IB dates without naming its source with the same caution you would apply to a flight time.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, track by track
paragraphs: Everything above concerns the two years of school. Ministry of Education equivalency concerns what the certificate is worth afterwards, and it is the part of the UAE system families discover latest. Equivalency is the process by which a school-leaving certificate from an international curriculum is recognised for use in the UAE, and it is handled by the ministry and the attestation channel in your emirate rather than by a school or a tutoring provider.

For the British track the published requirements are specific. A student must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five required subjects. A page currently ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the published clarification says five, and the difference is a whole year of subject choices.

For the American track, English proficiency is shown by a score of 5 in the academic IELTS, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying. For the IB Diploma, no points threshold is published in the source we were able to read, so this page publishes none. Check it on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate, and distrust any figure that appears without a ministry link beside it.

Two practical notes. Equivalency is a regulatory process, not a teaching one, and tutoring is not required for it: any page implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency. And the paperwork is easier to start before results day than after, because attested transcripts and school leaving certificates are faster to obtain while your child is still enrolled and the school office is still open for the year.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor at a UAE address against one-to-one over live video
paragraphs: The market gives you a straight choice, and both options have real costs. Published rates read in October 2026 put budget online tuition at roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik advertising from AED 45 to AED 65 and Tutopiya from AED 33 to AED 52. A qualified subject tutor online sits around AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. A visiting tutor including travel runs from about AED 180 to AED 500, on Bestimate's 2026 rate table for Dubai and on home-tutor advertising. Specialists are quoted at AED 200 to AED 450 and above, with TutorChase publishing AED 270, and premium or examiner-labelled tutors reach AED 500 to AED 650, where BartyED's AED 650 sits.

Monthly packaging tells the same story more plainly. Online packages advertised at AED 799 a month for eight sessions sit against in-home packages of AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits. Bestimate's monthly estimates for a weekly one-hour session run AED 240 to AED 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to AED 1,200 in the middle, and AED 1,000 to AED 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. None of these are IB Gram prices; they are what the market published, and they are quoted here because no competitor page in this search publishes any AED figure at all.

Set that beside the school fee. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under the emirate's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion. A frozen fee does not free up money automatically, but it does mean a tutoring decision made this year can be costed against a known school bill rather than a moving one.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one tuition to UAE families over live video, and does not send anybody to a UAE address; home visits are part of what we offer in India only. The case for that is in the table rather than in adjectives. A visiting tutor costs more per hour, consumes a further thirty to ninety minutes of an evening in traffic, imposes a two-hour minimum often enough to be normal, and draws from whoever lives nearby. Live video costs less per hour, starts on time, and draws from whoever teaches the course.

sections.heading: Academic honesty, and the line a paid tutor does not cross
paragraphs: The Diploma core and every internal assessment carry an honesty declaration, and the student signs it. Candidates confirm the work is their own, and the supervisor or coordinator confirms that, to the best of their knowledge, it is. That makes the question of what outside support may include a question about the Diploma's validity rather than about etiquette. A breach is investigated as malpractice, and the consequences fall on the student.

In practice the line is clear once stated. A tutor may teach the content, explain what a criterion is asking for, question a research question until it is narrow enough to answer, show how data should be presented, point at a paragraph and say that it does not yet address the criterion, and insist on sources being recorded as they are found. A tutor may not supply sentences for submission, restructure the work so the words stop being the student's, or produce any part of an assessed piece. The student does the work; the tutor makes the work better by teaching.

One competitor in this search sells finished internal assessments at AED 3,750. That is the purchase most likely to cost a student their whole Diploma, and it is worth knowing it exists so you can recognise it: the signs are a price quoted per assessment rather than per hour, a promised word count, and a delivery date instead of a lesson time. Anything sold by the deliverable rather than by the session is selling the wrong thing.

A tutor who works this way also leaves your child's coordinator with accurate answers. When the coordinator asks whether outside support was used, the honest reply is that a tutor taught the subject and gave feedback against published criteria on work the student produced. That answer creates no problem for anybody, which is the entire point of drawing the line before the first session rather than during an investigation.

process.title: Tell us the school, the emirate and the subject
process.description: The first message needs three things: which school your child attends, which subjects and levels are the problem, and which session they are sitting. The emirate tells us which authority holds the school file; the subject and level tell us which specialist to look for. Guessing any of these wastes the trial lesson.

process.title: A free trial lesson, with the conditions stated
process.description: One lesson at no charge with the proposed tutor, no card details taken and no obligation to continue. It is a teaching session rather than a sales call: the tutor diagnoses where marks are being lost and says what a term of work would cover. If the match is wrong, say so and nothing is owed.

process.title: The match, and what we tell you about the tutor
process.description: You are told which course the tutor teaches, how long they have taught it, and which board specifications they work with. We do not describe anyone as an examiner without evidence of current status, and we do not claim regulator approval for any tutor. Ask to see the private tuition work permit before the first paid lesson.

process.title: A plan pinned to your school's dates
process.description: The schedule is built backwards from fixed dates: your school's internal coursework deadlines, its mock window, the awarding body's entry deadline and the examination series. Mandatory ministry subject assessments go on the same calendar, because those are the weeks where three deadlines collide and something gets dropped.

process.title: Termly review, and honest unavailability
process.description: Every term we look at whether the hours are still buying marks, and in which subject. If no specialist is free for a niche subject and level in the week you need, we say so rather than substituting somebody from a neighbouring subject. A waiting time you can plan around beats a tutor who cannot teach the course.

whyPoints.title: Matched by subject and level, not by postcode
whyPoints.description: The tutor is chosen because they teach your child's exact course, not because of where they live. For a UAE family that is the difference between a Higher Level Chemistry specialist and the best available A-Level teacher within a twenty-minute drive, and online delivery is what makes the first option possible everywhere in the Emirates.

whyPoints.title: Every figure carries its source and its date
whyPoints.description: The AED ranges on this page are market rates read in October 2026, attributed to the provider or rate table that published them. School and enrolment numbers come from KHDA and the Dubai Media Office. Where no source exists, as with IB session dates and an IB equivalency threshold, this page says so and publishes nothing.

whyPoints.title: No regulator endorsement claimed, because none is held
whyPoints.description: IB Gram makes no claim of approval, accreditation, licensing or partnership involving KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no office, centre or branch in the UAE. We explain what each body does so you can check our account against theirs.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line is drawn before the first lesson
whyPoints.description: Teaching, questioning and criterion-based feedback on work the student has produced. No part of an assessed piece is produced for a candidate, and no past papers or mark schemes are supplied as downloads because they belong to the awarding bodies. This is stated upfront so your child's coordinator declaration stays accurate.

whyPoints.title: Scheduling built for the UAE week
whyPoints.description: Sessions run in Gulf Standard Time around the Monday-to-Friday school week, the school-bus timings that decide when a child is actually home, and the shortened days of Ramadan, when post-Iftar slots work better than late afternoon ones. Lessons continue through the summer for families who stay, and pause for families who travel.

faqs.question: Is IB tuition near me the right search in a country where my child's school may be in another emirate?
faqs.answer: It is the search parents type, so it is worth answering honestly: it returns proximity, and proximity is not the useful variable here. Thousands of UAE families live in one emirate and school their children in another, which already separates home from the authority that regulates the school. What decides whether tuition works is whether the tutor teaches your child's exact subject and level and knows the criteria their coordinator applies. That is independent of distance. Search by subject, level and session instead, and let the lesson come over live video.

faqs.question: What is the difference between a UAE school being licensed, inspected and supervised?
faqs.answer: They are three different jobs done by different bodies. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, which concerns a school's right to operate. KHDA describes its role in Dubai as enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education, which is where inspection sits. Sharjah's authority and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge regulate private education and approve fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. In Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools. Knowing which applies tells you where to look for published material about your school.

faqs.question: Is IB Gram approved, accredited or licensed by KHDA, ADEK or the Ministry of Education?
faqs.answer: No, and any tutoring provider telling you otherwise should be asked for a permit number. A KHDA Educational Services Permit is a specific instrument issued to training institutes with premises and staff in Dubai, renewed annually and requested at least thirty days before expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit, operates no premises in the UAE, and claims no relationship with any regulator or awarding body. What the permits do cover is individual tutors: ask the person teaching your child for their MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is the document that genuinely applies to them.

faqs.question: Does the authority that regulates our school also approve its fees and assessment methods?
faqs.answer: In two emirates, yes, explicitly. The Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. So a Sharjah school's assessment arrangements are approved rather than freely chosen, and it is reasonable to ask the school how that shapes internal assessment timing. In Dubai, KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not increase for 2026-27 under the emirate's second economic incentives package. Fee regulation and academic regulation are handled by the same authority, which is why parents meet both in one letter.

faqs.question: Seventeen curricula are taught in Dubai's private schools, so how do I find which one my child's school is licensed for?
faqs.answer: Ask the school directly and check the regulator's published material for the emirate, which names the licensed curriculum for each school. The distinction matters because some schools are licensed for one curriculum to Year 11 and another in the sixth form, and the tutoring your child needs in Year 11 may not be the tutoring they need in Year 12. Dubai alone had 227 private schools offering 17 curricula in 2024-25, with UK provision at 37 per cent of enrolment and the IB at seven, so assuming an IB school because it offers the Diploma later is a common error.

faqs.question: Three of Dubai's seven new schools for 2026-27 are IB schools. Does that make a tutor easier to find?
faqs.answer: Eventually yes, immediately no. The expansion creates 16,846 new places and follows six openings in 2025-26 with enrolment up six per cent, which genuinely increases IB capacity in the emirate. In the short term it moves experienced Diploma teachers between schools and produces first-year cohorts where one teacher covers several levels of a subject. That tightens local tutor availability in exactly the subjects families need most. A national pool reached over live video is less exposed to that churn than a search limited to whoever lives in your community this term.

faqs.question: How much weekly lesson time must a mandatory UAE subject be given?
faqs.answer: KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time in 40-minute lesson units. Schools may vary the length of individual lessons as long as the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run for at least 25 minutes. That gives you something checkable at a parents' evening: if the timetable shows Arabic or Islamic Education in very short fragments, ask how the weekly total is reached. These subjects are mandatory in all Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, with implementation required from the start of the 2025-26 academic year.

faqs.question: Which parts of Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies can a tutor legitimately help with?
faqs.answer: The teaching, not the syllabus. For these subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is prohibited, so a tutor cannot substitute their own programme. Support means working through the content the school must deliver: grammar and extended writing in Arabic, terminology and source texts in Islamic Education, and written answers in the correct language of instruction. It also means timetable work, because mandatory-subject assessments often land in the same weeks as Diploma internal assessment deadlines, and that collision is what families ask for help with most.

faqs.question: Our daughter sits in the non-Arab Arabic stream. Can tuition move her into the first-language stream?
faqs.answer: No, and no tutor should imply it can. KHDA requires schools to organise separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes are prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Placement is the school's decision under those rules. What tuition can do is raise attainment inside the stream she is in, which is assessed on its own terms, and build the script, vocabulary and speaking confidence that make the assessed tasks less daunting. Any change of stream is a conversation with the school.

faqs.question: Does an Arabic or Islamic Education tutor need the same approval my child's schoolteacher needs?
faqs.answer: Schools are required to ensure that all their teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate KHDA approval for those subjects. That obligation sits on the school and its staff, not on a private tutor, but it tells you what to ask about. A private tutor needs the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and separately needs real familiarity with the ministry-set content your child is actually assessed on. Fluency in Arabic is not the same qualification as experience with the prescribed curriculum, and the question to ask is about the second.

faqs.question: Which official websites should I read myself before trusting a tutoring company's claims?
faqs.answer: Five are enough. u.ae sets out which authority regulates private schools in each emirate. mohre.gov.ae carries the private tutor licensing service and the permit rules. web.khda.gov.ae publishes Dubai's mandatory-subject requirements and training-institute permit conditions. moe.gov.ae holds the equivalency requirements. For examinations, cambridgeinternational.org, qualifications.pearson.com and ibo.org publish the only authoritative timetables. Any claim on a tutoring site that cannot be checked against one of those pages should be treated as marketing. That includes claims about our own service, which is why this page names its sources.

faqs.question: Why does this page quote other companies' hourly rates instead of your own?
faqs.answer: Because quoting the market is honest and quoting a single rate out of context is not. UAE tutoring prices depend on level, format, session length and how close the examination is, so one number would mislead more than the ranges do. Published rates read in October 2026 run from about AED 45 an hour at the budget online tier to AED 650 for premium named tutors, with qualified subject tutors online around AED 150 to AED 300. Your own figure comes from the consultation after a free trial lesson, quoted against the subjects and frequency you actually need.

faqs.question: If every lesson is online, why does my emirate matter at all?
faqs.answer: Because your emirate decides the rules your child studies under, even though it no longer decides who teaches them. It determines which authority holds the school file and publishes material a tutor can be briefed from, whether assessment methods are approved locally, which attestation channel you will use for Ministry of Education equivalency, and in Abu Dhabi whether a particular teacher may be paid to tutor your child. The emirate sets the context; live video removes the geography. Those two facts are the reason this page is organised around regulation rather than around neighbourhoods.

faqs.question: What information do you need about our child, and what will you not ask us to send?
faqs.answer: We ask for the school, the emirate, the subjects and levels, the examination session, and a plain description of where marks are being lost. If you have a recent mock paper or a report comment, that shortens diagnosis usefully. We do not need a photograph, a passport copy, a full academic history or medical information to arrange a trial lesson, and you should be wary of any provider that asks for those before teaching anything. UAE personal data law applies to information about minors, and less collected means less to protect.

faqs.question: Our school teaches a UK curriculum to Year 11 and the Diploma afterwards. Which tutor do we need now?
faqs.answer: In Year 11 you need an IGCSE specialist for the board your school actually enters, because those grades are external, they feed Ministry of Education equivalency on the British track, and they decide sixth-form subject choices. From the summer before Year 12 the requirement changes completely: criterion-marked internal assessment, command terms, Higher and Standard Level paper structures and the Diploma core. Many UAE schools run exactly this route, and the handover summer is the cheapest time to close the gap. Tell us which year your child is in and the match changes accordingly.

faqs.question: How long does it take to confirm whether a specialist is free for the subject and slot we want?
faqs.answer: For mainstream Diploma subjects at Standard Level, usually a day or two, because the pool is national rather than limited to your emirate. For Higher Level sciences, the two maths routes and less common languages it can take longer, particularly for an early-evening Gulf Standard Time slot, which is the busiest part of the week. If nobody suitable is free we tell you the waiting time instead of offering a tutor from an adjacent subject. A date you can plan around is more useful than a substitution that wastes a term.

ib-tuition-near-me.closingHeading: Start with the system, then book the lesson
ib-tuition-near-me.closingBody: An IB family in the UAE is working inside a school system with five regulators, a mandatory set of ministry subjects, a permit regime for private tutors and an equivalency process at the end of it. None of that is visible on a map of nearby tutors. Tell us which school your child attends, which emirate it sits in, and which subjects and levels are losing marks, and we will arrange a free trial lesson with a specialist in that exact course, delivered one-to-one over live video in a Gulf Standard Time slot. If the match is wrong, say so after the trial and nothing is owed.

ib-tutor.tutorsIntro: The profiles below are IB Diploma and MYP specialists who teach UAE students online each week. Each one lists the subjects and levels they examine at, the syllabus they teach from, and the hours they hold open on Gulf Standard Time. Read the level before the biography.

intro.heading: Nobody publishes the price, so here it is
paragraphs: Ask six UAE tutoring providers what an IB tutor costs and three of them will not answer. We fetched and read the pages ranking for this search in October 2026: half publish no figure at all, and the two that do quote US dollars, a currency no family in Dubai or Abu Dhabi pays a tutor in. One competitor's own frequently-asked-questions block poses the question and then declines to answer it. That silence is not modesty. It is how a quote of AED 400 an hour gets accepted by a parent who had no way of knowing AED 220 would have bought the same lesson.

So this page starts with the number. IB tuition rates in AED, across the UAE, split by tier and format, with the provider who publishes each band named beside it. Market rates for a qualified subject specialist teaching online run roughly AED 150 to AED 300 an hour. An IB, IGCSE or A-Level specialist sits closer to AED 200 to AED 450. An in-home one-to-one visit, once the tutor's travel is priced in, runs AED 180 to AED 500. A named examiner at the premium end has been advertised at AED 650. Those are market figures from published competitor pages and from Bestimate's Dubai rate survey, not IB Gram's price list.

Once you can see the bands, the useful question changes. It stops being how much and becomes what moves the number. Six things do, and only two of them are about the tutor's seniority: the level your child sits at, how scarce that subject is in the UAE, how close the May session is, whether the hour includes travel, how long each session runs, and whether you are buying teaching or marking. A Maths AA HL tutor costs more than a Maths AI SL tutor for a reason that shows up in the assessment structure, not in a biography.

The second half of the value question is what the hour defends. A Diploma grade is built from components with fixed weightings: the Internal Assessment is 20% of the final mark in Mathematics and in each of the sciences, and 20% at Higher Level in Economics. Paper 3 carries 20% of the HL Mathematics grade and 30% of HL Economics. Those percentages are what you are paying to protect, and they are the reason a cheap generalist hour and an expensive specialist hour are not the same product even when the clock runs the same length.

IB Gram sells one format in the UAE: one-to-one tuition delivered live online, over video, with screen sharing and a shared whiteboard. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the Emirates; home visits are a service we run only in India. That is a deliberate choice rather than a limitation, and the comparison table further down makes the case in cost-per-contact-hour terms. A family in Al Reem Island gets the Chemistry HL specialist who matches their syllabus rather than whichever qualified teacher happens to live inside a thirty-minute drive at 4pm.

Everything below is organised the way a budget decision actually gets made: the rate, what drives it, what a year totals, where the money gets wasted, and what the assessment structure means for which hours are worth buying. The regulators, the MoE equivalency paperwork, the academic-honesty boundary and the Ramadan scheduling question all carry a cost implication too, and each gets its own section rather than a footnote.
