ib-tutor-for-indian-students.tutorsIntro: The tutors listed below teach IB Diploma and MYP subjects to students who came through CBSE, ICSE or an Indian state board. Several have taught both systems, which is what makes the mapping work useful rather than theoretical.

intro.heading: The jump is not about ability. It is about what the marker rewards
paragraphs: Indian-curriculum schooling is the second largest curriculum group in Dubai's private sector, accounting for 26% of enrolment against 37% for UK-curriculum schools, 14% American and 7% International Baccalaureate, across 227 licensed schools and 387,441 pupils in 2024-25. Those proportions explain a pattern that repeats every September: a strong CBSE student enters DP1 at an IB school, works as hard as always, and receives a grade 4 in a subject where they used to score in the high eighties. The family concludes the child has slipped. Almost always, nothing has slipped.

What has changed is the thing being measured. A CBSE paper rewards a complete, accurate, well-presented answer to a question whose shape was predictable from the textbook. An IB paper rewards a response that does precisely what the command term asked, in the register the subject expects, with reasoning visible rather than implied. A student who writes everything they know scores well in one system and poorly in the other. That is a translation problem, and translation problems close in weeks once they are named.

The second shift is independence. CBSE and ICSE assess almost entirely through examinations set outside the school. The Diploma asks a sixteen-year-old to choose a research question, design an investigation, carry it out over months and write it up against published criteria, with internal deadlines set by their own school. Students arriving from a system where the syllabus told them what to do next find this genuinely disorienting, and the usual failure is not poor work but work started far too late.

The third is the grade scale itself. A one-to-seven subject grade built from criterion marks does not map onto a percentage, and the conversion is not linear. Parents who read a 5 as sixty-odd per cent and panic are misreading a scale on which a 5 is a solid, university-viable grade in a Higher Level subject. Before any tutoring is bought, it is worth understanding what the number means, because a surprising amount of the pressure Indian families put on Diploma students comes from a scale misread.

An IB tutor for indian students in the UAE is therefore doing three concrete jobs: mapping content coverage from the Indian board onto the IB subject guide, teaching the answer construction an IB examiner marks, and putting a realistic internal assessment schedule in place against the school's own deadlines. All three are finite. None of them is general tuition, and none of them requires the volume of hours families often assume.

Lessons are delivered online, one to one, over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; those are offered only in India. For an Indian family in Sharjah or Ajman, where the specialist supply of Higher Level teachers is thinner than in Dubai, the online format is what makes a genuine subject specialist reachable at all.

ib-tutor-for-indian-students.programmesIntro: An Indian-curriculum student can enter the IB at three points, and the work needed differs sharply at each. These notes describe the entry rather than the programme.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks against criteria, typically A to D, each on a one-to-eight scale, converting to a one-to-seven subject grade. A student arriving from CBSE Class 7 or 8 finds the content lighter and the assessment stranger: marks go to process, reflection and the quality of an investigation rather than to a correct final answer. The adjustment takes a term and is best handled at entry.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools run MYP only to Year 9 before switching to IGCSE, which matters to an Indian family choosing a school: a child entering Year 8 may sit MYP assessments for two years and external IGCSE papers after that. Ask which programme the school runs in each year group rather than which programmes it is authorised for overall.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: Six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. For a Class 10 CBSE student this is a narrowing in breadth and a steepening in depth: fewer subjects, each pursued much further, with coursework in every one of them that runs across two years.
programmes.countryNote: The practical UAE detail is the option block. A school may offer Higher Level Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics on paper and timetable only two of the three together. Indian families aiming at engineering routes need to confirm the exact combination runs in their child's cohort before accepting a place, because the brochure lists subjects and the timetable decides them.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Many Indian families move at Class 8 or 9 into an IGCSE stream rather than waiting for the Diploma, because it gives two years to adjust before the heavier coursework arrives. Cambridge syllabus codes such as 0580 Mathematics and 0620 Chemistry carry a Core and Extended tier split that caps the available grade; Pearson codes look like 4MA1 and 4CH1 and work differently.
programmes.countryNote: An Indian-curriculum student usually finds IGCSE mathematics and science content familiar and the written-answer expectations unfamiliar. The gap is in explanation: a question worth four marks wants four distinct points, which is a convention nobody states. That single habit, practised against a published mark scheme, moves grades faster than extra content coverage.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: Transdisciplinary units replace subject periods, there are no external examinations, and progress is reported in a way that gives a family used to monthly tests very little to hold on to. Children adapt quickly. Parents often do not, and the useful intervention at this stage is usually a conversation about what the reporting actually says.
programmes.countryNote: Families moving from an Indian-curriculum primary school in the UAE often find the homework volume drops sharply, which reads as a lowering of standards. It is a different model rather than a lighter one, and the risk is overcorrecting with so much external tutoring that the child has no time left for the reading the programme assumes.

ib-tutor-for-indian-students.subjectsIntro: These are the Diploma subjects Indian families ask about most often, with the specific transfer issue attached to each rather than a general description of the course.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most engineering and economics courses expect. CBSE and ICSE students usually arrive with stronger algebraic technique than their classmates and weaker proof writing. Higher Level adds proof by induction, complex numbers and vectors, plus a paper three investigation that asks students to explore an unfamiliar structure rather than apply a known method.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling, statistics and technology led. It suits students heading for business, psychology or design, and it is the wrong choice for a student aiming at a quantitative degree that specifies Analysis and Approaches. Check published entry requirements for the universities on the list before the option form is signed, because the choice is hard to reverse later.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Content overlap with CBSE Class 11 and 12 physics is high, so the transfer problem is almost never knowledge. It is the extended-response questions that ask for an explanation in a specified number of steps, and the internal assessment, which requires an independent investigation with genuine uncertainty analysis rather than a verification of a known result.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms and energetics are where Indian-curriculum students most often have a procedural answer and not a conceptual one. The IB rewards reasoning from structure; a memorised reaction sequence earns much less. The independent investigation is the other pressure point, because it has no textbook precedent and is marked on design as much as on results.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Volume of content is familiar territory; command-term discipline is not. Explain, outline, suggest, evaluate and distinguish each demand different structures, and a complete recall of a topic answers none of them well. Practising against the command-term list rather than rereading notes is the single highest-return change for a transferring student.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries disproportionate weight and the commentary work requires students to connect published news articles to syllabus theory. Students from Indian boards often have the theory and have never written to that brief, so early sessions deal with article selection and structure rather than with economics content.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Marks go to applying a tool to one named organisation, not to describing the tool. Students who learned business through definition-and-example find the applied writing style the real work. The internal assessment rewards research discipline and a narrow question, and a broad question is the most common reason a strong student scores badly.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: Often chosen by students with strong coding backgrounds who then lose marks on the theory papers and on the solution-development documentation. The programming is rarely the constraint. Writing up design decisions against the criteria, and justifying them, is where the available marks sit.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Students from English-medium Indian schools usually read fluently and have had little practice with unseen close analysis under time pressure. The individual oral, which argues a global issue across two texts, has to be planned over months. Placement into English A rather than English B is a decision worth questioning early if it looks wrong.

subjects.name: Hindi and other language B options
subjects.description: A home language taken as a language B can be a reliable grade, but only if the level matches: a near-fluent speaker in an ab initio course is capped, and a weak reader in a Higher Level literature course is exposed. Ask what the school actually timetables, because language B options vary much more between UAE schools than the main subjects do.

subjects.name: Arabic ab initio and Arabic B
subjects.description: Relevant to every Indian family in a Dubai private school, because Arabic is mandatory regardless of the licensed curriculum and KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils. For most Indian-curriculum students the route is Arabic as an additional language, and the grade depends far more on stream placement than on hours bought.

ib-tutor-for-indian-students.regionsTitle: Where Indian-curriculum families sit across the emirates
ib-tutor-for-indian-students.regionsIntro: Indian-curriculum schooling is spread unevenly across the UAE, and so is the supply of IB schools families move into. The constraint is rarely demand; it is whether a specific Higher Level combination is timetabled nearby.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: The deepest market on both sides: the largest concentration of Indian-curriculum schools in the country and the widest choice of IB schools to move into. Regulated by KHDA, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate and publishes annual inspection reports families can compare directly.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: A substantial Indian-curriculum population with a narrower set of IB options, regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which also approves curricula, programmes, courses and assessment methods. Families frequently commute into Dubai for a Diploma place, which reshapes what time a weekday session can realistically start.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Indian-curriculum schools are well established in the capital, and the move into the Diploma often means a longer commute. ADEK is named by almost no tutoring provider online, so advice reaching these families is usually written for Dubai.

regions.name: Ajman and Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education. Indian-curriculum provision exists; IB provision is thin, so a family wanting the Diploma is often choosing between a commute and a boarding arrangement. Online support is frequently the only way to reach a Higher Level specialist in a shortage subject.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Regulated by the Department of Knowledge, which regulates private education and approves fees, curricula, programmes and assessment methods. A small market where option blocks are tight, meaning a student may have to self-support a subject the school cannot timetable.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education and the least documented market in the country: across the competitor pages researched for this project, Fujairah drew no mentions at all. Families here are working with almost no published local guidance.

regions.name: Outside the UAE
regions.note: Because lessons are online, support can begin while a family is still in India and continue unchanged after the move, with the schedule shifting from Indian Standard Time to Gulf Standard Time. For a student mid-way through Class 10 and starting DP1 in August, that continuity removes an awkward gap.

The last category matters: it tells a family where not to spend money.

For most CBSE and ICSE transfers this is where the grade movement comes from, because the content was rarely the problem.

modes.title: Internal assessment supervision alongside the school
modes.description: Structured support across the months an internal assessment runs: scoping a viable research question, understanding how each criterion is applied, planning against the school's own deadlines, and feedback on drafts the student has written. The student does the work; the tutor teaches, questions and reviews it.
bullets: The school's internal deadlines used as the schedule, not a generic plan
Criterion-by-criterion explanation of what the marker is looking for
Feedback on the student's own draft, never text supplied for submission
A narrower research question agreed before any data is collected

sections.heading: What actually changes when a CBSE or ICSE student enters the IB
paragraphs: Three things change, and only one of them is content. The first is the unit of assessment: a CBSE paper asks a predictable question and rewards a complete answer; an IB paper asks a question framed by a command term and rewards exactly what that term demanded. Explain wants a causal chain. Outline wants a brief summary. Evaluate wants a judgement supported both ways. A student who answers all three the same way loses marks three times, and no amount of revision fixes it because revision addresses knowledge.

The second is the locus of responsibility. In CBSE and ICSE the syllabus tells the student what comes next, and the school's job is to get through it. In the Diploma the student is asked to originate: a research question, an investigation design, a global issue to argue, a line of inquiry for the Extended Essay. For a sixteen-year-old who has spent ten years being told what to learn, the hardest part is not the standard but the blank page. Students do not usually fail these components; they start them far too late and submit something rushed.

The third is the scale. A one-to-seven subject grade is built from criterion marks and does not convert to a percentage in any intuitive way. A Higher Level 5 is a respectable, university-viable grade. A family reading it as roughly sixty per cent applies pressure that the grade does not justify, and the student responds by buying hours they do not need. Understanding the scale is free and often more useful than the first month of tutoring.

The content gap, when it exists, is usually small and asymmetric. Indian-curriculum students tend to arrive ahead in algebra, calculus technique and the quantitative parts of physics and chemistry, and behind in statistics, experimental design and the extended written subjects. A mapping exercise makes that concrete, and concrete gaps close quickly.
bullets: Command terms decide the shape of an answer, and are rarely taught explicitly
Internal assessments require an originated question, which is the real difficulty
A Higher Level 5 is a solid grade, not the equivalent of a weak percentage
Transferring students are often ahead in technique and behind in experimental design

sections.heading: Class 10 to DP1: a subject-by-subject mapping
paragraphs: The useful version of this conversation is not whether the IB is harder than CBSE. It is which specific topics a Class 10 student has met, which they have met in a different form, and which they will see for the first time in DP1. That mapping differs by subject and is the piece of work most families skip, which is why the first term is spent discovering gaps one surprise at a time.

In mathematics the overlap is substantial and the framing differs. A CBSE Class 10 student has met coordinate geometry, trigonometric ratios, quadratics and basic statistics, and has usually not met function notation used as rigorously as the IB does, nor the modelling language that Applications and Interpretation runs on. In the sciences the content overlap with Class 11 material is high, but the IB asks for uncertainty, error and experimental design in a way the Indian boards largely leave to the practical file.

The written subjects show the widest divergence. An ICSE student arrives with strong formal English and limited practice at unseen literary analysis. An economics student arrives with definitions and diagrams and no experience of applying them to a news article in 800 words. A history student arrives with narrative coverage and little source evaluation. None of these is a deficiency in the student; they are different assessment traditions, and each has a short list of transferable techniques.

The table below is the starting shape of that mapping. It is not a substitute for setting your child's own school syllabus against the IB subject guide, which is what a mapping block does, but it shows the kind of gap worth looking for before term starts rather than in November.

sections.heading: The maths route decision, and why it is the one to get right
paragraphs: No other option choice in the Diploma constrains a student's university options as sharply as the mathematics route. Analysis and Approaches is the algebra, calculus and proof route. Applications and Interpretation is the modelling, statistics and technology route. Both exist at Higher and Standard Level, giving four distinct courses, and the entry requirements of quantitative degrees frequently specify one of them rather than accepting either.

Indian-curriculum students are usually better prepared for Analysis and Approaches than their cohort, because CBSE and ICSE mathematics builds technique relentlessly. That is an argument for choosing it where the destination requires it, not an argument for choosing it automatically. A student aiming at business, psychology, architecture or design is often better served by Applications and Interpretation, where the statistical and modelling content is more relevant and the grade more achievable.

The failure mode is predictable: Higher Level Analysis and Approaches selected on prestige, for a student who neither needs it nor enjoys it, with the Higher Level grade then dragging the total down and the Extended Essay suffering because mathematics has absorbed the week. The second failure mode is the reverse: Applications and Interpretation chosen for comfort by a student who later applies to engineering and finds the course does not meet the stated requirement.

Check the published entry requirements of the specific universities on your child's list, in the countries they are likely to apply to, before the option form is signed. Then confirm with the school which of the four courses it actually timetables in your child's cohort, because a school may offer all four in its brochure and run two.

sections.heading: From percentages to a one-to-seven scale: reading the first report honestly
paragraphs: The first IB report a family receives after years of percentage marks causes more unnecessary tutoring than any other single event. A 4 looks like a fail. A 5 looks mediocre. In fact the Diploma's subject grades run one to seven, with three Higher Level and three Standard Level subjects contributing up to 42 points and up to three further points available from the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. Universities set offers in those terms, and a profile of 5s and 6s is a working profile.

The mechanics underneath the number also differ. Many components are marked against published criteria rather than a mark-per-fact scheme, so the student is placed in a band described in words. Two students can both write accurate answers and sit in different bands because one addressed the command term and the other did not. That is why a tutor's most valuable first intervention is often to show a student their own answer rescored against the actual criteria.

Early-term grades in DP1 are also noisy by design. Teachers set challenging assessments deliberately in the first months, often marking to the standard expected at the end of the course rather than at the beginning. A grade 4 in October and a grade 6 in June from the same student is a normal trajectory, not a recovery. Reading the first report as a prediction is the error.

Where a genuine problem exists, it shows as a pattern rather than a number: the same comment across subjects, work consistently late, or a wide gap between internal assessment marks and examination marks. Those are diagnosable. A single low grade in the first term is usually information about the assessment, not about the student.

sections.heading: Where Indian-curriculum students actually lose IB marks
paragraphs: The losses cluster in four places, and all four are techniques rather than knowledge. The first is command terms. An IB question is a precise instruction, and the mark allocation tells the student how many distinct points to make. A four-mark explain question wants four linked statements, not a paragraph containing everything relevant. Students trained to write generously lose marks for a surplus, which feels deeply unfair until it is seen once in a marked script.

The second is experimental design. Indian boards generally assess practical work through a file of prescribed experiments. The IB internal assessment in each science requires a question the student chose, a method they designed, data with an honest treatment of uncertainty, and an evaluation that identifies real limitations. A verification of a textbook result scores poorly however neatly it is presented, and that is the single commonest internal assessment error in this group.

The third is extended writing to a brief. Economics commentaries, history source papers, English analysis and the Extended Essay all reward a narrow argument supported by selected evidence. Students trained to demonstrate coverage write broadly and score in the middle bands. Narrowing the question is almost always the fastest improvement available, and it costs nothing.

The fourth is time. Coursework in the Diploma is produced over months against school-set deadlines, and a student used to being carried by end-of-year examinations will under-prioritise it. By the time a family notices, the internal assessment window has often closed. A schedule built backwards from the school's own dates, written down and reviewed weekly, prevents more grade damage than any amount of content teaching.
bullets: A four-mark question wants four distinct points, matched to the command term
An internal assessment that verifies a known result scores poorly by design
A narrow research question outscores an ambitious one in almost every subject
School-set coursework deadlines, not the exam session, are the binding dates in DP1

sections.heading: Languages: Hindi, English placement and the Arabic requirement
paragraphs: Language choices decide a surprising share of the final points total, and Indian families often treat them as administrative. The Diploma requires a studies-in-language-and-literature subject and a language acquisition subject, and the level placement in each is worth as much attention as a Higher Level science. A near-fluent speaker placed in a beginner course is capped. A student placed above their real reading level in a literature course is exposed for two years.

English placement is the first decision. English A Language and Literature assumes a student can analyse unseen text closely under time pressure; English B assesses comprehension and productive writing in specified text types. Students from English-medium Indian schools are usually placed in English A, which is often right and sometimes optimistic. If the first term's unseen analysis marks are far below the student's other subjects, that placement deserves a conversation rather than a tutor.

A home language taken as a language B or in the school-supported self-taught route can be a reliable source of points, but availability varies sharply between UAE schools. Ask which language options are actually timetabled in your child's cohort, not which are listed. Where a language is not offered, the school-supported self-taught route exists for literature at Standard Level and needs planning rather than improvisation.

Separately, Arabic is not optional. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited, and mandates the school's licensed-curriculum language for non-Arab pupils in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies. For most Indian-curriculum pupils this means the Arabic-as-an-additional-language stream, and a correct placement matters more than tuition hours.

sections.heading: What this costs in dirhams, and what drives the number
paragraphs: Three of the six competitor pages researched for this project publish no price at all, and the two that do quote United States dollars. The figures below are market rates in dirhams with the publisher named, so a family can calibrate before the first call. They are other providers' numbers, not IB Gram's price list, and a family should ask any provider for its own rate in writing with the VAT position stated.

Budget online tutoring, usually delivered by university students, is advertised from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits between AED 150 and 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits, which carry the tutor's travel inside the rate, run AED 180 to 350 on Bestimate's Dubai table and AED 200 to 500 for independent home tutors. IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists are quoted from AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named tutors reach AED 650 as published by BartyED.

What moves a family up those bands is not usually ambition but specificity. A Standard Level subject taught to a Year 11 student is widely supplied and priced accordingly. Higher Level Chemistry in the term before final papers, or a less commonly taught language, is thinly supplied and prices accordingly. Rates also rise closer to exam sessions as specialist availability tightens, which is an argument for a mapping block early rather than an intensive block late.

Two pieces of context sit alongside any tutoring figure. Monthly packages visible in the market include around AED 799 for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 for four two-hour in-home sessions, and Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end up to AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. And school fees themselves are not rising in Dubai this year: KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in private school fees for the 2026-27 academic year, under an incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total.

sections.heading: Equivalency, university routes and what the Diploma is being built for
paragraphs: Indian families in the UAE are usually planning towards one of three destinations, and each sets different constraints on the Diploma. Universities in India increasingly accept the IB, with requirements set institution by institution and often expressed in subject-specific terms. Universities in the UAE, the United Kingdom, North America and Europe each publish their own expectations. And the UAE Ministry of Education runs an equivalency process for secondary certificates, which concerns recognition of the qualification rather than admission to a particular course.

On the British track the equivalency requirements are published and specific: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. On the American track, English proficiency requires IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in SAT Math.

For the IB specifically, no points threshold is published here because none could be verified from the Ministry's own material. Ask the Ministry of Education or the emirate's attestation authority directly, and get the answer in writing. One competitor site already publishes an incorrect subject count for the IGCSE rule, which shows how quickly an unsourced figure propagates. Nobody, including IB Gram, performs or guarantees equivalency; the process belongs to the authority and the family.

The practical planning point is that subject choices made in Year 9 and Year 11 constrain all three destinations at once. A student who drops mathematics to a level a destination requires, or who takes only four subjects that count towards an equivalency rule, discovers it two years later. This is the most useful hour a family can spend with a tutor who knows both systems: not teaching, but checking that the combination on the option form survives contact with the destination list.

sections.heading: The honesty line, and what to ask a provider before paying
paragraphs: This market contains operators selling finished internal assessments. One advertises completed work at a published price. That is an academic-integrity breach under IB rules and the risk sits with the student, whose diploma is the thing at stake. Any Indian family under pressure about a deadline should know that the shortcut on offer is the single most expensive thing in this market, and that the provider carries none of the consequence.

What a tutor can do is substantial. Teach the content an assessment rests on. Explain how each published criterion is applied and show the student what each band looks like. Discuss whether a research question is viable before any data is collected. Read a draft the student has written and say where it does not yet meet the criteria. Build a schedule against the school's own deadlines and hold the student to it. What a tutor cannot do is supply text for submission or rework a draft into a finished piece.

The same line applies to materials. Published syllabuses, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson, and the right practice is to reference and link the official source rather than redistribute it. A provider offering a private library of papers is doing something worth asking about.

There is also a permit question families are entitled to ask. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and is granted free of charge for two years, covering registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's reported ethics rules separately bar school staff from paid tutoring of pupils at their own school.
bullets: Ask for the tutor's own rate in writing, with the VAT position stated
Ask what happens if the tutor becomes unavailable mid-term
Ask how feedback on coursework is given, and what the provider will not do
Be sceptical of examiner claims, star ratings and promised outcomes

process.title: Send the syllabus, not the worry
process.description: The first useful message contains the Indian board and class last completed, the UAE school's subject list with levels, and the last two reports. From that, a tutor can say what the real gap is likely to be. A description of the anxiety produces reassurance; documents produce a plan with an end point.

process.title: A free trial lesson with a subject specialist
process.description: One lesson at no cost with a tutor who teaches that subject at that level, used as a working session rather than a sales call. The tutor teaches something, then reports what they found. If the fit is wrong, a different tutor is proposed before any payment is involved.

process.title: A mapping block that produces a written list
process.description: Two to four sessions comparing the completed Indian syllabus against the IB subject guide, producing three lists: never covered, covered differently, already ahead. The third list is the one that saves money, because it shows where no support is needed at all.

process.title: Weekly sessions built on answer construction
process.description: Sessions in Gulf Standard Time, late enough to sit after school and activities, focused on command terms, mark allocation and structure using the student's own subjects and mark schemes. Each lesson ends with notes naming what was covered and what was set for the week.

process.title: A coursework schedule reviewed weekly
process.description: Internal assessment and Extended Essay dates come from the school, not from a generic calendar, and are reviewed each week against what the student has actually produced. This is the part that prevents the common failure of a strong student submitting rushed coursework in the final fortnight.

whyPoints.title: Tutors who have taught both systems
whyPoints.description: A mapping exercise only works if someone knows what a CBSE Class 10 syllabus actually contains as well as what an IB subject guide requires. Tutors who have taught on both sides can tell a family which topics are genuinely new and, more usefully, which are already covered in more depth than the IB needs.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery, so the specialist is not local
whyPoints.description: Indian-curriculum families are spread across every emirate, including Sharjah, Ajman and Ras Al Khaimah where Higher Level specialist supply is thin. Lessons run live online in Gulf Standard Time, which means the choice of tutor is made on subject and level rather than on who lives within a short drive.

whyPoints.title: Figures in dirhams, with the publisher named
whyPoints.description: Every market rate on this page is attributed to the provider that published it, and no price is presented as IB Gram's own. Where a number could not be verified it is left out: no IB points threshold for equivalency, no invented inspection rating, no fine amount, and no statistic without the detail behind it.

whyPoints.title: Work that is designed to stop
whyPoints.description: A mapping block ends with a recommendation, sometimes that no ongoing support is needed. Weekly sessions are reviewed each term against the written gap list. Indian families are offered a great deal of open-ended tutoring in this market; support that names what it is fixing is easier to judge and cheaper to run.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on coursework
whyPoints.description: Internal assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge work must be the student's own. Teaching, criterion explanation and feedback on the student's draft are what is on offer. Finished coursework is not available here at any price, which in a market where it is openly sold is a real distinction.

faqs.question: My son scored 92% in CBSE Class 10 and got a 4 in DP1 Chemistry. What went wrong?
faqs.answer: Most likely nothing about his chemistry. Early Diploma assessments are often marked to the standard expected at the end of the two-year course, so a grade 4 in the first term is a normal starting point rather than a prediction. The second factor is answer construction: IB questions are framed by command terms and a mark allocation that tells the student how many distinct points to make. A student trained to write a full, generous answer loses marks for not doing exactly what was asked. Have a tutor rescore one of his own scripts against the published criteria before buying any hours.

faqs.question: Should my daughter take Analysis and Approaches because she comes from a CBSE background?
faqs.answer: Only if her destination requires it. CBSE and ICSE mathematics does prepare students unusually well for Analysis and Approaches, which is an argument for being able to choose it, not for choosing it automatically. Applications and Interpretation is the better fit for business, psychology, design and many social sciences, and the grade is often higher. Check the published entry requirements of the specific universities on her list, because quantitative degrees frequently name the route. Then confirm with the school which of the four maths courses it actually timetables in her cohort, since brochures list more than timetables run.

faqs.question: Is the IB Diploma recognised by Indian universities if we move back?
faqs.answer: Recognition is set institution by institution and is best confirmed directly with each university's admissions office, in writing, for the year of entry. Requirements are often expressed in subject terms rather than as a single points figure, so the combination on the option form matters as much as the total. Separately, the UAE Ministry of Education runs its own equivalency process for secondary certificates, which is about recognition of the qualification rather than admission to a course. No tutoring provider performs or guarantees either process, and any site quoting an unsourced threshold should be treated carefully.

faqs.question: Why is my child doing Arabic when we chose an IB school?
faqs.answer: Because the licensed curriculum and the regulator's requirements are separate obligations. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and KHDA set those requirements to be implemented from the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited. For most Indian-curriculum pupils the stream is Arabic as an additional language, and correct placement matters more than extra hours.

faqs.question: How many hours a week of tutoring does a DP1 student from an Indian board need?
faqs.answer: Usually fewer than families expect, and in a narrower range of subjects. One or two sessions a week in the single subject genuinely at risk, plus a bounded mapping block at the start, covers most cases. Buying support in all six subjects at once is the commonest overspend in this group, and it crowds out the reading and coursework time the Diploma actually requires. A mapping block exists partly to identify the subjects where no support is needed, which is the part that saves money rather than spending it.

faqs.question: My daughter's Physics internal assessment just verifies Ohm's law. Is that a problem?
faqs.answer: Yes, and it is the most common error in this group. The science internal assessment is marked on an independent investigation: a question the student chose, a method they designed, data with an honest treatment of uncertainty, and an evaluation that identifies genuine limitations. A neat verification of a textbook result scores poorly however carefully it is presented, because the criteria reward design and analysis rather than confirmation. The fix is to narrow and personalise the question early, before data collection, which is exactly when a tutor can help without touching the work itself.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help write my son's Extended Essay if he has left it very late?
faqs.answer: No, and any provider who says yes is putting his diploma at risk rather than their own reputation. The essay has to be his own work under IB academic-honesty rules. A tutor can teach the subject content, explain how each criterion is applied, question whether the research question is viable, give feedback on drafts he has produced, and build a realistic schedule against the school's internal deadline. Those things, done urgently, recover a late essay more reliably than a rushed submission. Operators in this market do sell finished coursework; that is the practice this boundary exists to rule out.

faqs.question: We are moving from Mumbai in August and school starts immediately. Can support begin before we land?
faqs.answer: Yes, because lessons are delivered online over live video. Support can start while the family is still in India, scheduled in Indian Standard Time, and shift to Gulf Standard Time after the move with the same tutor and no restart. For a student finishing Class 10 and entering DP1 weeks later, that continuity removes the awkward gap where the mapping work would otherwise happen in the first stressful fortnight of a new school. Send the Class 10 syllabus and the new school's subject list and the mapping can be done in advance.

faqs.question: Do you come to our flat in Bur Dubai for lessons?
faqs.answer: No. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one to one, over live video, and IB Gram does not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; those are offered only in India. In practice the online arrangement suits Indian-curriculum families well: no travel cost sitting inside the hourly rate, a late slot available when the week overruns, and a tutor chosen for the subject and level rather than for living nearby. Where a sibling needs a different subject, the two can run at different times with different specialists.

faqs.question: Which Higher Level combination should an engineering-bound student take?
faqs.answer: Commonly Mathematics Analysis and Approaches, Physics and Chemistry at Higher Level, but the decision belongs to the destination list rather than to convention. Check each target university's published requirements, since some specify the mathematics route by name and some require a particular science at Higher Level. Then ask the school a separate question: which of those Higher Levels actually run together in the timetable for your child's cohort. A combination offered in the brochure and blocked against itself in the timetable is a problem discovered at option-form stage, not in DP1.

faqs.question: Is Theory of Knowledge worth spending tutoring time on?
faqs.answer: A little, and early. Theory of Knowledge combines with the Extended Essay to contribute up to three additional points on top of the subject total, so it is not decorative. Students from examination-led systems often find it the strangest component, because it rewards a well-argued position rather than a correct answer. One or two sessions on what the assessment actually asks, and on how to structure a claim and counter-claim, is usually enough. Beyond that, time is better spent on the subjects carrying the bulk of the points.

faqs.question: Our school in Sharjah does not offer Higher Level Economics. What are the options?
faqs.answer: Three, in order of practicality. Ask the school whether the subject can be timetabled if there is sufficient demand, since in Sharjah curriculum and programme approval sits with the Sharjah Private Education Authority as well as the school. Ask whether a school-supported arrangement or an online provider recognised by the school can deliver it. Or reconsider the subject combination against the destination requirements, which sometimes shows the Higher Level was never required. Option blocks in smaller emirates are genuinely narrower, and this is a question to settle before accepting a place.

faqs.question: How do the Diploma points add up, and what total should we aim for?
faqs.answer: Six subjects each graded one to seven give up to 42 points, with up to three further points available from the combination of Theory of Knowledge and the Extended Essay. Universities publish offers in those terms, and the right target is set by the destination list rather than by a round number. A profile of 5s and 6s with the required Higher Levels meets a great many published offers. Aiming at a total without checking the subject-specific conditions attached to an offer is the error that catches families who focused only on the headline figure.

faqs.question: What should we ask a tutoring provider before we pay anything?
faqs.answer: Five things, in writing. What the hourly rate is in dirhams and whether VAT is included. Whether the same tutor teaches every session and what happens if they become unavailable. What evidence there is that the tutor has taught that subject at that level. How coursework feedback is given, and explicitly what the provider will not do with an internal assessment. And whether the tutor holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit, which is granted free of charge for two years. A provider reluctant to answer any of those in writing has told you something useful.

faqs.question: My younger child is in Year 8 at a CBSE school. Is it better to switch now or after Class 10?
faqs.answer: Switching before the final two years is generally easier, because the student adjusts to criterion assessment and independent coursework while the stakes are low. Moving at Class 10 into DP1 compresses the adjustment into the same months as the heaviest coursework. The counter-argument is continuity: a settled child in a strong school with a clear route is not obviously better off moving. Check which programme the receiving school runs in each year group, since some run MYP only to Year 9 and then switch to IGCSE, which changes what the move actually involves.

faqs.question: Do the tutoring rates on this page include VAT, and why are they ranges?
faqs.answer: The figures are other providers' published rates, quoted so a family has a reference point, and each provider states its own VAT position rather than this page stating it for them. The UAE VAT treatment of tuition is a question for the Federal Tax Authority's own guidance, not for a tutoring site. The ranges are wide because the market is: budget online tutors advertise from around AED 45 an hour and premium named tutors reach AED 650. Ask any provider for its own figure in writing, with the VAT position and the cancellation terms stated.

ib-tutor-for-indian-students.closingHeading: Map the gap first, then decide what to pay for
ib-tutor-for-indian-students.closingBody: An Indian-curriculum student entering the IB in the UAE is rarely behind. They are usually ahead on technique, unfamiliar with the assessment, and unprepared for coursework they have to originate themselves. Those are three specific problems with three specific fixes, and none of them needs tutoring in all six subjects. Send the board and class your child completed, the new school's subject list and the last two reports, take a free trial lesson with a specialist in the subject that worries you most, and ask for the mapping in writing. Lessons run online, one to one, in Gulf Standard Time. If the honest answer is that your child needs a term rather than a tutor, that is what you will be told.

ib-tutor-for-new-expat-students.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the IB Diploma, the Middle Years Programme and Cambridge or Pearson IGCSE to students who arrived in the UAE part-way through a course. Each works from your child's own school documents and the published syllabus, not from a generic transition workbook.

intro.heading: Arriving mid-course is an administrative problem before it is an academic one
paragraphs: Families relocating to the UAE usually discover the academic problem second. The first problem is procedural: a school asks for a transfer certificate you have not been issued, a registrar mentions equivalency for a child who has two years of school left, and a timetable arrives with three subjects on it that were never discussed at the open day. None of that is anyone being obstructive. It is the consequence of a private-school sector that is licensed emirate by emirate, with five separate authorities setting the rules, and a federal baseline that applies to all of them.

Dubai alone licensed 227 private schools in the 2024-25 year, teaching 387,441 pupils across 17 different curricula, with the International Baccalaureate accounting for roughly 7% of that enrolment and UK-curriculum schools for the largest share. That mix is why two children on the same street can be sitting completely different qualifications, and why advice from a neighbour whose child attends a different school is often confidently wrong. The question is never "what do UAE schools do" but "what does this licensed school, under this regulator, do with my child's year group".

The academic gap that follows is specific and measurable. A student who studied in England for Year 10 has covered content but has often been entered for a different board, with different papers and a different tiering model. A student arriving from an American high school has breadth but has rarely written to a single-subject syllabus in the way a Diploma subject demands. A student from an Indian board has the algebra but not the command-term vocabulary that an IB examiner marks against. In each case the deficit is identifiable within one diagnostic session, and in each case it is finite.

An IB tutor for new expat students in the UAE is useful precisely because the work is bounded. Three sessions to map a previous syllabus against the new one, a term of weekly support to close the gap, then a decision about whether to continue. That is a different proposition from open-ended tutoring, and it is why the first conversation is about documents, year groups and exam entry dates rather than about study skills.

Lessons are delivered online, one to one, over live video. IB Gram does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE: home visits are a service offered only in India. For a family that has just moved, the online format solves a problem rather than compromising on one, because it means the choice of tutor is not restricted to whoever happens to live a short drive from a new address you are still learning to describe.

What follows is the information a newly arrived family actually needs, in the order it becomes urgent: who regulates the school, what paperwork the school will ask for, where the previous curriculum lands, what the mandatory UAE subjects do to the timetable, what the tutoring market charges in dirhams, how to read an inspection report, and how far away the first real exam deadline is.

ib-tutor-for-new-expat-students.programmesIntro: Three IB programmes are taught widely across the UAE, and a mid-year arrival can land in any of them. The notes below describe what each demands of a student who joins late, rather than restating the programme brochure.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The PYP is organised around transdisciplinary units rather than subject periods, so a child arriving from a textbook-and-worksheet system often reads as behind when the issue is unfamiliarity with the format. There are no external exams. What a new arrival needs is fluency in the working habits the classroom assumes: recording a line of enquiry, explaining a method aloud, and writing more than one sentence of reasoning.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE the PYP sits alongside the mandatory Arabic and Moral, Social and Cultural studies lessons required of every Dubai private school, so a PYP timetable carries curriculum content that the programme itself does not define. For a family new to the country this is the first visible sign that the licensed curriculum and the regulator's requirements are two separate things, both of which apply.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The MYP marks against criteria A to D in most subjects, on a one-to-eight scale per criterion, which converts to a one-to-seven subject grade. A student arriving from a percentage-based system has usually never been assessed this way. The practical consequence is that a strong pupil scores poorly for a term while learning what each criterion rewards, and parents read a drop that is really a translation error.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools run MYP to Year 9 and then switch to IGCSE for Years 10 and 11, while others run MYP 5 as the direct route into the Diploma. A new arrival therefore needs to know not just that the school teaches MYP, but where the school's MYP stops, because that determines whether the next qualification is an external IGCSE or an internal MYP assessment.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is six subjects, three at Higher Level and three at Standard Level, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Internal assessments in each subject are produced over months and carry real weight in the final grade. A student joining DP1 after the first term has to pick up both content and a set of coursework deadlines that have already started running.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit the May session, which means a student joining DP1 in a UAE school in the autumn has around eighteen months before final papers and considerably less than that before internal assessment deadlines set by the school. Confirm every IB date with the school's Diploma coordinator or on ibo.org, because internal deadlines vary by school and are usually earlier than families assume.

programmes.name: Cambridge and Pearson IGCSE
programmes.description: Most UK-curriculum schools in the UAE run IGCSE at 16 before splitting into A Level or the IB Diploma. Cambridge syllabuses carry four-digit codes such as 0580 for Mathematics and 0625 for Physics; Pearson codes look like 4MA1 and 4PH1. Core and Extended tiers in the Cambridge model cap the available grade, which is the single most consequential detail for a transferring student.
programmes.countryNote: A child who started GCSE in England may be moved onto a different board on arrival in the UAE, and the paper structure, tiering and coursework arrangements differ even where the content overlaps. Ask the registrar for the exact syllabus code before buying a single revision guide, because the wrong code means the wrong papers and the wrong mark scheme.

ib-tutor-for-new-expat-students.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects newly arrived families ask about most, with the particular transfer risk attached to each. The description is about what changes when a student crosses systems, not a general subject summary.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: The route most universities expect for engineering, economics and physical sciences. Transferring students usually have the algebra and lack the proof and reasoning habits: a question asking them to show a result rather than calculate one. HL adds proof by induction, complex numbers and vectors, and the paper three investigation that no other maths course asks for.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Modelling and statistics led, with technology assumed throughout. It suits students arriving from systems where graphing calculators were not standard, but the calculator fluency has to be built deliberately. Check the entry requirements of any university your child is likely to apply to before choosing it, because some quantitative degrees still specify Analysis and Approaches.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: The transfer problem in Physics is rarely the content and almost always the mathematical fluency the paper assumes. Students from systems with lighter algebra arrive able to describe a phenomenon but not to rearrange the relationship that governs it. Electricity and fields are where marks disappear first, because they reward algebraic confidence under time pressure.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic chemistry and the energetics topics are the usual landing points for a transferring student, because both depend on a mechanism-level understanding that a memorised sequence does not supply. The internal assessment requires a genuinely independent investigation, which is a new experience for most arrivals and the component most often started too late.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Content heavy and command-term sensitive. A student who writes everything they know about a topic scores poorly against a question that said explain, and well against one that said outline. New arrivals improve fastest here by practising against the command-term list rather than by rereading notes, because the gap is in answer construction rather than knowledge.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: Students from systems that taught literature through plot summary find the unseen analysis paper hardest, because it rewards close reading of an unfamiliar text under time limits. The individual oral requires a global issue argued across two texts, which has to be planned months ahead rather than revised for.

subjects.name: English B
subjects.description: The right course for a student whose schooling was conducted in another language, and the wrong one for a near-native speaker, which is a placement decision the school makes early and a family can question. Productive writing in specified text types, with register and audience marked explicitly, is the part that needs practice rather than vocabulary drilling.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy carries disproportionate weight, and the commentary work asks students to connect a published news article to syllabus theory. Transferring students often have the theory and have never written to that brief, so the first few pieces are about structure, selection and the real-world link rather than about economics.

subjects.name: Arabic
subjects.levels: Arabic A, Arabic B and ab initio
subjects.description: Placement matters more than tuition in the first term. A student arriving with no Arabic enters a different course from one who studied it in Lebanon or Egypt, and KHDA requires Dubai private schools to teach Arabic to all pupils with separate classes for Arab and non-Arab groups. Get the course level right before worrying about the grade.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: Case-study based, with marks for applying a tool to a specific organisation rather than describing the tool. The Higher Level extension and the internal assessment both reward research discipline. A student arriving mid-course can usually catch up on content quickly and needs longer on the applied writing style.

ib-tutor-for-new-expat-students.regionsTitle: Which emirate you have landed in changes the rules
ib-tutor-for-new-expat-students.regionsIntro: Relocation packages tend to treat the UAE as one place. Education policy does not: the authority that licenses your child's school, approves its fees and inspects it depends on the emirate, and so does the route for any later attestation question.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Regulated by KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. The densest school market in the country, inspected annually on a six-band scale, with the widest choice of IB and IGCSE schools and the tightest competition for places in popular year groups.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi and Al Ain
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK is named by almost no tutoring provider online, which means Abu Dhabi families are routinely served advice written for Dubai, including advice about inspection reports that uses the wrong framework.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Curriculum approval sitting with the regulator is a detail that matters if your child needs a subject the school does not currently run.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Regulated by the Department of Knowledge, which regulates private education in the emirate and likewise approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. A smaller school market means narrower option blocks, so a Diploma student may find a Higher Level subject combination unavailable locally.

regions.name: Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah
regions.note: The federal Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in these three emirates. Families here are the least well served by published guidance: across the competitor pages researched for this project, Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain drew no mentions at all.

regions.name: Across all emirates
regions.note: Private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. That federal baseline is why a mandatory-subject requirement appears on a British, American or IB timetable alike.

regions.name: Outside the UAE
regions.note: Because lessons run online, a family posted to the UAE from a third country, or one whose child is finishing a term elsewhere before joining, can start support before the move. The schedule is set in Gulf Standard Time once the family lands, and in the departure time zone until then.

schoolClusters.city: Dubai IB and IGCSE schools new arrivals commonly join
schoolClusters.note: These are schools whose students IB Gram tutors support. They are listed as context for a family comparing offers of places, not as any form of relationship. Curriculum and programme offerings change, so confirm what a school runs in your child's year group directly with its registrar.

schoolClusters.city: Abu Dhabi and Sharjah schools outside the Dubai market
schoolClusters.note: Families posted to the capital or to Sharjah have a smaller set of IB options and a different regulator reading the inspection report. The practical effect on tutoring is scheduling: a longer school run and a different weekend pattern move the realistic start of a weekday session later.

ib-tutor-for-new-expat-students.schoolDisclaimer: Named schools are context about the market a family is choosing within. No affiliation, partnership or endorsement is implied, and every school name should be checked against the relevant regulator's own published school listing.
ib-tutor-for-new-expat-students.modesIntro: A newly arrived family usually needs one of three shapes of support, and the right one depends on how far into a course the student has joined rather than on how much help the family thinks is needed.

modes.title: Transition diagnostic, two to three sessions
modes.description: A bounded piece of work that maps the syllabus your child was following against the one the new school teaches, identifies the specific topics never covered, and produces a written list in order of exam weight. It ends with a recommendation, which is sometimes that no ongoing tutoring is needed. Families use it most in the first month after enrolment.

A topic-by-topic gap list ordered by paper weighting
A written view on whether the current subject level is the right one
No commitment to continue beyond the diagnostic

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one over live video
modes.description: The standard arrangement: one or two sessions a week with the same tutor, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school run and after-school activities. The tutor works to your child's school deadlines and assessment calendar rather than to a generic scheme of work, which matters when the student has joined a course already in progress.
bullets: Same tutor each week, so the context does not need rebuilding
Session notes after each lesson naming what was covered and what was set
Timetable set in Gulf Standard Time, with slots up to the late evening
Rescheduling without penalty when a school trip or travel intervenes

modes.title: Intensive block before a session or an internal deadline
modes.description: A compressed set of sessions over a few weeks, built backwards from a fixed date: a school mock window, an internal assessment deadline, or a Cambridge or Pearson entry series. Useful for a family that arrived close to an exam series and needs coverage of specific papers rather than a whole course.
bullets: Built backwards from the real deadline, not from a fixed lesson count
Past-paper work against the published mark scheme for the exact syllabus code
Two or three sessions a week where the calendar demands it
Stops when the deadline passes rather than rolling on by default

sections.heading: What a family arriving mid-year has to settle in the first three weeks
paragraphs: The first three weeks after a move decide most of what the following year looks like, and almost none of it is about tutoring. The jobs are: confirm which authority licenses the school, obtain or chase the transfer certificate from the previous school, establish the exact syllabus and board for each subject, find out what the school's internal assessment calendar already says, and find out which mandatory UAE subjects have been added to the timetable. Each of those is a short conversation with a registrar, and each one is easier to have before term settles than after.

The order matters because the answers depend on each other. You cannot judge whether your child is behind until you know which syllabus the school teaches, and you cannot judge whether a Diploma subject choice is viable until you know which Higher Level options the school actually runs in that year group. Schools in smaller emirates run narrower option blocks, so a combination that was routine at the previous school may simply not be timetabled here. That is a question to ask during enrolment, not in October.

A specific trap for Year 11 and Year 12 arrivals is exam entry. Cambridge and Pearson entries close months ahead of the papers, and a student who moves after the deadline may not be entered for the series the family assumed. In the UAE the choice is between a June series and a November series, so an arrival in January has almost certainly landed after the June entry closed and is looking at November instead. That is a different tutoring plan, a different revision runway and a later results date. The school can explain what is still possible; nobody else can.

Tutoring belongs at the end of that list rather than the start, and it is more useful once the facts are in. A diagnostic session that begins with the school's own syllabus codes and assessment calendar produces a short, ordered list of what to fix. A diagnostic that begins with a vague sense that maths is weak produces a term of general revision. The difference is entirely in the preparation the family did first.
bullets: Ask the registrar for the exact syllabus code of every externally examined subject
Ask for the school's internal deadlines for internal assessments and the Extended Essay
Ask which Higher Level subjects actually run in your child's cohort, not which are listed
Ask whether your child has been entered for the next exam series, and by which date

sections.heading: Which regulator governs your child's new school
paragraphs: There is no single UAE schools authority. Private education is regulated emirate by emirate, and the body that licenses, inspects and in some emirates approves the curriculum of your child's school depends entirely on where the campus sits. This is the single most useful thing a newly arrived parent can learn, because it determines which inspection framework a report uses, which website publishes the rules, and which authority a later question about equivalency routes through.

In Dubai the Knowledge and Human Development Authority is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, the Department of Education and Knowledge supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah's authority regulates private education in that emirate, as does the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and both approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. For Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah, the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools directly.

The practical differences show up in small places. An Abu Dhabi family reading advice written for Dubai will be told to look up a KHDA inspection band that does not apply to their school. A Sharjah family wanting a subject the school does not run needs to understand that curriculum approval sits with the regulator rather than solely with the school. And an Abu Dhabi parent should know that ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, which rules out the arrangement many families instinctively ask for first. That rule has been press-reported and is worth confirming against the current ADEK policy document before relying on it.

None of these authorities accredits, approves or licenses IB Gram, and no tutoring provider should tell you otherwise. What a regulator does is govern schools and, through MoHRE, the permit an individual tutor needs. Naming a regulator correctly is a sign that a provider has read the rules. Claiming its endorsement is the opposite.

sections.heading: The paperwork a new school asks for, and what holds it up
paragraphs: Enrolment in a UAE private school runs on documents issued by an institution you have already left, which is why the paperwork is the part that slips. The transfer certificate is the usual culprit: it has to come from the previous school, it often needs to be signed by a named officer, and a school that has broken for a holiday cannot produce it. Families who request it before the final term ends save themselves weeks. Families who assume it can be emailed from abroad in August frequently cannot start on day one.

Reports for the previous two years are the second request, and they do more than satisfy an administrator. They are what a placement decision is made from: whether your child enters Year 10 or Year 11, whether an English B or English A placement is proposed, and whether a Higher Level request is accepted. A thin report with percentages and no subject comment gives the school very little to work with, so if the previous school can supply subject-teacher comments or internal assessment data, ask for them.

Equivalency is where arriving families most often misunderstand the timeline. The Ministry of Education's equivalency process concerns a secondary certificate at the end of school, and the British-track requirements are published: five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects. That rule shapes subject choices in Year 9, which is why it belongs in a conversation now rather than in Year 13. Verify the current requirements on the Ministry's own channels before acting on them, and treat any provider offering to perform or guarantee equivalency with caution.

The one document families forget is the list of what the school will ask for next. Ask the registrar, in writing, for the complete admissions checklist including anything required later in the year. It costs one email and removes most of the surprises.

sections.heading: Where your child's previous curriculum lands in a UAE classroom
paragraphs: Every transfer creates a gap, and the gap is never general. It is a short list of topics, skills and conventions that the previous system either taught differently or did not teach at all. Naming that list is most of the work: once it exists, the teaching is straightforward, and the family can see the end of the project rather than signing up for indefinite support.

The commonest cases follow patterns. A student from England who started GCSE has the content but may now be on a different board, with different paper structures and, in the Cambridge model, a Core or Extended tier that caps the grade available. A student from an American high school has breadth and a GPA built from coursework, and has rarely been assessed by two or three timed papers that decide the whole grade. A student from an Indian board usually has strong procedural mathematics and little practice with command terms or an independent investigation. A student from MYP 5 knows the assessment language and underestimates the content jump into Higher Level.

The skills that transfer worst are the ones nobody teaches explicitly. Reading a command term and answering only what it asked. Writing a conclusion that refers to uncertainty rather than restating the result. Showing a line of reasoning when the answer alone earns one mark out of five. Planning a piece of coursework over three months rather than a weekend. These are learnable in weeks, and they are the difference between a student who looks weak and a student who is unfamiliar.

A diagnostic session is the cheapest way to turn an anxiety into a list. Two or three sessions with the previous reports and the new syllabus open produces a written gap list ordered by exam weight, which means the family can decide what to pay for rather than buying a term of general support and hoping.

sections.heading: The mandatory UAE subjects nobody mentions at the open day
paragraphs: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year starts in April. This surprises almost every arriving family, because the admissions conversation is about the IB or the British curriculum and the timetable that follows carries subjects neither of those defines.

The rules are detailed rather than nominal. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited due to the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language; Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab pupils; and the school's licensed-curriculum language is used for non-Arabs in Islamic Education and in Moral, Social and Cultural studies.

Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit. Schools may vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and KHDA advises that any mandatory-subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited, which is a real constraint on how any Arabic, Islamic Education or Social Studies tutoring can be described: support means teaching the approved material well, not supplying an alternative syllabus. Schools are also required to ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic have appropriate KHDA permission to teach those subjects.

For a new arrival the consequence is arithmetic. Mandatory subject time comes out of the week, so the licensed curriculum has fewer periods than the equivalent school in London or Mumbai. A child who was coasting on classroom time alone will feel that compression first. It is also why Arabic placement is worth getting right in the first month: a pupil put in the wrong Arabic stream spends two years in the wrong class.
