sections.heading: What tutoring actually costs in the UAE market
paragraphs: Published pricing is scarce in this market. Of the competitor pages researched for this project, three of six publish no price at all, and the two that do quote United States dollars, which is not a currency UAE families transact in. The figures below are market rates in dirhams, attributed to whoever published them, so an arriving family has a reference point before the first phone call. They are not IB Gram's price list.

At the bottom of the market, online lessons from university-student tutors are advertised from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour, with EdFlik listing from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52. Qualified subject tutors working online sit in the AED 150 to 300 band, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits, which include the tutor's travel, run higher: Bestimate's Dubai rate table puts them at AED 180 to 350 and private home tutors at AED 200 to 500. IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists are quoted at AED 200 to 450 and above, with TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named or examiner-level tutors reach AED 650, as published by BartyED.

Monthly packages visible in the market include around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240 to 600 at the budget end, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year support. Those are useful anchors for a relocation budget, which is usually built before the family knows what the school will require.

Two pieces of context belong next to any tutoring figure. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. And rates rise closer to exam sessions as specialist availability tightens, which is an argument for booking a transition diagnostic in the first term rather than in the term before papers.

sections.heading: Reading a KHDA inspection report when two schools both have places
paragraphs: A relocating family often has to choose between two schools that both have a place in the right year group, which is a decision inspection reports are genuinely useful for. Dubai private schools are inspected annually by KHDA on a six-band scale running from Outstanding down to Very Weak, and the reports are published. The band on the cover is the least informative part. What matters is the detail underneath it, and specifically whether the strong judgements sit in the phase and subjects your child is actually entering.

A school can hold a strong overall band on the strength of its primary phase while the Diploma cohort is small and the Higher Level option blocks are thin. The reverse happens too. So read the report for the phase your child joins, look at the subject-level attainment and progress judgements rather than the headline, and check how the inspectors described teaching in the specific subjects your child will take at Higher Level. Then ask the school directly which Higher Level subjects ran last year and with how many pupils in each.

Supply matters as much as quality. Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 new places; six new schools opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose 6%. A family told that a preferred school is full in October may find the position different for the following year, and a new school opening nearby changes the local picture more than an inspection band moving one step.

Abu Dhabi families should note that ADEK operates its own framework rather than the KHDA bands, so a report from one emirate cannot be compared directly with one from the other. Reading a Dubai inspection band against an Abu Dhabi school is one of the commonest errors in relocation advice, and it comes from guidance written for the Dubai market being applied across the country.

sections.heading: Counting backwards from the exam session your child has just joined
paragraphs: Nothing catches an arriving family out more reliably than an entry deadline. Exam registration happens months before papers, and a student who transfers after the window has closed can lose a whole series. Of the competitor pages researched for this project, the word November returned no hits at all: no session named, no registration deadline, no results date. That absence is why this section exists.

Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Every exam centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. For a family that has just moved emirate or country, that is not a detail: the zone is a property of the centre, not of the student.

The published Pearson dates show how far ahead the real deadline sits, and they are the ones a UAE family can check for themselves. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams run in May/June and November each year; the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Entries for that November series closed long before the first candidate sat down in late October. Cambridge's two UAE series, June and November, follow the same arithmetic, but Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, says it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, and states that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. So the Cambridge dates that bind your child come from your own centre rather than from a page like this. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always work from the live official timetable rather than a restated date.

IB dates are deliberately absent here. UAE schools sit the May session, but no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself, so confirm every Diploma date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org. The school's internal deadlines for internal assessments and the Extended Essay are usually the binding ones anyway, and they are earlier than most families expect.

sections.heading: What a tutor may and may not touch
paragraphs: This matters more for an arriving family than for a settled one, because a student who has joined a course late is behind on coursework and the temptation to buy a shortcut is highest exactly then. The boundary is not a matter of taste. Internal assessments, the Extended Essay, Theory of Knowledge essays and the Personal Project must be the student's own work, and a breach puts the student's diploma at risk rather than the provider's reputation.

A tutor can teach the underlying content, explain how the assessment criteria are applied, discuss whether a research question is viable, give feedback on a draft the student has produced, model the analysis of a different example, and help plan a realistic schedule against the school's deadlines. A tutor cannot supply text for the student to submit, rework a draft into a finished piece, or hand over material presented as the student's own. One operator in this market openly sells finished internal assessments; that is an academic-integrity breach and a malpractice trigger for the student who buys it.

The same line applies to past papers and syllabus documents. Published syllabuses, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides belong to the IB, Cambridge and Pearson, so the right approach is to reference and link to the official source rather than to redistribute it. A tutor who offers a private library of question papers is doing something a family should ask questions about.

There is also a legal boundary on the tutor's side. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit: the MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure should be quoted at you. MoHRE's own service page is the application route, and ADEK's ethics rules separately bar Abu Dhabi school staff from paid tutoring of pupils at their own school.

process.title: Send the documents, not a description
process.description: The first message that produces useful advice contains the last two school reports, the new school's subject list and, where you have them, the syllabus codes. A description of the problem produces a description of a solution. Documents produce a specific plan, and often reveal that the issue is placement rather than attainment.

process.title: A free trial lesson with a specialist in the subject
process.description: One lesson, at no cost, with a tutor who teaches that subject at that level. It is a working session rather than a sales call: the tutor teaches something and tells you afterwards what they found. If the fit is wrong, say so and a different tutor is proposed before any money is involved.

process.title: A written gap list ordered by exam weight
process.description: After the trial and any diagnostic sessions you receive a short list of what to fix, in the order the assessment rewards. That list is what the tutoring is then measured against, and it is also what lets a family decide to stop. A plan with no end point is not a plan.

process.title: Weekly sessions in Gulf Standard Time around the school run
process.description: Sessions are set in local time, with slots late enough to sit after sport and music, and are moved without penalty when travel or a school trip intervenes. Each lesson ends with notes naming what was covered and what was set, so a parent can see progress without attending.

process.title: Reassess at the end of the term
process.description: At term's end the tutor says plainly whether the gap has closed. Where it has, support stops or drops to a single session before assessments. Where a subject needs a different specialist, that is said rather than absorbed, and a replacement tutor is proposed with the context already handed over.

whyPoints.title: The regulator map is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Every claim about KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the RAK Department of Knowledge or the Ministry of Education on this page is attributed to u.ae or to the authority's own published document. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from any of them, and says so, because a provider that blurs that line is the one to be careful with.

whyPoints.title: Access to a specialist rather than to a neighbour
whyPoints.description: Online delivery means the Higher Level Chemistry teacher does not have to live a twenty-minute drive from your new address. For a family that has just arrived in a smaller emirate, where option blocks are narrow and specialist supply is thin, that is the difference between the right tutor and the available one.

whyPoints.title: Figures carry their source and their date
whyPoints.description: Market rates on this page are attributed to the provider that published them and the dirham is the unit throughout. Where a number could not be verified, it is left out: no IB exam date, no inspection rating invented for a school, no fine amount, and no statistic without the detail behind it.

whyPoints.title: Bounded work with a written end point
whyPoints.description: A transition diagnostic produces an ordered gap list and a recommendation, which is sometimes that tutoring is not needed. Families relocating have enough open-ended commitments. Support that names what it is fixing and when it should stop is easier to budget and easier to judge.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is drawn in public
whyPoints.description: Internal assessments, the Extended Essay and Theory of Knowledge work must be the student's own. Teaching, criteria explanation and feedback on a student's draft are what a tutor provides. Finished coursework is not available here at any price, and in this market that is a real distinction rather than a disclaimer.

faqs.question: We land in Dubai in January. Has my daughter already missed the exam entry deadline?
faqs.answer: Possibly, and the school is the only body that can answer it. Cambridge entries close months ahead of the papers, and the two UAE series are June and November, so a mid-year arrival has usually landed after the June entry shut. Pearson runs May/June and November series with its own deadlines; its November 2026 timetable ran to 19 November 2026, which tells you how early that autumn entry had to be lodged. Ask the new school's exams officer two questions in writing: whether your daughter can still be entered for the next series, and which syllabus codes she would be entered for. If the window has closed, the realistic plan is the following series, which changes what tutoring should prioritise.

faqs.question: Which authority actually regulates my child's new school in the UAE?
faqs.answer: It depends on the emirate. KHDA oversees private education in Dubai. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, and the Department of Knowledge does so in Ras Al Khaimah; both also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. This matters because inspection frameworks differ, so a report from one emirate cannot be compared directly with one from another.

faqs.question: Why does my son's timetable include Arabic and Islamic Education when we chose an IB school?
faqs.answer: Because the licensed curriculum and the regulator's requirements are separate obligations that both apply. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the international curriculum the school is licensed to teach, and KHDA set those requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. KHDA also requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab pupils in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited. The practical effect is that mandatory subject time reduces the periods available to the rest of the timetable.

faqs.question: My child was partway through GCSEs in England. Will the UAE school teach the same board?
faqs.answer: Often not. UAE schools choose between Cambridge and Pearson syllabuses, and a school may use a different board from the one your child started with, or a different syllabus code within the same board. The content overlaps substantially, but paper structures, tiering and coursework arrangements differ, and in the Cambridge model the Core or Extended decision caps the grade available. Ask the registrar for the exact code for every subject before buying revision material, because the wrong code means the wrong past papers and the wrong mark scheme, which is the most common wasted purchase a relocating family makes.

faqs.question: What does the UAE Ministry of Education ask for on the British track for equivalency?
faqs.answer: The published British-track requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with either one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. That exclusion is the detail at least one ranking tutoring site gets wrong by stating that six IGCSE subjects are needed. Verify the current requirements through the Ministry's own channels, and treat any provider claiming to perform or guarantee equivalency with caution.

faqs.question: Is there an IB points threshold for UAE equivalency that we should be planning towards?
faqs.answer: No figure is published on this page because none could be verified from the Ministry's own material. The British-track and American-track requirements are sourced and stated above, including the American-track English requirement of IELTS academic 5, TOEFL iBT 61 or 450 in SAT reading and writing, and SAT Math of at least 450. For the IB specifically, ask the Ministry of Education or the emirate attestation authority directly and get the answer in writing. Any site quoting an IB points threshold without naming its source is guessing, and an incorrect threshold drives the wrong subject choices two years early.

faqs.question: Does my child need a tutor at all, or just time to settle in?
faqs.answer: Frequently just time, and a diagnostic is how you tell the difference. A transferring student commonly looks weak for a term because the assessment language is unfamiliar rather than because the knowledge is missing: an MYP criterion grade or an IB one-to-seven scale reads alarmingly to a family used to percentages. Two or three sessions with the previous reports and the new syllabus open will show whether there are genuine content gaps, and if there are not, the honest recommendation is to wait. Settling-in anxiety is real and does not need paying for.

faqs.question: How much should we budget for tutoring in our relocation planning?
faqs.answer: Market rates in the UAE, in dirhams, run from roughly AED 45 to 150 an hour for budget online tutors, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for in-home visits including travel, and AED 200 to 450 and above for IB, IGCSE and A-Level specialists, reaching AED 650 at the premium end as published by BartyED. Monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run around AED 240 to 600 at the budget end and AED 1,000 to 2,000 and above for specialist exam-year work. Those are other providers' published figures, quoted so you have a reference.

faqs.question: Can you send a tutor to our villa while we are still settling in?
faqs.answer: No. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one to one, over live video, and IB Gram does not provide in-home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service offered only in India. For a family still unpacking, that is usually the easier arrangement: no travel fee inside the hourly rate, no dependence on a tutor who happens to live nearby, and a session that can move to a late slot when the week falls apart. It also means the specialist you get is chosen for the subject and level rather than for the postcode.

faqs.question: Our posting is to Abu Dhabi rather than Dubai. Does any of this change?
faqs.answer: Several things do. ADEK, not KHDA, supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, and it runs its own inspection framework, so a Dubai inspection band cannot be read across. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported to prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, which rules out the arrangement many families ask for first. Verify that against the current ADEK policy document before relying on it. Most published tutoring advice is written for Dubai and does not say so.

faqs.question: How quickly can lessons start once we have arrived and enrolled?
faqs.answer: Usually within a few days for mainstream subjects at Standard Level or IGCSE, where specialist supply is deepest. A narrow Higher Level combination, a less common language, or a specific syllabus code can take longer, and where no suitable specialist is available that is said rather than filled with whoever is free. The sequence is a short conversation about documents, a free trial lesson with a subject specialist, then a weekly slot in Gulf Standard Time. Nothing is charged before the trial lesson has happened and you have decided to continue.

faqs.question: Does a private tutor in the UAE need a permit, and how do we check?
faqs.answer: Yes. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page, Issuance of a New Work Permit for private tutor licensing, lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Those offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published.

faqs.question: Can the same tutor help across two or three subjects while we find our feet?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth being sceptical about. One tutor can reasonably cover closely related subjects such as Physics and Mathematics, or Chemistry and Biology at Standard Level, because the underlying skills overlap. Across a Higher Level science, a Higher Level humanity and a language, a single tutor is unlikely to be strong in all three, and the convenience costs more than it saves. The honest arrangement is usually one tutor for the subject that is genuinely at risk, with a diagnostic for the others before committing further.

faqs.question: What can a tutor do with my son's Internal Assessment, and what is off limits?
faqs.answer: A tutor can teach the content it rests on, explain how each assessment criterion is applied, discuss whether a research question is viable, give feedback on a draft the student has produced, and help build a schedule against the school's internal deadlines. A tutor cannot supply text for submission or rework a draft into a finished piece. The work has to be the student's own, and a breach of IB academic-honesty rules puts the diploma at risk. One operator in this market sells finished internal assessments outright; that is the practice this boundary exists to rule out.

faqs.question: Should we choose the school with the higher inspection band or the shorter commute?
faqs.answer: Read the inspection report for the phase your child is joining before deciding either way. A strong overall band can rest on a strong primary phase while the Diploma cohort is small and Higher Level option blocks are thin. Ask each school which Higher Level subjects actually ran last year and with how many pupils, then look at subject-level attainment and progress judgements rather than the headline band. Supply is also moving: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three IB, creating 16,846 places.

faqs.question: My daughter joins DP1 in the second term. What should the first month of tutoring cover?
faqs.answer: Coursework timing first, content second. A student joining the Diploma mid-year inherits internal assessment deadlines that have already started running, and those are set by the school rather than by the IB, so they are usually earlier than families expect. The first sessions should establish what has been missed in each subject, what the school's internal deadlines are, and which single piece of coursework is most at risk. Content gaps can be worked through across a term; a missed internal deadline cannot be recovered the same way.

ib-tutor-for-new-expat-students.closingHeading: Start with the documents, and the rest gets simpler
ib-tutor-for-new-expat-students.closingBody: Most of what makes a relocation academically stressful is information the family did not have yet: which authority regulates the school, which board and syllabus code each subject uses, what the mandatory UAE subjects take out of the week, and how far away the next entry deadline really is. Send the last two school reports and the new school's subject list, take a free trial lesson with a specialist in the subject that worries you most, and ask for the gap list in writing. Lessons run online, one to one, in Gulf Standard Time. If the honest answer is that your child needs a term to settle rather than a tutor, that is what you will be told.

intro.heading: Near me, in a country with five school regulators
paragraphs: A proximity search is a cheap filter, and in the UAE it is also a misleading one. Dubai alone licensed 227 private schools in 2024-25, teaching 387,441 students across 17 different curricula, and the International Baccalaureate is a minority share of that enrolment. The nearest IB school to your address may be the only one for several districts. The nearest adult who has actually taught your child's exact subject at Higher Level may be nowhere within driving range. Distance predicts traffic well. It predicts nothing about whether anyone inside the radius has sat in front of that syllabus, marked that component, or read the examiner's report that explains where the marks went.

The second problem with a radius is that the UAE does not have one school system. It has five regulators, and which one holds your child's file depends on the emirate you live in rather than the curriculum the school teaches. Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah has its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Move thirty minutes up Sheikh Mohammed Bin Zayed Road and the inspection framework, the fee-approval route and the published report all change hands.

There is a third problem, and it is the one that surprises families most. The closest qualified adult to your child is usually their own subject teacher at school. That is the one person who, on the published position, may not take the work. Gulf News has reported that the Department of Education and Knowledge's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and that the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct with the same restriction. Verify the current wording with the authority or the school before relying on it, but plan on the basis that it holds.

So here is what IB Gram actually does, in plain words, before you read another section. Tuition for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time. We do not arrange home visits anywhere in the Emirates; that service exists only in India. There is no UAE office to drive to. The first session is a free 45-minute trial lesson, taken before any payment, so you judge the teaching rather than a profile. Coursework help is feedback and questioning on work the student has written; nobody here writes an Internal Assessment, an Extended Essay or a Theory of Knowledge essay.

This page is built for the parent who has already searched IB tutor near me in the UAE and wants the part the map leaves out: who is legally permitted to teach your child, what the market charges once travel is stripped out of the fee, how much of an evening a visiting tutor really consumes, which authority to ask for a school's inspection report, what Arabic and Islamic Education add to the week, when exam entries close, and what the Ministry of Education wants on file after the Diploma finishes. Every figure below is attributed to the body or the publication it came from.

ib-tutor-near-me.programmesIntro: IB Gram covers the three mainstream IB programmes plus the Career-related Programme. What changes between them is not only the content but what the regulator in your emirate requires alongside it, and how much of the final grade sits in work marked inside the school.

programmes.name: Primary Years Programme
programmes.description: The Primary Years Programme has no external examination, which makes it the stage where a proximity search misleads most. Nothing is riding on a paper, so families often wait. What is actually forming is the number sense, reading stamina and written explanation that Middle Years assessment will test two years later. Useful tuition at this stage is short, frequent and diagnostic: find the gap in place value or fractions, close it, and move on. Sessions run 30 to 45 minutes because attention, not timetable, is the limit.
programmes.countryNote: In Dubai, KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies in every private school from the primary years regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with separate classes organised for Arab and non-Arab students. A PYP family is therefore running two curricula at once from the start, and the Arabic strand is the one most often left unsupported until it becomes a Middle Years problem.

programmes.name: Middle Years Programme
programmes.description: The Middle Years Programme marks against four criteria per subject, each lettered A to D and each with its own mark band, and the descriptors reward explanation and reflection as much as the right answer. Students who have been scoring well on content alone lose marks here for the first time and cannot see why. Tuition works best when it is aimed at a criterion rather than a topic: take the task the school has set, read the descriptor out loud, and rebuild the response against it.
programmes.countryNote: Middle Years students in the UAE sit inside a school that is inspected on attainment and progress against both the programme standards and the emirate's own framework, whether that is a KHDA inspection rating in Dubai or an ADEK school rating in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain. A Good or Very Good overall judgement is an average across the school, so it can sit comfortably on top of one department that cannot staff a subject properly.

programmes.name: Diploma Programme
programmes.description: The Diploma is where the geography of tutoring breaks down completely. A student takes three subjects at Higher Level and three at Standard, plus Theory of Knowledge, the Extended Essay and Creativity, Activity, Service. Each subject carries an Internal Assessment marked in school and moderated externally. Finding someone nearby who has taught one of those six subjects is plausible. Finding someone nearby who has taught the specific Higher Level option your child's school chose, and marked its Internal Assessment, is mostly luck.
programmes.countryNote: UAE Diploma families carry an extra piece of administration no local search surfaces: the Ministry of Education equivalency file that converts a Diploma into a UAE-recognised secondary certificate for local university applications. The Ministry publishes explicit subject-and-grade rules for the British and American tracks. For the IB there is no points figure we are willing to print without reading it on moe.gov.ae, so treat any site that quotes one with scepticism and check the Ministry's own page.

programmes.name: Career-related Programme
programmes.description: The Career-related Programme pairs two or more Diploma courses with a career-related study, a reflective project, a service-learning requirement and language development. It is offered by relatively few UAE schools, which makes the local tutor pool for its specific components very thin indeed. The Diploma courses inside it are marked exactly as they are for a full Diploma candidate, so the subject teaching is identical; the reflective project is where students need process coaching rather than content.
programmes.countryNote: Because few schools in the Emirates run it, a Career-related Programme family searching locally will often find nobody who has seen the reflective project assessment criteria at all. This is the clearest case for a national rather than a neighbourhood pool, and it is also the case where you should ask the Ministry of Education directly about equivalency rather than assume the Diploma rules transfer.

ib-tutor-near-me.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects UAE families ask for most, written as what the component actually demands rather than as a list of topics. Where a subject appears below with Higher Level named, the scarcity of a local specialist is the whole reason this page exists.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches
subjects.description: Proof, calculus and algebraic fluency carry the Higher Level paper, and the exploration is marked on criteria that reward genuine mathematical reasoning over presentation. Marks go missing in Paper 1 where no calculator is allowed and partial working is not shown. Students who arrived from a Middle Years course that leaned on a graphical display calculator feel this immediately.

subjects.name: Mathematics: Applications and Interpretation
subjects.description: Statistics, modelling and technology-assisted problem solving dominate. The route is often chosen late and for the wrong reason. Before switching, check the published entry requirements of the specific university courses your child is aiming at, because some engineering and economics programmes name Analysis and Approaches. That check belongs in Year 11, not in the February of Year 13.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Organic mechanisms, energetics and equilibrium account for most of the lost marks, and the scientific investigation is where able students most often underperform because the research question is too broad to control. The Higher Level extension topics are the single hardest thing to staff locally; this is the subject families most often cannot cover inside a driving radius.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Fields, circular motion and the unit-two mechanics work reward students who can convert a described situation into a free-body diagram quickly. Data analysis questions carry marks for uncertainty treatment that students skip under time pressure. Online lessons handle this well because the worked solution is built on a shared screen and stays available afterwards.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: Command terms decide the mark here more than in any other science. Explain, outline, suggest and evaluate each have a defined expectation, and a correct biological fact written against the wrong command term scores nothing. Tuition that drills the command term against the subject guide wording moves grades faster than more content revision.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy, real-world application and the evaluation paragraph are the three marks students leave behind. The internal assessment commentaries must be built on recent news articles and kept inside a strict word limit, and the most common failure is a commentary that summarises the article instead of applying a named diagram to it.

subjects.name: Business Management
subjects.description: The case study paper rewards students who read the stimulus material as evidence rather than as background, and the Higher Level extension requires quantitative tools many candidates meet for the first time in Year 13. The project is marked on the quality of the research question and the use of primary or secondary data, not on the length of the appendix.

subjects.name: English A: Language and Literature
subjects.description: The individual oral and the paper on unseen non-literary texts are where UAE candidates with strong written English still lose marks, because both are assessed on close analysis of technique rather than on fluency. Preparation means repeated timed practice on unseen extracts with feedback on the analytical move, not on the vocabulary.

subjects.name: Arabic B and Arabic ab initio
subjects.description: Arabic sits in two places for a UAE family at once: as an IB language acquisition subject with its own assessment, and as a Ministry-mandated school subject with its own class organisation and language-of-instruction rules. The two are marked differently and taught differently, and conflating them is the usual reason a strong student is doing badly in one of them.

subjects.name: Geography
subjects.description: Case-study recall decides the extended-response marks, and most candidates carry too many cases at too shallow a depth. The fieldwork-based internal assessment needs a question narrow enough to collect real data against, which is harder in the Emirates than in the textbook examples and is worth planning with a specialist early.

ib-tutor-near-me.regionsTitle: What "near me" means in each emirate
ib-tutor-near-me.regionsIntro: The same search produces a different result in each emirate, because the regulator, the school density and the realistic travel radius all change. Below is what a family in each place is actually working with, and which authority holds the school's file.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Regulated by KHDA, which published 227 private schools and 17 curricula for 2024-25 and confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees would not rise for 2026-27. Highest school density in the country, so a local search returns the most results and the least filtering: plenty of generalists, few Higher Level specialists.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Distances between Khalifa City, the island and Al Reem mean an evening slot that works in September drifts by November, which is the practical argument against a tutor who has to drive at all.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also ADEK territory, with a smaller IB school cluster than the coast. A family here searching for a Higher Level subject specialist within a sensible radius will frequently find nobody at all, and the fallback is usually a generalist who has not taught the component.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Many families live here and commute to a Dubai school, so the usable session window starts late and prayer times shape the evening.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority. The local IB pool is small enough that proximity stops being a useful filter entirely, and the commute to a Dubai or Sharjah school already consumes the early evening.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Private education is regulated by the emirate's Department of Knowledge, which also approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. RAK is one of three emirates that returned zero mentions across the competitor pages reviewed for this page, which tells you how thin local coverage of these searches is.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the Ministry of Education. On the east coast, a search radius wide enough to include a subject specialist would include a mountain road, which is the clearest illustration on this page that distance and teaching quality are unrelated variables.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under Ministry of Education supervision. The smallest private-school market in the country, and the place where an online pool changes the answer most: the question moves from who is available here to who has taught this syllabus anywhere.

schoolClusters.note: The densest IB and IGCSE cluster in the Emirates, which is why Dubai families most often assume proximity solves the problem. Students we support attend schools across the city, and the pattern we see is a strong school with one department that cannot cover a Higher Level option in the year it is needed.

ADEK territory, with the IB and British clusters spread across the island, Khalifa City and Al Raha. Travel between them in the early evening is the reason families here move to live video first. Al Ain's smaller cluster means a subject-level specialist is rarely available locally at all.

Three different regulatory arrangements sit inside this cluster: SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Families often commute south to a Dubai school, which compresses the usable tuition window into a narrow evening slot.

modes.description: One subject, one tutor, the same time every week, booked around the school run rather than around a drive. The session follows your child's own school deadlines: the test on Thursday, the draft due at the end of the month, the topic the class is on now. A short written note after each lesson records what was covered and what to practise before the next one.

Past-paper questions are attempted under timed conditions by the student first, then marked and rebuilt against the published criteria. We reference official papers and mark schemes and link to the board's own site rather than redistributing them.

The tutor reads it, asks questions, points at the criterion that is not being met and explains what the descriptor is asking for. The student then rewrites it. Nobody writes, rewrites or completes any part of the work.

sections.heading: What a search for an IB tutor near me actually returns
paragraphs: A map result set is built from one input: a pin inside the area your screen is showing. Everything a parent actually wants to know sits outside that input. Whether the person has taught the Diploma rather than a national curriculum. Whether they have taught the subject at Higher Level rather than Standard. Whether they have ever marked the component your child is losing marks on. Whether they hold the permit the UAE requires. None of that is in the ranking signal, and none of it is in the distance.

The result set also reflects who has done the local marketing rather than who can teach. Agency pages built for a district name rank for that district name. A tuition centre with premises ranks because it has an address to verify. An independent teacher with fifteen years of Diploma Chemistry and no website does not appear at all. So the parent who searches IB tuition near me is reading a map of marketing spend, and reading it as a map of teaching quality.

The honest version is simpler. Proximity is only worth paying for if the thing you are buying has to be physically present. A violin lesson arguably does. A Mathematics exploration conversation does not: it needs a screen with the student's own working on it, a tutor who knows what criterion C is asking for, and an hour nobody has spent in a car. sections.heading: The nearest qualified adult is often the one person who may not take the work
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit, not left to the market. The private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is issued through MoHRE, and it is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Anyone offering private tutoring without that permit is, in the Ministry's own words, subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so no figure appears on this page.

That eligibility list is where proximity collapses. The closest adult who already knows your child's syllabus, your child's teacher, and your child's actual weakness is their own subject teacher at school. Gulf News has reported that ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and that the MoHRE permit's code of conduct carries the same restriction on serving students affiliated with their own school. We treat that as press-reported rather than as a quotation of policy, and any family relying on it should check the current ADEK document or ask the school directly.

Two practical consequences follow for a parent. First, never let a conversation start with the idea of hiring your child's own teacher privately, however convenient the drive. Second, the one checkable credential in this market is the MoHRE private tuition work permit, and asking for it costs nothing. A tutor who holds it will show it. A tutor who deflects has told you something useful. The table sets out each category of person who might teach your child, where their permit comes from and what a parent can realistically verify.

sections.heading: Your address decides your regulator, and the regulator decides what you can ask for
paragraphs: Parents often assume the curriculum determines the oversight. It does not. The emirate does. A KHDA inspection rating covers a Dubai school whatever curriculum it teaches, and an ADEK school rating covers an Abu Dhabi or Al Ain one on a different framework. Sharjah's authority and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge go further than inspection: both approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. In Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools directly.

This matters to a tutoring decision in two concrete ways. It tells you where the inspection report lives, which is the single most useful free document a parent can read before spending anything. And it tells you who approved the fee schedule and the assessment arrangements, which is who to ask when the school's answer does not satisfy you. Across the competitor pages reviewed for this page, ADEK was named by nobody at all and Sharjah's authority appeared once, which is a fair measure of how little of this reaches parents.

Read the report at subject level, not at headline level. An overall judgement is an average across phases and departments. A school rated Very Good can hold one department that lost two specialists in August and is being covered by a generalist until January, and that is precisely the situation a parent diagnoses from the subject tables in the report rather than from the front page. The federal baseline sits underneath all of it: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

sections.heading: Distance to a tutor is not distance to a Higher Level specialist
paragraphs: A Diploma student takes six subjects, three of them at Higher Level, and the Higher Level extension material is where the grade is decided. The pool of adults who have taught that extension material, for that subject, and marked its Internal Assessment, is small in absolute terms anywhere in the world. Restricting it to a thirty-minute drive from a specific UAE address usually reduces it to zero, and a parent who does not know that reads the empty result as absence of need rather than absence of supply.

What happens next is predictable. The family hires the nearest available person who teaches the subject at any level, because the alternative looks like doing nothing. The sessions are pleasant, the content is revised, and the Higher Level paper still goes badly, because nobody in the room had seen the extension topics under exam conditions. This is the most common tutoring failure UAE families describe to us, and it is a supply problem dressed up as a motivation problem.

An IB Higher Level tutor online solves it by changing the search space rather than the search term. A family in Al Ain, Ras Al Khaimah or Fujairah gets the same pool as a family in Jumeirah. An IB Diploma tutor near me is a question about roads; a specialist in the component your child is losing marks on is a question about who has taught it. The list below is where we see local searches run out first, with the question to put to your school's IB coordinator before you spend anything.

sections.heading: What the UAE market charges, and how much of it is the car
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible competitor pages in this market publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. So here are the published AED bands, with the kind of provider that publishes each one and the date they were read. These are market rates, not an IB Gram price list. What IB Gram quotes depends on subject, level and session length, and it starts with a free trial lesson rather than a rate card you have to decode.

Read the bands as a function of two things: who is teaching, and what else is inside the fee. A university student working online sits at the bottom. A subject specialist who has taught the Diploma for a decade sits in the middle. A named examiner-led service sits at the top. The in-home band sits high for a reason that has nothing to do with teaching quality: the fee is carrying a car, a driver's hour and a fuel cost, and the parent is paying for all three at the teaching rate.

Monthly packages seen in this market run around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and roughly AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Bestimate's published monthly estimates for one weekly hour run AED 240 to 600 at the budget tier, AED 600 to 1,200 in the middle and AED 1,000 to 2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Set that against the KHDA confirmation of 22 May 2026 that private school fees would not rise in Dubai for 2026-27, and tuition is the part of the education budget still moving.

sections.heading: The hidden hour: what a visiting tutor costs in evening minutes
paragraphs: Cost in this market is usually discussed as a rate and almost never as time. That is the wrong unit for a school night. A UAE secondary student finishes the school run somewhere between half past three and half past five depending on the emirate and the bus route, needs food, and has homework the school set that day. The question is not what an hour costs. The question is how many of the remaining usable minutes the arrangement consumes, and how many of those minutes are teaching.

Do the arithmetic once and it settles the format argument without any marketing in it. Take a 60-minute lesson with a tutor who lives ten minutes away and arrives at six. Add the doorstep, the settling, the drink, the small talk with a parent and the pack-up: the household has given up roughly eighty minutes to buy sixty. Now move that tutor across a city in the five-to-seven window. The hour is unchanged, the arrival time is not, and a slot that drifts week to week is the slot that eventually gets cancelled.

Live video costs about sixty-five minutes of the evening for sixty minutes of teaching, and the five are spent logging in. It also produces artefacts a visit does not: a shared screen with the student's own working annotated on it, a worked solution that stays on file, and a recording of the explanation they can replay the night before the test. None of that is an argument that screens are warmer than rooms. It is an argument about where the minutes go.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies: the timetable nobody searches for
paragraphs: Every UAE family running an international curriculum is actually running two. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai's private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. The federal position sits underneath that: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

The rules are more specific than most parents realise, and they constrain tutoring directly. KHDA requires separate classes for Arab and non-Arab students in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic must be the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arab students and for Arabic as a first language; Social Studies is delivered in Arabic for Arab students; non-Arab students take Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the school's licensed-curriculum language.

Two further details matter. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length as long as the total weekly time is met, and it is advised that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. And for these subjects the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the Ministry of Education, is strictly prohibited. That last line is why a tutor supporting Arabic or Islamic Education should be working from the school's own prescribed material and the student's own set work, not from an imported workbook.

sections.heading: The exam timetable your postcode sits inside
paragraphs: Here is a geography fact about examinations that no local search will ever surface. Cambridge International allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones, each with its own version of the timetable, and the guidance to exams officers is blunt: it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Your child's paper time is therefore a function of where the centre sits, which is the one sense in which near me genuinely decides something.

The second thing nobody tells parents is how far in front of the paper the real deadlines fall. In the UAE there are two Cambridge series to count back from, June and November, and the honest answer about the June one is that its entry date is not a single global number: Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, publishes a timetable per zone, says it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and warns that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. What is fixed is the gap rather than the day. Entries close earlier in the same school year, forecast grades go in before the papers begin, the papers themselves run from late spring into June, and results follow in August. Pearson's parallel series gives you a hard set of numbers to sanity-check that gap against: its Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A family that starts looking for support in the spring is looking after the entry decision has already been made.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSEs run in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable running from late October to 19 November 2026. June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August; November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so always open the live official PDF rather than trusting a restated date. For the IB we publish no session or results date here: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so confirm every IB date with your school's IB coordinator or on ibo.org itself.

sections.heading: Academic honesty does not change with distance
paragraphs: There is a part of this market that sells completed Internal Assessments. One site found during the research for these pages advertises them at a fixed price. Buying one puts a student's entire Diploma at risk, because submitting work that is not their own is malpractice under IB rules and the consequence falls on the candidate, not the vendor. No proximity, convenience or price argument survives that. It is worth saying plainly on a page about finding a tutor, because the same search results contain both kinds of provider and they look alike from outside.

So here is the boundary IB Gram works to, in operational terms. A tutor may teach the underlying skill, explain what a criterion is asking for, model a different problem of the same type, ask the questions a supervisor would ask, read the student's own draft and say which descriptor it is not meeting, and help plan a research question that can actually be answered. A tutor may not write any part of the work, rewrite a passage into its final form, supply a near-match exemplar to be adapted, or produce data the student did not collect. IB Internal Assessment feedback means feedback, and it is given on the student's own writing.

The same restraint applies to materials. We reference IB, Cambridge and Pearson syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and subject guides by citing them and linking to the official site; we do not reproduce or distribute them. A tutor who offers you a folder of mark schemes, a bank of completed exemplars or a topic-matched essay to work from is offering something that is either a copyright problem or an honesty problem, and often both. Ask the question directly at the trial lesson and listen to how fast the answer comes.

sections.heading: Ministry of Education equivalency, and the one number nobody should publish
paragraphs: Equivalency is the process that converts an international school certificate into a UAE-recognised one, and it is the piece of administration that most often surprises a family in the final year. The Ministry publishes explicit requirements for the British and American tracks. On the British track, a student must show five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

One detail in that rule is worth reading twice, because a ranking competitor page gets it wrong: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE and IGCSE count. A site telling UAE candidates they must take six IGCSE subjects is publishing an inflated figure. On the American track, English proficiency is demonstrated by a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying.

For MoE equivalency for IB students there is no points figure on this page, and you should be wary of any page that gives you one. The source we read for the British and American tracks states no IB threshold, so printing one would be an invention. Check moe.gov.ae or the emirate's attestation authority directly. Equivalency is also not something IB Gram performs, submits or influences, and no amount of tutoring is required for it. Tuition is for the grades; the paperwork is a separate administrative track with its own official channel.

process.title: Tell us the subject, the level and the component
process.description: Not the year group and not the postcode. The useful version is specific: Chemistry Higher Level, losing marks on energetics, scientific investigation due in six weeks, school uses the Cambridge pathway for the sibling in Year 11. That sentence is enough to match a specialist. A district name is not, which is the whole argument of this page.

process.title: Take the free trial lesson
process.description: One 45-minute session over live video, before any payment and with no card details taken. Use it to watch the teaching rather than to read a profile: does the tutor diagnose, or just explain? Do they know what the criterion is asking for? Ask them directly what they will and will not do with a coursework draft.

process.title: Agree a plan against your school's dates
process.description: Your child's school sets the deadlines that matter: the mock window, the internal assessment submission, the entry deadline the exams officer is working to. The plan is written against those dates, not against a generic term structure, and the exam board's own timetable PDF is the reference rather than a date restated on a website.

process.title: Weekly sessions, with a written note after each
process.description: Same tutor, same slot, on Gulf Standard Time. After each session a short note records what was covered, what the student got wrong and what to practise before the next one. If the match is not working, say so and we move you; a tutor nobody clicked with is a worse outcome than a tutor nobody could reach.

whyPoints.title: Matched by syllabus, not by radius
whyPoints.description: The filter is which board, which level and which component your child is losing marks on. A family in Fujairah or Al Ain gets the same pool as a family in Jumeirah, because the pool is not drawn as a circle on a map. That is the only real advantage online delivery has, and it is a large one at Higher Level.

whyPoints.title: The delivery model stated before you ask
whyPoints.description: Lessons are live video, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time. IB Gram does not arrange home visits anywhere in the Emirates and holds no UAE office or centre; home tutoring is a service we run in India only. Several pages in this market conceal non-UAE delivery behind a foreign phone number, which is a trust failure we would rather avoid by saying it first.

whyPoints.title: Coursework support that keeps the work the student's
whyPoints.description: Feedback, questioning and criterion-level explanation on a draft the student wrote. No writing, no rewriting to final form, no exemplar supplied to be adapted. In a market where completed Internal Assessments are sold openly, being explicit about the boundary is more useful to a parent than another sentence about quality.

whyPoints.title: Figures attributed, or left out
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page is the market's, with the kind of provider that published it and the month it was read. The regulatory lines are quoted from u.ae, KHDA and MoHRE. Where a number is not verifiable, such as an IB session date or an IB equivalency threshold, it is absent rather than estimated.

whyPoints.title: Coverage limits disclosed, not hidden
whyPoints.description: Some subject and level combinations have no specialist free in the window a family wants. We say so, give a realistic timeframe, and suggest the nearest sensible alternative, which is sometimes a different component focus rather than a different tutor. No competitor page reviewed for this project discloses a coverage limit at all.

faqs.question: What does searching for an IB tutor near me actually return in the UAE?
faqs.answer: A map of who has a business pin inside the area your screen is showing, ranked largely by local marketing rather than teaching record. It cannot tell you whether anyone in that set has taught your child's subject at Higher Level, marked the component losing marks, or holds the MoHRE private tuition work permit. It also silently excludes experienced teachers without a website. The more useful questions are which board and level someone has taught, which papers they have marked, and what time a session can realistically start on a school night during term.

faqs.question: Is the closest tutor to our address the right one for Higher Level Chemistry?
faqs.answer: Rarely, and the reason is supply rather than quality. The number of people who have taught the Higher Level extension topics and marked a scientific investigation is small anywhere. Restricting that pool to a thirty-minute drive from one UAE address often reduces it to nobody. Families then hire the nearest person who teaches Chemistry at any level, revise content pleasantly for months, and still find the Higher Level paper goes badly, because nobody in the room had seen the extension material under exam conditions. Widening the pool, not the radius, is what fixes it.

faqs.question: Can my child's own subject teacher tutor her privately after school?
faqs.answer: Plan on no. Gulf News has reported that ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, and that the MoHRE private tuition work permit carries a code of conduct with the same restriction on serving students affiliated with their own school. We treat that as press-reported rather than as a quotation of policy, so confirm the current wording with ADEK or ask the school directly. Either way, do not make the nearest convenient arrangement the one that puts a teacher's position at risk.

faqs.question: Which authority holds my child's school file, and how does that change my choices?
faqs.answer: The emirate decides, not the curriculum. Dubai schools answer to KHDA, Abu Dhabi and Al Ain to ADEK, Sharjah to the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah to the federal Ministry of Education. That tells you where the inspection report lives, which is the most useful free document available to a parent before spending anything. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority also approves fees, curricula, courses and assessment methods, so there is somewhere to ask when the school's answer is unsatisfying.

faqs.question: How do I check that a tutor has the MoHRE private tuition work permit?
faqs.answer: Ask to see it, and ask when it was issued. The permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page is titled Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system with a two-working-day completion time. Because it costs nothing, there is no financial excuse for not holding one. Anyone tutoring without it is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so treat any quoted figure with caution.

faqs.question: What do UAE families pay per hour, and how much of that is travel?
faqs.answer: Published market rates run roughly AED 33 to 150 for budget online tutoring, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified online subject tutor, AED 180 to 500 for a visiting tutor in the home, AED 200 to 450 and above for an IB or IGCSE specialist, and up to AED 650 for a premium named service. Those bands were read in October 2026 from providers' own pages and from Bestimate's Dubai cost table. The in-home band sits high largely because the fee carries a car, a driver's hour and fuel, all billed at the teaching rate.

faqs.question: We live in Ras Al Khaimah. Does distance from Dubai limit the subjects available?
faqs.answer: Under a proximity model, severely. Ras Al Khaimah has a small private-school market, its own Department of Knowledge as the regulator, and it was one of three emirates that returned no mentions at all across the competitor pages reviewed for this page. A local search for a Higher Level specialist will often return nobody. With live video the question changes from who is available in the northern emirates to who has taught this syllabus anywhere, and the answer stops depending on the drive down Emirates Road.

faqs.question: How many minutes of an evening does a visiting tutor actually use?
faqs.answer: More than the hour you are paying for. A tutor living ten minutes away and arriving at six typically costs the household about eighty minutes once the doorstep, the settling, the drink and the pack-up are counted, to buy sixty minutes of teaching. Move that journey into the five-to-seven window and the hour is unchanged but the arrival time is not, so the slot drifts week to week. Live video costs around sixty-five minutes for the same sixty, and the annotated working and worked solutions stay on file afterwards.

faqs.question: Do Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies still run beside the IB Diploma?
faqs.answer: Yes. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai's private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 where the school year begins in April. The federal baseline is the same: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. In practice your child is running two curricula at once, and the Arabic strand is the one most often left unsupported.

faqs.question: Can a tutor use my child's school's own Arabic worksheets in a session?
faqs.answer: Working from the school's prescribed material and your child's own set tasks is the right approach, and it is also the compliant one. KHDA's mandatory-subject guidance states that for these subjects the use of any different or additional content, without prior permission from the Ministry of Education, is strictly prohibited. So a tutor importing an unrelated workbook is not helping. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided total weekly time is met, and the guidance advises at least 25 minutes for any mandatory-subject lesson.

faqs.question: What paperwork does the Ministry of Education want after the Diploma finishes?
faqs.answer: Equivalency converts an international certificate into a UAE-recognised one. For the British track the published rule is five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3, plus either one Advanced Level subject at no less than E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. For the IB we publish no points figure, because the source we read states none; check moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation authority directly. Equivalency is not something IB Gram performs, and tuition is not required for it.

faqs.question: What is a tutor allowed to do with a draft of the Extended Essay?
faqs.answer: Read it, question it, and explain which criterion it is not yet meeting. A tutor may help shape a research question that can actually be answered, model how a comparable argument is built, and point out where evidence is asserted rather than shown. A tutor may not write any part of it, rewrite a passage into its final form, supply a near-match exemplar to adapt, or produce data the student did not collect. Submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice under IB rules, and the consequence falls on the candidate.

faqs.question: When should an IGCSE entry be made, and who makes it?
faqs.answer: Your school, acting as the exam centre, and far earlier than most families expect. Cambridge sits UAE candidates in a June series and a November series, and final entries for either close months before that series' first paper; the operative date is the one your centre gives you on the statement of entry, because Cambridge timetables by administrative zone rather than by country. Pearson Edexcel International GCSEs run in May/June and November, with the November 2026 final timetable ending 19 November 2026 and results reaching students the following January. Always open the board's live official timetable rather than a restated date, since provisional timetables are revised.

faqs.question: How does a live video lesson handle a Physics practical write-up?
faqs.answer: The practical work itself happens in the school laboratory, as it must. What a tutor works on is everything around it: the research question, the control of variables, the uncertainty treatment, the graph choice and the evaluation paragraph, which is where most of the available marks are actually lost. Over video the student's own write-up sits on a shared screen and is annotated live, so the feedback attaches to their words rather than being described in the abstract. The annotated version and the worked example stay available afterwards.

faqs.question: Our school is rated Good. Does that mean every subject is taught well?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the most common misreading of a KHDA inspection rating or an ADEK school rating. An overall judgement is an average across phases and departments. A well-run school can still hold one department that lost two specialists in August and is being covered by a generalist until January. Read the subject-level tables in the published report rather than the headline band, and ask the school directly who is teaching the Higher Level group this year. That single question is more informative than any rating.

faqs.question: What happens when nobody in the UAE covers my child's subject combination?
faqs.answer: We tell you, with a realistic timeframe, rather than filling the slot with whoever is free. Some combinations are genuinely thin: a Career-related Programme reflective project, a minority language at Higher Level, or an unusual option within a science. Sometimes the better answer is a different focus with an available specialist, such as exam technique with a subject teacher rather than content with nobody. No competitor page reviewed during the research for this page discloses a coverage limit at all, which is precisely why stating one is worth doing.

ib-tutor-near-me.closingHeading: Stop measuring the distance, start checking the permit and the component
ib-tutor-near-me.closingBody: If you take three things from this page, take these. Ask any tutor for the MoHRE private tuition work permit, because it is free, it is checkable, and it costs you nothing to request. Read your child's school inspection report at subject level, from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Department of Knowledge or the Ministry of Education depending on where you live. And describe the problem by component rather than by location: Chemistry Higher Level energetics, not a district name. Then take the free 45-minute trial lesson and judge the teaching. Lessons run live online, one-to-one, on Gulf Standard Time, which is why your address decides nothing about the tutor you get.

ib-tutors.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach the IB Diploma and Middle Years Programme to families across the seven emirates. Each one is matched by subject, level and syllabus guide version rather than by postcode, because the version of the guide your child sits changes what a 7 looks like far more than the city does.

intro.heading: What a UAE parent is actually buying when they hire an IB tutor
paragraphs: The IB Diploma is the same programme in Dubai that it is in Geneva. The system around it is not. A family in the UAE is working inside three emirate-level regulators and one federal ministry, a school fee framework tied to inspection ratings, a set of Ministry of Education subjects that run alongside the Diploma, and an equivalency process that decides whether a 38-point Diploma is accepted by a UAE institution at all. None of that changes what Paper 2 asks a candidate to do. All of it changes what a parent has to plan around, and almost none of it appears on the pages currently selling tuition.

That is why this page is organised around the system rather than the subject. Most pages advertising IB tutors in the UAE describe the Diploma, list some subjects and stop. A parent who already knows the Diploma needs something else: which authority inspects their child's school, what the rating on the front of the report does and does not measure, which subjects the Ministry of Education requires beyond the six IB courses, what the MoE equivalency certificate asks for, who is legally permitted to tutor here, and where the line sits between a tutor helping with an Internal Assessment and a tutor committing malpractice on a student's behalf.

On delivery, IB Gram is plain about the format. Teaching for UAE families happens one-to-one over live video on a shared screen, timed to Gulf Standard Time around school pick-up, sport and prayer times. Home visits are part of what we offer in India, and not part of what we offer here. The reason is not cost. A Diploma cohort in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain is small, and a Chemistry HL specialist who knows the 2023 science guide is not necessarily living within a thirty-minute drive of the family who needs one. Working over video takes the drive out of the matching problem entirely.

Prices on this page are market figures, attributed to whoever published them. The UAE tutoring market publishes very little in dirhams: of the competitor pages reviewed for this page in October 2026, three carried no price at all and two quoted US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. The AED bands further down come from published competitor rate cards and from Bestimate's Dubai tutoring cost table. They describe what the market charges. They are not an IB Gram price list, because a sensible quote depends on the subject, the level, and how many weeks are left before the session.

What follows is the regulatory map first, then the school and marking system, then the honesty rules, then cost, then the comparison between a tutor in the room and a tutor on the screen. Read the sections that apply to your emirate and skip the rest. If your child is in Year 12 at a KHDA-inspected school in Dubai and the problem is Maths AA HL, the sections on inspection ratings, on who marks what, and on academic honesty are the three that will change what you do this term.

The federal Ministry of Education covers Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah
