igcse-a-star-coaching.programmesIntro: Four routes feed into or out of an A star target in the UAE. Each has a different calendar, and the date a family needs to act on depends on which one their school runs. Check the board on the statement of entry rather than the school's prospectus, because schools frequently enter different subjects with different boards.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: The two-year course most UK-curriculum schools in the UAE run to Year 11. Cambridge examines it in a June series and a November series, with syllabus codes such as 0580 for Mathematics and 0625 for Physics printed on the statement of entry. Many syllabuses are graded A* to G, some on 9 to 1, and a few are tiered so that the entry decision itself sets a ceiling on the grade available.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE, the Cambridge calendar collides with a school year that starts in late August or early September and with a Ramadan term that shortens the teaching day. A Year 11 cohort here typically gets its mocks in the window between the winter break and the February half term, which is also the last point at which a tiering decision can realistically be revisited with a head of department.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's international qualification, examined in May/June and November each year, with codes such as 4MA1 for Mathematics. Pearson publishes provisional timetables well ahead of each series and then a final timetable, so the dates a family writes on the fridge in October may shift before the papers arrive. Results dates differ from Cambridge's, which matters when a university or a school place has a deadline attached.
programmes.countryNote: The November series is heavily used in the UAE by candidates retaking a single paper or sitting one subject early. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and the previous November series reached students on 22 January 2026. A family deciding in September whether to use November needs those two dates side by side before committing to a term of coaching.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Checkpoint
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE course begins, assessed through Checkpoint tests that Cambridge offers in March, May and October. Checkpoint results carry no grades on a certificate, but they are the earliest honest signal of whether a student is on a path towards the top band in a subject, and they arrive while there is still time to change the subject options rather than the revision plan.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools use Checkpoint differently from one another: some sit it as a formal series, some skip it, some use internal tests instead. Families here often meet the question of A star potential for the first time at the Year 9 options evening, which in most UAE schools falls between January and March. That is the single cheapest moment to intervene in a Maths or Science trajectory.

programmes.name: AS and A Level follow-on
programmes.description: What the IGCSE grades buy. Cambridge International A Level runs in the same June and November series pattern; Pearson International A Level runs alongside its International GCSE dates. A student's IGCSE profile decides which subjects are open at AS, and in several subjects an A at IGCSE and an A star at IGCSE lead to noticeably different first terms in Year 12.
programmes.countryNote: For UAE families, the A Level year is also where Ministry of Education equivalency becomes concrete: the British route asks for one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, on top of five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects. The five-subject count is set at IGCSE, which is why an A star plan should be built with the equivalency file already in view.

igcse-a-star-coaching.subjectsIntro: A star coaching is subject-specific by definition, because the last few marks in each subject go missing in different places. The list below names where the near-miss usually sits rather than restating the syllabus contents, which your child's teacher already has. Codes are given only where a school is likely to see them printed on an entry.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580, Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, or single tier
subjects.description: The top band is usually lost on the last question of each paper rather than across the paper. Multi-step problems combining algebra with geometry, bounds and error, and transformations of functions take disproportionate marks from strong candidates. Coaching here means timed sets of final-question items, not another pass through the whole syllabus.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625)
subjects.description: Extended candidates aiming high usually lose marks on practical description, uncertainty and the extended-response items where a method has to be explained rather than calculated. Electricity and electromagnetic induction produce the most near-misses. Alternative-to-practical papers reward a specific style of answer that is learnable in a handful of sessions.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles calculations and organic reaction pathways separate the A band from the A star band. Strong candidates who can do the chemistry still drop marks by not stating conditions, not balancing an equation they wrote correctly in words, or writing a qualitative answer where the paper asked for a number with a unit.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: The content is largely learnable, so the top grade turns on command terms and data handling. A question asking to explain rather than describe, or to suggest rather than state, has a mark scheme shape. Coaching for the top band mostly means practising answer length against marks available: four marks means four distinct points.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences
subjects.description: A double-award entry gives two grades from a combined syllabus, and the top band is harder to reach because the paper samples broadly with little room to specialise. Families choosing between three separate sciences and a combined route should make that call at options stage, not in Year 11, because it changes the grade ceiling.

subjects.name: English Language
subjects.description: The top band depends on directed-writing and summary technique rather than vocabulary. Strong writers lose marks by missing the audience and form instructions, by paraphrasing rather than condensing in summary tasks, or by running over on one question and under on another. Timed practice with the mark scheme visible is the whole intervention.

subjects.name: English Literature
subjects.description: Essay structure under time pressure is where the grade sits. Candidates who know the texts well still land in the A band by narrating instead of arguing, or by quoting at length without analysing the quotation. Coaching focuses on paragraph architecture and on closed-book recall of short, usable quotations.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: The long-answer evaluation marks decide the grade. A candidate who defines terms accurately and draws a correct diagram can still miss the top band for never weighing one side against the other or never reaching a judgement. Diagram labelling and the evaluate command term are the two highest-yield things to drill.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Case-study application separates grades. The content is short; the marks come from using the stimulus material by name rather than answering generically. Calculation questions on margins and break-even are routinely lost to unit errors by candidates who understand the concept perfectly well.

subjects.name: Computer Science
subjects.description: The written paper rewards precision in pseudocode and trace tables, which strong programmers often treat casually. Data representation and number-base conversion produce avoidable losses. The practical or project component has its own internal deadline, usually months before the written papers, and that deadline is where the grade quietly leaks away.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language
subjects.description: Taken as an examined subject by Arab students in many UAE schools, and separately mandated as a school subject by the emirate regulators. It is examined in its own right, with its own paper structure, but it does not count among the five accredited subjects the Ministry of Education requires for British-track equivalency.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics
subjects.description: Sat by strong Maths candidates in some UAE schools in Year 11 alongside the main syllabus, usually as preparation for A Level. It is a sensible target only once the main Maths grade is secure, and it is a poor use of coaching hours for a student still short of the top band in the core paper.

igcse-a-star-coaching.regionsTitle: The seven emirates, and what the calendar looks like in each
igcse-a-star-coaching.regionsIntro: Where a family lives changes two things about an A star plan: which authority regulates the school and therefore who approves its curriculum and assessment arrangements, and what the evening actually looks like once the school run and the commute are done. Online delivery removes the second problem; the first one still has to be understood.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Regulated by the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which oversees the quality of private education in the emirate. Dubai held 227 private schools and 387,441 pupils in 2024-25, with 37 per cent on a UK curriculum, so the IGCSE cohort here is the largest in the country and the one most likely to sit both Cambridge and Pearson entries in the same year group.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which rules out the arrangement many families reach for first.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK. School-run distances are longer here and the practical consequence for an exam-term plan is that a 4pm start is often unrealistic. An online slot after 6pm, or a weekend double session banked against the February half term, usually works better than trying to protect a weekday hour that keeps collapsing.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods in the emirate. Many Sharjah families commute into Dubai for work, so the hour between the end of school and the end of the working day is the one that disappears from a revision plan.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here fall under the federal Ministry of Education, which supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Cohorts are smaller, which means a school may run only one set of each IGCSE option and a student short of the top band in a single subject has nobody in the building teaching an alternative route.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Regulated by the Department of Knowledge, which approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Specialist subject cover is thinnest in the northern emirates: a candidate chasing an A star in Economics or Computer Science often has no local option at all, which is exactly where a video lesson stops being a compromise.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under the federal Ministry of Education. The east-coast position puts an hour or more of road between most families and any tutoring centre in Dubai or Sharjah, so the in-home and centre-based models that dominate the Dubai market are close to irrelevant here. Timetabling around the exam window is the real constraint, not travel.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under the federal Ministry of Education. The smallest IGCSE cohort in the country, which has one practical consequence worth planning for: if a subject is entered through a neighbouring emirate's centre, the Cambridge administrative zone that governs the timetable may not be the one the family assumed.

schoolClusters.note: UK-curriculum schools here enter large IGCSE cohorts and often split boards by department, with Cambridge for the sciences and Pearson for Maths or vice versa. Students supported by IB Gram coaches attend schools of this type; the boards and series below should always be read from the statement of entry rather than assumed from the school's name.

ADEK-regulated schools in the capital run the same two boards with a different term rhythm, and the ethics rules on staff tutoring their own students are enforced more visibly here than elsewhere. Students supported by IB Gram coaches attend schools of this type, usually for one or two subjects rather than a whole timetable.
schools: The British International School Abu Dhabi

igcse-a-star-coaching.modesIntro: Three ways of buying hours, chosen by where the family sits in the calendar rather than by budget. A candidate fourteen months from the paper and a candidate fourteen days from it should not be buying the same thing, and the most common waste in this market is a weekly hour running on autopilot through a term when it should have become something else.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one across the series
modes.description: One hour a week on a fixed slot, running from the start of the course to the exam window, with the plan rewritten after each school assessment. This is the right shape when there are two terms or more left, because it lets content teaching and paper technique alternate instead of competing. It is the wrong shape in the last month.
bullets: A written plan keyed to the school's own scheme of work and assessment dates
Monthly checkpoint note naming what moved and what did not
Slot held through Ramadan, moved rather than cancelled
Rebuilt after the mocks, when the first reliable evidence arrives

modes.title: A backwards-planned revision block
modes.description: A fixed number of hours placed deliberately across the weeks between the mocks and the papers, each session tied to one paper and one topic cluster. The block is designed from the exam timetable, so a subject sat in the first week of the window gets its hours earlier than a subject sat in the last. Most families underestimate how much that ordering matters.
bullets: Built from the centre's own timetable, including the zone version
Weighted towards papers sat earliest in the window
Timed sections marked against published mark schemes
Ends before the paper, not on the morning of it

modes.title: Single-paper clinics
modes.description: Two to four sessions on one component: the alternative-to-practical paper, the directed-writing question, the long-answer evaluation, the trace table. Used by candidates whose overall grade is already strong and whose loss is concentrated in one predictable place. Cheapest intervention per mark on this page, and the one families reach for last when it should often be first.
bullets: Diagnosed from a marked past paper, not from a school report
One component, one mark scheme, repeated under time
Useful at any point in the year, including the final fortnight
Stops when the component stops leaking marks

sections.heading: What an A star actually asks for, and what no coach can tell you
paragraphs: An A star is the top grade on the lettered IGCSE scale. Cambridge reports many of its IGCSE syllabuses on A* to G and a number of them on 9 to 1; Pearson reports International GCSE mostly on 9 to 1, where the grades doing the work of an A* are 9 and 8. The first thing to establish, before any hours are bought, is which scale each of your child's syllabuses uses. It is printed on the statement of entry, and the school's exams officer can confirm it in one email.

The second thing to establish is the tier. Several Cambridge IGCSE syllabuses are offered at Core and Extended, and the Core route does not award the top grades at all. That decision is made by the school when it registers the entry, and it is made months before the paper. A family that discovers the tier in April has discovered it too late. This is the single most expensive date on the whole calendar and almost nobody puts it on a tutoring page.

The third thing is the part nobody can supply: the mark. Grade thresholds are set after each series has been marked, when the board can see how the cohort handled that specific paper, and the board publishes them afterwards. They move year to year because papers vary in difficulty. So a mock marked against an old threshold gives you a region, not a result, and any coach offering this year's number in advance is guessing. What a coach can do is count the marks a student is currently dropping, name where they go, and work through them in order of how many are available.
bullets: Confirm the grading scale per syllabus from the statement of entry
Confirm the tier, because a Core entry caps the grade available
Treat old grade thresholds as context, never as a target mark
Diagnose from a marked paper before buying a block of hours

sections.heading: The A star calendar, counted backwards from the paper
paragraphs: Work from the paper date and move backwards. Each row below is a milestone a UAE family has to clear, in reverse order of how late it can be left. The point of reading it this way is that the earliest rows are the ones with the most leverage and the least cost: a subject option changed at the Year 9 options evening costs nothing, while the same problem addressed six weeks before the paper costs a term of hours and still may not move the grade.

The dates in the right-hand column follow Cambridge's two UAE series, June and November, because those are the only ones a candidate here can be entered for; the February and March sitting belongs to India, and the Checkpoint tests that run in March, May and October are not IGCSE at all. The distance that matters is still large. Final entries for the June series close months before the first paper rather than weeks, which is why the tier decision is effectively locked before the revision term starts, and the exact deadline comes from the centre, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones with its own timetable. Pearson gives the same gap in hard numbers: its Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

For a UAE family sitting the June series instead, the shape is the same and the dates shift: entries close months before the window, forecast grades are collected during it, and results arrive in August. Pearson's June 2026 International GCSE results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Build the plan from your own centre's letter, not from this page, because only the centre knows which series and which zone apply. What this page can tell you is which rows exist and roughly how far apart they sit.

sections.heading: Two boards, two calendars: read the one your centre actually uses
paragraphs: A UAE school commonly enters its Year 11 cohort with both Cambridge and Pearson, split by department. That means one family can be working to two different sets of deadlines and two different results dates in the same summer. Reading the wrong calendar is a quiet and common mistake, and it costs most in the week a family thinks it still has and does not.

Cambridge examines IGCSE, O Level and International A Level in a June series and a November series, and offers Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson's International GCSE is available in May/June and November each year. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series before issuing the final version, so dates copied from a provisional document in the autumn should be checked again in the spring rather than trusted.

The results dates diverge in a way that matters for anything with a deadline attached — a school place, a sixth-form offer, an equivalency file. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026 and its previous November series reached students on 22 January 2026, which is a January result from an autumn sitting. Cambridge puts June series results with centres in August and November series results in January, so the two boards' autumn routes land within weeks of each other while the summer routes do not. If a family is choosing a series specifically to have a grade in hand by a particular month, those gaps are the whole decision. There is a second reason to pin the board down early. Entry deadlines, forecast-grade deadlines and review windows are set per board and per series, so a family working to one calendar while the school works to another will miss a window it did not know existed. Write both boards on the same sheet of paper in September, with the series beside each subject, and check it against the statement of entry when that arrives.

sections.heading: The zone letter on the timetable, and why it can cost a paper
paragraphs: Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the exam timetable. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong zone timetable. That is an unusually blunt sentence from an exam board, and it exists because the mistake happens.

In the UAE the mistake has a specific shape. A family has relatives or friends with children at another school, sometimes in another emirate, and a timetable circulates on a messaging group. The dates look authoritative. They may belong to a different zone. A second version of the shape: a tutor working with students across several centres builds one revision plan from one timetable and applies it to everyone. The plan is then wrong for whichever students sit in a different zone.

The fix is cheap and takes one message. Ask the school's exams officer for the timetable version that applies to your child's centre, in writing, and work only from that. Then order the revision block from it: a candidate whose Physics papers fall in the first days of the window and whose English falls three weeks later should not be revising them in alphabetical order. On an A star plan, where the margin is a handful of marks per paper, getting the last fortnight pointed at the right subject is worth more than an extra hour a week in January.
bullets: Ask the exams officer which of the six zones your centre sits in
Work only from the timetable version issued for that zone
Never build a plan from a timetable shared by another school
Re-sequence the revision block so the earliest paper gets the earliest hours

sections.heading: What A star coaching costs in the UAE market
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for this kind of search publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars. UAE parents do not transact in dollars, so here are the AED bands actually visible in this market, attributed to whoever publishes them. These are market rates, not IB Gram's price list: our own figure comes with the consultation and the free first lesson, because the right number depends on the subject, the series and how many weeks are left.

At the bottom of the market, online tutoring from a university student runs from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour; EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor working online sits roughly between AED 150 and AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150 and IB from AED 200. In-home one-to-one visits, travel included, run from about AED 180 to AED 500 — Bestimate's 2026 rate table puts the band at AED 180 to 350 and independent home tutors at AED 200 to 500.

A subject specialist working at the top of an IGCSE syllabus is quoted between AED 200 and AED 450 or more; TutorChase publishes AED 270 and Bestimate's specialist band reaches AED 450 upwards. Named or examiner-level tutors go higher, with BartyED at AED 650. Monthly packages seen in this market include AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home sessions. Set against that, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27, which is the only part of a UAE education budget that is holding still.

sections.heading: Online, in-home or a centre: what each format does to an A star plan
paragraphs: Answer the home-tutoring question honestly before answering it commercially. In-home one-to-one tuition in the UAE is a real and widely used service, it costs roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour with travel built in, and its pool of available tutors is whoever is prepared to drive to your address at the hour you want. In Dubai that pool is large. In Fujairah, Umm Al Quwain or the outer parts of Al Ain it is small, and in a subject like Economics or Computer Science at the top band it may be empty.

IB Gram does not sell home visits in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. What we deliver to a UAE family is the same hour of one-to-one teaching over live video, with the tutor chosen from a national pool rather than from a twenty-minute radius. For an A star target that trade is strongly in the family's favour: the binding constraint is finding someone who has taught this syllabus to this grade, and geography has nothing to do with that.

Group classes at a centre are the third option and they have a legitimate place — they are cheaper per hour and the social pressure helps some students work. They are the weakest fit for the top band, because a group has to teach to its middle and the marks an A star candidate is losing are individual to them. The comparison below sets out the four variables that actually differ between formats. Note the travel row: an hour of lesson at a centre in Dubai during the evening commute can cost a family ninety minutes of road.

sections.heading: Where an A becomes an A star: the marks that go missing
paragraphs: A student sitting on an A is not a student who needs more content. In nearly every case the remaining marks are concentrated in two or three identifiable places, and the first job of coaching at this level is to find them on a marked paper rather than to guess at them from a school report. A report that says 'good progress, could extend further' tells you nothing you can teach against.

The method is mechanical. Take a full past paper under time, mark it against the published scheme without generosity, then group every dropped mark by component and by command term rather than by topic. What usually emerges is a pattern: all the losses are on the six-mark explain questions, or on the practical paper, or in the last fifteen minutes of every paper. That pattern is the plan. Topic revision, which is what most families buy, is often the least efficient response available.

The table below lists the near-miss patterns that recur most often across the subjects UAE schools enter in volume. None of it is exotic. The value is in the ordering: fixing a timing problem is a two-session job that applies across every paper the student sits, while fixing a content gap in one topic buys marks in one question. On a plan with eight weeks left, work from the top of that list downwards. One caution about the session counts in the final column: they describe how long it usually takes to stop a particular leak, not how long it takes to move a grade. A student with three leaks has three jobs, and they rarely fit into the same fortnight. Count the sessions the diagnosis implies, compare that with the weeks actually left after the mandatory school subjects and the exam timetable are accounted for, and if the two numbers do not meet, narrow the subject list rather than thinning the work.

sections.heading: Ramadan, UAE term dates and the twelve weeks that decide the grade
paragraphs: A UAE revision plan built on a UK calendar breaks. The school year here starts in late August or early September, the winter break falls in December, and Ramadan shortens the school day for several weeks on a date that moves earlier each year. For a June candidate, Ramadan has recently been landing across the period between the mocks and the papers — which is exactly the twelve weeks a backwards plan depends on.

The practical answer is to move the hour rather than lose it. A shortened school day frees the late afternoon and congests the early evening; a post-Iftar slot works well for some families and badly for others, and the only way to find out is to try one week and then decide. Sessions delivered over video make this cheap to test, because nothing has to be rescheduled around anybody's drive. A family that pauses coaching for a month instead usually comes back to a plan that no longer fits the timetable it was built from.

Two further UAE-specific collisions are worth planning for. The mandatory subjects every private school must deliver — Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies — continue through the exam term and take real timetable space, so the revision window is smaller than a family counting free periods assumes. And internal coursework or project deadlines in subjects like Computer Science typically fall months before the written papers, often in the same weeks as the mocks. Put both on the calendar in September, not in February.
bullets: Move the weekly slot during Ramadan rather than pausing the plan
Test a post-Iftar time for one week before committing to it
Count the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education periods out of the revision window
Put internal coursework deadlines on the calendar alongside the exam dates

sections.heading: Five subjects at grade E or above: the threshold that is not an A star
paragraphs: An A star is a university and sixth-form currency. Ministry of Education equivalency is a different threshold entirely, and a surprising number of UAE families meet it late. For the British track, the requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, together with one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail that catches families is which subjects count. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. A student who sat five subjects in total, two of them Arabic and Islamic Education, has three towards the count and will find that out at the wrong moment. One competitor page currently ranking for these queries states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five accredited subjects, excluding those two. Check it against the ministry's own guidance rather than against any tutoring site, including this one.

For the American track, the same guidance sets English proficiency at a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics at a minimum of 450 in the SAT Math test. For the IB Diploma, no points threshold is published in that source, so any figure you see quoted for IB equivalency should be verified on moe.gov.ae before you plan around it. IB Gram does not process equivalency files and no tutoring provider should charge you to handle one — the application route is the ministry's own.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies beside the IGCSE timetable
paragraphs: Every private school in Dubai must teach Arabic, Islamic Education and social or moral studies regardless of the international curriculum it is licensed to deliver, and KHDA set the start of the 2025-26 academic year as the point by which its requirements had to be in place. The federal position is the same in outline: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must follow the ministry's general regulations.

Two of KHDA's rules shape what help is even permitted. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and social studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and the advice is that no mandatory-subject lesson runs shorter than 25 minutes.

The rule that matters most for tutoring: for these mandatory subjects, using any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. So a coach supporting a student in Arabic or Islamic Education works from the material the school is licensed to use, not from a private workbook. KHDA also requires schools to ensure that teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate permission from the authority to teach those subjects. If you are buying help in these three subjects, ask what material will be used before the first session, not after it.

sections.heading: What a coach may and may not do with a draft
paragraphs: This matters on an A star page because the temptation is sharpest at the top. A student two marks from the grade, with a coursework component or a project due, is precisely the student somebody will offer to help a little too much. One provider in this market sells finished Internal Assessments at a published price. That is an academic-integrity breach, it is a malpractice trigger for the student rather than for the seller, and a family who buys it is risking the whole certificate for a component worth a fraction of it.

The honest boundary is easy to state. A coach may teach the content, explain the mark scheme, discuss a plan, read a draft the student wrote and say where it is weak, ask questions that make the student notice a gap, and mark practice work against the published criteria. A coach may not supply sentences for a piece that must be the student's own, edit a draft into its final state, source and summarise the material on the student's behalf, or hand over model work to be adapted.

The practical test is whether a student could explain, unprompted, why every choice in their own work is there. If the answer is yes, the help was teaching. If not, it was something else. IB Gram coaches work on that side of the line, and we would rather lose an enquiry than sit on the wrong side of it. There is a second reason beyond ethics: a component written by somebody else leaves the student unable to answer the written paper on the same content, which is where the grade actually comes from.
bullets: Teaching content, mark schemes and planning: legitimate
Feedback on a draft the student wrote themselves: legitimate
Supplying sentences, model work to adapt, or a finished component: not
The test: can the student explain every choice in the work unprompted?

sections.heading: Permits, regulators and how a UAE family checks a coach
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, it is granted free of charge for two years, and eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no schedule of amounts is published, so treat any specific figure you read as unverified.

MoHRE's own service is listed as 'Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing', applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days. That is the route to send anyone who tells you a permit is unnecessary. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a separate matter: that needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, with initial approval first and annual renewal requested ahead of expiry. IB Gram holds no such permit because it operates no UAE premises, and no page here should suggest otherwise.

One more boundary worth knowing before you ask the obvious question. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff in Abu Dhabi prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the permit holder's own school. So the arrangement many families reach for first — your child's own teacher, privately, after hours — is the one arrangement that is closed. Verify the current wording against ADEK's own policy document before relying on it.

sections.heading: Starting, and what happens when no specialist is free
paragraphs: The order is: tell us the subject, the board and the series; sit a free first lesson with a coach who teaches that syllabus; get a written plan counted backwards from the paper. The free lesson is one per student and takes no card details. Nothing is booked until the plan exists, because a plan written before anybody has seen the student's marked work is a sales document rather than a plan.

The honest part most pages leave out is what happens when the match is not available. IGCSE Economics, Computer Science and Additional Mathematics at the top band are thinly covered everywhere in this market, and in the northern emirates the thinness is severe. If no UAE-based coach covers a subject at the level required, we say so and offer the alternatives: a coach elsewhere working to Gulf Standard Time, a later start when a specialist frees up after a series, or a referral out. What we do not do is put a generalist in front of a student two marks from an A star and let the family find out in March.

Timing changes what is sensible to buy. Twelve months out, a weekly hour and a plan rebuilt after each assessment is the right shape. Eight weeks out, a backwards-planned block built from the zone timetable is better than a weekly slot. Two weeks out, a single-paper clinic on the component that is actually leaking marks is the only thing with time to work, and we will tell you that rather than sell a term of hours into three fortnights. Ask for the plan first; the hours follow from it.
bullets: Free first lesson, one per student, no card details taken
Written backwards plan before any block of hours is booked
Coverage gaps named openly rather than filled with a generalist
What to buy depends on weeks remaining, not on budget alone

process.title: Send the three facts that matter
process.description: Subject, board and series — Cambridge or Pearson, June or November, and the syllabus code from the statement of entry if you have it. Those three decide which calendar applies and which coaches are even relevant. A year group and a school name are not enough, because schools split boards by department.

process.title: Sit a free first lesson with a subject specialist
process.description: One lesson, free, one per student, no card details taken. It is a diagnostic rather than a sample: the coach works through a marked paper or a piece of recent work and groups the dropped marks by component. You should finish it knowing where the marks are going, whether or not you book anything.

process.title: Get the plan counted backwards from the paper
process.description: A written plan starting at the exam date and working back through the zone timetable, the mock window, the forecast-grade date and the entry deadline. It names what should be finished by each point and what is being deliberately left out. If you disagree with the sequencing, that is the moment to say so.

process.title: Run weekly hours with a monthly checkpoint
process.description: A fixed slot on Gulf Standard Time, held through Ramadan and moved rather than cancelled, with a short written note each month saying what moved and what did not. The note exists so the plan can be rewritten against real evidence instead of impressions, particularly after the school's own assessments.

process.title: Rebuild after the mocks, then narrow
process.description: The mock is the first reliable evidence of the year. The plan is rewritten from it, re-ordered against the exam timetable so the earliest paper gets the earliest hours, and then narrowed: in the last fortnight the work should be one or two components, under time, marked against the published scheme.

whyPoints.title: The calendar is the product
whyPoints.description: Most tutoring is sold as hours. On a top-band target the hours are commodity and the sequencing is not. Every plan here starts from the paper date, the zone timetable and the entry deadline, and works backwards, because the same hour is worth very different amounts depending on which week it lands in.

whyPoints.title: Subject specialists, not all-rounders
whyPoints.description: A coach here works one syllabus hard rather than covering six adequately. The last five marks in IGCSE Physics 0625 and the last five in English Language go missing in completely different places, and somebody who teaches both at once knows neither set of places well enough to be useful at this level.

whyPoints.title: Online removes the geography constraint
whyPoints.description: Lessons run one-to-one over live video, so the coach is chosen from a national pool on teaching fit rather than from whoever can reach your address by five o'clock. For families in Fujairah, Umm Al Quwain or the outer parts of Al Ain this is the difference between a specialist and nobody.

whyPoints.title: Figures that carry their source
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page names the provider who publishes it and the month it was read. Every exam date names the board. Where a figure is not verifiable — IB equivalency points, this year's grade thresholds, the fine for tutoring without a permit — we say it is not verifiable instead of filling the gap.

whyPoints.title: A clear line on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Coaches teach, explain mark schemes, read drafts the student wrote and give feedback. They do not supply sentences, model answers to adapt, or finished components. This is a commercial disadvantage against the essay sellers in this market and we accept it, because the risk of the alternative falls entirely on the student.

whyPoints.title: Coverage stated honestly
whyPoints.description: Where no specialist is available for a subject at the level required, we say so and name the alternatives rather than placing a generalist. No competitor page in this market discloses a coverage limit, which is why so many families discover one in exam term.

faqs.question: What does an A star at IGCSE actually require that an A does not?
faqs.answer: Usually not more content. The gap between the two grades is typically a handful of marks per paper, concentrated in predictable places: the final questions on a Maths paper, practical description and uncertainty in the sciences, evaluation marks in Economics, audience and form instructions in directed writing. A student on an A generally knows the syllabus. What is missing is precision against the mark scheme and control of time across the whole paper. That is why the first useful step is marking a full past paper honestly and grouping the dropped marks by component rather than by topic, which tells you what to teach instead of guessing at it.

faqs.question: Can anyone tell us in advance what mark an A star will take this series?
faqs.answer: No. Grade thresholds are set after each series has been marked, once the board can see how the cohort handled that particular paper, and the board publishes them afterwards. They move between series because papers vary in difficulty. A coach who offers you this year's number in advance is guessing. What you can do is mark a mock against a published threshold from an earlier series and read the result as a region rather than a result: comfortably above suggests one plan, two marks short suggests another. Treat any site quoting a fixed percentage for the top grade with real caution.

faqs.question: Does a Core tier entry put the top grade out of reach?
faqs.answer: On the Cambridge IGCSE syllabuses offered at Core and Extended, yes — the Core route does not award the top grades. The decision is made by the school when it registers the entry, months before the paper, which makes it the single most consequential date on the whole calendar and one most families never see. If you are aiming at the top band, ask the head of department which tier your child is entered for and ask it in writing before the final entry deadline. After that deadline the ceiling is fixed, and no amount of coaching changes it.

faqs.question: Our son is sitting at a B in November of Year 11. Is an A star still realistic for June?
faqs.answer: It depends almost entirely on where the B is coming from. If the marked papers show losses spread evenly across every topic, that is a content gap and seven months is tight but workable with weekly hours. If the losses cluster in one component — the practical paper, the long-answer evaluation, the last fifteen minutes — that is a technique problem, and technique problems move faster than content gaps. Either way the honest answer comes from a marked paper, not from a school report. Ask for the diagnosis before anybody quotes you a number of hours.

faqs.question: How many weeks of coaching does one subject usually need before the June papers?
faqs.answer: For a content gap, plan on two terms of one weekly hour, with the plan rewritten after each school assessment. For a technique problem located in a single component, three to six sessions is a realistic range, and the cheapest intervention on this page is two sessions of paper-wide pacing, because timing improvements apply to every paper the student sits rather than to one question. Starting in February for a June series is not hopeless, but it limits you to technique work on what is already taught. Starting in April limits you to one or two components.

faqs.question: Our daughter wants the top grade in nine subjects. Is that a sensible target to coach towards?
faqs.answer: It is a target worth examining before it is worth funding. Nine top grades means nine sets of final-question technique, nine mark schemes and nine papers to pace, and the available evenings in a UAE exam term are finite once the mandatory Arabic, Islamic Education and social studies periods and the commute are counted out. A more productive conversation usually starts with which three or four subjects the next step actually requires, and whether a strong profile with four top grades beats a thin one with nine near-misses. Then fund the subjects that carry weight.

faqs.question: Our exam timetable arrived with a letter beside the dates. Which version should we revise from?
faqs.answer: The one issued for your centre's zone. Every Cambridge centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones and each zone has its own timetable version. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong one. So ask your school's exams officer, in writing, which zone the centre sits in and which timetable applies. Never build a revision plan from a timetable shared by friends at another school, which is how the mistake usually happens in the UAE.

faqs.question: Why does an entry deadline sit so long before the actual paper?
faqs.answer: Because the board has to build timetables, allocate papers to zones and print materials for centres worldwide before anybody sits anything. Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones, publishes a separate timetable for each, and says it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version, all of which has to be settled before the first paper. The result is that final entries for the June series close months ahead of it, and the same is true of the November series. Pearson shows the same pattern with dates you can check for yourself: its November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran to 19 November 2026, with entries for it closed well before that. For a family, the practical consequence is that tier and subject decisions become irreversible well before the revision term even begins.

faqs.question: If we only have the winter and spring breaks left, where should the hours go?
faqs.answer: Into the component that is losing the most marks, in the subject sat earliest in the exam window. Both halves of that sentence matter. Diagnose from a marked paper so you are spending on a known loss rather than a suspected one, then order the work from the centre's own zone timetable, because a subject examined in the first days of the window needs its hours before one examined three weeks later. Breaks are also the only blocks long enough for full timed papers, which are hard to fit into a school week and are where pacing problems actually surface.

faqs.question: What is the honest price range for top-band IGCSE coaching across the UAE?
faqs.answer: Published market rates in the UAE run roughly as follows. Budget online tutoring from a university student sits between AED 45 and AED 150 an hour; EdFlik advertises from AED 45 to 65 and Tutopiya from around AED 33 to 52. A qualified subject tutor online runs about AED 150 to AED 300, with Unitors publishing IGCSE from AED 150. A subject specialist is quoted between AED 200 and AED 450 or more, TutorChase at AED 270, and premium named tutors higher again, with BartyED at AED 650. Those are the market's figures, not ours; our number follows the consultation.

faqs.question: The school says our son is on track for an A. What should we ask next?
faqs.answer: Four questions. Which tier is he entered for, and does it award the top grade? Which board and series, so we know which calendar applies? Can we see a recent full paper with the marks shown per question rather than a percentage? And where were the marks lost — which component, which command term? A report saying 'on track for an A, could extend further' is not actionable. The per-question breakdown is, and most schools will provide it if asked directly. Everything on an A star plan starts from that breakdown.

faqs.question: Should we start coaching in Year 10 or wait until Year 11?
faqs.answer: Year 10 is cheaper per mark and Year 11 is more urgent, which is why most families buy in Year 11 and most of the leverage sits in Year 10. In Year 10 a subject can still be dropped or a tier revisited, content teaching is ahead of revision, and a weekly hour can alternate between the two. By Year 11 the entry is fixed, the mocks are close, and the work narrows to technique on content already taught. If the budget covers only one year, Year 10 buys more. If the problem is already visible, do not wait.

faqs.question: Does a run of top grades change what the Ministry of Education equivalency file needs?
faqs.answer: No. Equivalency is a threshold, not a ranking. For the British track the sourced requirement is five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. So a strong profile clears it easily, but a student whose five subjects include those two may be short on the count. Verify the current rules on moe.gov.ae rather than on any tutoring site.

faqs.question: If the top grade misses by a mark or two, what can we actually do about it?
faqs.answer: Two routes exist and both are time-limited, which is why they should be understood before results day rather than after. The first is a review of results, requested through the centre, not by the family directly. The second is a retake in the next available series: Cambridge runs June and November, and Pearson runs May/June and November, with a November sitting reaching students the following January in the most recent series. Ask your exams officer now for the review deadline that will apply to your series, and ask what the centre charges for it.

faqs.question: Does a coach come to our villa for these sessions, or is everything on video?
faqs.answer: Everything is on video. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, scheduled on Gulf Standard Time around a UAE school day. IB Gram does not run home visits anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we offer only in India. On a top-band target that is an advantage rather than a compromise, because the coach is chosen from a national pool on the strength of having taught that exact syllabus, instead of from whoever is willing to drive to your address at five in the afternoon. In the northern emirates it is often the difference between a specialist and nobody.

faqs.question: What may a coach write on a draft, and what has to stay the student's own work?
faqs.answer: A coach may teach the content, explain the published criteria, discuss a plan, read a draft the student wrote and say where it is weak, and ask questions that make a gap visible. A coach may not supply sentences, edit a draft into its finished state, research and summarise material on the student's behalf, or hand over model work to be adapted. The practical test is whether the student could explain every choice in the piece unprompted. One provider in this market sells finished assessed work outright; the risk of that falls on the student, not the seller.

igcse-a-star-coaching.closingHeading: Start from the paper date and work backwards
igcse-a-star-coaching.closingBody: Send three things: the subject, the board and the series. We will match a coach who teaches that syllabus, give you a free first lesson — one per student, no card details — and come back with a written plan that starts at the exam date and counts backwards through the zone timetable, the mock window, the forecast-grade deadline and the entry deadline. If no specialist is free at the level you need, we will say so and name the alternatives. Lessons run one-to-one over live video on Gulf Standard Time, anywhere from Fujairah to Al Ain. Ask for the plan first; decide about hours afterwards.

Each profile names the boards and the papers they have taught most recently, because that is the detail that decides whether an hour is worth its rate rather than the rate itself.

intro.heading: The price of an IGCSE class is not one number, and the spread is the story
paragraphs: Ask five providers what IGCSE classes in the UAE cost and you will get five answers that differ by a factor of twenty. Tutopiya advertises from AED 33 an hour. EdFlik starts at AED 45. Unitors publishes IGCSE tuition from AED 150. TutorChase quotes around AED 270. BartyED lists AED 650. Every one of those figures is real, and every one of them is for something different. The hour is the same length in all five cases; what changes is how many other children are in the room, who is teaching, how much of the fee pays for a car journey, and whether the person on the other side of the screen has taught your child's exact syllabus code this series or something adjacent to it.

That is the whole problem with the way this market prices itself. Three of the six highest-ranking providers in this cluster publish no price at all, and two of the three that do quote in US dollars, a currency no UAE family transacts in. The parent is left comparing an hourly rate against a monthly package against a per-session fee, with no way to normalise them. So this page normalises them. Every band below is given in AED per hour, attributed to the provider or rate survey that published it, with the format and the class size that the figure assumes stated beside it.

The second half of the question matters more than the first. A rate is only meaningful against what the hour delivers, and the single biggest variable is how many minutes of a teacher's attention your child actually receives. In a school class of twenty-four, a fifty-minute lesson gives each student rather less than three minutes of individual attention, which is why a child who has fallen behind on moles or on circuit calculations rarely recovers inside the timetable. A group class of eight at AED 60 an hour sounds cheap until you divide it. A one-to-one class at AED 220 is twenty times the attention for roughly four times the price.

Timing moves the number as reliably as format does, and it moves availability first. Cambridge sets its final entry deadline months before the paper, and a UAE family has two of those deadlines to watch rather than one, because candidates here sit the June series and the November series. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November on the same logic: its November 2026 timetable finished on 19 November 2026, with entries closed well before the first candidate sat down, and November 2025 results had reached students on 22 January 2026. The practical effect is that the market tightens twice a year, ahead of the June papers and again ahead of the November ones. A family that starts looking for classes six weeks before a paper is shopping in the thinnest part of the market, and pays for that.

What follows is organised the way a budget is organised, not the way a brochure is. Formats and their market rates first. Then the drivers that move a quote up or down, with a way to check each one. Then a whole-year plan at three budget levels. Then the line items nobody puts in a quote: entry costs, private candidacy, remarks, retakes, and the mandatory Ministry subjects that are already inside your school fee. IB Gram delivers all of this as one-to-one online classes over live video; home visits are something we offer in India, not in this market, and the comparison table makes the case for the online format on its merits rather than by omission.

igcse-classes.programmesIntro: Four qualification routes sit behind the phrase IGCSE classes in the UAE, and each carries its own price behaviour. The board decides the paper structure, the tier decides the grade ceiling, and the year group decides how much of the bill is prevention and how much is repair.

programmes.name: Cambridge International IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge syllabuses carry four-digit codes that appear on the school report and on every past paper: 0580 Mathematics, 0625 Physics, 0620 Chemistry, 0610 Biology, 0500 First Language English. Most subjects are tiered into Core and Extended, and the tier is fixed on the entry form rather than in the classroom. Cambridge examines IGCSE in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Classes priced for a Cambridge cohort are priced against those codes and those papers.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge allocates every exam centre worldwide to one of six administrative zones, and its exams officers' guide states that using the correct version of the timetable for your zone is essential, since Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss a paper after using the wrong one. For a UAE family that detail is a cost item: a class block built against the wrong zone timetable buys revision in the wrong order.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson codes read 4MA1 Mathematics A, 4PH1 Physics, 4CH1 Chemistry, 4BI1 Biology, 4EA1 English Language A. The structure differs from Cambridge in ways that change how many hours a subject needs: Mathematics A is tiered Foundation and Higher rather than Core and Extended, several science papers sit in a different split, and a modular route is available on some specifications. Pearson examines International GCSE in May/June and November each year.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, with a November window often up long before the papers are sat, and revises them, which is why a class plan should be pegged to the live official timetable rather than to a date copied off a tutoring site. The November 2026 final timetable ran to 19 November 2026; June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August and students on 20 August 2026, and November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

programmes.name: Lower Secondary, Years 7 to 9
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE course are where the cheapest hours in the whole plan sit. A Year 8 student who cannot rearrange a formula, balance an equation or write a paragraph with evidence in it will need the same gap closed later at Extended-tier prices and under an entry deadline. Lower Secondary classes are usually bought one subject at a time, often fortnightly, and the market charges its lower bands for them because the content is not yet examined externally.
programmes.countryNote: UAE families move schools and curricula more often than most, and Years 7 to 9 are where a CBSE, American or MYP background either converts cleanly into an IGCSE course or does not. The questions worth paying someone to answer at this stage are narrow: which board the school enters, whether the maths route leads to Extended, and which of the three mandatory Ministry subjects the child will sit in Arabic rather than in English.

programmes.name: After Year 11: AS, A Level and the IB Diploma
programmes.description: What comes next sets how much an IGCSE grade is worth in cash terms. A school that requires grade 7 or A for Extended-tier entry into AS Chemistry turns a 6 into a resit or a route change, and a route change made in September of Year 12 costs more to support than the ten hours that would have prevented it. Families planning for the Diploma face the same arithmetic in the maths route, where the IGCSE ceiling shapes whether Analysis and Approaches is realistic.
programmes.countryNote: The Ministry of Education's British-track equivalency rules reach backwards into this decision. Students must show one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade no lower than E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. Verify the current wording on moe.gov.ae before building a plan around it.

igcse-classes.subjectsIntro: Scarcity, not difficulty, is what prices a subject. A syllabus that most tutors have taught sits in the middle of the market; one that few have examined recently sits at the top of it, and the top of the market is also where availability runs out first before a series.

subjects.name: Mathematics (0580 / 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The most heavily taught IGCSE subject in the UAE and therefore the one with the widest choice of classes at every rate band. Marks are lost on non-calculator arithmetic, on bearings and vectors, and on multi-step problems where the method mark is available but the working is not shown. Expect mid-market rates and a genuine choice of tutors, including at short notice.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside Extended Mathematics by stronger cohorts, usually in schools pointing students at Analysis and Approaches or A Level Mathematics. Far fewer tutors have taught the calculus and trigonometric identity content recently, so this is one of the first subjects where a family meets upper-band pricing and a wait for a slot rather than a choice of slots.

subjects.name: Physics (0625 / 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity, moments and the practical paper are where the marks go. Students who can recite a definition and still cannot rearrange and substitute lose most of their marks in calculation questions, not in recall. Classes bought for Physics are usually bought for the alternative-to-practical or practical component as much as for the theory, and that changes how the hours should be spent.

subjects.name: Chemistry (0620 / 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic chemistry account for most of the lost Extended-tier marks. The subject punishes a student who has memorised equations without understanding which species are actually present in solution. Chemistry sits at mid to upper market rates because the practical and data-handling components need a tutor who has marked that specific paper style.

subjects.name: Biology (0610 / 4BI1)
subjects.description: Marks are lost in extended-response questions that require a named process in the right order, and in data questions where students describe a graph instead of explaining it. Biology is widely taught and widely tutored, so it prices in the middle band; the cost risk is buying content revision when the real gap is command-term discipline.

subjects.name: English Language (0500 / 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the summary question carry the marks that move a grade, and both are coachable in a small number of hours because they are formats before they are talents. Students in the UAE often sit First Language English alongside Arabic as a first or additional language, which affects how much reading and writing load a single week can carry.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language English with a different mark scheme, and the entry decision between them is made by the school rather than by the student. Classes are cheaper than First Language classes at the same level of experience, but a student entered for the wrong one of the two has a capped grade that no number of hours will lift.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (0455 / 0450)
subjects.description: Both subjects reward a student who can apply a definition to a named context and lose marks when answers stay generic. Case-study papers are the expensive part to fix late, because the skill is built over a term rather than in a revision week. Mid-band rates, with reasonable availability outside the eight weeks before a series.

subjects.name: Computer Science (0478)
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and the problem-solving paper are where marks go, and the subject attracts fewer experienced IGCSE tutors than the sciences because many candidates come from a programming rather than an examining background. Expect upper-band pricing and a narrower choice of times, especially for Paper 2.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First or Additional Language
subjects.description: Dubai private schools must teach Arabic regardless of their licensed curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Families often pay for extra Arabic without checking which of the two routes their child is actually on, which is the most common wasted spend in this list.

igcse-classes.regionsTitle: Where you live changes the price of a class, mostly through travel
igcse-classes.regionsIntro: Delivery is online everywhere in this list, so distance does not enter an IB Gram schedule. It enters the market price, because a visiting tutor's rate carries the journey and because the depth of the local tutor pool differs sharply between the seven emirates.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum on 37 per cent of the roll. The deepest tutor pool in the country, which keeps mid-band rates competitive, and the heaviest traffic, which is why a visiting tutor's quote and an online quote diverge most here.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. A smaller IGCSE tutor pool than Dubai at the specialist end, so Additional Mathematics and Computer Science classes are where families most often hit a wait rather than a price.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a school network spread far enough apart that a visiting tutor covering two students in an evening is unusual. The practical effect on price is a higher minimum session length on in-home quotes, often two hours, which raises the real cost per taught minute.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and its remit includes approving tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Families commuting into Dubai schools from Sharjah lose the 4pm slot entirely, which pushes demand into the 7pm to 9pm window.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate authority. A thin local market for Extended-tier sciences means an online class is frequently the only way to reach a tutor who has taught 0620 or 4CH1 in the current series rather than several years ago.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education here and, like Sharjah, approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. Named by none of the researched competitors, which tells you how little of this market is served locally. Travel-inclusive rates are the highest relative to teaching value anywhere in the country.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Ministry of Education territory, on the other side of the Hajar mountains from the main school clusters. A visiting tutor is rarely a realistic line item at any price, so the comparison for a Fujairah family is between an online class and no class, not between online and in-home.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: The smallest private-school market in the country and also under the federal Ministry of Education. Families here routinely enter children at a centre in another emirate, which adds a travel cost to the exam itself and makes the entry deadline a logistics date as well as an administrative one.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four UK curriculum and three International Baccalaureate, creating 16,846 places; six opened during 2025-26 and enrolment rose by 6 per cent. A growing UK-curriculum roll is the reason IGCSE class demand in Dubai peaks twice a year rather than once.

ADEK licenses and accredits these schools, and its professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. Families who assume they can simply hire the class teacher privately find the price of that shortcut is that it is not available.

SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain. Specialist IGCSE classes are scarce enough locally that an online slot is usually cheaper than the nearest in-home alternative rather than merely more convenient.

igcse-classes.modesIntro: Three ways to buy IGCSE classes, each with a different cost shape. All three are delivered one-to-one over live video, and the right one depends less on budget than on what the hour is being asked to fix.

modes.title: One subject, one class a week
modes.description: The default, and the cheapest plan that reliably changes a grade. One sixty-minute online class a week on a single subject, with work set between sessions so the hour is spent diagnosing and teaching rather than reading. Bestimate's monthly estimate for a weekly one-hour session runs AED 240-600 at the budget end and AED 600-1,200 mid-market. The limitation is obvious: one subject.
bullets: Billed per session or as a monthly block of four
Suits a single diagnosed weakness rather than a general slide
Set work between classes is what makes the rate worth paying
Easiest plan to pause and restart around a school holiday

modes.title: Two subjects across a split week
modes.description: Two classes a week on different subjects, often sciences paired with maths because the calculation skills overlap. Market monthly estimates roughly double, to AED 1,200-2,400 at mid-market rates. The saving is in continuity rather than in the rate: one tutor covering both subjects sees the same error twice and only has to diagnose it once, which is why asking whether a single tutor can cover the pair is a cost question.
bullets: Ask whether one tutor can cover both subjects before splitting them
Pair subjects that share a paper style or a calculation habit
Expect a review after six weeks, not after a term
Fewer total hours than two separate single-subject plans usually need

modes.title: Pre-series intensive block
modes.description: A fixed block of classes in the eight to twelve weeks before a series, priced as a block rather than by the hour in most of the market. Hours are counted in papers rather than in topics: a student sitting four written papers and one practical gets a plan built around those five documents. This is the most expensive format per taught minute, because it is bought in the thinnest part of the market.
bullets: Book the slot before the discount; availability narrows before price moves
Plan against the correct zone timetable for the centre
Full past papers under timed conditions, marked against the real scheme
Decide the Core or Extended question before the entry closes, not after

sections.heading: What an IGCSE class actually is, and why one hour carries six prices
paragraphs: An IGCSE class in the UAE costs between roughly AED 33 and AED 650 an hour as of October 2026, and the variable that explains most of the spread is not tutor quality. It is how many other children are in the room. Every figure in the table below was published by the provider named beside it, and every one assumes a different class size, a different delivery format and a different amount of travel baked into the rate. Comparing them without those three columns is how families end up paying upper-band money for lower-band attention.

The attention column is the one nobody publishes. A school lesson of fifty minutes with twenty-four students in it divides into rather less than three minutes each, and that is the arithmetic behind most requests for extra classes: not a failing teacher, simply a timetable that cannot pause for one child's gap in moles or in vector notation. A group class of eight at AED 60 an hour gives roughly seven or eight minutes each, which is enough for drill and past-paper routine and not enough to diagnose why a method keeps breaking. One-to-one gives sixty minutes of sixty.

Read the table as a menu rather than a ranking. A student who needs volume of practice and a weekly deadline is well served by a group class and badly served by paying four times as much for the same drill. A student who has sat two mocks at Extended tier and lost the same marks in the same way both times needs the diagnosis, and that is a one-to-one job. The format question comes before the rate question, and getting it in that order is worth more than any discount in this market.

sections.heading: The six things that move an IGCSE hourly rate, and how to check each one
paragraphs: A quote is not a fixed property of a tutor. It moves with six identifiable things, and five of them are visible to a parent before any money changes hands. Knowing which one is pushing a particular number up is the difference between negotiating and guessing. It is also the difference between paying a premium that buys something and paying a premium that buys scarcity you created yourself by starting late.

The driver that costs families most is the one that looks like nothing: board mismatch. A tutor who has taught Cambridge 0580 for years and is handed a Pearson 4MA1 student is not incompetent, but the tiering is different, the paper split is different and the first few classes go on reconciliation rather than teaching. The syllabus code is printed on the mock paper and usually on the school report. Reading it takes a minute and saves a term. One competitor page in this market gets the UAE subject count wrong in print, which is a reminder that confident publishing and accuracy are different things.

Proximity to the series behaves differently from the other five, because availability contracts before price rises. From roughly eight weeks out, the specialist slots at 5pm and 6pm Gulf Standard Time go first, and what remains is late evening or a less specialised tutor at the same rate. Families reading this in September for a June series are in the cheap part of the year and will not believe it until February. The honest version is that the discount for booking early is small and the difference in who is still free is large.

sections.heading: Pricing two whole IGCSE years against nine subjects
paragraphs: Most UAE students sit eight to ten IGCSE subjects, and no family buys classes in all of them. The useful planning question is not what one hour costs but how a fixed monthly figure should be divided across two academic years. The three plans below are built from Bestimate's published monthly estimates for the Dubai market: AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-market and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support, each assuming a weekly one-hour session.

The pattern that works is front-loaded and narrow. Spending in Year 10 is cheaper per unit of effect than spending in Year 11, because in Year 10 the gap is still small, the tier decision has not been submitted and there is no deadline distorting availability. Two subjects taught properly from October of Year 10 will usually cost less across two years than five subjects rescued from February of Year 11, and the second version carries a grade risk the first does not.

The plans also differ in what they cannot do, which is the column families should read first. A budget group plan cannot diagnose; it can only drill. A two-subject plan cannot cover a coursework portfolio and a practical component in the same term. An exam-year intensive cannot build a skill that takes a term to form, such as applying economics definitions to an unseen case. Every plan has a boundary, and a provider who will not name it is selling something other than teaching.
