sections.heading: Tuition beside the school fee, in the year Dubai held fees flat
paragraphs: Tutoring is a second education bill arriving on top of a first, and the first one stopped growing in Dubai this year. KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there will be no increase in school fees for private schools in the emirate for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. That is the right anchor for a tuition conversation, because it tells a Dubai family that the household education line is stable and any growth in it this year is a choice they are making.

It also sets expectations about who controls a price. School fees are approved by the emirate authority, not set freely by the school: in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the regulators approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Private tuition carries none of that oversight. There is no approved rate card for IGCSE classes anywhere in the country, which is exactly why the spread runs from AED 33 to AED 650 and why the burden of comparison sits with the parent.

The table puts the items side by side in the units they actually arrive in. Note that two of the rows are not hourly at all. Coursework and pre-series support are commonly sold as blocks, and a monthly package seen widely in this market is AED 799 for eight online sessions, with in-home monthly packages at AED 1,599-1,799 for four two-hour visits. Converting every line to a per-hour figure before comparing is the only way those numbers mean anything together.

sections.heading: A group class, a visiting tutor, or live online: the same subject priced three ways
paragraphs: Parents searching for IGCSE classes in the UAE are usually choosing between three delivery models without a straight comparison of what each one costs per taught minute. Here it is. A visiting tutor's published band of AED 180-500 includes a car journey across a city with some of the worst 4pm to 7pm traffic in the region, and that journey is why in-home quotes carry minimum session lengths of two hours in most of the market. An online class of the same length with the same tutor removes the journey from both sides of the transaction.

IB Gram's position is plain: classes are delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are part of what we offer in India and are not part of what we offer in this market. That is stated here rather than buried, because the alternative is to let a parent discover it after a deposit. The case for the online format is not that it is a substitute; it is that it changes which tutor is reachable. A family in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain can be taught 0620 Chemistry at Extended tier by somebody who marked that paper style last series, instead of by whoever lives within a thirty-minute drive.

The honest limitation of online delivery is the practical component, and it deserves naming in a cost discussion. A video class cannot put a child in front of a Bunsen burner. It can prepare the alternative-to-practical paper thoroughly, rehearse apparatus diagrams, teach measurement and uncertainty, and walk through the mark scheme of a required practical the school has already run. For the practical itself, the school laboratory is where the learning happens, and no tutoring spend changes that.

sections.heading: Core or Extended: the tier decision that sets both the ceiling and the bill
paragraphs: Most Cambridge IGCSE subjects are tiered, and the tier goes on the entry form. For a June series that form closes months earlier in the same school year, which means the decision is made well before the spring mocks make it obvious, and the exact closing date reaches you through the centre rather than as a single published worldwide deadline. A November entry has its own, later window on the same pattern. Pearson tiers Mathematics A as Foundation and Higher on the same principle. The decision changes the grade ceiling, the content taught, and the number of classes a student needs to reach the grade their next step requires.

The money consequence runs in both directions. Entering Extended tier when the student is not ready means buying hours to chase content the grade will not reward, and risking a low grade where a secure Core grade was available. Entering Core when the student could have managed Extended caps the grade below the entry requirement for AS or for the Diploma, and the cost of that appears a year later as a resit, a route change, or a university application built on a weaker profile. Neither error is recoverable with money after the deadline.

The table sets out what a family is actually choosing between. The row to weigh most carefully is the last one, because the honest input to a tier decision is not ambition but evidence: two mock papers at the tier in question, marked against the real scheme, with the marks broken down by question type. That is a defensible reason to buy a small number of classes in October of Year 11 rather than a large number in March.

sections.heading: Five ways a UAE family overpays for IGCSE classes
paragraphs: Waste in a tutoring budget rarely looks like an inflated rate. It looks like the right rate spent on the wrong thing, and it is remarkably consistent across families. The five patterns below came out of looking at how this market sells and how parents describe their own spending in the question banks behind these pages. None of them is about being careless with money; all of them are about buying before diagnosing.

The most expensive of the five is buying content when the gap is technique. A student who understands moles and still drops eleven marks across two papers is not short of chemistry. They are answering an explain question as though it were a describe question, or losing method marks by not writing working. Three classes spent on command terms and on mark-scheme discipline move more marks than a term of re-teaching topics the student already half knows, and they cost a fraction as much.

The second most expensive is paying twice for something the school fee already covers. Dubai private schools are required to teach Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies regardless of their licensed international curriculum, with the requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. Families who buy Arabic classes without first asking which route their child is on, first language or additional language, frequently buy the wrong one. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ, so the two routes are not interchangeable.
bullets: Buying content classes when the lost marks are a command-term or working problem
Paying for Arabic or Islamic Education support without checking which route the child sits
Starting eight weeks before a series and paying scarcity pricing for the leftover slots
Booking a tutor on the wrong board, then spending the first classes reconciling two syllabuses
Buying a general tutor for a scarce syllabus such as 0606 or 0478, then buying a specialist anyway

sections.heading: The line items nobody puts in a tuition quote
paragraphs: A tuition quote covers teaching. It does not cover the administrative costs that arrive around an IGCSE series, and those are the ones that surprise families, particularly families whose child sits a paper as a private candidate rather than through their own school. Amounts here are deliberately not published: entry charges are set by the centre and the board and change between series, so the only reliable figure is the one the school's exams officer gives you in writing for your series.

Private candidate entry is the item worth understanding earliest. A student who has moved schools mid-course, who is sitting a subject their school does not offer, or who is retaking a single paper may need to enter through a centre that accepts external candidates. That carries a centre administration charge on top of the board's entry charge, a separate deadline, and a requirement to sit the paper wherever the centre is, which for a family in Umm Al Quwain or Fujairah may mean travel on the morning of the exam.

Remarks, enquiries about results and retakes sit at the other end of the series. Each has a deadline measured in days or weeks after results, each carries a charge set by the board, and the decision has to be made quickly and with information the family usually does not have. Asking the exams officer for the window dates before results day, rather than after, is free and converts a panicked fortnight into a planned one.

sections.heading: What no amount of money may buy: coursework, practicals and the honesty line
paragraphs: There is a market in the Gulf for assessed work sold as a finished product. One operator in this search cluster lists completed IB Internal Assessments at AED 3,750. Treat any version of that offer as a transaction that buys a malpractice investigation rather than a grade. The student whose name is on the work is the person who faces the consequence, and the consequence reaches the whole qualification, not the single component. No saving and no deadline justifies it.

The legitimate version of coursework support is narrower and genuinely useful, and it is worth paying for. A tutor may teach the skills the task assesses, explain the assessment criteria and how marks are allocated across them, discuss a planned approach before work begins, read a draft the student has written and give feedback in general terms, model the method on a different example, and teach referencing properly. What a tutor may not do is produce any part of the assessed piece, supply text for it, or rewrite a passage so the submitted wording is somebody else's. That boundary is the same whether a family pays AED 60 an hour or AED 650.

Practical work carries the same logic in a different form. Required practicals must be carried out by the student in a school laboratory, and a video class cannot stand in for that. Where paid classes genuinely earn their rate is in the paper that examines practical skills: apparatus diagrams, measurement and uncertainty, identifying the controlled variable, reading a mark scheme for an experimental write-up. A provider who will not draw this line in writing before taking money is telling you something about everything else they sell.

sections.heading: Already paid for: the three Ministry subjects inside the school week
paragraphs: Every IGCSE student in a UAE private school carries subjects that are not IGCSE subjects. Federal rules require private schools to follow Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed curriculum, and in Dubai KHDA requires Arabic, Islamic Education and Social and Moral Studies in all private schools regardless of curriculum, with those requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. These subjects compete for the same Year 10 and Year 11 week as nine IGCSE courses, which is a scheduling cost before it is a money one.

The structural detail that matters to a family's budget is the separation rule. KHDA states that for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language, and Arabic is the primary language for Social Studies for Arab students, while non-Arabs study Islamic Education and Moral, Social and Cultural studies in the language of the school's licensed curriculum.

Two consequences follow for anybody buying classes. First, support bought for the wrong route teaches the wrong syllabus in the wrong language, which is the clearest example of wasted spend in this whole page. Second, the content itself is constrained: for the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. KHDA also requires schools to ensure teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold the appropriate approval from KHDA to teach them, and the instructional time is calculated on a forty-minute lesson unit, with any mandatory subject lesson advised to run at least twenty-five minutes.

sections.heading: Equivalency, the five-subject rule, and what finding out late costs
paragraphs: An IGCSE certificate has a second audience beyond the school: the Ministry of Education, when a student applies to a UAE university or needs a secondary certificate recognised locally. On the British track, students must submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, and must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among those five required subjects.

That exclusion is where money gets lost. A student who treats Arabic as one of the five counted subjects may reach the end of Year 11 with four qualifying grades rather than five, and the repair is a later entry in a subject nobody planned for, at a later series, with classes bought under deadline. The count is worth checking in Year 9, before option blocks are chosen, and it is worth checking against the Ministry's own page rather than against a tutoring site. One competitor that ranks for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five.

Two cautions belong with this. The equivalency process is run by the Ministry of Education and the emirate attestation authorities, not by any tutoring provider, and nobody should charge a family to perform it. And no IB points threshold for equivalency should be taken from a tutoring page at all, including this one: the British-track figures above come from a published report of the Ministry's clarification, the IB figure does not exist in that source, and the only place to confirm any of it is moe.gov.ae or the attestation authority directly.

process.title: Tell us the code, not just the subject
process.description: Send the syllabus code from the school report or mock paper, the tier, the series your child is entered for and the centre. That is four facts, and they decide which tutors are a real match and which quote is comparing like with like. Guessing the board is the single most expensive assumption in this market.

process.title: Take the free trial class before paying for anything
process.description: One class, no charge, with the tutor who would teach the block. Treat it as a diagnostic rather than an audition: by the end you should have a named weakness, the papers it affects and an estimate of hours. If the tutor cannot name the gap in sixty minutes, that is useful information too.

process.title: Agree the format, the hours and the rate in writing
process.description: A written note before payment should state the rate per class, the class length, how many classes, the cancellation terms, what happens to unused sessions, and whether any figure quoted includes VAT. Quoted figures on this page are market rates published by other providers, not an IB Gram price list.

process.title: Review at six weeks against marks, not against feelings
process.description: Bring the most recent marked paper and compare it with the one from six weeks earlier, question type by question type. Classes that are working show up as marks recovered in a named category. Classes that are not should be stopped or redirected rather than renewed out of politeness.

process.title: Hear it plainly when nobody suitable is free
process.description: Some syllabuses have a thin pool, particularly Additional Mathematics, Computer Science and minority languages close to a series. If no specialist in that exact code is available at a workable Gulf Standard Time slot, we say so and give the realistic wait rather than filling the slot with a general tutor at a specialist rate.

whyPoints.title: Rates are published with the source attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED figure on this page names the provider or rate survey that published it, with the month it was read. Three of the highest-ranking pages for these searches publish no price at all and two quote in US dollars. A figure you can trace is a figure you can argue with.

whyPoints.title: The format question is answered before the rate question
whyPoints.description: A group class, a small group and a one-to-one class solve different problems, and the cheapest adequate format is the right one. We will say when drill in a group is enough, because selling a one-to-one hour for work that a worksheet and a deadline would fix is how trust is lost.

whyPoints.title: One-to-one over live video, stated up front
whyPoints.description: Classes are taught one-to-one over live video and scheduled in Gulf Standard Time. Home visits are part of our service in India and not in the UAE. Saying that before a deposit, rather than after, is the minimum a family is owed by anybody taking money for teaching.

whyPoints.title: A national pool rather than a local one
whyPoints.description: Online delivery changes which tutor is reachable from Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain. A family outside the main school clusters gets a tutor who has taught their exact syllabus code recently rather than the nearest available generalist, and pays a published online band instead of a travel-inclusive one.

whyPoints.title: The coursework boundary is in writing
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches the skill, explains the criteria and the mark allocation, and gives feedback on work the student wrote. A tutor does not supply assessed text. Where a competing offer in this market sells finished Internal Assessments for AED 3,750, saying this explicitly is the differentiator.

whyPoints.title: No approval we do not hold, and no numbers we cannot source
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform. We hold no accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and we do not publish a statistic without saying where it came from and when it was read.

faqs.question: Why does the same IGCSE subject cost AED 45 in one class and AED 650 in another?
faqs.answer: Because the two prices are for different products. The AED 45 figure, which EdFlik advertises from, usually assumes a group room with several other children and a university-student tutor. The AED 650 figure, listed by BartyED, buys a named specialist one-to-one. Between them sit Unitors from AED 150 for IGCSE, TutorChase at around AED 270, and visiting tutors at AED 180-500 with travel inside the rate. Class size, tutor experience in your exact syllabus code, and how much of the fee pays for a car journey explain most of the spread. Compare the format first; the rate only means something once the format is fixed.

faqs.question: How many children can a group class hold before the saving stops being worth it?
faqs.answer: Around four. In a group of four, a sixty-minute class gives each child roughly fifteen minutes of direct attention, which is enough to spot a recurring error and correct it. At eight, that falls to seven or eight minutes, which supports drill and past-paper routine but not diagnosis. At twenty-plus, which is a school class, it is under three minutes and the format cannot pause for one student's gap. Group classes are good value for volume of practice and a weekly deadline. They are poor value when the problem is a method that keeps breaking in the same place, because nobody has time to watch it break.

faqs.question: We have AED 1,500 a month for classes. How should that be spent?
faqs.answer: At Bestimate's mid-market monthly estimate of AED 600-1,200 for a weekly one-hour session, that budget buys one subject taught properly one-to-one with room left over, or two subjects at the lower end of the band. Spend it on the weakest subject rather than spreading it across three, and start in Year 10 rather than Year 11, where the same money buys more because the gap is smaller and no entry deadline is distorting availability. Keep a reserve of two or three hours for a marked mock review before the tier decision. One subject moved two grades is worth more than three subjects nudged.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects are hardest to buy a specialist for?
faqs.answer: Additional Mathematics 0606, Computer Science 0478 and minority languages are consistently the thinnest. Many candidates for those subjects come from a professional rather than an examining background, so the number of tutors who have taught that exact code to Year 11 in a recent series is small. The practical effect is not mainly price; it is availability. Close to a series, the specialist slots at 5pm and 6pm Gulf Standard Time are taken first, and what remains is a late-evening slot or a generalist at a specialist rate. For these codes, book months out rather than weeks out.

faqs.question: Does Extended-tier teaching cost more per hour than Core?
faqs.answer: Usually by around AED 30-80 an hour in this market, and the reason is content rather than status. Extended covers the core material plus the supplement, which is where most of the additional classes go, and the paper combination sets harder question styles that need more marked full papers under timed conditions. The more important cost is the tier decision itself. Cambridge fixes the tier on the entry form, and that form closes months before the series it covers, so for a June sitting the choice is already made during the earlier part of the school year, long before the mocks make the right answer obvious. Two mock papers marked against the real scheme are a cheaper input to that decision than either wrong answer.

faqs.question: Our daughter sits nine IGCSEs. Does she need classes in all of them?
faqs.answer: No, and buying nine would be the clearest waste on this page. Most families fund one or two subjects well rather than many thinly. Pick the subjects where the grade she needs for the next step is genuinely at risk, and where the gap is diagnosable: a method that fails repeatedly, a paper she runs out of time on, a component she has never been taught to answer. Subjects where she is a grade below ambition but secure on content rarely repay weekly classes. A single marked-paper review across several subjects is often a better first purchase than a term of lessons in one.

faqs.question: What should we have in writing before paying for a block of classes?
faqs.answer: Six things: the rate per class and whether it includes VAT, the length of a class, how many classes the payment covers, the cancellation and rescheduling terms, what happens to sessions you do not use, and the named syllabus code and tier being taught. Add one more for coursework subjects: a plain statement of what the tutor will and will not do with assessed work. Any provider who will not put those in a message before taking money is asking you to rely on memory, and in a market where rates range from AED 33 to AED 650 an hour, memory is not enough.

faqs.question: Does an IGCSE entry carry a cost separate from the teaching?
faqs.answer: Yes. The board charges for each subject entry and the centre collects it, usually months before the paper: Cambridge closes final entries for its June series well ahead of the first paper, and its November series works the same way on a later window. Amounts change between series and between centres, so the only figure to rely on is the one your school's exams officer gives you in writing for your series. Private candidates entering through an external centre pay a centre administration charge on top of the board's entry charge, on the centre's own deadline. None of that is inside a tuition quote, and none of it is something a tutoring provider sets.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying for a remark when a grade sits one mark under a boundary?
faqs.answer: It can be, but the decision is a deadline problem before it is a money problem. Enquiries about results and remarks have a short window after results day, each carries a charge set by the board, and the information needed to judge the odds, such as the component marks, arrives at the same time as the pressure. Ask the exams officer for the window dates and the charge before results day rather than after, so the decision is made with a calendar rather than in a panic. A remark changes a mark only where the paper was misapplied against the scheme, not because a grade was disappointing.

faqs.question: Why are practical and coursework subjects quoted differently from written-paper ones?
faqs.answer: Because the work has its own clock and its own boundary. A written paper can be prepared in weekly hours up to the series; a coursework portfolio or a practical component has internal school deadlines spread across the year, which is why support for it is commonly sold as a block rather than per hour. The boundary matters as much as the billing: a tutor may teach the skill the task assesses, explain the criteria and the mark allocation, and give feedback on a draft the student wrote, but may not supply any of the assessed text. Expect that distinction in writing before paying.

faqs.question: Someone offered us a finished piece of assessed work for a fee. What happens if we take it?
faqs.answer: The student takes the consequence, and it reaches the qualification rather than the component. One operator in this search cluster lists completed IB Internal Assessments at AED 3,750; the same model exists for IGCSE coursework. Submitting work that is not the student's own is malpractice under board rules, and an investigation can affect the whole certificate, not just the piece in question. No deadline and no saving makes that a reasonable trade. The legitimate alternative costs less and is available: hours spent on the criteria, on method, and on feedback against a draft the student actually produced.

faqs.question: Our child sits Arabic as an additional language. Does that need a paid class of its own?
faqs.answer: Check the route before you buy anything. KHDA requires schools to organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes are strictly prohibited because curriculum expectations and the language of instruction differ. Arabic as an additional language is a different course from Arabic as a first language, with different expectations. Support bought against the wrong route teaches the wrong syllabus, sometimes in the wrong language. Ask the school which route the child is on and what the reported weakness actually is, then decide whether any paid class is needed at all.

faqs.question: What does discovering the five-subject equivalency rule late actually cost a family?
faqs.answer: An unplanned subject entry at a later series, the classes to prepare for it under deadline, and in some cases a delayed university application. On the British track the Ministry requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than E or grade 3, plus one Advanced Level at E or two Advanced Subsidiary Levels, and Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. A student who assumed Arabic counted can finish Year 11 one qualifying subject short. Checking the count in Year 9, against moe.gov.ae rather than a tutoring page, costs nothing. One ranking competitor states six subjects; the sourced rule is five.

faqs.question: Where do these IGCSE classes actually take place?
faqs.answer: On a video call, one tutor to one student, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school day and around prayer times where that matters to the family. Nobody travels to a UAE address: home visits are part of what IB Gram offers in India, not here. What that changes for a family is reach rather than convenience. A student in Ras Al Khaimah or Fujairah can be taught 0620 Chemistry at Extended tier by somebody who has taught that exact paper recently, at a published online band of roughly AED 150-300 for a qualified subject tutor, instead of a travel-inclusive AED 180-500 for whoever lives nearby.

faqs.question: Does starting in January for a June series need more hours than starting in September?
faqs.answer: Almost always, and the extra hours are the smaller part of the difference. Starting in September means the entry and tier decisions are still open, the gap is smaller, and the 5pm and 6pm specialist slots are available. Starting in January means the tier is already submitted, the plan has to be counted in papers rather than in topics, and the choice of tutor has narrowed to whoever is left. The rate itself may rise by AED 25-100 an hour close to a series; the real cost is that the cheapest fix, a decision made in time, is no longer purchasable.

faqs.question: How do we judge whether a cheap class is good value or just cheap?
faqs.answer: By what the first hour produces, not by how it felt. A class worth its rate ends with a named weakness, the papers and question types it affects, and work set before the next session. Six weeks later, bring a marked paper and compare it with the one from six weeks earlier by question category. Marks recovered in the named category is the test. A tutor at AED 60 an hour who does that is better value than one at AED 400 who does not, and the free trial class exists so that the comparison costs nothing to run.

igcse-classes.closingHeading: Start with the syllabus code, then the format, then the rate
igcse-classes.closingBody: The useful order is narrow and it does not start with price. Find the syllabus code and tier your child is entered for, decide whether the gap needs drill or diagnosis, and only then compare rates within that format. Market bands for IGCSE classes in the UAE run from roughly AED 33 an hour in a shared room to AED 650 for a named specialist, and the figures on this page are other providers' published rates, read in October 2026, not an IB Gram price list. Our classes are one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time, and the first one is a free trial lesson so the diagnosis costs you nothing. Send the code, the tier and the series, and we will tell you plainly what is available and what is not.

This page sets that system out in order, then shows where one-to-one coaching legitimately fits. Lessons are delivered live online, over video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, in every emirate from Dubai to Umm Al Quwain.

igcse-coaching.tutorsIntro: The coaches below work on Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE specifications at Core and Extended tier, over live video. Each one is matched to a named subject and syllabus code rather than to a city, so a family in Ajman draws on the same specialist a family in Jumeirah does.

intro.heading: The rulebook your child's IGCSE already sits inside
paragraphs: Parents searching for IGCSE coaching in the UAE have usually noticed something uncomfortable first. The school year turns on dates and decisions the family never sees: a tier entry submitted in Year 10, a syllabus code chosen by a head of department, a Ministry subject block that eats two periods a week, an entry deadline that shut while everyone was thinking about mocks. Coaching bought without understanding those fixed points tends to be coaching bought at the wrong moment, for the wrong specification, at the most expensive time of year.

The UAE adds a layer most IGCSE guidance written in Britain leaves out. A private school here answers to an emirate authority, not to Ofsted. In Dubai that is the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, described on the federal portal u.ae as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. In Abu Dhabi and Al Ain it is the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah fall to the federal Ministry of Education.

Those bodies do more than inspect. The u.ae guidance states that Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. So the licence above your child's school reaches into what is taught and how it is assessed, which is why a coaching plan has to start from the school's actual specification rather than from a general idea of what IGCSE contains. The federal baseline is narrow by design: private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, provided they keep to the Ministry's general regulations.

Underneath the regulator sits the board. Cambridge International and Pearson Edexcel run separate specifications, separate codes, separate series and separate grading conventions, and a UAE school may use both in the same year group across different subjects. Coaching that assumes Cambridge when the entry is Pearson wastes hours on papers your child will never sit. The single most useful document a parent can produce before booking anything is the statement of entry, because it names the board, the code and the tier in one place.

What follows is ordered the way the system actually bears on a family: what the school's licence makes the school responsible for, how to read its published report, what the board code decides, what the grade scale means on a UAE university file, how the papers are entered, what happens when a child arrives mid-course from another system, what the market charges in AED, and where the line sits between coaching and malpractice. IGCSE coaching online is the delivery model throughout, and the comparison section explains why that is the honest answer for the Emirates rather than a compromise.
bullets: Five separate authorities regulate private schools across the seven emirates, and your file sits with exactly one of them
Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies run alongside the IGCSE block regardless of the licensed curriculum
Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE differ on codes, series, tiering and grade scale
The Ministry of Education equivalency route for the British track counts five accredited subjects, not nine

igcse-coaching.programmesIntro: An IGCSE is a two-year block with a run-up before it and two possible exits after it. Coaching that only looks at Years 10 and 11 arrives late to the decisions that matter. These are the four stages a UAE family passes through, with what the emirate context adds at each one.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary and Key Stage 3
programmes.description: The three years before the IGCSE block, ending in the option choices that set everything after them. Cambridge runs Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, and a school may use those results to stream Year 10. This is where a maths gap is cheap to close: algebraic manipulation, fractions as operators, and rearranging formulae are the skills Year 10 assumes without reteaching, and the ones most Year 11 crises trace back to.
programmes.countryNote: UAE families move schools more often than the British average, and a child arriving in Year 9 from a different system reaches option choices with a partial record. Emirate authorities approve curricula but do not harmonise them, so a transfer between two licensed schools can still mean a different scheme of work. Ask the receiving school which specification its Year 10 will be entered for before the option form is signed.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE subjects carry four-digit codes such as 0580 for Mathematics, 0625 for Physics and 0620 for Chemistry, and most are tiered into Core and Extended. Grades run A* to G, with a Core entry capped below the top grades and Extended opening the full range. For candidates in the UAE, Cambridge runs a June series and a November series; the February and March sitting is offered to India rather than here. Every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, each with its own timetable version.
programmes.countryNote: Cambridge states plainly that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the centre's zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. For a UAE family that is a practical warning: a revision plan built from a timetable found online, rather than from the school's own zone timetable, can put a paper on the wrong day.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson's international qualification uses codes such as 4MA1 for Mathematics A and 4PH1 for Physics, grades on the 9 to 1 scale, and tiering described as Foundation and Higher in the subjects where it applies. Exams are available in May or June and in November each year. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, which is why a coaching plan should link the live official timetable rather than restate a date that can be revised.
programmes.countryNote: Pearson's published pattern gives UAE families a second entry point inside one academic year, and the turnaround is documented: June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, while November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A November resit therefore lands its grade inside the following spring, which matters when a university file has a deadline.

programmes.name: International A Level and IB Diploma routes
programmes.description: The IGCSE grade is a gate, not a destination. International A Level entry usually asks for a strong grade in the same subject, and a Diploma school will read the IGCSE profile when placing a student at Higher or Standard Level. A Core-tier maths grade can quietly close an A Level Mathematics door or push a Diploma student towards Applications and Interpretation rather than Analysis and Approaches.
programmes.countryNote: Dubai's private sector is dominated by the UK curriculum, at roughly 37 per cent of the private-school roll in 2024-25, with the International Baccalaureate at about 7 per cent. A family planning a Diploma after IGCSE is therefore moving against the local flow of provision, and should check the receiving school's Higher Level entry expectations in Year 11 rather than after results.

igcse-coaching.subjectsIntro: Coaching is bought subject by subject, and the subject is only half the information. The code and the tier decide what is on the paper. These are the IGCSE subjects UAE families ask for most, with the codes to check against the statement of entry.

subjects.name: Mathematics
subjects.levels: Cambridge 0580 Core and Extended · Pearson 4MA1 Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The tier decision with the widest consequences. Extended adds functions, vectors, more demanding trigonometry and harder algebraic fractions. Marks go missing on exact-value answers, on rounding instructions ignored, and on method marks lost because working stopped at the answer. A coach should be working from past papers for the correct tier, not a general maths syllabus.

subjects.name: Physics
subjects.description: Electricity, moments and the practical paper carry most of the lost marks. Candidates lose marks describing a method without naming the variable being controlled, and in calculations where the unit is wrong or the prefix was never converted. Extended adds quantitative treatment of topics Core only requires qualitatively, so an Extended candidate taught from Core notes is being under-prepared.

subjects.name: Chemistry
subjects.description: Moles, electrolysis and organic reaction conditions separate grades here. The common failure is reciting an observation without the explanation the command term asked for, and writing ionic equations without balancing charge. Practical technique is examined on paper, so a coach works through described experiments and asks the student to predict what the examiner wants recorded.

subjects.name: Biology
subjects.description: A content-heavy paper that rewards precision in definitions. Osmosis, transport in plants, and genetics crosses are where answers drift into everyday language and lose the mark. Extended adds detail on respiration, excretion and inheritance. Coaching time is best spent on command terms and on converting a diagram into the three or four marking points an examiner is counting.

subjects.name: Co-ordinated and Combined Sciences
subjects.description: The route many UAE schools use for students taking nine or ten subjects. The content is drawn from all three sciences but trimmed, and the trimming is the thing a coach has to know exactly. Teaching a Co-ordinated Sciences candidate the full separate Physics syllabus wastes hours; teaching too little leaves gaps in the papers that do carry the topic.

subjects.name: First Language English
subjects.description: Reading response and directed writing carry the marks, and the marks are lost on form rather than content: a letter written as an essay, a summary that quotes instead of condensing, an analysis that names a device without saying what it achieves. Coaching here is mostly structured redrafting of the student's own writing against the published assessment criteria.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language
subjects.description: A different qualification from First Language English, and the one many UAE schools enter for students who speak another language at home. It tests listening, reading, writing and in some routes speaking. Universities and the Ministry read the two differently, so the first question a coach should ask is which code the school has entered, not how well the child speaks.

subjects.name: Economics
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and the difference between describe, explain and discuss decide the grade. Candidates lose marks drawing a correctly labelled diagram then not referring to it in the written answer. The UAE context is useful teaching material here: fuel subsidies, expatriate remittances and a fixed exchange rate are live examples of syllabus concepts.

subjects.name: Business Studies
subjects.description: Case-study application is what separates a grade 6 from a grade 8. A student who knows the theory but answers in general terms, without using the figures in the stimulus, stalls in the middle bands. Coaching focuses on reading the case material for evidence and on writing evaluation that actually reaches a judgement.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT
subjects.description: Two different subjects frequently confused at enrolment. Computer Science examines algorithms, data representation and programming concepts; ICT examines applied use of software and the practical papers that go with it. A coach needs the code, because a Computer Science candidate coached in spreadsheet technique has lost a term.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language and Arabic as a Foreign Language
subjects.description: Two separate codes for two separate groups of students, and the distinction mirrors the classroom rule the authorities already impose on schools. A student entered for the first-language code needs literary and formal register work; a foreign-language candidate needs vocabulary breadth and controlled writing. Confirm which code the school entered before any coaching begins.

subjects.name: Geography and History
subjects.description: Source-handling and case-study recall carry the papers. In Geography the lost marks are on data-response questions where the figure in the resource was never quoted; in History they are on answers that narrate instead of arguing. Both reward a small number of well-rehearsed case studies over broad, thin coverage.

igcse-coaching.regionsIntro: The authority above the school changes with the emirate, and so does what a parent can look up before enrolling. Coaching is delivered over live video to all seven emirates on the same terms, but the paperwork around it is not uniform.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Private schools answer to KHDA, which publishes inspection reports and in May 2026 confirmed no increase in private school fees for 2026-27. Seven new private schools join the 2026-27 intake, four UK curriculum and three IB, adding 16,846 places. The deepest IGCSE provision in the country, and the most competitive option blocks.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate, and is named by essentially none of the tutoring sites competing for this search. Press reporting also describes ADEK ethics rules barring school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which is worth knowing before accepting an offer.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a smaller and more spread-out set of British-curriculum schools. Families here feel subject-specialist scarcity more sharply than Abu Dhabi island does, particularly in Extended-tier sciences and Additional Mathematics, which is the clearest argument for coaching delivered over video.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate, and the federal guidance notes that Sharjah's authority approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A coaching plan here should be built from the school's own approved scheme of work.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools fall under the federal Ministry of Education, which supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Fewer British-curriculum options locally means more families using a Dubai or Sharjah school, with a commute that pushes any weekday session past 17:00 Gulf Standard Time.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula and assessment methods. RAK returns almost no mentions across the competing tutoring sites, so a family here is usually working without any locally written guidance at all.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under the federal Ministry of Education. The east coast is the clearest case against a visiting coach: the drive from Dubai is long enough that travel costs more than the lesson, and the pool of Extended-tier specialists within reach of a Fujairah address is very small. Video removes the geography from the decision.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, and the smallest private-school market in the country. Families commonly enrol in Sharjah or Ajman and absorb the journey, which makes evening session timing the practical constraint rather than tutor availability.

schoolClusters.note: The densest concentration of Cambridge and Pearson entries in the Gulf, and the place where option-block clashes are most common because large year groups force schools to timetable popular subjects against each other. Students we support attend schools across this group.

ADEK-regulated schools with strong British-curriculum provision on the island and in Khalifa City, thinning noticeably towards Al Ain. Specialist scarcity at Extended tier shows up first in Additional Mathematics and in separate sciences.

A mix of SPEA-regulated schools in Sharjah and Ministry-supervised schools further north. Smaller cohorts mean fewer option sets and more students taking Co-ordinated Sciences rather than three separate sciences.

This is the cheapest version of IGCSE coaching over two years because it removes the emergency block most families end up buying in Year 11.

sections.heading: What the school's licence makes the school responsible for, and where coaching fits
paragraphs: A licensed private school in the UAE carries obligations a parent can name and ask about. The emirate authority approves the curriculum and, in Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah, the fees and assessment methods with it. The school chooses the board and the code, decides the tier entry, supervises any coursework, and makes the exam entry to the centre. Coaching that duplicates those responsibilities is wasted money; coaching that fills the gaps between them is where the value sits.

The clearest example is the tier decision. Core and Extended tier entry is made by the school, usually on the evidence of internal assessment, and the ceiling it sets is real: a Core entry in Cambridge Mathematics caps the achievable grade and can close an International A Level route two years later. A parent is entitled to ask what evidence the decision rests on and when it is reviewed. A coach can produce the evidence that changes the conversation, by putting Extended papers in front of the student under timed conditions.

The other example is the mandatory UAE subject block. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are required in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and the school must deliver them. That is not something a family needs to buy. What families do sometimes need is help with the register and literacy demands of the first-language Arabic code, which is a teaching gap rather than a provision gap.

Reading the table below before a first enquiry changes what you ask for. Most families arrive asking for more teaching of a subject the school already teaches adequately, when the actual problem is a tier entry made on thin evidence or a coursework deadline nobody flagged.

sections.heading: Five authorities, one country: whose decisions your plan runs on
paragraphs: Almost every guide to IGCSE a UAE parent finds online was written for Britain, where one inspectorate covers everything. Here the map has five entries, and the one that applies to your child depends only on which emirate the school sits in. Dubai is KHDA. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain are ADEK. Sharjah is SPEA. Ras Al Khaimah has its own Department of Knowledge. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah come under the federal Ministry of Education, which the federal portal describes as playing a pivotal role in supervising private schools in those three emirates.

The practical difference is in what each authority reaches. Inspection is the visible part, but the u.ae guidance notes that the Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah authorities also approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. A Sharjah parent who disagrees with how a subject is assessed internally is therefore arguing inside a system where assessment methods were approved by a named authority, and that is a different conversation from one about teaching quality.

ADEK is the gap worth knowing about. It is named by almost none of the tutoring businesses competing for this search, yet it governs private schooling for a large share of UAE families and its professional-ethics expectations have been reported in the Gulf press as barring school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school. If a teacher at your child's Abu Dhabi school offers paid evening lessons, that offer is the one to decline, whatever the convenience.

None of this means IB Gram holds any status with any of these bodies. We do not. What a family gets from understanding the map is leverage: the right authority to look up a school's published report with, the right question to ask about assessment, and a clear view of which decisions are the school's to make and which are not.

sections.heading: Reading a school's published report as a coaching diagnostic
paragraphs: A KHDA inspection report is the most underused document in UAE parenting. Families read the headline band and stop, when the useful information is further in, broken down by subject and by phase. A school can be strong overall and still carry a weaker judgement on attainment in a specific subject at secondary phase, and that is precisely the line that should decide whether you buy coaching and in what.

Read it as a diagnostic rather than a verdict. A judgement on students' attainment tells you where the cohort sits against curriculum standards. A judgement on progress tells you what the school adds. Those two can disagree, and when they do the gap is informative: high attainment with modest progress often means a selective intake coasting, which is the pattern where a capable child drifts towards a grade 6 nobody notices.

The report also carries judgements on teaching for effective learning, on assessment, on curriculum adaptation, and on the provision for Arabic and Islamic Education. A weak assessment judgement is the one most relevant to tier entry, because tier decisions rest on internal assessment. If a report flags assessment as the weaker area, a parent has a documented reason to ask what evidence a Core entry was based on.

What a band does not tell you is whether your child specifically is at risk. An Outstanding school still has students sitting Core-tier maths and students who have never been taught to read a command term. sections.heading: The code on the statement of entry decides everything after it
paragraphs: Two boards dominate UAE British-curriculum schools and they are not interchangeable. Cambridge International runs IGCSE with four-digit codes, A* to G grading, Core and Extended tiering, a June series and a November series for candidates here, and six administrative timetable zones. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE with codes such as 4MA1, grading on the 9 to 1 scale, Foundation and Higher tiering where it applies, and series in May or June and November. Neither board sits a UAE candidate in February or March; that window belongs to Cambridge's India series, and the Checkpoint tests in March, May and October are a different assessment entirely.

A UAE school may use both in the same year group. It is routine for a school to enter Cambridge for the sciences and Pearson for Mathematics, or to move boards in one subject between cohorts. Which means the question is never which board the school uses, but which code this child is entered for in this subject. The statement of entry answers it; a school office will confirm it in writing before that.

The consequences of getting this wrong are concrete rather than abstract. Pearson's modular and linear arrangements differ from Cambridge's. The practical assessment route differs. The number of papers and their weightings differ. A past paper from the wrong board looks close enough that a student will work through it without noticing, and the questions that do not transfer are exactly the ones that decide the top grades.

Cambridge's own guidance adds a warning most families never see: every centre is allocated to one of six administrative zones, it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for that zone, and Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong zone timetable was used. Build the revision plan from the school's own zone timetable, not from the first PDF a search returns. Pearson, for its part, publishes provisional timetables that can be revised, so the live official timetable is the only safe source for a date.

sections.heading: Letters, numbers and the floor a UAE university file has to clear
paragraphs: One of the quieter sources of confusion in this market is that two certificates in the same drawer can use different grade scales. Cambridge IGCSE reports grades from A* down to G. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports on the 9 to 1 scale. Some Cambridge subjects are graded 9 to 1 for UK centres. A parent comparing a 7 with a B is comparing two different measuring systems, and a child comparing them with a classmate is doing something worse.

The tier compounds it. A Core or Foundation entry does not give access to the full grade range, so a strong performance at Core tier produces a grade that looks middling on paper. That is not a marking problem, it is the ceiling the entry decision created months earlier, and it is why the tier conversation belongs in Year 10 rather than after results.

For a UAE university file, the number that matters is the Ministry of Education equivalency floor rather than any comparison between scales. As reported when the Ministry clarified the requirements in July 2026, the British track asks for five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five.

That five-subject rule is worth stating plainly because at least one ranking competitor in this market publishes six. Note also what is not published: no IB points threshold appears in that clarification, so any figure quoted for IB equivalency should be checked on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority directly. sections.heading: Sitting the papers through the school, or as a private candidate
paragraphs: Most UAE students are entered by their school, which acts as the exam centre and owns the entry deadline. That deadline sits much earlier than families expect. For the June series the entry closes months before the first paper, in the earlier part of the same school year, and the exact day is set per administrative zone and issued to the family on the statement of entry rather than published as one worldwide date. Pearson's parallel series makes the size of that gap checkable: its Edexcel International GCSE November 2026 timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, which means the entry behind it was closed long before any of those papers began.

A private-candidate entry is the other route, and it exists for specific situations: a subject the school does not offer, a resit after the school has moved on, a child educated at home, or a student whose school declines an Extended entry the family believes the evidence supports. The entry is made through a centre that accepts private candidates, and the family carries the administration the school would otherwise have handled.

The complication is components. A subject with coursework or a supervised practical element is harder to enter privately, because somebody has to supervise and authenticate that work. In practice this pushes private candidates towards subjects assessed entirely by written paper, or towards the alternative-to-practical route where the specification offers one. Checking the specification before committing to a private entry saves a wasted series.

Coaching changes shape for a private candidate. Nobody is setting homework, nobody is marking mocks, and nobody is watching the deadlines. The coach ends up carrying the scheduling discipline the school would normally supply, which means the plan has to be written down with dates against it from the first session rather than drifting towards the exam.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in the same week as nine IGCSEs
paragraphs: A UAE timetable is fuller than a British one, and the reason is regulatory rather than academic. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with KHDA's requirements to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. The federal position behind that is that private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies.

The organisational detail matters for any coaching plan. KHDA requires separate classes by group: for Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language.

Instructional time is specified too. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the weekly total is met, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Which means the hours are real hours out of a Year 11 week, sitting next to nine or ten IGCSE subjects and whatever revision the family has planned.

There is one firm limit on what outside support can do here. For the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited. So coaching in this space is about access skills rather than alternative material: reading fluency, formal register, structuring a written answer in Arabic, and understanding what the school's own assessment is asking for. Anything that looks like a substitute curriculum is outside the rules the school has to work within.

sections.heading: Arriving mid-course: moving into IGCSE from another system
paragraphs: UAE schools absorb transfers constantly, and an IGCSE block is an awkward thing to join halfway. The qualification is two years of cumulative content with a tier entry already submitted in some subjects, so a child arriving in Year 10 or Year 11 is joining a race partway round. The receiving school confirms placement, but the gap analysis is usually nobody's job, and that is where families lose a term.

The gaps are predictable by system of origin. A student from an Indian-curriculum school often arrives strong on procedural mathematics and weaker on extended written answers and data-response technique. A student from an American middle school usually has the writing but not the algebraic fluency Extended maths assumes. A student from a Ministry-curriculum school may be strong in Arabic and Social Studies and meeting English-medium science vocabulary for the first time.

Emirate authorities approve curricula school by school rather than harmonising them, so two licensed schools in the same emirate can follow different schemes of work for the same code. A transfer within the UAE is therefore not automatically smooth, and a transfer between emirates adds a change of regulator on top. Ask the receiving school which code each subject is entered for, and ask for the scheme of work rather than a reading list.

Coaching for a transfer student should start with a diagnostic rather than a syllabus. The useful first question is not what the child has covered but what the new specification assumes they already have. sections.heading: What IGCSE coaching costs across the UAE market
paragraphs: Three of the six best-ranking pages for these searches publish no price at all, and the two that do quote in US dollars, which no UAE family transacts in. The figures below are IGCSE coaching rates in AED per hour as published by the providers named, read in October 2026. They are market rates, not IB Gram's price list, and they are set out so a parent can tell whether a quote is ordinary or exceptional before agreeing to it.

The range is wide for understandable reasons. At the bottom end sit university students and generalist online platforms. In the middle sit qualified subject teachers working online. Above that sit specialists in a particular board and tier, and above them a small premium tier of named practitioners. A home visit adds the travel to the hour, which is why in-home figures start higher than online figures for the same quality of teaching.

Two things move a quote more than anything else. The first is the month you start: a Year 11 family booking in February for a May or June series is buying scarce time, and scarcity sets prices. The second is the specificity of the ask. A generalist maths tutor is plentiful; an Extended-tier Additional Mathematics specialist who knows the current code is not, and the second one costs more because fewer people can do it.

IB Gram does not publish an hourly rate on this page because the honest answer depends on subject, tier and the time of year, and a number invented for a landing page helps nobody. What we do publish is the model: one-to-one over live video, a trial lesson at no charge with no card required and one per family, and a written plan before any block is agreed.

sections.heading: A coach in the room against a coach on a screen, under UAE conditions
paragraphs: Families searching for IGCSE coaching in the UAE often picture someone arriving at the villa on a Tuesday evening, and the market will sell that. It is worth understanding what it actually buys. A visiting coach is selected from the people willing to drive to your address in the evening peak, which in practice means a radius of perhaps twenty to thirty minutes. The teaching pool is defined by geography rather than by who knows the specification.

The travel also has a price, and it appears in the published figures: home-visit rates in this market start higher than online rates for comparable teaching, with Bestimate's range running from AED 180 to 350 and home tutors quoted from AED 200 to 500. Part of that difference is the drive. For families in Al Ain, Fujairah, Ras Al Khaimah or Umm Al Quwain the drive is long enough that the specialist simply is not available at any sensible price.

IB Gram delivers IGCSE coaching for UAE families as one-to-one tuition over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. We do not send a coach to an address anywhere in the Emirates; home visits are a service we run in India only. That is a straightforward trade: a family gives up a person in the room and gets a coach chosen for the board, the code and the tier rather than for the postcode, with no travel in the price and no cancelled session because of an accident on Sheikh Zayed Road.

The comparison below is the case on its merits rather than a sales argument. Some children genuinely do better with someone beside them, and a family who wants that should buy it locally with eyes open about the pool they are choosing from. Most IGCSE problems, though, are specification problems, and specification problems are solved by the right specialist on a screen more reliably than by the nearest available adult.

Using the wrong board's paper is the common waste

sections.heading: The UAE term year against an IGCSE series, counted in both directions
paragraphs: A British revision calendar does not map onto a UAE school year. Terms start in late August or early September, the long winter break lands in December, Ramadan moves earlier each year and shortens the school day while it lasts, and Eid takes a variable block out of the spring term. A coaching plan built on a generic calendar will schedule its hardest work in the weeks the family has least capacity.

Counting from the other direction, the dates that genuinely lock are set by the boards and published by them. Cambridge publishes key dates for each series it runs here, June and November, and in both cases final entries close months ahead of the first paper while forecast grades go in before the papers begin; results follow in August for a June series and in the following January for a November one. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable runs from late October to 19 November 2026, its June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students the following day, and its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

IGCSE coaching during Ramadan is a scheduling question rather than a pedagogical one. The school day shortens, energy drops in the afternoon, and the sensible move is to pull sessions later into the evening and to use the period for consolidation and past-paper marking rather than for new content. Families who plan that in September rather than discovering it in the second week lose nothing from the term.

The table reads the UAE year as a sequence of things the school is doing and things a coaching plan should be doing alongside. It is deliberately not a list of exam dates: board timetables are revised, Cambridge zones differ, and the only safe source for a specific date is the school's own zone timetable or the live official timetable on the board's site.

sections.heading: Coursework, past papers and the line a coach does not cross
paragraphs: This market contains businesses that sell finished assessed work. One of them offers completed Internal Assessments at a published price. For a student, accepting that is a malpractice finding and potentially the loss of the qualification; for the family it is money spent on a risk nobody disclosed. The boundary is therefore worth stating on a page about coaching rather than leaving to a terms-and-conditions link.

What a coach does is teach method, model technique on a different example, and give feedback on work the student has already produced themselves. What a coach does not do is supply text, sentences, structure written out for copying, or an improved version to be submitted. The practical test is simple: if the student could not explain every line of what they are submitting, it is not theirs, and an examiner asking a follow-up question will find that out.

Past papers and mark schemes sit in a related place. These are copyright documents belonging to Cambridge and Pearson. A coach can work through them with a student and cite where they came from; a provider should not be reproducing them as downloads or presenting unreleased material at all. Any provider offering a library of mark schemes as a selling point is worth a question about where those documents came from.

The same honesty applies to what we claim. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation, licence or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, MoHRE, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and nothing on this page should be read as implying one. We name those bodies to explain how the system works. Separately, private tuition in the UAE runs on a permit: the MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers categories including registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals tutoring without one are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, and no fine schedule is published, so no amount should be quoted to you either.
bullets: Teaching, modelling and feedback on the student's own work is coaching; supplying text is not
