process.title: Send the statement of entry, or the codes in writing
process.description: The first thing we ask for is not a description of the problem but the board and code for each subject, ideally from the statement of entry. Without it a coach is guessing between Cambridge and Pearson specifications that look similar and examine differently. If the document has not been issued yet, the school office will confirm the codes by email.

process.title: A diagnostic session, not a sales call
process.description: One session on the subject in question, working through questions from the correct code at the entered tier. The output is a short written note: what is secure, what is not, and whether the tier entry looks right on the evidence. Families use that note in the conversation with the school as often as they use it with us.

process.title: Match to a coach by code and tier
process.description: We match on the specification rather than on location, which is the whole reason the delivery is online. A family in Umm Al Quwain and a family in Jumeirah draw on the same pool. Where a subject at a particular tier has no coach free at the requested time, we say so and give a date rather than filling the slot with a generalist.

process.title: A trial lesson at no charge, one per family
process.description: One lesson with the matched coach before anything is paid, with no card required at booking. The point is to see whether the child talks to this particular adult, which is not a thing any profile can tell you. If the match is wrong, we rematch once at no charge before any block starts.

process.title: A written plan with dates on it
process.description: Before a block is agreed, the plan is written down: number of sessions, the slot in Gulf Standard Time, the topics in order, the school deadlines and the series the work is building towards. Ramadan and the Eid break are placed in the plan at the outset. Plans change, but they change against a document rather than a memory.

process.title: Review at the mock, then again at entry
process.description: Two fixed review points rather than continuous reassurance. The mock script is the most honest diagnostic of the year and is read properly, question by question. The entry deadline is the second, because tier and series decisions stop being reversible there. Both reviews are written, so a parent can see what changed and why.

whyPoints.title: The code comes before the coach
whyPoints.description: Every match starts from the board and syllabus code on the statement of entry, because Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE examine the same subjects differently. A coach working from the wrong specification can teach well for months and still leave a student unprepared for the papers they will actually sit.

whyPoints.title: Specialist pool instead of a driving radius
whyPoints.description: Delivery over live video means the choice of coach is not limited to whoever will drive to your address in the evening peak. For Extended-tier sciences, Additional Mathematics and the less common codes, that difference is the difference between a specialist and the nearest available adult, particularly outside Dubai and Abu Dhabi.

whyPoints.title: Every figure attributed, or not published
whyPoints.description: The AED rates on this page are market figures with the provider named and the month they were read. We publish no invented hourly price, no satisfaction percentage, no star rating and no outcome statistic, because a number without a source behind it is worth nothing to a parent comparing quotes.

whyPoints.title: The honesty boundary stated, not buried
whyPoints.description: Coaching here means teaching, modelling and feedback on the student's own work. We do not supply assessed work, redraft a submission to completion, or trade in mark schemes. That is a real difference from parts of this market, and it is stated on the page rather than left to a document nobody opens.

whyPoints.title: Built around the system, not around Britain
whyPoints.description: The regulator above the school, the mandatory UAE subject block, the Ministry of Education equivalency route and the Cambridge zone timetable all change what a sensible plan looks like. A plan copied from UK guidance will miss all four, and most of the guidance a UAE parent finds online is copied from UK guidance.

whyPoints.title: Availability disclosed before you pay
whyPoints.description: Where no coach is free for a subject at a tier and time, we give a date rather than filling the slot. Where a UAE-based coach is unavailable, we say which pool the match is coming from. No competing page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, and the limit is the thing a family needs to plan around.

faqs.question: Does IGCSE coaching have to follow the exact syllabus my child's school is licensed to teach?
faqs.answer: It has to follow the specification the school has entered your child for, which is a narrower thing than the school's licensed curriculum. The emirate authority approves the curriculum; the board and code decide what is on the paper. A school licensed for the UK curriculum might enter Cambridge for sciences and Pearson for mathematics in the same year group. So coaching should be built from the code on the statement of entry, not from the school's curriculum label. Ask the school office for the codes in writing before the first session if the statement has not been issued yet.

faqs.question: Our school entered my daughter for Cambridge, but her tutor has been teaching Edexcel material. Does that matter?
faqs.answer: It matters more than it looks. Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE cover similar subject content but differ on paper structure, weightings, tiering language, practical assessment and grade scale. A past paper from the wrong board reads as plausible, so a student will work through it without noticing, and the questions that do not transfer tend to be the ones separating the top grades. Check the code on the statement of entry, then ask the coach to work only from that board's materials. If several months have gone on the wrong specification, a diagnostic session against the correct papers will show how much is genuinely transferable.

faqs.question: One of my children has letter grades and the other has numbers. Which scale does a UAE university actually read?
faqs.answer: Both, because they are different qualifications. Cambridge IGCSE reports A* to G. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE reports 9 to 1, and some Cambridge syllabuses are graded 9 to 1 for UK centres. Universities read each certificate against its own scale rather than converting between them. For a UAE file the number that matters is the Ministry of Education equivalency floor: as reported when the Ministry clarified requirements in July 2026, the British track asks for five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than grade E or grade 3. Confirm the current rule on moe.gov.ae before relying on it.

faqs.question: If the school refuses an Extended entry we think the evidence supports, who can we take that to?
faqs.answer: The tier entry is the school's decision, made on internal assessment, so the first step is to ask what evidence it rests on and when it is reviewed. That question is more productive with evidence attached, which is what a coached block of timed Extended papers produces. If the conversation stalls, the school is licensed by an emirate authority: KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, or the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah those authorities also approve assessment methods.

faqs.question: Which of the IGCSE series makes sense for a resit, and how far ahead do we need to decide?
faqs.answer: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for candidates in the UAE, and Pearson offers May or June plus November. The February and March sitting that gets quoted online is Cambridge's series for India and is not available here. The decision point is the entry deadline rather than the exam: for either Cambridge series, final entries close months before the first paper, and the operative date comes from your own centre with its administrative zone attached. Pearson's November results have reached students in late January, 22 January 2026 for the November 2025 series. Work backwards from the live official timetable on the board's own site, because provisional dates can be revised.

faqs.question: Does a school inspection report tell a parent anything useful about where to spend on coaching?
faqs.answer: More than the headline band does. Read the sections rather than the summary: attainment tells you where the cohort sits against curriculum standards, progress tells you what the school adds, and the two can disagree. High attainment with modest progress is the pattern where a capable child drifts. The judgement on assessment is the one most relevant to tier entry, because tier decisions rest on internal evidence. A weaker assessment judgement gives you a documented reason to ask how a Core entry was arrived at. A strong overall band does not mean no child in the school needs help.

faqs.question: We have just moved to Dubai from an Indian-curriculum school in Year 9. What does the jump into IGCSE involve?
faqs.answer: Usually a smaller content gap than families fear and a larger technique gap than they expect. Students arriving from CBSE or ICSE are often strong on procedural mathematics and less practised at extended written answers, data-response questions and the command-term discipline IGCSE marking rewards. The first priority is confirming which board and code the receiving school will enter each subject for, and whether the tier decision has already been made. A diagnostic session against the actual papers is worth more than a reading list. Expect roughly ten to sixteen weeks of support per affected subject before internal assessments settle.

faqs.question: Can a parent check that a coach is permitted to tutor in the UAE, and what should the permit cover?
faqs.answer: Private tuition here runs on the MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and granted free of charge for two years. Eligible categories include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students, and school students aged 15 to 18. Ask to see it, and ask who the holder's employer is, because the permit carries a code of conduct. Anyone tutoring without a permit is subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so treat any specific amount quoted at you as unverified.

faqs.question: Does the Ministry of Education count all nine of my son's IGCSE subjects, or only some of them?
faqs.answer: Only some. As reported when the Ministry clarified equivalency requirements in July 2026, the British track requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. At least one competing site in this market publishes six, which is a useful reminder to verify on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority rather than trusting a tutoring page, including this one.

faqs.question: The Arabic lesson is timetabled against my daughter's Chemistry option. What can coaching do about a clash like that?
faqs.answer: Nothing about the timetable itself, which is the school's to set under the terms of its licence. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools whatever international curriculum the school is licensed for, and KHDA calculates the time on a 40-minute lesson unit with a minimum of 25 minutes per lesson. What coaching can do is recover the taught content she misses in the subject that loses out, working from the school's own scheme of work. Raise the clash with the school early: option blocks are easier to adjust in September than in February.

faqs.question: Ramadan falls inside our revision term. How should that change the coaching plan?
faqs.answer: Plan it in September rather than reacting in the second week. The school day shortens, afternoon capacity drops across the whole household, and Eid removes a variable block afterwards. The practical adjustments are to move sessions later into the evening, to use the period for consolidation and past-paper marking rather than new content, and to protect the weeks immediately after Eid for the heavier work. Written plans survive this better than informal arrangements, because everyone can see what was moved and where it landed. Session slots through Ramadan typically run after Iftar, in Gulf Standard Time as usual.

faqs.question: How many coached hours does one IGCSE subject usually absorb across Years 10 and 11?
faqs.answer: It depends on what is being fixed. A weekly slot across both years is roughly sixty to seventy sessions, which is the pattern that costs least per session and catches misconceptions within days. A targeted block starting in January of Year 11 for a May or June series is usually twelve to twenty sessions per subject, depending on how much content is secure. A single diagnostic plus a tier-evidence block before entry can be as few as six. Buying weekly from Year 10 is almost always cheaper than buying the emergency block families end up with in Year 11.

faqs.question: Can the same coach take Maths and Chemistry for one IGCSE student?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth asking, because a single coach sees patterns across both subjects that two coaches miss: the same weakness in rearranging formulae shows up in Chemistry calculations and in Extended maths. But the limit is the specification. A coach should hold the actual code for both, at the entered tier, rather than general competence in science and mathematics. Where that combination is not available at the time you want, two specialists matched to their own codes is the better outcome than one generalist covering both approximately.

faqs.question: Nobody is free for Business Studies at the time that suits us. What happens then?
faqs.answer: We say so and give you a date, rather than filling the slot with someone who does not hold the code. Where a UAE-based coach is not available for a subject at a tier and time, we tell you which pool the match is coming from before anything is paid, including when that is outside the Emirates. Evening slots between 17:00 and 19:00 Gulf Standard Time are the tightest, so a family with flexibility on the hour usually gets matched faster. No competing page in this market discloses a coverage limit at all, which is exactly the information a plan needs.

faqs.question: Is coaching delivered the same way in Ajman and Umm Al Quwain as in Dubai?
faqs.answer: Yes, because it is delivered over live video in all seven emirates. The coach is matched to the board, code and tier rather than to a location, so a family in Umm Al Quwain draws on the same pool as a family in Jumeirah. IB Gram does not send a coach to any UAE address; home visits are a service we run in India only. What does differ further north is the school commute, which pushes a realistic weekday start past 17:00 Gulf Standard Time, and the local supply of Extended-tier specialists, which is thin enough that video is the only route to one.

faqs.question: Do you coach the UAE mandatory subjects, or only the IGCSE option subjects?
faqs.answer: We work on the access skills around Arabic, and we are careful about the limit. For the mandatory subjects, KHDA guidance states that the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry is strictly prohibited, and schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ. So coaching here means reading fluency, formal register and structuring a written answer, built from the school's own material. It does not mean a parallel curriculum. If the subject is examined as Cambridge 0508 or 0544, the code decides the approach.

igcse-coaching.closingHeading: Start with the code, not with the panic
igcse-coaching.closingBody: Most IGCSE problems in the UAE are not teaching problems. They are system problems: a tier entry made on thin evidence, a coach working from the wrong board, a Ministry subject block nobody accounted for, an entry deadline that closed in November. Send us the statement of entry or the codes in writing, take a diagnostic session, and read the written note that comes out of it. If the answer is that the school has this covered and nothing needs buying, that is a useful answer too. If coaching does make sense, you will be buying it for a named code at a known tier, at a slot in Gulf Standard Time, with the plan and the dates written down before anything is paid.

igcse-crash-course.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE subjects at the level the papers actually test: Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel syllabuses, by code, with the mark scheme open. For an intensive block we match on the specific component that is losing marks — Paper 4 in 0580, the alternative-to-practical in 0625 — rather than on the subject name alone.

intro.heading: Start with the date, then decide what an intensive block can do
paragraphs: Most families search for an IGCSE crash course in the UAE at one of three moments: the week the January mocks come back, the week the statement of entry appears in the school bag, and the week study leave starts. Those three moments sit a long way apart, and they buy completely different things. Twenty weeks out, an intensive block can reteach whole units and still leave time to practise them. Eight weeks out, it can repair three topics and rebuild paper technique. Three weeks out, it can only change the marks that are lost to process — units left off an answer, a rubric misread, a six-mark question abandoned after the first line. All three are worth doing. They are not the same purchase, and a provider who quotes the same package for all three is not planning around your child's calendar.

So this page is organised by date rather than by subject. It counts the IGCSE year backwards from the first paper and names, at each distance, who owns the deadline that falls there and what an intensive block of one-to-one hours can still move. The dates themselves come from the boards. Cambridge International runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, and allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones; Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for the zone, and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. Those two sentences decide more about a revision plan than any tutoring method does.

The second thing this page does is publish numbers. Of the UAE tutoring pages we examined in October 2026, three of six published no price at all and the two that did quoted US dollars, a currency no UAE family transacts in. The AED bands further down are market rates gathered from providers who published them and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table, each attributed to whoever published it. They are not IB Gram's price list. What an intensive block costs with us depends on the subject, the number of weeks left and how many hours a week the student can absorb without the school work collapsing, which is a conversation rather than a table.

Delivery matters here more than on a weekly-tuition page, because a crash course concentrates hours into a short window. Lessons are delivered online, one-to-one, over live video, with a shared screen for the paper and the mark scheme. IB Gram does not send a tutor to a UAE address; home visits are part of what we offer in India only. For an intensive block that constraint turns into an advantage. A family in Al Ain or Fujairah that needs eight hours of Cambridge IGCSE Chemistry 0620 in three weeks is not choosing from whoever will drive to their community at 7pm; they are choosing a 0620 specialist and booking the hours at times that survive a shortened Ramadan school day, study leave, and a paper sat on a Thursday morning.

One honest warning before the detail. A crash course cannot teach a two-year syllabus in a month, cannot alter a tier entry the school has already submitted, and cannot touch a coursework piece that has been handed in. It also cannot promise a grade, and anybody who does should be asked how they intend to keep that promise. What it can do is find the marks the student is already close to earning and make them reachable before the paper. That is a smaller claim than the adverts make, and it is the one worth paying for.
bullets: Twenty weeks out: whole-unit reteaching, tier confirmation, syllabus-code audit
Eight weeks out: three-topic repair plus timed paper technique per component
Three weeks out: process marks only — command terms, units, working shown, question order
Exam fortnight: between-paper triage, one subject at a time
After the last paper: review-of-results window, retake series, Ministry equivalency file

igcse-crash-course.programmesIntro: An IGCSE crash course is not one product. These are the four shapes an intensive block takes in UAE schools, with what each is for and how the UAE school calendar bends it.

programmes.name: IGCSE course years
programmes.description: The standard two-year run to a June or November series. An intensive block inside these years is usually bought twice: once after the Year 10 end-of-year papers, when there is still a full year to use, and once after the Year 11 mocks, when there is a term. The first block can afford to reteach; the second has to triage. Both work from the syllabus code — 0580, 0620, 0625, 4MA1 — because the paper structure, not the subject label, decides where the hours go.
programmes.countryNote: UAE schools sit this course under their emirate regulator while also running the federally mandated Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies lessons, which do not count towards the IGCSE result. An intensive block has to be timetabled around those lessons rather than through them, and in Dubai they sit on a timetable KHDA requires schools to implement.

programmes.name: Year 9 and Lower Secondary
programmes.description: The year before the IGCSE course begins, and the only point where an intensive block is genuinely preventative rather than remedial. Cambridge runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, so there is an external marker available before the IGCSE syllabus starts. A block here works on the two things that cost marks for the next two years: algebraic fluency and writing to a command term. Nothing about it is a crash course in the usual sense; it is the cheap version of one.
programmes.countryNote: Year 9 is also where UAE families make the tier-relevant decision without knowing it, because setting decisions taken in Year 9 often determine whether a child is entered for Core or Extended two years later. Families moving in mid-year from a CBSE, American or MoE-curriculum school are the group most likely to need this block, and the gap is usually in notation rather than knowledge.

programmes.name: Retake and private candidate
programmes.description: A retake block is the purest form of crash course: a known result, a known paper, a fixed next series, and no new syllabus to learn. It starts from the statement of results rather than a diagnostic, because the component marks already say where the grade was lost. The planning question is which series to enter — Cambridge November, a Pearson November sitting, or the following summer — and that decision is driven by the entry deadline and by what the student is applying for.
programmes.countryNote: Private candidates in the UAE sit at an exam centre that accepts external entries, and the centre, not the family, holds the timetable version and the entry. Confirm the centre will take an external candidate for your subject before planning any block of hours, because availability varies by syllabus and by series and cannot be assumed from the board's general timetable.

programmes.name: Post-IGCSE bridge
programmes.description: The eight to ten weeks between the last IGCSE paper and the start of DP1 or AS, which most families leave empty and a few use well. For a student going into IB Diploma Maths Analysis and Approaches HL, or into Chemistry HL from a grade 6 at 0620, this is the block that prevents the first term being spent catching up. It is taught as new content rather than revision, which makes it the one intensive block that is not built backwards from an exam date.
programmes.countryNote: In the UAE this window overlaps the long summer break, when many families travel, and results arrive inside it. A block planned for July often has to be rearranged once the August results date lands, so it is usually booked as a smaller number of hours with the dates agreed after results rather than before.

igcse-crash-course.subjectsIntro: An intensive block is bought for a component, not a subject. These are the IGCSE subjects UAE families most often compress, with the syllabus codes and the part of the assessment where the hours earn their keep.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 / Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended · Foundation and Higher
subjects.description: The subject with the most recoverable marks in a short block. Losses cluster in multi-step Paper 4 and Higher-tier questions that are abandoned after the first line, and in method marks that were earned but not shown. Six to eight focused hours on structured working and on question stems usually moves more marks than any other single purchase.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: Taken alongside 0580 by students heading for Maths AA HL or A Level Maths. Calculus and trigonometric identities are where marks go, and the paper rewards fluency rather than insight, which makes it well suited to intensive drilling. Students arriving from a syllabus without calculus need this treated as teaching, not revision.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 / Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and circuits, moments, and the experiment-description questions on the alternative-to-practical paper account for most of the gap between a 5 and a 7. The experimental questions are learnable in a way the topics are not: there is a structure to a good answer about variables, control and fair testing, and it can be taught in two hours.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 / Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Mole arithmetic, electrolysis half-equations and organic reaction pathways. Chemistry rewards an intensive block better than most sciences because the content is modular — a student can repair moles without touching organic — so hours can be aimed precisely at two or three units rather than spread across the syllabus.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 / Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: The command-term subject. Marks go when explain is answered as describe, when a diagram is labelled but not used, and when a six-mark question is answered in three sentences. Content gaps in transport, homeostasis and inheritance are usually narrower than they look; the answer-writing gap is wider.

subjects.name: Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences (Cambridge 0653 / 0654)
subjects.description: Three sciences compressed into one or two grades, which changes revision economics completely: the weakest of the three sciences drags the whole award. An intensive block starts by identifying which of the three is costing the grade, then spends almost all of the hours there rather than dividing them evenly.

subjects.name: First Language English (Cambridge 0500 / Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading response. Marks go to register and audience in the writing task and to unsupported assertion in the analysis. This is the subject where marking a student's own past-paper answers together, line by line against the published descriptors, does more in four hours than any amount of content coverage.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 / 0511)
subjects.description: Sat by a large share of UAE candidates. The listening and reading papers are technique-heavy and respond quickly to timed practice; the writing task responds to a bank of structures. A block of six hours here is one of the few that can reliably move a whole grade late in the year.

subjects.name: Economics and Business Studies (Cambridge 0455 / 0450)
subjects.description: Both papers are won on evaluation marks that most students never attempt. The data-response and case-study questions have a predictable shape, and a tutor can teach the shape in two sessions. Definitions and diagrams are the cheap marks; the judgement paragraph is where the grade sits.

subjects.name: Computer Science and ICT (Cambridge 0478 / 0417)
subjects.description: Pseudocode, trace tables and the written theory paper. Students who code confidently often lose marks because the paper wants pseudocode in the board's own notation rather than working Python. That is a two-hour fix, and it is invisible until someone marks a past paper properly.

subjects.name: Arabic (Cambridge 0508 and 0544)
subjects.description: Separate from the mandatory Arabic lessons UAE schools must run, and often confused with them. The IGCSE syllabuses have their own papers and their own marking, while the school's mandatory Arabic provision follows Ministry content. A block has to be clear which of the two it is preparing for before the first session.

igcse-crash-course.regionsTitle: Running an intensive block from each emirate
igcse-crash-course.regionsIntro: A crash course lives or dies on when the hours can actually sit. These notes are about the school day, the commute and the break calendar in each emirate, because those decide the realistic start time for a session in the final term.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: 227 private schools and 17 curricula in 2024-25, with the UK curriculum the largest share of enrolment, so most IGCSE candidates in the country sit here. Evening slots from 5pm are usually workable; families in communities with a long school-bus route often push the first session to 6.30pm in the final term.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Schools run under ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules bar school staff from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, as press-reported, which is exactly why an outside online tutor is the normal route for an intensive block here.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a smaller British-curriculum school set and a correspondingly thin local tutor pool for specific syllabus codes. This is the clearest case for online delivery: a 0620 or 4CH1 specialist is reachable for an evening block without anyone driving across the emirate.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and, with Ras Al Khaimah's authority, approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Many Sharjah families commute into Dubai schools, so sessions realistically start after 6pm on a weekday in the exam term.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, which plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Ajman students commuting to Sharjah or Dubai schools lose the most time to the road, which argues for fewer, longer sessions in an intensive block.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate and approves curricula and assessment methods. RAK appeared in none of the competitor pages we examined, and local availability for a named IGCSE syllabus code is limited, so an online block is usually the only way to get a subject specialist rather than a generalist.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under federal Ministry of Education supervision, with the smallest IGCSE cohort of the seven emirates. Families here are the group most often told no local tutor covers their subject; an online intensive block removes the geography from the problem entirely.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also federally supervised. With very few British-curriculum places in the emirate, most IGCSE candidates travel to Sharjah or Ajman for school, so the session window is narrow on weekdays and weekend mornings carry most of an intensive block's hours.

schoolClusters.note: The largest concentration of IGCSE candidates in the country, and the cluster where mock timetables and study-leave dates vary most between schools even within the same series. Students we support attend schools across this group; the exact entry dates and tier decisions always come from the school's own exams officer.

A smaller British-curriculum set under ADEK, where the ethics rules on staff tutoring their own students shape how families find support. Mock windows here tend to sit slightly earlier than in Dubai, which shortens the useful window for a January intensive block.

Fewer schools, longer commutes and the thinnest local supply of syllabus-specific tutors, which is why nearly every intensive block in this cluster runs in the evening and online. Break calendars here can differ from Dubai's by a few days, so the block is planned against the school's own published calendar.

igcse-crash-course.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named here as context for the IGCSE school system UAE families work inside. IB Gram claims no affiliation with, endorsement by, or relationship to any school named.
igcse-crash-course.modesIntro: Four ways IGCSE intensive revision gets arranged. The difference between them is not teaching style; it is how many weeks are left and how much the student can absorb before the school work suffers.

modes.title: Intensive block before a series
modes.description: A fixed number of hours inside a fixed number of weeks, booked as a block and planned in the first session. Typically six to twelve hours per subject across three to six weeks, two or three sessions a week, with a written plan naming which topics are in and which are deliberately abandoned. The abandonment list is the part families find uncomfortable and the part that makes the block work.
bullets: Diagnostic paper marked before any teaching happens
A named topic list, and a named list of what the block will not cover
Every session ends with a timed question set under exam conditions
Plan rewritten once, after the first marked paper comes back

modes.title: Paper-by-paper clinics
modes.description: Single sessions aimed at one component rather than one subject: Paper 4 in 0580, the alternative-to-practical in 0625, directed writing in 0500. Used by students whose content is sound and whose marks are lost to structure and timing. Often bought two or three at a time in the last fortnight, when there is no longer room for anything cumulative.
bullets: One component, one session, the mark scheme open throughout
Student writes under timing; the tutor marks it with them afterwards
Command terms and mark allocations read aloud from the paper
Suited to the exam fortnight, between papers

modes.title: Holiday and study-leave intensives
modes.description: The same hours compressed into a school break or into study leave, when there is no homework competing for them. Winter and spring breaks are where most UAE intensive blocks actually sit, and study leave is where the final ones do. Mornings work better than evenings in a break, and a long block is split into two shorter daily sessions rather than one marathon.
bullets: Two shorter daily sessions beat one long one for retention
Scheduled around travel, which most UAE families do in the long breaks
Shortened Ramadan school days free an afternoon slot that the term does not
Works as the bridge block between the last IGCSE paper and DP1 or AS

modes.title: Weekly through the final term, then intensive
modes.description: One hour a week from the mocks to study leave, rising to three or four in the last fortnight. This is the cheapest shape per mark gained, because the early hours are spent on content while there is still time to practise it, and the late hours on technique when practice is all that is left. It only exists for families who plan from the mock results rather than from study leave.
bullets: Starts from the January mock paper, not from the exam date
Hours step up on a date agreed in advance, not on panic
Keeps the same tutor across both phases, so no re-diagnosis is needed
Pauses for the school's own coursework deadlines

sections.heading: What an IGCSE crash course actually buys, and what it cannot
paragraphs: An IGCSE crash course is a fixed block of hours, concentrated into weeks rather than terms, aimed at marks the student is already close to earning. It is not a compressed syllabus. The honest version of the offer is narrow: find the gap between what the student knows and what the paper rewards, and close as much of it as the remaining weeks allow.

That gap has three parts, and they close at different speeds. Content gaps are the slowest — a student who has never met electrolysis needs teaching, and teaching takes hours that a three-week block does not have for more than two or three topics. Technique gaps close faster: a student who knows the chemistry but writes four marks' worth of answer to a six-mark question can be fixed in two sessions, because the problem is the shape of the answer rather than the knowledge behind it. Process gaps close fastest of all, and they are the ones nobody teaches. Units omitted, working not shown, significant figures discarded, the last question left blank because the clock ran out, the wrong rubric answered. In a marked mock paper these usually account for more lost marks than the content does, and they are the first thing an intensive block should take.

The limits are equally specific. A block cannot change a tier entry once the school has submitted it. It cannot touch a coursework or practical component that has been completed and handed in. It cannot create an entry for a subject the school did not enter, and it cannot make a candidate eligible for a series their centre is not running. It cannot promise a grade, and the providers in this market who imply one are making a claim they have no mechanism to keep. What it can do is make the next paper a fairer test of what the student actually knows, which in most marked mocks is worth one grade and sometimes two.
The rest of this page is the calendar that decides which of those three gaps your block will be working on.
bullets: Content gaps: slowest to close, two or three topics maximum in a short block
Technique gaps: close in sessions, not weeks — answer shape and command terms
Process gaps: close fastest and are usually worth the most marks
Out of reach: submitted coursework, a filed tier entry, a series the centre is not running

sections.heading: The IGCSE exam year counted backwards
paragraphs: Every useful decision about an intensive block is a function of one number: how many weeks until the first paper. The table below counts the IGCSE year backwards from that paper and names, at each distance, what is happening, who owns the deadline that falls there, and what hours bought at that point can still change. It is the part of this page worth reading with the school calendar open next to it.

Two things in the table are worth saying in prose because families consistently get them wrong. The first is that the IGCSE exam entry deadline sits months before the exam, not weeks. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE series is the clearest illustration a UAE family can check for themselves: the last paper on that final timetable sat on 19 November 2026, and entries for the series closed in the early autumn, months rather than weeks ahead of the first paper. Cambridge behaves the same way for the two series UAE centres are entered for — entries for the June series close in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper, and the exact date for your centre is on the statement of entry rather than on anything a parent can look up a year ahead. The consequence is identical on either board: by the time a crash course feels urgent, the entry that fixed which tier and which subjects are being sat has usually already been filed. The second is that the entry is made by the school, not by the parent, which means every tier and subject decision in the twenty-weeks-out row is a conversation with the exams officer rather than something a tutor or a family can action directly.

The right-hand column deliberately narrows as the weeks run down. At sixteen weeks a block can reteach a unit and still practise it. At four weeks the same hours spent on new content are largely wasted, because there is no time to consolidate, and the same hours spent on timed papers and marking are not. Families who buy hours late and insist on content coverage are buying the wrong thing at the right time.

Where a row names a board date, confirm it against the board's live timetable for your centre's zone before building a plan around it. Pearson publishes provisional International GCSE timetables months ahead of each May/June and November series, and labels them provisional precisely because dates can be revised before the final version is issued to centres.

sections.heading: Which series your child is actually sitting
paragraphs: Before any block is planned, one question has to be answered precisely: which series, and which timetable version. Cambridge runs IGCSE, O Level and International A Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. On top of those, Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable version for each; Cambridge is explicit that it is essential to use the correct version for the zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version was used.

That zone rule is the single most common source of wrong revision plans in the UAE. A parent finds a timetable online, builds a plan around it, and discovers the paper sits two days earlier for their centre. The timetable version that matters is the one the school's exams officer is working from, and it is worth asking for it in writing at the point the statement of entry appears.

The table below sets out the series with the dates each board has published, and what each implies for an intensive block. One row needs a caveat rather than a cell: Cambridge's February/March series is offered to India only, so a UAE family who finds a February exam window online has found another country's timetable, and the series to plan hours around here is June, with November as the resit route. IB session dates are not listed anywhere on this page, because ibo.org blocks automated checking and no IB date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. If you need a Diploma date, take it from your school's IB coordinator.

A last practical point. Where two children in one household sit different series, the household is running two calendars with different deadlines, different results dates and different retake windows. Write both on one sheet before booking anything.

sections.heading: The first session is a diagnosis, not a lesson
paragraphs: In a short block, the first session is the one that decides whether the rest of the hours are spent well. It should produce a document, not a feeling. The student sits a past paper under timing — a whole component, not a question set — and the tutor marks it against the published mark scheme with the student watching. Every lost mark is then tagged: content, technique or process. That tagging is the plan.

What comes out is usually not what the family expected. A student described as weak at Chemistry turns out to be sound on everything except moles and electrolysis, and to be losing eleven marks across the paper to unstated units and unshown working. A student described as careless turns out to have a genuine gap in one unit that makes the last third of the paper unreachable. These two students need opposite blocks, and no amount of discussion in a first phone call distinguishes them. Only a marked paper does.

The diagnosis also sets what the block will not do. If eight hours remain and the tagging shows four content gaps, three of them get written down as out of scope. Families sometimes push back on that. The alternative — touching all four — reliably produces a student who has seen everything once and can do none of it under timing. Writing the exclusions down is what stops the block drifting back into general revision.

One thing a tutor cannot do in this session, or any session, is supply finished text for a piece the student will submit. Past papers, mock papers and practice questions are marked together and rewritten by the student. Anything heading for a board or a school is the student's own work from first draft to last, and we say so plainly because this SERP contains providers who sell the opposite.

IB Gram offers a trial session at no charge before any block is booked — one per family, 30 minutes, no card details taken. For a crash course that trial is best spent on the diagnostic paper rather than on conversation.
bullets: A whole component sat under timing, not a selection of questions
Marked live against the published mark scheme, with the student watching
Every lost mark tagged content, technique or process
A written topic list, and a written list of what the block excludes

sections.heading: Where the marks go, subject by subject
paragraphs: Marked mock papers from UAE schools show the same losses in the same places. The table below is the pattern, by syllabus code, with what an intensive block aims at first and a realistic number of hours for that specific repair. The hours are for the named repair only, not for the subject.

Reading the table properly means accepting that the first target is rarely the topic the student finds hardest. In 0580 the fastest marks are in structured working on Paper 4 questions the student already half-knows, not in the topic they dread. In 0625 the alternative-to-practical paper is more teachable in three weeks than the electricity unit, because a good answer about variables, control and fair testing has a shape that can be learned. In 0610 the content is usually closer than the family thinks and the command-term handling is further away.

The number in the last column is a repair estimate, not a package. Two students with the same code and the same grade can need six hours and sixteen, depending on how much of the loss is process rather than content. That is why the diagnostic comes before the quote, and why a provider quoting a fixed number of hours before seeing a marked paper is guessing.

Where a subject has both a Cambridge and a Pearson version, the papers differ enough that a plan has to name which one. A student on 4MA1 and a student on 0580 are not revising the same assessment, and material for one is partly wrong for the other.

sections.heading: What an intensive block costs in the UAE market
paragraphs: Price is the thing this market hides. Of the UAE tutoring pages examined for this project in October 2026, three of six published no hourly figure at all, one asked the price question in its own FAQ and then declined to answer it, and the two that did publish quoted US dollars. The table below is the market in AED, with each band attributed to whoever published it, so a UAE family can see the shape of the market before anyone quotes them anything.

These are market rates, not IB Gram's price list. What we charge for a block depends on the subject, the component, the number of weeks and how many hours a week the student can take without the school work suffering, and it is quoted on a call after the diagnostic rather than printed as a package. The reason is visible in the table above it: the same grade in the same subject can need six hours or sixteen.

Two patterns in the market are worth naming. Monthly packages are common — around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions, and AED 1,599 to 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits at a UAE address — and they are priced for a term, which makes them poor value for a four-week block and good value for a plan that starts at the mocks. Bestimate's monthly estimates for weekly one-hour sessions run AED 240-600 at the budget end, AED 600-1,200 mid-range, and AED 1,000-2,000 or more for specialist exam-year support. Second, rates quoted close to a series are sometimes higher than the same provider's term rate, which is one more argument for planning from the IGCSE mock results rather than from study leave.

Whatever the figure, ask what it excludes. Marking time, past-paper materials, a written plan and a report after the block are included by some providers and billed by others, and the exam entry itself is set by the board and the centre and is never part of a tutoring fee.

sections.heading: Core, Extended and the tier decision a block arrives too late to change
paragraphs: In tiered Cambridge syllabuses the entry decides the grade range available. Core and Extended are different papers with different grade ceilings, and the entry is submitted by the school against the board's published final entry deadline. Confirm your subject's own tier structure and grade range on the syllabus page at cambridgeinternational.org, because it varies by subject and changes between syllabus versions.

The timing problem is simple. The entry closes months before the paper, and the student's position usually becomes clear afterwards, in the mocks. A family that discovers in February that their child is capable of the higher tier is often discovering it after the entry has gone in. The window where a crash course can affect a tier decision is the twenty-weeks-out row of the calendar table, which is exactly the point at which almost nobody is thinking about tutoring.

So the practical advice runs the other way round. If your child is borderline on a tier in Year 10 or early Year 11, that is when to buy hours, because the hours can still change which paper they sit. If the entry is already in, the block's job is to maximise the grade available inside that tier, and pretending otherwise wastes the hours. A Core entry with excellent preparation is a better outcome than an Extended entry the student cannot reach, and a school that has made the lower-tier call usually has mock evidence for it.

Where a family disagrees with a tier decision, the conversation is with the school and it has a deadline. Ask the exams officer what evidence the decision rests on, what the board's final entry date for your series is, and whether an amendment is possible before it. A tutor can help you read the mock evidence; the decision and the deadline belong to the school.
bullets: Tier entries are submitted by the school against the board's published deadline
Grade ranges differ by tier and by subject — check the syllabus page, not a forum
Hours bought in Year 10 can change the tier; hours bought in April cannot
After the entry, the block's job is the ceiling available inside that tier

sections.heading: Ramadan, study leave and the three Ministry subjects
paragraphs: A UAE revision calendar has features a UK or Indian one does not. Ramadan moves roughly eleven days earlier in the Gregorian calendar each year, so in some years it sits across the mock window and in others across the final revision block. UAE schools run a shortened day during Ramadan, which removes evening energy and adds an afternoon slot. For an intensive block that is a scheduling change rather than a loss: sessions move earlier, run shorter, and sit more often. Eid then takes several consecutive days out, and those days have to be planned around rather than discovered.

Study leave is the second feature, and schools in the same emirate do not agree on when it starts. A block planned for the four weeks before the first paper can turn out to overlap three weeks of study leave at one school and one week at another, which changes how many hours a week a student can realistically absorb. Ask the school for the study-leave date in writing at the same time as the timetable version.

The third feature is the set of subjects the IGCSE timetable does not contain. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements had to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, with April 2026 for schools whose year starts in April. KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and states that combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. These lessons continue through the exam term and do not count towards the IGCSE result, which makes them a fixed block in the week an intensive plan has to work around.

They also come with a content rule worth knowing before anyone offers to tutor them: for the mandatory UAE subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Support for those subjects therefore follows the school's own material rather than an external scheme, and KHDA's instructional-time requirement is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, with the advice that any mandatory-subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes.
None of this changes the exam dates. It changes how many usable hours sit between today and them, which is the number an intensive block is actually spending.

sections.heading: What a tutor may touch, and what has to stay the student's own
paragraphs: Short blocks create the most pressure on this boundary, because they often arrive in the weeks when a coursework or practical component is still open. The rule is not negotiable and it is worth stating in the plain form a parent can hold a provider to: a tutor teaches, questions, explains and gives feedback on work the student has already produced. The submitted text is the student's own, first draft to final.

In practice that means a tutor can read a draft and say which assessment criterion is not yet evidenced, can ask the question that makes a weak paragraph collapse, can teach the technique the piece needs, and can mark a past paper line by line against the published descriptors. A tutor cannot supply sentences for submission, cannot rewrite a section into its final form, and cannot produce any part of an assessed piece on the student's behalf. The distinction is between teaching and authorship, and every provider in this market knows where the line is even when their advertising sits across it.

This matters commercially as well as ethically. One page in this SERP sells completed Internal Assessments outright. A student who buys that risks their qualification; the provider risks nothing. Families comparing providers should treat an offer to produce assessed work as disqualifying rather than convenient, and should ask any prospective tutor directly what they will and will not do with a draft.

There are two further boundaries specific to materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to the boards, so they are referenced and linked rather than reproduced or distributed. And where a school sets its own internal deadline ahead of a board deadline, the school's date is the one the plan follows, because missing it has consequences the board's calendar does not describe.
bullets: Feedback on produced work: yes. Supplying text for submission: never
Past papers marked together, with the student rewriting the answer
Board materials referenced and linked, not reproduced or distributed
The school's internal deadline outranks the board's where the two differ

sections.heading: The regulator map, the tutor permit and what a parent can verify
paragraphs: Private schooling in the UAE is regulated emirate by emirate, and the regulator matters to an intensive block mainly because it is who publishes the school's inspection report and who sets the mandatory-subject rules the weekly timetable has to carry. Dubai sits with KHDA, which is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools there. Sharjah sits with the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge, and Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah with the federal Ministry of Education. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval and not merely inspection sits at emirate level.

Private tutoring itself is regulated separately and federally. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and covers teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18 and university students. MoHRE's own service page is Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, listing no fee and a two-working-day completion time, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws; no fine schedule is published, so no amount is quoted here.

A parent can therefore verify two things before committing to a block: whether the individual teaching their child holds the permit, and whether the provider is claiming any status it does not hold. IB Gram holds no approval, accreditation or licence from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Ministry of Education, the IB, Cambridge or Pearson, and claims none. A tutoring operation with premises and staff in Dubai is a different legal animal from an individual tutor and needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute; that permit is a specific document with a number, and any provider implying it should be asked to show it.

One Abu Dhabi rule shapes who can teach your child. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE permit's code of conduct also bars serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. That is press-reported rather than quoted from the policy document here, so verify it against the current ADEK text before relying on it. The practical effect is unambiguous: nobody should be marketing your child's own class teacher to you privately.

sections.heading: After the last paper: results, reviews, retakes and the equivalency file
paragraphs: A crash course ends at the last paper, but the calendar does not. The gap between the final paper and the result is longer than families expect and it contains decisions with their own deadlines. For the series a UAE candidate actually sits, the shape holds on both boards even where the exact day is not published a year out: Cambridge issues results for the June series in the summer and for the November series in the winter, several weeks after the final paper, with printed certificates following months later again, and the exams officer holds the dated schedule for your centre's zone. Pearson's June 2026 results reached centres on 19 August 2026 and students on 20 August 2026, and the November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026.

Those dates set three tasks. First, know in advance where the result will be collected from and who in the family will be able to act on it, because August results in particular land while UAE families are travelling. Second, know the review-of-results route before you need it: a request to have marking looked at again runs through the exam centre, not the family, and it has a deadline measured in weeks. Third, know the next series and its entry deadline, because a retake decision taken late misses the entry rather than the exam.

The Ministry equivalency file is the one administrative task worth starting early. For the British track the Ministry requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, plus either one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One ranking competitor states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced rule is five. For the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the SAT reading and writing section, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test before applying.

No IB points figure appears in that source, so none is published here. Verify any IB equivalency threshold on moe.gov.ae or with your emirate's attestation channel. Equivalency and attestation are Ministry processes: they are described on this page and they are not something IB Gram performs, expedites or guarantees, and tutoring is not required for any of them.

process.title: Send us the series, the date and the mock paper
process.description: Not the subject and the grade. The series, the centre's timetable version if the school has issued it, the school's study-leave date, and the marked mock paper. Those four pieces decide how many usable weeks exist and what the hours can be spent on, and they take a parent ten minutes to gather.

process.title: A diagnostic paper before any teaching
process.description: The student sits a full component under timing and the tutor marks it live against the published mark scheme. Every lost mark is tagged content, technique or process. The output is a written plan with a topic list and an exclusion list, which is what makes a short block different from general revision.

process.title: Hours mapped onto the weeks that remain
process.description: The plan allocates hours by distance from the paper, not evenly. Content work goes early or not at all; timed papers and marking take the final fortnight. Where the arithmetic says the block cannot cover what the family wants, we say so before taking the booking rather than afterwards.

process.title: Every session ends under exam conditions
process.description: A timed question set, then marking together. The student rewrites their own answer; the tutor does not supply a model to copy. This is the loop that converts knowledge into marks, and in an intensive block it runs every session rather than once a term.

process.title: A handover before the first paper
process.description: In the last session before the series, the tutor writes down what was covered, what was deliberately left out, and the three things to do in the exam fortnight. Families with two children sitting different series get both calendars on one sheet, because that is where the clashes show up.

process.title: A results-day plan, agreed in advance
process.description: Before the block ends we note the results date for the series, who in the family will be able to act that day, the review-of-results route through the centre, and the entry deadline for the next series. Decided in May, those are administrative; decided in August, they are a scramble.

whyPoints.title: The dates come from the boards, not from us
whyPoints.description: Every Cambridge and Pearson date on this page is traceable to the board that published it, and the Cambridge zone rule is quoted because it is the rule most often broken by plans built from a timetable found online. Where a date is not verifiable, it is left off rather than estimated.

whyPoints.title: No IB exam dates are published here
whyPoints.description: ibo.org blocks automated checking, so no IB session or results date in this project has been confirmed from the IB itself. Rather than reprint a date circulating secondhand, this page tells you to take Diploma dates from your school's IB coordinator. A wrong date in a revision plan is worse than no date.

whyPoints.title: AED figures are attributed, ours are quoted after the diagnostic
whyPoints.description: The rate table names who published each band. IB Gram's own figure for a block depends on the component, the weeks remaining and the hours a week the student can absorb, so it is quoted on a call rather than printed as a package that would be wrong for most families who read it.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery widens the specialist pool
whyPoints.description: Lessons run live online, one-to-one, over video; home visits are offered only in India. For a family in Al Ain, Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain that is the difference between a 0620 specialist and whoever is available locally, and in a four-week block the specificity of the match is most of the value.

whyPoints.title: We say no when a block will not help
whyPoints.description: If the arithmetic shows that the remaining weeks cannot cover what the family is asking for, we say which part is reachable and which is not before any hours are booked. Selling twelve hours against a request that needs forty is the easiest sale in this market and the one that damages students.

whyPoints.title: The academic-honesty line is stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: A tutor teaches, questions and gives feedback on work the student has produced. Nothing submitted is authored by anyone else. This page states that in plain words because this search results page contains providers who sell the opposite, and families deserve to know which kind they are speaking to.

faqs.question: What does an IGCSE crash course cover that weekly tuition does not?
faqs.answer: A crash course is defined by a date rather than a syllabus. Weekly tuition works through content in the order a course teaches it; an intensive block works backwards from the first paper and spends its hours only on marks reachable in the weeks remaining. That means it will deliberately skip topics a weekly plan would cover, and it will spend an unusual share of its time on timed papers, marking and answer structure. The practical difference shows in the first session: weekly tuition usually starts teaching, while a block starts by sitting and marking a paper to decide what to abandon.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the papers does an intensive block stop being useful?
faqs.answer: It never stops being useful, but what it can do narrows sharply. At twelve weeks a block can still reteach whole units and practise them. At six weeks the sensible target is three topics plus paper technique. At two weeks only process marks are realistically reachable: units, working shown, command-term handling, question order, and the questions usually left blank. Even during the exam fortnight single sessions between papers help, because the next paper's structure can be rehearsed. What changes is the honest claim. Hours bought late buy fewer marks, and any provider promising otherwise is selling the calendar, not teaching.

faqs.question: How many hours a week should an IGCSE crash course run?
faqs.answer: Two to three sessions a week per subject is the usual ceiling while school is still running, rising to daily shorter sessions during study leave or a school break. The limiting factor is not willingness but consolidation: content met and never practised is content the paper will not reward. In our plans the arithmetic runs the other way round, from the hours available to the topics they can cover, rather than from a topic list to an impossible timetable. Two shorter daily sessions in a break retain better than one long one, which is why holiday intensives are split rather than stacked.

faqs.question: Can an intensive block cover a whole IGCSE syllabus from scratch?
faqs.answer: No, and a provider who says otherwise should be asked how. A two-year syllabus met for the first time in a few weeks produces recognition rather than recall, and IGCSE papers test recall under timing. Where a student genuinely has not been taught a subject, the honest options are a later series, a different subject, or a longer plan that starts now and runs to the next sitting. What a short block can do with an untaught subject is cover the highest-yield units well enough to secure the grades those units carry, which is a real outcome and a much smaller one than full coverage.

faqs.question: What should the first session of a crash course produce?
faqs.answer: A marked paper and a written plan. The student sits a full component under timing, the tutor marks it live against the published mark scheme, and every lost mark is tagged as content, technique or process. The plan that comes out names the topics in scope and, just as importantly, the topics deliberately excluded. If a first session produces only a conversation and a reassurance, the block has started without a diagnosis, and the hours after it will be spent on whatever the student mentions rather than on whatever the paper is taking from them.

faqs.question: Which IGCSE subjects respond fastest to an intensive block?
faqs.answer: English as a Second Language and First Language English respond quickly, because the gains are in technique and structure rather than content. Mathematics responds well because losses cluster in showable working and abandoned multi-step questions. Chemistry responds better than the other sciences because its content is modular, so moles can be repaired without touching organic chemistry. Biology responds through command-term work rather than content. Combined and Co-ordinated Sciences respond slowest, because the weakest of three sciences drags the whole award and the hours have to be concentrated there rather than spread.

faqs.question: What does an intensive IGCSE block cost in the UAE market?
faqs.answer: Published UAE rates run from AED 45-150 an hour at the budget end, where EdFlik lists AED 45-65 and Tutopiya AED 33-52; AED 150-300 for a qualified online subject tutor, with Unitors listing IGCSE from AED 150; and AED 200-450 or more for an IGCSE or A-Level specialist, with TutorChase at AED 270. Monthly packages around AED 799 for eight online sessions are common. Those are other providers' published figures, quoted as the market. What a block costs with us depends on the component and the weeks remaining, and is quoted after the diagnostic paper rather than printed as a package.

faqs.question: Is a holiday intensive better value than spreading the same hours over a term?
faqs.answer: It depends which problem the student has. A holiday intensive is better for content gaps, because there is no homework competing for attention and a topic can be taught and practised on consecutive days. Spreading the hours is better for technique and process, because those improve through repetition against school work rather than in a burst. Most families get the best of both by starting weekly at the mock results and switching to intensive during the break or study leave. Note that monthly packages are priced for a term, which makes them poor value for a four-week block.

faqs.question: Can a crash course still change my child's Core or Extended tier?
faqs.answer: Only if it starts early enough. Tier entries are submitted by the school against the board's published final entry deadline, which falls months before the paper, so hours bought in Year 10 or early Year 11 can affect which paper a child sits and hours bought in the final term cannot. If the entry is already in, the block's job is to reach the highest grade available inside that tier. Check your subject's tier structure and grade range on the syllabus page at cambridgeinternational.org, and take the entry deadline and any amendment possibility from the school's exams officer.

faqs.question: Does a crash course work for a private candidate sitting IGCSE exams in the UAE?
faqs.answer: Yes, with one piece of homework first. A private candidate sits at an exam centre that accepts external entries, and the centre holds the entry, the candidate number and the timetable version. Confirm that a centre will take an external candidate for your specific syllabus and series before planning hours, because availability varies by subject and by sitting and cannot be inferred from the board's general timetable. Once that is confirmed, the block itself is simpler than a school candidate's, because there is no school mock calendar or internal deadline competing with it.

faqs.question: Will a crash-course tutor mark my daughter's past papers for her?
faqs.answer: A tutor marks past papers with her, against the published mark scheme, and she rewrites her own answers afterwards. That is the loop that converts knowledge into marks, and it is the core of an intensive block. What no tutor here will do is supply text for anything she submits to a school or a board: feedback on produced work is teaching, supplying finished answers is authorship, and the line between them is not blurred in our sessions. If a provider offers to hand over model answers to be copied into an assessed piece, that is the kind of help that puts a qualification at risk.

faqs.question: How does a block handle a subject where the coursework has already been submitted?
faqs.answer: It works on the written papers only, and the plan says so explicitly. A completed and submitted component is closed: it cannot be revisited, improved or replaced, and any mark already banked is part of the final grade whatever happens in the examination. The useful consequence is arithmetic. Once the coursework mark is known or forecast, the marks still available in the remaining papers can be counted, and the block can be aimed at the components where the grade is genuinely still moving rather than at the whole subject.

faqs.question: My son is retaking two IGCSE subjects. Does an intensive block suit a retake?
faqs.answer: A retake is the cleanest case for one. There is a known result, a known paper, no new syllabus, and a fixed next series. The first session starts from the statement of results rather than from a diagnostic paper, because the component marks already say where the grade was lost. The planning question is which series to enter and when its entry closes: a Cambridge or Pearson November sitting gives a term if the decision is made in August and about four weeks if it is made in October. Enter first, then book hours.

faqs.question: How do we find the exact paper dates a crash course should be built around?
faqs.answer: From the school's exams officer, in writing, and not from a timetable found online. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a different timetable version for each, stating that it is essential to use the correct version and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong one was used. Ask for the zone timetable version, the statement of entry, the school's mock dates and the study-leave start date together. Pearson also publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series, so a date seen early can still be revised.

faqs.question: Are the mandatory Arabic and Islamic Education lessons part of an intensive block?
faqs.answer: They sit outside the IGCSE result and inside the school week. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA requires separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, with combined classes strictly prohibited. For the mandatory subjects, using different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is strictly prohibited, so support for them follows the school's own material. For an intensive block the point is scheduling: those lessons are fixed hours the plan works around.

faqs.question: What happens if no specialist is free for the subject and series we need?
faqs.answer: We say so, and we say it before taking a booking rather than after. Close to a series the specialist pool for a specific syllabus code thins, and the honest options are a different time slot, a shorter block with a narrower target, or a later series. Where a UAE-based tutor is unavailable, delivery is online in any case, so the pool is not limited to the emirates. What we will not do is place a generalist against a component-level problem and let the family discover the mismatch in week three of a four-week block.

faqs.question: Does an intensive block do anything for the Ministry of Education equivalency file?
faqs.answer: Not directly. Equivalency is a Ministry process and tutoring is not required for it. What a block can do is affect the grades the file will contain. For the British track the Ministry requires five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE at no less than grade E or 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from those five, plus one Advanced Level subject at E or two Advanced Subsidiary subjects at the same grade. Knowing which five subjects carry the file sometimes changes where a block spends its hours. Verify the current requirements on moe.gov.ae.

igcse-crash-course.closingHeading: Start from the date on the statement of entry
igcse-crash-course.closingBody: If you are weighing an IGCSE crash course in the UAE, the first thing to find is not a tutor. It is the series, the centre's timetable version, the school's study-leave date and the most recent marked mock paper. With those four things an intensive block can be planned honestly: this many usable weeks, these topics, these components, these marks reachable and these not. Without them any quote is a guess. Send us the four and we will tell you what the weeks can carry, including when the answer is that they cannot carry what you are asking for. An online IGCSE crash course removes the drive from the plan, and IGCSE retake support works the same way, starting from the statement of results instead. Lessons run live online, one-to-one, timed to Gulf Standard Time.
