igcse-exam-preparation.tutorsIntro: The tutors below teach IGCSE subjects at Core and Extended tier for Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel candidates sitting papers from UAE centres. Each works from the syllabus code on your child's statement of entry, in one-to-one online lessons scheduled against the school's own mock and coursework calendar.

intro.heading: Exam preparation begins with what the centre has already fixed
paragraphs: A UAE family searching for IGCSE exam preparation is usually weeks or months past the point where the largest decisions were made. The school chose Cambridge or Pearson Edexcel. The school entered your child against a particular syllabus code. The school decided, or accepted, whether that entry was Core or Extended. The school belongs to one of Cambridge's six administrative zones, and that zone decides which version of the timetable applies. Preparation works inside those decisions rather than around them. A tutor who does not know them is guessing about which paper your child will open on the morning.

So the first useful conversation is not about teaching. It is about three documents. The statement of entry names the board, the code, the tier and the components. The school's own calendar names the mock window and the date the centre needs forecast grades. The regulator's published inspection report describes how that school teaches the subject and where its results sit. Put the three together and the hours almost plan themselves, because you then know how many papers are coming, what each component is worth, how many weeks remain, and which parts of the course the school has probably covered thinly.

The second thing to settle is delivery. Tutors matched through IB Gram teach UAE students one-to-one online, over live video, screen-sharing the paper both people are reading. Home visits are part of what we do in India, not here. For exam preparation that tends to be the stronger arrangement rather than a compromise. A family in Al Ain or Fujairah reaches a Physics 0625 specialist instead of whoever can get to the community by half past four, and no part of a paid hour is spent on Sheikh Zayed Road in February traffic.

The third thing is money, and this market is oddly quiet about it. Among the ranking pages examined in October 2026, three published no price at all and two quoted United States dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. The rate tables further down carry AED figures beside the provider or survey that published them, because a number without a source is not information. None of those figures is an IB Gram price list. Our own arrangement starts with an introductory lesson and a frank conversation about how many hours the remaining calendar genuinely leaves.

Last, administration decides more outcomes than most parents expect. An access arrangement nobody applied for cannot be granted in the exam hall. A forecast grade is produced by the centre and used for administration, not handed over as a prediction a family can argue with. An entry that closed in November will not reopen in January because revision has gone well. Knowing which doors are already shut is what tells you where an hour of teaching still pays, and that is the argument this page is built on.
bullets: Find the syllabus code on the statement of entry before booking any hours
Cambridge timetables differ by administrative zone; read the version issued for your centre

Market revision rates across the UAE run from roughly AED 45 to AED 650 an hour by tier

Five accredited subjects at no less than grade E or 3 sit behind a Ministry equivalency file

igcse-exam-preparation.programmesIntro: IGCSE sits in the middle of a longer Cambridge or Pearson route, and exam preparation looks different at each stage of it. The four stages below are the ones UAE centres actually enter candidates for. Each note describes how the stage behaves in UAE schools specifically, because the series a centre chooses and the subjects it offers vary a great deal between emirates.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge IGCSE is a two-year course assessed by written papers at the end, with some subjects carrying a practical or coursework component. Subjects are identified by a four-digit syllabus code, and the code matters more than the subject name: Mathematics 0580 and Additional Mathematics 0606 are different courses with different papers. Many subjects are tiered, so a candidate is entered either for Core papers, which cap the available grade, or Extended papers. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates; the February/March series is offered to India only, so a February window found online belongs to another country's timetable.
programmes.countryNote: UK-curriculum schools account for the largest share of Dubai's private-school enrolment, with UK-curriculum enrolment at 37% across 227 schools in 2024-25, so Cambridge IGCSE is the single most commonly examined route in the emirate. Entries are made by the school as a centre, and every UAE centre is allocated to one of Cambridge's six administrative zones. That allocation changes which timetable document is correct for your child, which is why two Dubai schools can publish different start times for the same paper.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE uses codes beginning with a numeral, such as 4MA1 for Mathematics A, 4PH1 for Physics and 4CH1 for Chemistry. The structure differs from Cambridge in ways that matter for revision: fewer, longer papers in several subjects, a different approach to tiering, and in some specifications a modular pattern where a component can be sat in an earlier series. Pearson publishes International GCSE series in May and June and again in November each year.
programmes.countryNote: A good number of UAE schools run a mixed entry, putting Mathematics and the sciences through one board and languages or humanities through another, which is why a parent should never assume the whole timetable comes from one place. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and the board publishes provisional timetables for later series in advance. Read the live official timetable rather than a date copied onto a tutoring website.

programmes.name: Cambridge Lower Secondary Checkpoint
programmes.description: Checkpoint tests are diagnostic rather than certificated. Cambridge offers Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint test series in March, May and October, and a school uses the results to place students and to judge readiness for the IGCSE course that follows. The marks are reported against Cambridge's own scale rather than as IGCSE grades, so they cannot be converted, but they do show which strands of Mathematics, English and Science a cohort entered Year 10 weak in.
programmes.countryNote: Several UAE schools share Checkpoint outcomes with parents and then do nothing further with them, which is a wasted signal. If your child sat Lower Secondary Checkpoint in Year 9 and the Science strand on number handling or scientific enquiry came back low, that is the strand most likely to cost marks on an IGCSE practical or data paper two years later. Asking the school for the strand breakdown is free and takes one email to the head of year.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The qualification most UAE IGCSE candidates move into next is International AS and A Level, taken in two stages or as a linear two-year course depending on the centre. Entry requirements are set by the school, and a subject usually asks for a specific IGCSE grade in that subject or in Mathematics. This is where tier choices made in Year 10 become visible, because a Core entry that capped the grade can close a subject off at sixth form before the student has read a single A Level page.
programmes.countryNote: For a UAE family the A Level stage also carries the Ministry of Education equivalency route. On the British track, the published requirement includes one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, alongside five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at no less than E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among those five, which changes which subjects a Year 11 revision plan should protect.

igcse-exam-preparation.subjectsIntro: Exam preparation is subject-specific and code-specific. The subjects below are the ones UAE families most often ask for in the final two terms, with the Cambridge and Pearson codes written out, because a tutor working from the wrong specification will teach content your child is not examined on. Where a subject is tiered, the tier changes both the paper and the grade ceiling.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge 0580 · Pearson 4MA1)
subjects.description: The most entered subject and the one where tier choice bites hardest, because Core papers cap the grade available. Marks go missing on multi-step problems where method marks are lost to unshown working, on transformations and vectors, and on reading the degree of accuracy a question demands. Pearson 4MA1 sets two longer papers; Cambridge 0580 splits the Extended entry across Papers 2 and 4.

subjects.name: Additional Mathematics (Cambridge 0606)
subjects.description: A separate syllabus, not an extension of 0580, and frequently confused with it by families booking hours. It carries calculus, series and trigonometric identities that 0580 does not, and is often taken by students heading for A Level Mathematics. A tutor who prepares a 0606 candidate on 0580 material will leave the differentiation and integration questions untouched until it is far too late.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge 0625 · Pearson 4PH1)
subjects.description: Electricity and magnetism are where UAE candidates most often stall, followed by anything requiring a graph to be drawn and then read. Practical skills are assessed, by an examined paper in some routes and by alternative-to-practical in others, and that distinction decides whether revision needs apparatus diagrams or laboratory technique. Formula recall is less decisive than correct unit handling.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge 0620 · Pearson 4CH1)
subjects.description: Moles calculations, ionic equations and organic chemistry account for a large share of lost marks, and the losses are usually mechanical rather than conceptual: unbalanced equations, missing state symbols, a mole ratio inverted. Qualitative analysis tests are memorisable and routinely under-revised. A diagnostic lesson on a past paper separates the arithmetic problem from the chemistry problem quickly.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge 0610 · Pearson 4BI1)
subjects.description: Biology rewards precision of language more than any other science at this level, and that is exactly what slips in a second language. Answers lose marks for describing a process when the command word asked for an explanation, and for naming a structure without naming its function. Transport in plants, homeostasis and genetics crosses are the recurring weak strands in UAE cohorts.

subjects.name: English Language (Cambridge 0500 · Pearson 4EA1)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the reading passages carry most of the risk. Candidates who read widely still lose marks on the summary task by copying phrasing from the passage instead of compressing it, and on the composition by writing well without answering the form specified. Timing is a technical skill here, and it is coachable in a handful of sessions with a clock running.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge 0510 · 0511)
subjects.description: A different syllabus from 0500 with a different mark scheme, and the choice between them is a school decision that sometimes surprises parents. The listening and speaking components are weighted meaningfully, so a candidate who prepares only for reading and writing has left marks on the table. Exam technique on the note-making and summary tasks is the fastest available gain.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy decides the upper band. A supply and demand diagram with unlabelled axes or an unmarked new equilibrium point scores below one drawn properly, whatever the written answer says. The data-response paper rewards candidates who quote the figures given rather than writing around them, and evaluation marks need a judgement, not a list of two sides.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge 0450)
subjects.description: A subject where strong students plateau because they write general business sense instead of applying it to the case study in front of them. Marks sit behind application and evaluation, so the coachable skill is reading a case and quoting it. Calculation elements, including break-even and basic ratios, are small in weight and are frequently dropped entirely.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge 0478)
subjects.description: Theory papers reward exact definitions, and the pseudocode and algorithm questions reward practice rather than reading. Candidates commonly lose marks on trace tables, on binary and hexadecimal conversion under time pressure, and on describing how a technology works when the question asked what it is used for. Short, frequent practice beats long sessions in this subject.

subjects.name: Geography (Cambridge 0460)
subjects.description: Case-study recall and map skills are the two separable halves, and most candidates are strong in one and weak in the other. Named examples with figures score; generic examples do not. Cross-sections, gradient calculation and grid references are mechanical skills that can be fixed in two or three sessions, which makes them the best value revision in the subject.

subjects.name: Arabic as a First Language (Cambridge 0508)
subjects.description: Taken by Arab students alongside the mandatory Arabic required by UAE regulators, and the two are not the same course. Preparation focuses on formal register, text analysis and composition structure in Standard Arabic. Because the school's mandatory Arabic provision follows Ministry-approved content, additional material for a Cambridge entry needs to be planned with the subject teacher rather than around them.

igcse-exam-preparation.regionsTitle: IGCSE exam preparation across the seven emirates
igcse-exam-preparation.regionsIntro: Which emirate your child's school sits in changes which authority holds its file, how many UK-curriculum schools are within reach, and how realistic a weekday evening session is. Online delivery removes the travel problem, but it does not remove the administrative differences, and those are the ones that affect an entry.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: Regulated by KHDA, with 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25 across 17 curricula. The deepest pool of UK-curriculum centres in the country, and the emirate where mixed Cambridge and Pearson entries are most common within a single school.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school, so the obvious evening arrangement is not available here.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK. Fewer UK-curriculum centres than the island, which historically limited the choice of local subject specialists for tiered sciences. Live online lessons are the practical route to an Extended-tier Chemistry or Physics specialist without a ninety-minute each-way drive.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: Regulated by the Sharjah Private Education Authority, which regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That approval scope is broader than inspection alone, and it is worth knowing before assuming a school can simply add a subject.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: Private schools here are supervised by the federal Ministry of Education rather than an emirate-level authority. Families often commute to Sharjah or Dubai centres, which makes a weekday session before seven in the evening difficult and a live online slot the only workable one on school nights.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: The Department of Knowledge regulates private education in the emirate, and like Sharjah it approves curricula and assessment methods as well as fees. Named by essentially none of the tutoring sites competing for these searches, which tells you how much local detail those pages actually carry.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Supervised by the Ministry of Education. The smallest set of UK-curriculum options on the east coast, and the clearest case for online delivery: subject choice at Extended tier stops being a function of who lives nearby and starts being a function of who teaches the code.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also under Ministry of Education supervision. Families here frequently sit papers at a centre in another emirate, which makes the zone timetable question and the travel plan for exam mornings worth settling in January rather than the week before the first paper.

schoolClusters.note: UK-curriculum centres across Dubai enter candidates for both Cambridge and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE, and several run split entries by department. Students we support attend schools of this kind; the list is context for the cohort a tutor is teaching into, not a claim about any relationship with the school.

ADEK-regulated centres in the capital run strong UK-curriculum provision, and the ethics rules on staff tutoring their own students make an independent tutor the normal arrangement rather than the fallback. Families here usually book around a longer school day and later commute.

SPEA-regulated schools in Sharjah and Ministry-supervised schools further north offer a narrower set of IGCSE options, which pushes some students towards private-candidate entries for subjects their centre does not run. That decision has deadlines attached and should be made early in Year 10.

igcse-exam-preparation.schoolDisclaimer: Schools are named as context for the UAE examination ecosystem; IB Gram claims no affiliation, partnership or endorsement from any school, group or regulator.
igcse-exam-preparation.modesIntro: Exam preparation is a different product from term-time catch-up, and the shape of it should change as the series gets closer. These are the three arrangements UAE families most often use between January and the first paper, all delivered one-to-one online over live video.

modes.title: Weekly one-to-one across two terms
modes.description: A single recurring slot per subject from the start of the IGCSE year, working through the specification alongside the school's scheme of work. This is the arrangement with the best return per dirham because it reaches topics before they are taught badly or skipped, and it gives a tutor enough contact to know whether a weak answer is a content gap or an exam-technique gap.
bullets: One subject per slot, 60 or 90 minutes
Planned against the school's own topic order
Written feedback after each session
Paused and restarted around mock weeks

modes.title: Pre-series intensive block
modes.description: A concentrated set of sessions in the weeks before the papers, built from a diagnostic on a recent past paper rather than from the specification start. The block targets the three or four topics producing the largest losses and the exam-technique habits costing marks across every question. It is the right shape when a family arrives late, and it is honest work only if the diagnosis comes first.
bullets: Diagnostic on a recent paper in session one
Two or three sessions a week for a fixed number of weeks
Timed questions under exam conditions
A written list of what is not being covered

modes.title: Paper-by-paper review clinic
modes.description: Short, frequent sessions where the student works a paper, submits it, and the tutor reviews it line by line on screen against the mark scheme's logic. This is marking plus teaching rather than teaching alone, and it suits candidates whose content knowledge is sound but whose marks do not reflect it. It is also the cheapest way to fix command-word misreading.
bullets: Student attempts the paper unaided and to time
Review focuses on where each mark was available
Patterns logged across papers, not just errors
Works alongside, not instead of, school marking

sections.heading: What the centre has already decided, and what a tutor can still move
paragraphs: IGCSE exam preparation in the UAE is constrained work. By the time a family starts looking, the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the series are usually settled, and several of them cannot be changed at all. That is not a reason to lower expectations; it is a reason to spend hours where they still have purchase. The honest version of this conversation separates the fixed from the open in the first twenty minutes, so nobody pays for sessions aimed at a decision that closed last term.

The commonest expensive misunderstanding concerns tier. A Core entry in Cambridge Mathematics 0580 caps the grade a candidate can be awarded, so a family paying for intensive Extended-level teaching against a Core entry is buying knowledge their child cannot be credited for. Entry amendments have deadlines, they sit with the exams officer, and after a point they simply are not possible. Ask what the entry says before the first lesson, not after the mock.

What preparation genuinely moves is narrower and more useful than the marketing on most tutoring sites suggests. It moves accuracy under time pressure. It moves whether a candidate reads a command word correctly. It moves whether method marks are available on a question that was ultimately got wrong. It moves how much of a specification has actually been revised rather than re-read. Those are the things a weekly hour changes, and they are enough to move several grade boundaries across a timetable of nine subjects.

Confirm the tier for every tiered subject, not just Mathematics
Check whether a practical or alternative-to-practical route applies in each science
Confirm which board each subject sits with; mixed entries are common in UAE schools

sections.heading: Six administrative zones, and the timetable your child actually sits
paragraphs: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and it states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone. The same sentence carries the consequence: Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong zone's timetable was used. That is an unusually blunt statement from an awarding body, and it exists because the mistake happens.

For a UAE family the practical effect is that a timetable printed from a general internet search, or copied from a cousin's school in another country, may show a different start time or even a different day for the same paper. Two schools inside the same emirate can legitimately publish different times. The only timetable that matters is the one issued for your child's centre, and the exams officer holds it. Ask for the zone-specific version in writing and keep it somewhere other than a parent WhatsApp group.

Zones also explain why some apparently sensible revision plans go wrong. If a candidate has two papers separated by a single day in one zone's sequence and three days in another, the amount of last-minute revision available between them is different, and so is the sensible order of the final week's sessions. A tutor planning the final fortnight should be working from the actual timetable rather than from a generic subject order, which is a small thing that is cheap to get right and awkward to fix late.

sections.heading: Access arrangements: the application only an exams officer can file
paragraphs: Access arrangements are the adjustments an awarding body can approve for a candidate who needs them, and they are the single most commonly missed piece of IGCSE administration in international schools. They are applied for by the centre, through the exams officer, to the board. A family cannot apply directly. Nor can a tutor, a paediatrician, an educational psychologist or an agency, however helpful the report any of them has written. The report is evidence the centre uses; the application is the centre's to make.

Timing is the part that catches people. An arrangement has to be in place before the series, which means the conversation belongs in the autumn term of Year 11 at the latest, and earlier if a formal assessment is still needed. A family who raises it in April after a difficult mock is usually too late for that series, and the answer they get will feel arbitrary when it is simply a closed window. If your child has ever had support at school for reading speed, writing or attention, ask the exams officer in writing what is already recorded and what the board has approved.

Where a tutor is genuinely useful is in the evidence trail and in the preparation itself. A candidate approved for additional time has to learn to use it, which sounds obvious and is not: most students who are given extra time spend it rereading rather than answering, and that habit is trainable in a few timed sessions. A tutor can also document, session by session, what a student can do when the clock is not the constraint, which is exactly the kind of normal-way-of-working record a centre wants when it builds a case.
bullets: Ask the exams officer what access arrangements are already on file, in writing
Raise any new need in the autumn term of Year 11, not after the mocks
Keep the assessment report; the centre needs the evidence, not a summary of it
Practise working with the arrangement in timed conditions before the series

sections.heading: Forecast grades, mocks, and the difference between them
paragraphs: A forecast grade is a prediction the centre supplies to the awarding body as part of running the series. Cambridge sets a forecast-grade deadline for each series that falls very late in the run-up, close to and sometimes inside the examination period itself, and the dated version for your centre sits on the exams officer's key-dates list. That ordering tells you what the figure is for: it is administrative information for the board, not a report to parents, and it is not a negotiation.

Mock results are a different object entirely, produced by the school for the school. They are marked by teachers against their reading of the mark scheme, sat under conditions that are usually close to but not identical to the real thing, and frequently scaled to a boundary set locally. A mock grade is therefore most useful as a diagnostic and least useful as a forecast. The question worth asking is not what grade came back but which marks were available and not taken, question by question.

Parents often want to challenge one or both numbers, and that energy is better spent elsewhere. What changes a forecast is the evidence the subject teacher holds, and the only honest way to change the evidence is for the student's work to improve in class, in assessments, and on paper. A tutor who promises to influence a prediction is selling something they cannot deliver. A tutor who takes the mock script apart with the student, finds the eleven marks lost to unshown working and fixes the habit, is doing the job that eventually moves both numbers.

sections.heading: A UAE series counted backwards, with published dates
paragraphs: Nobody in this search results page publishes a session calendar, which is strange, because the calendar is what determines whether a plan is realistic. The table below counts backwards through Pearson Edexcel's International GCSE November 2026 series, one of the two windows a UAE candidate can actually sit, using the dates the board published on its own final timetable. Cambridge families should read it for the shape rather than the days: Cambridge runs a June series and a November series here, the February/March series is offered to India only, and the exact deadlines come from the centre's zone timetable. Either way the shape repeats, because entries close months before the papers and results arrive months after them.

Read the first row carefully. The entry is filed months before the papers, not weeks: Pearson's November 2026 papers finished on 19 November 2026 and the entries behind them were made well before the autumn term was over, while for the Cambridge June series entries close in the spring, roughly four months ahead of the first paper, on a date printed on the centre's statement of entry. Everything a family decides about which subjects, which tier and whether to sit at all happens before that point. A revision plan that starts a month out is working inside decisions made a season earlier, which is precisely why the first conversation with a tutor should be about the entry rather than about content.

The far end of the table matters for a different reason. A November result does not land until the following January, and the November 2025 series reached students on 22 January 2026, while the June route runs to a different rhythm, with June 2026 results going to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the day after. For a UAE family that interval is when the Ministry of Education equivalency file is assembled and when any review of results or retake entry has to be decided. Always open the board's live official timetable rather than trusting a date on a tutoring site.

sections.heading: Who regulates the school that enters your child
paragraphs: Five separate authorities oversee private schools across the seven emirates, and almost none of the tutoring sites competing for these searches names more than one of them. KHDA oversees private education in Dubai and is responsible for enhancing and overseeing its quality. ADEK supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in Abu Dhabi, including Al Ain. The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in Sharjah, and Ras Al Khaimah's Department of Knowledge does the same there. The Ministry of Education plays a pivotal supervisory role for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

The distinction is not bureaucratic trivia. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so curriculum approval sits with the emirate and not only with the school. In Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from giving paid private tuition to students enrolled at their own school. A Dubai family and an Abu Dhabi family therefore face genuinely different options when someone offers evening lessons.

What a regulator does not do is mark the papers. Grading, grade boundaries and certification belong to Cambridge or Pearson, and no emirate authority adjusts them. The regulator's useful output for a family preparing for examinations is the published inspection report, which describes teaching quality subject by subject and is free to read. Treat it as a diagnostic: if a report flags attainment in science as weaker than in mathematics, that is a sensible place to put the first paid hour.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies in an exam-term week
paragraphs: Private schools in the UAE are not obliged to follow a specific national curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, and they must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations. In Dubai those subjects are mandatory in every private school regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA's requirements were to be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year. They do not pause in Year 11 because nine IGCSE papers are coming.

The detail matters for a revision timetable. KHDA calculates mandatory-subject instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit, allows schools to vary lesson length provided the total weekly time is met, and advises that any mandatory subject lesson should run at least 25 minutes. Schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs in Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because the curriculum expectations and language of instruction differ.

So when a family asks whether these periods can be dropped to free up revision time, the answer is no, and the better question is how to make them cost less. Teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic require the appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, and for the mandatory subjects the use of any different or additional content without prior Ministry permission is strictly prohibited. That rules out a tutor inventing a parallel syllabus. What a tutor can do is work on the transferable skill underneath — formal written Arabic, or structured extended writing — which pays in the mandatory subject and in a Cambridge language entry at the same time.

sections.heading: What exam-term revision hours cost in the UAE market
paragraphs: Three of the six pages ranking for these searches in October 2026 published no price at all, and the two that did quoted dollars. The table below carries AED, with the provider or survey that published each figure, so you can see where a number came from. These are market rates rather than an IB Gram price list. Our own conversation starts with an introductory lesson and an honest count of how many hours the remaining weeks allow.

Rates in this market are set mostly by what the tutor can evidence and only partly by subject. Across the published figures, budget online tuition from university students and generalist platforms runs from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour. A qualified subject tutor working online sits in the AED 150 to AED 300 range. An IGCSE, IB or A Level specialist is quoted between AED 200 and AED 450 and above. Named or examiner-branded provision reaches AED 650. Monthly packages appear too, including around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour in-home visits.

Two things are worth doing with those numbers. First, calculate the whole plan rather than the hourly rate: one weekly hour in each of three subjects for twenty weeks is sixty hours, and at mid-market rates that is a four-figure monthly commitment that deserves a plan rather than a reflex. Second, ask what the hour includes. A rate with written feedback, a marked paper and a session plan behind it is a different product from an hour of conversation, and the market prices them almost identically. Context helps here as well: KHDA confirmed in May 2026 that private school fees in Dubai would not rise for 2026-27, so tuition is one of the few education costs a family still controls.

sections.heading: A visiting tutor against live online in the last eight weeks
paragraphs: In the final stretch before a series, the format decision stops being about preference and becomes about arithmetic. A visiting tutor costs travel time that somebody pays for, in money or in a shortened session, and in Dubai or Abu Dhabi at five in the afternoon that is not a rounding error. The published in-home band of roughly AED 180 to AED 500 an hour already carries the journey inside it.

The reach argument is larger still. A family in Ajman, Al Ain or Fujairah choosing a tutor who can physically arrive is choosing from whoever lives nearby and is free at that hour. A family choosing a tutor who teaches Cambridge Chemistry 0620 Extended is choosing from everyone who teaches that code. In a tiered science eight weeks before the paper, that difference decides whether the hour is spent on the right questions at all. IB Gram delivers UAE tuition one-to-one online for exactly this reason, and home visits are part of our India service rather than something we offer here.

Online delivery also fits the thing exam preparation actually needs, which is a shared screen. Both people look at the same scanned paper, the tutor annotates it live, and the annotated version is saved and sent afterwards. Sessions can be twenty-five minutes on a day with three papers and ninety minutes on a Friday. A missed slot can be rescheduled the same week instead of forfeited, and nothing in the plan depends on traffic on Al Khail Road. The one genuine advantage of a person in the room — a reluctant student with nowhere to hide — is real, and is better solved by booking shorter, more frequent sessions than by paying for a car journey.

sections.heading: Command words, and the marks that hang on reading them properly
paragraphs: A large share of marks lost by able IGCSE candidates in the UAE has nothing to do with not knowing the content. It comes from answering a question that was not asked. Command words are the instruction at the front of the question, and each one asks for a specific shape of answer. A candidate who describes when the question says explain has written something true that earns nothing, and that pattern repeats across every subject on the timetable.

This is the cheapest improvement available in the final weeks, and it is also the most reliably ignored, because it looks like a technicality rather than learning. It is not: a mark scheme is written around the command word, and the examiner is looking for the thing it names. Two or three sessions spent sorting past-paper questions by command word, predicting the shape of the answer and then writing it, usually produces a visible change in marks before any new content is taught.

Second-language candidates, who make up a substantial part of UAE cohorts, feel this most sharply in Biology, Geography and Economics, where the difference between a describe and an explain answer is a single connective phrase. The table below is a plain-English guide rather than a reproduction of any board's glossary; the official definitions sit in the syllabus document for each subject, which the school can supply and which is worth reading once with your child rather than once alone.

sections.heading: Where a tutor stops: assessed work, practicals and past papers
paragraphs: There are tutoring businesses in this market that sell finished assessed work, and one of them advertises completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. That is academic malpractice, it puts the candidate's whole entry at risk, and it is the clearest line in this industry. A tutor teaches, reviews work the student has already done, and gives feedback the student then acts on. Assessed work stays the student's own from first draft to submission, and that boundary is stated here because it is a real difference rather than a formality.

In practice the boundary is easy to apply once named. A tutor may teach the skill a coursework task assesses, talk through a plan the student has drafted, explain why a paragraph does not answer the question, and mark a practice piece that will never be submitted. A tutor may not write, rewrite or edit-to-completion anything that goes to the board, and a tutor who offers to is telling you what kind of operation they run.

The same restraint applies to materials. Syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes and grade-boundary tables belong to Cambridge, Pearson and the other boards. We reference them and point to the official site; we do not host or supply them, because reproducing them is a copyright matter and, for unreleased material, considerably worse. Your child's school can provide the papers it is licensed to use, and the boards publish a good deal themselves. If a tutoring site offers a bundle of leaked or unreleased papers, that is a reason to close the tab.

sections.heading: Is the person teaching your child in the evening permitted to do it?
paragraphs: Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated by permit. The MoHRE private tutor work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, and the official service is listed as Issuance of a New Work Permit — Private Tutor Licensing, applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system, with no fee and a two-working-day completion time. The permit is granted free of charge for two years. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, employees in the government and private sectors, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule is published, so any site quoting you a specific figure is guessing. The permit also carries a code of conduct, and in Abu Dhabi, ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff bar paid private tutoring of students enrolled at the teacher's own school. If someone offers you your child's own classroom teacher for paid evening lessons, that is the arrangement to decline.

A separate and often confused point: an operation with premises and staff in Dubai needs a KHDA Educational Services Permit for a training institute, which involves initial approval, a maximum of six months to complete the permit and licence steps, and annual renewal requested at least thirty days before expiry. That permit belongs to centres with a building. IB Gram holds no regulator permit or accreditation, operates no UAE office or centre, and says so plainly, because the alternative — implying an approval that does not exist — is the most common and most dangerous claim in this part of the internet.

The permit is free and valid for two years; nobody should charge you for it
No published fine schedule exists, so treat any quoted figure as invented
A training-institute permit applies to premises, not to an individual teaching online

sections.heading: The five grades behind a Ministry of Education equivalency file
paragraphs: For a UAE family, IGCSE results are not only a school matter. On the British track, Ministry of Education equivalency requires proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade, together with passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3. Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects. One competing site currently tells UAE parents that six IGCSE subjects are needed; the sourced requirement is five.

That rule has a direct effect on how a Year 11 revision plan should be ordered. If five accredited subjects have to clear a floor and Arabic and Islamic Education do not count towards it, then the five candidate subjects nearest that floor are the ones a limited budget should protect first. A family spending every available hour pushing an already-strong subject from a 7 to an 8 while a different subject sits at risk of falling under the threshold has optimised the wrong number. It is a boring piece of arithmetic that nobody in this search results page does for parents.

Two cautions. The American-track requirements are different, with English proficiency shown by a score of 5 in IELTS academic, 61 in TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics by at least 450 in the SAT Math test. And no IB points figure for equivalency should be trusted from a tutoring site, including this one — the sourced article does not state one. Equivalency is also not something a tutoring service performs or can promise: describe it, check it on the Ministry's own channel, and start the file before results day rather than after.

process.title: Send the statement of entry
process.description: Before anything is booked, we ask for the board, the syllabus codes, the tier for each tiered subject and the series. If you do not have them, the exams officer does. This takes one email and it prevents the commonest waste in exam-term tutoring, which is paying for teaching aimed at the wrong specification.

process.title: A diagnostic first lesson, not a sales call
process.description: The first session is spent on a recent past paper or mock script with the student, finding where marks were available and not taken. That produces a short written list of the topics and habits costing the most, which is what any plan should be built from. Content teaching starts in session two.

process.title: Count the weeks backwards from the series
process.description: We take your child's zone timetable, the school's mock window and the forecast-grade date, and work out how many teaching hours genuinely remain per subject. That number is often smaller than families expect, and seeing it early is what makes the choice between three subjects and five an informed one rather than an optimistic one.

process.title: Weekly one-to-one online lessons
process.description: Lessons run over live video in Gulf Standard Time, with a shared screen for papers and annotations that are saved and sent afterwards. Sessions sit where the school week leaves room, and shift around mock weeks and coursework deadlines rather than competing with them.

process.title: Written feedback and a mid-term review
process.description: After each session you get a short note on what was covered and what the student should practise. Around session ten we review whether the marks are moving, and if a subject is not improving we say so and discuss changing tutor, format or plan instead of quietly continuing.

process.title: A final fortnight built on the real timetable
process.description: In the last two weeks the plan follows the zone-specific timetable: which paper is when, what is worth revising in the gaps between papers, and what is now too late to start. This is timed practice and technique, and it is the part most families leave unplanned.

whyPoints.title: The code comes before the lesson
whyPoints.description: A tutor working from Cambridge 0580 cannot prepare a Pearson 4MA1 candidate properly, and a tutor working from 0580 cannot prepare a 0606 candidate at all. We confirm the syllabus code and tier before the first session, which sounds basic and is skipped surprisingly often across this market.

whyPoints.title: Subject reach instead of driving distance
whyPoints.description: Delivering online one-to-one means a family in Fujairah or Al Ain chooses from tutors who teach their child's specification rather than from those who can reach the community by five. In a tiered science weeks before a paper, that is the difference between useful hours and pleasant ones.

whyPoints.title: AED figures with their source attached
whyPoints.description: Every rate on this page names the provider or survey that published it and the month it was read. Three of the pages ranking for these searches publish no price at all. A family deciding how to spend several thousand dirhams deserves to see where a number came from.

whyPoints.title: Administration treated as part of the job
whyPoints.description: Entry deadlines, zone timetables, access arrangements and forecast-grade dates change what preparation can achieve. We raise them in the first conversation because a family who learns about a closed window in April has lost options that an email in October would have kept open.

whyPoints.title: A stated line around assessed work
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, review and give feedback. Assessed work remains the student's own, and we do not host or supply board-owned papers and mark schemes. In a market where one operator sells finished Internal Assessments, saying this plainly is a position rather than a disclaimer.

whyPoints.title: No borrowed authority
whyPoints.description: IB Gram holds no permit, accreditation or partnership from KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, MoHRE, the Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson, and operates no UAE office. We name those bodies to explain what they do. Anyone implying their endorsement is making the most dangerous claim available on pages like this one.

faqs.question: Our daughter's school has already entered her for the next series. What is actually left for a tutor to change?
faqs.answer: The board, the syllabus code, the tier and the series are fixed by the centre, and after the entry amendment deadline the tier usually cannot move either. What preparation still changes is how many of the available marks get taken: accuracy under time pressure, whether working is shown so method marks stay available, whether command words are read correctly, and how much of the specification has been actively revised rather than reread. Across nine subjects those habits are worth more than most families expect. Ask the exams officer for the entry details in writing first, so the hours are aimed at the right papers.

faqs.question: Two schools in Dubai printed different IGCSE start times for the same paper. How is that possible?
faqs.answer: Cambridge allocates every examination centre to one of six administrative zones, and each zone has its own version of the timetable. Two centres in the same emirate can sit the same paper at different times or on different days, so a timetable taken from a search result or a parent group may be wrong for your child. Cambridge states that it is essential to use the correct version for your zone and that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an examination after the wrong one was used. Ask the exams officer for the zone-specific timetable in writing and plan the final fortnight from that document.

faqs.question: My son needs extra time in his papers. Who applies for that, and how early?
faqs.answer: The centre applies, through the exams officer, to the awarding body. A family cannot apply directly, and neither can a tutor, a doctor or an educational psychologist, however useful their report is as evidence. The arrangement has to be approved before the series, so the conversation belongs in the autumn term of Year 11 at the latest, and earlier if a formal assessment is still needed. Raising it in April after a weak mock is usually too late for that series. Ask the exams officer in writing what is already recorded for your child and what the board has approved, and keep the original assessment report.

faqs.question: If extra time is approved, does my child automatically use it well?
faqs.answer: No, and this is the part almost nobody prepares for. Most students granted additional time spend it rereading the paper rather than answering more of it, which converts a genuine adjustment into no advantage at all. The habit is trainable: timed practice with the actual arrangement in place, a plan for what to do with the extra minutes on each paper, and a rule about which questions to return to. Three or four sessions usually change the behaviour. A tutor can also keep a session-by-session record of what your child produces without time pressure, which is the kind of normal-way-of-working evidence a centre draws on.

faqs.question: The school asked for a forecast grade in February and the papers had already started. Is that the right order?
faqs.answer: Yes. Forecast grades are administrative information the centre supplies to the awarding body as part of running the series, and Cambridge sets that deadline very late in each series, close to and sometimes inside the examination period itself. That ordering is a good reminder of what the figure is for. It is not a report to parents, not a prediction you can appeal, and not something a tutor can influence directly. What shapes it is the evidence the subject teacher holds, which is why improving classwork and assessed practice is the only honest route to a different number.

faqs.question: Entries closed in November for a February series. Why is the gap so long?
faqs.answer: Awarding bodies need the entry data months ahead to produce papers, allocate centres to timetable zones, print materials and plan marking capacity. Pearson's November 2026 International GCSE papers ran to 19 November 2026 and the entries behind them were filed months earlier, while Cambridge's June entries close in the spring, roughly four months before the first paper. The practical consequence for a family is that every decision about which subjects, which tier and whether to sit at all is made before that point. A revision plan beginning a month out is working inside choices already locked, which is why the first tutoring conversation should be about the entry rather than the content.

faqs.question: Dubai schools answer to KHDA. Does the regulator have any say in how the papers are graded?
faqs.answer: No. KHDA is responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in Dubai, and the equivalent bodies are ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education for Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. None of them marks papers or sets grade boundaries; that belongs to Cambridge or Pearson. What the regulator gives you is the published inspection report, which describes teaching quality subject by subject and is free to read. Use it to decide where the first paid hour should go.

faqs.question: The timetable gives Arabic and Islamic Education several periods a week in Year 11. Can my child drop them to revise?
faqs.answer: No. Private schools in the UAE must provide Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies alongside their licensed international curriculum, and in Dubai those subjects are mandatory in every private school whatever curriculum it teaches. KHDA calculates the instructional time on a 40-minute lesson unit and advises that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes. The better question is how to make those periods cost less. Work on the transferable skill underneath, such as formal written Arabic or structured extended writing, and it pays in the mandatory subject and in any Cambridge language entry at the same time.

faqs.question: What does the UAE Ministry of Education want to see from an IGCSE candidate heading to a local university?
faqs.answer: On the British track the published requirement is passes in five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at no less than grade E or grade 3, plus one accredited subject at Advanced Level at no less than grade E or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five. One ranking tutoring site tells UAE parents six subjects are needed, which is wrong. Verify the current rule on the Ministry's own channel, and treat equivalency as something you prepare for rather than something a tutoring service performs for you.

faqs.question: Rates jumped when we started asking about revision help in January. Is that normal in this market?
faqs.answer: Demand concentrates in the weeks before a series, and availability for the better-evidenced tutors shrinks rather than their rate card changing. Published figures as at October 2026 run from roughly AED 45 to AED 150 an hour for budget online tuition, AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 200 to AED 450 and above for an IGCSE or A Level specialist, and AED 650 at the named-provider end. Those are other providers' published rates, not ours. Booking in the autumn secures a specialist at the ordinary rate; booking in April buys whoever is still free.

faqs.question: Is it worth paying a premium for a tutor described as an examiner?
faqs.answer: Only if the claim can be evidenced, and only for what it genuinely provides. Examiner experience can mean a sharper sense of how mark schemes reward answers, which is useful. It does not mean access to papers, boundaries or marking decisions, and anyone implying otherwise is describing something that does not exist. Ask which board, which subject, which component and in which years, and ask what the premium changes about the lesson. One published figure in this market reaches AED 650 an hour for named provision. Compare that against an evidenced specialist at AED 270 before deciding what the label is worth.

faqs.question: Ramadan falls between the mocks and the papers this year. What do UAE families usually do with the schedule?
faqs.answer: School days shorten, energy patterns change, and the examination series does not move for any of it, so the schedule has to. The arrangements that work tend to be shorter and more frequent rather than longer: forty minutes of timed questions after Iftar rather than ninety minutes in the afternoon, with the heaviest content work shifted into the weeks before and after. Eid holidays remove teaching days entirely, so count them out of the plan rather than discovering them. Online delivery helps here because a session can be moved to the hour that actually works that week instead of a fixed visit.

faqs.question: My daughter writes long, careful answers and still loses marks. What is going wrong?
faqs.answer: Most often she is answering a question that was not asked. Each command word asks for a specific shape of answer, and the mark scheme is written around it. A describe answer where the question said explain can be entirely true and score nothing, and the habit repeats across every subject. The fix is cheap and fast: sort past-paper questions by command word, predict the shape of the answer, then write it under time. Two or three sessions usually move marks before any new content is taught, and the official definitions sit in each subject's syllabus document, which the school can supply.

faqs.question: The coursework has already gone to the board. Can a tutor still help with the externally marked parts?
faqs.answer: Yes, and that is the normal arrangement. Once assessed work is submitted it is closed, and no tutor should be touching it in any case. What remains is the written papers, which in most subjects carry the larger share of the grade. The work is paper technique, timed practice, and the specific topics the mock script shows are weak. A tutor may teach the skills a coursework task assessed, mark practice pieces that will never be submitted, and explain why an answer missed the question. Producing or editing-to-completion anything that goes to the board is malpractice, not help.

faqs.question: How can I check that the person teaching my child in the evenings is permitted to do it?
faqs.answer: Ask whether they hold the MoHRE private tutor work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023 and applied for through the MoHRE smart app, website and e-services system. It is granted free of charge for two years, so nobody should be charging you for it, and eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and school students aged 15 to 18. Those tutoring without a permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws, though no fine schedule is published, so treat any quoted amount as invented.

faqs.question: A teacher at our son's own school in Abu Dhabi has offered paid evening lessons. Is that allowed?
faqs.answer: Decline it. ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the MoHRE private tuition permit carries a code of conduct that also bars serving students affiliated with the teacher's own school. Beyond the rule, the arrangement puts your child in an awkward position with the person who marks their classwork and contributes to a forecast grade. An independent tutor who does not teach at the school has no such conflict, and in Abu Dhabi that is the ordinary route rather than the fallback.

faqs.question: Does the school's inspection rating tell me anything useful about my child's chances in a particular subject?
faqs.answer: The headline band tells you little on its own, but the body of the report often does. Inspection reports describe attainment and progress subject by subject, and a report that praises mathematics while flagging science attainment is pointing at where a cohort is likely to be underprepared. Read it alongside your child's own marks: if both agree, that subject earns the first paid hour. The report is published by the emirate's authority and costs nothing to read. It is a diagnostic rather than a verdict, and it says nothing about how the board will mark an individual script.

faqs.question: We are moving from Sharjah to Abu Dhabi in January. Does the examination entry move with us?
faqs.answer: Not automatically, and this is worth raising with both schools immediately rather than in the new term. Entries are made by a centre, so a mid-year move raises whether the original centre keeps the entry, whether the new one can accept a transfer, and whether the subject and tier are even offered there. Timetable zones may differ as well. The regulators change too, from SPEA to ADEK, which affects school-level matters rather than the board's. Ask both exams officers in writing what happens to each subject, and get the answer before the series entry deadline rather than after.

faqs.question: The first paper is six weeks away and nothing has been arranged. Is starting now a waste of money?
faqs.answer: It is late for new content and not late for marks. Six weeks will not cover an unlearned specification, and any tutor who says otherwise is selling. What six weeks does cover is a diagnosis on a recent paper, the three or four topics producing the biggest losses, and the technique problems costing marks everywhere at once. That is often a meaningful number of marks across several subjects. The honest version of this plan includes a written list of what is not being covered, so the decision to start is made with the limits visible rather than discovered in the exam hall.

igcse-exam-preparation.closingHeading: Start with the entry, then book the hours
igcse-exam-preparation.closingBody: If you are arranging IGCSE exam preparation in the UAE, the first step costs nothing: email your child's exams officer and ask for the board, the syllabus code, the tier and the zone timetable for every subject. Bring those to an introductory lesson and we will put a real number on how many teaching hours the remaining weeks allow, which subjects deserve them, and what is now too late to begin. Lessons run one-to-one online over live video in Gulf Standard Time. If no specialist is free for a particular code at the hour you need, we will tell you that instead of filling the slot.

igcse-february-march-exam-preparation.tutorsIntro: The tutors below cover Cambridge IGCSE and Pearson Edexcel International GCSE at Core and Extended tier. intro.heading: The February series is India-only, and what that means here
paragraphs: Cambridge International offers its February-March series to India only. A UAE exam centre cannot enter your child for it, which means a February paper window found through a search engine is almost always another country's timetable being read by a UAE parent. What Cambridge runs here is a June series and a November series, alongside Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October that are not IGCSE at all and carry none of its weight. The useful thing to take from that is not the disappointment but the timing: the decision that puts a child into any exam hall is taken months earlier, in the middle of a term, by an adult who is not you.

The series is a centre-level decision. Cambridge allocates every exam centre to one of six administrative zones and publishes a separate timetable for each zone. Its exams officers' guide is blunt about the consequence: it is essential that a centre uses the correct version of the timetable for its zone, and Cambridge cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after the wrong version has been used. Which series a school enters a child for, and which subjects it opens inside that series, is set by the centre and its exams officer. A parent cannot enter a child for a Cambridge series independently by filling in a form on a website, and no form anywhere will open an India-only series to a UAE candidate.

Behind the school sits an emirate regulator, and in the UAE that is not one body but five. Dubai's private schools answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. Sharjah has the Sharjah Private Education Authority, Ras Al Khaimah its Department of Knowledge, and the federal Ministry of Education supervises private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. In Sharjah and Ras Al Khaimah the authority also approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, which places exam arrangements inside a licensing conversation rather than a purely commercial one.

Pearson Edexcel works to a different pattern. Pearson's International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026. There is no February-March International GCSE series. If your child's school teaches 4MA1 rather than Cambridge IGCSE 0580 maths, a February question has an even shorter answer: neither board offers a February sitting to a UAE candidate, so the real choice is May/June or November. Plenty of UAE schools run both boards across different subjects inside one building, which is why the honest answer differs subject by subject and has to be checked with the exams officer rather than assumed.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform, not a school and not an exam centre. Lessons for UAE families are delivered one-to-one over live video: screen-shared past paper work, a shared whiteboard, a recording the student can replay the following week. Home visits are a service we offer only in India, and nobody is sent to a UAE address. For a February entry that is a practical gain rather than a compromise. A child sitting Cambridge Physics 0625 Paper 4 in the first week of February needs someone who has taught that paper repeatedly, not whoever happens to live within a twenty-minute drive of the villa.

What follows maps the series a UAE candidate can actually sit against the system a UAE parent has to work inside: who controls the entry, what each regulator governs, where the mandatory UAE subjects sit while papers are running, how Ramadan reshapes a revision week, what the market charges in dirhams, what the Ministry of Education will later count towards equivalency, and what a tutor may and may not do with a piece of assessed work three weeks before it is due.

Pearson Edexcel International GCSE runs May/June and November only - no February-March series exists
