sections.heading: Five subjects at grade 3 or E: what the equivalency file changes about the budget
paragraphs: The Ministry of Education equivalency file is where IGCSE spending decisions and UAE university access meet, and almost no competitor page mentions it. On the British track, reporting in July 2026 set out that students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates at a grade no less than E or grade 3, alongside one accredited subject at Advanced Level at grade E or better, or two at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade.

The detail that changes a budget is what is excluded. Arabic and Islamic education are not counted among the five required subjects. A family buying weekly Arabic tuition in the belief that it strengthens the equivalency count is spending in a place the count does not look, and the same money moved to a tiered science or to Mathematics 0580 would be working on a subject that does count. One page currently ranking in this market states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects; the sourced figure is five.

Two cautions belong with that. The first is that this is a regulatory process that changes, and it should be verified on moe.gov.ae or with the attestation authority in your emirate before any plan is built on it; this page describes it and points you there rather than performing it. The second is that no amount of tutoring is required for equivalency, and any provider implying otherwise is manufacturing urgency around a government procedure. There is no published IB points threshold we can verify, so this page prints none.

sections.heading: Ramadan, Eid and paying for weeks that are not teaching weeks
paragraphs: The UAE academic year does not deliver four identical teaching weeks a month, and a tutoring budget built as though it does leaks money. Ramadan shortens the school day. Eid removes a week. Mock fortnights fill the evenings a student would otherwise revise in. A June Cambridge series or a late-October Pearson series sits at a fixed distance from all of that, and the revision has to fit around it rather than the other way round.

Handled well, this is a scheduling question rather than a cost increase. During Ramadan, sessions move to post-Iftar slots, which for many families produce better concentration than a 5pm session on a shortened school day ever did. Across Eid, the sensible move is to pause rather than compress, then resume with the same tutor in the same slot. In a mock fortnight, the single most valuable hour is spent marking the mock paper that has just come back, because it is the most recent evidence anyone has.

The practical rule is to count teaching weeks before agreeing a block, and to put the count in writing. A twelve-week term containing Eid and a mock fortnight is not twelve sessions. A family that books ten and keeps two in reserve for the week a paper comes back marked will spend less and get more than a family that bought twelve and lost three to the calendar. This is also the honest answer to whether rates rise before a series: demand firms up, so the slot is worth booking early.

sections.heading: What a tutor may not sell you, at any price
paragraphs: Some of what is for sale in this market should not be bought. There are providers advertising finished coursework and completed assessed pieces to IGCSE and Diploma students in the Gulf, priced in the thousands of dirhams. What a family is buying there is a malpractice risk attached to their child's name, and the exposure sits with the candidate, not the seller. A board that identifies work which is not the student's own can withdraw a grade and, in the IB's case, a whole certificate.

The line a legitimate tutor works inside is clear enough to put in writing. A tutor may teach the content, explain what a criterion is asking for, model the technique on a different question, and give feedback on a draft the student produced. A tutor may not supply text that ends up in a portfolio, may not hand over a finished piece, and may not sit alongside a controlled assessment. Where a school's deadline is on Friday, the answer is feedback on Wednesday on what the student has written, not a replacement.

Two related claims belong in the same bin. A provider describing its tutors as approved by a regulator or a board is describing something that does not exist for individual tutors: KHDA's educational services permit is issued to training institutes with premises, and the MoHRE permit is a work authorisation, not a quality mark. And a tutor described as an examiner should be able to evidence it, because examiner status is often used to imply access to marking standards and boundaries that no individual can offer.

Ask for evidence behind any examiner claim, and discount it if none arrives

sections.heading: Six paid hours in: what you should be able to see
paragraphs: The weakest part of most tutoring arrangements is that nobody agreed what success would look like. Six hours is enough to answer the question if the evidence was specified in advance. What a parent should have after six sessions is not a feeling that things are better. It is a marked past paper with the marks attributed by question, a comparison against an earlier paper of the same type, and a short written list of what is still losing marks.

Three signals say the money is working. Marks are recovering in the band the diagnostic identified, not in general. The student can say what a command term is asking for and show the difference between a describe answer and an explain answer on their own script. And the tutor's notes are specific enough that you could hand them to a different teacher and they would know where to start. If all three are present after six hours, extend the block. If none are, change something before buying twelve more.

The reverse is worth saying too. If a subject was triaged in and turns out not to need paid hours, stop paying for it. Dropping a subject from the plan after four weeks is a sign the triage worked, not that the money was wasted. The point of starting with one diagnostic block in one subject, rather than four weekly slots across four, is that it keeps every decision reversible while the evidence is still cheap to collect.

process.title: Say which codes, not which subjects
process.description: Send the statement of entry or the last report with the syllabus codes on it: 0580 or 0607, 0620 or 4CH1, Core or Extended. A code tells us which specialist to look for and which past papers to mark. A subject name tells us almost nothing, and is how families end up paying for the wrong assessment.

process.title: Triage before you buy
process.description: We go through the timetable subject by subject and separate content gaps from technique losses from subjects that only need practice. The output is a short list of which one or two subjects repay paid hours this term, which is usually fewer than the family arrived expecting.

process.title: A trial lesson on the real material
process.description: One lesson with the matched tutor, using your child's own marked work rather than a generic assessment, before any block is confirmed. It exists so you can judge the match on evidence. If the fit is wrong, we match again rather than asking you to make it work.

process.title: Book the block in teaching weeks
process.description: Sessions are scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school day, the commute and Ramadan timings, and the block is counted in teaching weeks rather than calendar months so Eid and mock fortnights do not quietly absorb sessions you have paid for.

process.title: Review on marked papers at six hours
process.description: At the six-hour mark we look at a marked paper against an earlier one of the same type, with the marks attributed by question. That conversation ends in one of three decisions: extend the block, change the focus, or stop paying for this subject because it no longer needs the hours.

whyPoints.title: The rates are on the page, with sources
whyPoints.description: Three of six competitor pages measured in October 2026 publish no price at all, and the two that do quote US dollars. Every AED band here carries where it came from and the month it was read, so a quote you receive can be compared against something rather than taken on trust.

whyPoints.title: Matched on the syllabus code
whyPoints.description: Mathematics 0580 and International Mathematics 0607 are different courses with different papers, and Cambridge and Pearson sciences are not interchangeable. Tutors are matched to the code on the statement of entry, which removes the single most common source of wasted IGCSE tutoring hours.

whyPoints.title: Online delivery stated, not implied
whyPoints.description: Lessons for UAE families are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time. Visiting tutors are a service IB Gram offers only in India. You know which product you are buying before you book, rather than discovering the delivery model after a deposit has moved.

whyPoints.title: Reach beyond the driving radius
whyPoints.description: A family in Fujairah, Umm Al Quwain or Al Ain choosing an in-home tutor is choosing from whoever will travel. Teaching over video replaces that constraint with a subject constraint, which is how an Extended-tier Chemistry or a 0478 Computer Science specialist becomes reachable at all.

whyPoints.title: Fewer paid subjects, chosen deliberately
whyPoints.description: A Year 11 timetable carries eight to ten qualifications, and tutoring all the weak ones is how a budget disappears. Triage puts the hours where the gap is widest and the cause is fixable, and takes subjects off the plan when the evidence says they do not need paying for.

whyPoints.title: The honesty line in writing
whyPoints.description: Tutors teach, explain criteria, model technique and give feedback on work the student has produced. Nobody supplies text for a portfolio or hands over a finished piece. That is a boundary worth stating plainly in a market where completed assessed work is openly advertised.

faqs.question: We have been quoted AED 180 and AED 450 for the same IGCSE subject. Which quote is right?
faqs.answer: Both can be legitimate, because they are usually selling different things. Read in October 2026, the UAE market advertises AED 150 to AED 300 for a qualified subject tutor working online and AED 180 to AED 500 for a visiting tutor with travel inside the fee. Ask three questions before deciding: is the rate per 60 minutes or per 45-minute period, which syllabus code does the tutor actually teach, and is travel being billed. A higher figure is only better value if it buys a specialist in the exact code on your child's statement of entry.

faqs.question: My son takes nine IGCSE subjects. How many should we actually pay for tuition in?
faqs.answer: Usually one or two at a time, not four. A Diploma student has six subjects, so tutoring every weak one is at least arithmetically possible. A nine-subject Year 11 timetable is not: weekly hours in four subjects at market rates passes AED 3,000 a month. Triage each subject by what is holding the grade there. Content gaps need a block. Command-term register needs a handful of hours. Volume of practice needs time, not money. Most families find two subjects genuinely need paid support and the rest need past papers and a quiet evening.

faqs.question: Does a grade 4 to grade 6 move cost the same as a grade 7 to grade 9 move?
faqs.answer: No, and the difference is large. A 4 to a 6 is mostly about recovering marks the student is already close to earning: method marks, diagram labels, answering describe when the question says describe. Those are dense on the paper and respond quickly. A 7 to a 9 competes for the discriminating marks at the top, which are few and much less responsive to a weekly hour. If one subject is funded, put the money where the gap is widest and the cause is technique, not where the child is already strong.

faqs.question: Is the quoted IGCSE rate per 60-minute hour or per school period?
faqs.answer: Always ask, in writing, because a 45-minute period billed as an hour raises the real rate by about a third without changing the headline figure. Market comparisons across the UAE are published per hour, so a per-period quote is not comparable to them until you convert it. The same applies to any package: ask how long a session is, how many sessions the month contains, and how many of those weeks are actually teaching weeks once Eid, half-term and the mock fortnight are taken out.

faqs.question: Should we pay for Arabic tuition to strengthen the Ministry of Education equivalency file?
faqs.answer: Not for that reason. Reporting in July 2026 on the UAE equivalency requirements stated that Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects the file counts. If Arabic needs support for its own sake, that is a separate decision, and the mandatory stream is in any case taught and assessed inside your school fee under KHDA's requirements. Money moved from Arabic to Mathematics 0580 or a tiered science is working on a subject the count actually looks at. Verify the current rules on moe.gov.ae before planning around them.

faqs.question: Our daughter is on the Core tier in Maths. Is paying for Extended-level tuition wasted money?
faqs.answer: It is misaimed while the entry stands, because the Core papers award a restricted upper grade range however well she is taught. The useful spend is on the tier conversation itself: bring a marked past paper to the school before the centre's final entry deadline and ask what evidence would support an Extended entry. A UAE candidate sits Cambridge IGCSE in June or November, and the centre's final entry closes months before the papers - in the spring for a June sitting - so this is a Year 10 and early Year 11 decision rather than something to raise in the spring of Year 11. Once the entry closes, tutoring should target the papers she is actually sitting.

faqs.question: How much is the IGCSE exam entry itself, and who sets that figure?
faqs.answer: Entry fees are set and billed by the exam centre rather than published as a single national figure, so any page quoting you one number is guessing. A school normally bills entries with term fees. A private candidate pays the centre's own published candidate fee, which varies by centre and by subject. Ask your child's exams officer for the per-subject figure in writing before deciding how many subjects to enter, and treat it as a separate budget line from tutoring. No tutor should be charging an entry fee on your behalf.

faqs.question: Is small-group IGCSE tuition genuinely better value than one-to-one?
faqs.answer: It can be, on one condition: the students are on the same board, the same syllabus code and the same tier, and are losing marks in roughly the same place. Two Extended 0580 candidates both forfeiting method marks will learn well together. A Core candidate and an Extended candidate in the same hour means one of them is in the wrong lesson. Watch the pricing too: a group rate should be per student and visibly below the one-to-one rate, and a group session priced at the individual rate is simply a higher margin.

faqs.question: Does the hourly rate for IGCSE support rise as the exam series gets closer?
faqs.answer: Demand firms up, and so do slots. In the eight to twelve weeks before a series, the evenings a Year 11 student can use are contested, and the specialists in scarce codes fill up first. The practical answer is not to hunt a discount in February but to reserve the slot in autumn, when the same tutor and the same hour are available and the cheapest teaching weeks of the whole course are still ahead. A family that books the slot early is buying availability as much as a rate.

faqs.question: Should a provider charge us for IGCSE past papers and mark schemes?
faqs.answer: No. Board syllabuses, past papers, mark schemes, grade-boundary tables and subject guides are copyright material belonging to Cambridge and Pearson, and a provider should be pointing you to the official site rather than selling a resource pack. What you are legitimately paying for is the teaching around that material: a paper marked against the published scheme with the losses attributed by question. If a resource charge appears on an invoice, ask what it covers and where the material came from.

faqs.question: The private tuition permit is free, so why does a permitted tutor charge more?
faqs.answer: Because the permit is a legal authorisation, not a quality mark. The UAE private tuition work permit was introduced under Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and MoHRE's own service page lists no fee and a two-working-day completion time. Eligible applicants include registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed residents, university students and students aged 15 to 18. So a rate difference reflects subject expertise and experience, never permit cost, and no permit or licensing line belongs on your invoice.

faqs.question: We have eight weeks before the first paper. What is a sensible amount to spend now?
faqs.answer: Enough for one subject, properly, rather than a little for three. Eight weeks supports a weekly session plus a full past paper in the subject where marks are most recoverable, which is usually the one losing method marks or command-term register rather than the one with a content hole from Year 10. Spend the first session on a marked paper so the remaining seven have a target. Spreading the same budget across three subjects in eight weeks generally produces three sets of notes and no measurable change on any paper.

faqs.question: Does a Pearson Edexcel entry spread the cost more evenly than Cambridge?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, and it is worth checking against the specification. Pearson examines International GCSE in May/June and November each year, and some qualifications allow units to be sat across more than one series rather than all at once, which spreads the exam risk and the tutoring spend. Cambridge runs a June series and a November series for UAE candidates, each a complete set of papers, so support tends to concentrate into one block, with November standing as the resit route if a June grade falls short of what a sixth form asked for. Neither is better; they just ask for money at different times. Your school has usually already chosen the board.

faqs.question: If we pay for a term and the match turns out to be wrong, what happens?
faqs.answer: That is a question to settle before any money moves, in writing. Ask what happens to unused sessions, whether a rematch costs anything, and how many sessions' notice a change needs. The trial lesson exists so the match is tested on your child's own marked work first, which is cheaper than finding out in week five. Treat any provider that will not put the rematch terms in writing as a risk, and be cautious of outcome-linked refund offers, since no tutor controls grade boundaries or the paper itself.

faqs.question: Does IB Gram send an IGCSE tutor to our address anywhere in the Emirates?
faqs.answer: No. For families in the UAE, IGCSE teaching is delivered one-to-one over live video, scheduled in Gulf Standard Time around the school day, the commute and Ramadan timings. Visiting tutors are a service IB Gram offers only in India. The reason is the size of the pool: outside Dubai, the in-home market cannot staff syllabuses such as Computer Science 0478 or International Mathematics 0607 at any travel rate, while a video lesson is matched on the code rather than on the postcode.

faqs.question: How do we tell after a month whether the tutoring is worth the money?
faqs.answer: Agree the evidence before the first paid hour. After about six sessions you should have a past paper marked against the published scheme with the marks attributed by question, a comparison against an earlier paper of the same type, and a written list of what is still losing marks. Your child should also be able to show, on their own script, the difference between a describe answer and an explain answer. If those are present, extend the block. If none are, change the focus or the tutor before buying another twelve hours.

igcse-home-tutors.closingHeading: Start with the arithmetic, then book one subject
igcse-home-tutors.closingBody: The useful next step is not a bigger budget. It is a shorter list. Send the statement of entry or the last report with the syllabus codes on it, and we will go through the timetable subject by subject and say which one or two genuinely repay paid hours this term and which need past papers and a quiet evening. A trial lesson on your child's own marked work comes before any block is confirmed, so the match is judged on evidence rather than on a profile. Lessons are one-to-one over live video, timed to Gulf Standard Time, anywhere in the Emirates.

igcse-may-june-exam-preparation.tutorsIntro: The tutors below are matched to a named syllabus and a named series, not to a subject in general. A Cambridge IGCSE 0580 Extended candidate sitting Papers 2 and 4 needs a different run-in from a Pearson Edexcel 4MA1 candidate on a modular route, and the match reflects which one your child is actually entered for.

intro.heading: What is already fixed by the time January arrives
paragraphs: Most UAE families meet the May/June series as a date on a school letter. By the time that letter reaches you, three decisions have been taken without you. The examination board has published the series and its timetable. The school, as a registered centre, has submitted final entries, which closes the subject list and in most syllabuses the Core and Extended tier. And the emirate regulator has approved a school calendar that determines how many teaching weeks sit between the mock papers and the first real one. None of those three can be reopened by a parent in February.

What remains open is larger than most families assume, and it is the reason this page exists. The weeks from January to the first paper are almost entirely a household decision. Schools in Year 11 move from new content to revision programmes and then to study leave, at which point the timetabled teaching stops and the student is working at home. Who checks that work, how often, and against which mark scheme, is nobody's statutory responsibility. That is the gap one-to-one online lessons are built to fill, and it is a different job from classroom teaching.

The regulatory picture matters because UAE parents are working inside two systems at once. Private schools in Dubai answer to the Knowledge and Human Development Authority, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain answer to the Department of Education and Knowledge, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah answers to the Sharjah Private Education Authority and Ras Al Khaimah to its Department of Knowledge, both of which approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah sit with the federal Ministry of Education.

What none of those bodies controls is the examination itself. Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level in a June series and a November series. Pearson Edexcel runs International GCSE in May/June and November. The board sets the window, issues the zone timetable, marks the scripts and releases the grades. Pearson sent its June 2026 results to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026. A regulator can inspect the school that enters your child. It does not move a paper.

IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform, not a school and not a licensed training institute. We do not hold KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson approval, and nothing on this page should be read as implying one. Tutoring for UAE families is delivered online, one-to-one, over live video. We do not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. For the May/June series that is usually the stronger arrangement anyway, and the comparison further down this page shows why.

Mock season in January and February is usually the last block of genuinely new teaching
Study leave removes timetabled lessons at exactly the point revision intensity peaks

igcse-may-june-exam-preparation.programmesIntro: Four qualification routes meet in a UAE Year 11 classroom, and the May/June series means something different on each. Below is what each one commits a candidate to, and the specific wrinkle UAE families hit with it. Your child's statement of entry, not the school prospectus, is the document that tells you which route they are actually on.

programmes.name: Cambridge IGCSE
programmes.description: Cambridge International runs IGCSE and O Level exams in a June series and a November series, with Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October. Most subjects are tiered: a Core entry and an Extended entry sit different papers from the same syllabus document. Cambridge also allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states that it is essential to use the correct version of the timetable for your zone, adding that it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after working from the wrong one.
programmes.countryNote: The June series is the one almost every UK-curriculum school in the UAE sits, and UK curriculum accounted for 37 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25. Zone allocation is a live issue here: two UAE schools can print different start times for the same paper and both be correct. Before any revision plan is written, check which zone timetable version your child's centre is working from, because it changes exam-morning planning and nothing else can fix a missed paper.

programmes.name: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE
programmes.description: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE exams are available in May/June and November each year. Some subjects run on a modular route, where units are sat across more than one series and the final grade is aggregated, and others are linear. Pearson publishes a provisional timetable before each May/June and November series and then revises it, which is why the live PDF on qualifications.pearson.com is the only version worth planning around and why any date reprinted elsewhere should be treated as out of date. Syllabus codes begin with a number, as in 4MA1 for Mathematics A.
programmes.countryNote: A modular entry changes what May/June means for a UAE family entirely. A student may already hold a banked unit result from November and be sitting only the remaining papers in the summer, which makes a generic full-syllabus revision programme largely wasted money. Pearson's published dates give UAE parents something to plan against: June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026, and the November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026.

programmes.name: IB Middle Years Programme, Years 4-5
programmes.description: The Middle Years Programme is the route a UAE family chooses instead of IGCSE when the school is an IB World School through to Year 11. It is assessed on criterion-referenced internal work and, where a school opts in, on eAssessment, rather than on a board-set paper series in May and June. Students finish it at the same age as an IGCSE cohort and move into the same Year 12 options, which is why the two routes end up being compared directly by parents choosing a school.
programmes.countryNote: International Baccalaureate programmes accounted for 7 per cent of Dubai private-school enrolment in 2024-25, and three of the seven new private schools opening for Dubai's 2026-27 intake are IB. Families who move a child from an MYP school to an IGCSE school mid-cycle meet the harder version of this: an MYP Year 4 report says very little about readiness for a tiered Extended paper, so the first task is a timed past paper rather than a conversation about predicted grades.

programmes.name: International AS and A Level
programmes.description: The qualification a May/June IGCSE grade usually feeds into. International AS and A Level are the British-track continuation most UAE schools offer alongside or instead of the IB Diploma, and sixth-form entry conditions are written in IGCSE grades, typically a minimum grade in the subject itself plus a profile across the five or more subjects a student has passed. The Ministry of Education's equivalency rules for the British track also reach up into this level, not just the IGCSE year.
programmes.countryNote: This is where the five-subject rule bites. Gulf Today's report on the UAE's clarified equivalency requirements states that British-track students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must also submit proof of one accredited subject at Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at Advanced Subsidiary Level at the same grade. A thin IGCSE profile in June becomes an equivalency problem two years later.

igcse-may-june-exam-preparation.subjectsIntro: These are the subjects UAE families ask for most often in the January-to-June run-in, with the syllabus code where it is useful. The code matters more than the subject name: a tutor working from the wrong specification can teach a topic competently and still leave a student unprepared for the paper they are entered for.

subjects.name: Mathematics (Cambridge IGCSE 0580)
subjects.description: The highest-volume request in the UAE and the one where tier confusion does the most damage. Extended candidates sit a different paper set from Core candidates on the same syllabus, so the past papers a student practises on have to match the entry. Marks are most often lost on method presentation in multi-step questions and on the non-calculator paper's arithmetic under time pressure.

subjects.name: Mathematics A (Pearson Edexcel 4MA1)
subjects.description: The Edexcel equivalent, with its own paper structure and its own command vocabulary. UAE schools sometimes run 4MA1 for one cohort and Cambridge 0580 for another in the same building, which is why the first question in any maths run-in is the code on the statement of entry rather than the year group.

subjects.name: Physics (Cambridge IGCSE 0625)
subjects.description: Electricity and circuits, and the alternative-to-practical component, are where UAE candidates most often lose marks. The practical paper rewards experimental reasoning rather than recall, which is hard to build from notes alone and responds well to timed question work with a tutor watching the written answer form.

subjects.name: Chemistry (Cambridge IGCSE 0620)
subjects.description: Mole calculations, electrolysis and organic chemistry carry the heaviest mark concentration in the final weeks. Chemistry also rewards precise definitions: a correct idea written in loose language collects part marks when the mark scheme wanted a specific term, and that is a fixable habit in six to eight sessions.

subjects.name: Biology (Cambridge IGCSE 0610)
subjects.description: A content-heavy syllabus where the failure mode is recall without application. Candidates who can name a process lose marks explaining it in an unfamiliar context. Extended candidates also face data-handling questions that look like maths and are marked like biology, which is a specific skill to practise.

subjects.name: English as a Second Language (Cambridge IGCSE 0510 and 0511)
subjects.levels: Core and Extended, with and without coursework
subjects.description: Reading comprehension and the writing tasks are where the grade moves. The listening component punishes students who have practised only on written material. For many UAE students this is also the grade that carries most weight in an equivalency file, because English proficiency is assessed separately on other tracks.

subjects.name: English First Language (Cambridge IGCSE 0500)
subjects.description: Directed writing and the response to a reading passage reward structure over vocabulary. Students who write a great deal often score below students who answer the actual question asked, and the quickest gain in the final term is usually in planning discipline rather than in style.

subjects.name: Economics (Cambridge IGCSE 0455)
subjects.description: Diagram accuracy and command-word discipline decide the grade. An answer that explains when the paper asked for an evaluation is capped, no matter how well written. This is a subject where a handful of marked past-paper answers moves more than a term of re-reading the textbook.

subjects.name: Business Studies (Cambridge IGCSE 0450)
subjects.description: Case-study application is the whole assessment. Candidates who answer from general business knowledge rather than from the stimulus material in front of them lose application and analysis marks consistently, which is diagnosable in one session with a past paper and a mark scheme.

subjects.name: Computer Science (Cambridge IGCSE 0478)
subjects.description: The written paper on theory and the pre-release material for the programming component need different preparation and different weeks. UAE candidates often arrive strong on code and weak on the theory paper, or the reverse, and the run-in should be weighted to whichever half is actually behind.

subjects.name: Geography (Cambridge IGCSE 0460)
subjects.description: Case-study specificity is the differentiator. A named example with figures earns credit where a generic description does not, and UAE students frequently have fewer locally taught case studies to draw on than the mark scheme assumes. Building a small, reusable bank of named examples is the efficient fix.

subjects.name: Arabic as a first and additional language
subjects.description: Two different things that parents routinely conflate. The KHDA mandatory subjects requirement is a school obligation; an Arabic IGCSE entry is a board examination. A student can be doing one, both or neither, and the tutoring brief differs entirely depending on which.

igcse-may-june-exam-preparation.regionsTitle: The May/June series, emirate by emirate
igcse-may-june-exam-preparation.regionsIntro: The series is federal in effect but the school system around it is not. Each emirate has its own regulator, its own approved calendars and its own density of examination centres, and all three change what a May/June run-in looks like in practice. Ras Al Khaimah, Fujairah and Umm Al Quwain are named by almost nobody writing about UAE tutoring, which is odd, because families there have the least local choice.

regions.name: Dubai
regions.note: 227 private schools and 387,441 students in 2024-25 across 17 curricula, regulated by KHDA, with UK curriculum at 37 per cent of enrolment. The practical consequence for a May/June candidate is choice: multiple centres, multiple zone timetable versions in the same city, and a crowded evening tutoring market where published rates vary by a factor of ten.

regions.name: Abu Dhabi
regions.note: Regulated by ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools in the emirate. ADEK is named by none of the competitor pages researched for this project. Abu Dhabi's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported to bar teachers from paid private tutoring of students enrolled at their own school, which matters when an evening offer arrives from inside the school.

regions.name: Al Ain
regions.note: Also under ADEK, with a smaller and more spread-out school network. Distances between communities make a visiting tutor expensive in travel time and make scheduling fragile in the exam term, when a cancelled visit cannot be rebuilt into the week. This is the clearest case in the country for keeping the hour and dropping the drive.

regions.name: Sharjah
regions.note: The Sharjah Private Education Authority regulates private education in the emirate and approves tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. That is a wider remit than inspection alone. Many Sharjah families also commute into Dubai for school, which means the May/June study-leave weeks are the first time in two years the commute stops.

regions.name: Ajman
regions.note: The Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, alongside Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Fewer local IGCSE centres means a narrower choice of subjects taught to Extended tier, and families more often discover late that a desired subject is being entered at Core.

regions.name: Ras Al Khaimah
regions.note: Regulated by the Department of Knowledge, which, like Sharjah's authority, approves fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods. The emirate has a thin specialist tutoring market, so the January-to-June question is usually not which local tutor to choose but whether a specialist for a particular paper exists within driving distance at all.

regions.name: Fujairah
regions.note: Under federal Ministry of Education supervision, on the east coast and across the mountains from the main school corridor. A specialist in Edexcel modular Physics is not going to be a short drive away. Live online is not a compromise here; it is the only way most Fujairah families reach a subject specialist for a named paper.

regions.name: Umm Al Quwain
regions.note: Also supervised by the federal Ministry of Education, and the smallest private-school market in the country. Families here routinely enrol children in Sharjah or Ajman schools, which puts the exam centre in one emirate and home in another, and makes early-evening sessions after a long school run the realistic slot rather than late afternoon.

schoolClusters.note: Dubai's UK-curriculum schools run the largest May/June IGCSE cohorts in the country, and Dubai's 2026-27 intake adds seven new private schools, four of them UK curriculum, creating 16,846 new places. Students we support attend schools across this cluster; the point of listing them is that each one sets its own mock window, coursework deadlines and study-leave date, and a revision plan has to be built against the school's calendar rather than a generic one.

ADEK-regulated schools, with cohorts spread across Khalifa City, Al Raha, Saadiyat and the Al Ain communities. Travel times between these areas are the reason a 4pm visiting session rarely survives the exam term intact. Families we work with in this cluster typically hold two fixed online slots a week and add a third in the fortnight before a named paper.

SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, and the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. Subject coverage at Extended tier is thinner here than in Dubai, so the gap a tutor is asked to close is more often a whole topic the school did not teach in depth than a technique the student has not practised.

igcse-may-june-exam-preparation.schoolDisclaimer: Named schools are listed as context for the school system UAE families work inside; no affiliation, partnership or endorsement is implied, and IB Gram is not a client or supplier of any school named here.
igcse-may-june-exam-preparation.modesIntro: Three ways families use one-to-one online lessons across a May/June run-in. They are not packages with fixed prices; they are patterns of use, and most households move between them as the series approaches. All three are delivered over live video in Gulf Standard Time, and none involves a tutor travelling to a UAE address.

modes.title: Two-term weekly, September to study leave
modes.description: One or two fixed slots a week from the start of Year 11, running through the mock season and ending when the papers start. This is the pattern that catches syllabus gaps while there is still time to teach them rather than paper over them, and it is the only version in which a tutor sees the mock scripts before the feedback has gone cold.
bullets: Gaps found in October are teachable; the same gap found in April is only manageable
Mock papers reviewed question by question against the mark scheme, not by total mark
Pace set by the school's own scheme of work, read from the student's exercise book

modes.title: January-to-June intensive run-in
modes.description: The most common starting point for UAE families, beginning after the mock results and running to the last paper. Two to three hours a week, weighted toward timed question practice rather than new content, with the weeks around study leave deliberately heavier because that is when school teaching stops and nothing replaces it.
bullets: Session structure: a timed section, then the marking, then the specific repair
One subject at a time where the mock profile shows a single clear weakness
Scheduling rebuilt when the school announces its study-leave date

modes.title: Named-paper block and post-results work
modes.description: A short, defined block aimed at one component: an alternative-to-practical paper, an Economics Paper 2, a non-calculator maths paper. It is also the shape of the work that follows August results, when a family is deciding subject by subject whether a November resit is worth a term of effort.
bullets: Six to ten sessions against a single named component
Past-paper work from the correct syllabus code and the correct tier
After results: an honest read on whether a resit changes the outcome that matters

sections.heading: What a May/June entry has already decided for your child
paragraphs: A May/June IGCSE entry is a set of commitments made by a school on a candidate's behalf, several months before anyone sits anything. The centre chooses the board, the syllabus code, the components and, in tiered subjects, the Core and Extended tier. It submits those choices at the board's final entry deadline. After the amendment window shuts, the entry is what the student will sit, whatever happens to their performance between then and the summer.

This is the single most useful thing a parent can understand in January, because it reframes the question. The useful question is not whether a tutor can lift a grade in general. It is what specifically this candidate is entered for, and whether the preparation now under way matches it. A student drilling Extended past papers for an entry submitted at Core is practising questions they will never see. A student working from a Cambridge specification for a Pearson Edexcel International GCSE entry is in the same position.

The document that settles it is the statement of entry, which the centre issues to the candidate. It lists the candidate number, the syllabus codes, the components and the series. It is worth reading line by line, including the spelling of the name, because an error there is correctable while an error discovered in results week usually is not. Everything in the rest of this page assumes you have that sheet in front of you, because without it any revision plan is a guess dressed up as a schedule.
bullets: Read the syllabus code, not the subject name, off the statement of entry
Confirm the tier for every tiered subject before buying any revision material
Check the components listed: a missing practical or coursework line is a question for the exams officer
Note the series code; a modular Edexcel candidate may be sitting fewer papers than the cohort

sections.heading: The May/June series counted backwards from the last paper
paragraphs: Almost nobody publishes the exam calendar in the direction parents actually need it: backwards from the papers. Counted that way, the picture changes. The decisions that most affect a grade are taken furthest from the exam, and the decisions available closest to the exam are the least powerful. Pearson's published dates for a series a UAE candidate can actually sit make the lead time concrete: the November 2026 International GCSE timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, the entry that fixed the candidate list closed months before that first paper, and the results did not reach students until the new year - the November 2025 series landed with students on 22 January 2026. Counted the same way, a summer series puts the binding decisions in the spring and the grades in August: Pearson's June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Cambridge's June and November series for UAE candidates have the same shape, with the exact entry deadline printed on the centre's statement of entry rather than inferable from a calendar.

Those are March-series dates, used here because they are published and verifiable, and because the shape repeats for every series including May/June. Entries close roughly a term before the papers. Forecast grades can be due while the examinations are in progress. Results land months after the last script is written. Pearson's published figures for a May/June series show the back end of that shape for International GCSE: June 2026 results went to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students the following day.

The table below is the milestone sequence rather than a dated calendar, because the exact dates differ by board, by series and by zone, and because a board can revise a provisional timetable. Pearson publishes provisional timetables ahead of each series and says so plainly, which is why every plan should be anchored to the live PDF on the board's own site rather than to a date copied off a tutoring page. Use the sequence to work out which decisions in your household are still live, and which have already gone.

sections.heading: Why UAE schools put nearly every candidate in this series
paragraphs: A UAE IGCSE candidate can, in principle, sit in more than one series. In practice the summer series carries almost the entire cohort, and the reason is the academic year rather than the examination. The UAE school year ends in the early summer. A Year 11 student finishing in June walks straight into a Year 12 place in September, with results arriving in August in between. The November series sits in the middle of Year 12, which means a resit candidate is preparing for an old qualification while starting a new one.

Cambridge names its main series June and Pearson names the same window May/June, which is where the search phrase comes from. Both boards also run a November series. Cambridge does run one additional sitting in February and March, but it is offered to centres in India only and a UAE candidate cannot be entered for it, so June and November are the whole of the picture here. Cambridge also runs Primary and Lower Secondary Checkpoint tests in March, May and October, which are diagnostic tests rather than certificated qualifications and are frequently confused with the real thing by parents of younger children - a Checkpoint date in March is not an IGCSE exam date.

The practical reading for a UAE family is this. The summer series is the one to plan for, the November series is the fallback and the only realistic second attempt within the same academic cycle, and nothing else on the calendar is a certificated IGCSE. If a school mentions a March entry, ask specifically whether the centre is in a zone allocated to that series, because Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and the timetable differs between them.

sections.heading: The summer term is the thinnest teaching term in the UAE year
paragraphs: Parents often assume that the closer the papers get, the more teaching a child receives. The opposite is true, and it is structural rather than anyone's fault. A Year 11 week in September contains a full timetable of new content. The same week in April contains revision sessions, past papers and, before long, no timetabled lessons at all, because the student is on study leave at home. The teaching hours available for genuinely new syllabus content fall away months before the first paper.

Three UAE-specific features sharpen this. The mandatory UAE subjects continue to occupy timetable space through the exam term under the emirate regulator's requirements. Ramadan shortens the school day in whichever weeks it falls, altering lesson lengths and compressing evenings for fasting households. And the school calendar itself, approved by KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, the Department of Knowledge or the federal Ministry of Education depending on the emirate, sets the term and study-leave dates that decide how the final weeks are shaped.

Read the table below against your own child's year and the arithmetic becomes uncomfortable. If a topic has not been taught properly by February, the school timetable contains almost no hours in which to teach it, and study leave contains none. This is the honest case for one-to-one support in the run-in: not that a tutor teaches better than a school, but that in the final term a tutor is the only person with scheduled hours left to teach anything new at all.

sections.heading: Who regulates the school, and what the regulator does not control
paragraphs: UAE private schools are regulated at emirate level, and the map is complete and short. Dubai sits with KHDA, which u.ae describes as responsible for enhancing and overseeing the quality of private education in the emirate. Abu Dhabi and Al Ain sit with ADEK, which supervises the licensing and accreditation of private schools. Sharjah sits with SPEA, which regulates private education in the emirate, and Ras Al Khaimah with its Department of Knowledge. The Ministry of Education plays a pivotal role in supervising private schools in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah.

Two of these bodies have an unusually wide remit that parents underestimate. Sharjah's and Ras Al Khaimah's authorities approve tuition fees, curricula, programmes, courses, activities and assessment methods, so the approval of what a school teaches and how it assesses sits with the emirate, not only the inspection of how well it does it. At federal level, private schools are not obliged to follow a specific curriculum beyond Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies, but must adhere to the Ministry's general regulations.

What none of them does is run the examination. The board publishes the series, allocates the zone timetable, marks the papers and releases the grades. A regulator cannot move a paper, change a mark or extend an entry deadline. That distinction decides where a parent's time goes when something is wrong. A clash in the school's internal calendar, a coursework deadline handled badly or an access-arrangement application never filed are school matters, escalated to the head of centre and then to the emirate regulator. A disputed mark is a board matter, and only the centre can lodge it.

sections.heading: Arabic, Islamic Education and Social Studies beside the exam timetable
paragraphs: Every February a UAE parent asks whether the mandatory UAE subjects can be set aside so the student can revise. The answer is that they are not the school's discretion to drop. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, and KHDA stated that its requirements must be implemented by the start of the 2025-26 academic year, or April 2026 for schools whose year begins in April. The federal position behind that is the same: Arabic language, social studies and Islamic studies are the baseline every private school must teach.

The KHDA mandatory subjects guidance is specific in ways worth knowing. For Arabic as a first language, Islamic Education and Social Studies, schools must organise separate classes for Arabs and non-Arabs, and combined classes for both groups are strictly prohibited because of the different curriculum expectations and language of instruction. Standard Arabic is required as the main language of instruction for Islamic Education for Arabs and for Arabic as a first language. Instructional time is calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit, schools may vary lesson length if the weekly total is met, and it is advised that any mandatory subject lesson runs at least 25 minutes.

Two further points shape what tutoring is even permitted here. Schools must ensure that all teachers of Islamic Education and Arabic hold appropriate KHDA approval to teach those subjects, which is a checkable credential rather than a claim. And for the mandatory subjects, the use of any different or additional content without prior permission from the Ministry of Education is strictly prohibited. Support for these subjects therefore means working with the school's own material and the student's own understanding of it, not importing a parallel course.

sections.heading: What a January-to-June run-in costs in this market
paragraphs: Three of the six most visible competitor pages in this market publish no price at all, and two of the rest quote in US dollars, a currency UAE families do not transact in. So here are the AED bands, with the source and the date attached, because a parent budgeting for a five-month run-in needs a number rather than an adjective. These are market rates read in October 2026 from published UAE provider rate cards and from Bestimate's Tutoring Cost Dubai 2026 rate table. They are not an IB Gram price list.

Two patterns are worth naming. First, the spread is enormous: the same hour is sold from under AED 50 to over AED 600, and the difference is tutor qualification and specialism rather than anything about the format. Second, monthly packages quoted in this market cluster around AED 799 a month for eight online sessions and AED 1,599 to AED 1,799 a month for four two-hour visits at a UAE address, which tells you most of what you need to know about what travel time costs when someone else is paying for it.

For context on the household side, KHDA confirmed on 22 May 2026 that there would be no increase in school fees for private schools in Dubai for the 2026-27 academic year, under Dubai's second economic incentives package valued at AED 1.5 billion within a AED 2.5 billion total. A flat school fee makes the tutoring line the variable one in a family budget, which is a good reason to decide the number of hours deliberately rather than drifting into more of them as the papers approach.

sections.heading: A locally hired visiting tutor against live online in the final twelve weeks
paragraphs: This is the decision most UAE families are actually making in January, so it deserves a straight answer rather than a sales pitch. Hiring someone to come to the villa or apartment has real advantages, and they are mostly about a teenager who will not otherwise sit down. It also has costs that only become visible in the exam term, when the schedule is under pressure and a missed visit cannot be rebuilt into a week that no longer has spare evenings in it.

The sharpest difference is who you can choose from. A visiting tutor has to live within a workable drive of your home, which means the available pool is defined by geography rather than by subject. For a mainstream Maths or Biology entry in Dubai that pool is large. For an Edexcel modular Physics unit, a Cambridge 0478 pre-release task or an Economics Paper 2 in Fujairah, it may be empty. Live video removes the drive from the equation and leaves only the question of whether the tutor knows the paper.

IB Gram delivers one-to-one online lessons and does not send tutors to homes anywhere in the UAE; home visits are a service we run only in India. The table below sets out the comparison honestly, including the places where a locally hired visiting tutor wins. If your child genuinely cannot work without someone physically present, that is a real constraint and the right answer may be a local arrangement. For most families in the final twelve weeks, specialist match and schedule resilience matter more than presence.

sections.heading: Results arrive in August, when half the country is away
paragraphs: A May/June series produces its results in the middle of the UAE summer break. Pearson sent its June 2026 International GCSE results to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Many UAE families are out of the country on that date, often in a different time zone and sometimes without reliable access to the school's systems. The decisions that follow results are the most time-pressured of the entire cycle, and they are frequently taken from a hotel room.

Three of those decisions have real deadlines. An enquiry about results, which includes a review of marking, is lodged by the centre and not by the family, and the window is short. A sixth-form or college place conditional on a grade may need confirming within days. And an entry for the autumn series has to be made within weeks of August results if a resit is going to happen in the same academic cycle, since Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026.

The practical preparation is unglamorous and takes an hour in June. Know who at the school can act in results week and how to reach them when the office is on reduced summer hours. Know which of your decisions needs a person physically in the UAE and which does not. Write down the fallback for each subject before results exist, because a plan written calmly in June is better than one written in twenty minutes on 20 August. Where a grade is genuinely borderline, decide in advance what you would do with each possible outcome.
bullets: Confirm before the summer break who at the centre handles results-week queries and on what hours
Note that only the centre can lodge an enquiry about results, and that the window is measured in days
Decide in advance, per subject, what a grade below the forecast would actually change
Check the autumn-series entry deadline against your travel dates, not against term dates

sections.heading: The five grades the Ministry of Education counts
paragraphs: For families who intend their child to study at a UAE university or to use the certificate locally, the May/June results feed into a Ministry of Education equivalency file. The British-track rules were clarified publicly and are specific. Gulf Today reported that students must pass five accredited subjects in GCSE or IGCSE certificates with a grade of no less than E or grade 3, and must submit proof of one accredited subject at the Advanced Level with a grade of no less than E, or two accredited subjects at the Advanced Subsidiary Level with the same grade.

The detail that catches people is the exclusion: Arabic and Islamic education are not included among the five required subjects for the GCSE or IGCSE count. A student can sit nine subjects, pass all of them, and still need to check which five are being counted. One competitor page currently ranking for these searches states that UAE candidates must take six IGCSE subjects, which does not match the published clarification. If a page tells you a number, check it against moe.gov.ae or your emirate's attestation authority before you plan around it.

For completeness: on the American track, English proficiency requires a score of 5 in the IELTS academic test, 61 in the TOEFL iBT, or 450 in the reading and writing section of the SAT, and mathematics requires at least 450 in the SAT Math test. No International Baccalaureate points threshold appears in the source read for this page, so no IB figure is published here. Equivalency and attestation are processes the Ministry runs, not services IB Gram performs, and no amount of tutoring is a requirement for either.

sections.heading: Where a tutor stops, and who is permitted to teach in the evening
paragraphs: Some of what sells in this market should not be bought. One page ranking for these searches sells completed Internal Assessments at a fixed price. Assessed work has to be the student's own. A tutor can teach the underlying skill, explain a mark scheme, discuss a draft the student has written and point out where an argument fails. A tutor cannot write it, rewrite it, or edit it to completion, and a tutor should not supply or reproduce board syllabus documents, past papers, mark schemes or grade-boundary tables as downloads. Those are the board's material to publish, and referencing them with a link is the correct approach.

Second, the permit. Private tutoring in the UAE is regulated. The MoHRE private tuition work permit was introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and is applied for through MoHRE's own service, Issuance of a New Work Permit - Private Tutor Licensing, via its smart app, website and e-services system, with a stated completion time of two working days. Eligible applicants include teachers registered in government or private schools, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, school students aged 15 to 18, and university students.

Individuals offering private tutoring without a permit from MoHRE are subject to fines and penalties outlined in the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so no amount is quoted here, and any page that quotes one is guessing. A separate point for Abu Dhabi families: ADEK's professional-ethics rules for private and charter school staff have been reported to prohibit teachers from providing paid private tutoring to students enrolled at their own school, and the permit's code of conduct has been reported to bar serving students affiliated with the tutor's own school. Verify the current wording with ADEK before relying on it.

process.title: Send the statement of entry
process.description: Not the report card. The statement of entry lists the board, the syllabus codes, the components and the series, and it is what decides which tutor is the right one. If it has not been issued yet, the exams officer can confirm the codes and the tier by email in a sentence.

process.title: A consultation about the series, not the subject
process.description: A short call that establishes what is already fixed, how many weeks remain before the school's study-leave date, which components are internally marked and already submitted, and where the mock evidence says the marks are actually going missing.

process.title: One diagnostic session on a real past paper
process.description: A timed section from the correct syllabus and tier, marked against the mark scheme in front of the student. This produces a specific list rather than an impression, and it occasionally shows that the problem is exam technique rather than knowledge, which changes the plan entirely.

process.title: A written plan to the last paper
process.description: Week by week to the final component, weighted toward the weeks when school teaching stops. It names the topics, the papers to be sat under timed conditions and the dates the plan will be revised, including what happens if the school moves study leave.

process.title: Weekly sessions, with the coverage position stated
process.description: Fixed slots in Gulf Standard Time. If no specialist is available for a niche component, we say so at the start rather than offering a general tutor and hoping. Where a UAE-based tutor is unavailable for a subject, any alternative arrangement is disclosed before the first lesson.

process.title: Results week, and the resit decision
process.description: A short review after August results, subject by subject: whether the grade is borderline enough for the centre to consider an enquiry about results, and whether an autumn entry changes the outcome that actually matters or simply occupies a term of Year 12.

whyPoints.title: The series is the unit of planning, not the school year
whyPoints.description: Preparation is built backwards from a named component on a named timetable, in the correct Cambridge administrative zone, rather than forwards from a generic revision calendar. That is why the first document we ask for is the statement of entry and the second is the school's study-leave date.

whyPoints.title: Figures with their sources attached
whyPoints.description: Every AED band on this page carries the provider type and the date it was read. Every regulatory statement names the authority it came from. Where a fact could not be verified, including IB session dates, we say so instead of publishing a number that reads convincingly and is wrong.

whyPoints.title: Specialist match beats geography
whyPoints.description: A family in Fujairah or Umm Al Quwain gets the same access to an Edexcel modular Physics specialist as a family in Jumeirah, because the match is made on the paper rather than on the drive. Online delivery is the mechanism that makes that possible, not a compromise on the way to it.

whyPoints.title: Clear limits on assessed work
whyPoints.description: Coursework, practical write-ups and any internally marked component stay the student's own work. We teach the skill, discuss the student's draft and explain the criteria. We do not write, rewrite or complete assessed work, and we do not reproduce board material as downloadable files.

whyPoints.title: Honest about what we are not
whyPoints.description: IB Gram is an independent tutor-matching platform with no KHDA, ADEK, SPEA, Ministry of Education, Cambridge or Pearson approval, no UAE office or centre, and no affiliation with any school named on this page. Tutors are matched individuals, and their permit status is a fair question to ask before the first lesson.

whyPoints.title: Coverage stated before you commit
whyPoints.description: If a component has no available specialist, that is said at the consultation. No competitor page in the research behind this project discloses a coverage limit, and several route UAE parents to non-UAE phone numbers without mentioning where delivery happens. Both are avoidable failures of trust.

faqs.question: Why do UAE schools put almost every IGCSE candidate into the summer series rather than the autumn one?
faqs.answer: Because the academic year, not the examination, decides it. A UAE Year 11 finishes in the early summer, results arrive in August, and a Year 12 place starts in September. The summer series fits that sequence exactly. The autumn series sits in the middle of Year 12, so a candidate sitting it is revising an old qualification while beginning a new one. Cambridge names the main series June and Pearson Edexcel names the same window May/June; both also run a November series, which in practice functions as the resit route rather than a first attempt for a mainstream UAE cohort.

faqs.question: The papers are in May and June, so why did the school ask for entry decisions back in the autumn?
faqs.answer: Because entries close roughly a term before the first paper, and they close the tier with them. Pearson's published dates for its November 2026 International GCSE series make the lead time visible: the papers ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and the entry that fixed the candidate list, the syllabus codes and the tier had been lodged months before that. The same shape applies to a May/June series, where entries close in the spring. The board needs the candidate list, the syllabus codes and the components finalised long before it prints a timetable and distributes scripts. For a parent, the consequence is that the useful conversation about subjects and tier happens a term or more ahead of the papers, not in the weeks before them.

faqs.question: Results arrive in August while we are out of the country. Does that actually create a problem?
faqs.answer: It can, because the decisions that follow results are the most time-pressured of the cycle. Pearson sent its June 2026 results to centres on 19 August 2026 and to students on 20 August 2026. Within days you may need to confirm a sixth-form place, decide whether to ask the centre to lodge an enquiry about results, and consider an autumn-series entry. Only the centre can lodge that enquiry, not the family. The fix is preparation rather than presence: before the break, confirm who at the school is reachable in results week and write down what you would do with each possible grade.

faqs.question: My son's first paper is in early May and his last in mid-June. Is a gap that long normal?
faqs.answer: Yes. A summer series spreads components across several weeks, and a candidate taking nine subjects can easily have papers at both ends of the window. It creates a specific problem: the subjects examined last are often the ones revised least, because attention collapses onto whatever is next. A plan built backwards from each paper rather than from the start of the window handles this. Check the zone timetable your centre is working from, since Cambridge allocates every centre to one of six administrative zones and states it cannot accept responsibility for candidates who miss an exam after using the wrong version.

faqs.question: Our school teaches Cambridge for some subjects and Edexcel for others in the same summer series. Can that work?
faqs.answer: It is common and it works, but it changes what preparation means. The two boards publish different specifications, different paper structures and different command vocabulary for the same subject name, and Pearson Edexcel runs some International GCSE subjects on a modular route where units are banked across series. A tutor working from the wrong specification can teach the topic competently and still leave a student unready for the paper. This is the entire reason the syllabus code matters more than the subject name, and why the statement of entry is the first document to read.

faqs.question: Does the Core or Extended decision have to be made before the entry closes?
faqs.answer: Effectively yes. The Core and Extended tier is part of the entry, and once the board's amendment window shuts, the candidate sits the paper set for the tier submitted. The decision belongs to the centre, usually on subject-teacher judgement, with family input. What a parent can influence is the evidence that judgement is formed from: mock performance, classwork and a timed past paper under real conditions. What a parent cannot do is lift the tier in April because revision has gone well. If the tier matters to your child's next step, raise it in the autumn term.

faqs.question: Eid falls between two of my daughter's papers. Should she keep studying through it?
faqs.answer: That is a household judgement rather than an academic rule, and families answer it differently. What is worth planning for is the shape of the gap. A long break between papers tends to help the subject sat after it and harm the one sat before, because preparation drifts to whatever is next. A practical compromise many UAE families use is a short daily block of timed questions in the subject still to come, kept to a fixed hour, with the rest of the day genuinely free. Sessions can be scheduled around prayer times and after-Iftar hours.

faqs.question: Year 11 goes on study leave in April. Who is responsible for the teaching after that?
faqs.answer: Formally, nobody. Study leave removes timetabled lessons, and the student is working at home in the weeks when revision intensity should be at its highest. Most schools offer revision clinics and remain available for questions, but the structure is gone. That is the honest case for one-to-one support in the run-in: not that a tutor teaches better than a school, but that during study leave a tutor is often the only person with scheduled hours in the week and sight of the student's actual written answers rather than their reported confidence.

faqs.question: Which authority do we complain to if the school mishandles an examination entry?
faqs.answer: Start with the school's head of centre, because entry administration is a centre function and most errors are correctable there if raised early. If that fails, escalate to the emirate regulator: KHDA in Dubai, ADEK in Abu Dhabi and Al Ain, SPEA in Sharjah, the Department of Knowledge in Ras Al Khaimah, or the federal Ministry of Education in Ajman, Umm Al Quwain and Fujairah. What no regulator can do is change anything the examination board controls, including the timetable, the marking and the results date. A disputed mark is a board matter and only the centre can lodge it.

faqs.question: Does the Social Studies lesson my daughter sits in Year 11 appear anywhere on her IGCSE certificate?
faqs.answer: No. The mandatory UAE subjects are a school requirement set by the emirate regulator, not a board entry, so they do not appear on an IGCSE certificate unless the school separately enters the student for a board subject such as an Arabic IGCSE. They are also not optional during the exam term. Arabic, Islamic Education and Social or Moral Studies are mandatory in all Dubai private schools regardless of the licensed international curriculum, with instructional time calculated on a 40-minute lesson unit and a recommended minimum lesson length of 25 minutes.

faqs.question: A grade in the summer results is lower than the school predicted. What can be done, and by when?
faqs.answer: Two routes, both with short windows. The centre can lodge an enquiry about results with the board, which may include a review of marking; the family cannot lodge it directly, so the conversation has to happen with the school within days of results. Separately, the candidate can be entered for the autumn series. Pearson's November 2026 final timetable ran from late October to 19 November 2026, and its November 2025 results reached students on 22 January 2026, which shows how the second attempt sits inside Year 12 rather than before it.

faqs.question: Is the autumn series a sensible second attempt, or a wasted term?
faqs.answer: It depends entirely on what the grade is for. If a specific grade is blocking a sixth-form subject, a university prerequisite or a Ministry of Education equivalency file, a focused resit in one or two subjects is often worth it. If the grade is adequate and the motive is tidiness, the term is usually better spent on Year 12, where new content is arriving fast. Decide subject by subject, not as a block, and decide it in the week after results rather than in October, because the entry deadline arrives quickly.

faqs.question: We need a Ministry of Education equivalency file ready for a September start. Does an August results date leave enough time?
faqs.answer: It is tight, which is why the paperwork should be assembled before results exist. The British-track requirements are published: five accredited GCSE or IGCSE subjects at a grade no less than E or grade 3, with Arabic and Islamic education excluded from that count, plus one accredited A Level at no less than E or two AS Levels at the same grade. Know in advance which five subjects you intend to count. Equivalency and attestation are processes the Ministry runs through its own channels, and no tutoring provider performs or guarantees either.

faqs.question: What do revision hours cost in the UAE between January and the summer papers?
faqs.answer: Market rates read in October 2026 run from AED 45 to 150 an hour for an independent university-student tutor, AED 150 to 300 for a qualified subject tutor online, AED 180 to 500 for a visiting tutor at a UAE address with travel included, and AED 200 to 450 or more for an IGCSE or A Level specialist, with named premium tutors published at AED 650. Monthly packages quoted locally cluster around AED 799 for eight online sessions. Those are market figures from published provider rate cards and Bestimate's 2026 table, not an IB Gram price list.

faqs.question: A university student has offered to tutor our son for AED 80 an hour. Is that lawful in the UAE?
faqs.answer: It can be, provided the permit is in place. The MoHRE private tuition work permit, introduced by Ministerial Resolution No. 710 of 2023, is granted free of charge for two years, and university students are expressly among the eligible applicants, alongside registered school teachers, government and private-sector employees, unemployed individuals, and school students aged 15 to 18. Individuals offering private tutoring without a MoHRE permit are subject to fines and penalties under the applicable laws. No fine schedule has been published, so treat any specific amount you read online as unverified.

faqs.question: Can a tutor help with coursework that the school marks before it goes to the board?
faqs.answer: Within clear limits. A tutor can teach the skill the component assesses, explain what the assessment criteria reward, discuss a draft the student has written and point out where an argument or a method does not hold. A tutor cannot write it, rewrite it or edit it to completion, and should not supply board material such as mark schemes or past papers as files. Internally marked work is also submitted on the centre's own deadline, usually a term before the papers, so the window for useful feedback closes earlier than most families expect.

faqs.question: How many weeks before the first paper should one-to-one support start?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most families start, for a structural reason rather than a commercial one. Teaching hours for new syllabus content fall away months before the papers: the mock season absorbs January and February, March and April are given to revision programmes, and study leave contains no timetabled lessons at all. A gap found in October can be taught; the same gap found in April can only be managed. If you are starting late, the honest plan narrows to the components where marks are most recoverable rather than covering the whole syllabus thinly.

faqs.question: My daughter is entered as a private candidate for one extra subject this series. What changes for her?
faqs.answer: The administration moves to her and to whichever centre accepts the entry, rather than sitting with her school. She needs a centre willing to enter her, an entry made by that centre's deadline, and a statement of entry from it, and she sits that paper on the centre's zone timetable, which may differ from her school's. Components involving internally marked coursework or practical work are the usual complication, since they need a centre able to administer them. Confirm all of this with the centre's exams officer in writing before planning any preparation.

igcse-may-june-exam-preparation.closingHeading: Start from the statement of entry, not the calendar on the fridge
igcse-may-june-exam-preparation.closingBody: If your child is sitting the summer series, three documents decide how the next few months should be spent: the statement of entry, the school's study-leave date and the last set of mock scripts. Send those and we can tell you in one conversation what is still movable and what is not. IGCSE May June exam preparation in the UAE works best when it is built backwards from a named component rather than forwards from a general wish to do better. Lessons are one-to-one, delivered over live video in Gulf Standard Time, anywhere in the seven emirates, and we will say plainly at the start if no specialist is free for the paper your child is entered for.
